vice-president of the committee on the environment, public health and food safety.– madam president, on behalf of the committee on the environment, public health and food safety (envi), i would like to present this objection pursuant to rule 106 on emissions from light passenger and commercial vehicles, the euro 6 standards. air pollution causes over 430 000 premature deaths in the eu every year and costs up to an estimated eur 940 billion a year as a result of its health impacts. in particular, nitrogen oxides (nox) are major air pollutants which cause, inter alia, lung cancer, asthma and many respiratory diseases, as well as environmental degradation such as eutrophication and acidification. according to the eea, nox emissions are the cause of at least 75 000 premature deaths in the european union yearly. diesel vehicle exhausts are a major source of nox in urban areas in europe, and the euro 6 limit value for nox emissions from diesel vehicles is 80 mg/km under so-called normal use conditions. the draft measure, the subject of the objection, aims to establish the so-called real driving emission requirements to limit the tailpipe emissions of light passenger and commercial vehicles. the motion for a resolution considers that the draft commission regulation would result in a de facto blanket derogation from applicable emission limits, which is not compatible with the aim and content of regulation 715/2007 and exceeds the implementing powers provided for in regulation 396/2005. the envi committee objects to the draft measure, in particular because it would allow vehicles to emit 168 mg/km of nitrogen oxide in the real driving emissions test, applicable to all new vehicles from september 2019, which means four years after the entry into force of the euro 6 80mg/km limit value. surpassing the regulation by 110% is something that deeply undermines not only the regulation itself but also, i believe, the credibility of the regulating eu bodies. the resolution therefore calls on the commission to withdraw the draft regulation and submit a new proposal by 1 april 2016 at the latest, introducing a real driving emissions test that would ensure the effectiveness of emission control systems.

in writing. ‒ when deciding whether to suspend the immunity of a member in a given case, the european parliament applies its own permanent principles. one of those principles is that immunity is normally suspended where the offence is covered by article 9 of protocol no 7, provided that there is no serious and well-founded suspicion that the case was brought before the court with the aim of causing political damage to the member. in the present case, the request for suspension of mr czesław adam siekierski's immunity was made in connection with an alleged infringement of the rules on speed limits in a residential area. mr czesław adam siekierski admitted that he was driving the vehicle at the time in question, although he failed to indicate on the relevant form whether he accepted or refused to pay the fine. in the circumstances of the case, it appears that the alleged infringement and the criminal liability resulting therefrom clearly have no connection with mr czesław adam siekierski's position as a member of the european parliament. on the basis of the above considerations and in accordance with the rules of procedure, the committee on legal affairs proposes that the european parliament suspend the parliamentary immunity of mr czesław adam siekierski.
in writing. ‒ according to the polish high authority for traffic police, czesław adam siekierski, member of the european parliament, exceeded the maximum speed allowed in a residential area at 8:22 on 10 january 2015 while driving and therefore applied to the european parliament for the suspension of the member's immunity. in its report, the parliament's legal affairs committee found that the alleged infringement was not directly or manifestly connected with the performance of the duties of member of the european parliament by mr czesław adam siekierski and that there was no serious and well-founded suspicion that the request was made with the aim of causing political damage to the member, and therefore recommended that the immunity be suspended. i voted accordingly.
in writing. ‒ on 13 august 2015, the prosecutor general of the republic of poland forwarded to the president of the parliament the request of the polish high traffic police to authorise the prosecution of czesław adam siekierski, member of the european parliament, in connection with an infringement of the speed limit. the polish highway traffic police claimed that siekierski was driving in a residential area at 77 km/h and on being called admitted to driving the car and sent a photocopy of his european parliament id. following the s&d group's decision, i supported the suspension of the immunity.

in writing. ‒ the european commission has proposed to incorporate the recommendations of the international commission for the conservation of atlantic tunas (iccat) for the conservation of bluefin tuna into european fisheries legislation. i voted in favour of the report, in agreement with the group of the european people's party. 30% of the world's oceans are overfished, and marine fish stocks are in danger. it is therefore understandable that the european union is forced to restrict marine fisheries appropriately in order to maintain marine fish stocks. so the amount of sea fish caught is decreasing steadily and significantly. the cfp should therefore pay much more attention to sustainable fisheries, i.e. aquaculture, and in particular freshwater fisheries. a significant part of the hungarian wetlands is located in natura 2000 areas. these fish farms do not represent any threat to the natural values of these areas. in fact, in many cases it is our closed systems of wetlands that have created and preserved unique associations of aquatic habitats. therefore, freshwater aquaculture should be given priority and maximum support from the union. moreover, this area should be freed from unnecessarily stringent and unnecessary sustainability standards that are justified only for marine fisheries and aquaculture.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report, which sets out the challenges facing europe and the world in the context of globalisation, migration, inter-religious and intercultural conflicts and the rise of radicalism. it also makes important recommendations for an open and respectful exchange of ideas between people and groups from different cultural backgrounds or worldviews in the european union. i agree with the statement that the european union must promote full respect for the universal declaration of human rights, both internationally and within its member states. i also support the idea of integrating cultural dialogue and diversity in a transversal way into policies such as child and youth policy or home affairs. better and more coherent cooperation is needed between the different policy structures and themes, not only at eu level but also at national and local level. finally, i share the rapporteur's view that respect and acceptance of cultures is not just a matter for the authorities and decision-makers, but for society as a whole. however, i would like to draw attention to the work done by individual member states in this area, which has not helped to promote intercultural dialogue but, on the contrary, has been a campaign of incitement. the european union must be clear about its opposition to such openly hateful activities.

i did not vote for the report on eu regulation of financial services, partly because it prescribes things with future effects that were already rules in the past and would have been particularly important in preventing the tragedies of foreign exchange credit. what am i thinking here? the report includes, for example, the obligation to provide customers with thorough information when borrowing, which has been in place until now. it holds bankers accountable - they should have been - many of them should be in jail by now, and it has strong banking supervision. i don't understand why that didn't work either. i asked the european commissioner during the debate what the union wanted to do to help the very distressed, tragic foreign currency borrowers. of course, in his usual impudent manner, he didn't answer.
in writing. ‒ the report sets out the issues that should be examined in order to facilitate the path towards a capital markets union. preamble to the commission green paper on building a capital markets union and parliament's resolution of 9 july 2015 on the green paper. these documents, as their title indicates, deal with the implementation of the capital markets union. the report takes the view that, as the eu capital market remains fragmented, the commission should take measures to facilitate the creation of a single capital market. some measures are acceptable to mitigate the potential for financial crises, although it should be stressed that crises are a consequence of the financial liberalisation and deregulation of the 1990s and are not intended to reverse it, but only to limit it to a certain extent. the fundamental objective, however, is to achieve the full integration of the union in the financial field, which means the centralisation of measures in the financial field, and is thus one of the means of achieving the objective set by the union's leadership of an ever closer union, that is to say, of creating a centralised european empire. i disagree with that aim, so i rejected the whole report.
in writing. ‒ the financial and debt crisis that erupted in 2007/2008 required comprehensive action by european legislators and international standard-setters. since then, a number of legislative initiatives have been launched in the area of financial services in the union with the aim of restoring financial stability, strengthening consumer protection and implementing the lessons learned from the crisis. many pieces of legislation have already been successfully adopted and the deadlines for implementation and application have been met or are about to be met. this own-initiative report is a first step to provide an overview of this legislative work, to address the shortcomings identified in the financial services legislation and to respond to concerns raised in particular because the effects of individual legislative measures and their interactions have not been adequately analysed and the cumulative impact of the general legislation has not yet been fully assessed. in my view, important new commission initiatives such as the investment package and the capital markets union can achieve better results if they build on existing regulation on financial services that works effectively and efficiently.
in writing. ‒ the report supports the achievement of an objective whose reality is becoming less and less, and therefore can only be supported in detail. certain measures may be acceptable in order to mitigate the potential for financial crises. it is true that these crises are the consequences of the financial liberalization and deregulation that took place in the 1990s, and the report does not speak of reversing them, only of restricting them to a certain extent. the main objective is to achieve full integration of the union in the financial field, which is one of the means of achieving the goal set by the union's leadership of an 'ever closer union', i.e. a european union of the united states type. except for the weaker countries getting caught up in it. that's hard to agree with.
in writing. ‒ since the financial and debt crisis of 2007/2008, a number of legislative initiatives have been launched in the area of eu financial services, aimed at restoring financial stability, strengthening consumer protection, and drawing lessons from the crisis. the report of the economic and monetary committee aims to provide an overview of this legislative work, to address the shortcomings identified in the financial services legislation and to address concerns raised in particular by the failure to adequately analyse the effects of and interactions between individual legislative measures. the report is concerned about possible contradictions and inconsistencies in the current regulation and suggests to follow up the informal initiative that the commission launched already at the beginning of 2014. the combined impact assessment and the mandatory regular checks on consistency and proportionality ensure that the application of financial services legislation is less complex, accessible to smes and better adapted to their needs. the report states that the current legislation needs to be fully implemented and strictly applied in the member states. it considers it important that financial stability and consumer protection continue to be a priority for lawmakers and that greater emphasis be placed on the consistent application of the risk-based approach. i supported the adoption of the report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the overview and challenges of eu regulation of financial services. the current financial and debt crisis has indeed had unprecedented adverse consequences in europe, but by now the european institutions have managed to put in place a financial framework that has strengthened the eu's financial structure against future crises. however, i agree with the report that the capital market in the union remains fragmented and that smes and micro-enterprises continue to be severely affected by the lack of capital. the capital markets union can indeed provide a valuable framework to ensure equal access to finance for smes across the union and to foster the emergence of innovative forms of market-based finance. the capital markets union would provide an opportunity for smes to complement bank-based financing, an area in which the united states has made stronger progress since the financial crisis. i consider it very important and welcome that the report proposes an integrated approach to the commission with regard to the cmu, including the digital single market. furthermore, the rapporteur has very rightly emphasised the importance of consumer protection in the financial services sector. consumers should be informed in a quality, accurate, user-friendly, reliable, timely and, above all, understandable language that facilitates the right decision-making. however, it is a matter of concern that consumers are often confronted with unclear information that is not intended to serve their needs.

in writing. ‒ entrepreneurship is a mindset that enables individuals to turn their motivation and capacity to identify an opportunity and fully realize it. enterprise policy has been a political priority since the entry into force of the lisbon treaty, but the european union is still lagging behind: in 2009, the proportion of entrepreneurs was 12% in the eu-27, compared with 27% in china and 21% in the united states. to get europe growing again and creating new jobs, the european union needs more entrepreneurs. the gender gap in entrepreneurship is still evident; in 2012, only 31% of all self-employed citizens in the union of 28 were women. directive 2004/113/ec expressly prohibits direct or indirect discrimination in the field of financial services, including bank loans. there is no evidence of direct discrimination in member states, as the refusal to provide financing to female entrepreneurs may also be the result of an economic logic whereby investors in more profitable and male-dominated sectors seek higher returns from larger companies. however, some evidence suggests that indirect discrimination, influenced by women's perceptions of access to finance, does occur.

in writing. ‒ the positive benefits of a common digital single market based on a common set of rules include growth, strengthening the single market and job creation. however, it will provide an opportunity for entrepreneurs to spread their innovative ideas and for the smooth functioning of the barrier-free cross-border e-commerce market. this innovative trend is impacting a large part of society and, more importantly, is creating opportunities for growth. it is important to mention that the opportunities are not limited to the challenges faced by all digital market participants. in order to make this market seamless, sustainable and accessible to all, efforts should be made to improve access to services, in particular with regard to unjustified territorial content restriction. this also includes the proposal to eliminate unfair price discrimination based on geographical location or nationality, which has the direct effect of creating monopolies and driving some consumers towards illegal content. this restriction on content undermines the rights of national minorities, as some content is not available in their mother tongue. we need to move forward step by step on this issue, after the competition problems have been resolved.
in writing. ‒ on 6 may 2015, the commission decided on 16 initiatives under the 'digital strategy for europe' to be implemented by the end of 2016. as a member of the hungarian people's party delegation, i voted in favour of the kallas-gebhardt report, which is the european parliament's response to the strategy proposed by the commission. the digital single market opens up new opportunities to boost the economy through e-commerce, and makes it easier for businesses to comply with administrative and financial regulations, and strengthens consumer rights through e-government. the digital single market requires a regulatory framework that facilitates the development of cloud computing, borderless mobile data connectivity and simplified access to information and content, while guaranteeing the protection of privacy and personal data, cybersecurity and net neutrality. the adopted report proposes further steps towards the completion of the digital single market and addresses the impact of the completion of the digital single market on society and the economy as a whole.
in writing. ‒ while the eu's trade legislation has been largely harmonised, the digital market is still fragmented and needs to be further harmonised, given the high level of cross-border traffic. unjustified territorial discrimination and content restrictions against consumers should be eliminated and consumer protection strengthened. the digital market also needs to strike a balance between excessive expectations and reality. it will not solve europe's accumulated economic problems or its unemployment problem, but there is no doubt that the rapid growth of online platforms has already led to economic recovery in the union and opened up new prospects. there are legitimate privacy concerns. the regulation should ensure that everyone has full control over the handling of their own data. it's going to be difficult to find harmony between the digital world, the resulting overwhelming mechanization, virtuality and the future of man as a soul-body being, but we have a duty to strive for it.
in writing. ‒ the digital single market offers a huge opportunity for eu businesses and companies to grow and for the eu labour market to fully recover from the economic crisis and the measures taken in its wake. the innovation in the digital sector is constantly changing the way citizens communicate, share and consume, and even their behaviour, and therefore innovation offers new opportunities for both businesses and consumers. the use of digital technologies is also increasingly facilitating citizens' access to information and culture, increasing their employment opportunities and making a wider range of products available to them. it also offers the opportunity to make the governance and administration of the union and the member states more efficient. the joint report by the committee on industry, research and energy and the committee on the internal market and consumer protection, in response to the european commission's proposal 16, provides further details on the steps needed to complete the digital single market and the impact of the completion of the digital single market on society and the economy as a whole. it points out that stimulating a dynamic economy is essential for innovation to flourish and innovative companies to expand, and that this is what the european commission, together with the member states, should focus on. more needs to be done to promote an entrepreneurial culture, including innovative business models, and to connect europe's many successful technology hubs. i supported the adoption of the report.

in writing. ‒ the commission has proposed the adoption of a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on the placing of personal protective equipment on the union market. the placing on the market of personal protective equipment in the union is harmonised by council directive 89/686/eec. over the past 25 years, the directive has made it possible to create a well-functioning single market, but it still needs to be updated in line with the new legislative framework, a package of measures to streamline and simplify the rules governing the single market for goods. the committee on the internal market and consumer protection has recommended that parliament should support the proposal, with more than 150 amendments. i voted for the report.
in writing. ‒ since 1989, the placing of personal protective equipment (ppe) on the eu market has been fully harmonised by council directive 89/686/eec. during the 25 years of intervention, the directive has made possible a functioning single market. nevertheless, the existing ppe legislation needs to be updated in line with the new legislative framework, the package of measures to streamline and simplify the regulation of the single market for goods. i voted for the motion.
in writing. ‒ in our work on the proposal for a regulation on personal protective equipment, our first objective was to propose amendments that would ensure that the current directive does not give rise to interpretations that undermine its effectiveness and legal certainty. the basic premise is that only truly effective means can ensure the safety of workers, taking into account that accidents at work are caused not only by the use of inappropriate personal protective equipment, but also, often, by its incorrect application. we also found that the effective effectiveness of the protective device can be ensured by developing and introducing products that are adapted to the needs of their end-users. therefore, it is emphasised that the wearer of the equipment should be taken into account and that the following categories of users should be distinguished: men, women, young workers and persons with disabilities. furthermore, we consider that certain aspects of the technical specifications of the regulation should be reviewed to cover all risk categories and probabilities in order to minimise the possibility of ambiguity and misinterpretation.
in writing. ‒ the commission has proposed the adoption of a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on the regulation of the internal market in gas-fired equipment. directive 2009/142/ec currently lays down the essential requirements that gas-fired equipment must meet in order to be placed on the union market. the legislation should be updated in line with the new legislative framework, the package of measures to streamline and simplify the rules on the single market for goods. the committee on the internal market and consumer protection has reported that parliament should support the proposal, albeit with more than 200 amendments. i voted for the report.
in writing. ‒ the rapporteur supports the proposal for a regulation on gas-fired equipment, which aims to replace directive 2009/142/ec. this directive is an example of union harmonisation legislation ensuring the free movement of gas-fired equipment. the directive has made a significant contribution to the establishment and functioning of the single market and harmonises the conditions for the marketing and/or putting into service of gas-fired equipment covered by it, taking into account the safety risks associated with gas and the rational use of energy. the union currently has 470 million gas-fired units and this number is increasing, with 30 million units sold annually. i voted in favour of the document.
in writing. ‒ i support the proposal for a regulation on cableway installations, which is an example of eu harmonisation legislation. the proposal aims at harmonising the conditions for placing on the market of sub-assemblies and safety components to be incorporated into cableway installations and at ensuring the free movement of those products within the union. all safety components and sub-assemblies shall be designed and manufactured in accordance with the essential requirements laid down in this regulation. it also provides for the full harmonisation of the essential requirements to be met by cableway installations. this regulation repeals and replaces directive 2000/20/ec of 9 march 2000 on passenger rolling stock.
in writing. ‒ the commission has proposed the adoption of a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on the harmonisation of the conditions of placing on the market of sub-assemblies and safety components for use in cableway installations and on the free movement of such products within the union. it replaces directive 2000/20/ec on passenger rolling stock. this regulation aligns the provisions on cableway installations with the package of goods adopted in 2008 and in particular with decision no 768/2008/ec on a common framework for the placing of products on the market. the committee on the internal market and consumer protection has reported that parliament should support the proposal with almost 150 amendments. i voted for the report.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution, agreeing with the report's priorities reflecting the indivisible and universal nature of human rights , which guide the european union's representatives in their work at the un human rights council this year. the detailed resolution addresses the protection of human and civil rights in the traditional sense, but also addresses women, children and other groups particularly vulnerable to violations, as well as economic and environmental aspects. for my part, i particularly welcome the emphasis on the two most pressing challenges facing the eu and the international community today, the refugee crisis and terrorism, and their many human rights implications. in considering this issue, i have taken into account the regrettable fact that the european union, in its present political state, is ill-suited to the role of global guiding and norm-setting that it has traditionally played in the promotion and protection of universal human rights, owing to the behaviour of certain member states. thus, the government of my own country has made the inhumane treatment of refugees, the discrimination and oppression of our own minorities and the poor, or the severe restrictions on the basic human and civil rights of the population on the pretext of the threat of terrorism, an integral part of its policy. i hope that this guiding decision of the ep will also contribute to the eradication of such practices by member states and thus to the restoration of the political and moral credibility of the eu.

in writing. biodiversity ensures the maintenance and renewal of resources without which soil formation, nutrient and water cycles would not be possible. the loss of biodiversity is a loss for nature and for the economy. we have not done enough to preserve the biodiversity that is the foundation of our existence. the european commission's mid-term assessment shows that more than three quarters of the eu's important natural habitats are in poor condition and several species are threatened with extinction. the amendment i tabled with my austrian colleague elisabeth köstinger was supported by a large majority in the committee on the environment. in order to avoid negative impacts on biodiversity, the precautionary principle should be fully applied when gmos are authorised in the union. pest resistant gm crops make it impossible to apply integrated pest management, which means that we only intervene when the presence of pests justifies it. to protect biodiversity, we can never completely eradicate the pest population, we can only reduce it to a certain level. it is also of serious concern that co-cropping of genetically modified and conventional crops may never be fully feasible in practice. gm crops can contaminate areas under organic cultivation. finally, i would point out that due to their typical large-scale, monoculture farming methods, gmos pose a food safety risk in the countries and regions that receive such crops.

in writing. ‒ the convention on long-range transboundary air pollution, signed in 1979 and entered into force in 1983, established a framework for monitoring and reducing the adverse effects of transboundary air pollution on human health and the environment. one of the two aarhus protocols of 1998 supplementing the convention aims to reduce and control anthropogenic emissions of lead, cadmium and mercury into the air. the accession of the community to the protocol was approved by council decision 2001/379/ec of 4 april 2001. the protocol entered into force on 29 december 2003. the protocol was amended by three decisions of the parties in december 2012. decision 2012/5, which provides for stricter limit values for dust emissions from these significant fixed sources and introduces transitional measures in favour of parties acceding to the amended protocol before the end of 2019, should be ratified by the parties. the draft decision submitted by the council suggests that this should be done. the committee on the environment, public health and food safety, in its report, finds that the amendment is fully in line with the union legislation in force and therefore recommends that parliament add its consent to the draft decision. i voted accordingly.
in writing. ‒ the ratification of the amendments to the recommendation represents a significant step towards a higher level of protection of human health and the environment from transboundary air pollution. the explanatory memorandum refers to several studies (between 1972 and 1977) showing that air pollutants travel thousands of kilometres before they are deposited. i agree that the problems caused by air pollution must be addressed at international level. a binding international instrument in the form of a convention came into force in 1983, establishing a framework for monitoring and reducing harmful effects. the 1998 additional protocol on heavy metals aims to reduce and control anthropogenic emissions of lead, cadmium and mercury into the air. it requires the parties to reduce their annual cumulative emissions below 1990 levels. the aim of the protocol is to reduce emissions from industrial sources (iron, steel and non-ferrous metals), combustion processes (energy production, road transport) and waste incineration. the protocol sets limits and requires the use of best available techniques. the parties shall establish and maintain an emission inventory of lead, cadmium and mercury emissions, eliminate the use of leaded petrol and reduce the amount of mercury in alkaline cells. the amendments are fully in line with the existing eu legislation and i therefore supported the recommendation.
in writing. ‒ the convention on long-range transboundary air pollution aims to protect the human environment from air pollution. between 1972 and 1977, several studies showed that air pollutants travel thousands of miles before they settle. the convention, signed in 1979 and entered into force in 1983, was the first international instrument in this field to have binding legal force. the convention has been supplemented by eight protocols to date, which set out specific measures to be taken by the parties to reduce emissions of air pollutants. in particular, the amended protocol provides for stricter limits than before for emissions from significant localized sources and introduces transitional measures that favour parties joining the amended protocol before the end of 2019, including countries in eastern and south-eastern europe. i voted in favour of the document.
in writing. ‒ i think it is important to draw attention to the report, since the convention in question has been supplemented by eight protocols to date, which set out specific measures to be taken by the parties to reduce emissions of air pollutants. the first protocol to the convention was signed in 1984 and provided for a financing system for activities under the emep. the second protocol on sulphur emissions was the first major measure to reduce air pollution. the third, fourth and fifth protocols dealt with nitrogen oxides, volatile organic compounds and again sulphur emissions and their transboundary flows. the 1991 protocol on volatile organic compounds moved towards a more efficient group approach to the regulation of individual substances. this continued under the two 1998 protocols on heavy metals and persistent organic pollutants. the eighth protocol on action against acidification, eutrophication and ozone depletion is the first multi-pollutant, multi-effect protocol and contains specific national emission limit values and emission reduction commitments for different substances.
in writing. ‒ the purpose of the second aarhus protocol of 1998 supplementing the convention on long-range transboundary air pollution, referred to in paragraph 2, is to control, reduce or eliminate discharges, emissions and losses of persistent organic pollutants into the environment. the accession of the community to the protocol was approved by council decision 2004/259/ec of 19 february 2004. the protocol entered into force on 23 october 2003. the protocol was amended by four decisions of the parties in december 2012. among these, decision 2012/1, which includes seven new substances, updates the implementation requirements for a number of substances, updates the restrictions for dioxins/furans from multiple sources and extends the range of substances subject to annual emission limitations and reporting obligations to include polychlorinated biphenyls, is subject to ratification by the parties. the draft decision submitted by the council suggests that this should be done. the committee on the environment, public health and food safety, in its report, finds that the amendment is fully in line with the union legislation in force and therefore recommends that parliament add its consent to the draft decision. i voted accordingly.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the recommendation as the ratification of the amendments will be a significant step towards a higher level of protection of human health and the environment from transboundary air pollution and is fully in line with existing eu legislation. it is worth noting that between 1972 and 1977, several studies showed that air pollutants travel thousands of miles before they settle. therefore, the problems caused by air pollution must be addressed at international level. the convention, signed in 1979 and entered into force in 1983, was the first international legally binding instrument in this field, establishing a framework for monitoring and reducing harmful effects. the 1998 protocol also aims to control, reduce or eliminate the release, emissions and losses of persistent organic pollutants (pops). the latter requires parties to restrict the use of dichlorodiphenyltrichloroethane (ddt), hexachlorodiphenylcyclohexanes (hch) and polychlorinated biphenyls (pcbs) and to reduce their total annual emissions of polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (pahs), dioxins/furans (pcdd/pcdf) and hexachlorobenzene (hcb) compared to 1990 levels. i agree with the reasoning in the recommendation that the special exemptions for economies in transition and flexible transition schedules allow parties to comply with the protocol.

in writing. ‒ in the case of a member of the european parliament, immunity from liability applies not only to the views expressed by the member in official sessions of parliament but also to those expressed elsewhere, for example in the media, where there is a link between the views expressed and parliament's tasks. thus, when meps express their views on the foreign policy of the european union and third countries in public, it is within their mandate. for these reasons, it decides not to suspend the immunity of florian philippot.
in writing. ‒ the government of qatar has brought proceedings before the court of nanterre against florian philippot, member of the french european parliament, accusing him of slandering the aforementioned state in a radio broadcast of 9 january 2015 and a television broadcast of 19 january 2015, by suggesting that this state finances terrorism. on 2 september 2015, the minister of justice of the french republic sent a request to the european parliament to suspend the immunity of mr philippot in the context of the ongoing procedure. in its report, the committee on legal affairs states that both article 8 of protocol no 7 on the privileges and immunities of the european union and article 26 of the french constitution prohibit civil or criminal proceedings against a member for an opinion expressed in the performance of his duties and that it is within the competence of members of the european parliament to express publicly an opinion on the foreign policy of the european union and of third states. it also notes that the immunity of a member of the european parliament does not only apply to the opinions expressed by that member in official sessions of parliament, but also to those expressed elsewhere, for example in the media, in so far as there is a link between the opinions expressed and the tasks of parliament. in view of the above, it recommends that parliament not suspend florian philippot's immunity. i voted for the motion.

in writing. ‒ at the beginning of its current mandate, the european parliament committed itself to tackling one of the most disturbing and complex socioeconomic problems, undeclared work. the complexity of the challenge stems from the nature of the problem, namely that these are paid activities which are legal in nature but remain hidden from the relevant public authorities. this is a form of tax evasion that increases the size of the black economy, violates the principle of shared responsibility, and places a disproportionate burden on those doing honest, declared work and thus on taxpayers. implementation should be coupled with proactive policies and measures of an incentive nature aimed at regularising the remaining undeclared jobs. such measures may include income tax rebates, tax reductions and the introduction of support schemes. the fact that the practice of undeclared work in the member states is not decreasing shows that there is a demand for these jobs, as well as a supply. in a strong, work-based and wage-based society, which promotes national interests, undeclared work and its various forms cannot be tolerated. the ep's proposal will strengthen and make more effective the functioning of the platform on undeclared work, which is why i supported the adoption of the report.

in writing. ‒ the mid-term evaluation of the community-level biodiversity strategy highlights several points of interest and problems related to the implementation of the strategy and the achievement of its objectives. the rapporteur mentions that the objectives of the strategy should be achieved by the member states by 2020 at the latest, but that in many member states the integration of these objectives into the different national policies has not yet begun, let alone the actual objectives have been achieved. one of the greatest positives of the report is the criticism not only of the member states and the commission for inaction and inconsistency, but also of the strategy, which is criticized for its excessive expectations and objectives, and for its one-sidedness. it is important that the member states and, in particular, the commission should take greater account of the precautionary principle when authorising the production or marketing of various genetically modified organisms. however, there are parts of the report that would result in the removal of national competence in some sub-areas, for example, it would create a single eu-level environmental control system, which could also be a precursor to the introduction of a single eu-level environmental penalty. on balance, i found the report to be generally supportive.

in writing. ‒ the committee on the environment, public health and food safety has presented a report on the mid-term evaluation of the eu biodiversity strategy. the report concludes that biodiversity is a vital foundation for our health, well-being and economic prosperity, but it is also under serious pressure, both globally and in europe. however, european efforts to halt biodiversity loss failed in 2010, and the eu developed a new strategy in 2011 to halt biodiversity loss and the degradation of ecosystem services, restore them where possible by 2020, and help reverse biodiversity loss worldwide. the report concludes that without further significant efforts, the eu will again fail to meet its 2020 targets. a wealth of statistical data demonstrates that investing in nature and biodiversity is socially and economically necessary, and calls for stronger political will to effectively halt biodiversity loss. i voted for the report.

in writing. ‒ the proposed regulation allows for the temporary suspension of the preferences provided for in the eu-moldova association agreement in the event that a significant increase in imports from moldova would threaten to damage the eu's internal market. the adoption of the proposal is necessary in order to ensure the practical application of the so-called anti-circumvention procedure laid down in the association agreement.
in writing. ‒ the proposed regulation allows for the temporary suspension of the preferences provided for in the eu-moldova association agreement in the event that a significant increase in imports from moldova would threaten to damage the eu's internal market. the adoption of the proposal is necessary in order to ensure the practical application of the so-called anti-circumvention procedure laid down in the association agreement.
in writing. ‒ the association agreement with moldova , like most of our trade agreements, includes a bilateral safeguard clause. this instrument allows for the temporary suspension of trade preferences in case their application would result in an unexpected and significant increase of imports, causing significant economic damage to the domestic industry of the importing party (i.e. it is possible to either suspend further tariff liberalisation or re-establish the most favourable tariff rate). furthermore, that agreement contains a so-called anti-circumvention mechanism which provides for the possibility of reinstating the mfn in case imports of certain agricultural products originating in moldova exceed a certain threshold and do not provide adequate justification for their precise origin. i am convinced that a regulation of the european parliament and of the council is needed to introduce into eu internal law the instrument for the application of the bilateral safeguard clause and the anti-circumvention mechanism.
in writing. ‒ the proposed regulation allows for the temporary suspension of the preferences provided for in the eu-moldova association agreement in the event that a significant increase in imports from moldova would threaten or damage the eu's internal market. the adoption of the proposal is necessary to make the so-called anti-circumvention procedure laid down in the association agreement applicable in practice.
in writing. ‒ report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council implementing the anti-circumvention mechanism for the temporary suspension of safeguard clauses and tariff preferences contained in the association agreement between the european union and the european atomic energy community and their member states, of the one part, and the republic of moldova, of the other part. the proposed arrangements allow for the temporary suspension of the preferences provided for in the eu-moldova association agreement in the event that a significant increase in imports from moldova would threaten to damage the eu internal market. the adoption of the proposal is necessary in order to ensure the practical application of the so-called anti-circumvention procedure laid down in the association agreement.
in writing. ‒ the association agreement with moldova contains a bilateral safeguard clause which allows for the temporary suspension of trade preferences if their application would result in an unexpected and significant increase in imports, causing significant economic damage to the domestic industry of the importing party. the agreement also contains a so-called anti-circumvention mechanism, which allows the reintroduction of the mfn in cases where imports of certain agricultural products originating in moldova exceed a certain threshold and no justification is given for their precise origin. however, a regulation of the european parliament and of the council is needed to introduce the necessary instrument for the application of the bilateral safeguard clause and the anti-circumvention mechanism into eu internal law. the commission has proposed that this be done. the international trade committee report notes that the proposed regulation implements the provisions of the eu-moldova association agreement to which the european parliament gave its consent on 13 november 2014. acceptance of moldova is necessary to enforce its obligations under the agreement in order to protect union producers where appropriate. i voted for the motion.
in writing. ‒ the proposed regulation allows for the temporary suspension of the preferences provided for in the eu-moldova association agreement in the event that a significant increase in imports from moldova would threaten to damage the eu's internal market. the adoption of the proposal is necessary in order to ensure the practical application of the so-called anti-circumvention procedure laid down in the association agreement.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the adoption of the decision, given that the additional provisions contained therein are essential for the implementation of the association agreement and are essentially identical to the safeguard mechanisms used in trade agreements with other eu partners. the trade policy safeguards and measures to prevent circumvention are also appropriate to ensure that the benefits granted to moldova are not exploited by other third parties. i also considered the fact that moldova is a preferential trading partner of the eu, but that a significant part of its exports is agricultural products and that any conflict of interest of eu producers due to the association agreement should be avoided.

in writing. ‒ the association agreement with moldova , like most of our trade agreements, includes a bilateral safeguard clause. this instrument allows for the temporary suspension of trade preferences in cases where their application would result in an unexpected and significant increase of imports, causing significant economic damage to the domestic industry of the importing party. the adoption of the proposed regulation is necessary in order to enforce the obligations of the moldova agreement and to protect union producers where appropriate. i voted in favor of the motion.
in writing. ‒ the eu-georgia association agreement contains a so-called anti-circumvention procedure which allows the re-introduction of duties applicable to the most favoured nation if imports of certain agricultural products from georgia exceed the threshold set in the agreement without adequate justification. this regulation is necessary in order to incorporate it into the internal legal framework of the eu in a proper manner and thus to make the anti-circumvention procedure applicable.

in writing. ‒ i would like to stress that the proposed regulation implements the relevant provisions of the eu-georgia association agreement approved by the european parliament on 18 december 2015. the adoption of the proposed regulation is necessary in order to enforce the obligations of georgia under the provisions of the agreement on the anti-circumvention mechanism, thereby protecting european producers where necessary. i also welcome the commission's reporting obligation in the proposal, whereby the commission will submit an annual report to the co-legislators on the application and implementation of the regulation, which will then be made public. the european parliament may invite the commission to an ad hoc meeting of its competent committee to present and explain any question arising in connection with the implementation of the agreement. the report also calls for the eu to take action to ensure that the eu's trade policy is properly implemented. in the light of the above considerations, i propose, in agreement with the rapporteur, that the european parliament adopt the commission proposal without amendments.

in writing. ‒ the draft resolution, on the basis of a petition 924/2011 from the peti committee, urges the member states that are blocking minorities in the european council to stop obstructing the ratification process of the marrakesh treaty (marrakesh treaty to facilitate access to published works by visually impaired persons and persons with print disabilities) by the european union. despite the fact that the treaty was adopted in june 2013, the european union has not yet ratified it, mainly due to disputes between the european commission and the council (e.g. competence and certain implementation-procedural issues). however, the draft decision is outdated due to the formal communication of the luxembourg presidency, as, on the one hand, the european commission applied to the court of justice of the european union on 14 july 2015 to provide guidance on the scope and nature of the treaty. the european commission also promised in october 2015 to present a concrete legislative proposal to settle the disputed issues, which is of a guaranteeing nature for the subsequent proper implementation of the convention. from this moment on, we are faced with a legal question, not a political one, which must be resolved before ratification can take place. in view of all this, i have now abstained from the vote, continuing to support a swift, effective ratification, guaranteeing a clear implementation.

in writing. ‒ the marrakesh treaty on the facilitation of access to published works for the blind, visually impaired and print-disabled was adopted on 27 june 2013. the treaty was signed by the union and its member states in april 2014, giving a political commitment to ratify it. however, seven eu member states have formed a minority group that is hampering the process of ratifying the treaty, despite the fact that according to a 2010 estimate by the world health organisation, there are some 26 350 000 visually impaired people in europe, on whose behalf numerous petitions have been filed to gain access to books and other printed products. the report of the committee on petitions recommends that the european parliament should express its deep indignation in a resolution and call on the council and the member states to speed up the ratification process, without tying it to a review of the eu legal framework or a ruling by the court of justice of the european union. i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution.

in writing. ‒ the world health organisation estimated in 2010 that there were 2 550 000 blind and 23 800 000 visually impaired people in europe, giving a total of 26 350 000 visually impaired people. the so-called marrakesh treaty, signed by the union and the member states in april 2014, aims to facilitate access to published works for blind and visually impaired persons and persons who are unable to read printed text. they have committed to ratify it. i voted in favor of the motion.
in writing. ‒ the genetically modified soybean fg72 produces 2mepsps and hppd w336 proteins, which make it resistant to the herbicides isoxaflutole and glyphosate. the risk assessment carried out revealed several deficiencies, including: • in the field trials, the fg72 soybean control was not an isogenic line but a selected unmodified conventional line; • the genetically modified fg72 soybean differed significantly from the control in terms of its content of components, phenotypic and agronomic characteristics. however, efsa did not consider any of the significant differences to be such as to require further studies, as they were not biologically relevant. the use of plant protection products containing such active substances may be increased during cultivation, which may subsequently increase the residues in the crop. in 2015, the who classified glyphosate as a 'probable human carcinogen'. high doses also increase the incidence of resistant yeast populations. in my view, gm products should not be authorised in the european union unless they have been subject to adequate health and environmental safety checks. scientific studies to identify risks are inadequate, therefore, in accordance with the hungarian basic law and the precautionary principle, i do not support the authorisation of gm products.

in writing. ‒ on the basis of the draft commission implementing decision on the authorisation of the placing on the market of products containing, consisting of, or produced from genetically modified soybean pursuant to regulation (ec) no 1829/2003 of the european parliament and of the council, i consider that the commission implementing decision is not in accordance with union law as it is incompatible with the objective of regulation (ec) no 1829/2003 and regulation (ec) no 396/2005 of the european parliament and of the council, which, in accordance with the general principles laid down in regulation (ec) no 178/2002 of the european parliament and of the council, is to provide a basis for a high level of protection of human life and health, animal health and welfare, the environment and consumer interests with regard to genetically modified food and feed, while ensuring the effective functioning of the internal market. in the light of the above, i call on the commission to withdraw its draft implementing decision.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution on the placing on the market of products containing, consisting of, or produced from genetically modified fg72 soybean. the background to the opinion is that on 24 june 2011 bayer cropscience submitted a marketing authorisation application to the competent belgian authority. that soybean expresses the protein 2mepsps, which confers resistance to glyphosate-containing herbicides, and the protein hppd w336, which confers resistance to herbicides containing the active substance isoxaflutol. the who international agency for research on cancer classified glyphosate as a probable human carcinogen in 2015. since the entry into force of regulation (ec) no 1829/2003, authorisation decisions have been adopted by the commission without the opinions of the member state committees and it has become common practice for gm food and feed to have a specific exceptional decision-making procedure where the dossier is returned to the commission for final approval. i agree that even if production necessarily takes place in the territory of a member state, trade in gmos is cross-border, which means that the national 'sale and use' ban proposed by the commission could not be enforced in the single internal market. that is why i supported the withdrawal of the implementing regulation and the commission's presentation of a new legislative proposal, taking into account the concerns often expressed by member states that are not only related to the health or environmental risks posed by gmos.
in writing. ‒ bayer cropscience ag has submitted an application to the competent authority of belgium for the placing on the market of foods, food ingredients, and feed containing, consisting of, or produced from fg72 soybean. as described in the application, the genetically modified soybean mst-fgø72-2 expresses the protein 2mepsps, which confers resistance to glyphosate-containing herbicides, and the protein hppd w336, which confers resistance to the herbicides containing the active substance isoxaflutol. the rapporteur requests the commission to withdraw its draft implementing decision in this case. i voted in favour of the s&d group's position on this issue.
in writing. ‒ single modified soybean sheets of mon 87708 (dicamba produces monooxygenase protein) and mon 89788 (cp4 produces epsps protein) have been combined to create the double modified genetically modified soybean mon 87708 x mon 89788. this made the soybean resistant to the herbicides dicamba and glyphosate. the use of dicamba and glyphosate-based herbicides during cultivation may be increased, which may subsequently increase the residual levels of the crop. their widespread use also increases the emergence of a resistant gypsy population. the risk assessment carried out revealed several deficiencies, including: • no 90-day rat feeding study has been conducted with the product;• no repeat dose study has been conducted with cp4 epsps protein. the amount of formaldehyde produced in gm soybeans is not a purely natural process, as the neutralization of the active substance dicamba is also accompanied by the formation of formaldehyde. this substance is classified as a human carcinogen. new research suggests that formaldehyde may accumulate in herbicide-tolerant gm plants due to a disruption in the metabolism of detoxifying enzymes. in my view, gm products should not be authorised in the european union unless they have been subject to adequate health and environmental safety checks. scientific studies to identify risks are inadequate, therefore, in accordance with the hungarian basic law and the precautionary principle, i do not support the authorisation of gm products.

in writing. ‒ regulation (ec) no 1829/2003 of the european parliament and of the council of 22 september 2003 on genetically modified food and feed lays down the procedure for authorising the placing on the market of such products. on 23 march 2012, monsanto europe s.a. submitted to the competent authority of the netherlands an application to place on the market foods, food ingredients and feed containing, consisting of, or produced from mon 87708 × mon 89788 soybean. the commission adopted a draft commission implementing decision on the authorisation under that regulation. in its report, the committee on the environment, public health and food safety referred to parliament's resolution of 16 december 2015 on commission implementing decision (eu) 2015/2279 of 4 december 2015 authorising the placing on the market of products containing, consisting of, or produced from genetically modified maize nk603 × t25 recommends that parliament express its opinion that genetically modified organisms are inherently harmful to human health. i am convinced that it is not for politicians but for scientists to decide on the impact of gm foods on human health, and i therefore abstained from voting on the resolution.
in writing. ‒ in my view, gm products should not be authorised in the european union unless they have been thoroughly tested for health and environmental safety. scientific studies to identify risks are inadequate, therefore, in accordance with the hungarian basic law and the precautionary principle, i do not support the authorisation of gm products.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution on the placing on the market of products containing, consisting of, or produced from genetically modified soybean mon 87708 x mon 89788. on 23 march 2012, monsanto europe s.a. submitted a marketing authorisation application to the competent authority of the netherlands. the genetically modified soybean expresses the proteins dicamba monooxygenase, which confers tolerance to dicamba-containing herbicides, and the cp 4 epsps protein, which confers tolerance to glyphosate-containing herbicides. the who international agency for research on cancer classified glyphosate as a probable human carcinogen in 2015. since the entry into force of regulation (ec) no 1829/2003, authorisation decisions have been adopted by the commission without the opinions of the member state committees and it has become common practice for gm food and feed to be returned to the commission for final approval. i agree that even if production necessarily takes place in one member state, trade in gmos crosses borders. the commission's proposed ban on national 'sales and use' could therefore not be enforced in the single internal market. i supported the withdrawal of the regulation and the commission's presentation of a new legislative proposal that would provide a basis for a high level of protection of human and animal health, the environment and consumer interests in relation to genetically modified food and feed, while ensuring the effective functioning of the internal market.
in writing. ‒ monsanto europe s.a. has submitted an application to the competent authority of the netherlands for the placing on the market of foods, food ingredients, and feed containing, consisting of, or produced from mon 87708 × mon 89788 soybean. i voted in favour of the s&d group's position on this issue.
in writing. ‒ mon 87705 and mon 89788 single-modified soybean sheets have been combined to create the genetically modified soybean mon 87705 x mon 89788 with double modifications. this has made soybeans resistant to herbicides containing the active substance glyphosate and has a different fatty acid profile. despite the fact that the active substance referred to above is not considered to be of emerging toxicity, there are numerous data in the scientific literature on its adverse effects on human and animal health. the risk assessment carried out revealed several deficiencies, including: • the genetically modified soybean mon 87705 x mon 89788 differed significantly from the control in terms of its content of constituents (excluding altered fatty acid profile), phenotypic and agronomic characteristics. however, efsa did not consider any of the significant differences to be such as to require further studies, as they were not biologically relevant. • in vivo feeding studies were replaced by an in vitro digestion test, which is not always suitable to replace the feeding experiment. in my view, gm products should not be authorised in the european union unless they have been subject to adequate health and environmental safety checks. scientific studies to identify risks are inadequate, therefore, in accordance with the hungarian basic law and the precautionary principle, i do not support the authorisation of gm products.

despite the positive changes that have taken place in recent decades, the level of air pollution is a matter of concern. the number of premature deaths could be as high as 400,000. the commission has also received comments from interested parties on the measures taken by the goc to address the concerns raised by the commission in the opening decision. the volkswagen scandal has demonstrated the need for real-world testing. the commission implementing regulation is not appropriate to achieve the environmental objective pursued. the adoption of the proposal has resulted in the possibility of exceeding the required target emissions by up to twice by 2020. for all these reasons, i supported a parliament resolution rejecting the european commission's proposal.
in writing. ‒ the european union has been working for years to find a solution to the problem that vehicle emissions are much higher in real driving conditions than in laboratory testing. the painful truth is that according to the latest calculations by the european commission, the emissions of euro 6 diesel engines currently produced on the road exceed the test bench results by an average of 400%! the european commission's draft implementing regulation is an important part of the solution to the problem, which aims to reduce emissions as quickly as possible in real terms. the commission notes that the commission has not provided any evidence that the exemption from the requirement of a minimum speed limit is justified by the fact that the maximum speed limit is set at a lower speed than the maximum speed limit. in reality, the regulation represents a major step forward. the commission considers that the aid is compatible with the internal market if it is granted in accordance with the rules on state aid. the new limits, however, provide for real emission reductions, significantly reducing the health and environmental risks. in my view, the draft law strikes the right balance between environmental and public health objectives and the preservation of domestic jobs and the competitiveness of industry. i am convinced that a responsible decision-maker does not make rules based on wishful thinking. it would be irresponsible to insist on something that has been proven technically impossible over time. we can't fool anyone by accepting unrealistic rules.

in writing. ‒ i consider the objection to and the vote on the new rules on diesel car emissions to be an important agenda item. the draft new rules, in addition to introducing what i consider to be a good real-world emission test (rde), will increase the 2007 limit for nitrogen oxides from diesel cars by up to 110%. this package was approved by the eu member states by the decision of the technical committee on motor vehicles of 28 october, in which the european commission proposed to increase the nox emission limit for motor vehicles by 110% for new models from september 2017 and for all new motor vehicles from september 2019. i voted in favour of the objection to the draft decision. in my opinion, the majority's failure to support the objection is a step backwards and not right. i think it is important to note that the european parliament's environment committee has already decided that parliament should veto the relaxation of the limit values because it undermines compliance with existing eu standards. i am sure that, in addition to the negative environmental and health aspects of the issue, it raises other technical problems which i will take into account in my work on the diesel scandal committee.
in writing. ‒ air pollution causes more than 430 000 premature deaths in the union each year, and the estimated cost of its health effects is €940 billion per year. as nitrogen oxides (nox) are among the main pollutants, they cause lung cancer, asthma and many respiratory diseases, among others, and are also responsible for cases of environmental damage. the draft measure requires manufacturers to ensure that emissions during the real driving test at type-approval and throughout the life cycle of the vehicle do not exceed certain 'non-exhaustible (nte) emission limits'. i voted in favor of the motion.
the report concerns a multilateral agreement on international trade in services. this agreement threatens eu standards and jobs for services, public services for eu citizens and the right of member states to regulate. so i rejected this new step towards globalization. the task of the union's leadership is not to open up new markets to multinational companies, partly at the expense of developing countries and partly at the expense of weaker eu member states, but to protect the citizens and jobs of the union and to help developing countries to produce their own needs and services and not to alienate europe. that's why i turned down the offer.

in writing. ‒ the european parliament plays a key role in the union's trade policy. not only do representatives have the final say on trade agreements, but they should also be promptly and fully informed at all stages of the negotiation and conclusion of trade agreements in order to be able to monitor trade negotiations on an ongoing basis. in order to shape the course of the negotiations, parliament may express its position at any time during the negotiation process. the report by the committee on international trade assesses the first two and a half years and 13 rounds of negotiations on a trade in services agreement (tisa) and recommends that parliament make clear and firm recommendations to the european commission. it suggests that parliament should take the view that the tisa negotiations should ensure increased reciprocity in market access, a level playing field at global level, tangible benefits for consumers and access to negotiations for stakeholders in order to facilitate the future multilateral framework. it also proposes that public and cultural services, fundamental rights to data protection and fair working conditions, and the right to regulate should not be negotiated and should be clearly excluded from the scope of the agreement. i supported the motion.

in writing. ‒ four draft resolutions have been tabled on a new european strategy on women's rights and gender equality for the period after 2015: the proposal of the efdd, the epp and the ecr groups, and the joint proposal of the s&d, alde, gue/ngl and verts/ale groups. i voted for the latter.
in writing. ‒ gender equality is one of the fundamental values of the european union. this is important not only for the role of women in the economy and society, but also for the eu's broader economic objectives. on the other hand, we see that even the objectives of the 2010-15 strategy have not been met, that political momentum has slowed down over the last decade and that the commission is reluctant to adopt a document for the next period. all this while discrimination against women is at the governmental level in hungary, the average hourly gender pay gap in some member states is as high as 25-30%, and 16 member states are inexplicably reluctant to ratify the istanbul convention on violence against women, including hungary, but also germany. how can we credibly promote gender equality in our development policy in third countries when we have so much to do in our own member states? it is clear that further efforts are needed to establish a coherent legal framework. it is unacceptable that when both the european parliament and the council, as representatives of the member states, are urging a specific strategy to continue the programme which expires in 2015, all with the overwhelming agreement of european citizens, the european commission is not fulfilling its duty and is not adopting a specific document. we need concrete commitments with directions and a budget for that. without them, there's no way to measure progress and there's no way to move forward.
in writing. ‒ i supported the resolution on the new strategy on women's rights and gender equality for the period after 2015. i believe that the pursuit of gender balance is an important objective. gender equality is one of the eu's fundamental values, recognised in the treaties and in the charter of fundamental rights of the european union. the european union is committed to mainstreaming this objective in all its activities, as gender equality is a strategic objective and a key element in achieving the 2020 pan-european targets for growth, employment and social inclusion. the commission's 2016 work programme, published in november 2015, does not specifically mention the eu strategy on gender equality for the period after 2015, and i share the view of the resolution that it is regrettable. the european commission has published only one commission staff working document entitled 'a strategic engagement for gender equality (2016-2019) '. in doing so, it not only submitted a classified internal document, but also limited the duration of the intervention.
in writing. ‒ gender equality is one of the eu's core values recognised in the treaties and in the charter of fundamental rights of the european union, which the eu has committed to mainstreaming in all its activities, and whereas gender equality as a strategic objective is essential to achieve the pan-european targets for growth, employment and social inclusion by 2020. whereas the right to equal treatment is a fundamental right recognised in the treaties establishing the european union and deeply rooted in european society, indispensable for the further development of that society, and whereas that right must be guaranteed in legislation, practice, case-law and everyday life; i voted in favour of the s&d group's position.

in writing. the european structural and investment funds were set up to achieve sustainability and growth, which promote economic, social and cohesive development. as we know, the economic and social conditions are in place to contribute to these funds and make them more accessible to the member states. in addition to the linking of the european structural and investment funds and the european fund for strategic investments, the issue of giving local and regional authorities a greater role in the management of the funds is also important. in the past, particularly for smaller organisations or companies, excessive controls and red tape have caused additional costs and time constraints. therefore, this amendment could have the advantage of a more rational allocation of resources, in addition to simplifying accessibility, thus increasing the motivation of users. if local and regional authorities can manage the funds more directly, the conditions can be more flexible and more specific, in line with the specific territorial and other circumstances.

madam secretary, mr. president, i have to go. the danube and adriatic macro-regions are important mechanisms for achieving synergies in these regions. this is particularly important in the field of transport, including rail transport. these macro-regions are crossed by very important ten-t routes, but the existing transport networks are fragmented and mostly concentrated in one country or region. expansion of cross-border railway lines, better coordination of timetables and modernisation of equipment would be necessary. the system of macro-regions can be of great help in this. however, it is important to note that these macro-regions also include countries that are not yet full eu members. the ten-t network has expanded beyond the eu member states to include the candidate countries, thanks to the negotiations in vienna last summer. this has finally resulted in a map of europe covering the entire continent. this could also improve the competitiveness of the danube and adriatic macro-region and reduce its isolation from the rest of europe. however, in order to achieve positive logistical and economic effects on transport throughout the entire length of the corridors and to create the so-called corridor effect, it is necessary to rethink the funding mechanisms provided by the eu. the different legal and financial status of the candidate countries means that the synergy between the macro-regions cannot be fully exploited and that, despite all goodwill, the bottlenecks remain. i would therefore urge the commission to create the right legal and financial backdrop for better integration of the candidate countries in the ten-t corridor review. we in the european people's party want to help the commission to formulate solutions that are realistic, that are in line with the possibilities, but that allow for further development.

in writing. the adriatic-danube macro-region is a major european transit route, so the development of environmentally friendly transport routes is of prime interest, but particular attention should be paid to ensuring that this objective does not overshadow the nature conservation aspects, which are also a priority. the danube, which is the region's water feature and also its ecological conditions as a green corridor and aquatic habitat, is traditionally the region's most important shipping route. at the same time, the development of shipping poses a serious threat, as it threatens to destroy the most valuable ecosystems: the closure of estuaries, the construction of dams, dredging, navigation aids and protective structures, among others, are the main threats to the river's aquatic habitats, according to a report by the european court of auditors. moreover, since the implementation of the danube strategy, the development of the transport corridor is typically supported by eu funding there is a strong possibility that the destruction of irreplaceable natural resources is financed unintentionally by the eu itself. experience so far has shown that the natura 2000 network of sites, the birds and habitats directives have proved to be effective tools for conserving biodiversity and protecting habitats. i believe it is very important to coordinate european objectives, in this case to prevent development from being achieved through habitat erosion. in the context of environmentally friendly shipping development, ships should be adapted to the river and not the other way around: the danube should remain a living water, not a canal.
