in writing. the free choice of employment within the union is one of the four fundamental freedoms of the european union. every day, some 1.1 million eu citizens cross the border to work in a neighbouring country. in addition, in 2013, some 7 million european citizens lived and worked in other member states. the high unemployment rates in some regions of europe have led to the recognition of the need to strengthen labour mobility within the union. this will contribute to the development of a european labour market with a high level of employment, as the rate of labour mobility within the union of 0,29% is relatively low in relation to the size of the labour market and the active population of the eu. this regulation aims to make the eures network an effective tool for jobseekers/employers by creating the largest database of job vacancies and jobseeker profiles. i support the inclusion of apprenticeships and traineeships in the europe-wide network. i propose to introduce an appropriate exchange of general information on mobility within the union in the field of apprenticeships and traineeships, which should be recognised in the same way as diplomas awarded by the member states' mainstream education systems. the reform should enable public employment services to lay the foundations for closer cooperation with education and training institutions, in particular in the field of continuing training, extending this to those over 40 years of age, allowing the use of information and communication technologies.
in writing. the eures network and employment mobility portal, which is now more than two decades old, has become even more important in the light of the crisis, as mobility within the union opens up new employment opportunities and can thus contribute to reducing unemployment. the problem of mass unemployment in some parts of the union can be solved by the mobility of workers. eures supports workers and employers in exploiting the opportunities offered by the principle of free movement of persons. eures and the public employment services in the member states consider it their mission to contribute to the balance of supply and demand in the labour market and to provide employers, workers and recruitment agencies with easy access to the local, national and european labour markets. the report also mentions several points aimed at increasing the effectiveness of eures, while stressing that employment policies are a matter for the member states. most of the proposals mentioned in the presentation (e.g. to extend eures to include traineeship opportunities, to provide all jobseekers with full information on employment conditions in the country where the job is located, to make the eures platform as user-friendly as possible) contain valuable ideas that can effectively contribute to reducing unemployment in the union.
in writing. i consider the right to free choice of employment within the union to be an integral part of the right to free movement, one of the four fundamental freedoms of the european union, which is an important element of eu citizenship, which has been put at risk by the current migrant crisis. today, there are 23 million unemployed in the eu, and one in five young people is out of work. despite rumours to the contrary, the mobility of eu workers within the union is low compared to the size of the labour market and the active population of the eu, and even compared to its larger competitors (the usa, japan) the eu-27 mobility rate is only 0.29%. the regulation aims to make the eures network an effective tool for jobseekers and employers, while respecting the competences of the member states in respect of labour market regulation, which remains a national competence. my view is that the employment problem should not be reduced by adding more non-eu and particularly unskilled immigrants, but by strengthening the free movement of eu citizens. in this context, i believe that, as regards the filling of vacant posts, the member states and the commission should ensure that priority is given to nationals of the member states of the union in order to ensure that the principle of union preference is also applied.
in writing. the proposal for a regulation on the table in parliament aims to improve workers' access to services to support labour mobility within the eu, thereby promoting equitable mobility and ensuring better access to employment opportunities across the union. the main tool for this is the european employment services (eures) network of some 900 counsellors. however, it is clear that this instrument in its current form is not able to encourage further equitable mobility patterns, in particular due to the size of the union workforce and the nature of the challenges of the current economic situation. the proposal provides an answer to this, but it must also be noted that, in addition to encouraging labour mobility, we must also provide support for those who have left their country of origin for economic reasons and are engaged in work which is sometimes underpaid and unfair in relation to their qualifications. if there is an eu resource to facilitate the mobility of european citizens, there must also be a way to help those who want to get back to thriving in their home countries.

in writing. ‒ the hague convention of 15 november 1965 established a system of document service between the signatory countries. it is important to note that the convention is a cross-border service which only applies to documents coming from or going to third countries. twenty-six of the 28 member states have already applied the convention and the two remaining member states, malta and austria, have also expressed their wish to join. since the convention has proved useful, it is in the common interest that the two member states in question should have a simple procedure for the cross-border service of documents in third countries. in the plenary vote, i voted in favour of the accession of the two member states to the hague convention.
in writing. the hague convention of 15 november 1965 established a system whereby official documents may be served in another state party. it should be noted that the convention applies only to the cross-border service of official documents originating in or sent to third countries: regulation (ec) no 1393/2007 of the european parliament and of the council of 13 november 2007 on the service of judicial and extrajudicial documents in civil or commercial matters applies to the cross-border service of official documents within the european union. the convention has already been applied by 26 of the 28 member states. the remaining two member states, austria and malta, also indicated their intention to join. the convention does not allow for the accession of international organisations. however, following the adoption of union legislation on the cross-border service of documents, the union acquired exclusive external competence in this matter under article 3 (2) tfeu. this approach was confirmed by the court in its opinion of 1/13. on that basis, the union should authorise those member states to act on its behalf with a view to acceding to the convention. it is in the interest of both the union as a whole and the two member states in question to have a uniform system for the uniform service of documents in their cross-border relations with third countries.

in writing. ‒ the agreement represents an important step in efforts to combat tax fraud and tax evasion and updates the 2004 agreement which ensures that the republic of san marino applies measures equivalent to the eu directive on taxation of interest income on savings. the new agreement establishes an automatic exchange of information between the eu and the republic of san marino on the financial accounts of each other's residents as from 2017. the aim is to address situations where taxable persons seek to conceal income or capital representing assets for which tax has not yet been paid. i support the objective of the agreement to apply enhanced measures equivalent to the union legal framework updated in december 2014 (amending the dac2 directive on administrative cooperation) and to comply with the automatic exchange of financial account information procedures called for by the 2014 oecd global standards.

in writing. ‒ with today’s vote we gave our consent to the commission recommendation to the council to allow croatia to adhere to the convention on the protection of the european communities’ financial interests. the act of 2011 concerning the conditions of accession of croatia to the european union simplified its accession to the conventions and protocols concluded by the member states: it is no longer necessary to negotiate and conclude specific accession protocols. the council, in order to take a decision determining the date on which this convention will enter into force in relation to croatia and making all the adjustments required by reason of the accession of this new member state to this convention, will act on a recommendation by the commission, after consulting the european parliament. the libe committee recommended that the european parliament give its consent to the commission recommendation. as fidesz-epp we therefore voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ annex i to the act of accession lists the conventions and protocols concerned. that list includes the convention of 26 july 1995 on the protection of the european communities' financial interests, the protocols of 27 september 1996 and 29 november 1996 and the second protocol of 19 june 1997 adopted for the purpose of establishing a common fund for the criminal law protection of the ec's financial interests under title vi of the ec treaty. the convention and its protocols of 27 september 1996 and 29 november 1996 entered into force on 17 october 2002 following ratification by the then 15 member states, the protocol of 19 june 1997 entered into force on 19 may 2009 following ratification by the then 27 member states. in order to make the adjustments required by the accession of croatia to the abovementioned convention and its protocols in accordance with article 3 (5) of the act of accession, a commission recommendation is not necessary. the commission proposes that the council adopt a decision fixing the date of entry into force of these conventions for croatia. i therefore propose, in agreement with the rapporteur, that the commission's recommendation be adopted.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the people's party because i consider the free choice of work within the union to be an integral part of the right to free movement, one of the four fundamental freedoms of the european union, which is an important element of eu citizenship, which has been put at risk by the current migrant crisis. today, there are 23 million unemployed in the eu, and nearly one in five young people are out of work. despite rumours to the contrary, the mobility of eu workers within the union is low compared to the size of the labour market and the active population of the eu, and even compared to its larger competitors (the usa, japan) the eu-27 mobility rate is only 0.29%. the regulation aims to make the eures network an effective tool for jobseekers and employers, while respecting the competences of the member states in respect of labour market regulation, which remained a national competence. my view is that the employment problem must be reduced not by adding more non-eu and specifically unskilled immigrants, but by strengthening the free movement of eu citizens. in this context, i believe that, as regards the filling of vacant posts, the member states and the commission should ensure that priority is given to nationals of the member states of the union in order to ensure that the principle of union preference is also applied.
in writing. ‒ the european commission has proposed a regulation to the parliament and the council to strengthen labour mobility within the union in order to improve the employment prospects of workers and to help employers to fill vacancies better and faster. it proposes to create the largest database of job vacancies and jobseeker profiles available to anyone at eu level. in order to make eures an effective tool for jobseekers and employers, the report of the employment and social affairs committee considers it important that the public and private employment services of the member states, which are well-functioning, participate in the network and that the network is made known throughout europe through communication measures by the commission and the member states. it also stresses that member states and the commission should ensure that priority is given to eu nationals when filling vacancies. the report also proposes that parliament adopt the proposal, albeit with more than 150 amendments. i voted in accordance with that.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on further integration of labour markets, as i believe that any instrument that strengthens the labour market contributes to a stronger european union. i believe that there is a significant advantage in effectively linking the public and private sector job vacancies in the member states. however, i should note that the willingness of workers to move is not uniform across the union, and in many cases there is also a lack of mobility and labour shortages, depending on the region and the season. i think it is a matter of concern that social benefits and working conditions differ in the various member states. so i think that the new eures instrument can be useful, but it is not enough on its own. regional information is needed, incentives for employment and services. all this is done so that all information is available simultaneously in all 24 languages. i believe that the concessions made to prevent the 'brexit' now being outlined could seriously jeopardise this important endeavour. requests for concessions may also arise in other member states, but in this case the interconnection of the system may have a dubious effect.
in writing. ‒ the purpose of this proposal for a regulation is to improve workers' access to services supporting labour mobility within the eu, thereby promoting equitable mobility and ensuring better access to employment opportunities throughout the union. the general objective of the proposal is to make the eures network an effective tool for all jobseekers and employers interested in the mobility of workers within the eu. i voted in favor of the motion.
in writing. ‒ the european commission proposes to open a temporary unilateral tariff quota of 35 000 tonnes per year for tunisian olive oil exports to the eu. this concession would be granted by the union to tunisia until december 2017. the mediterranean countries are the eu's main olive oil producers. these countries have also been severely affected by the crisis. unemployment is high, above the eu average in all four countries. (portugal, spain, italy, greece the former two have unemployment rates above 10% and the latter two above 20%). solidarity with tunisia is a positive thing in itself, but it would be more justified in this case to be concerned about our own industry, our own economy. the rapporteur also acknowledges this in his explanatory statement for the draft:however, he reiterates that eu solidarity is at the expense of farmers in southern europe, in this case olive oil producers. the eu is a world leader in the olive oil sector, whose production is the main economic and social driver of the production areas. in particular, in the large areas of the eu countries that have been severely affected by the economic crisis, the olive oil sector provides thousands of jobs and its significant share of exports to third countries contributes to the eu's positive trade balance. other all in all, i was not in favour of the motion being passed.
in writing. ‒ the terrorist attacks in tunis on 18 march 2015 and in sousse on 26 june 2015 have dealt a severe blow to an already struggling tunisian economy. in this difficult situation, the european union wishes to emphasise that it will continue to actively support tunisia, in particular its economic development. in this context, the commission proposes to open a temporary unilateral duty-free tariff quota of 35 000 tonnes per year for the export of olive oil from tunisia to the union for a total of 70 000 tonnes per year in the form of autonomous trade measures without increasing the total import volume. the tariff quota in question will be available for a period of two years from 1 january 2016 to 31 december 2017 and will become available after the exhaustion of the duty-free tariff quota of 56 700 tonnes currently in force, as set out in the association agreement between the union and tunisia. however, if the new quota is detrimental to the commercial interests of the member states or has a negative impact on the internal market, the union shall be entitled to take the necessary steps to eliminate it.

in writing. ‒ i believe it is important to show solidarity with tunisia and to use our existing instruments to help stabilise the economy and democratic political system of the north african country. international terrorism poses a serious threat to the country and discourages tourists, without whom tunisia's economy could collapse. let us consider the aftermath of the terrible attack in sousse last year. therefore, the trade preference granted to assist the tunisian olive oil producers is to some extent justified. but we must show at least as much solidarity with european union producers. the exemption granted by the commission for an additional 35 000 tonnes of olive oil must not be allowed to become a routine measure. therefore, in the vote, i considered it a particular point to omit the clause on the extension of the duty-free period from the report.

in writing. ‒ in the wake of the terrorist attack in sousse on 26 june 2015, the eu has seen the need to provide further assistance to tunisia in its political and economic transformation through concrete and targeted actions that can deliver results in the short term. on the basis of the above, the european commission proposes to open a temporary unilateral duty-free tariff quota of 35 000 tonnes per year in the form of autonomous trade measures for exports of olive oil from tunisia to the union. the tariff quota in question will be available for a period of two years from 1 january 2016 to 31 december 2017. this additional quantity will be available after the exhaustion of the duty-free tariff quota of 56 700 tonnes currently in force and fixed in the agreement. i agree with the rapporteur that it is necessary for the european union to contribute to the recovery of the economy of this country in this undoubtedly difficult period. however, it is important to note that the union's solidarity is at the expense of farmers in southern europe, in this case olive oil producers. the eu is a world leader in the olive oil sector, whose production is the main economic and social driver of the production areas. in particular, in the large areas of the eu countries that have been severely affected by the economic crisis, the olive oil sector provides thousands of jobs and its significant share of exports to third countries contributes to the eu's positive trade balance.
in writing. ‒ the terrorist attacks in tunis on 18 march 2015 and in sousse on 26 june 2015 have dealt a severe blow to an already struggling tunisian economy. in this difficult situation, the european union wishes to emphasise that it will continue to actively support tunisia's economic development. therefore, the commission proposes to open a temporary unilateral duty-free tariff quota of 35 000 tonnes per year for a total of 70 000 tonnes for exports of olive oil from tunisia to the union in the form of autonomous trade measures without increasing the total import volume. the tariff quota in question will be available for a period of two years from 1 january 2016 to 31 december 2017 and will become available after the exhaustion of the duty-free tariff quota of 56 700 tonnes currently in force, as set out in the association agreement between the union and tunisia. however, if the new quota is detrimental to the commercial interests of the member states or has a negative impact on the internal market, the union shall be entitled to take the necessary steps to eliminate it.

in writing. ‒ the commission has proposed the adoption of a regulation of the parliament and of the council to support the tunisian economy, which is experiencing serious difficulties, and at the same time the democratization process in tunisia which is under way. to this end, it proposes to open a temporary unilateral tariff quota for tunisia for duty-free exports of 35 000 tonnes per year for a period of two years, for a total of 70 000 tonnes of olive oil, without increasing the total import volume. given that olive oil is tunisia's main agricultural export product to the union and that the tunisian olive oil sector indirectly employs more than one million people, representing one fifth of the total number of people employed in tunisian agriculture, the measure constitutes a major aid to tunisia. in its report, the committee on international trade recommends that parliament should support the adoption of the regulation with a few amendments. i voted in accordance with that.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution because i believe it is important for the european parliament to speak out on one of the most serious humanitarian disasters of our time and to use its international clout vis-à-vis saudi arabia and other parties to the conflict to improve the situation. i consider it urgent that the maritime blockade be lifted and that hostilities cease throughout yemen in order to allow humanitarian aid to reach its destination without hindrance. the situation is particularly worrying because of the high number of children among the victims and the serious threats to the safety of international aid workers. while agreeing that international efforts to resolve the situation in yemen should be pursued under the auspices of the un, i also took into account the fact that this issue also raises the specific responsibility of eu member states, in particular with regard to compliance and enforcement of the rules on restricting the supply of arms to the region. i believe that this aspect will have to be closely monitored by the european parliament in the future.
in writing. ‒ the terrorist attacks in tunis on 18 march 2015 and in sousse on 26 june 2015 have dealt a severe blow to an already struggling tunisian economy. in this difficult situation, the european union wishes to emphasise that it will continue to actively support tunisia, in particular its economic development. in this context, the commission proposes to open a temporary unilateral duty-free tariff quota of 35 000 tonnes per year for the export of olive oil from tunisia to the union for a total of 70 000 tonnes per year in the form of autonomous trade measures without increasing the total import volume. this measure will have a positive impact on a large part of the tunisian economy. i voted for it.
in writing. ‒ the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) aims to support the reintegration into the labour market of workers and self-employed persons made redundant as a result of globalisation, as a result of major structural changes in world trade patterns, or as a result of the prolongation of the global financial and economic crisis or a new global financial and economic crisis. on 19 august 2015, belgium submitted an application, under reference number egf/2015/007 be/hainaut-namur glass, for a financial contribution from the egf, following redundancies in the regions of hainaut and namur in belgium. the committee considered that the application met the requirements of the relevant regulation and therefore i voted in favour of the adoption of the proposal.
in writing. ‒ the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) aims to support the reintegration into the labour market of workers and self-employed persons made redundant as a result of globalisation, as a result of major structural changes in world trade patterns, or as a result of the prolongation of the global financial and economic crisis or a new global financial and economic crisis. on 19 august 2015, belgium submitted an application, under reference number egf/2015/007 be/hainaut-namur glass, for a financial contribution from the egf, following redundancies in the regions of hainaut and namur in belgium. the measures financed by the egf are expected to involve 412 redundant workers and 100 unemployed young people under 25 years of age (neets) living in the hainaut region who are not in training or education. the request was made on the basis of the intervention criterion, which allows derogation in exceptional cases for redundant workers under article 4 (1) of the egf regulation and for neets under article 6 (2) of the egf regulation. the european parliament therefore supported by a large majority the disbursement of a financial contribution of eur 1 095 544 to be granted on the basis of the request submitted by belgium. on the basis of the above, i voted in favour of the adoption of the proposal.

in writing. ‒ the european globalisation adjustment fund aims to provide additional support to workers affected by the consequences of major structural changes in world trade. the fund shall not exceed a maximum annual amount of eur 150 million in 2011 prices. on 19 august 2015, belgium submitted an application to mobilise the fund, in the amount of eur 1 095 544, to support the reintegration into the labour market of workers made redundant in two enterprises in the provinces of hainaut and namur. the commission has concluded that the application fulfils the conditions for a financial contribution from the egf and that the measures envisaged by the belgian authorities constitute active labour market measures falling within the scope of the egf regulation and has therefore submitted to the parliament and the council a proposal to authorise the mobilisation of eur 1 095 544 from the european globalisation adjustment fund. in its report, the committee on budgets proposes that parliament adopt the commission's proposal and, on the basis of the request submitted by belgium, make a contribution to the mobilisation of the egf of eur 1 095 544. i supported the motion.

in writing. ‒ the european globalisation adjustment fund was established to provide additional support to workers affected by the consequences of major structural changes in world trade. on 20 january 2016, the commission adopted a proposal for a decision to mobilise the european globalisation adjustment fund for belgium to support the reintegration into the labour market of workers made redundant by two companies in the belgian regions of hainaut and namur. the request concerns 412 dismissed workers and approximately 100 unemployed young people not in education or training. i voted for the motion.

in writing. since the crisis, both private and public investment figures have varied between member states. unfortunately, during the semester dossier discussions, it became clear that investment continues to be hampered by both regulatory and non-regulatory challenges. i therefore consider it of the utmost importance that the identification and elimination of investment-disrupting challenges should be part of the efforts to improve framework conditions, reduce administrative barriers and eliminate regulatory bottlenecks. i welcome the fact that the european commission has once again started to explore policy areas and tools in this semester cycle that can provide an overview of the main challenges that are holding back investment at national level. i also believe that the analysis of the main challenges summarised in the country-specific briefings should, however, be continued in the context of the european semester, in particular in the country reports. i believe that it is time to re-launch dialogue with the member states - including in the form of thematic discussions in the council and in council committees - in order to identify these challenges and possible steps and measures to overcome them, otherwise the european semester process will not be able to fulfil the role we intended it to play when we created it.

in writing. ‒ i welcome the fact that the european commission's annual growth survey also highlights the need to pay greater attention to social equity in the new national, stability and reform programmes, and therefore to include three employment indicators (activity rate, youth unemployment and long-term unemployment) in the process of addressing macroeconomic imbalances; it is urgent that these indicators be given a genuine equal weight with the existing ones in order to allow for in-depth analyses in the member states concerned and to ensure that further examination of internal inequalities is carried out and that economic and social reforms can be proposed and monitored.
in writing. ‒ since the crisis, the number of both private and public investments has varied across member states. unfortunately, during the semester dossier discussions, it was demonstrated that investment continues to be hampered by regulatory and non-regulatory challenges. i therefore consider it important that identifying and addressing the challenges to investment should be part of the efforts to improve framework conditions and reduce administrative obstacles. i welcome the fact that the european commission has once again started to explore policy areas and tools in this semester cycle that can provide an overview of the main challenges that are holding back investment at national level. i believe that the analysis of the main challenges summarised in the country-specific briefings should certainly be continued in the context of the european semester, in particular in the country reports. it is time to re-engage with member states, including through thematic discussions in the council and in council committees, to identify these challenges and the steps and actions to address them. without them, the european semester process will not be able to fulfil the role we intended it to play when we created it.
in writing. ‒ on 26 november 2015, the commission published its report on growth in 2016. the report by the economic and monetary affairs committee notes that while the european union is experiencing economic recovery, it is rather uneven, with some member states continuing to struggle with low growth rates and global economic growth slowing down. it points out that europe continues to face a significant investment gap, which significantly weakens longer-term growth potential, and that the employment rate is improving, but not enough to significantly reduce unemployment and poverty. finally, it points out that, despite the growing current account surplus in the euro area and the significant reductions in current account deficits and specific labour costs in several member states, private and public debt remains high in many countries and net external debt as a proportion of gdp has not decreased in most member states. in the light of these challenges, the report seeks to contribute with proposals to the definition of economic policy priorities for 2016. it calls for measures to be geared to a stronger recovery, for the governance of emu to be deepened in the interests of stability and convergence, and for accountability, relevance and effectiveness to be enhanced by strengthening democracy. i voted for the report.
in writing. ‒ i voted against the european semester for economic policy coordination: annual growth report 2016. in my view, it is too euro-centric and completely ignores the role of non-euro-area countries in the european semester. while the report notes that the implementation of the country-specific recommendations is inadequate, it does not address the fact that the compliance with the recommendations varies widely between euro-zone and non-euro-zone countries. (in 2014, euro area countries made some progress on 61% of recommendations, while non-euro area countries made at least some progress on only 33% of recommendations. ) although the rapporteur encourages a public debate on this, i am concerned about the proposal to create a mechanism through which the commission can better encourage member states to implement the country-specific recommendations. i also miss mentioning social equity, which is also a central element of policies to stimulate the economy. overall, although the report covers a number of important topics, it lacks the specific details on these issues and thus does not sufficiently emphasise the ep's expectations.

in writing. ‒ the report of the committee on the internal market and consumer protection on the integration of the single market into the 2016 european semester. the report stresses the importance of further developing the single market and is concerned that the implementation of its recommendations for the european semester 2011-2014 has been weaker than expected. it therefore calls on the commission to propose a mechanism to encourage countries to implement the country-specific recommendations and to include monitoring of this in the european semester. i disagree with the report because it is essentially a continuation of the faulty economic policy and philosophy that has been in place up to now, which does not take into account the huge differences between the member states (e.g. five times the wage differentials, the significantly different economic structure, the division of the union into competing debtor and creditor countries, etc.) and continues to enforce a policy that has long since been shown to have failed. the union could develop much faster than the united states under a different, non-neoliberal policy, because catching up with the less developed countries would provide a significant dynamic. based on all of this, i rejected the report.
in writing. ‒ the single market governance report is one of the three parliamentary reports on the 2016 european semester. the crisis has shown that europe needs to take steps to improve its economic model and restore its competitiveness. this requires both public funding and targeted investments. however, the potential of the single market is not being realised at present. i believe that the union should support member states to significantly increase cross-border trade and to act urgently to make better use of digital technologies. i believe that the governance of the single market must be strengthened to make the union a driving force for growth and job creation. this requires the reintroduction of the highest level of political oversight, the harmonisation of the transposition and implementation of eu rules, and the development of more effective means to ensure that the single market truly benefits citizens and businesses. the functioning of the single market will be reviewed in the context of the europe 2020 strategy. it is necessary to look precisely at where progress has been made and to try to identify where difficulties remain. these should be the basis for defining policy priorities.

in writing. ‒ tunisia is the cradle of the arab spring and the only country in the middle east and north africa to have undergone a process of democratic and political transformation: a new constitution, adopted on 26 january 2014, is exemplary in protecting rights and freedoms, and free, plural and transparent elections were held at the end of 2014. in this respect, tunisia is an example of democratic transition for other countries in the region. the eu and tunisia also have close and long-standing relations: the first agreement on trade cooperation was concluded in 1969 and tunisia was the first country on the southern shore of the mediterranean to sign an association agreement with the eu in 1995. the commission therefore considers that the opening of negotiations on a free trade agreement between the eu and tunisia on 13 october 2015 is appropriate and appropriate to ensure the smooth conclusion of the negotiations. considers it important, in order to do so, that the agreement takes into account the significant economic differences between the two parties, provides for the progressive, gradual and asymmetric opening of sectors of the tunisian economy and that the eu provides substantial financial and technical assistance to tunisia in order to implement the various provisions of the free trade agreement in a proper manner. i supported the motion.

in writing. ‒ the proposal aims to draw attention to the poor conditions in which pet animals are placed under the current system. an important step towards promoting the maximum application of animal welfare considerations would be for the commission to adopt a regulation on animal diseases and to establish a complex pet animal registry system, also under a delegated act. the clear advantage of a comprehensive register would be to prevent the spread of infectious diseases affecting such animals and to locate the source of infection, and to allow for the harmonisation of the different official certificates issued to animals in the member states and for better traceability of the passport of animals. the current animal passport regime contains loopholes which allow black farmers to exploit the benefits of the passport to transport pet animals from one member state to another for commercial purposes. this market generates billions of euros in revenue for operators in the black economy every year, but it also poses a serious threat to the genetic deterioration of farmed animals and to the animal welfare of individual individuals. it is important that, by eliminating the loopholes, a system is established which, thanks to the complex register, allows the control of the place of origin of the specimens concerned and the recording of the animal health data. on the basis of the foregoing, i voted in favour of the motion.

rapporteur.– madam president, the report on the protection of the eu’s financial interests is one of the most important reports that we discuss on a yearly basis here in parliament. not only because this is about money, a lot of public money, but also because in the troubled times that we have right now, building back confidence in eu institutions is a key issue for the european institutions and for every responsible european politician. we have to assure citizens of the european union that their money is used properly, is transparent and is spent in a way which is in line with the eu regulation. the report which we discuss on a yearly basis generally mirrors the opinion of the commission and this year we had a good and quite detailed report. of course parliament as usual has its own priorities and issues to be raised in the debate. the report we voted on in the committee on budgetary control (cont) has wide backing from different political groups and was voted for almost unanimously in the cont committee. basically we concentrate on two levels of protection of the eu’s financial interests. the first is protection of the revenue of the european union, the own resources of the eu. from this perspective i think that it is very important to emphasise that vat fraud is clearly an eu competence as vat is part of the eu own resource system. the vat gap is varying too not only at european level but also at member state level. the vat gap reached eur 168 billion in 2013. so we welcome that the commission supports a strong pif directive, including vat in the scope, but we have also to include it in the directive or the regulation on the european public prosecutor’s office to be effective. a couple of days ago too the european court of auditors published a special report on vat issues and this supports our view that the eu system on vat is not effective enough: data coming from the member states is not reliable; exchange of information among the member states is not working properly; tax authorities do not cooperate effectively and the european anti-fraud office (olaf) does not have competence to investigate cross-border vat fraud, so it is an important issue. but we also have to point out the problems with the recovery rate because in 2014 it was at the level of 24% which is a historical lowest point and this has to change. the second level of the protection of the financial interests of the eu is proper spending of eu resources. the member states and the commission have shared responsibility for implementing approximately 80% of the european union’s budget so the commission has a lot of things to do here. we need sound financial management while spending eu money and it should be combined with a ‘best use of every euro’ approach. we accepted a new public procurement directive but it is also important to check its implementation. i also have to mention the corruption index in our report. i have to raise the issue of the biannual anti-corruption report of the commission, which we are eager awaiting in parliament and we hope that this year it is going to include the 29th chapter on the eu institutions as well, and better protection for whistle-blowers in the european union and in the member states as whistle-blowers are a very important part of anti-corruption activity. i think that we had very good cooperation together with the shadow rapporteurs. we have prepared a report which i believe can count on well founded grounds on your support in the vote.
vice-president of the commission.– madam president, i would like to thank everyone very much for all the comments and suggestions they have made. i will try to answer everyone, especially those who have put forward questions to the commission. let me start first with the role of prevention. as mr pirinski indicated, we are putting in place early warning systems that allow us to integrate different databases so that, as in the last intervention, we can actually see where money comes from and who the beneficiary is and then trace the route of the money. we now have multiple systems, and they do not always talk to each other, and that is a problem we are concentrated very much on resolving. in the budget focus for results initiative, we also want to create a way for us to see not only the movement of money, but also what we are getting for the money – what the benefit is, what the impact is. this will take time, but the efforts are structured and consolidated and, as i mentioned in my opening comments, already in the next quarter we will see some operationalisation of a better integration of these systems. secondly, there was a point made on the importance of separating irregularities and fraud. of course, fraud is the most dangerous – it is cancerous in societies – but it is also the more difficult to catch, because in fraudulent activities there is usually a lot of effort and smart investment to hide what is being done. what does it mean for us? two things: one, to simplify the rules so that it is more difficult to create misinformation, and that simplification certainly would not only reduce fraud but also would reduce irregularities. secondly, in the analyses we do to sketch more clearly the lessons learned when we catch fraud, what does it mean in terms of the systems in place to prevent it from happening? here comes the point on institutional capabilities. we are currently missing a hammer when we know from the work of olaf that there is irregularity and, more importantly, there is fraud because we send the information back to national authorities and it is up to them. in countries where the legal system is strong, action is taken; in countries where there are difficulties in the legal system, it may not be taken. we know that people here recently reflected on only 24% being claimed back – this is, by the way, not only about fraud, but also about irregularity. our thinking in the commission was that, with the european public prosecutor’s office, we will provide this extra hammer to go after fraud. we put forward the proposal, but unfortunately what we have seen is a watering down of the original proposal. we are concerned about it and have expressed our concerns, including the fact that vip fraud now seems to be excluded from the mandate of the eppo, which of course would mean a big chunk of potential abuse being out of action. of course, it is for member states to complete their deliberations on the european public prosecutor’s office, but i would agree with those of you who have said that it has to be value added for us to fund it. we do not need institutions for the sake of institutions; we need them for effectiveness, for doing the right job. there has been a very important point made that we are strong when we equip people with the opportunity to speak up. in that sense, protection for whistle—blowers is critical. we do it for staff in the commission, and the question is: what more can we do to support member states in enhancing their whistle-blower legislation? that is a conversation still to be had – what is our responsibility? we want to be sure, we want to be prudent, and we do not want to step out of line of what is our responsibility. we heard a comment that if we do not respect sovereignty and subsidiarity there could be more trouble than benefit, and we are, of course, very mindful of this. let me finish by saying that we hope next year will come, mr pirinski, with a very good analysis of why the level of fraud has gone up. is it because we detect more, so we catch more, or is it actually bad news, because more is taking place? hopefully we would already integrate that analysis into the action by the commission.
rapporteur.– madam president, i would like to thank the commissioner for her contribution and all the members who participated in the discussion tonight for the lively debate. very briefly i would like to say – as a short reaction to the different issues which were raised – that i believe that there are four basic elements in the fight against corruption and fraud in the european union. the first – and this links to the question of prevention – is full transparency. there is no fraud and there is no corruption if there is transparency. this is, for example, about the mandatory lobbying register in the eu, but there are also some worrying developments in the member states regarding transparency. this is also about better reporting by the national authorities. the second element is enhanced cooperation between the member states. mrs macovei mentioned that it is impossible to fight against carousel fraud – vat fraud – without good cooperation between the member states and the member state authorities, which is not happening right now. the third element is strong institutions. when we talk about olaf, of course we can criticise it, but olaf cannot be effective without the rights it needs to be effective. that is why we need to strengthen olaf, for example by checking how olaf’s recommendations are respected in the member states. we also need more institutions such as the european public prosecutor’s office. the fourth, and last, one is the question of sanctions. i think that there are serious shortcomings here in the european institutions. how can we make sanctions? how can we enforce that the member states respect the rules we set up? this is essential. without this there will be no effective fight against fraud and corruption.

in writing. ‒ i voted in line with the line of the european people's party in support of the political agreement reached on the draft animal health regulation. the new regulation combines the contents of 50 existing eu legislation. it was established to simplify and increase the transparency of official veterinary procedures. it is important that the list of animal diseases registered in the european union is drawn up on the basis of transparent and scientifically based decisions. in addition, member states will be able to increase the protection of their disease-free zones. furthermore, quarantine measures, going beyond the prohibition of animal movements, may be introduced where justified.
in writing. ‒ in may 2013, the commission proposed a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on communicable animal diseases and amending and repealing certain animal health acts. in april 2014, parliament adopted the commission proposal with amendments at first reading. the austrian federal council stated that it considered the draft legislative act to be incompatible with the principle of subsidiarity (as justified in the report of the committee on agriculture and rural development). in september 2014, an interinstitutional consultation was launched on parliament's decision at first reading. the council published its position at first reading in december 2015. in its report, the committee on agriculture and rural development recommends that parliament, at second reading, agree with the position adopted by the council at first reading and that it declare that the regulation has been adopted in accordance with the council's position. i voted for the motion.
in writing. ‒ i did not vote for the rejection of this animal health report, as i think it is good that we are finally dealing with a common segment of animal and public health, communicable diseases, in one report. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the european union's fisheries policy is not distorted by the current crisis. the draft also targets animal welfare and illegal trade in both cases and combines some 40 legal acts, thus also pointing towards simplification. the approach places a strong emphasis on prevention and helps professionals to keep up with scientific developments. i am glad that the issue of antibiotics is included in the report, because we have to deal with the issue of antibiotic resistance in a very high level. by linking animal health and public health, we can reduce the use of antibiotics and reduce the growth of antibiotic resistance. i think that further reduction could be achieved with alternative, non-antibiotic based medicines. the objectives set out in the report point to an effective, uniform protection system at european level, as it encourages both authorities and manufacturers to put greater emphasis on prevention and control. in my view, the decentralisation of the public health service system in hungary may be an obstacle to this effective action.

in writing. ‒ the draft regulation and its committee-amended version, while using eu funds without co-financing from the member states, provide member states with the possibility to choose the range of products to be distributed in their schools and to prioritise local products where possible. the report also provides for the freedom to distribute special products specific to the region to schools, such as honey or olive oil and similar products. in its recommendations, it also takes care to draw attention to the so-called school fruit programme and the inclusion of individual agricultural links in training, as well as the requirement of sustainability and fair trade. it proposes that aid be allocated differentially between member states or even between regions, depending on needs and access. on these grounds, i supported the adoption of the regulation.
in writing. ‒ school milk and school fruit programmes play an important role in the eu's common agricultural policy in two ways: they help to reduce any surpluses that may accumulate in certain agricultural product lines, and they also have a major social role: every child has access to healthy milk or milk products and fruit at least once a day, as part of school meals. the latter is particularly important in terms of promoting the development of the young organism, the development of healthy eating habits within educational institutions. the eu's contribution to the co-financed programmes is currently eur 100 million per year for school milk and eur 150 million per year for school fruit. that amount is not sufficient in my opinion. that's why we're fighting with the epp members to increase the eu budget for these programs.
in writing. ‒ the majority of the hungarian people's party amendments to the report were included in the report adopted by the european parliament. the european parliament therefore calls on the commission to take account of the accelerated payment needs of cohesion investments at the planning stage and to increase the resources to the necessary level. it is important that the commission already in the draft budget foresees an accelerated implementation of regional development programmes in the member states and increases cohesion resources proportionately. we aim to have the european commission pay in full in 2017 the bills that have been incurred in connection with the projects already implemented in the member states. the european parliament takes the view that the 2017 budget should also ensure that the resources mobilised to address the migration crisis are not used to the detriment of other existing union programmes. our proposal protects cohesion and agricultural funds when determining the resources to deal with the migration crisis. the european parliament resolution stresses the importance of school milk and school fruit programmes. in our proposal, the european commission should examine how the 2017 budget could increase the eu funds available to finance these programmes. we firmly rejected the socialist initiative which hypocritically invokes 'solidarity' and wants to punish member states who reject plans for the mandatory resettlement of migrants with eu budgetary resources. we know that the aim of the socialists is to deprive these member states of cohesion funds.
in writing. ‒ school milk and school fruit programmes play an important role in the eu's common agricultural policy. on the one hand, they help to eliminate any surplus crops that may accumulate in certain agricultural product lines, and on the other hand, they fulfil an important social task: every child has access to healthy milk or milk products and fruit at least once a day, as part of school meals. the eu's contribution to the co-financed programmes is currently eur 100 million per year for school milk and eur 150 million per year for school fruit. i don't think that's enough money. that's why we're fighting with the epp members to increase the eu budget for these programs. we've had our first success. the amendment tabled jointly with my colleague tamás deutsch succeeded in including a similar call to the european commission in the version of the parliament's report on the eu budget for 2017, which was voted on in the ep's committee on budgets.
in writing. ‒ in january 2014, the commission proposed the adoption of a regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending regulations (eu) no 1308/2013 and (eu) no 1306/2013 as regards the aid scheme for the supply of fruit and vegetables, bananas and milk in educational establishments. in april 2015, the committee on agriculture and rural development decided to open an interinstitutional consultation before adopting its report to be submitted by parliament in the preparation of its position at first reading. in january 2016, the committee on agriculture and rural development endorsed the text adopted in the interinstitutional negotiations and in its report recommends that parliament adopt the draft regulation at first reading, as amended accordingly. i supported the motion.
in writing. ‒ i believe that encouraging children to eat healthy food is essential, which is why i voted in favour of the report. in the future, a package of meals for milk, fruit and vegetables and bananas will be introduced as a common programme in educational institutions. on the one hand, i am glad that there is a unified eu-wide approach, because the eu is much more effective in certain matters than the member states individually. on the other hand, i think it is a shame that some member states are unable to solve this problem on their own and are therefore giving up on children. i believe that the inaction of the member states can only be remedied by a united action at eu level. public consultation is required in the implementation of the programme in the member states, thus ensuring the use of high quality local products in the programme. it is unfortunate that some member states are unable to tackle this on their own and are thus sacrificing the health of children. the hungarian government not only cannot solve the problem of healthy child nutrition, but it is also imposing a shameful 27% vat on food, including products intended for children's nutrition. the central logic behind the programme is that we should not be afraid of the idea of a common eu-wide duty-free food system, but that it is time to finally implement it for the benefit of citizens.
in writing. ‒ experience gained in the application of the current programmes, the conclusions of external evaluations and subsequent analysis of the different policy options and social difficulties of the member states show that the continuation and strengthening of both school programmes is of the utmost importance. the consumption of fresh fruit and vegetables and dairy products is currently on a declining trend, especially among children, while the number of children who are morbidly obese is increasing due to consumption patterns that increasingly favour highly processed foods, often high in added sugar, salt, fat or additives. it is therefore important that union aid financing the allocation of certain agricultural products to children in educational establishments should promote more healthy eating habits and the consumption of local products. i voted in favour of the report.
in writing. ‒ the proposal aims to promote the more efficient operation of europe's seaports and to contribute to better water connectivity. the modernisation of port services and operations and the increase of port investment are an essential part of the proposal. the regulation creates the necessary conditions for ports that are currently not functioning properly. it does this by applying to the 319 main sea ports identified in the ten-t guidelines, which handle 96% of european freight and 93% of passenger traffic. the commission has also been able to reach a compromise with the major political groups and to agree on key issues such as financial transparency, independent supervision and port services and infrastructure charges. the amendments on financial transparency and the freedom to provide port services are particularly important among the proposals of the pp group. the substantial changes referred to above will contribute to the better and more sustainable operation of european ports in the future, thus increasing the union's competitiveness in international shipping relations. i voted in favour of allowing the trilateral negotiations to begin.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on access to the market for port services and the establishment of a framework for financial transparency in ports. i agree with the rapporteur that ports play a major role in the long-term competitiveness of european industries, creating added value and jobs in all coastal regions of the union. increasing their efficiency is a priority. in my view, the report has further strengthened the commission's input, which will thus contribute more effectively to a more integrated and sustainable functioning of the ten-t. i welcome amendments that emphasise making port operations safer and more environmentally sustainable. the amendments not only promote the modernisation of port services, but the rapporteur has also clearly stated the importance of social provisions governing the port labour law system and workers' rights, including better training and improved safety conditions for port workers. however, i would like to emphasise that i voted in favour of amendments nos 146 and 147 with the greatest possible weight. overall, the rapporteur's work has contributed to the efficient functioning of the ten-t network and to improving legal certainty in ports.
in writing. ‒ the commission proposal aims to contribute to a more efficient, interconnected and sustainable operation of the ten-t by creating a framework that improves the functioning of ports and helps them adapt to changing transport and logistics requirements. the main objectives of the proposal include the modernisation of port services and operations and the establishment of a framework to attract port investment. i voted for the document.
in writing. ‒ the commission has proposed the adoption of a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on harmonised indices of consumer prices and repealing regulation (ec) no 2494/95. in its report, the committee on economic and monetary affairs recommends that parliament adopt the draft regulation at first reading with a substantially amended text. the amendment would remove two issues from the list of those on which the commission could decide under the regulation's powers and propose that these be directly established by the regulation. the first is to identify sub-indices of the harmonised indices of consumer prices whose proportion in the total basket is negligible, and the second is to identify sub-indices whose production can be suspended because some of them do not relate to final consumption expenditure of households or because the degree of methodological harmonisation is not yet sufficient. i supported the motion.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the harmonised consumer price index. without high-quality, reliable statistics and their comparability, there can be no responsible economic policy management. in this way, up-to-date, comparable statistical methods are in the interest of all eu citizens. as the existing regulation on harmonised indices of consumer prices (hicps) dates from 1995, it was indeed timely to amend it. i agree with the amendment which stresses that the single framework for harmonised consumer price indices should be adapted to current needs, inter alia by improving the relevance and comparability of the hicp. i also share the view that the legal framework should provide for more comprehensive monitoring of complementary indicators that allow for the measurement, analysis and forecasting of inflation. i also welcome the amendment on hicp flash estimates, as early information is indeed important for the monetary policy of the euro area. finally, i am also in favour of encouraging pilot studies on harmonised cost of living indices.
in writing. ‒ the commission proposal for a regulation establishes a uniform framework for the development, production and publication of harmonised indices of consumer prices and house prices (hicps and hpis respectively) at eu, national and sub-national level. the hicp allows the measurement of inflation, which provides valuable information on, among other things, the deflation of economic values such as wages, pensions and interest rates, and thus forms the basis for economic and monetary policy decisions. it is therefore crucial that those statistics are objective, unbiased and comparable across member states and product categories. i voted in favour of the report.

in writing. ‒ equality between women and men is a fundamental right recognised by the eu, a common value of the eu and a necessary condition for achieving the eu's objectives on growth, employment and social cohesion. the report of the committee on women's rights and equal opportunities examines the application of this principle in the work of the european parliament. since 2009, a network of representatives responsible for gender equality in ep committees has been established. each member of the network was asked to complete a questionnaire to examine the activities and policy instruments in each committee for the general promotion of gender equality. the report is based on an evaluation of the responses. these responses have shed light on a number of good practices, but also on problematic cases that call into question the effectiveness of the current framework for the general promotion of gender equality. the report proposes a series of measures to strengthen and make more effective the current structure for gender equality. i supported the adoption of the report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution, as equality between women and men is a fundamental right, a common value and a necessary condition recognised by the eu, and is essential to the achievement of the eu's objectives. gender equality is key to the protection of human rights, the functioning of democracy, respect for the rule of law, and economic growth, social inclusion and sustainability. the principle of universal equality between men and women and the elimination of all forms of discrimination against women is an internationally accepted strategy. nevertheless, the promotion of equality between women and men is one of the main weaknesses listed in the european commission's evaluation of the gender equality strategy for the period 2010-2015. in my view, the european parliament has a key role to play in addressing gender inequalities. in practice, this means promoting equal economic, social and political participation of women and men and extending the policy framework on gender equality. the proposal strengthens and makes more effective the current structure for gender equality, including through the creation of a strong interinstitutional network, on the one hand, for enhanced cooperation with national parliaments for regular exchange and contacts, and on the other hand, for a stable link with the ep's high level group on gender equality and diversity.
in writing. ‒ the principle of universal gender equality is already an internationally accepted strategy for achieving gender equality. the mainstreaming of gender equality in practice means integrating the gender dimension into the process of planning, developing, implementing, monitoring and evaluating policies, regulatory measures and spending programmes, with a view to promoting equality between men and women and combating discrimination. i voted in favour of this report in order to promote it.

in writing. - mr president, i have to go. it would be important for both the euro and non-euro member states to join the european banking union. this is a prerequisite for the protection of depositors in banks in hungary, for example, to be similar to that of depositors in the euro area, regardless of the type of bank they are customers of. if a member state is no longer covered by the european deposit guarantee scheme, customers may move to banks based in the euro area, which offer greater protection. the spiral could bring other banks down, even financial institutions the size of otp. deposits in a member state acceding to the banking union are backed by european protection. the single european resolution fund for banks means that when a bank is in difficulty, the costs are borne not by taxpayers but by creditors, shareholders and investors. the european deposit guarantee fund (edf) provides full protection for small deposits of less than eur 100 000 in the event of a bank failure. the banking union's pillars, the bank rescue and deposit guarantee fund, can help prevent crises and make the european financial system more stable and predictable. this is not a sovereignty issue, but a matter of survival for hungarian bank depositors.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the reduction of sulphur content in liquid fuels, which supports the related commission codification process. the european commission proposal takes account of the interinstitutional agreement of 20 december 1994 on an accelerated procedure for the formalisation of the legislative texts. the directive combines a number of legal acts and also aims to reduce sulphur dioxide emissions from individual liquid fuels. i believe that every step we take in this direction will reduce the amount of harmful substances that we put on people and the environment. for example, the directive sets maximum sulphur levels in the european union for heavy fuel oil, gas oil, marine gas oil and marine diesel oil. this is done by allowing member state and regional variations where environmental conditions allow, and by granting concessions for combustion plants which comply with the emission limit values of directives 2001/80/ec and 2010/75/eu of the european parliament and of the council. with all this, i think we can ensure the principle of gradualness.

in writing. ‒ the commission has proposed the adoption of a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on the prevention of diversion of trade in certain essential medicines into the european union. the advisory working party of the legal services of the european parliament, the council and the commission considers that the proposal provides for a simple consolidation of the existing texts without substantial changes. in its report, the committee on legal affairs therefore recommends that parliament give its consent to the proposal as amended in accordance with the recommendations of the said advisory working party. i voted accordingly.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report, as the advisory working party of the legal services of the european parliament, the council and the commission considered that the proposal in question contained a simple consolidation of the existing texts without any substantial amendment. the codified text states that price segmentation between the developed countries and the poorest developing countries is necessary to provide the poorest developing countries with basic pharmaceutical products at greatly reduced prices. these prices cannot, of course, be considered as reference prices for the same products in the markets of developed countries. the proposed codified rules are intended to prevent the importation into the union of products subject to tiered pricing by establishing appropriate derogations. i consider it an important additional element that the regulation establishes common principles on the basis of which the customs authorities of the member states and other competent authorities can initiate concrete action.

in writing. ‒ the report concerns a proposal for a council decision on the conclusion, on behalf of the european union, of the amending protocol to the agreement between the european community and the principality of andorra on the taxation of savings income in the form of interest payments. the european union and andorra signed an agreement on the automatic exchange of financial account information on 12 february 2016 with the aim of improving international tax cooperation and compliance. the agreement represents an important step in the fight against tax fraud and tax evasion. it updates the 2004 agreement, which ensures that andorra applies measures equivalent to the eu directive on taxation of savings income in the form of interest payments. the new agreement establishes an automatic exchange of information between the eu member states and andorra on financial accounts held by nationals of the other country on the territory of one of the countries, as from 2018, on data collected as from 1 january 2017. the aim is to address situations where taxable persons seek to conceal income or capital representing assets for which tax has not yet been paid. the aim of the agreement is to ensure the automatic exchange of information allowing full tax transparency and cooperation between tax authorities, and i have therefore supported its adoption.
in writing. ‒ the european union and andorra signed an agreement on 12 february 2016 on the automatic exchange of financial account information to improve international tax cooperation and compliance. the agreement constitutes an important step in efforts to combat tax fraud and tax evasion and updates the 2004 agreement which ensures that andorra applies measures equivalent to the eu directive on taxation of savings income in the form of interest payments. the new agreement establishes an automatic exchange of information between the eu member states and andorra, as from 2018, on financial accounts held by nationals of the other country in the territory of one of the countries, on data collected as from 1 january 2017. the aim is to address situations where taxable persons seek to conceal income or capital representing assets for which tax has not yet been paid. under the new agreement, the tax authorities of the member states and andorra will be able to identify the taxpayers concerned with precision and clarity; to fulfil and enforce their tax obligations in cross-border situations; to assess the likelihood of tax evasion; and to avoid unnecessary further investigations.
in writing. ‒ the eu and andorra agreed in 2004 that the principality would apply measures equivalent to the eu directive on taxation of interest income on savings. on 12 february 2016, an agreement was signed to establish, as from 2018, an automatic exchange of information between the member states of the union and andorra on financial accounts held by nationals of the other country in respect of data collected as from 1 january 2017. the aim is to address situations where taxable persons seek to conceal income or capital representing assets for which tax has not yet been paid. the council has submitted a proposal for a decision on the ratification of the agreement. in its report, the committee on economic and monetary affairs recommends that parliament give its consent to the conclusion of the protocol amending the agreement. i voted accordingly.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report between the european community and the principality of andorra on the taxation of interest income from savings. the report is certainly welcome and should be supported, as it endorses the updating of the 2004 agreement between the eu and andorra, which takes the union further serious steps in the fight against tax fraud and tax evasion. under the new agreement, andorra will apply measures equivalent to the latest eu directive on taxation of savings income and automatic exchange of information between the two parties on financial accounts from 2018. this avoids taxable persons from concealing income or capital representing assets for which tax has not yet been paid. this objective is also consistent with the ambitions of the ep's tax2 committee. the agreement is mutually beneficial, helps to curb tax evasion and ultimately serves the interests of all honest taxpayers, in particular individuals and smes.

in writing. ‒ the purpose of this directive is to provide procedural safeguards for children who are suspected or accused of committing a crime. the text voted today guarantees that the best interests of minors will be protected throughout the procedure. the most important provisions of the directive for me are the following: the right to information, the right to legal assistance, the right to an individual assessment, the right to a medical examination, the right to audio-visual recording of interrogations and special safeguards in the custody of children. it is equally important to me that we be clear in the wording, so that for example 'child' as a concept clearly applies to anyone under the age of 18. in the light of the above, i voted in favour of the adoption of the report.
