in writing. ‒ the european commission estimates that more than 1 million children are prosecuted in the union every year. research shows that the rights of children are currently not sufficiently guaranteed at different stages of proceedings within the european union. in this context, the commission has submitted a proposal for a directive of the european parliament and of the council to establish a limited but comprehensive list of the rights of children who are suspects or accused persons in criminal proceedings (or children subject to european arrest warrant proceedings). the report by the committee on civil liberties, justice and home affairs recommends that parliament adopt the commission's proposal at first reading, with almost 80 amendments. the vast majority of the amendments are designed to refine, extend, strengthen or clarify the rules relating to the various rights referred to in the commission proposal. it is also proposed to introduce a new article providing for remedies in the event of infringement of rights under the directive and to insert a new paragraph at the beginning of article 12 to provide for certain minimum guarantees applicable in the event of the detention of a child not covered by the commission text, including access by a person exercising parental responsibility or another appropriate adult. i supported the motion.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the proposal to introduce a european union directive to ensure that children brought before the courts of the member states receive information, legal advice and parental protection appropriate to their age. in my work as a member of parliament, i have always been strongly committed to promoting the protection of the most vulnerable groups in society, especially children. i also voted to emphasise that this priority protection is also given to the child as an accused or suspect, as the case may be. i find the catalogue of rights and guarantees relating to due process contained in the draft directive useful and, in particular in the case of children, i agree with the principle of the regulation that the main objective of the procedure or punishment should be the prevention of recidivism. the proposed legislation, in my view, provides reassuring guarantees for the separation of children from adult offenders and for the adequate training of prosecutors and judges in relation to children. i hope that our decision will make this directive another piece of european legislation that will make a real contribution to the practical implementation of legal certainty, equality and social solidarity in all the member states.
in writing. ‒ the european commission estimates that more than 1 million children are prosecuted in the union each year, representing 12% of all those involved in criminal proceedings in the same area. in addition to the figures, it is also worrying that the treatment of children under criminal proceedings varies considerably between member states. research at eu level shows that the rights of children are currently not sufficiently guaranteed at the various stages of proceedings within the european union, and the european court of human rights often finds member states guilty. i supported him with my vote.
in writing. ‒ the report provides general guidelines for the preparation of the 2017 budget and covers the commission section. it is the section that formulates the general economic policy of the union, since most of the expenditure is allocated to individual directorates-general, i.e. the commission budget essentially represents the economic policy of the eu as a whole. the report stresses that the union budget has only a limited capacity to deal with these crises through the use of the flexibility instrument agreed in the negotiations on the mff. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environmentally friendly use of energy. this is in fact true, but the report is ultimately an endorsement of the neoliberal economic policies that have been applied and failed. this has forced austerity measures on member states, which have depressed real wages and contributed to the prolongation of the economic and social crisis. the eu budget should be used in such a way as to give priority to integration and cohesion policies aimed at genuine convergence, based on social progress and solidarity, the creation and protection of fair, quality and secure jobs, and the sustainable use of natural resources. on the basis of all this, i voted against the report.
in writing. ‒ the majority of the hungarian people's party amendments to the report were included in the report adopted by the european parliament. the european parliament therefore calls on the commission to take account of the accelerated payment needs of cohesion investments at the planning stage and to increase the resources to the necessary level. it is important that the commission already in the draft budget foresees an accelerated implementation of regional development programmes in the member states and increases cohesion resources proportionately. we aim to have the european commission pay in full in 2017 the bills that have been incurred in connection with the projects already implemented in the member states. the european parliament takes the view that the 2017 budget should also ensure that the resources mobilised to address the migration crisis are not used to the detriment of other existing union programmes. this proposal protects cohesion and agricultural funds when determining the resources to deal with the migration crisis. the european parliament resolution stresses the importance of school milk and school fruit programmes. in our proposal, the european commission should examine how the 2017 budget could increase the eu funds available to finance these programmes. in view of the above, i voted in favour of the adoption of the report.

in writing. ‒ the committee on budgets has tabled a motion for a resolution on the preparation of the 2017 budget. the proposal stresses that the budget should lay the foundations for a path towards economic growth and job creation, while the eu's economic recovery and investment levels remain below potential and the investment gap persists. it points out that the union budget is currently able to address these crises mainly through the use of all the instruments jointly agreed in the negotiations on the tpp, and in particular the specific instruments such as the flexibility instrument. it stresses, however, that in the event of further deterioration of the crisis, the full use of the existing flexibility provisions will not be sufficient to resolve the problem. reiterates in this context that the payment appropriations for the specific instruments (flexibility instrument, european union solidarity fund, european globalisation adjustment fund and emergency aid reserve) should be calculated beyond the ceilings set out in the tens, as are the commitments, and proposes that parliament should express strongly the expectation that this issue will be resolved in the context of the tens mid-term review. i supported the motion.

in writing. ‒ the report is based on the fact that the european parliament has repeatedly called for the 2003 interinstitutional agreement (between the european parliament, the council of the european union and the european commission on better regulation) to be updated. however, the proposal does not contain any decisive elements, subsidiarity is not given sufficient emphasis, and the democratic deficit persists: only the commission can submit a legislative proposal. it is to be criticised that the proposal to improve the quality of legislation does not comply with the principle of transparency, that the individual points are vague, burdensome and do not involve the participation of a legal professional. there is no guarantee that the quality of legislation will improve, and no guarantee that central regulation will gradually be reduced, but instead the stealthy devolution of powers supported by the european court of justice and the commission is becoming more and more powerful. the reason why i did not reject the report, despite the foregoing, but abstained from voting, is point 12. welcomes the fact that the commission has taken the necessary steps to ensure that the rules on political dialogue with national parliaments are better used; stresses in this context the important role conferred on national parliaments by the treaty of lisbon and stresses that, in addition to monitoring compliance with the principles of subsidiarity and proportionality, they have the opportunity to make a meaningful contribution to political dialogue and are making use of this opportunity; encourages better use of the existing subsidiarity and proportionality mechanisms laid down in the treaties;
in writing. ‒ the current interinstitutional agreement is the first revision of the legal rules of the game between the eu institutions since 2003. at the same time, this legal language and form must effectively convey the political will that created it, and this report further reinforces this. better and more effective legislation should seek to avoid both extreme over- and under-regulation. it is therefore important that all stakeholders are involved and heard in the legislative process, not just the largest but also the smallest, smes and citizens. the report gives an interpretation of the interinstitutional agreement in which the interests of smes are guaranteed; the legal form of political will is ensured by the mandatory nature of pre-decision impact assessments, and the balance between delegated and implementing acts is an important objective for institutional actors. however, the success of the interinstitutional agreement lies in its implementation. i voted in favour of the report.

if you look at the title of this report, which says 'the agreement on tobacco products' (the pmi agreement), you think that pmi is probably a small part of the eu's multi-stakeholder bureaucracy, and the acronym for it. however, upon reading the report, it turns out that this is philip morris international, a giant tobacco company. and the report reveals that the european union has contractual relations with four other tobacco companies. i have a suggestion: in every single european union country - including my own, hungary - show the students who are about to graduate only this title, that the agreement between the european union and philip morris international. and if you don't know why that's unacceptable, then you don't have the right civic skills to graduate, you have to relearn what transparency is, what corruption is, and so on.
in writing. ‒ the fight against smoking is one of the main health policy objectives in the eu member states. according to the world health organization, smoking is the number one cause of preventable disease in europe, responsible for 87% of all deaths from chronic diseases. in my view, the prevention of illicit tobacco trade is a public task which should be carried out by the state alone, in complete independence from the tobacco industry. the hungarian government is known to be committed to reducing smoking and is a leader in this field at eu level, with a number of measures that sometimes break with traditional means. in addition to the uk, ireland, france and norway, hungary has recently prepared a draft of the legal framework for the uniform packaging of cigarettes, which could be submitted to the government in early spring. since the agreement between philip morris international and the union in 2004, the market and the regulatory environment have also changed significantly. the majority of the illegal trade today is in soft white cigarettes, which these agreements cannot handle. the new legal framework established by the union tobacco products directive and the relevant protocol to the world health organisation framework convention on tobacco control already covers all elements of previous agreements with tobacco companies. in view of all this, i am opposed to the extension of the eu agreement with philip morris international or to any form of renewal of the agreement.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the joint motion for a resolution opposing the renewal of the agreement between philip morris international (pmi) and the european commission, which expires in july 2016. it can be seen that, while smuggling initially decreased as a result of the pmi agreement, the gap was soon filled by unbranded, smuggled so-called cheap white cigarettes, as economic, social and regulatory conditions changed. the commission should also be able to assess the impact of the measures taken on the union market, in particular the impact of the measures taken on the union market, on the union's financial interests and on the union's financial stability. i believe that the profits of manufacturers, the traffic of smugglers and counterfeiters in the black zone and the revenue of governments from tobacco taxes are both in the sky. meanwhile, national governments, especially the orbán government, which is sweeping everything into the pockets of the big spenders, are surrounded by all sorts of corruption allegations. that is why i supported the european commission not renewing its expiring agreements in their current form, while agreeing with the approach of fighting smuggling at all levels, including the commission, with all eu and international legal instruments. this is because, in addition to the health aspects, the illegal trade in tobacco products, and in particular the trade in contraband and counterfeit cigarettes, causes the eu and its member states to lose more than eur 10 billion in revenue each year (duties, vat and excise duties).
in writing. ‒ the main objective of the agreement with pmi is to reduce the near monopoly of counterfeit pmi products on the eu's illicit tobacco market. the decrease in the smuggling of pmi products did not lead to an overall decrease in the volume of illicit products on the union market. the commission should take immediate steps to ensure full transposition of the tobacco products directive in all member states. i voted in favour of the s&d group's position.

in writing. eritrea is now a country that everyone is fleeing from whoever can. the fourth largest number of migrants to europe comes from this country. today's decision highlights that part of the country's grave security risk is that, whatever the laws say, there is no real freedom of religion in the country. according to open doors, eritrea ranks third on the list of countries where christians are most severely and most frequently subjected to atrocities, with an extreme rating. forcing seminarians into military service, banning church members from traveling, imprisoning christians - among many other things - are all part of the local reality, according to field reports by the international aid organization acn. local church leaders years ago expressed desperation in open letters about the mass flight of their followers. it is a grave mistake for the union to ignore this and to give these systems substantial development aid without taking account of human rights abuses. we cannot leave without a word in the face of today's dramatic events in the wider region. in ethiopia, extremists have looted churches, church hospitals, and child care facilities. local christian leaders were shocked to report that all of this was done by those whose churches had previously supported them with funds. in yemen, islamist gunmen brutally murdered four nuns and 15 residents of a charity founded by mother teresa. the martyrs should remind us europeans that we have a responsibility to the persecuted christians.

madam president, on the basis of this report, we are pleased to note that, despite all the political divisions and the contradictions still alive in the process of democratization, montenegro is our partner at the forefront of the western balkans accession process, with consistently good results in the recovery process. i would draw the commission's attention to the fact that this is in itself a value that the eu should use to motivate and stabilise the country and the whole region towards european values through a more active and flexible accession negotiation strategy. first of all, of course, to restore the credibility of our own enlargement policy and then to re-energize it. let us finally move beyond the secondary treatment of enlargement policy, since in the current situation of the union we need all the positive impulses towards integration.
in writing. in line with the report before the european parliament, i welcome the progress made in the accession negotiations with montenegro and the efforts made to implement the legislation. the 2015 country reports are a balanced, objective document that highlights the achievements of the past year, but also highlights the country's shortcomings where it needs to show more significant results. montenegro's foreign policy is commendable, as the country is successfully coordinating its foreign policy with the european union. given the similarity of the conditions for accession to nato and the eu, the country's membership of nato will result in better preparedness during accession negotiations. however, the parliament's report also points out that montenegro needs to take a stronger stance against corruption, which undermines the country's democratic foundations and its social and economic development. the report also highlighted the issue of media freedom, fair and equal access to the media by political parties and media self-organisation. it is important in my field that the report acknowledges the government's commitment to extend quality early childhood education and welcomes the increase in kindergarten enrollment that has been experienced as a result of the targeted campaign. i think that in general, there is a good progress in improving the quality of education, and particularly of early childhood education, and in improving the skills of educators. since the report realistically presents the current situation in montenegro and the results achieved over the past year, i propose that it be adopted.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the proposal that the european union should ensure the importation of a total of 70 000 tonnes of tunisian olives at 0% duty into the member states of the union as a unilateral trade measure after the expiry of the current duty-free quota over two years. i recalled that tunisia is an important mediterranean partner of the eu, whose promising democratization efforts were interrupted by the serious terrorist attacks of march and june 2015 and the political uncertainty that followed, which had an impact on the country's already fragile economy. given the key role of olive production and exports in the country's economy and labour market, this unilateral trade preference could significantly help strengthen the tunisian economy, without significantly damaging the interests of eu producers or the ongoing eu-tunisia trade negotiations. i am convinced that the eu's trade decision will also provide political support for tunisia's democratic development.
in writing. ‒ the terrorist attacks in tunis on 18 march 2015 and in sousse on 26 june 2015 have dealt a severe blow to an already struggling tunisian economy. in this difficult situation, the european union wishes to emphasise that it will continue to actively support tunisia, in particular its economic development. this measure will have a positive impact on a large part of the tunisian economy. the tunisian olive oil sector indirectly employs more than one million people, representing one fifth of the total agricultural employment in tunisia. with this concrete commitment, the european union is not only supporting tunisia's economic development, but also its democratic process. i voted in favor of the motion.
in writing. ‒ the draft regulation on veterinary medicinal products completely reworked the existing legislation, which was applied until now under directive 2001/82/ec and regulation (ec) no 726/2004. the new proposal aims to regulate the authorisation, manufacture, placing on the market, distribution and use of veterinary medicinal products throughout the life cycle of the medicinal product. the text approved by the committee on the environment focuses on the problem of access to veterinary medicinal products, which can be solved by strengthening innovation. the market for veterinary medicinal products is small and highly fragmented, with little incentive for operators to innovate and introduce new products to the market. the draft law contains a number of important advances for our country compared to the current legislation. taking into account the characteristics of the veterinary sector, the new rules encourage the extension of already authorised preparations to additional animal species. new antimicrobials and products developed for so-called less important animal species will enjoy increased data protection. the report gives priority treatment to medicines authorised for bees, with a data protection period of 20 years. the changes could help the emergence of new antibiotics in veterinary medicine and improve the availability of products in a sector of high importance in hungary, such as beekeeping. although the draft still needs to be improved to take full account of the interests of the sectors affected by the regulation, the report provides an excellent basis for trilogues with the council. good move in the right direction.

in writing. ‒ the draft regulation on which this report, which i support, is based aims to regulate the authorisation, manufacture, placing on the market, distribution and use of veterinary medicinal products throughout the life cycle of the medicinal products and to regulate the applicable pharmacovigilance procedure. problems have been encountered in the application of the existing legal framework, including the lack of availability of veterinary medicinal products, administrative burdens, the functioning of the internal market and, of course, the phenomenon of antibiotic resistance. therefore, a new regulatory framework was needed. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of electronic communications networks and services. the report also calls on the european commission to develop guidance on this, which i believe is a step in the right direction. i agree with the report that the provisions for the control of antimicrobials should be much more ambitious, which could be achieved by including the definition of different types of treatment (curative, mass and preventive), a ban on the prophylactic use of antibacterial agents and alternative non-antibiotic agents. i believe it is important and i support the need to strengthen incentives to support innovation. the veterinary medicinal products market is highly fragmented, with little incentive for operators to innovate and introduce new products to the market.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report because i believe that there are many advantages to the separation of marketing authorisations for veterinary medicinal products and medicinal products for human use. the report made considerable progress, for example, with the achievement of important compromises by the political groups on the authorisation and supervision of generic medicines. the report proposes amendments to the commission's proposal on several points, such as the composition and level of fees to be paid or the fixing of the remuneration paid to the competent national authorities by means of non-implementing acts. i agree that the european parliament should be fully involved in the setting of agency fees, as is the case with the legislation on pharmacovigilance activities. the fight against and the monitoring of antimicrobial resistance is also an important part of the report, and has already received considerable attention, in part in the case of medicated feed, including my own work as a shadow rapporteur. finally, i consider it important that the new measures take into account the specificities of the veterinary pharmaceutical sector and that the fees remain affordable for the veterinary pharmaceutical industry. this is important to promote the development and availability of new medicines in the eu.

in writing. ‒ the data-driven economy is one of the main lines of the digital union strategy for the economic future of the european union. the current report builds on the so-called big data market. in the near future, businesses based on this will be able to create many jobs, increase competitiveness and make a significant contribution to economic growth. however, this requires that special attention be paid to the potential risks in addition to the opportunities. the report therefore also needs to include the protection of citizens' data. for this complex plan to be successful, infrastructure development must be a priority. it should also be borne in mind that these developments create new conditions on the labour market, which can be accompanied by a new pool of knowledge and adequately qualified workers. these are primarily for smes to exploit as potential big data market players. the commission has also concluded that the measures under investigation are in line with the principles of the union state aid rules. in the long term, this could facilitate the development of e-governance and e-democracy. these guidelines form the basis of the digital union and are therefore of crucial importance for the future of europe.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the commission's communication on the road to a thriving data-driven economy, which raises a number of valid questions about the commission's 'big data' strategy, such as common standards, interoperability, high-speed networks, high-performance computing infrastructure, consumer protection and data protection. i agree with the view that the data-driven economy requires advanced skills and could create a significant number of jobs in europe in the coming years. to do so, it is essential to strengthen partnerships between businesses and higher education and research institutions, as the report rightly points out. this will certainly encourage innovation in big data technology. i also welcome the fact that data protection has been given a high priority. the commission has also proposed that the data protection rules should be amended to ensure that the protection of personal data is not restricted to the processing of personal data by the union institutions and bodies. the respect for fundamental rights, in particular privacy, must not be compromised.
in writing. ‒ the benefits of the data-driven economy at national and european level will have an impact on society and on all types of enterprises in the value chain. the creation of a data-driven economy is a central element of the digital single market strategy and will help europe regain its competitiveness in advanced sectors and accelerate europe's economic recovery, investment for growth and innovation across all sectors. those can only be achieved if the right business environment and tools are in place to enable the digital transformation and if those technologies comply with the union legal framework on data protection in order to address the risks and challenges associated with them, in particular with regard to fundamental rights and the protection of privacy and data protection. i supported him with my vote.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report, mainly in the hope that the shocking facts it contains will finally reveal to the european institutions and governments the explanation for the relatively large number and proportion of eritrean citizens arriving via the mediterranean sea or drowning at sea while trying to escape. the report makes clear that in this case, it is not war but a brutal authoritarian regime that refuses to back down from violence, torture and humiliation against its own citizens that is driving masses to flee. on the basis of all this, i am convinced that - especially in the light of the failure of the international community's pressure to date - much more effective and urgent action is needed against such a brutal regime pursuing such an extremist policy, especially by the eu and the european external action service. i believe that this would also address one of the important causes of the migration wave that is a major challenge for the union.
in writing. ‒ eritrea has been under a state of emergency since the 1998-2000 war with ethiopia. eritrean citizens are arbitrarily detained or arrested on numerous occasions for unsustainable reasons such as criticism or opposition to the government, journalistic activity, practice of an unofficial religion, evasion or desertion of compulsory military service, cooperation with foreign organisations, attempts to leave the country or flight of a family member or without clear justification. between 2012 and mid-2015, almost twice as many eritreans applied for asylum in europe as syrians. according to the un high commissioner for refugees, more than 400,000 eritreans - 9% of the total population - have fled the country. i voted for the s&d position.
in writing. ‒ in its 2015 report on the former yugoslav republic of macedonia, parliament highlighted that the political crisis experienced in the recent period reflects the lack of effective institutional checks and balances in the country. the only way out of this situation, according to the report, is the full implementation of the political agreement of pristina. in line with the report, i draw attention to the importance of voting and its promotion to the highest international standards, including the guarantee of free and fair voting procedures. parliament also identified further shortcomings in the area of media freedom and media reforms. however, the report rightly highlights the achievements made, welcoming the constructive rules on regional and international cooperation and high-level cooperation with neighbouring countries for the development of the region. the country's relationship with nato can contribute to greater security and political stability in south-eastern europe. however, the increase in elite migration, especially among young people, is a cause for concern. the country's education system faces enormous challenges, and i would like to stress the need for a comprehensive analysis in this regard. the emigration of highly qualified and skilled people must be reduced. in conclusion, the 2015 report on the former yugoslav republic of macedonia has become a balanced report, which i voted in favour of adopting.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the adoption of the report assessing macedonia's preparation for european integration in 2015. the compilation also indicates that the opening of accession negotiations with a country that has already made many sacrifices in preparing for eu membership and has had to bear much of the burden of the refugee crisis is still hampered by a number of external and internal factors. i agree with the authors of the report that now that there is a real chance to ease the final internal political divisions and to accelerate the reform programme following the june snap elections, it is finally time to move beyond the period of so-called name-quarrel, an external factor that has been paralysing the accession process for a long time. i think it is important that the report recognises, in essence, that this is primarily the eu's responsibility, alongside the un's efforts, and that it is unacceptable that the enlargement process should continue to be blocked by a bilateral dispute between an eu member state and an important western balkan partner. i hope and will be urging the commission, as a representative of the ep, to work with the two parties and the other european institutions to develop a roadmap for a mutually acceptable political solution in the near future, following the report and the ep resolution.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the 2015 annual report on bankunio. the banking union is one of the eu's most important achievements since the global financial crisis. it was created with the aim of restoring confidence, promoting the growth of investment in the real economy and providing citizens with a higher level of security against the possible failures of banks and financial companies. the rapporteur gave a full picture of the performance to date of the two pillars, the single supervisory mechanism and the single resolution mechanism, which are now fully operational. among the many constructive recommendations, the suggestion to extend initiatives to better finance smes to start-ups, micro-enterprises and mid-caps is particularly welcome. in addition, i also support the stabilisation of the supervisory and regulatory framework, which is an important element in restoring investor confidence. furthermore, like the rapporteur, i am in favour of the creation of an integrated european rulebook on financial regulation and consumer rights, which would replace the current complex legislation.
in writing. ‒ the banking union plays a key role in ensuring stability and restoring confidence in the euro area banks, promoting financial integration, reducing financial and moral risk within the european banking system, and contributing to the dismantling of the state-bank nexus and the promotion of risk-sharing within the monetary union. the banking union plays a key role in financing investment and, consequently, in promoting growth and job creation across the eu. i voted for it.

have social, human and economic aspects all at once. these affairs are not less important than they have been up to now. not less important than they were in 2011, when – during the hungarian presidency – a project called roma strategy was launched. hungary is proud of having called the attention of the community to those european roma competitors who should be considered as human resources but often have no chance to prove it. youngsters from the roma population have to face extra difficulties if they want to break out of their cultural or material circumstances, which are ruled by the strict tradition and tight bonds of their community. even if they manage to overcome these factors, they have to face the discriminating prejudices of society. the roma population needs special aid in this effort to be able to overcome these disadvantages and other complexes. our task is to form the attitude in society to be more respectful and adapting. the european union’s main duty is to create the professional framework through special programmes focusing on this issue. that is why the roma strategy has called on the member states to refuse all kinds of segregation, discrimination and racism. these roma programmes and invested resources can be refunded only if we take action together with them on the basis of common decisions. we have to bring together not only roma but also non-roma if we want to create sustainable projects. it is of great importance that the culture and history of roma should be integrated in the education of the youth and that the new generation does not grow up without any knowledge or with false information concerning the 10 million roma citizens in europe. europe has decided to face what it has missed so far and will pay attention to creating equal opportunities and providing early childhood aid, which is the most important action, even if the results are apparent only much later. this is how targeted school and pre-school programmes started in the member states, and this was the way to give more and more roma children the chance to get help from early childhood. as we open the doors for schools wider and wider, likewise we have to open the gates of the churches as well, so that a receptive and solidarity-based spirit can pervade roma communities. let us be proud of roma intelligence; let us give roma youngsters the opportunity to obtain degrees, and let us create the circumstances for them to work among us. in europe, the unique hungarian roma college network serves as a good example to help hundreds of roma students to get a degree. among them are doctors, researchers, teachers and artists. we started this work together; let us continue together.

madam president, it is a long-debated issue whether member states should sell citizenship and residence permits or not. states have of course full sovereignty to decide to whom, and how, to grant their respective nationality, but of course it is eu nationality. however, recent global developments put this question into another perspective. the serious risk represented by terrorists, the worrying scale of tax evasion, and the refugee crisis, force us to revise the issue. economic citizenship programmes run by member states are just like harmful tax competition. conditions vary greatly. however, they all lack transparency and therefore represent a breeding ground for fraud, corruption and even terrorism. some countries are openly offering rich individuals and companies the opportunity for tax planning, thus assisting tax evasion, or even potential money laundering by terrorist organisations on eu territory. the fact that these schemes make it so easy for the rich to gain rights within the eu while others literally risk their lives to get here also sends a wrong message. therefore, the question arises: do we want to support tax evasion, make things easy for terrorists and maintain unequal treatment of migrants based on their financial background, or finally create a common system with strict rules and monitoring to prevent all this?

in writing. ‒ the commission proposal aims to consolidate the existing text of council regulation (ec) no 1528/2007 (market access regulation) into a single text. the annex contains the general rules for economic partnership agreements establishing or leading to the establishment of partnership agreements with acp (african, caribbean and pacific) states. annex 1 to the regulation contains the list of states to which it applies. the agreements covered by this regulation are intended to lay down rules for products originating in certain member states. under the current commission proposal, the european parliament, on the basis of article 290 tfeu, empowers the commission to amend the annex to the regulation in order to remove from the list those states with which the agreement has already been concluded. in addition to the current proposal for amendment, the regulation has been amended several times in recent years and it was therefore appropriate to consolidate each of those amendments into a single text.

in writing. ‒ the commission has proposed to the european parliament and the council the adoption of a regulation applying the rules on products originating in certain african, caribbean and pacific states (acp states). the proposal concerns the harmonised structure and recasting of council regulation (ec) no 1528/2007 on market access. the reason for the consolidation is that the market access regulation has been amended nine times since its adoption in 2007. the recast proposal concerns two points. the eu and the southern african development community concluded an economic partnership agreement on 15 july 2014, the provisions of which will replace the corresponding provisions of the eu-south africa trade, development and cooperation agreement. the proposed amendment to article 3 (4) would allow the commission to subsequently adopt delegated acts to determine the arrangements applicable to products originating in south africa. the proposal also proposes to delete the reference to article 134 of the treaty establishing the european community in article 22, since that article has been repealed by the treaty of lisbon. in its report, the committee on international trade recommends that parliament support the commission's proposal. i voted accordingly.

in writing. ‒ the commission proposal aims to consolidate the existing text of council regulation (ec) no 1528/2007 (market access regulation) into a single text. this regulation lays down the general rules for economic partnership agreements establishing or leading to the establishment of partnership agreements with acp (african, caribbean and pacific) states. annex 1 to the regulation contains the list of states to which it applies. the agreements covered by this regulation are intended to lay down rules for products originating in certain member states. under the current commission proposal, the european parliament, on the basis of article 290 tfeu, empowers the commission to amend the annex to the regulation in order to remove from the list those states with which the agreement has already been concluded. in addition to the current proposal for amendment, the regulation has been amended several times in recent years and it was therefore appropriate to consolidate each of those amendments into a single text.
in writing. ‒ the commission proposal concerns the unified structure and recast of council regulation (ec) no 1528/2007 on imports of certain products from acp countries, the so-called market access regulation. this temporary instrument provides duty-free and quota-free access to the union market for products originating in acp countries other than those belonging to the group of least developed countries until 1 october 2016, pending the conclusion and application of wto-compliant economic partnership agreements with those countries. i voted for it.
in writing. ‒ in line with the guidelines of the european people's party, i voted in favour of parliament's consent to the protocol. 30% of the world's oceans are overfished, and marine fish stocks are in danger. it is therefore understandable that the european union is forced to restrict marine fisheries appropriately in order to maintain marine fish stocks. so the amount of sea fish caught is decreasing steadily and significantly. the cfp should therefore pay much more attention to sustainable fisheries, i.e. aquaculture, and in particular freshwater fisheries. a significant part of the hungarian wetlands is located in natura 2000 areas. these fish farms do not represent any threat to the natural values of these areas. in fact, in many cases it is our closed systems of wetlands that have created and preserved unique associations of aquatic habitats. therefore, freshwater aquaculture should be given priority and maximum support from the union. moreover, this area should be freed from unnecessarily stringent and unnecessary sustainability standards that are justified only for marine fisheries and aquaculture.

in writing. ‒ the european union has a specific fisheries partnership agreement with the government of denmark and the home rule government of greenland (hereinafter referred to as the 'eu/greenland fisheries partnership agreement'). the agreement entered into force on 1 january 2007, currently applies until 31 december 2018 and provides access to a wide range of fish stocks for union vessels in the greenland eez. the protocol attached to the original fisheries partnership agreement was in force from 1 january 2007 to 31 december 2012, and was replaced by a protocol concluded for a period of three years from 1 january to 31 december 2015. the commission, having received a mandate from the council on 25 september 2014, held negotiations with the government of greenland and representatives of the government of denmark with a view to renewing the protocol. the new protocol was initialled on 20 march 2015 and the commission adopted the proposal for its renewal on 16 july 2015. the council submitted a draft decision on the conclusion of the new protocol. in its report, the committee on fisheries recommends that parliament agree to the council's draft. i voted accordingly.
in writing. ‒ in line with the guidelines of the european people's party, i voted in favour of parliament's consent to the protocol. the common fisheries policy should pay much more attention to sustainable fisheries, aquaculture and, above all, freshwater fisheries. a significant part of the hungarian wetlands is located in natura 2000 areas. these fish farms do not represent any threat to the natural values of these areas. in fact, in many cases it is our closed systems of wetlands that have created and preserved unique associations of aquatic habitats. therefore, freshwater aquaculture should be given priority and maximum support from the union. moreover, this area should be freed from unnecessarily stringent and unnecessary sustainability standards that are justified only for marine fisheries and aquaculture.
in writing. ‒ the european union has concluded a number of fisheries partnership agreements and protocols with third countries in recent years. fisheries partnership agreements provide the eu with financial and technical assistance in exchange for fishing rights for a wide range of fish stocks within the exclusive economic zones of partner countries. the original fisheries agreement between the eu, on the one hand, and the government of denmark and the home rule government of greenland, on the other, dates back to 1985. this agreement was in force for 10 years and was extended for a further 6 years until it was finally replaced by the fisheries partnership agreement, which is still in force. i supported the report because the new protocol is in line with the objectives of the fisheries partnership agreement: it strengthens cooperation between the union and greenland. it will help to build a partnership framework in which a sustainable fisheries policy can be developed by exploiting fisheries resources in greenland's fishing zone responsibly, for example by supporting local employment. this is in the interest of both parties, in accordance with the relevant conservation and management measures and to the extent of available surplus resources. the recommendation also draws attention to some factors that need to be improved based on the protocol analysis of the previous convention, including the sustainable exploitation of fish stocks, the fight against illegal fishing, the correction of some operational difficulties, closer follow-up of scientific advice and the principle of available surplus and stricter control and adjustment of the financial contribution from the eu.
in writing. ‒ the european union (eu) has concluded a number of fisheries partnership agreements and protocols with third countries in recent years. fisheries partnership agreements provide the eu with financial and technical assistance in exchange for fishing rights for a wide range of fish stocks within the exclusive economic zones of partner countries. i supported him with my vote.
in writing. ‒ international air links were based on bilateral agreements between member states and third countries until the 2002 decision of the european court of justice, which ruled that bilateral air agreements were in breach of eu law. in this context, the european commission has renegotiated the eu-macao agreements. the new agreement was signed on 23 november 2013, subject to the consent of the european parliament. as a member of the hungarian people's party delegation, i therefore supported the agreement's entry into force as soon as possible.

in writing. ‒ international air links between member states and third countries were previously governed by bilateral air transport agreements. however, the court of justice of the european union ruled in 2002 that traditional designation clauses in bilateral air transport agreements between member states infringe union law if they allow a third country to refuse, revoke or suspend the licences or authorisations of an air carrier designated by a member state which is not majority owned and effectively controlled by that member state or its nationals. the commission has therefore negotiated an agreement to replace some of the provisions of the 15 existing bilateral air services agreements between the member states of the union and the macao special administrative region of the people's republic of china. the agreement replaces the traditional designation clauses with an eu designation clause, which allows all eu air carriers to exercise their right of establishment, and by this change brings other provisions of bilateral agreements into line and prohibits anti-competitive behaviour. the council adopted a draft decision on the conclusion of the agreement, subject to parliament's consent. the committee on transport and tourism recommended in its report that parliament give its consent to the conclusion of the agreement. i voted accordingly.
in writing. ‒ international air links were based on bilateral agreements between member states and third countries until the 2002 decision of the european court of justice, which ruled that bilateral air agreements were in breach of eu law. in this context, the european commission has renegotiated the eu-macao agreements. the new agreement was signed on 23 november 2013, subject to the consent of the european parliament. as a member of the hungarian people's party delegation, i therefore supported the agreement's early entry into force.
in writing. ‒ international air links between member states and third countries have been governed by bilateral air transport agreements. the court of justice of the european union ruled in 2002 that the traditional designation clauses in bilateral air transport agreements between member states are in breach of eu law. the commission has therefore negotiated an agreement to replace some of the provisions of the 15 existing bilateral air services agreements between the member states of the union and the macao special administrative region of the people's republic of china. the agreement was signed on 23 november 2013. the council shall require the consent of the european parliament for the conclusion of this agreement. i voted for it.
in writing. ‒ the minimum rates for vat are justified by the fact that for crossborder purchases below a certain threshold, vat is still payable in the country of origin rather than in the country of destination. the minimum standard rate of taxation applicable in all member states which is currently in force therefore serves as a useful safeguard for the proper functioning of the internal market. given that all member states currently impose a flat rate of taxation above 15%, the current rules on a minimum flat rate of at least 15% also provide member states with room for manoeuvre for reforms aimed at reducing the flat rate, thereby broadening the vat base and limiting the use of reduced rates. in these circumstances and subject to decisions on the final form of the definitive system i agree with the commission's proposal, and have voted in favour of the report, which retrospectively maintains the principle of a minimum standard vat rate of 15% and proposes to extend the current measures for two years.

in writing. ‒ taxation is a national competence, so the setting of a general tax rate is a matter of national sovereignty, but at the same time the reduction of the possibilities of tax avoidance should be encouraged. however, the 15% rate is unjustifiably high for a number of product groups. i do not think the report is good enough in this form, and i would suggest a different methodology and a more complex approach to achieving the objectives.
in writing. ‒ directive 2006/112/ec on the common system of value added tax (vat) (vat directive) ensured that the general rate of vat for the period from 1 january 2011 to 31 december 2015 could not be lower than 15%. the commission proposed to the council to amend the vat directive to extend the scope of that directive on the minimum common key to the period from 1 january 2016 to 31 december 2017. the council shall consult parliament before deciding on the proposal. the report of the committee on economic and financial affairs recommends that parliament support the commission's proposal, but proposes that the directive be extended to 31 december 2018 instead of 31 december 2017. i voted in favour of the proposal from the committee on economic and monetary affairs.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report amending directive 2006/112/ec on the common system of value added tax. the provision which expired on 31 december 2015, the extension of which was approved in the report, ensures that the general tax rate in the member states cannot be less than 15%. this rule is an important safeguard for the proper functioning of the internal market under the current system. as the commission plans to publish its action plan on the definitive single market vat system in 2016, it was therefore reasonable for the commission to propose to extend the current measure for two years until 31 december 2017.
in writing. ‒ the vat directive provides that from 1 january 2011 to 31 december 2015 the general tax rate shall not be less than 15%. the provision based on article 113 tfeu requires the council to adopt provisions on the harmonisation of legislation on turnover taxes to the extent necessary for the establishment and functioning of the internal market and to avoid distortions of competition. in view of the circumstances and subject to decisions on the final form of the definitive system , the rapporteur agrees with the commission's proposal to retain the principle of a 15% minimum standard vat rate retroactively and to propose a two-year extension of the current measures. i supported him with my vote.
in writing. ‒ with today’s vote we approve the conclusion of the agreement on strategic cooperation between europol and brazil. this agreement has the objective of supporting and strengthening action and mutual cooperation in preventing and combating organised crime, terrorism and other forms of serious crime, through the exchange of operational, strategic or technical information, including personal data and classified information. we support this agreement with brazil, since it’s an important contribution in the fight against international organised crime.
in writing. ‒ i approve the parliament's position on the agreement on strategic cooperation between brazil and europol. the conclusion of this strategic agreement with brazil is important as the country plays a significant role in the fight against organised crime, trafficking in human beings, drug crime and credit card fraud and other computer-related crime activities. and let's not forget that rio de janeiro is hosting the 2016 olympic games, so crime is predicted to increase. overall, strategic cooperation between europol and brazil would help and strengthen the fight against organised crime and contribute to strengthening international law enforcement cooperation.
in writing. ‒ the 2016 summer olympic games will be hosted by brazil in august. never before have the olympics been held in a south american city. today, international terrorism poses a very serious challenge to all countries. underestimating this could lead to unfortunate consequences such as those caused by the negligence of the belgian authorities. i believe that this cooperation should have been strengthened a long time ago, and i hope that it is not too late.
in writing. ‒ the council adopted a draft decision approving the conclusion by europol of the agreement on strategic cooperation between the federal republic of brazil and the european police office (europol). the council shall consult parliament before giving its consent. the strategic agreement excludes the exchange of personal data, so there is no data protection problem. according to europol, brazil is playing an increasing role in the fight against organised crime and deserves special attention in the areas of counter-terrorism and asset recovery. in its report, the committee on civil liberties, justice and home affairs recommends that parliament support the draft council decision in order to combat organised crime and strengthen international law enforcement cooperation. i voted accordingly.
in writing. ‒ i have voted in favour of the european parliament giving its support to the council for the formal authorisation of the conclusion of the strategic cooperation agreement between europol and brazil. i have considered all the information that indicates that brazil is an increasingly important partner for europe in the fight against international organised crime and terrorism. the hosting of this year's olympic games in brazil is an additional element that has made it urgent to place this cooperation, the exchange of professional methods and information, and mutual advice within an organised legal framework. the european and other experiences in the fight against international terrorism show that major sporting events such as the olympics are prime targets for terrorists, and i therefore considered it appropriate that this important agreement should not be delayed in any way during the consultation of the ep.
in writing. ‒ under the current council decision on europol, the council, after consulting the european parliament, is to authorise the conclusion of international cooperation agreements with third countries or international organisations. such an agreement may cover the exchange of operational, strategic, technical or classified information. the operational cooperation agreement shall also include the exchange of personal data. this proposal concerns the proposed approval of the agreement on strategic cooperation between brazil and europol. i voted for it.

in writing. ‒ the un general assembly established a preparatory commission in july 2015 with the aim of developing by the end of 2017 a binding international agreement on the conservation and sustainable use of marine biological diversity in areas beyond national jurisdiction, in line with the un convention on the law of the sea (unclos). the committee on fisheries report recommends that parliament welcome this step and advocate that the union play a leading role in the development and implementation of the agreement. it also stresses that the new convention should cover fisheries activities and, to this end, calls for the un fish stocks agreement (unfsa) to be incorporated into the new agreement. finally, it stresses that the new agreement must also include the possibility of accountability for all actors involved. i voted for the resolution.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the un convention on the law of the sea. i welcome the decision of the un general assembly to develop, within the framework of unclos, a binding international instrument on the conservation and sustainable use of marine biodiversity in areas beyond national jurisdiction, in order to address current shortcomings. this instrument will play a key role in the conservation and sustainable use of the oceans and seas and their resources. i also support the report's call for the commission to promote and support efforts to conserve marine protected areas, which can only be achieved with the widest possible involvement of stakeholders.
in writing. ‒ marine activities are developing and multiplying at a rapid pace, so that the pressure to maintain and conserve marine biodiversity is increasing. i voted for the document.
in writing. ‒ today's decision concerns a very important report in this field, one could say a uniform regulation on livestock farming. the report is complementary in that it harmonises the breeding of cattle, sheep, goats, pigs and horses, the marketing of their breeding material and the breeding programme for each species within the eu, which had previously been the responsibility of the member states. improving the genetic performance of livestock farming is more successful when more individuals are carriers of genetic diversity in the population. thus, the uniform treatment of breeding material for breeding animals at eu level helps farmers to select the most appropriate genetic stock for their breeding purposes, which directly affects their livelihood. despite all these positives, i abstained from the final vote, as the majority decided by a separate vote not to exclude any discrimination against third country propagating material. this is risky, as no eu-compatible regulation is in place, which is particularly dangerous in the light of the free trade agreement currently under negotiation with the us.
in writing. ‒ i shall vote in favour of the parliament's position. we ask the commission to refer the matter back to parliament if it intends to substantially amend its proposal or to replace it with another text. the main objective of the single market is to bring together all the directives on the technical regulation of the various animal breeds into a single legal text. the commission's efforts in this area should be supported, but certain provisions should be adapted to encourage free trade in agricultural products within the union. in addition, the concept of 'species', 'breeding programme', 'protection programme' and 'threatening of the conservation or genetic diversity of a species' are missing, which are key to the interpretation of the regulation.
in writing. ‒ the commission has presented a proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on the conditions governing intra-union trade in and imports into the union of breeding animals and their germinal products. the commission intends to consolidate in a single legal text all the directives aimed at regulating the breeding techniques of the various animal species in the form of this regulation, with a view to achieving a single market in this field. the commission proposes a harmonised structure for livestock farming, which will have a significant impact on the animal genetics sector in europe, beyond merely consolidating and simplifying the texts. the committee on agriculture and rural development supports this general approach in its report, but considers that some issues need to be defined more precisely or reviewed. it therefore proposes that parliament adopt the commission's draft with almost 200 amendments. i supported the motion.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report, which improves and supports the commission proposal in the single framework on the principles of breeding, trade and import of bovine, porcine, ovine, caprine and equine animals and, to a lesser extent, other animal species. i agree that the rearing of these animals occupies a strategic place in the eu's agriculture from an economic and social point of view. i share the view that livestock farming, in addition to ensuring food security and creating jobs in the union, is also essential for the conservation of biodiversity. the report highlights that the survival of local varieties could be threatened in the absence of maintaining adequate numbers, which would be a loss in terms of genetic diversity. i believe that animal health and welfare are aspects that all operators in the breeding technology sector should take into account, in particular with regard to improving the genetic stock of breeds. cross-border cooperation between breeding and hybrid breeding organisations should be promoted, while ensuring freedom of establishment and removing obstacles to the free trade in breeding animals and their germinal products. europe - and hungary among them - has a rich local animal breed and genetic population, which breeding organisations and cooperatives play a central role in preserving and improving. i therefore believe that we need to protect their activities on the basis of clear, uniform principles.
in writing. ‒ the eu's breeding legislation aims to encourage free trade within the union and facilitate the import of breeding animals and their germinal products, ensuring that breeding programmes and programmes for the conservation of genetic resources in europe are maintained. i supported the relevant document.

in writing. ‒ the single market is a key tool for boosting economic growth and job creation in the union. a single market that does not place too much burden on or jeopardise production, innovation and trade is a tool to bring back jobs and growth to europe that would have been possible elsewhere. however, the report of the committee on the internal market and consumer protection concludes that the single market for goods has been achieved but not for services; more than 20 years after its formal establishment, the single market is still in tatters, in particular because member states have not fully transposed or correctly implemented eu legislation. it stresses that improving the single market does not mean removing all rules, nor does it mean reducing the level of regulation, but rather eliminating unnecessary regulation and negative effects. it points out that single market legislation should take into account the new opportunities offered by the digital revolution and be consistent with the e-government dimension. i voted in favour of the draft resolution.

in writing. ‒ i voted against the report on improving the single market regulation because it does not represent the direction needed to strengthen the single market. however, it is appropriate to treat the improvement of the single market regulation as a priority and a shared responsibility of the eu institutions, as recommended in the report. as the report points out, we need to aim for regulation that benefits citizens, thus contributing to improving competitiveness, job creation and the development of smes, while ensuring a high level of consumer protection. the commission should continue its efforts and regularly update its regulatory guidance to meet the challenges of the digital age. despite my negative vote, i share the rapporteur's concern that europeans have very little information about the services and organisations that help them exercise their consumer rights. the commission and the member states should play a more active role in promoting such tools, while also examining the effectiveness of the services.
in writing. ‒ improving the single market is a shared responsibility of all the institutions of the european union. this is the concept under which the european union is seeking to improve the regulation of the single market. it means a shared responsibility to respect the principle of subsidiarity when deciding whether action is needed; to be able to decide on the most appropriate action if regulation is needed; and finally to ensure that the measures and obligations developed are simple and are applied effectively and efficiently to achieve the policy objectives pursued. i voted in favour of the report.

in writing. ‒ the european union is facing new challenges today, so it is more important than ever that schools and the public debate about the european union, its values, and the benefits and system of european integration. the current lack of knowledge among eu citizens about the european union and the functioning of its institutions is shown by the eurobarometer spring 2014 survey: 44% of eu citizens do not understand how the union works. it is no wonder that citizens feel alienated from the union and increasingly turn their backs on its policies and projects. we can improve this by providing citizens with better information at school age. one way to do this is to increase the eu dimension of school education, which can prepare citizens to live in an increasingly complex and globalised world. i am convinced that in today's europe there is an even greater need to know the founding pillars and values of the european union, and that knowledge and understanding of the history and values of the union and its member states are key to further peaceful coexistence, mutual understanding, tolerance and solidarity. in line with the position of the fidesz-kdnp group, i voted in favour of the adoption of the report.
in writing. ‒ eu citizens in general currently have little knowledge of the european union and its institutions, and feel distant from brussels and the eu institutions. this can be changed by improving the information available to citizens, and one of the key ways of doing this is to increase the eu dimension of school education. the european dimension of the ncps is often too general, making it difficult for learners to get a comprehensive picture of the union. given its impact on citizens' daily lives, the union should be given greater visibility in educational materials, at all levels and in all forms of education. examples should be sought to illustrate the role of the eu in the daily lives of learners. the opportunities offered by union programmes in the fields of education and culture should be exploited at european level to promote language skills, active citizenship, cultural sensitivity and intercultural understanding. wider access to mobility opportunities provided by these programmes is essential to ensure and increase the civic awareness and civic participation of the younger generation.

in writing. ‒ the european union has been going through a serious economic and financial crisis in recent years, the social and political effects of which are calling into question the legitimacy of the institutions and the common values of the union, and with them the notion of a european identity. in this respect, it is more important than ever that citizens regain their faith in the benefits and necessity of the european integration process. by comparison, only 42.61% of eu citizens and only 27.8% of 18-24 year olds voted in the last european parliament elections, the lowest turnout since 1979. according to a 2014 eurobarometer survey, 44% of eu citizens feel that their knowledge of how the eu works is limited, and 52% feel that their opinion does not matter in the union. the report by the committee on culture and education points out that a lack of knowledge about the union can create a sense of democratic deficit and lead to a widespread euroscepticism in the member states. however, increasing the eu dimension of school education can help to overcome euroscepticism. the report states that under the conditions created by the maastricht treaty, which places the content of the curriculum and the organisation of the education system under the exclusive competence of the member states and explicitly excludes the coordination of national laws and regulations, how can the strengthening of the eu dimension of school education be achieved? i voted for the resolution.

in writing. ‒ the eu unemployment rate remained at 10.2% in 2014 and youth unemployment stood at 22.1%. meanwhile, there is a structural labour shortage in the labour market, as indicated by a high vacancy rate. the differences in this area are huge between european regions: in some, the real rate is close to zero, while in others unemployment has stabilised above 40% among younger people, many of whom have not been able to obtain a secondary education or a vocational qualification. genuine mobility opportunities are therefore an essential part of any overall strategy to boost the economy and reduce youth unemployment. the replacement of the previously separate programmes by erasmus+ has represented a significant step forward in the understanding of the concept of mobility in relation to the european higher education area. however, while the earlier leonardo programme successfully implemented the first phase of the introduction of exchanges with countries other than the country of residence and of linked learning-work periods, the single structure of erasmus+ and, since 2008, the consequences of the economic crisis have exposed the structural weaknesses of programmes for mobility linking learning and work. the report of the committee on culture and education takes account of the areas of the erasmus+ programme which, if given greater quantitative and qualitative characteristics, could provide an answer to this problem. i supported the bill.

in writing. ‒ the report of the economic and monetary committee is ruthlessly honest about the consequences of the lack of unified representation of the eu and the euro area in the various international financial organisations. in this way, europe's effective influence in the international institutions that ensure the stability of the financial system is significantly undermined. the strategic importance of the financial sector for growth and jobs requires a rethinking of multilateral global cooperation, reinforcing the weight of the eu and the euro area, and this requires a unified representation of member states in international financial organisations. the implementation of this would be a major step towards a federal europe, which is why i strongly supported the draft resolution.

member of the commission.– madam president, thank you for the opportunity to add a short comment in response to your questions about money laundering. you are right that we have to put in place a number of measures to ensure that authorities have stronger powers to fight money laundering and that suspect transactions are reported to them. as you know, we have already achieved considerable results with the fourth anti—money laundering directive, adopted in december 2014, which, among other things, provides for the setting-up of central registers of beneficial ownership. it now awaits speedy transposition and implementation by the member states, which is crucial because it has to be brought to life. the registers should be set up by the end of 2016. the commission is prepared to provide all necessary support for this transposition, and i am keeping actively in touch with my counterparts in the member states on this issue. you are also right that the commission is now working on the revision of this directive. as announced in the action plan on terrorist financing, the revising proposal should be submitted on 1 june; it is focused primarily on addressing risks posed by terrorist financing, and especially on anonymous payments and the like, given that, according to security experts, financial transactions are very often the first indications that terrorist attacks are being prepared. so we need to tackle this issue. finally, as also announced in the action plan, the commission will take forward a legislative proposal harmonising money laundering-related criminal offences and penalties.

rapporteur.– mr president, first of all let me thank all of you for being present at this late hour. i especially appreciate the vice-president/high representative being present here. her stamina and perseverance is actually both admirable and indeed exceptional in these long foreign policy debates. today we have already discussed a number of pressing problems, deadly crises, complex policy problems and precarious situations around the world. the region that we are going to talk about in the last item on today’s agenda, central asia, may not seem to require such urgent attention. it may not produce a pressing demand on our resources, but it is – and this is one of the most important conclusions of the report – a region of increasing strategic importance to the european union. as rapporteur on the implementation and review of the eu-central asia strategy, the first fact that i have learned from my colleagues is that we all agree on the growing relevance of the region to the european union. so this debate comes last, but not least, on today’s foreign policy agenda. first of all, allow me to express my sincere gratitude to the shadow rapporteurs, whose dedication, flexibility and professionalism resulted in the rich – and indeed not very short – text. i am also grateful to the various representatives of the european external action service (eeas), who proved to be very helpful throughout the entire process. let me start with the observation that the central asia strategy, as formulated nine years ago, had the right level of ambition. the achievements of the implementation were rather less spectacular though. that limited success requires that all parties involved – the eu, the member states and the five countries of central asia – need to make a serious and concerted effort to reach the aims laid down in the various official documents and treaties which we have with the region. we agree on a number of points within parliament on the strategy review. for instance, we also see a need for a more differentiated, conditional and incentive—based approach, and it should be applied so that regional programmes are more tailored to the needs of the interested parties within the region, not necessarily comprising the entire set of five countries. central asia has weak interregional links. some would even doubt whether it is a region in its own right. it would make sense to develop projects aimed at those countries which are willing to participate and willing to foster these kinds of links. we emphasise that the disbursement of eu funds should be incentive- and performance-based and that benchmarks should be developed for each and every country. these need to be formulated to assess their progress. the key areas include, among others (and i am sure my colleagues would list more than these) democratisation, fighting and preventing corruption, free and fair elections, ending drug trafficking, respecting labour laws and so on. the countries of the region need to develop their human rights records. some indeed seem to be inhospitable terrain for even the basic political rights. because of the precariousness of the human rights situation in some countries of the region, we urge the eeas to base their assessments not on the laws enacted but on the facts established on the ground. for such a strategy to become viable we need a unified approach. this is not the first or the last time that we have said that. we need to speak with one voice, together with the member states. no bilateral negotiations should undermine our efforts.
