mr president the eu-turkey agreement is the final outcome of the legal arrival of migrants in the european union. the eu leaders say there are good migrants and bad migrants. a bad migrant is one who arrives in greece on a ferry without proper travel documents, and is sent back. but the one who is sent to europe by turkey with this contingent is a good migrant. i ask them: will they fit into european societies? aren't they going to build a parallel society? are there any terrorists? there are no guarantees. this agreement fulfils the vision of president juncker, who made it clear in a speech here in parliament that europe needs immigrants, and cited australia and canada as examples. mrs zimmer just said that we are the european union. no, in a democracy we are not the european union, we are the people of the european union. but the majority of them do not want to make europe a continent of immigrants. thank you very much.
madam president, i have to ask you to leave. we're having another emotional argument i don't know how many times. if a voter asked me how many times we've discussed this issue, i couldn't tell you. are we effective? i ask the question. part of it is... we're talking about a delicate compromise that was born at the right time. of course, there is always room for improvement, but in the circumstances it was the right decision to go through the western balkans route without checks. the decision to close the route to human traffickers was also a good one. and the right decision was made to restore order and control at the borders. the decision was made for the safety of 500 million european union citizens. yes, greece's burdens have continued to grow, so it is right that we help to solve the burdens and bear the burdens. look at this compromise: the agreement is not perfect, of course. the turks are not sure they want to and can keep the deal. so we have to check, we have to check all the time. president erdogan had an interesting statement about whether they can actually keep this agreement. but look to the future. and the future is about hotspots not working, it's about the registration system needing to be overhauled, it's about the education system not working, the health care system not working. this is the future of europe.
in writing. i am very grateful that the recent decisions of the european council, based on the commission's concrete proposals, and the agreement with the turkish government with all its political contradictions, which have received a lot of political support are bringing a real european solution to the refugee crisis at last within sight. however, it should be stressed that this is only an initial effort and that the comprehensive solution must include the strengthening of the schengen system, the complete transformation of the dublin system and the introduction of effective relocation and resettlement practices applicable to all member states. at the same time, i would like to draw the attention of the representatives of the commission and the council to the fact that millions of european citizens are not affected by the important decisions of 17 and 18 march, precisely because of the hypocritical policies of their own governments and leaders. mostly in hungary, where government propaganda and anti-foreigner incitement are being carried out specifically against the decisions of the european council, while the orbán regime is organizing a self-affirming referendum against european decisions that do not actually exist. such irresponsible policies may be seen as marginal and temporary, but in reality they could distort the perception of the population of these member states about refugees, the image of europe for decades, while also jeopardising the urgent renewal of european migration policy. i believe that not only the authority of the european council but the very meaning of the european decision-making system will be called into question if the responsible leaders of the european institutions and the other member states are unable to deal with this anomaly.
in writing. ‒ the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) aims to support the reintegration into the labour market of workers and self-employed persons made redundant as a result of globalisation, as a result of major structural changes in world trade patterns, or as a result of the prolongation of the global financial and economic crisis or a new global financial and economic crisis. sweden has submitted an application to mobilise the egf, under the reference number egf/2015/009 se/volvo trucks, for a financial contribution from the egf. the committee considered that the application met the requirements of the relevant regulation and therefore i voted in favour of the adoption of the proposal.
in writing. ‒ on 16 february 2016, the commission adopted a proposal for a decision to mobilise the european globalisation adjustment fund for sweden to support the reintegration into the labour market of workers made redundant by five companies operating primarily in the upper norrland region of sweden. this appropriation is intended to cover the financing of the expenditure of the european school in brussels. the request concerns 500 workers made redundant. the personalised services to be provided to redundant workers include the following measures: various job search activities and coaching, entrepreneurship and start-up support, education and training, help in finding a job with private sector providers, job search support. the request was lodged with the commission on 16 september 2015 and supplemented by additional information until 11 november 2015. the commission has concluded that the application meets the conditions for a financial contribution from the european globalisation adjustment fund, in accordance with the relevant provisions of the egf regulation. on the basis of the above, i voted in favour of the adoption of the report.

in writing. ‒ the european globalisation adjustment fund was established to provide additional support to workers affected by the consequences of major structural changes in world trade. the fund shall be managed by the commission in accordance with the principles laid down in the staff regulations of officials of the european union and in the conditions of employment of other servants of the european union. the corresponding amounts shall be entered as a reserve in the general budget of the union. the main objective is to support the reintegration of workers affected or made redundant as a result of major structural changes in world trade. parliament has repeatedly stressed the need to improve the added value, efficiency and employability of the egf as a union instrument to support workers made redundant. the parliament's resolution stresses the importance of general awareness of the egf and the visibility of the fund. i voted for the resolution.
in writing. ‒ the european globalisation adjustment fund aims to provide additional support to workers affected by the consequences of major structural changes in world trade. the fund shall not exceed a maximum annual amount of eur 150 million in 2011 prices. on 16 september 2015, sweden submitted an application to mobilise the fund, for an amount of eur 1 793 710, in respect of redundancies at the umeå site of volvo group truck operation emea, involving 470 workers, and at four supply and downstream companies (il logistics ab, lemia, caverion and isringhausen), involving 177 workers. the commission has concluded that the application fulfils the conditions laid down in article 4 (1) (a) of the egf regulation and that sweden is therefore eligible for the aid requested. it also concluded that the application meets the requirements for determining the financial contribution from the egf as laid down in article 13 of regulation (eu) no 1309/2013 and therefore proposed to the parliament and the council a decision authorising the mobilisation of eur 1 793 710 from the european globalisation adjustment fund. in its report, the committee on budgets proposes that parliament adopt the commission's proposal and, on the basis of the request submitted by sweden, make a contribution to the mobilisation of the egf of eur 1 793 710. i supported the motion.
in writing. ‒ the european globalisation adjustment fund was established to provide additional support to workers affected by the consequences of major structural changes in world trade. this is the second application to be examined under the 2016 budget and the 22nd for the production of motor vehicles, trailers and semi-trailers and is for the mobilisation of a total of eur 1 793 710 from the egf for the benefit of sweden. the request concerns 500 workers made redundant. i supported him with my vote.
in writing. ‒ i believe that networking and the exchange of information on the egf play an important role in the effective use of the egf, and therefore support the funding of the expert group of the egf contacts and the networking seminars on the implementation of the egf. i expect that this exchange of information will contribute to a better and more detailed analysis of the success rate of measures financed by the egf and, in particular, the re-employment rate of beneficiaries in the member states. it is important not only to make decisions on the use of the fund that appear to be well-founded, but also to monitor the effectiveness of their implementation. these assessments could form the basis for the assessment of future requests to the ep.
in writing. ‒ on 22 february 2016, the commission adopted a new proposal for a decision to mobilise the european globalisation adjustment fund. the proposal is to mobilise eur 380 000 from the fund for technical assistance to the commission. the technical assistance shall be aimed at financing the supervision, the information and knowledge platform and the advice to be provided to member states on the use, monitoring and evaluation of the european globalisation adjustment fund. article 11 (1) of the egf regulation provides that, on the initiative of the commission, 0,5% of the annual ceiling of the egf (i.e. eur 828 060 in 2016) may be used for technical assistance each year. the amount of assigned revenue in accordance with article 21 (3) of the financial regulation is estimated at eur 100000. on the basis of the above, i voted in favour of the adoption of the report.

in writing. ‒ the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) was established to provide additional support to workers affected by the consequences of major structural changes in world trade. the fund shall not exceed the maximum annual amount of eur 150 million as provided for in article 12 of regulation (eu, euratom) no 1311/2011 of the european parliament and of the council of 12 december 2011 laying down the multiannual financial framework for the years 2014 to 2020 (6) and in article 15 of regulation (eu) no 1309/2013 of the european parliament and of the council (7). the corresponding amounts shall be entered as a reserve in the general budget of the union. sweden has submitted an application to mobilise the egf, in particular in respect of redundancies in the nace revision 2 sector (manufacture and conversion of motor vehicles and trailers) in the nuts ii region of upper norrland (se33). of the 647 redundant workers eligible for egf contribution, 500 are expected to participate, as 470 of these workers lost their jobs as a result of the reduction of the workforce at the volvo group truck operation emea plant in umeå and another 177 at four suppliers and a downstream company. however, the support from the egf shall not replace measures which are the responsibility of undertakings under national law or collective agreements, or measures aimed at restructuring undertakings or sectors. i welcome the measures taken by sweden in respect of workers made redundant and i support mr negrescu's report with my vote.
in writing. ‒ the european globalisation adjustment fund aims to provide additional support to workers affected by the consequences of major structural changes in world trade. the fund shall not exceed a maximum annual amount of eur 150 million in 2011 prices. on 22 february 2016, the commission presented to the parliament and the council a proposal for a decision to mobilise eur 380 000 from the fund for technical assistance. the amount requested is intended to finance the following activities: monitoring and data collection, information, creation of a knowledge base and application platform, administrative and technical support, organisation of a seminar, evaluation. the report of the committee on budgets states that, under regulation (eu) no 1309/2013, a maximum of 0,5% of the annual ceiling of the egf may be mobilised each year for technical assistance at the initiative of the commission. takes note that the commission has not yet adopted a decision on the application of the union's financial contribution for the period 2014-2020; i voted accordingly.

in writing. ‒ the report concerns the establishment of a new instrument for the provision of emergency assistance within the union for the financial year 2016 of the european union. the report concludes that the emergency situation created by the mass influx of refugees and migrants into europe is beyond the capacity of the member states most affected to respond, and that at the same time there is no adequate tool at eu level to address the situation within the union. in particular, there is a need to reinforce the staff of the european counter-terrorism centre within europol, in view of the current security situation in the european union. the council has presented a draft amending budget aimed at creating the budgetary structure for the instrument concerned by means of a transfer within chapter 3 of the multiannual financial framework. the transfer will provide the new facility with a commitment appropriation of eur 100 million and a payment appropriation of eur 80,2 million to meet immediate funding needs. the report is to be supported, but the source of the money is still up for debate. it seems appropriate to implement the new instrument not at the expense of the flexibility framework but to transfer it from less important sites. this argument is also to be supported because the flexibility instrument is not a permanent task but is intended to finance exceptional cases, while immigration will unfortunately not be an exceptional but a permanent situation.
in writing. ‒ the report proposes to accept without amendment the european commission's proposal, which has two main elements: the creation of a new budgetary structure for the eu emergency fund, with a commitment of eur 100 million and a transfer of eur 80.2 million in payments under budget chapter 3, and the strengthening of the european counter-terrorism centre within europol. given that draft amending budget no 1/2016 is in line with the financial annex to the adopted regulation on humanitarian aid within the union and that the funds to be mobilised are set aside from chapter 3, i voted in favour of the adoption of the report.

in writing. ‒ the report is correct that the mass influx of refugees and migrants into europe exceeds the capacity of the member states most affected to respond, and that there is no adequate eu-wide tool to deal with the situation. it is now clear that the eu has been wrong about the migration issue, as evidenced by the attacks carried out by people who returned to europe as migrants, with combat experience and terrorist training. there has to be some way to finance a way out of the impasse, to resolve the situation that has arisen, or at least to manage the situation.
in writing. ‒ on 2 march 2016, the commission presented a proposal for a council regulation to create the missing means to address humanitarian needs within the union. on 15 march 2016, the council adopted regulation (eu) 2016/369 and presented draft amending budget no 1/2016 providing for a commitment appropriation of eur 100 million and a payment appropriation of eur 80,2 million for immediate financing needs related to regulation 2016/369. the commission has also identified a number of specific areas where the union should be able to contribute to the implementation of the union's macro-financial assistance. in its report, the committee on budgets recommends that parliament welcome the commission's proposal to allow emergency support from the union budget to address the humanitarian consequences of the current refugee crisis within the union, approve the draft amending budget no 1/2016 of the council and confirm that, in view of the urgency of the situation, it is ready to accept it in the form submitted by the commission. i voted in favour of the committee on budgets' proposal.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution which, on the basis of a proposal from the european commission and a council resolution, allows for the immediate establishment of a new ad-hoc mechanism to deal with the impact of the refugee crisis. in making my decision, i considered the serious humanitarian situation created by the influx of refugees into europe, as well as the recent eu-turkey agreement, which creates further urgent needs for supplies and funding. the new mechanism will allow for the reallocation of budgetary resources of eur 300 million this year and an additional eur 200 million in 2017-18, while i am reassured by the commitment in the resolution that the commission will not make this a burden on the eu's external humanitarian aid framework. i also regard as important the commission's commitment that the staff of eu organisations dealing with refugees and counter-terrorism will not be subject to any future reduction in costs or staffing requirements, and that the staff of the european counter-terrorism centre at europol will be increased. however, i agree with the rapporteurs i do not agree that this new emergency mechanism, as proposed by the commission, does not fit into a comprehensive strategy on asylum and migration, and that this also undermines the decision-making rights of the european parliament; i am confident that this shortcoming will be remedied once the most urgent crisis situations have been addressed.

in writing. ‒ the committee on the environment, public health and food safety of which i am a member has lodged an objection to the commission's draft implementing regulation concerning the placing on the market of plant protection products containing the active substance glyphosate. in this regulation, the european commission intends to extend the authorisation of these substances for a maximum of 15 years. in march 2015, the international agency for research on cancer classified glyphosate as a substance likely to cause cancer in humans. in addition, glyphosate has endocrine disrupting properties. however, the european food safety authority has concluded that glyphosate is unlikely to be a carcinogen to humans. in this unclear but worrying situation, the committee, in its motion for a resolution, called on the commission to withdraw its draft implementing regulation and to submit a new proposal, in accordance with the precautionary principle. the parliament's plenary session amended the proposal on a number of points and fixed the period of authorisation for a further seven years subject to the fulfilment of other conditions. that is an unacceptably long period of time in my judgment. nevertheless, i supported the amended proposal in the final vote because, if it had not been accepted, the original decision of the commission, which was unconditional, would have remained in force for 15 years.
in writing. ‒ a number of research findings of concern have emerged regarding the carcinogenic potential of the pesticide glyphosate and therefore increased vigilance should be exercised when renewing the union authorisation of the active substance. of all the herbicides, glyphosate is currently the most popular drug in the world, with global use increasing dramatically over the past 40 years. the problem is that this plant protection product can be used by almost anyone in many member states, from large-scale farming to forestry to hobby gardening, without the appropriate qualification and restrictions on use. in my view, the compromise proposed by the ppe group is capable of striking a proper balance between the concerns of european citizens and the legitimate interests of farmers. the adopted amendment proposes that the european commission should renew the marketing authorisation for glyphosate for only 7 years instead of 15 years, subject to strict restrictions on use, with a professional qualification. in parallel, it should ensure that the toxicity of glyphosate is independently reviewed for its carcinogenicity and endocrine-disrupting properties. it should be noted that the authorisation may be withdrawn at any time should new evidence on the safety of the product become available in the meantime. the inclusion of all these safeguards could lead to the sustainable use of glyphosate in europe, which is already a common practice in hungary.

in writing. ‒ glyphosate is a non-selective herbicide, and global use has increased 260-fold in the last 40 years. the international agency for research on cancer (iarc) classified glyphosate as a substance likely to cause cancer in humans in march 2015, while the european food safety authority (efsa) concluded in november 2015 that glyphosate is not likely to be carcinogenic to humans. the commission, in its draft implementing regulation renewing the approval of the active substance glyphosate in accordance with regulation (ec) no 1107/2009 of the european parliament and of the council concerning the placing of plant protection products on the market, and amending the annex to implementing regulation (eu) no 540/2011 ('the draft implementing regulation'), proposes to approve glyphosate until 30 june 2031. the committee on the environment, public health and food safety recommends that parliament declare that the draft implementing regulation does not ensure a high level of protection of human and animal health and the environment and exceeds the implementing powers provided for in regulation (ec) no 1107/2009. it is therefore appropriate to withdraw the draft implementing regulation and to submit a new draft not renewing the approval of glyphosate. it also calls on the commission and efsa to publish without delay the scientific evidence on which the positive classification and proposed re-approval of glyphosate is based. i voted in favour of the draft resolution.

in writing. ‒ the report of the committee on foreign affairs takes the view that the multiplicity and simultaneity of crises shows that no single member state can respond alone, and that europeans must jointly guarantee their own security. it states that threats to member states must be considered as threats to the union itself, that the borders of the member states are the borders of the union and must be protected as such. this requires strong unity and solidarity among member states and requires a consistent common foreign and security policy. it points out that in the future, the member states of the european union will have to act more unitedly and prepare to take on greater responsibility for their common security and territorial defence, relying less on the united states. it considers it a key objective to move towards permanent multinational joint military units, joint defence forces and the establishment of a common defence policy, which will eventually lead to a common defence. it calls for the establishment of a permanent eu high command to improve military crisis management capability and provide emergency response. finally, it called on the european union and its member states to strengthen defence capabilities and to make full use of the provisions of the lisbon treaty in the area of the common security and defence policy. i voted in favour of the draft resolution.

in writing. ‒ the world health organisation (who) declared the zika virus outbreak a public health emergency of international concern in a statement on 1 february 2016, announcing that a cause and effect relationship between zika virus infection during pregnancy and microcephaly is highly likely, although this is still pending scientific proof. several european countries have reported cases of infection caused by the introduced zika virus: on 11 february 2016, the european centre for disease prevention and control (ecdc) reported a case of microcephaly in a pregnant woman from slovenia, where the zika virus infection occurred during the pregnant woman's stay in brazil. the report of the committee on the environment, public health and food safety takes account of the options and actions that the european authorities can take to prevent the introduction of the zika virus into europe and the spread of infection in europe. it also places a strong emphasis on what the eu can do to help the competent authorities in different regions of the world, in particular in the outbreak areas in the north-east of brazil, to combat and eradicate the further spread of the outbreak. i voted in favour of the draft resolution.
in writing. ‒ i supported the motion on the zika virus epidemic because i believe we need to raise awareness of all the challenges to public health. this virus is transmitted to humans by the bite of certain mosquitoes and causes small- headedness in newborns, among others. it is important to note that the same mosquito is the carrier of dengue, chikungunya, and yellow fever. i believe that this is why we need to put a strong emphasis on scientific research, development and prevention. more so, since the infection can easily spread to europe. rapid testing, treatment and vaccination are needed to prevent the spread of the epidemic. the european union already has a health protection tool, namely the early warning and response system (ewrs). in order to ensure that this system is fully effective, its functioning needs to be continuously reviewed. in addition to zika virus, the proposal also addresses the link between the occurrence of smallpox in brazil and the larvicide piriproxifen, which was introduced into the drinking water system in 2014 in the affected areas of brazil, according to argentine and brazilian researchers. i think that this element should not be ignored, and we should also call attention to the unreasonable use of chemicals.
in writing. ‒ zika virus is a newly emerging mosquito-borne virus first identified in 1947 in the zika forest in uganda through a yellow fever monitoring network in rhesus monkeys. the zika virus outbreak highlighted the inequalities in the countries affected, including in terms of public health systems and living conditions, disproportionately affecting the poorest members of society, who often live near open water sources and are not adequately equipped to prevent and combat the disease. i supported him with my vote.

in writing. on 15 february, bosnia and herzegovina submitted its application to join the eu, the only former yugoslav member state to do so, ahead of kosovo. it is noteworthy that the european commission has for the first time given a more positive assessment of bosnia and herzegovina's ambitions than in previous years. however, it is not disputed that the accession process is hampered by several factors. bosnia and herzegovina has a number of problems to overcome before full membership. the main requirements for accession include reform of the public administration, the establishment of an independent judiciary, economic growth and social justice, and, perhaps most importantly, the development of a coordination mechanism for cooperation between the two parts of the country and the brcko district in order to join the union. it is also necessary to amend the discriminatory electoral law against the non-national minorities of the three constituent states. the submission of the application for membership in february was historic, giving bosnia an opportunity to accelerate the process of economic and political stabilisation and to embark on the path of accession supported by its citizens. i am therefore confident that, 21 years after the dayton peace agreement, genuine reforms will help to accelerate the process of integration of bosnia and herzegovina into the european union. i believe that supporting bosnia and herzegovina's european union perspective is also key to a united europe.
rapporteur.– mr president, i think the topic we are going to discuss at this early hour on the last day of our part session this week is very important. first of all, allow me to thank everybody who has contributed to the work, especially the shadow rapporteurs, who have been very helpful, very flexible and very professional in working out a text which i believe can command a fairly large consensus in the house. this was not very easy to achieve. it was very important that the shadows put their work and their commitment into the whole topic. although i am listed as the author, i have to thank all my colleagues in my group and especially my advisers, who helped considerably in putting together a text which has a chance of passing, and which i hope will pass on the vote today. we are not getting any closer to the 2020 anti-poverty target. we are actually, by all important measurements, further away from the 2020 anti-poverty targets than when they were originally formulated. this is only partly due to the financial crisis of 2008 – after all, we are in the ninth year after the crisis – so we have a basic structural problem. the report is not on that, but one of the key elements in this attempt to reduce poverty in the european union is related to basic resources, household costs and household expenditure. i believe that, fundamentally, energy and water are essential resources which are necessary for the survival of any household in the european union. they are essential especially because we are more and more dependent, individually and in groups, on energy. at the same time, energy prices have been continually rising in the last almost half a decade, which makes the problem more serious than we would have thought at the time when the anti-poverty target was put together. at the time when this was formulated there was a widespread consensus that poverty is a complex global phenomenon which requires complex global treatment. so some of my colleagues, with an honest conviction, thought that selecting a particular type of poverty from the complex web of poverty might be a mistake. i would like to defend the view that energy poverty, or fuel poverty, is one of the most important elements in this, because it usually requires an upfront investment. simple direct income support is not going to help those who are in this trap, because it requires an upfront investment. that is why what we are asking for primarily is to have a complex policy set which simultaneously attacks all the three elements of energy poverty, one of them being insufficient income, another being energy efficiency – basically the quality of the housing stock in much of europe. eastern europe is significantly different in this respect to western europe. in eastern europe we do not have a meaningful social housing system, and that contributes to, and exacerbates, the problem. finally, i would like to mention that we believe that a winter disconnection moratorium on heating is a must. nobody should die in europe because of not having heating available.
on behalf of the verts/ale group - mr president! there is a very important report on the table in parliament today. in europe, the number of citizens affected by energy poverty is estimated to be between 50 and 120 million. energy poverty can take different forms in different member states, which is why well-targeted, well-designed european measures are needed, and equally, national measures are needed to eliminate or reduce energy poverty in europe. the social instruments have been discussed a lot, and i have to say that the most important thing about the various social transfers is that they are properly targeted, that the aid from public funds reaches those who really need it. equally important are the safeguards that the report includes: eviction restrictions and other tools to help prevent european citizens and families from being put in an impossible situation. but in the long run, we have one coherent, sustainable, effective way to reduce energy poverty, and that is not by helping to reduce it or paying the bills out of public money, but by reducing energy use, and that is by providing the right forms of financing to help citizens access energy efficiency and renewable resources.

rapporteur.– mr president, i would like to assure the commissioner that as long as the house passes this report, she can count on my cooperation with her at any time on any elements of the question. this was indeed a rich and thoughtful debate. i regularly learn a lot in this house, and this was one of those occasions. i would like to thank everyone who contributed. there is only one element that i would like to raise from the report, which has not been directly addressed so far, which is that on the energy poverty side we have a clear technical problem: we do not have a common definition. i would very much like the house to understand that, without having a common definition with which we can compare the situation across the board, we are not going to be able to tackle the problem seriously. it is the necessary beginning of the long, hard work that is needed on this. i would say to my colleague from the efdd, who may already have left, that he might have been less surprised by the tone and the elements of this report had he been consulting his group’s own shadow rapporteur, who did not find elements of the text to be part of a communist manifesto. i would also say to my colleague, mrs morvai, that we agree that austerity measures do contribute to poverty, but such austerity measures are introduced and actually practised at member state level. it is member state governments which are responsible for the austerity measures most of the time. therefore, much of the increase in poverty is also the responsibility of the member states’ governments. thank you again for your contributions. i hope that you will vote for the report in plenary.
in writing. the european parliament blames high government expenditure for the fight against poverty, noting that only a few member states have improved poverty-related indicators. hungary is among these countries thanks to the success of its reduction of rescission and i am therefore pleased that the report, following my amendment, encourages the exchange of good practice between eu countries. by accepting my amendment, the report also asks the commission to grant member states greater flexibility in the use of the european structural and investment funds, so that they can allocate eu funds more effectively to reducing energy poverty or improving housing conditions. i should point out that in line with the report, which urges member states to support investments in renewable energy sources or energy efficiency, hungary is continuing the home heating programme, under which the ministry of national development provides non-repayable aid of huf 5 billion for the energy upgrading and renovation of family homes. i think it is important to point out that, in parallel with the reduction of the deficit, there is a need for consumption incentives to increase resources for consumer durables or for domestic tourism. it is also important that the commission works on the basis of objective data, for which it is essential to take into account the actual financial situation (housing, debts) instead of the current surveys, which are partly based on self-declaration.
in writing. the problem of energy poverty, to which the report gives a laudable amount of attention, deserves to be approached from another angle, that of fundamental rights. the process of extension of rights cannot be stopped, because economic and technological development and the modernisation of society force fundamental rights to be reconsidered and supplemented from time to time. for example, the right to vote and to stand as a candidate did not become a universally recognised fundamental right until the second half of the 20th century, even in europe. i believe it is time to recognize access to energy, clean water and the internet as a fundamental right. finland, estonia, greece, spain, france, belgium have already recognised one or the other of these as a fundamental right. this is not a matter of financial capacity, but rather of political will to expand; countries that are not at the top of the world in terms of gdp per capita, such as india, congo, bolivia or mexico, are moving in this direction. my party, the democratic coalition, has included in its program the provision of a minimum amount of energy and drinking water, as well as a minimum bandwidth of internet access free of charge to households in hungary. south africa provides 25 litres of water a day to every household free of charge, and belgium has had a law since 1997 guaranteeing free minimum water, electricity and natural gas services to all. in the near future, i intend to propose that the european union also recognise access to energy, drinking water and the internet as a fundamental right and call on member states to provide these minimum public services free of charge.

my fellow citizens! why do we need data protection? why do we need to protect privacy, privacy, privacy? that's a question a lot of people ask me these days. short story: i have heard from both men and women how ashamed they were of themselves and how humiliated they felt when it was customary to call several patients for a medical examination at once under our previous system, the so-called socialism. they had to strip in front of each other and talk about their illnesses. why was that such a big deal? well, they all have bodies, they're called identical, women have female bodies, illness is a natural thing, there's no shame in it, we might say. yet they felt, and rightly so, that their right to human dignity had been violated by the intrusion into their innermost, most intimate privacy - so to speak - by this humiliating measure. i'll take it from here in my next speech.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the adoption of the data protection package. the compromise text of the data protection dossier was formally approved by the european council on 8 april, after which it only needed to be approved by the parliament. once approved by the plenary, member states will have two years (until 2018) to transpose it into national law. these rules overwrite and modernise more than 20 years of eu data protection legislation, since at that time there was no mass internet use, no facebook, no google. the objective is to guarantee the widest possible control of individuals over their personal data, while ensuring that data processing does not hinder the development of the digital single market or the acquisition of data to counter terrorist threats. the data protection package consists of a regulation on the protection and use of personal data and a public security data protection directive, which provides for data processing to facilitate the flow of information between law enforcement and judicial bodies.
in writing. ‒ on 25 january 2012, the commission presented a proposal to replace directive 95/46/ec with a regulation establishing a general eu framework for data protection. on 12 march 2014, parliament discussed the proposal at first reading, while the belgian chamber of deputies, the german bundesrat, the french senate, the italian chamber of deputies and the swedish parliament submitted reasoned opinions to the effect that the draft legislative act is not compatible with the principle of subsidiarity. the council's position at first reading of 8 april 2016 reflects the political agreement reached between the european parliament and the council at the informal trilateral consultation of 15 december 2015. the commission agrees with the council's position at first reading. in its recommendation for second reading, the committee on civil liberties, justice and home affairs recommends that parliament endorse the position adopted by the council at first reading. i voted accordingly.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the recommendation to adopt the council position, as the political agreement approved by the council preserved the objectives of the commission proposal, which i also supported, which were primarily aimed at strengthening personal rights, consolidating the eu internal market, tightening enforcement and creating global data protection standards.
in writing. ‒ the rapporteur agrees with the position adopted by the council at first reading and notes that the legislative act was adopted in accordance with the council's position. it therefore proposes the signing of the legislative act. i supported him with my vote.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the protection of trade secrets against their unlawful acquisition, use and disclosure, a regulatory area of crucial importance for the functioning of the internal market and the eu's competitiveness. i agree with the additions which stress the importance of a balanced approach, since in addition to protecting against the unauthorised acquisition of trade secrets, it is also necessary to bear in mind that knowledge and the flow of information are the basic conditions for innovation. i also support the amendment which points out that while some member states already have legal provisions to protect against the misuse of trade secrets, some eu countries have not even defined the concept of trade secrets and have not introduced binding legislation to protect against the misuse of trade secrets. those differences hamper the effective functioning of the internal market and it is therefore necessary to define at union level the situations in which the acquisition, use and disclosure of a trade secret are lawful and those in which they are not. i also support the idea that the measures contained in the directive should not be applied in such a way as to unfairly restrict competition or impede the mobility of workers.
in writing. ‒ protection against the unauthorised acquisition, disclosure and use of trade secrets is one of the keys to ensuring a fair business environment for businesses. however, it is important to remember that the flow of knowledge and information is also essential for innovation and the creative process. companies often have a greater interest in sharing trade secrets than in keeping them secret. at the same time, transparency and access to information are also necessary for the informed design of important public policies, such as environmental, health and consumer protection. i supported him with my vote.

in writing. ‒ the report on the estimated revenue and expenditure of the european parliament for the financial year 2017 reflects the agreement reached between the bureau of the european parliament and the committee on budgets on the draft budget of the european parliament for 2017. the main points of the agreement are: to provide an additional €47.64 million in 2017 for security investments and €3.7 million for the introduction of irish as an official language; not counting the above amounts, to reduce the draft of the presidency of the european parliament by €20 million in other lines, so that the increase in the budget in 2017 compared to 2016 does not exceed 1.4%; and to introduce a new budget line in the ep budget to finance construction. on the basis of the above, i voted in favour of the adoption of the report.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on parliament's revenue and expenditure for the financial year 2017. i agree with the parts of the report that emphasise the importance of physical and cyber security, and with the request that the secretary-general provide detailed information on current and future security and cyber security measures and the distribution of their costs. i agree with the rapporteur that any security measures should be based on a clear assessment of parliament's needs and that they should be proportionate to the risks involved. i also welcome the comment on the parliament's website that it should be made more informative and user-friendly for citizens. i also welcome the proposals made under the paperless initiative, which not only increases efficiency but also has a positive economic impact.

in writing. ‒ turkey is a strategic partner of the union because of its economic and strategic location and its important role in the region, underlines the report on turkey, which was voted on today and deals with the country's progress in the european accession negotiations launched in 2005. the document also examines the commitment of the turkish authorities to reforms and their implementation in the areas of the judiciary, the rule of law and fundamental rights and freedoms. the document specifically highlights the importance of the country in dealing with the refugee and migration crisis. while supporting renewed political cooperation between the two sides in the context of the crisis, it also stresses that eu-turkey cooperation on migration should not be linked to the accession negotiations process. turkey urgently needs reforms in the areas of justice, the rule of law and human rights. the report says that turkey must respect its commitments to european integration in line with european values, guarantee fundamental rights and ensure the cultural, social and political rights of the kurdish national community. in the light of these arguments, i voted in favour of the adoption of the report.

in writing. ‒ the commission presented its 2015 report on turkey. the report of the committee on foreign affairs on the presentation recalls that turkey has committed itself to meeting the copenhagen criteria, implementing adequate and effective reforms and gradually approximating to the union acquis. in contrast, the pace of reforms has slowed in terms of political criteria and there have been significant setbacks in the areas of freedom of expression and freedom of assembly. turkey still has the highest number of imprisoned journalists in the world, and according to the freedom house ranking of press and media freedom, turkey is still considered a country with no press freedom and only partial internet freedom. the report covers the main aspects of the accession negotiations: the rule of law, democracy, respect for human rights and fundamental freedoms, the kurdish peace process and the situation in the south-east of turkey, eu-turkey cooperation in the refugee and migration crisis and progress in the negotiations on the reunification of cyprus. i supported the motion.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the adoption of the report, agreeing with its critical assessment, which is drafted with strict regard to european democratic values. it points out, inter alia, that the democratic rule of law in the sense of the copenhagen criteria has deteriorated during the more than a decade of accession negotiations between the eu and turkey. the rights of national and other minorities, women, the political opposition, and, more recently, the media critical of the government, and even the personal security of their representatives, are still severely violated. i accept, however, that this annual report, after a long absence, supports the opening of chapters 23 and 24 of the accession negotiations, since it is in these chapters that many shortcomings in the internal legal order and the judiciary can be identified. the report also gives a fair view of the important role turkey is playing in dealing with the current refugee crisis and commends the cooperation with the eu in this area. at the same time, i agree with the conclusion that the union should not, for this reason, turn a blind eye to turkey's shortcomings in democracy, the rule of law and integration preparedness.
in writing. ‒ on 3 october 2005, accession negotiations with turkey were opened, and the opening of these negotiations marks the beginning of a process based on a long and open outcome, fair and rigorous conditionality and a commitment to reform. the pace of reforms has slowed down in terms of political criteria and there have been significant setbacks in the areas of freedom of expression and freedom of assembly. i voted in favour of the s&d group's position.

in writing. ‒ i have given my assent to the motion for a resolution of the european parliament on the 2015 albanian country report. albania has made steady progress towards accession to the union. i welcome the country's efforts to reform key areas. these include reform of public administration and efforts to combat discrimination against vulnerable groups. however, they must implement a substantial reform of the judiciary. we must support albania by all means possible, because the goal is to achieve eu accession, which will lead to further stability in the western balkans. first of all, in order to implement the reforms, we call on all political parties to make further efforts to initiate a more constructive and genuine political dialogue.
in writing. ‒ the presentation of the 2015 report on albania by the committee on foreign affairs states that although albania has made steady progress towards eu accession, there are still problems that need to be resolved quickly and effectively in order to make further progress. it urges, in particular, an increase in reform efforts in the areas of the rule of law, judicial reform, the fight against corruption and organised crime, public administration reform and fundamental rights. notes that there is a political consensus on the eu accession process and that it enjoys broad public support in albania; welcomes the commitment to comprehensive and in-depth judicial reform and the adoption of the public administration and public finance reform strategy. it remains concerned about widespread corruption, condemns the ill-treatment of suspects in the police, the overcrowding of prisons, and the inadequate medical care and poor conditions in detention facilities, and warns that institutional mechanisms for protecting children's rights remain inadequate. stresses the importance of professional, independent and versatile public service broadcasting and privately owned media; is concerned about the widespread self-censorship among journalists, who are sometimes physically prevented from reporting on certain events; i voted for the motion.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the adoption of the annual report on albania, with particular appreciation for the fact that albania, perhaps the furthest-reaching country in the western balkans' accession process to the european union, is now one of our most promising partners as a candidate country. in my opinion, the work of the european parliament's rapporteur reflects precisely the responsible approach which, by confirming albania's achievements, by correctly identifying the demanding integration tasks facing the country, is able to motivate the partner country. we need this today to give the eu a new impetus and renew its credibility. among the areas highlighted in the report, strengthening the rule of law, fighting corruption and organised crime are priorities for virtually all western balkan countries in meeting the accession conditions, but i see an opportunity to use the encouraging progress of albania as a positive example for the other countries.

in writing. ‒ the commission has presented its 2015 report on bosnia and herzegovina. the draft resolution of the committee on foreign affairs on this subject welcomes the submission of the application for eu membership by bosnia and herzegovina on 15 february 2016. urges the continuation of constitutional and political reforms that will transform bosnia and herzegovina into an effective, inclusive and fully functioning state, and that will ensure equality and democratic representation for all state-forming peoples and citizens, irrespective of their ethnic or religious background; calls on political and religious leaders to refrain from polarizing, nationalist and separatist rhetoric in society and to continue political dialogue and activities aimed at building mutual respect, consensus and cooperation between legitimate political representatives and protecting the diversity of society; expresses its concern at the independent foreign and security policy of the republika srpska, which is capable of undermining state-level politics, and condemns the law on public order still in force in the republika srpska, which undermines the fundamental democratic rights related to freedom of assembly, freedom of association and freedom of the media. i supported the foreign affairs committee's report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the adoption of the report, also appreciating that it contains good news for the revival of the eu enlargement policy, including the dynamisation of the western balkans accession process: the commission has for the first time in a long time given a fundamentally positive assessment of the processes of democratisation and reform in bosnia and herzegovina, and as a result the country submitted a formal application for eu accession two months ago. in assessing the report and developments in bosnia and herzegovina, i also took into account the fact that it is also in the union's interest to promote the integration capacity of our western balkan partner, which is in a situation that is the most complicated for political and historical reasons, to accelerate the accession process and to catch up with the other countries in the region. the report reflects the traditionally supportive and constructive approach of the ep. i hope that the european parliament's resolution will also be able to draw the attention of the commission's officials to the fact that the handling of the accession dossier for bosnia and the expected success of the preparations will be an important test for regaining the credibility of the eu's enlargement policy.

in writing. ‒ the report blames high public spending on the fight against poverty, noting that only a few member states have improved poverty-related indicators. hungary is among these countries thanks to the success of its reduction of recession, and it is therefore welcome that the report encourages the exchange of good practices between eu countries. the report also calls on the european commission to provide member states with greater flexibility in the use of the european structural and investment funds, so that they can allocate eu funds more effectively to reducing energy poverty or improving housing conditions. the report also calls on member states to support investments in renewable energy sources or energy efficiency, such as insulation, solar energy and energy-efficient equipment. in my country, hungary, the home heating program continues this year, with which the ministry of national development provides non-refundable support for the energy modernization and renovation of family homes starting from july 1, 2016 with a budget of huf 5 billion. the commission considers that the aid is compatible with the internal market if it is granted through state resources and does not distort competition and affects trade between member states. it is important that the commission works on the basis of objective data, for which it would be essential to take into account the actual financial situation (e.g. housing, debt) instead of the current surveys based on partial self-declaration. i voted in line with the people's party, i supported the report in its entirety.
in writing. ‒ the report of the committee on employment and social affairs links social policy and energy policy. the elimination or at least the reduction of energy poverty could be an important element in achieving the europe 2020 poverty reduction targets, as the union has significant untapped potential to reduce the main household costs of poor households through existing renewable energy and energy efficiency projects. energy efficiency, emissions and renewable energy targets can also contribute to the anti-poverty objectives of the europe 2020 strategy. in fact, an important tool in the fight against poverty, in particular extreme poverty, is the effective reduction of household costs by making the different funds more targeted towards the most vulnerable households and by removing obstacles to the efficient use of resources. the europe 2020 strategy aims to achieve 20% of energy consumption from renewable sources by 2020, 20% more energy efficiency and 20% less greenhouse gas emissions (compared to 1990). the commission will continue to monitor the implementation of the union's energy efficiency and climate change policy, including the implementation of the energy union strategy. i supported the adoption of the report.
in writing. ‒ in developing countries, the private sector provides about 90% of jobs and is therefore crucial in the fight against poverty. it also has a key role to play in sustainable agricultural production, especially in view of the need to feed 9 billion people by 2050. as the potential of the private sector drives sustainable development in developing countries, the role of private sector actors is also becoming increasingly important in international development. given that, according to a recent commission assessment, eu support has made a significant contribution to the strengthening of the private sector in developing countries over the period 2004-2010, the commission proposes to build on these successes by adopting a strategic framework that can further strengthen the role of the private sector in contributing to the long-term strategy for sustainable development in these partner countries. i therefore voted in favour of the report.

mr. president, i have to go. in addition to the economic crisis that has been going on for several years and the ever-increasing competition, freight transport companies have had to face a new problem: the consequences of migration. the increased frequency and the tightening of border controls have reduced their ability to deliver goods to customers in the same time, while at the same time their transport costs have increased due to the longer journey times. not to mention the unpredictability, the time-sensitive cargo, the wasteful passengers and the environmental impact. for all these reasons, it is very important to stress that the four freedoms and the single internal market cannot be allowed to be jeopardised, and that the proper functioning of the schengen system is essential for this. to do so, we must follow the rules that he has set. nor can we ignore the fact that the european road network is the workplace of truck drivers, with all its challenges and dangers. truck drivers are at risk, facing much greater challenges than before. in their case, a safe working environment has acquired a new, heightened meaning and importance. it is therefore important to ensure a safe working environment for professional drivers and the protection of drivers in the transport network, in accordance with directive 89/391 on the protection of the health of workers. tourism should not be forgotten either, as it is a sector that is highly sensitive to terrorist attacks and the threat thereof. when we know that tourism accounts for almost 10% of european gdp, it is clear that the whole economy can be very seriously affected by losses in tourism. i believe that a support mechanism should be set up to enable transport providers, especially small and medium-sized enterprises, and tourism to make up for the losses. i ask the commission to consider this proposal.
we now have all the technology that allows us to drive our vehicles without a driver. alongside the obvious positives, there are also a host of challenges and potential drawbacks, such as the much-mentioned issue of accountability, the drastic reduction in management jobs, the issue of privacy, etc. we must pay attention to safety, which must be a priority, especially for those most at risk on the roads: pedestrians and cyclists. the road to self-driving vehicles includes communication between vehicles. this could already be useful for sharing routing information. i believe that this technology should be extended to all vehicles, particularly trucks. this could save time and fuel, improve the working conditions of hauliers and bring us closer to achieving our environmental objectives. the key challenge is to create the legal framework that will enable the sustainable use of this new technology and at the same time facilitate further development. the challenge of reconciling different interests and objectives is a major one, but the unstoppable pace of technological development makes it urgent to establish a regulatory framework as soon as possible. in this process, the commission can count on the assistance of the european parliament.
madam president, the european investment bank provided 80 billion euros in aid in 2014. this is only 3% of the eu's total investment of 2700 billion, so it is not the eib that is to blame for the failure of the eu's economic policies. the bank's lending to the private sector has been particularly strong in the last few years, with a strong growth in the number of loans to smes. since 2008, it has been clear that the process of convergence between the countries of the centre and those of the periphery, and in particular between the new member states, has stopped and the gaps have started to widen. in future, the bank's lending activities should be directed more strongly towards the less-developed regions. this requires a strategic programme to identify the priorities that would best help to catch up the lagging regions and then to develop the investment bank's support policy in line with this strategy.
in writing.– the eib is one of the strongest players in the eu when talking about investments in big-scale projects, providing direct funds and guarantees to governments and private and public enterprises. but a state of play where the eib hides who the ultimate beneficiaries or the beneficial owners are, where the eib continues to fund projects which are under investigation by olaf or national authorities for fraud or corruption cannot be further tolerated. we demand that the eib finally ends those practices. the eib must have a policy of zero tolerance for fraud, corruption and collusion and commit to strong integrity and ethical rules. the eib should implement the highest transparency in their operations and focus on investments in environmentally-friendly and sustainable projects. here we have a lot of room for improvement, as only 1% of the funds were spent for the renewable energy capacity development for the 13 new member states in 2014. if we expect them to catch up and change their old-fashioned energy policies, then we clearly need to incentivise. last but not least we have to prevent transactions to enterprises registered in offshore financial centres or tax havens which resort to aggressive tax planning.
in writing. as the eu's bank, the eib's main task is to contribute to the development of the common market, deepen european integration, create jobs and thus increase the eu's competitiveness by supporting the right projects. the 2014 report shows a number of positive results in terms of financing for smes, supporting climate action or investing in education, skills development and youth employment. these results are certainly encouraging. however, despite the eib's efforts, social and economic inequalities in the eu have not diminished, but have become more severe. this is due to an unfair global tax system where smes and the wage earners bear the brunt of the tax burden, while governments introduce new austerity measures and big corporations get richer. in such circumstances, the struggle to promote cohesion and solidarity between member states, to improve the quality of life or to protect the environment seems to be a windfall. the eib should strengthen its due diligence activities related to its operations without delay in order to avoid cooperation with actors registered in offshore financial centres or tax havens and engaged in aggressive tax planning practices. this step is essential for the eib. however, in order to clearly perceive the added value of the bank's projects, harmful tax practices and offshore loopholes need to be eliminated once and for all.

madam president, we hear the debate about how the agreement between the european union and turkey is working, with fewer refugees coming to the european union. slowly and gradually, however, the process of relocation has begun, which means that european asylum policy seems to be beginning to bear fruit, despite all the difficulties. but there is another side to the story, which has not been mentioned much, although mr timmermans has just mentioned it. namely, what will happen to the people living in refugee camps in turkey? what are their perspectives? what kind of life awaits them there? no one knows how long they're supposed to be there. we have a responsibility to ensure that these people have a future, that they can study, that they can work. the european union must not only spend money to keep refugees away, but also to create conditions in the camps where these people can prepare for the future and preserve their human dignity. and there's something else we have to face. while we are doing everything we can to keep refugees out of europe, we are doing nothing, nothing at all, against those member states that refuse to take responsibility, that do not participate in the common european policy. we must say that this is the weakness that encourages these countries and the european far right. it should be made clear that those who do not take part in the common european policy should not expect support from the union in other areas.
in writing. since the eu-turkey cooperation agreement in march, the number of arrivals to the greek islands has fallen by more than two thirds, according to the eu border agency frontex. from these, we can confidently conclude that the common european asylum policy has started to work. in contrast, individual member state solutions, fencing and border closures have only increased human suffering, not provided a solution. the agreement with turkey is designed to ensure that refugees no longer risk their lives on the dangerous sea route and fall into the clutches of human traffickers. the turkish deal has created the possibility for refugees from the war to arrive in the eu in a legal, safe and regulated way. solidarity between eu member states is needed for the eu-turkey agreement to continue to work. only together can we tackle the biggest crisis in the eu's history, and every member state must do its part. let's be clear: the refugee crisis will not go away on its own, and we cannot delay further in comprehensively reforming the eu's asylum system. the eu's common border guard, the relief of frontline member states, eu solidarity, full harmonisation of asylum procedures and an eu green card similar to the us green card system serve this purpose. the eu's refugee policy can only be transformed in accordance with the principles of human dignity, humanity and solidarity. european values are not negotiable.

in writing. ‒ the commission has submitted to the council, on the basis of article k.3 of the treaty on european union, a proposal for a decision on the accession of the republic of croatia to the convention of 18 december 1997 on mutual legal assistance and cooperation between customs administrations. the council consulted the parliament before adopting this decision. the committee on the internal market and consumer protection has recommended that parliament approve the commission's proposal. i voted accordingly.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the recommendation for croatia to accede to the convention on mutual legal assistance and cooperation between customs administrations. the act of accession of the republic of croatia provides for a simplified procedure for the accession of croatia to the conventions and protocols concluded by the member states. by accepting this report, i have consented to this procedure.
in writing. ‒ the act of accession of the republic of croatia1 provides for a simplified procedure for croatia's accession to the conventions and protocols concluded by the member states on the basis of article 34 teu (formerly article k.3 teu) or article 293 ec. article 3 (4) of the act of accession provides only that croatia is to accede to the conventions and protocols on the basis of that act. i supported him with my vote.
in writing. ‒ the polish traffic police intend to initiate proceedings against bolesław g. piecha, a polish mep, for violating the speed limit in a populated area. on 29 october 2015, the prosecutor general of the republic of poland sent to the european parliament a request for suspension of the member's immunity. the alleged infringement took place before bolesław g. piecha was elected as a member of the european parliament and therefore has no direct or obvious connection with the performance of the duties of a member of the european parliament by bolesław g. piecha. the member agreed to pay the fine in his statement to the general inspectorate of traffic police, and there is therefore no serious and well-founded suspicion that the request was made with the aim of causing political damage to the member. in the light of all this, the report of the committee on legal affairs recommends that the european parliament suspend the immunity of mr bolesław g. piecha. i voted accordingly.
in writing. ‒ the prosecutor general of the republic of poland forwarded the request of the polish inspector general of traffic police, mr bolesław g. piecha, to suspend the immunity of a polish member of the european parliament; he had committed a traffic offence. since the alleged infringement took place before mr piecha was elected to the european parliament and since, according to practice, the infringement has no direct or obvious connection with the performance of the duties of a member of the european parliament by mr piecha, i voted in favour of it, in accordance with the position of the s&d group.
in writing. ‒ family and child protection must be addressed as a top priority today. a number of petitions have been submitted to the european parliament on child protection issues, which shows the importance of the subject. one of the key issues addressed in the proposal is the establishment of cross-border mechanisms that would allow for the exchange of information between the competent authorities of different member states. this includes the establishment of specialised chambers dealing with cross-border cases. in order to improve the flow of information, it is important to provide citizens with adequate information on each procedure and to ensure access to appropriate legal assistance and interpretation, which help the parties concerned to make an informed decision that is optimal for them. these are also the reasons for supporting the proposal, keeping the issue on the agenda and implementing any legislative changes.
in writing. ‒ i would like to remind you that the large number of petitions received in child cases shows that effective implementation of the current regulation in practice is a serious problem. this may also be a sign that the legislation is not sufficiently clear and that there are serious problems with its interpretation by the national authorities. in addition to the fact that it would be desirable to close these loopholes in the next review of the legislation, i would also like to draw the attention of the commission and the member states to another factor. in particular, to provide special training and education for social workers and all other professionals dealing with cross-border cases. in view of all this, i voted in favour of the motion.
in writing. ‒ the resolution adopted is based on a large number of petitions concerning children's rights received by parliament's committee on petitions. with free movement within the union, the number of crossborder family relationships has multiplied, and with it the need for crossborder settlement of disputes. the resolution calls on the commission and the member states to promote a more coordinated exchange of information and cooperation on cross-border issues in order to protect children's rights. the resolution, based on the questions raised by the petitions, deals with the circumstances surrounding the adoption of children, concerns court decisions to be enforced under the brussels iia regulation, and addresses the issues of placement of children, contact, withdrawal of custody, and the problems caused by adoption without consent and illegal removal abroad. increased european mobility has also brought about changes in the lives of families, which require union responses where appropriate. the parliament believes that, for example, in the case of adoption, children should be placed in a situation where they can learn, use and maintain contact with their cultural background in their mother tongue. parliament called on the commission to develop a website on the subject, which would provide practical information to eu citizens on child protection and parental rights in the various member states.

in writing. ‒ the committee on petitions' report points out that a large number of petitions in child cases are received, which indicates that the implementation of the so-called brussels iia regulation, i.e. council regulation (ec) no 2201/2003 of 27 november 2003 on jurisdiction and the recognition and enforcement of judgments in matrimonial matters and the matters of parental responsibility and repealing regulation (ec) no 1347/2000, presents a serious problem. it concludes in this context that the regulation is not free from legal loopholes and that it is therefore appropriate to improve its provisions, in particular with regard to transnational and cross-border mechanisms which take into account the specificities of cross-border conflicts, in the context of its forthcoming review. it covers issues of judicial cooperation within the union for the protection of children, the role of social services in child protection, child custody proceedings, placement and adoption of children, and the wrongful removal of children. i voted for the motion.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution on the protection of the best interests of the child. the proposal seeks to respond to petitions received by the committee on petitions in recent years from various eu member states concerning practices of child welfare authorities, the protection of children's rights, custody of children and the illegal removal of children abroad. i agree with the motion that all child protection systems should have transnational and cross-border mechanisms that take into account the specificities of cross-border conflicts. indeed, increased mobility within the european union has led to an increase in cross-border child protection cases involving the withdrawal of custody, with a significant impact on the lives of the individuals concerned. i therefore agree with the motion that it is absolutely necessary to review the brussels iia regulation. i also think it is appropriate to propose that member states set up specialised chambers within family courts dealing with cross-border cases. it is also appropriate to publish clear and easily accessible guides containing practical information for eu citizens on the institutional framework for child protection and to provide specific training for social workers to enable them to deal with cross-border cases. finally, like the motion, i believe that budgetary restrictions imposed as a result of austerity measures should in no way prevent the individual cases of family issues from being properly assessed.
in writing. ‒ the document calls on member states to introduce monitoring and evaluation systems within the national coordination framework for crossborder cases involving children. it also urged the european commission to coordinate the exchange of information between the relevant member state authorities and called on the council to report on the specific actions being implemented by the member states. i supported him with my vote.
in writing. ‒ the proposal involves consultation of the economic and social committee on the european pillar of social rights. the dialogue builds on the first draft of the european pillar of social rights, an initiative announced by president juncker last september, and has been accompanied by a wide public consultation on the subject. the initiative is currently targeted at the euro area, but other member states have the possibility to join. the online consultation will run until the end of 2016. the commission's aim in the consultation process is to assess the eu's current social achievements, to identify new trends in work and social settings and to gather views and feedback on the principles set out in the preliminary draft of the pillar. the consultation will run until 31 december 2016 and a harmonised draft of the european pillar of social rights will be presented in early 2017. i voted in favour of the initiative, especially in the midst of the migrant crisis, because, as commissioner thyssen put it: 'one of the greatest challenges of the 21st century is how to adapt to the changes in the world of work. globalisation, the digital revolution and new business models have changed the way we do our daily work to an extent never seen before. other

in writing. ‒ the regulation on the european railway agency is the technical part of the fourth railway package, which aims to amend the current legislation, define new tasks and remove the remaining administrative and technical obstacles. the agency's current task is to gradually approximate the different technical specifications and to develop common safety methods and objectives for the european rail system as a whole. these objectives are now being further extended, making it easier to authorise the placing on the market of new rolling stock (railway wagons) and to issue single european safety certificates. this simplifies the procedure currently in force for railway companies, which provides for separate patenting and registration in each member state. the council approved the first reading on 10 december 2015, which has now been formally confirmed by the european parliament at the second reading. the industry has been waiting for this change for a long time, which brings us one step closer to the single european railway area. so i voted in favour of the motion.
