in writing. on 30 january 2013, the commission proposed to the parliament and the council the adoption of a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on the european union agency for railways and repealing regulation (ec) no 881/2004. parliament adopted its position at first reading on 26 february 2014. the lithuanian parliament, the romanian senate and the swedish parliament submitted reasoned opinions to the effect that the draft legislative act was not compatible with the principle of subsidiarity. following a debate in the council on 14 march 2014, the interinstitutional consultation following parliament's first reading began on 13 october 2014. following the consultation, the council published its position at first reading on 15 december 2015. in its report, the committee on transport and tourism recommends that parliament endorse the position adopted by the council at first reading and declare that the regulation has been adopted in accordance with the council's position. i supported the motion.

in writing. ‒ the regulation on the european railway agency is the technical part of the fourth railway package, which aims to amend the current legislation, define new tasks and remove the remaining administrative and technical obstacles. the 2004 revision of the directive focuses on removing the administrative and technical obstacles that currently exist. in the context of increased interoperability, it aims to simplify the requirements for design, construction, maintenance and the qualifications of railway staff, as well as health and safety conditions. this will improve interoperability between member states, with citizens as the main beneficiaries. the council approved the first reading on 10 december 2015, which has now been formally confirmed by the european parliament at the second reading. the industry has been waiting for this change for a long time, which brings us one step closer to the single european railway area. so i voted in favour of the motion.

in writing. ‒ i agree that the eu rail market has undergone a profound transformation over the last decade, with several rail packages being introduced (this is the fourth). the aim is to make rail more competitive and interoperable at eu level, while maintaining a high level of safety. so i voted in favour of the recommendation. i think that the joint strategies are effective and that a lot of them are also affecting the neighbouring countries. the priority should be to improve accessibility to the regions concerned and to develop rail and public services. this requires regional systems that also cross non-eu borders, and attention must be paid to neighbouring countries. for example, the different printing times still cause problems between ukraine and hungary. unfortunately, rail transport still accounts for only a modest share of transport within the european union. the rail transport share currently stagnates at 6% within the eu market and according to eurobarometer 54% of users are not satisfied with rail services. i agree that the system launched by the new directive will bring europe closer to achieving the single european railway area. it will reduce administrative costs and speed up procedures while maintaining the current high level of security. it also helps to avoid disguised forms of discrimination, especially for new companies wishing to enter the railway market.

in writing. ‒ on 30 january 2013, the commission proposed to the parliament and the council the adoption of a directive of the european parliament and of the council on railway safety. the council discussed the proposal on 10 october 2013 and parliament adopted its position at first reading on 26 february 2014. the lithuanian parliament, the romanian senate and the swedish parliament submitted reasoned opinions to the effect that the draft legislative act was not compatible with the principle of subsidiarity. on 13 october 2014, the interinstitutional consultation following parliament's first reading began. following the consultation, the council published its position at first reading on 15 december 2015. in its report, the committee on transport and tourism recommends that parliament endorse the position adopted by the council at first reading and declare that the directive has been adopted in accordance with the council's position. i supported the motion.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the draft resolution on railway safety. directive 2004/49/ec on railway safety established a framework for harmonising the content of safety rules, safety certificates of railway undertakings, the tasks and role of safety authorities and the investigation of accidents. this has prevented member states from continuing to develop their safety rules and standards in accordance with national guidelines, based on national technical and operational considerations. however, the issuing of a safety certificate remained a national competence. the adoption of the draft directive is a welcome step towards extending the regulatory framework of the directive and towards the creation of a single market for rail transport services. i support the enhancement of the role of the european railway agency, the launch of new trainings for railway staff and the improvement of cross-border information exchange. however, proposals for the standardisation of further technical systems (e.g. safety devices) and the discussion of the pnr issue in the context of air travel were also omitted in the context of the extension of the framework of the railway safety directive.
in writing. ‒ to make further efforts towards the creation of a single market for rail transport services, a common regulatory framework for railway safety should be established. member states have developed their own safety rules and standards mainly in accordance with national guidelines, based on national technical and operational approaches. at the same time, differences in principles, methods and cultures have made it difficult to remove technical barriers and thus to establish international transport services. i did not support the efdd's proposal.
in writing. ‒ i believe that the eu initiative to create a common framework of benchmarks that are reliable and correctly used in each of the different member states will help to improve the single market. the european parliament's proposal to regulate benchmarks is in line with the principle of subsidiarity as set out in article 5 (3) of the treaty on european union (teu), which requires the union to act only when and to the extent that the objectives of the proposed action cannot be sufficiently achieved by the member states and can therefore, by reason of the scale or effects of the proposed action, be better achieved at union level. although a significant proportion of benchmarks are country-specific, the benchmark industry is international in terms of both the production and use of benchmarks. while national measures on country-specific indices can help to ensure that intervention is tailored to the national problem, this may result in non-uniform, divergent regulation, create unequal conditions of competition in the single market and create an inconsistent and uncoordinated approach. benchmarks are used to price a wide range of cross-border transactions, including in the interbank financing market and in derivatives markets, and it is therefore important that their regulation is adequately harmonised at both international and union level. that is why i supported the adoption of the report.

in writing. ‒ the commission has proposed to the european parliament and the council a regulation on indices used as benchmarks in financial instruments and financial transactions. the uk house of commons submitted a reasoned opinion that the draft legislative act was not compatible with the principle of subsidiarity. in its report, the committee on economic and monetary affairs recommends that parliament give its agreement to the commission's draft, with a substantial modification, at first reading. i voted accordingly.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on indices used as benchmarks in financial instruments and financial transactions. indeed, benchmarks are of crucial importance for the smooth functioning and stability of financial, commodity and other markets and the wider economy. i therefore agree that further legislative action is needed for benchmarks in wider use to improve governance mechanisms and to reduce conflicts of interest and other shortcomings. i support the triple objective of the report to strengthen governance systems and standards, in particular for widely used and systemically important benchmarks, to reduce their vulnerability to manipulation and abuse; to increase transparency by making more information available to all benchmark users, allowing informed decision-making; and finally to maintain a wide choice and availability of benchmarks, with proportionate application of governance requirements. i also support the addition to the report which, while highlighting the strategic importance of critical benchmarks, suggests that it may be appropriate to empower esma to take decisions directly applicable to benchmark administrators and, where appropriate, to benchmark data providers in cases where national competent authorities fail to apply this regulation or infringe union law.
in writing. ‒ the manipulation of libor and foreign exchange benchmarks, and the alleged manipulation of other indices, have drawn attention to the importance and vulnerability of benchmarks. in response to these findings, the union amended its market abuse legislation to clarify that the manipulation of benchmarks is illegal and to establish the criminal relevance of such conduct. i voted for it.

in writing. ‒ the european court of auditors, in its follow-up to its special reports, states that 23 of the 44 recommendations in the economic sub-areas concerned have been fully implemented, while in 18 cases there is no or only partial implementation. these recommendations which were not implemented concerned mainly the important areas of agricultural policy, social policy, competition policy and external relations. the report highlights a number of shortcomings, non-transparent decision-making and responsibility-sharing mechanisms and insufficient traceability of the previous recommendations. the figures above clearly show that compliance with the court's recommendations is barely above 50%, which calls into question not only efficiency but also the requirements for transparent operation. on all these grounds, i did not support granting the discharge.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the ep's resolution on discharge to the european parliament in respect of the implementation of the general budget of the eu for the financial year 2014. in considering the findings of the report, i took into account that 2014 was a special year from a budgetary point of view, due to the innovations introduced in the conduct of the elections to the european parliament and the election of the president, and that the ep budget, while adequately funding the ep's functioning, also met this challenge. i find the comments made in this connection in the evaluation part of the decision particularly useful, which i believe will be useful in the budgetary and methodological planning of the next election years.

in writing. ‒ following the presentation of the annual report of the european court of auditors for the financial year 2014, the european parliament's committee on budgetary control carried out a financial audit of the general budget of the european union in respect of the council in the context of the 2014 closure procedure. the committee's primary task is to ensure and monitor the proper and efficient implementation of the community budget. in its 2014 annual report, the court of auditors concluded that, on the basis of its audit work, the payments made by the institutions and bodies in respect of administrative and other expenditure for the financial year 2014 were, overall, free from material error. nevertheless, the committee objected to the council's cooperation with parliament during the final accounts procedure. the council refused to cooperate and consequently the panel was not able to carry out its tasks necessary for granting the exemption. in the plenary vote, i voted in favour of postponing the granting of immunity.

in writing. the council spends large sums of eu public money each year in a completely opaque way and has refused to give an account since 2009, i.e. to submit to the european parliament's discharge procedure. i supported the report because it is unacceptable that they refuse to account for the use of public funds and refuse to provide the information needed for the audit, to answer written questions and to participate in hearings and debates on the implementation of the council budget. eu citizens are right to expect the council to change its behaviour.
in writing. ‒ in its report, the committee on budgetary control, on the basis of the consolidated annual accounts of the european union for the financial year 2014 and the annual report of the court of auditors on the implementation of the budget for the financial year 2014, recommends that parliament postpone its decision granting the secretary-general of the council discharge in respect of the implementation of the budget of the european council and of the council for the financial year 2014. i supported the motion.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution, convinced that the council, like the other eu institutions, has an obligation to report and account for its budget to the european parliament and thus to the european citizens. i consider it important that the relevant council bodies and, where appropriate, the member states provide the european parliament with all the information and cooperation necessary to ensure transparency and to monitor the efficient and lawful use of the budget.
in writing. ‒ the council should be transparent and fully accountable to the citizens of the union for the funds entrusted to it by participating fully and in good faith in the annual discharge procedure in the same way as the other eu institutions. the effective monitoring of the implementation of the union budget requires cooperation between parliament and the council based on a cooperation agreement. i voted for it, following the s&d line.
in writing. ‒ the rapporteur, in relation to the discharge of the court for the year 2014, points out that the court has conducted transparent financial management. the annual report contains only minor deficiencies, such as the absence of information on the external activities or financial activities of the judges on the website. the number and use of official vehicles is not adequately limited and the budget allocated to them is therefore excessive. apart from all this, the ecj has been at the forefront of resource-efficient, green public procurement and transparent property management. in view of the above, i voted in favour of the report.

in writing. ‒ the court's annual accounts were prepared by an external audit firm, following the same principles of transparency and accountability as those on which the court's audits are based. it is based on the view that the accounts give a reliable and true picture of the court's financial position. it is worth noting that the court of auditors started its reform at the end of 2014 with the aim of streamlining audit processes, transforming the court into a task-oriented organisation, seeking to use available resources flexibly and expanding the staff's remit. in the latter respect, it should be noted that the institution is doing its utmost to ensure the regular training of its auditors, as evidenced by its cooperation with several higher education institutions and its efforts to establish specialised training for european auditors. in view of the positive findings of the audit firm, i supported the report.

in writing. ‒ the court of auditors plays a key role in ensuring that eu funds are used better and smarter, but it is also of paramount importance in providing the legislator and the budgetary authority with valuable opinions on the results achieved by eu policies and their outcomes in order to improve the economy, efficiency and effectiveness of the activities financed by the union. i voted for the motion.
in writing. ‒ for the discharge to the european economic and social committee (eesc), the rapporteur proposes to grant a discharge. it gives a positive assessment of the commission's management and highlights the results achieved in reducing the annual wage costs of interpreting and outsourced translation work, which has led to a reduction in the annual total budget. it should be noted, however, that the travel expenses paid to the eesc's beneficiaries, together with allowances, represented a very high amount, 13% of the total annual budget. in view of all this, i voted in favour of granting the discharge and accepting the report.

in writing. ‒ although the committee of the regions' budget is purely administrative and a significant part of it is spent on staff, the report has been critical of the rapporteur on several occasions. the commission has also received a number of letters from the european parliament and the council, including from the european parliament, the council, the european economic and social committee and the committee of the regions. the rapporteur shall propose a detailed description of the expenditure, the reporting of figures for future deployments and a cost-benefit analysis. although the rapporteur draws attention to other problems in the chapter on 'the rules on whistleblowing, conflicts of interest and revolving door phenomena', i nevertheless supported the motion, as the rapporteur emphasised that the court's examination had not revealed any significant weaknesses in the areas audited in relation to human resources and procurement.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the ep's decision on the discharge to the committee of the regions for the implementation of the general budget of the eu for 2014. in considering the findings of the report, i took into account the important democratic role played by the committee of the regions in achieving the union's objectives, in particular in promoting the principles of citizenship and subsidiarity. i am confident that the observations made have over time corrected the shortcomings in terms of the disproportion of the mission expenses and, through agreements and closer cooperation with the union partner institutions, in particular in terms of the more efficient functioning of the translation services and the administration.
in writing. ‒ in its annual report for the financial year 2014, the court of auditors found that no significant weaknesses were identified in the areas audited for the committee of the regions related to human resources and procurement. i voted for it.
in writing. ‒ the rapporteur notes that the european external action service (eeas) has continued to implement its budget without material error and that the overall error rate in the administrative budget has been estimated by the court of auditors at 0,5%. it points out that a new organisational structure has been introduced, streamlining the previous high-management administrative structure towards a less hierarchical system. it wrongly points out that the internal administrative and financial framework of the eeas is still too complex and rigid, which means that the current structure does not allow the eeas to respond to crises in a timely manner, and similarly access to key information is time-consuming. i disagree with the report's finding that the proportion of member state diplomats (59 out of 128) among heads of mission is excessive. in any case, the move towards excessive centralisation and the creation of a federal state is the merger of the diplomatic missions of the member states with those of the eu, citing cost-effectiveness. for these reasons, i did not support the adoption of the report.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the ep's decision on discharge in respect of the implementation of the general budget of the eu for the financial year 2014 in respect of the european ombudsman and his office. in considering the findings of the report, i took into account the fact that the ombudsman plays an important role in ensuring the credibility of the union, citizens' trust in the community institutions, transparency and legality. i am confident that the tensions mentioned in the report, such as the workload of the ombudsman, the high number of requests outside his mandate or external assignments, will be addressed by the present observations and will ensure even more fully the conditions for the effective functioning of this important european judicial institution in the future.
in writing. ‒ in its annual report for the financial year 2014, the court found that the european ombudsman had not identified any significant weaknesses in the areas audited relating to human resources and procurement. i voted in favour of the document.
in writing. ‒ the commissioner for data protection has unjustifiably classified the 2014 court of auditors report in his annual activity report, which i believe is a decision against transparency. in my opinion, the data protection commissioner should be asked to continue to include a scoreboard in his annual activity report and to attach to the document documents governing his property management. it is important that the costs associated with these remain rational. the rapporteur expects the edps to provide detailed information on the secondments of its members and staff and their costs by the end of may 2016 as part of the annual activity report . i find it difficult to understand that the edps has not published exhaustive information on his conflict of interest policy. in my view, this accidental or intentional deficiency should be corrected and the edps should, in accordance with the rules laid down in article 16 of the staff regulations and in line with the recommendations issued by the commission, establish clear and binding rules on the 'revolving door' phenomenon and inform parliament of this in the 2015 annual activity report. the same applies to public procurement procedures for which no relevant information is available on the website, and neither the selection criteria nor the contracts awarded or concluded are transparent. on the basis of the above, i voted against the adoption of the report.
in writing. ‒ following the presentation of the annual report of the european court of auditors for the financial year 2014, the european parliament's committee on budgetary control carried out a financial audit of the general budget of the european union concerning the european data protection supervisor in the context of the closure of the accounts procedure for 2014. the court of auditors has found that the payments made to the european data protection supervisor for administrative and other expenditure in the financial year ended 31 december 2014 were, on the whole, free from material error and that the supervisory and control mechanisms in place to ensure the correctness and effectiveness of the payments were effective. the final audit report concludes that the financial review was carried out in an orderly manner and that no major deficiencies were found during the investigation. in the plenary vote, i voted for the granting of immunity.
in writing. following the presentation of the annual report of the european court of auditors for the financial year 2014, the european parliament's committee on budgetary control carried out a financial audit of the general budget of the european union in respect of the european data protection supervisor in the context of the closure of the accounts procedure for the financial year 2014. the committee's primary task is to ensure and monitor the proper and efficient implementation of the community budget. the court of auditors has found that the payments made to the european data protection supervisor for administrative and other expenditure in the financial year ended 31 december 2014 were, on the whole, free from material error and that the supervisory and control mechanisms in place to ensure the correctness and effectiveness of the payments were effective. the final audit report concludes that the financial review was carried out in an orderly manner and that no major deficiencies were found during the investigation. the special committee decided at its meeting in early april to grant the discharge and to close the accounts for 2014. i voted in committee and in plenary to grant the discharge.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the ep's decision on the discharge for the implementation of the general budget of the eu for the financial year 2014 as regards the functioning of the european data protection supervisor. in considering the findings of the report, i have taken into account that the role of the edps and the issue of personal data protection in general have recently become increasingly important in eu legislation and in member state enforcement, partly due to the increased importance of the fight against international crime and terrorism, and partly due to the increased importance of external cooperation and the euro-atlantic trade negotiations. i am convinced that the edps is an important guarantee for european citizens of the eu's credibility and its legitimate functioning, and i therefore hope that the validation of the findings contained in the report will further improve the future conditions for the functioning of our community legal institution.
in writing. ‒ in 2014, the commissioner had a total budget of eur 8 012 953 (compared to eur 7 661 409 in 2013) and a budget implementation rate of 92% (compared to 84,7% in 2013). the report welcomes the improvement in performance. i supported him with my vote.
in writing. ‒ i supported the discharge report on the implementation of the budget of the european union agencies for the financial year 2014, as the examinations have shown that the final accounts of all decentralised agencies reflect the financial situation as at 31 december 2014 in all material respects and in accordance with the provisions of the relevant financial regulation and the accounting rules adopted by the commission's accounting officer. the transactions underlying the annual accounts for the year ended 31 december 2014 were legal and regular in all material respects for the institutions. despite my vote in favour, i consider it necessary to emphasise that the rapporteur expresses concern that some agencies are partly financed by fees paid by industry, as these financial ties may affect their independence. it calls on all agencies to take measures to ensure the independence of their internal and external activities. it is important to encourage institutions to adopt guidelines on reporting abuses and to do everything possible to improve the overall prevention of and fight against corruption.
in writing. ‒ following the presentation of the annual report of the european court of auditors for the financial year 2014, the european parliament's committee on budgetary control carried out a financial audit of the general budget of the european union concerning the performance, financial management and control of the agencies in the context of the 2014 closure procedure. the committee's primary task is to ensure and monitor the proper and efficient implementation of the community budget. the court of auditors states that it has obtained assurance as to the reliability of the annual accounts for the financial year 2014 and as to the legality and regularity of the underlying transactions. it emphasises the need to further reduce errors in the accounting policies of each agency. it proposes to strengthen communication and cooperation and to make better use of synergies between the agencies and parliament. the final audit report concludes that the financial review was carried out in an orderly manner and that no major deficiencies were found during the investigation. the special committee decided at its meeting in early april to grant the discharge and to close the accounts for 2014. i voted in favour of the report in both the committee and the plenary.

in writing. following the presentation of the annual report of the european court of auditors for the financial year 2014, the european parliament's committee on budgetary control carried out a financial audit of the general budget of the european union concerning the agency for the cooperation of energy regulators in the context of the 2014 closure procedure. the committee's primary task is to ensure and monitor the proper and efficient implementation of the community budget. the court of auditors concluded that it had satisfied itself that the agency for the cooperation of energy regulators had submitted a reliable annual accounts for the financial year 2014 and that the underlying transactions were legal and regular. acknowledges that the agency has implemented a number of measures to improve its budget planning and implementation processes; the final audit report concludes that the financial review was carried out in an orderly manner and that no major deficiencies were found during the investigation. the committee decided at its meeting at the end of march to grant the discharge and to close the accounts for 2014. i voted in committee and in plenary to grant the discharge.

in writing. ‒ the agency for the cooperation of energy regulators has submitted its final annual accounts for the financial year 2014. on 12 february 2016, on the basis of the court of auditors' report on the annual accounts, the council recommended that parliament give the director of the agency discharge in respect of the implementation of the agency's budget for the financial year 2014. the committee on budgetary control recommended in its report that parliament should grant this discharge. i voted accordingly.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the 2014 discharge report as it found the agency's performance for that year to be satisfactory in all respects. according to the financial statements, the budget of the agency for the cooperation of energy regulators for the financial year 2014 represents a decrease of 8,8% compared to 2013. the court of auditors, in its report on the annual accounts of the agency for the financial year 2014, has stated that it has obtained reasonable assurances that the annual accounts of the agency for the financial year 2014 are reliable and that the underlying transactions are legal and regular. the agency shall, in particular, ensure that the agency's annual report on the implementation of the union's macro-financial assistance is updated regularly. i believe that since we are talking about an entirely eu resource, we can only give the green light to the agencies with full transparency and proper financial implementation. the report notes that not only was the available resource correctly spent, but that budgetary control efforts during the financial year 2014 resulted in a budget implementation rate of 95%. the agency thus achieved its planned target, which represents an increase of 2,53% compared to 2013. the report also states that the agency's annual reports can play an important role in ensuring compliance with the principles of transparency, accountability and integrity. i hope that the hungarian institutions will also reach this level of transparency one day.
in writing. ‒ the court of auditors, in its report on the annual accounts of the agency for the cooperation of energy regulators for the financial year 2014, concluded that it had satisfied itself that the agency's annual accounts for the financial year 2014 were reliable and that the underlying transactions were legal and regular. i voted for the document.
in writing. ‒ following the presentation of the annual report of the european court of auditors for the financial year 2014, the european parliament's committee on budgetary control carried out a financial audit of the general budget of the european union concerning the european electronic communications regulators board in the context of the closure of the accounts procedure for 2014. the committee's primary task is to ensure and monitor the proper and efficient implementation of the community budget. the court of auditors has conducted its examinations with a view to establishing whether the annual accounts of the body for european electronic communications regulations for the financial year 2014 are reliable and that the underlying transactions are legal and regular. the agency needs to improve its it security controls and risk management processes. the final audit report concludes that the financial review was carried out in an orderly manner and that no major deficiencies were found during the investigation. the committee decided at its meeting at the end of march to grant the discharge and to close the accounts for 2014. the special committee decided at its meeting in early april to grant the discharge and to close the accounts for 2014. i voted in committee and in plenary to grant the discharge.

in writing. ‒ the translation centre for the bodies of the european union has submitted its final annual accounts for the financial year 2014. on 12 february 2016, on the basis of the court of auditors' report on the annual accounts, the council recommended to parliament that the director of the translation centre be relieved of his responsibility for the implementation of the centre's budget for the financial year 2014. the committee on budgetary control recommended in its report that parliament should grant this discharge. i voted accordingly.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the ep's decision on discharge in respect of the implementation of the general budget of the eu for the financial year 2014 in respect of the translation centre of the european union. as a member of the european parliament, i experience firsthand the importance of the work of translators in the smooth and legal functioning of all eu institutions, especially the large and multilingual european parliament, and i have taken this into account when considering the findings of this report. it is to be appreciated that the translation centre has also successfully met the challenge of the multiplied tasks posed by the enlargement of the eu from a budgetary point of view. in the interests of sound management, i myself particularly support the solutions that the translation centre seeks to exploit the synergies of its cooperation with the other eu institutions and bodies.
in writing. ‒ the budget of the translation centre for the bodies of the european union for the financial year 2014 was eur 56 268 041, a decrease of 7,81% compared to 2013. i voted in favour of the related document.
in writing. ‒ following the presentation of the annual report of the european court of auditors for the financial year 2014, the european parliament's committee on budgetary control carried out a financial audit of the general budget of the european union in the context of the 2014 closure procedure, concerning the european training and development centre. the committee's primary task is to ensure and monitor the proper and efficient implementation of the community budget. the court of auditors concluded that it had obtained reasonable assurances that the annual accounts of the european centre for the development of vocational training for the financial year 2014 were reliable and that the underlying transactions were legal and regular. it welcomes the dual education system used in some member states, but points out that it does not guarantee that the problem of youth unemployment will be solved. the final audit report concludes that the financial review was carried out in an orderly manner and that no major deficiencies were found during the investigation. the special committee decided at its meeting in early april to grant the discharge and to close the accounts for 2014. i voted in committee and in plenary to grant the discharge.

in writing. ‒ the european centre for the development of vocational training has submitted its final annual accounts for the financial year 2014. on 12 february 2016, on the basis of the court of auditors' report on the annual accounts, the council recommended to parliament that the director of the centre be relieved of his or her responsibility for the implementation of the centre's budget for the financial year 2014. the committee on budgetary control recommended in its report that parliament should grant this discharge. i voted accordingly.
in writing. ‒ the report gives a discharge to the director of the european centre for the development of vocational training in respect of the implementation of the centre's budget for the financial year 2014, as the centre's management in 2014 met all relevant criteria. that is why i voted in favour of the report. the report describes that the final budget of the centre for the financial year 2014 was eur 17 275 766, representing a decrease of 3,62% compared to 2013. the court of auditors, in its report on the annual accounts of the centre for the financial year 2014, stated that it had obtained reasonable assurances that the accounts of the centre were reliable and that the underlying transactions were legal and regular. following the budgetary control efforts during the financial year 2014, the budget implementation rate was 98,93%, which is the same as in the financial year 2013, which i consider to be a very good result. i consider it important that the centre's management board adopted its policy on conflict prevention and management in october 2014, adapted to the centre's situation and covering specific situations of conflict that may arise in the centre. in this context, a large number of the members of the centre's management board signed a public declaration that there was no conflict of interest in their case. the report urges those board members who have not yet signed the declaration to do so as soon as possible. the same steps would be particularly welcome for the hungarian authorities.
in writing. ‒ the court of auditors, in its report on the authority's annual accounts for the financial year 2014, concluded that it had satisfied itself that the centre's annual accounts were reliable and that the underlying transactions were legal and regular. i supported him with my vote.
in writing. ‒ following the presentation of the annual report of the european court of auditors for the financial year 2014, the european parliament's committee on budgetary control carried out a financial audit of the general budget of the european union concerning the european police college in the context of the 2014 closure procedure. the committee's primary task is to ensure and monitor the proper and efficient implementation of the community budget. the european parliament has approved the closure of the accounts of the european police college for the financial year 2014. although the court of auditors found the operations underlying the academy's annual accounts to be legal and regular, it also stressed that the rate of carry-overs to the following year was still high and therefore called for improvement and for compliance with the principle of the annual budget. the final audit report concludes that the financial review was carried out in an orderly manner and that no major deficiencies were found during the investigation. the special committee decided at its meeting in early april to grant the discharge and to close the accounts for 2014. i voted in committee and in plenary to grant the discharge.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the ep's resolution on the discharge for the implementation of the general budget of the eu for the financial year 2014 in respect of the european police college (cepol). i have paid particular attention to the findings of the report because, as a hungarian representative, i attach great importance to the fact that this relatively small but important eu office operates in my country's capital. i was pleased to note that the submission also showed that the relocation of the academy from the uk to budapest was organisational, operational and budgetary smooth and that cepol was operating in a dignified and in all respects adequate manner in the light of the particular attacks on the relocation decision. i believe this is also important because the academy will play an increasingly important role in the coming years in developing and applying a common approach to effective eu action against cross-border and international organised crime.
in writing. ‒ according to the financial statement, the budget of the european police college for the financial year 2014 was eur 8 575 859, representing an increase of 1,48% compared to 2013. i voted in favour of the budapest institute document.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the discharge report on the implementation of the budget of the european aviation safety agency for the financial year 2014, which clears the agency's accounts for the financial year 2014. like the rapporteur, i welcome the agency's cooperation with other agencies, in particular the fact that the agency provides free access to human resources tools and provides a permanent secretariat to serve the network of eu agencies. the measures taken by the agency to increase efficiency and save money should also be acknowledged. however, i agree with the report and find the agency's current procurement planning, particularly in relation to framework contracts, worrying. the agency should take action in this regard. finally, as the report also highlights, in the light of the rapid development of the civil aviation sector, it is necessary to provide the agency with the necessary financial, physical and human resources in the field of safety and environmental protection to successfully carry out its regulatory and enforcement tasks, without compromising its independence or impartiality.
in writing. ‒ the court of auditors, in its report on the annual accounts of the european aviation safety agency for the financial year 2014, has stated that it has obtained reasonable assurances that the agency's annual accounts are reliable and that the underlying transactions are legal and regular. i voted for it.

in writing. ‒ following the presentation of the annual report of the european court of auditors for the financial year 2014, the european parliament's committee on budgetary control carried out a financial audit of the general budget of the european union concerning the european banking authority in the context of the closure of the accounts procedure for 2014. the committee's primary task is to ensure and monitor the proper and efficient implementation of the community budget. the court of auditors concluded that it had obtained reasonable assurances that the annual accounts of the european banking authority for the financial year 2014 were reliable and that the underlying transactions were legal and regular. it stresses that the authority should exercise powers for consumer protection and calls for the authority to coordinate its actions with other european supervisory authorities. the final audit report concludes that the financial review was carried out in an orderly manner and that no major deficiencies were found during the investigation. the special committee decided at its meeting in early april to grant the discharge and to close the accounts for 2014. i voted in committee and in plenary to grant the discharge.

in writing. the report on the discharge of the european centre for disease prevention and control for the year 2014 states that the centre's budget execution rate for the year 2014 reached 98% and that it has therefore substantially exhausted its budget for that year. in addition, it requested a specific additional allocation (eur 2 million) for sweden alone to cover the additional expenditure incurred in that member state. the report analyses objectively the centre's budget for the financial year in question, but at the same time draws attention to the fact that, following the good practice already established by the other underlying institutions, an attempt is being made to reduce the carry-over of commitment appropriations to the following financial year. in view of the above, i voted in favour of the adoption of the report.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report approving the implementation of the budget of the european centre for disease prevention and control for the financial year 2014 by the director of the european centre for disease prevention and control. the report describes that the financial statements show that the budget of the european centre for disease prevention and control for the financial year 2014 was eur 60 486 000, representing an increase of 3,72% compared to 2013, and that 97% of the budget of the centre comes from the union budget. the court of auditors also found that it had obtained sufficient assurance as to the reliability of the centre's annual accounts for the financial year 2014 and the legality and regularity of the underlying transactions. i consider it an outstanding achievement that the budgetary control efforts during the financial year 2014 resulted in a budget implementation rate of 98,77%, an increase of 5,81% compared to 2013. the report notes that the centre reviewed the implementation of its internal control standards (ics) in 2014 and notes with satisfaction that three ics have been almost fully implemented and the others have been fully implemented. i find the centre's developed and launched infectious disease atlas on its website to be a useful tool. through this, the centre has published data on four diseases at union level as well as international data. i agree with the encouragement for the centre to continue this project.

in writing. ‒ the court of auditors, in its report on the agency's annual accounts for the financial year 2014, stated that it had satisfied itself that they were reliable and that the underlying transactions were legal and regular. it is important to highlight that the fees collected in 2014 from applications for registration of biocidal products from the agency's annual revenue covered only 17% of the expenditure for the tasks set out in the biocidal products regulation. however, its revenues from fees and charges related to activities related to the registration, evaluation, authorisation and restriction of chemicals (reach) and the classification, labelling and packaging of substances and mixtures (clp) were higher than planned, amounting to eur 27,8 million. the agency has fulfilled 98% of the recommendations on manpower and devotes 78% of its staff to operational activities, and has provided satisfactory solutions to both the transparency and conflicts of interest concerns raised by parliament. on the basis of the above, i voted in favour of the adoption of the report.

in writing. ‒ the report approves the implementation of the budget of the european chemicals agency for the financial year 2014. the court of auditors concluded that it had obtained reasonable assurances that the annual accounts of the agency for the financial year 2014 were reliable and that the underlying transactions were legal and regular. i voted in favour of the report for all these reasons. the report notes that the final budget of the european chemicals agency (the agency) for the financial year 2014 was eur 114 112 193, representing an increase of 6,37% compared to 2013, according to the financial statements. the report notes that the agency's procedures for the prevention and management of conflicts of interest cover both external and internal staff. notes that the court of auditors' audit findings on the annual accounts of the european food safety authority (efsa) for the financial year 2014 were based on a comparison of the agency's annual accounts with the european food safety authority's annual accounts for the financial year 2014, which are updated annually; due to its unique situation, the agency's management is not exclusively financed by the eu budget, but also receives significant revenue from, for example, the fees for registration of biocidal products or other chemical substances. in addition, revenue from fees and charges related to activities related to the classification, labelling and packaging (clp) of substances and mixtures is a significant item. i find it useful that the agency has decided to apply the conflict of interest procedure to members of its informal working groups, specialised groups and discussion forums, which requires an annual declaration of interest and opens each meeting with an oral declaration.
in writing. ‒ according to the financial statements, the final budget of the european chemicals agency for the financial year 2014 was eur 114 112 193, an increase of 6,3% compared to 2013. i voted for the document.
in writing. ‒ the rapporteur highlights that the european environment agency has reduced its staff in accordance with the principles of sound financial management as a condition for the discharge for the implementation of the general budget for the financial year 2014. at the same time, it is important to expect the agency to apply more strict confidentiality and exclusion measures in relation to public procurement and to carry out background checks in all cases. the consistent application of the exclusion criteria is necessary to exclude from participation in public procurement all companies for which the conflict of interests arises. this is essential for the strict protection of the financial interests of the union. in addition to the substantive remarks above, i voted in favour of the adoption of the report.

in writing. ‒ the report describes that the final budget of the european environment agency for the financial year 2014 was eur 52 573 071, an increase of 6,70% compared to 2013. it notes, however, that only 76,81% of the agency's budget comes from the union budget and that this increase is mainly related to the operational expenditure of the strategic actions. as the court of auditors stated in its report on the agency's annual accounts for the financial year 2014 that it has obtained reasonable assurances that the annual accounts of the european environment agency for the financial year 2014 are reliable and that the underlying transactions are legal and regular, i have therefore voted in favour of the report providing for a discharge. the report notes that the budgetary control efforts during the financial year 2014 resulted in a budget implementation rate of 99,19% and a payment appropriations execution rate of 87,19%. the agency has reduced its staff in accordance with the principles of the interinstitutional agreement on sound financial management. in this context, i consider it important to note that cuts should be treated with caution as they could have a detrimental impact on the implementation of the main parts of the agency's multiannual work programme.
in writing. ‒ the court of auditors, in its report on the agency's annual accounts for the financial year 2014, concluded that it had obtained reasonable assurances that the annual accounts of the european environment agency for the financial year 2014 were reliable and that the underlying transactions were legal and regular. i supported him with my vote.

in writing. ‒ the final annual accounts of the european fisheries control agency are the same as those annexed to the court of auditors' report. i voted for the document.
in writing. ‒ the report highlights the need for the authority to apply strict confidentiality and exclusion measures in relation to public procurement. in any case, it shall carry out background checks to exclude the companies concerned from participation in the event of a conflict of interest. this is linked to the recurring problem with the agency's work, which is that the authority must be free from actual or perceived conflicts of interest, in particular in the economic sectors it regulates. unfortunately, the authority has still not been able to clarify these allegations, nor does it apply the two-year withdrawal period that would apply to all material interests related to the regulated sectors. the authority has not been able to make a comprehensive improvement in the prevention and fight against corruption, as it has not even developed an anti-fraud strategy. because of the serious deficiencies mentioned above, i voted against granting the exemption.

in writing. ‒ the report states that according to the financial statements, the budget of the european food safety authority for the financial year 2014 was eur 79 701 222, representing an increase of 2,11% compared to 2013. this budget shall be entirely derived from the union budget. as the court of auditors stated in its report on the authority's annual accounts for the financial year 2014 that it had satisfied itself that the authority's annual accounts were reliable and that the underlying transactions were legal and regular, i voted in favour. the report notes that following the budgetary control efforts during the financial year 2014, the budget implementation rate was 99,69%, representing an increase of 0,86% compared to 2013. i consider it important that the authority has implemented a project to improve the efficiency and regularity of transaction processing through a central strategy, the introduction of planning, monitoring and reporting procedures and structures, and centralised financial and procurement processes and structures. the report highlights that this project will enable the authority to perform its task more efficiently and to reduce the time and manpower required for the procedures.

in writing. ‒ following the presentation of the annual report of the european court of auditors for the financial year 2014, the european parliament's committee on budgetary control carried out a financial audit of the general budget of the european union concerning the european institute for gender equality in the context of the 2014 closure procedure. the court of auditors concluded that it had obtained reasonable assurances that the annual accounts of the institute for the financial year 2014 were reliable and that the underlying transactions were legal and regular. it considers the recruitment and selection procedures, the centralised public procurement system and the conflict of interest policy, which allowed public access to cvs and declarations of interests, to be appropriate. the court of auditors confirmed that the annual accounts of the institute for the financial year 2014 present a reliable and true picture of the institute's financial position as at 31 december 2014 in all material respects and that the institute's operations and cash flows for the financial year 2014 are in accordance with the financial regulation. the final audit report concludes that the financial review was carried out in an orderly manner and that no major deficiencies were found during the investigation. the committee decided at its meeting at the end of march to grant the discharge and to close the accounts for 2014. i voted in committee and in plenary to grant the discharge.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the discharge report on the implementation of the 2014 budget of the european institute for gender equality, which approved the closure of the institute's accounts for 2014. my decision was confirmed by the court's finding in its report that the institute's accounts were reliable and that the underlying transactions were legal and regular. like the rapporteur, i welcome the fact that the institute achieved 95% of its planned results in 2014. it is also satisfied that the institute has applied for its public contracts as widely as possible, while in negotiated procedures for low-value contracts it has set the number of invited tenderers in such a way as to ensure a balance between publicity and proportionality. i am also pleased to see the fruitful cooperation between the institute and the committee on women's rights and equal opportunities. in agreement with the report, i consider that the objectives and tasks of the institute require that it should be maintained as a separate legal entity within the institutional framework of the union.
in writing. ‒ the institute was set up to contribute to and strengthen the promotion of gender equality, in particular by mainstreaming gender equality in all eu policies and related national policies, to combat discrimination based on sex and to raise awareness of gender equality among eu citizens. i voted in favour of the relevant document.
in writing. ‒ following the presentation of the annual report of the european court of auditors for the financial year 2014, the european parliament's committee on budgetary control carried out a financial audit of the general budget of the european union concerning the european insurance and occupational pensions authority in the context of the 2014 closure procedure. the committee's primary task is to ensure and monitor the proper and efficient implementation of the community budget. the court of auditors found that the audits provided sufficient assurance that the authority's annual accounts for the financial year 2014 were reliable and that the underlying transactions were legal and regular. the report welcomes the strengthening of purchasing capacity at company level, the introduction of clear definitions of the responsibilities of officials and staff. the final audit report concludes that the financial review was carried out in an orderly manner and that no major deficiencies were found during the investigation. the special committee decided at its meeting in early april to grant the discharge and to close the accounts for 2014. i voted in committee and in plenary to grant the discharge.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the discharge report on the implementation of the budget of the european insurance and occupational pensions authority for the financial year 2014, which approved the authority's accounts for 2014. it is to be welcomed that following the budgetary control efforts during the financial year 2014, the budget implementation rate was 100%, which ensured that the authority achieved its planned objective. i also support the part of the report that calls on the commission to introduce in the white paper for the second quarter of 2016 and in the legislative proposal for 2017 a financing system that ensures that the authority's independence is beyond doubt in the future. however, i share the rapporteur's regret that the authority has not always been able to adequately inform the eu legislator of all the details of its ongoing work and that it has been leaked to third parties before the eu legislator. i therefore support the call in the report for the authority to increase transparency in the future, to publish all its meetings with third parties and to provide timely and detailed information on the activities of the european parliament.

in writing. ‒ following the presentation of the annual report of the european court of auditors for the financial year 2014, the european parliament's committee on budgetary control carried out a financial audit of the general budget of the european union concerning the european institute of innovation and technology in the context of the 2014 closure procedure. the committee's primary task is to ensure and monitor the proper and efficient implementation of the community budget. the committee decided to grant the discharge at its meeting in early april, and in its judgment all questions concerning the management of the institute in 2014 were clarified. i voted in committee and in plenary to grant the discharge.
in writing. ‒ the european institute of innovation and technology has submitted its final annual accounts for the financial year 2014. on 12 february 2016, on the basis of the court of auditors' report on the annual accounts, the council recommended that parliament give the director of the institute discharge in respect of the implementation of the institute's budget for the financial year 2014. the committee on budgetary control recommended in its report that parliament should grant this discharge. i voted accordingly.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the implementation of the budget of the institute in budapest for 2014. the financial statements show that the budget of the institute for the financial year 2014 was eur 233 115 437, representing an increase of 65,54% compared to 2013. the increase is mainly due to the broadening of the portfolio and the range of beneficiaries and the change of the founding regulation. the total union contribution to the institute's 2014 budget was eur 169 807 303, representing an increase of 81,69% compared to 2013. even with such a drastic increase in the use of resources, the court found that it had satisfied itself that the institute's annual accounts were reliable and that the underlying transactions were legal and regular. the report states that, as a result of the budgetary control efforts during the financial year 2014, the budget implementation rate was 94,13%, representing a decrease of 2,84% compared to 2013, which in my view is acceptable in the context of the reorganisation of the tasks. i consider it a risky element to state in the report that since the establishment of the institute in 2009, staff turnover and the level of management have been unstable. i think it's necessary to examine the background of the ongoing exchange. in order to reduce the frequency of staff turnover, the institute has taken measures and in autumn 2014 the institute introduced an evaluation and reclassification system that provides better career prospects for its staff and strengthens the middle management level.
in writing. ‒ according to the financial statements, the total eu contribution to the institute's 2014 budget was eur 169 807 303, an increase of 81,69% compared to 2013. i voted in favour of the s&d group's position.
in writing. ‒ with regard to the decision on discharge in respect of the implementation of the general budget of the european medicines agency for the financial year 2014, i consider it important to point out that the court's report has indicated that the agency's fee rules set deadlines for the collection of fees from applicants and for payments by the agency to the competent authorities of the member states. the report shows that the agency did not respect these deadlines in the majority of the transactions examined by the court. the agency had originally planned to implement e-administration and further automation of these procedures by the end of 2015, but failed to do so. i consider it important to underline that the agency should take all further necessary steps to ensure that it can fully meet its pharmacovigilance obligations and report on the measures taken to do so, as the agency launched a pilot project on adaptive authorisation in march 2014 which was not supported by either parliament or the council. during the financial year 2014, the agency's own budget implementation rate reached 94,32%, representing a decrease of 2,44%. the implementation rate of payment appropriations was 82,30%, corresponding to a reduction of 3,98%. due to the shortcomings outlined above, i did not vote in favour of granting the exemption.
in writing. ‒ following the presentation of the annual report of the european court of auditors for the financial year 2014, the european parliament's committee on budgetary control carried out a financial audit of the general budget of the european union concerning the european medicines agency in the context of the closure of the accounts procedure for 2014. the court of auditors concluded that it had obtained reasonable assurances that the annual accounts of the european medicines agency for the financial year 2014 were reliable and that the underlying transactions were legal and regular. the final audit report concludes that the financial review was carried out in an orderly manner and that no major deficiencies were found during the investigation. in the plenary vote, i voted for the granting of immunity.

in writing. ‒ the european medicines agency has submitted its final annual accounts for the financial year 2014. on 12 february 2016, on the basis of the court of auditors' report on the annual accounts, the council recommended that parliament give the executive director of the agency discharge in respect of the implementation of the agency's budget for the financial year 2014. the committee on budgetary control recommended in its report that parliament should grant this discharge. i voted accordingly.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the discharge report as the court found that it had obtained reasonable assurance as to the reliability of the annual accounts of the european medicines agency for the financial year 2014 and the legality and regularity of the underlying transactions. the final budget of the european medicines agency for the financial year 2014 was eur 282 474 000, an increase of 12.29% compared to 2013, according to the financial statements, but only 12.53% of the agency's budget comes from the eu budget. the budget revenue of the agency, as provided for in the financial regulation, is composed of cash from union contributions and fees for marketing authorisation applications for medicinal products, post-authorisation activities and various administrative activities. i am pleased that the agency published its revised policy on the handling of conflicts of interest statements by members of the scientific committee and experts in november 2014, which entered into force in january 2015. the agency has thereby defined the notion of direct and indirect interests and has required all experts to identify in our annual conflict of interest declaration all direct and indirect interests in their case.
in writing. ‒ the court of auditors, in its report on the agency's annual accounts for the financial year 2014, concluded that it had obtained reasonable assurances that the annual accounts of the european medicines agency for the financial year 2014 were reliable and that the underlying transactions were legal and regular. i voted for it.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the discharge report on the implementation of esma's 2014 budget. as the final annual accounts of the european securities and markets authority are the same as those set out in the annex to the court of auditors' report, the closure of the authority's accounts for the financial year 2014 is not affected. the authority has a key role to play in promoting a common supervisory regime in the single market, in order to ensure financial stability and to make financial markets in the union more harmonised, transparent, efficient and secure. however, it is regrettable that, as the report pointed out, the authority has failed to inform the eu legislator in a proper and comprehensive manner of the details of its ongoing work. i agree with the rapporteur that the authority should avoid in future cases where member states or third parties have access to information which has not been shared with parliament.
in writing. ‒ the court of auditors, in its report on the annual accounts of the european securities and markets authority for the financial year 2014, has stated that it has obtained reasonable assurances that the authority's annual accounts for the financial year 2014 are reliable and that the underlying transactions are legal and regular. i supported him with my vote.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the discharge report on the implementation of the budget of the european agency for safety and health at work for the financial year 2014. the court of auditors, in its report on the agency's accounts for the financial year 2014, found that the transactions underlying the trust and the trust are legal and regular. in addition to the accuracy of the annual report, the report rightly acknowledges the agency's positive results in implementing the european union's strategic framework for safety and health at work 2014-2020. however, in agreement with the rapporteur, i propose that the report should pay greater attention in future to the rules on transparency, accountability and integrity.

in writing. ‒ following the presentation of the annual report of the european court of auditors for the financial year 2014, the european parliament's committee on budgetary control carried out a financial audit of the general budget of the european union in respect of artemis in the context of the 2014 closure procedure. the committee's primary task is to ensure and monitor the proper and efficient implementation of the community budget. the court stated that it had satisfied itself that the institute's annual accounts were reliable, but that it had not been able to find sufficient and appropriate audit evidence as to the legality and regularity of the transactions. it highlights the lack of an internal control system and a comprehensive set of rules for the prevention and management of conflicts of interest. it also highlights the low rate of budget implementation. the report points out that the committee did not recommend granting the exemption until these were clarified. at its meeting in early april, the committee decided to postpone the granting of the discharge, considering that further clarification of the agency's 2014 financial situation was required in order to receive the final accounts. i voted in committee and in plenary to postpone the granting of the discharge.

in writing. ‒ following the presentation of the annual report of the european court of auditors for the financial year 2014, the european parliament's committee on budgetary control carried out a financial audit of the general budget of the european union for clean sky in the context of the 2014 closure procedure. the committee's primary task is to ensure and monitor the proper and efficient implementation of the community budget. the court of auditors stated that the audits had provided it with assurance as to the reliability of the annual accounts for the financial year 2014 and the legality and regularity of the underlying transactions. it considers it important to strengthen a comprehensive policy of non-conflict. the final audit report concluded that the financial and regularity reviews did not reveal any serious deficiencies. the special committee decided at its meeting in early april to grant the discharge and to close the accounts for 2014. in the plenary vote, i voted for the granting of immunity.

in writing. ‒ i have voted in favour of the discharge report on the implementation of the budget of the clean sky joint undertaking for the financial year 2014, which clears the accounts of the joint undertaking for the financial year 2014. the court of auditors has found that the annual accounts of the joint undertaking for the year 2014 reflect, in all material respects, the financial position of the joint undertaking as at 31 december 2014 and the results of the financial and cash flow events for the year, in accordance with the provisions of its financial regulation. however, as the report points out, i would also urge that in future the court of auditors should present the annual financial performance, the state of implementation of multiannual projects and the results and their implementation in greater detail.
in writing. ‒ the court of auditors is of the opinion that the annual accounts of the joint undertaking for the year 2014 reflect the financial position of the joint undertaking as at 31 december 2014 in all material respects and in accordance with the provisions of the joint undertaking's financial rules. i voted for it.

in writing. ‒ following the presentation of the annual report of the european court of auditors for the financial year 2014, the european parliament's committee on budgetary control carried out a financial audit of the general budget of the european union in respect of the eniac joint undertaking in the context of the closure of the accounts procedure for 2014. the court stated that it had satisfied itself that the institute's annual accounts were reliable, but that it had not been able to find sufficient and appropriate audit evidence as to the legality and regularity of the transactions. the report highlights that it has been finding shortcomings in the legality and regularity of the annual budget for several years. information on the ex post control strategy is not sufficient to demonstrate the operational effectiveness of the control tools. there is little information on the contribution of the member states to the union payments. it notes that eniac has taken comprehensive measures to address the conflict of interest, but these need to be further developed. the report points out that the committee did not recommend granting the exemption until these were clarified. in the plenary vote, i voted in favour of postponing the granting of immunity.
in writing. following the presentation of the annual report of the european court of auditors for the financial year 2014, the european parliament's committee on budgetary control carried out its financial audit of the general budget of the european union in respect of the eniac joint undertaking in the context of the closure of the accounts procedure for the financial year 2014. the committee's primary task is to ensure and monitor the proper and efficient implementation of the community budget. the court stated that it had satisfied itself that the institute's annual accounts were reliable, but that it had not been able to find sufficient and appropriate audit evidence as to the legality and regularity of the transactions. the report highlights that it has been finding shortcomings in the legality and regularity of the annual budget for several years. information on the ex post control strategy is not sufficient to demonstrate the operational effectiveness of the control tools. there is little information on the contribution of the member states to the union payments. it notes that eniac has taken comprehensive measures to address the conflict of interest, but these need to be further developed. the report points out that the committee did not recommend granting the exemption until these were clarified. at its meeting in early april, the committee decided to postpone the granting of the discharge, considering that further clarification of the agency's 2014 financial situation was required in order to receive the final accounts. i voted in committee and in plenary to postpone the granting of the discharge.
