in writing. ‒ following the presentation of the annual report of the european court of auditors for the financial year 2014, the european parliament's committee on budgetary control carried out a financial audit of the general budget of the european union concerning the fuel cells and hydrogen joint undertaking in the context of the 2014 closure procedure. the committee's primary task is to ensure and monitor the proper and efficient implementation of the community budget. the report welcomes the fact that the court of auditors found the accounts of the fuel cells and hydrogen joint undertaking for the financial year 2014 to be reliable and that the underlying financial transactions were legal and regular in all material respects. the final audit report concludes that the financial and regularity reviews of the joint undertaking have not revealed any serious deficiencies. the special committee decided at its meeting in early april to grant the discharge and to close the accounts for 2014. in the plenary vote, i voted for the granting of immunity.
in writing. ‒ the fuel cell and hydrogen joint undertaking has submitted its final annual accounts for the financial year 2014. on 12 february 2016, on the basis of the court of auditors' report on the annual accounts, the council recommended to parliament that the executive director of the joint undertaking be relieved of his or her responsibility for the implementation of the joint undertaking's budget for the financial year 2014. the committee on budgetary control recommended in its report that parliament should grant this discharge. i voted accordingly.
in writing. ‒ the report states that the fuel cell and hydrogen joint undertaking was established in may 2008 by council regulation (ec) no 521/2008 as a public-private partnership for the period ending on 31 december 2017 to focus on the development of market applications and thereby facilitate further industrial efforts to accelerate the uptake of fuel cell and hydrogen technology. i voted in favour of the discharge report, although it says that the court's report is based on too many general observations rather than practical, concrete ones. the european parliament therefore calls for an audit that focuses more on the annual financial performance, the state of implementation of multiannual projects including a clear presentation of the implementation of the budget for the current and previous years and on results and implementation. the report notes that according to the 2014 annual activity report, the budget implementation rate for all sources of funding reached 98,48% for commitment appropriations by the end of the year, but considers that these indicators do not provide a true assessment of performance in the absence of a clear separation of information on the implementation of the seventh framework programme and horizon 2020. in view of all this, i therefore consider that, in addition to granting the exemption, a serious further investigation is necessary to analyse the activities of the company.
in writing. ‒ the court of auditors' 2014 annual report states that fch's 2014 annual report reflects, in all material respects and in accordance with the provisions of the joint undertaking's financial rules, the financial position as at 31 december 2014 and the outcome of the economic events that took place in the year ended 31 december 2014. i voted for it.
in writing. ‒ the rapporteur is concerned that the performance of operational ex ante controls on the payment of project costs has not been properly documented. it further notes that the ex-ante verification carried out by the joint undertaking's scientific officers did not identify and comment on the status of the projects (in progress, with deficiencies, suspended/cancelled) and their concrete results (no reservations, reservations requiring clarification, significant reservations). it points out that in several cases, payments were made without an official list of results adopted by the scientific officer. it is also important to note that, in the absence of a clear separation of information on the implementation of the seventh framework programme and horizon 2020, the use and commitment indicators for the operational activity do not provide a true assessment of performance. in this connection, the rapporteur mentions as a major weakness the fact that the commitment appropriations and payment appropriations for these two programmes are not separately included in the annual activity report. the evaluation of the joint undertaking's performance indicators has thus become opaque and unverifiable. it is important to highlight one sentence in the report in which the rapporteur summarises that there is no information on contributions in kind and in cash, which does not even ensure the minimum conditions for anti-corruption and transparent operation of the joint undertaking. in view of the above, i have voted against the discharge.
in writing. ‒ following the presentation of the annual report of the european court of auditors for the financial year 2014, the european parliament's committee on budgetary control carried out, in the context of the 2014 closure procedure, a financial audit of the general budget of the european union for the joint undertaking for research on innovative medicines. the court stated that it had satisfied itself that the institute's annual accounts were reliable and that the transactions in the accounts were legal and regular. the joint undertaking has made significant progress compared to the previous financial year and has been able to complete an action plan that has delivered clear and concrete results in terms of avoiding conflicts of interest and enhancing transparency. the panel decided to grant the waiver at its april meeting. i voted in committee and in plenary to grant the discharge.

in writing. ‒ the second joint undertaking for the innovative medicines research initiative has submitted its final annual accounts for the financial year 2014. on 12 february 2016, on the basis of the court of auditors' report on the annual accounts, the council recommended to parliament that the executive director of the imi joint undertaking be relieved of his or her responsibility for the implementation of the imi budget for the financial year 2014. the committee on budgetary control recommended in its report that parliament should grant this discharge. i voted accordingly.
in writing. ‒ the innovative medicines research initiative joint undertaking was set up in december 2007 for a period of 10 years to significantly improve the efficiency and effectiveness of the drug development process, with the long-term aim of making innovative medicines more effective and safer for the pharmaceutical industry. the report concludes that the court's report is based on too many general observations rather than practical, concrete observations. it therefore requests that an audit be carried out that focuses more on the annual financial performance, the state of implementation of multiannual projects (including a clear presentation of the implementation of the budget for the current and previous years) and on results and implementation. the report also notes that the court of auditors considers that the annual accounts of the joint undertaking are in all material respects in accordance with its financial regulation and the accounting rules adopted by the commission's accounting officer, reflecting the financial position as at 31 december 2014 and the results of the financial and monetary events for the year. that's why i voted to support the report to grant the exemption.
in writing. ‒ the innovative medicines research initiative joint undertaking was established in december 2007 for a period of 10 years to significantly improve the efficiency and effectiveness of the drug development process, with the long-term aim of making innovative medicines more effective and safer for the pharmaceutical industry. i supported the related report.
in writing. ‒ following the presentation of the annual report of the european court of auditors for the financial year 2014, the european parliament's committee on budgetary control carried out a financial audit of the general budget of the european union for the european joint undertaking for the development of fusion energy and iter in the context of the 2014 closure procedure. the committee's primary task is to ensure and monitor the proper and efficient implementation of the community budget. the court stated that it had not been able to find sufficient and appropriate audit evidence as to the legality and regularity of the transactions. although significant progress has been made in the internal control system, a number of measures still need to be implemented. the report points out that the committee did not recommend granting the exemption until these were clarified. in the plenary vote, i voted in favour of postponing the granting of immunity.

in writing. ‒ following the presentation of the annual report of the european court of auditors for the financial year 2014, the european parliament's committee on budgetary control carried out a financial audit of the general budget of the european union for the sesar joint undertaking in the context of the 2014 closure procedure. the committee's primary task is to ensure and monitor the proper and efficient implementation of the community budget. the court of auditors has found the annual accounts of the sesar joint undertaking for the financial year 2014 to be reliable and the underlying financial transactions to be legal and regular in all material respects. highlights the essential role of the joint undertaking in coordinating and implementing research in the context of the sesar project. notes that the annual accounts of the joint undertaking for the year 2014 present, in all material respects, the financial position of the joint undertaking as at 31 december 2014 and that the operations and cash flows are in line with the financial regulation; notes that the joint undertaking's annual activity report for the financial year 2012 was prepared by the court of auditors and that the annual activity report for the financial year 2012 was prepared by the court of auditors; the final audit report concludes that the financial and regularity reviews of the joint undertaking have not revealed any serious deficiencies. the special committee decided at its meeting in early april to grant the discharge and to close the accounts for 2014. i voted in committee and in plenary to grant the discharge.

in writing. ‒ the sesar joint undertaking was set up in february 2007 to manage the single european sky air traffic services research programme (sesar), which aims to modernise air traffic services in europe. i supported the related document.
in writing. ‒ the report on the european investment bank highlights that in 2014 the bank financed 285 000 smes, protecting 3.6 million jobs. this is certainly an important result. notes that the financial, economic and social crisis of 2008 resulted in a severe investment gap and a particularly high unemployment rate, especially among young people, together with a prolonged stagnation of the european economy; it addresses one of the most serious disproportions, namely that since 2008 the eu has ceased to function as a 'convergence machine' and has taken the opposite direction, with the result that the differences between regions and member states have increased sharply, and the social and economic inequalities within the union have become increasingly severe, hampering our economic life and further hindering social cohesion. the report's virtue is that it confronts the greatest challenges, not ignoring the failures in the areas in question. on these grounds, i supported the adoption of the report.
in writing. ‒ the report mainly summarises the conclusions of the eib's investment programme, outlines the main community objectives supported by the eib and the areas where the bank has been successful, such as stimulating economic recovery, supporting small businesses, supporting innovation, and tackling youth unemployment. the european parliament shall draw up a report each year on the basis of the annual report of the european investment bank. the committee on budgetary control supported the adoption of the report by a large majority, and the group also voted in favour of the draft report at the meeting of the people's party. i voted in favour of the report in the plenary.

in writing. the eib's support represents only 3% of eu investment, which is not significant for the eu's economic policy as a whole. this can be seen from the fact that only 250 000 smes have been financed, whereas there are 22 million smes in the union, employing 90 million people in total. so the 3.6 million jobs that are protected are a tiny fraction of the jobs that are in smes. in fact, the report notes that the aid is predominantly given to the core countries rather than the more needy periphery. overall, the report is welcome as it provides a true and comprehensive picture of the otherwise objectionable activities of the eib.
in writing. ‒ the european investment bank has submitted its annual activity report for 2014, its financial report for 2014 and its statistical report for 2014, and the eib's audit committee has also prepared its annual report for 2014. the committee on budgetary control concludes in its report that the eib's main task as the eu's bank is to provide financial support for projects that contribute to the balanced development of the internal market, social, economic and territorial cohesion and thus to strengthening european integration and job creation, and that it therefore has a key role to play in boosting the eu's competitiveness. the report sets out the key requirements for the eib and suggests that parliament should expect the eib to favour investments in economic recovery and productivity, policies to promote youth employment, innovation and sme development, support for environmental sustainability, economic and social cohesion and convergence, and to be consistent with the objectives of the european fund for strategic investments. i supported the adoption of the report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the eib's 2014 annual report. in addition to acknowledging the bank's many achievements, the report also details and provides guidance on the challenges still to be overcome. like the rapporteur, i welcome the eib's performance in financing smes, which has protected 3.6 million jobs in the eu. the eib's 'jobs for young people - investing in skills' initiative should also be acknowledged for its implementation in 2014. i also encourage further investment in education, skills development and youth employment, as youth unemployment is still dramatic. the introduction in 2014 of new innovative tools to support action on climate change is also commendable. however, i share the rapporteur's concern that support for renewable energy capacity building was concentrated in the majority of cases in the five largest economies in the union, and that a similar concentration is observed in the energy efficiency sector. in line with the rapporteur's opinion, i urge that future investments in renewable energy capacity building in the new member states be gradually increased. in addition, the adoption of the revised eib framework for the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing is particularly welcome. the commission notes that the bank has not provided any evidence that the bank has engaged in any form of illegal activity in the past.
in writing. ‒ as the eu's bank, the eib's main task is to provide financial support for projects that contribute to the balanced development of the internal market, social, economic and territorial cohesion and thus to strengthening european integration and job creation, and therefore plays a key role in enhancing the eu's competitiveness. i voted in favour of the report.
in writing. ‒ i strongly condemn all attacks against hospitals and schools occurring in armed conflicts around the world, with patients, students, medical and teaching staff, humanitarian aid workers, children and family members becoming targets and victims. these are the most cruel acts against humans and must be seriously punished. the right to health is a human right, and with today’s vote we call for the parties involved in armed conflicts to guarantee the availability, accessibility, acceptability and quality of medical services during the conflicts. i support today’s vote stressing that international condemnations must be followed by independent investigations and genuine accountability for all actors involved.
in writing. ‒ a motion for a resolution on this subject was tabled by the alde, ppe, ecr, verts/ale, gue/ngl and s&d groups. the six groups reached an agreement and worked out a joint compromise draft. i voted in favor of the compromise motion.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the joint motion for a resolution condemning the violation of international humanitarian law and calling for international condemnation of attacks on hospitals, schools and other civilian targets. i support the motion for a resolution calling on the member states of the union to strongly urge the un security council to use all the means at its disposal to enforce international humanitarian law. i also agree with the call to dispense with the right of veto in the security council when it comes to decisions on humanitarian matters and to increase respect for international legal standards for the protection of humanitarian workers. the unsc should ensure that acts constituting violations of those standards are consistently investigated and that persons suspected of having committed those acts are held accountable for their actions. like the motion, i condemn the participation of several partners of the union and its member states in serious violations of international humanitarian law. finally, in line with the motion, i believe that the eu should use all bilateral means at its disposal to persuade its partners to comply with international humanitarian law.
in writing. ‒ the international community is witnessing a harrowing trend of attacks on hospitals and schools in armed conflict zones around the world, along with unprecedented levels of denial of humanitarian aid and access, executions of civilians and humanitarian personnel, detention in inhumane conditions, and the hostage-taking and forced enslavement of civilian populations. i voted in favour of the s&d group's proposal.
in writing. ‒ full transparency is the basis for citizens' trust in the eu institutions and contributes to awareness of rights deriving from the eu legal order and to knowledge and awareness of the eu decision-making process, including the proper implementation of administrative and legislative procedures. the report highlights the shortcomings that have emerged in the tripartite interinstitutional consultations. on the one hand, the mechanisms under which conciliation meetings are organised are not transparent and, on the other hand, there is concern that the agreements reached in such conciliation meetings are not or are only known belatedly by the citizens and by the members themselves, who have to decide on the outcome of the conciliation in the parliamentary committee concerned. in the case of delegated acts, the lack of participation of co-legislators within the european supervisory authorities (eba, eiopa, esma) does not ensure transparency. there would be a need for a single register of all secondary law, which would be the task of the commission. as the report highlights a number of shortcomings and contains a reasoned opinion which is not only unfavourable to the commission but also to parliament and the council, i voted in favour of adopting the report.
in writing. ‒ article 15 of the eu treaty sets out the rules on access to documents by the eu institutions, bodies, offices and agencies. the detailed rules are laid down in regulation no 1049/2001. i believe that the above rules generally guarantee the necessary transparency. as a member of the fidesz people's party delegation, i support citizens' access to documents and the transparency of our institutions. at the same time, i believe that many of the elements in the report now before the vote will add to the bureaucratic burden on the administration, make many procedures more difficult, reduce efficiency and make interinstitutional agreements impossible. it therefore does not add value for european citizens. therefore, as a member of the fidesz people's party delegation, i abstained from the final vote.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the adoption of the annual report 2014/15 summarising the state and problems of public access to eu documents, with particular regard to the issue and the importance of compliance with relevant community legislation for the confidence of eu citizens in the institutions and the functioning of the union. the report also highlights problems that are still present, but which should be resolved in the near future, in particular as regards the transparency and accessibility of documents and decisions arising from trilogues, the lack of coordination of the rules on documents in the various eu institutions and the need to modernise the nearly 15-year-old directive on public access to documents. i consider it important to deal with them in order to counter the political attacks on the eu's credibility, including those against the citizens of my own member state, and i will follow them closely in my further work in parliament.
in writing. ‒ the report finds that access to information held by the eu institutions remains a barrier for citizens, due to the lack of a common interinstitutional approach based on full transparency, communication and direct democracy, which is intended to facilitate citizens' access to documents. i voted in favour of the s&d group's position.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on female domestic workers and carers in the eu. i agree with the report's call for member states to ratify ilo convention 189 as soon as possible and to apply it fully. the household and care sector which is predominantly female in the eu is characterised by a lack of representation, irregular working hours and a lack of safety at work. 2.5 million people live in such precarious environments in the union today. to change this, i support the recognition of the profession and value of domestic and care work as genuine work, and also the inclusion of those working in the sector under labour, health, social assistance and insurance and anti-discrimination legislation, recognising their social and economic contribution.

mr president in its introductory article 3 of the treaty on european union, it identifies the task of promoting territorial cohesion. well, let's look at the results of the last budget cycle in this light. the gap between the so-called centre countries and the periphery, above all the former socialist countries, has not diminished but increased. however, cohesion funds are 8.4% less in this cycle. that speaks for itself. in this context, the committee's proposal to ask the commission to facilitate the implementation of operational programmes in order to avoid suspension of payments is to be welcomed. however, we must distinguish between problems caused by excessive bureaucracy and a well-founded suspicion of corrupt use.
mr president in the debate on eu cohesion policy, we cannot ignore the fact that in some member states, eu funds are not used to promote the well-being of people, not to develop the economy, but to promote the well-being and enrichment of a few people close to the government. this is also the case in hungary, where corruption cases have forced the european commission to suspend 10 of the 15 eu operational programmes in hungary over the past few years. in some of these cases, such as the corruption case of the hungarian prime minister's son-in-law, the eu anti-fraud office has even launched an investigation. it's a lot of money, a lot of punishment. in the end, it may be necessary to pay a fine of up to huf 700 billion, representing 10% of eu funds. however, this fine will be paid by hungarian taxpayers and not by those who fraudulently obtained the funds. we therefore ask the commission to speed up the investigation of these cases and to develop legislation which will result in the punishment of criminals rather than the taxpayers of a member state.
in writing. a significant part of the european union's territory is covered by mountain regions, which offer many opportunities to achieve the union's objectives on employment, cohesion and environmental protection. i would like to draw the commission's attention to the importance of developing tourism in tackling the problems of unemployment, migration and ageing that are affecting the mountain region. today, 25 million europeans work in the sector, with a three-fold higher proportion of those under 24 than in any other sector, yet tourism is not considered a quality career. changing this trend requires, in particular, encouraging career opportunities and addressing issues of remuneration. the commission should develop concrete proposals to improve access to education (especially the ict platform), lifelong learning and mobility in mountain regions. in order to make mountain areas more attractive for economic activities, the commission and the member states should cooperate in channelling resources from the cohesion and investment funds to the regions. this should be addressed as a matter of priority in order to reduce youth unemployment and increase the efficiency of smes.

mr president the way the european commission relates to nord stream 2 compared to south stream is a typical case of double standards. the construction of south stream would have provided an alternative route to avoid ukraine for several european and central european countries, but the objections were voiced: based on competition law, bureaucratic, liberal principles, until the end result was that it failed. commissioner cañete, in answer to my written question, said that the problem with south stream was that it would have been diversified by the route. what about north stream 2? it's not diverting resources or routes. then why is it possible? obviously, the big difference is between the joint action of the four visegrad prime ministers and angela merkel. you made your decision based on that. what was not allowed to these countries, is possible for germany.
madam president, for the countries of central and eastern europe, the expansion of nord stream does not mean either diversification or an improvement in their competitiveness. and i'll go further than that, if this project is successful, on those gas pipeline interconnections that we've been working together to build to better connect the fragmented central and eastern european gas market to the much more liquid western european gas market, russian gas will be imported. it is therefore doubtful whether capacity will remain on the interconnectors for alternative transport. this would be a step backwards from the diversification objective. the central and eastern european countries are also not expected to benefit economically, as cross-border transport can significantly increase the price of the energy carrier. i ask the european commission to work towards the energy union objectives and to comply with eu legislation, in particular the third energy package. this is in the interest of the european citizens.
in writing. the common climate and energy policy objectives, the cop21 objectives and the principle of diversifying energy supply also call into question the need for nord stream 2. the project is also a source of concern because of its impact on both energy security and diversification of energy supply. in addition to the policy concerns, i would like to draw attention to an apparent double standard: in 2014, the european commission claimed that gazprom's business behaviour in the central and eastern european gas market constituted an abuse of a dominant position and infringed eu antitrust rules. he also called for the third energy cluster to stop the construction of the south stream. this position was appropriate from both an energy and a security policy perspective. however, now that germany wants to build a pipeline, gazprom suddenly appears as a reliable market player and, indeed, by referring to the specific rules for undersea pipelines, the commission may even consider the planned pipeline to be in line with the third energy package. strictly speaking, this may be justified, but it must be seen that the authorisation of a project which also affects the gas market in the cee region will also have a fundamental impact on the region's relationship with the union, as it will be assessed by the member states - not without reason - as a double standard. in the countries of the region, which are already in conflict with the union, this will have implications for the assessment of european integration as a whole.

in writing. ‒ the commission has proposed to the european parliament and the council a regulation on protection against subsidised imports from countries not members of the european union. the advisory working party of the legal services of the parliament, the council and the commission considers that the proposal in question contains a simple consolidation of the existing texts without any substantial amendment. in its report, the committee on legal affairs therefore recommends that parliament agree to the commission's proposal, as amended in line with the recommendations of the advisory working group. i voted accordingly.

in writing. ‒ in recent years, the european union has concluded a number of fisheries partnership agreements and protocols with third countries, providing financial and technical assistance in exchange for fishing rights within the exclusive economic zones of the partner countries. on 20 june 2014, the commission, acting on a mandate from the council, entered into negotiations with the government of liberia for the conclusion of the first sustainable fisheries partnership agreement and the implementation protocol between the european union and the republic of liberia. the tuna fisheries agreement and protocol were initialled by the parties on 5 june 2015 and are valid for five years and may be tacitly renewed. the protocol provides for a financial contribution from the union of eur 715 000 for the first year, eur 650 000 for the second, third and fourth years and eur 585 000 for the fifth year. the council intends to adopt a decision on the ratification of the agreement and the protocol, subject to parliament's consent. in its report, the committee on fisheries stresses that the agreement and the implementation protocol are consistent with the objectives of the common fisheries policy and bring significant mutual benefits to both parties, and therefore proposes that parliament give its consent to the conclusion of the agreement and the protocol annexed thereto. i voted accordingly.
in writing. ‒ the eu's conclusion of a sustainable fisheries partnership agreement with liberia in west africa is a major achievement. this is the first such agreement between the two parties. the active conservation of atlantic tuna and other fish stocks is a new chapter in the environmental history of the country, which has an exclusive economic zone of 246 152 km2. i am particularly pleased that the european union is making a significant contribution to reducing illegal, unreported fishing in liberian waters and to introducing the various techniques of sustainable fishing and aquaculture to liberians. hungary, as a country with experience and specific expertise in freshwater fisheries and aquaculture, can play a major role in boosting freshwater fisheries and aquaculture in liberia. in accordance with the guidelines of the european people's party, i voted in favour of the adoption of the report.
in writing. ‒ under the new eu-mauritania fisheries partnership agreement, eu vessels can catch 281 500 tonnes of fish a year off the coast of mauritania, 12 500 tonnes less than under the expiring agreement. this significant reduction is justified as some fish stocks have been severely depleted and therefore time should be allowed for their recovery. the trend towards the european union being forced to limit its sea fishing appropriately is evident not only in the current fisheries partnership agreements but also in others. the european supply of fish is therefore suffering from a steady and significant decline in the amount of sea fish caught. the eu should therefore pay greater attention to freshwater fish farming. a significant part of the hungarian wetlands is located in natura 2000 areas. these fish farms do not represent any threat to the natural values of these areas. in fact, in many cases it is our closed systems of wetlands that have created and preserved unique associations of aquatic habitats. it is important to give freshwater aquaculture greater prominence and to ensure that it receives the maximum possible eu support. the budget of the common fisheries policy beyond 2020 will need to be reformed in line with this guideline. in accordance with the guidelines of the european people's party, i voted in favour of the adoption of the report.

in writing. ‒ the european community concluded its first fisheries agreement with mauritania in 1989. the current partnership agreement entered into force in 2006 and was renewed in 2012 for a period of two years until the end of 2014. on 10 july 2015, the parties initialled a new protocol, which is also applied provisionally from 16 november 2015, allowing union fishing vessels to fish in mauritanian waters for a period of four years. the financial compensation to be paid by the european union in return for access to the exclusive fishing zone of mauritania by european vessels shall be eur 55 million per year, to be supplemented by a financial contribution of eur 16,5 million to be paid over the period of the agreement to promote the sustainable development of the fishing industry and the environmental protection of marine and coastal protected areas. the council intends to take a decision on the signing of the protocol on behalf of the eu, subject to parliament's consent. the committee on fisheries stresses in its report that the protocol represents a significant step forward and welcomes the new commitments by mauritania on transparency and priority access for the european fleet, and therefore recommends that parliament give its consent to the signing of the protocol. i voted accordingly.

madam president, please. the european union regularly promises change with these different, revolutionary new policies, and i've seen that in the seven years i've been here. what they have in common is that it will never, ever be better for the people of europe, and especially not for the people of the so-called new member states, who are considered second class. the latest keyword in cohesion policy is community-led local development. and what's interesting is that the obstacle to that is exactly what the european union is doing in the member states, which happens to be in hungary. how can we talk about community-led local development when the land has been stolen, there is no more local hungarian land, it has been taken over by foreigners. and then you need successful small businesses, but they don't exist because they've been destroyed by global corporations. there are no communities, and there are no local leaders, because the intelligent, well-educated people have already left their homelands for the european union. thank you very much.
in writing. ‒ the report focuses on two new territorial development instruments under the cohesion policy for the period 2014-2020, integrated territorial investment and community-led local development. the report recalls that greater flexibility and better integration are needed not only for eu programmes but also for national and regional policies in general. it also stresses that by guaranteeing a more general approach to governance reform, it can ensure that eu funds are not directed to national and regional policies within a parallel system, but rather embedded in a broader ambition to achieve sustainable economic outcomes. the two proposed measures were already subject to reservations by the proposers. for example, the committee on regional development has noted that the idea is complex and that some member states and regions consider the instrument unnecessary, as consultation with local actors is ongoing. in view of this, the two proposed new instruments do not provide added value and, as they are new instruments, there is no local expertise available, which may cause delays and implementation difficulties. in addition, the emergence of parallel administrative structures, lack of flexibility, commitment of funding for the entire financial planning period and lack of coordination with other development strategies may cause implementation problems. however, the strengthening of subsidiarity can be seen as a positive element. all things considered, i abstained from the vote.
in writing. ‒ in the development of the new territorial development instruments of the 2014-2020 cohesion policy, strategies need to be defined in the initial stages of the implementation process in cooperation with regional and local actors, in particular at the level of vocational and specialised training, as well as technical and financial support. this will facilitate effective partnership cooperation between regions, member states and the eu. i would like to draw attention to the fact that actions implemented under these instruments should take into account the priorities of local actors and be consistent with the overall objectives of the operational programmes and with other eu, national, regional and local development strategies and smart specialisation strategies. in addition, flexibility must be ensured. in view of the above, i voted in favour of the adoption of the report.
in writing. ‒ as one of the main objectives of the european union is territorial cohesion, the instruments for the financial planning period 2014-2020 will therefore, in addition to the existing developments, adopt an integrated approach that takes into account local needs. two new instruments will be introduced under the european structural and investment funds: community-led local development (clld) and integrated territorial investment (iti). they are likely to receive 5% of the cohesion policy budget. based on preliminary feedback, iti will be applied in 20 member states and clld in 18. the difficulties of the clld stem mainly from the emphasis and increased responsibility of local actors. member states already using leader have a significant experience advantage. the challenges facing the iti are related to the implementation of tasks by local bodies with limited expertise, the resulting delays and the lack of coordination between other development structures. the problems with both instruments are the increase in administrative burdens, the lack of confidence of member states in local influence on territorial development, the limited budget of the funds and the integration of several funds. development strategies should give priority to addressing pressing issues such as youth unemployment, the lack of resources for smes or adaptation to a new demographic situation. an important task for the future is the analysis by the commission of the use of the two instruments. the need for the earmarking of resources in the post-2020 cohesion policy regulation will be determined on the basis of effectiveness.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on territorial development in the plenary. the report focuses on two instruments, the community-led local development (clld) and the integrated territorial investments (iti) instruments. the rapporteur regrets that the two instruments are not being fully exploited by the member states and analyses the challenges that hinder the use of these instruments. the bottom-up approach, involving local actors in decision-making, is essential, but consultation at local level must have real added value and must not lead to a significant increase in an already complex and complex administrative burden.
in writing. ‒ as territorial cohesion is one of the union's fundamental objectives, the 2014-2020 financial period will place greater emphasis on integrated and local approaches to promote economic, social and territorial cohesion. in this context, community-led local development (clld) and integrated territorial investment (iti) instruments can provide a solution to better financing and to strengthening synergies between local and public actors. this approach helps to implement territorial strategies. however, local actors often lack the capacity to develop and implement development strategies for their own area. these actors need support at both national and union level to ensure that these instruments can deliver the desired impacts. in order to achieve a holistic approach, the possibilities for financing from several funds provided for in the new regulations should be exploited to the fullest extent possible. the report is a step in the right direction, and i welcome the rapporteur's efforts and approve it with a positive vote.

in writing. ‒ territorial cohesion is one of the fundamental objectives of the union. in order to achieve this, two new instruments were introduced under the european structural and investment funds in the financial planning period 2014-2020: community-led local development (clld) and integrated territorial investment (iti). the clld is a new tool for subregional use, based on the leader experience of community-led local development and a bottom-up approach. the iti helps to implement integrated territorial strategies by allowing the linking of funding from several priority axes of one or more operational programmes. the report by the regional development committee reviews the challenges encountered so far in the application of the two new instruments and makes recommendations on how to respond to these challenges. i voted in favour of the draft resolution.

in writing. ‒ the report amends the previous regulation on community statistics on balance of payments, international trade in services and foreign direct investment in order to allow the commission to modernise the regulation under the power of attorney. the main objective is to enable the statistics to be compiled to distinguish between greenfield foreign direct investment and foreign direct investment leading to acquisitions, the latter of which do not increase either the gross accumulation in the member state or the working capital of the business unit affected by the change of ownership during a given period. i supported the adoption of the report because the amendment of the regulation is intended to make capital flows more traceable. it should be noted, however, that this is necessary because the previous liberalization of capital flows, the deregulation of the financial sector, has created an opaque situation, which is a hotbed for tax evasion and speculation carried out by various methods.
in writing. ‒ european statistics on balance of payments, international trade in services and foreign direct investment (fdi) are key to ensuring informed economic policy decision-making and accurate forecasting of the economic outlook. this is of paramount importance both at the level of the european union and at the level of individual member states, and i therefore voted in favour of adopting the report.
in writing. regulation (ec) no 184/2005 on balance of payments, international trade in services and foreign direct investment is part of the overall eu framework for monitoring economic developments in individual member states and in the union as a whole. these statistics help to ensure consistency between the economic policies of the member states and the broad guidelines of the union and the legal requirements resulting from the eu economic governance framework. the parliament's report points to the revision of the regulation as a real opportunity to improve the transparency and detail of statistics on balance of payments, international trade in services and foreign direct investment. furthermore, to take advantage of the latest legal innovations that make these statistics more reliable tools for economic policy decisions. secondly, regulation (ec) no 184/2005 should be updated to ensure its consistency with the rules in the tfeu conferring on the commission the power to adopt delegated and implementing acts. this regulation should be aligned with the treaty of lisbon, as it distinguishes between the powers conferred on the commission as regards the adoption of non-legislative acts of general scope (delegated acts) supplementing or amending certain non-essential provisions of legislative acts as provided for in article 290 (1) tfeu and the adoption of uniform conditions for the implementation of binding union acts (implementing acts) as provided for in article 291 (2) tfeu. i voted for the report as a shadow rapporteur.
in writing. in the 11 years since the adoption of the original regulation, the volume and complexity of international capital flows have increased significantly and its modernisation is therefore timely. the primary objective of the report is to support the use of statistics to distinguish between greenfield foreign direct investment and foreign direct investment leading to acquisitions. the fight against tax fraud and aggressive tax planning is a hot topic today, and it could also be a good idea to review the rules to ensure that capital flows are better traced. i would point out that all this would not have been necessary if excessive liberalisation had not happened earlier.
in writing. ‒ the commission has proposed to the european parliament and the council to amend regulation (ec) no 184/2005 on community statistics relating to balance of payments, international trade in services and foreign direct investment. the amendment concerns implementing powers and would empower the commission to adopt certain measures. it aims to improve the transparency and detail of statistics on balance of payments, international trade in services and foreign direct investment and to bring regulation (ec) no 184/2005 into line with the treaty of lisbon. in its report, the committee recommends that parliament adopt the proposal with 28 amendments. i voted accordingly.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report amending regulation (ec) no 184/2005 on balance of payments, international trade in services and foreign direct investment. it is part of the overall union framework for monitoring economic developments in individual member states and in the union as a whole. in these areas, the production of reliable statistics is particularly important, as it is the only way to monitor developments in current account balances or in cash flows within and outside the eu. since the adoption of the original regulation and subsequent amendments, the volume and complexity of international capital flows have increased, making it more difficult to monitor and thus to combat tax fraud and aggressive tax planning. it was therefore necessary to update the regulation, thereby providing more reliable statistics for economic policy decisions. i support the amendment calling on the member states to provide the data needed to produce community statistics in a timely manner, in the form and with the required quality. furthermore, i agree with the use of innovative methods such as the global entity identifier.

in writing. ‒ articles 493 (1) and 498 (1) of regulation (eu) no 575/2013 exempt commodity exchanges from the provisions on large exposures and own funds requirements. the two exemptions expire on 31 december 2017. the commission has decided to combine the issue of the appropriate regime for commodity traders and the issue of prudential supervision of investment firms in a single review. this review has been initiated, but it is almost impossible that any act resulting from this review will be finalised, adopted and applied before the expiry of the current exemptions (end of 2017). it is therefore appropriate to extend the duration of those exemptions. to that end, the commission has proposed to the european parliament and the council that that regulation be amended. in its report, the economic and monetary committee recommends that parliament adopt the commission's proposal. i voted accordingly.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the proposal to amend regulation (eu) no 575/2013 which accepted the extension of the current exemptions provided for in the capital requirements regulation (crr). the relevant articles of the crr exempt commodity exchanges from the provisions on large exposures and own funds requirements. the purpose of this provision was to give regulatory authorities time to develop prudential rules that are appropriate to the risk profile of commodity traders. as both exemptions expire on 31 december 2017 and as the report points out, it is unlikely that the review of investment firms will be completed or the relevant legal act adopted and applied by the deadline, i supported the extension of the exemptions. moreover, it would create an unstable situation if, from the current system of exemptions from the provisions on large exposures and own funds requirements, commodity traders were first subject to a temporary regime fully implementing the requirements of the crr/crd and then very shortly thereafter to a framework specifically designed for them.
in writing. ‒ the requirements of regulation (eu) no 575/2013 (the capital requirements regulation, crr) and directive 2013/36/eu (the capital requirements directive, crd) apply to both credit institutions and investment firms. the capital requirements regime for investment firms is based on the regime for credit institutions, adapted to take account of the investment services provided by investment firms. i voted in favour, following the s&d group's position.

in writing. under regulation (eu) no 1169/2011 on the provision of food information to consumers, the european commission had to submit a report on the mandatory indication of the origin of certain foods. the results of the reports on dairy products and meat products other than beef, pigmeat, sheepmeat, goatmeat and poultrymeat are presented in full colour. the consumer demand for information on origin and the economic impact of the mandatory indication of origin also vary significantly between the different categories. while consumers are interested in the origin of milk and meat products used as ingredients in dairy products, their willingness to pay for this information seems to be rather modest. the disclosure of this information by the manufacturer would entail additional costs and administrative burdens. the report concluded that voluntary designation of origin would cause the least disturbance to the market and would not affect the price of the products. according to a national survey of hungarian consumers, the vast majority of consumers consider it particularly important that a food be of hungarian origin. they require, in order to make their purchasing decisions, to be provided with sufficient and reliable information on the origin of the product in the case of milk and milk products. the question is therefore whether the ratio of costs to benefits justifies the compulsory introduction of the indication of origin. to this end, voluntary and mandatory options for designation of origin should be examined, taking into account consumer considerations and the possibilities of food business operators.
in writing. we must put the health of the citizens of the european union first and support it in all our decisions. it's our duty, and everything else has to be secondary. the indication of the country of origin or place of provenance of meat and processed meat products has already generated serious debate at expert committee level. it has raised serious concerns among some operators, who consider that such mandatory indication of origin would lead to significant additional production costs. i did. however, such a price effect is only applicable if the raw material in question has so far been obtained from third, or even questionable, sources. however, if the raw material was sourced from the eu market or from a country with adequate quality assurance, this negative effect disappears. i do not accept the rhetoric of the tidal wave. and i would go further: why not extend this capability to other products? of course, this can only be solved by a serious planning and legislative process and by clarifying definitions. but i think the principle itself is supportive. i think it is important to mention that this is not a question of good or bad labelling, and i do not accept labelling as 'harmful' or 'healthy' simply because of the sugar or salt content. this is about ensuring that consumers can decide whether they want to buy food produced under the eu's high quality assurance system or choose another.

in writing. ‒ the report concerns the amendment of directive 2011/16/eu as regards the mandatory automatic exchange of information in the field of taxation. the problem of crossborder tax avoidance, aggressive tax planning and harmful tax competition has become an increasingly serious challenge for eu member states in recent years. under the current legal framework (directive 2011/16/eu on administrative cooperation), member states do not yet share their country-by-country reports with each other, but there is an urgent need to increase the transparency of taxation in order to prevent tax evasion. the amendment will require multinational groups of companies located or operating in the union with aggregate consolidated revenues of at least eur 750 million to submit country-by-country reports. the member state which received the country-by-country report shall communicate the report by automatic exchange to all other member states in which one or more of the companies of the multinational group of companies are resident for tax purposes. the country-by-country report shall contain information such as the amount of revenue, profit before tax, income tax paid and payable, number of employees, amount of registered capital, profit margin and tangible assets. since multinational groups are required to submit a country-by-country report for the reporting financial year each year from 2017 onwards and since the amendment is designed to curb tax avoidance, i voted in favour of the amendment.
in writing. ‒ in recent years, the challenges of cross-border tax avoidance, aggressive tax planning and harmful tax competition have become more acute. in the econ and taxe reports, we have strengthened the legal framework for the transparency of tax information, in particular by introducing country-by-country reporting for multinational groups of companies. the panama papers scandal has shown that there is a great need for increased transparency. i agree with the rapporteur that the proposal is a step in the right direction, particularly with regard to the need to increase transparency and the threshold for multinational groups of companies to be required to report on a country-by-country basis. the report welcomes the transparency requirements for multinational groups. increased transparency may also provide an incentive for multinational groups to meet their tax obligations to a greater extent in the country where they operate. the introduction of automatic exchange of information between national tax authorities is more important than ever. the competitiveness of european businesses and the performance of the economy are at stake. i congratulate my colleague from the rosati group on the excellent report which i supported with my vote in favour.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution, mainly because of its consumer protection aspects. as is well known, the european union is the world's largest market for seafood, with a significant share of imports from third countries. i think it is important that consumers are informed about where they are caught and that imported products comply with eu rules and standards. i share the concern that significant mislabelling and abuse on the eu market could lead to serious problems. i therefore agree that member state controls should be strengthened, that the fight against fraud should be stepped up and that a system of voluntary or compulsory certificates could be useful. the commission has also proposed that the european parliament and the council adopt a common position on the proposal for a regulation on the establishment of a european environment agency. this means that they are not only important from the consumer side, but they can also be effective tools from the producer side. i believe that, like the different foodstuffs, the different systems of authorisations for the marketing of fish in the member states can lead to misunderstandings and abuses, and i therefore welcome the convergence of these systems and their publication in all the official languages of the union. i also believe it is important to exploit marine resources sustainably and to fight against illegal fishing.

in writing. ‒ the proposal for a decision addresses the preconditions for the implementation of the 2030 agenda for sustainable development. as you know, the 2030 agenda was adopted at the united nations summit on sustainable development in new york in september 2015. united nations general assembly resolution 70/1 calls for an annual assessment of progress in this area in order to achieve the commonly agreed goals (basically to keep global warming below 2°c, but if possible below 1.5°c). to achieve the objectives, 17 strands have been identified, including 169 targets, and progress towards these has been measured by 230 global indicators. the resolution calls on the commission to prepare a proposal for its sustainable development strategy with the full involvement of parliament. as the high level political forum on the issue will reconvene in july 2016, the eu will have to define its own position and member states will have to develop their own indicators in line with the global indicators . the proposal limits the waste of resources that has been created in the developed countries, it would stop the destruction of the environment, one of the consequences of which is the catastrophic rapid extinction of animals, and that is why i voted in favour of the adoption of the resolution.

in writing. ‒ in recent decades, the european union has introduced two pieces of legislation on family leave. the maternity leave directive was adopted in 1992 and the original parental leave directive in 1996, which was adapted in 2010 following a new agreement with the european social partners on the issue. the aim of the report by the employment and social committee is to assess the implementation of parental leave legislation by the member states and to draw the necessary political conclusions. these conclusions state that:• the legislation on parental leave should be reviewed and strengthened in terms of duration, remuneration, transferability and scope; • the legislation on maternity leave should also be reviewed in line with recent european parliament resolutions;• european legislation should also be adopted on paternity leave;• these laws should be developed in a consistent manner, in particular on the basis of agreements between the european social partners. i supported the bill.

in writing. ‒ alternative ways of reducing prostitution and demand for it, and protecting the human rights of sex workers are issues that merit a separate parliamentary debate. the report on the prevention of trafficking in human beings and protection of victims is aimed at criminalising criminals who profit from the trafficking and exploitation of human beings, not at solving this issue. the criminalization of demand for prostitution has been in place in sweden for 15 years, in norway for 8 years. however, after all this time, there is no convincing evidence that this legal solution has reduced the number of sex workers and victims of forced sex work exploited by human trafficking. however, there are many examples and studies that show that it has increased the vulnerability of sex workers, contributed to their stigmatization, and reduced their access to health and justice. more and more large and well-known organizations are protesting this solution, citing these studies, arguing for alternative solutions to reduce demand. so, criminalizing demand not only failed to achieve the desired goal of reducing demand, but it also made people who were already on the black market even more vulnerable, forcing them to work in a much more dangerous environment, exposed to abuse and harassment. this is particularly worrying because these people are already living on the margins of society. the european parliament has a duty to protect the human rights of all europeans, including sex workers.

in writing. the ongoing energy transition from a fossil-based energy system to one based on renewable energy should result in stable, sustainable, affordable energy, energy-efficient products and housing, and a consumer-friendly energy market for citizens. the most effective and efficient way to increase the security of supply, which is so important for hungary, is to reduce consumption and to treat energy saving and energy efficiency as a priority. the present parliament's proposal places a strong emphasis on energy efficiency, consumer protection against unfair practices and increased transparency and publicity of invoices. as a country with a low dependence on economically recoverable fossil fuels and an export orientation, it is particularly important for our country to reduce energy consumption through energy efficiency measures, the use of innovative technologies and the development of a targeted approach, and the environmental awareness of social actors. sustainable and secure energy systems must be established, which also enhance the competitiveness of the economy. all these measures have other positive effects besides energy savings resulting in a healthier environment and quality of life, and greater energy independence.
in writing. the new energy guideline for consumers report is an important milestone in the achievement of the energy union's objectives. providing stable, affordable, efficient and sustainable energy is a primary interest of citizens. the development of consumer-friendly, competitive and well-functioning energy markets is key and full implementation of the third energy package is essential to achieve these objectives. as the report emphasises, adequate consumer information is a prerequisite for energy-saving behaviour. as a result, it is in our common interest to improve the transparency of invoices and to ensure the comparability of service invoices, as this may even lead to lower maintenance costs. it is particularly practical for consumers to be provided with up-to-date and understandable comparison tools, to create interfaces, to be informed about these possibilities. the provision of a switch to another provider is a fundamental condition for competition. although i do not agree with every point in the report, the direction is good and should be supported.
in writing. – energy poverty affects a large share of the world’s population. within the eu 11% of the population is not able to adequately heat their homes at an affordable cost and energy poverty affects around 54 million people (2012 figures). the problem is particularly prevalent in central, eastern and southern europe. at the global scale the climate agreement achieved in paris as well as the sustainable development goals adopted last autumn (sdg 7 in particular, ‘ensure access to affordable, reliable, sustainable and modern energy for all’) contribute to an enhanced cooperation in this field. yet the eu should make sure these global commitments are translated into actions. combatting energy poverty requires a complex and pragmatic approach. many eu member states do not assess energy poverty properly, they do not even identify vulnerable consumers, making it impossible to adequately target measures. energy efficiency improvements in low-income and vulnerable households should be strongly incentivized. raising awareness and enabling informed decisions would be also important. besides, the european commission should allocate a much higher share of eu funds to energy efficiency programmes for vulnerable, energy-poor households and it should provide recommendations to its member states on improved monitoring and on specific energy poverty measures.
in writing. - mr president, i have to go. the elimination of energy poverty is one of the most pressing challenges facing europe in the 21st century. while in europe about 50 million people live in energy poverty, in hungary, statistics show that every fifth household, or up to two million people, live in energy poverty. this situation is unsustainable and has not been resolved by the official pricing policy in hungary, i.e. the policy of reducing vat. the average hungarian household uses almost twice as much energy per square metre as the eu average. according to these figures, the energy poverty of a quarter of hungarian households is not caused by high energy prices relative to income per se, but to a significant extent by the low level of energy efficiency of buildings. we need to change that now. it is unacceptable that in 2016 someone cannot heat their home, bathe in cold water, turn on their reading lamp or charge their mobile phone. i therefore believe that we must guarantee in eu legislation the basic right to energy, the minimum energy service, which is a basic right for all citizens. at the same time, we need well-targeted social energy tariffs for those most in need. the medium-term solution is to start self-generating energy in otthoni, to support the deployment of domestic wind turbines and solar panels, and to support large-scale energy efficiency improvement programmes.

in writing. ‒ the report focuses on the rapidly expanding virtual currencies, of which bitcoin is the best-known example, and proposes that the commission establish a working group to study this. seven years after the launch of bitcoin, the first and most widely used virtual currency, it has become clear that the underlying innovation, shared ledger technology, is having a significant impact on the financial sector and beyond. this technology should allow for the decentralised, fast, reliable and relatively secure recording of any transaction together with the history of previous transactions in a shared ledger. increasingly, investment is being made in shared accounting technology and certain applications can quickly become system-wide. however, as the committee on the internal market and consumer protection points out, the use of virtual currencies carries potential risks to the financial system, both in terms of regulation and market surveillance and security, and may pose a threat to financial integrity and effective financial regulation. the spread of virtual currencies may increase the risks to financial stability. since the report merely proposes the creation of a working group to study the internet currency called virtual money, i supported it.
in writing. ‒ virtual currencies are innovative products, an opportunity to be seized, but as a novelty, we must be very careful about how we regulate them. the closest i can draw to comparing bitcoin to uber is that both are new, both are popular tools for our citizens, but both are dangerous. the first problem is that it has generated opposition among its traditional peers, and the second is that the national bodies have not yet been able to keep up with the pace of regulation. these factors weaken these products, including the largest virtual currency player, bitcoin, which is also mentioned in the report. i am convinced that virtual exchanges can offer the internal market further opportunities for development and can certainly be useful as a means of functioning as a basic account or as a facilitator of online purchases. of course, it is very important that we give our consumers a proper guarantee of the safety of the product. i believe that the issue and regulation of virtual exchanges should be manageable. it is important to consider the possibilities of technological progress, and the rapporteur has done a great job on this, so i voted in favour of the report.

in writing. virtual currencies operate in a crossfire of often conflicting opinions. the eu has no position of its own, although this rapidly expanding technology allows any transaction to be carried out in a decentralised, reliable, fast and secure manner, with a record of previous transactions. the report simply calls for the commission to set up a working group to study virtual currencies, which is a small but welcome step. this approach may lead to more competitive transaction costs within the single market in the near future, but the use of virtual currencies may also entail potential risks. it is certainly timely to review the new technology in more detail.
in writing. ‒ the report of the committee on economic and monetary affairs points out that transaction costs for payments remain surprisingly high, while virtual currencies and shared accounting technology offer the potential to reduce these transaction costs, are easy to use and provide a reliable and variable level of confidentiality. however, some risks are already apparent, such as the use of certain applications for criminal purposes, including money laundering or terrorist financing, and further risks may be identified with wider adoption. the report therefore calls for smart regulation to address risks, where appropriate, before they become systemic. the report therefore proposes the creation of a horizontal working group on shared accounting technology, chaired by the commission. i supported the adoption of the report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on virtual currencies, which gives a balanced picture of virtual currencies as an alternative to currencies in circulation. i believe it is appropriate that the rapporteur draws attention to the potential risks inherent in virtual currencies and shared accounting technology, such as terrorist financing, money laundering, tax evasion and tax avoidance, and to the risks that virtual currency holders may face, such as theft of virtual currencies, hacking or software/hardware malfunctioning. at the same time, the report highlights the benefits of this relatively new currency and the additional opportunities it offers. i agree with the extension of the scope of the aml directive to virtual currency trading platforms and support the proposal that the commission should carry out a comprehensive analysis of virtual currencies and, on the basis of this analysis, consider revising, if necessary, the eu legislation on payments, thereby helping to strengthen competition and reduce transaction costs. i also support the establishment of a coherent and comprehensive eu-wide strategy on virtual currencies and technologies that protects against the risks listed but does not hinder innovation or distort markets. finally, i particularly welcome the fact that the report has highlighted the importance of raising consumer awareness.
in writing. ‒ seven years after the launch of bitcoin, the first and most widely used virtual currency, it has become clear that the underlying innovation, shared ledger technology, is having a significant impact on the financial sector and beyond. increasingly, investment is being made in shared accounting technology and certain applications can quickly become system-wide. while there are still some questions about the extent of the current technological transformation, the enormous potential and the not-to-be-neglected risks make it timely for the european parliament to present its first report on virtual currencies and shared ledger technology. i supported him with my vote.
in writing. ‒ the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) aims to support the reintegration into the labour market of workers and self-employed persons made redundant as a result of globalisation, as a result of major structural changes in world trade patterns, or as a result of the prolongation of the global financial and economic crisis or a new global financial and economic crisis. france has submitted an application to mobilise the egf, under the reference number egf/2015/010 fr/moryglobal, for a financial contribution from the egf. the commission has examined the application and found that it complies with the requirements of the relevant regulation, and i have therefore voted in favour of the adoption of the proposal.
in writing. following redundancies at moryglobal sas, the french authorities submitted an application for a financial contribution from the egf under the reference number egf/2015/010 fr/moryglobal. following the evaluation of the application, the commission has concluded that, in accordance with all the relevant provisions of the egf regulation, the conditions for granting a financial contribution from the egf are met. the request concerns 2 132 workers made redundant by moryglobal sas. the amount requested is eur 5 146 800. the fidesz-kdnp delegation supports the motion in solidarity. it is important that dismissed workers receive appropriate support for their reintegration into the labour market.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the request from france to mobilise the egf. the union has established legislative and budgetary instruments to provide additional support to workers made redundant as a result of major structural changes in world trade patterns or as a result of the global financial and economic crisis, and to support their reintegration into the labour market. in the interests of european workers, workers who have been put in a difficult situation by the crisis should be given the possibility to take corrective measures to reposition them on the labour market. i agree with the rapporteur that france's request is justified, since the situation of the workers concerned was caused by the bankruptcy and liquidation of the undertaking. france has launched the social plan, in which moryglobal is also financially involved, before receiving the additional egf support. the redundancies at moryglobal are linked to the general decline in production in europe, which has led to a decrease in the volumes to be transported and a price war in the road transport sector.
in writing. ‒ the european globalisation adjustment fund aims to provide additional support to workers affected by the consequences of major structural changes in world trade. the commission has now proposed, at the request of france, the mobilisation of eur 5 146 800 from the fund to help resolve the situation of 2 132 workers made redundant following the judicial winding-up of moryglobal, a company engaged in the provision of services in the field of land and pipeline transport and ancillary services in the field of storage and transport. the report concludes that the conditions laid down in article 4 (1) (a) of regulation (eu) no 1309/2013 of the european parliament and of the council are met and that france is therefore entitled to that financial contribution. it therefore proposes that parliament contribute to the mobilisation of the european globalisation adjustment fund within the general budget of the european union for the financial year 2016, in the amount of eur 5 146 800, in the form of commitment and payment appropriations. i voted for the motion.
