in writing. ‒ the eu-us safe harbour convention was repealed by the european court of justice in its judgment of 6 october 2015. the court found that the convention did not provide adequate protection of the data of eu citizens, did not prevent mass surveillance and did not provide for adequate judicial redress against it. the european commission and the us authorities have been working together on a new agreement called the privacy shield. the agreement also aims to prevent national authorities from imposing rules that would prevent the transfer of personal data of eu citizens to the us after the abolition of safe harbour. this intention must be regarded as a restriction of national self-determination. the basic objection is that the ombudsman designated by the us in the draft treaty is not an institution adequate to provide an impartial remedy in the event of a conflict between the us authorities and eu citizens. analysis by civil society organizations suggests that the new contract could also contribute to the mass collection of data by the us intelligence community. the concerns listed in the joint motion for a resolution are mentioned only by way of reference and not as a specific requirement. support for the decision thus signifies that parliament agrees to the conclusion of the agreement in question. i therefore voted against the motion.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution tabled by my group colleagues. the protection of personal data, respect for privacy and private communications, the right to security, the right to know and to be informed and the right to conduct a business are all fundamental rights which, under the charter of fundamental rights of the european union, the eu must protect and balance within the community. transatlantic data flows provide opportunities for the us and the eu to expand trade and investment in the developing world. with the global growth of internet access, we need to focus on the opportunities for online international trade and the need for free data flows. moreover, data flows create new opportunities for smes to participate adequately in international trade and to better access new markets on other continents. the commission should be able to take into account the specific circumstances of the case, including the need to ensure that the data subject is protected in accordance with the law of the member state concerned.
in writing. ‒ the verts/ale, ppe, efdd, s&d, gue/ngl, ecr and alde groups have tabled a motion for a european parliament resolution on the subject. five of them, the epp, the efdd, the s&d, the ecr and alde, reached an agreement and adopted a compromise proposal. i abstained because i agree with the agreement reached between the european commission and the united states government, which does not require any further changes.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the motion for a joint resolution on transatlantic data flows. like the motion, i welcome the commission's work on a new data protection shield for transatlantic data flows. i agree that transatlantic relations remain of paramount importance to the parties, but at the same time the right of citizens to the protection of their personal data in the european union is unquestionable and cannot be infringed by the transfer of their data to third parties. i support the call in the motion for the commission to fully implement the recommendations of the article 29 working party on the privacy shield decision. i agree with the motion and believe that legal certainty on the protection of personal data moving between the eu and the us is also the basis for consumer confidence, transatlantic business development and law enforcement cooperation. it is therefore essential to ensure that the means by which such data flows are made possible comply with both primary and secondary community law.

in writing. the new energy guideline for consumers report is an important milestone in the achievement of the energy union's objectives. providing stable, affordable, efficient and sustainable energy is a primary interest of citizens. the development of consumer-friendly, competitive and well-functioning energy markets is key and full implementation of the third energy package is essential to achieve these objectives. as the report emphasises, adequate consumer information is a prerequisite for energy-saving behaviour. as a result, it is in our common interest to improve the transparency of invoices and to ensure the comparability of service invoices, as this may even lead to lower maintenance costs. it is particularly practical for consumers to have up-to-date and understandable comparison tools, to have platforms, to be informed about these possibilities. the provision of a switch to another provider is a fundamental condition for competition. although i do not agree with every point in the report, the direction is good and should be supported.

in writing. ‒ i supported the report by mr griffin, as the energy union must put the interests of present and future generations of citizens first and provide consumers with affordable and efficient energy and high quality energy-efficient products, services and buildings. however, in many member states market concentration is still high and the reduction in wholesale costs is often not reflected in retail prices. the commission should identify or develop further indicators for well-functioning consumer-friendly energy markets, taking into account the economic impact on energy consumers switching, technical barriers to switching or contracting, or levels of consumer awareness. in my view, market-determined prices are in the consumer's favour and network charges should therefore be designed to allow for a reasonable cost recovery and not to impede energy efficiency measures. the third energy package needs to be fully implemented, including the right to switch free of charge and improving consumer information on their rights.

in writing. ‒ the committee on industry, research and energy recommends that parliament welcomes the commission communication of 15 july 2015 entitled 'a new direction for energy consumers'. the report recalls that the ultimate goal should be to achieve an economy based on 100% renewable energy. to that end, the energy union should provide citizens with stable, affordable, efficient and sustainable energy and high-quality energy-efficient products, services and buildings; enable citizens to produce, consume, store and sell their own renewable energy, whether individually or collectively; contribute to the eradication of energy poverty; protect consumers from abusive, anti-competitive and unfair practices by market players; and create favourable conditions for a well-functioning and competitive internal energy market. i voted for the report.

in writing. ‒ the energy union should provide citizens with stable, affordable, efficient and sustainable energy and high-quality, energy-efficient products, services and buildings. i voted in favour of the accompanying document.
in writing. ‒ the economic crisis, from which the union is gradually recovering, has, according to statistical data, led to a dramatic increase in the number of people, both men and women, facing the threat of poverty and social exclusion. the latest statistical surveys available on income inequality in the eu show that 16.6% of the population of the eu-28 can be considered at risk of poverty, even when social benefits are taken into account. the risk rate was 17.2% for women and 16.1% for men. the gender pay gap and the pension gap are the result of the fragmentation of careers in an attempt to achieve a harmonious balance between work and private life. it is important that women receive equal pay for equal work and it is of the utmost importance that this principle is accepted and applied in practice. unfortunately, the report contains elements that urge steps towards the individualisation of rights in policies to ensure social equality (which may raise constitutional problems) or calls on the commission to develop proposals for the gender dimension of tax policy, which is a matter of national competence. equally absurd is the demand for the institution of joint pension rights for divorced or separated persons, or for additional rights and benefits for lgbti families. for all these reasons, i abstained on the motion, despite its positive elements.
in writing. ‒ the report of the committee on women's rights and equal opportunities analyses the problem of poverty affecting women at a higher rate than the average. it points out that according to statistical surveys, 16.6% of the eu population can be considered at risk of poverty, a risk rate of 16.1% for men and 17.2% for women. in addition, certain groups of women - particularly single mothers, pensioners, immigrants or women with disabilities - are exposed to significantly higher levels of exposure than the average. it points out that two thirds of all working hours in the world are worked by women, who nevertheless earn only 10 percent of the world's income and own less than 1 percent of the world's wealth. the report sets out the efforts that the union and the member states should make to ensure that everyone, regardless of gender, has equal opportunities and opportunities in employment, social security, earning a living, education, childcare and culture. it also identifies the instruments that europe and the member states already have in place to tackle the trends that threaten to impoverish half the population. it stresses that combating women's poverty is, at least in part, a way to solve the long-term problem of child poverty. i voted for the motion.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report, given that it provides a thorough analysis and lists some remarkable facts which demonstrate that women are the most vulnerable group in society, also in terms of social deprivation, and are exposed to many forms of discrimination. i am particularly concerned about the labour market situation and the marginalisation of women, which often takes place against the background of poverty. in connection with the report, i recalled that i had previously taken the initiative to ensure that women alongside other groups particularly exposed to crime such as children and the elderly automatically receive priority protection throughout the union from a police and judicial point of view. in the spirit of this debate and resolution, i believe that this type of preference should be applied with similar naturalness and automaticity in the social and labour field, and i will therefore, in my further work in parliament, seek to promote a better coordination of our various political and legislative efforts on gender equality, based on facts and arguments that are in many respects similar.
in writing. ‒ according to the latest eurostat data, the number of women living in poverty (currently 64.6 million) remains consistently higher than that of men living in poverty (currently 57.6 million). it shows that poverty affects women and men differently. for women, the risk of poverty in the eu-28 was particularly high in 2014, with a poverty rate of 46.6% for women without social benefits and 17.7% with social benefits. i voted in favour of the report on the agenda.
in writing. ‒ the report aims to remove the non-tariff barriers that exist in some member states and that restrict the free flow of services in particular. it is based on the assumption that the single market in services is estimated to represent some 70% of the european economy, but accounts for only around 20% of intra-union trade, and that is a small fraction. it stresses that the strengthening of the single market requires urgent action at both eu and member state level to remove these non-tariff barriers. i reject the whole thought process and intention. these non-tariff rules exist because each member state protects local society and entrepreneurs. the brussels centre does not assume the losses resulting from the dismantling of non-tariff barriers, which naturally primarily affect the less developed countries, since it is in the interest of the multinational companies of the centre countries to gain even more complete access to the services market. the dismantling of customs duties between six countries of similar development, which took about ten years at the beginning of integration, has been carried out very carefully, and now the member states with a highly heterogeneous economic and social structure, which has grown to 28 member states, want to impose uniform rules without first trying to bring each country to the same level through catch-up programmes. from all this, it's clear that i didn't support the report.
in writing. ‒ i am convinced that the removal of non-tariff barriers will help businesses across the union, but the main beneficiaries will be consumers. this is confirmed by a study prepared for the committee on the internal market and consumer protection, which concludes that 'the completion of the single market will benefit a few businesses, namely the most competitive and innovative ones, but will serve the interests of all consumers through lower prices and increased choice'. it is therefore in the interest of all member states and the european parliament to continue to remove those non-tariff barriers throughout europe in the interests of consumers. the notification obligation laid down in the services directive is a good example of the fact that the actions taken by member states do not reflect their commitments. i therefore agree with the rapporteur that the european commission can do more to ensure that these member states fulfil their commitments, but at the same time the member states themselves should also do more to keep their own promises. by cooperating and increasingly assessing each other's contribution to the single market, member states themselves can help to create a more competitive and open single market. for these reasons, i voted in favour of the report.

in writing. the report is highly unsportsmanlike, as if to say why should we have two separate events, the paralympics and the olympics, all competing for medals together. it is absolutely unacceptable, because these non-tariff rules are precisely designed to give individual member states a measure of protection for local society and businesses against the attacks of multinational companies. in the original spirit of integration, closure was a central aspect, for which the eu should now devote 5~7% of its gdp to closure in less developed regions. all that's forgotten today.
in writing. ‒ the creation of the single market is a major achievement. however, although customs barriers have been removed, businesses wishing to engage in cross-border trade or service activities in another member state may face a number of national regulations. the persistence of non-tariff barriers therefore hinders the full exploitation of the potential of the single market. the report of the committee on the internal market and consumer protection points out that not all non-tariff barriers need to be removed, but that some may exist which are contrary to the principles of proportionality and non-discrimination and which are not rooted in a public policy objective. the measures to improve the functioning of the single market should, according to the report, address these non-tariff barriers. the report stresses the need for two main changes: better and consistent enforcement of existing rules and a change in member states' attitudes to move away from increasingly protectionist measures and fully open up their domestic markets. it stresses that the removal of non-tariff barriers will help businesses across the union, but the main beneficiaries will be consumers. it is therefore in the interest of all member states and the european parliament to continue to remove those non-tariff barriers throughout europe in the interests of consumers.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report because it is sufficiently critical and can alert european decision-makers to the fact that governments serving the interests of producers with a high degree of economic and political influence are standing in the way of removing the non-tariff barriers that still restrict the single market too much. in my experience, some governments often see the arbitrary use of non-tariff barriers as a kind of political-tactical tool. of course, as the report indicates, practical considerations and the principle of subsidiarity require that, where appropriate, the use of non-tariff instruments should be possible in the future, in a timely manner and in a location. however, in my view, the primary consideration should be the interests of local smes and consumers throughout the eu, and in this context the promotion of healthy quality and price competition. the decades-long delay in completing the single market in reducing non-tariff barriers can only be overcome by a socially and politically sound approach to trade policy, which the report can help to develop, both for parliament and for the governments of the member states.
in writing. ‒ the report points out that more than 20 years after the single market was established, unjustified non-tariff barriers continue to create difficulties for trade and the free movement of goods and services between member states. the maintenance of these non-tariff barriers may be the result of protectionism and may involve bureaucratic burdens that are very often disproportionate to the objectives pursued. i voted in favour of the s&d group.
in writing. ‒ i supported the new eu strategy on the internal market, as i believe that the proposals in the reports can help to realise the potential of the single market and can serve as a good starting point for europe to succeed in the global economic arena. with today's ambitious and practical strategy, we're focused on results. the next step is for the eu institutions, in cooperation with the member states, to work towards implementing these concrete measures as quickly as possible. in my view, every effort should be made to ensure that consumers who wish to buy services or products in another member state, whether they buy online or in person, do not have to face different prices, changing sales conditions, different delivery methods, unless this can be justified by objective and verifiable arguments. the european commission and the european consumer centre often receive complaints alleging that consumers have been unfairly treated differently on the basis of their nationality or place of residence. this practice should be discontinued in the future. the reduction of investment restrictive measures and the creation of new opportunities for consumers, professionals and businesses must continue. the single market must keep pace with change and therefore encourage and embrace innovative new business models. on the basis of the above, i voted in favour of the adoption of the report.

mr president, we have heard a lot of important points and concerns regarding the belarusian nuclear power plant (npp) project, but i would like to turn your attention to the fact that, while we are worrying because of an npp construction close to the eu’s borders, there is also something to be worried about within the borders of the eu. in hungary, my state, two new russian—type blocks are going to be built in the next couple of years. this is just the same construction and the same technology as in ostrovets, belarus: the russian—type vver 1200 reactors. this member state, hungary, has already proved that it understands eu law in quite a ‘flexible’ way when it comes to nuclear projects. regarding this nuclear project in hungary, there was a veto from the euratom supply agency because the contract with russia was not in line with eu law. there is an ongoing infringement because of the lack of tendering, according to european public procurement law. there is an in-depth investigation because of non—tendering. there is an in-depth investigation because of possible forbidden state aid regarding the same project. that was a concluded pilot project because of the lack of transparency of the project. this member state intentionally violated the eu regulation regarding nuclear waste with unlawfully shipped nuclear waste from a former serious incident in the existing npp to russia in 2014. would you buy a used car from those guys? and do you think that it is a good idea to let it go when they plan to build a new russian nuclear power plant in the heart of europe? blue-card answer. – thank you for your question. i completely agree that we need strong cooperation between the member states. regarding this project, ten eu member states participated in the process under the espoo convention. still, i believe that there is not enough attention from the member states. mainly austria and germany expressed deep interest and concerns regarding the project, but i would like to ask the member states, including croatia, to be more active regarding this project. in small countries like hungary, nuclear investments are not single member state issues.
mr president just a few weeks ago, on 26 april, we recalled the chernobyl nuclear disaster, which, after ukraine and many other european countries, had the greatest impact on the population of belarus, with a lasting impact. this fact in itself shows that this is a european issue since in the event of a crisis, there are cross-border threats. it is in our common interest that the european union, despite the serious political differences, should take care to improve belarus' nuclear security. i would add that for this country, which is exposed to putin's power games in a thousand ways, this issue is not indifferent from the point of view of the eu's common foreign and security policy, since the energy component has long been a determining element of minsk's dependence on moscow. while we are trying to bring belarus into the 21st century with a common effort in terms of energy dependence and nuclear safety, we are having to deal with the fact that within the union, one of the member states, unfortunately my own country, the government of hungary, is using the paks ii treaty to return its country to the conditions of the 20th century. it's going to be a long decade of subjugating the country to moscow, both in terms of energy and in terms of finances. as a hungarian representative, i have therefore the duty to draw the attention of the commission and the european parliament to our agenda item: this is also a common european issue and a danger, since we are talking about a member state which, moreover, completely ignores everything that the commission has put before us in the context of the energy union, and which has received convincing support in this parliament. and let me conclude by saying that every new facility, every new nuclear facility is a new wound, a stab in the future of the earth. the spectacular progress made in renewable energy over the last ten years makes any further development of nuclear power plants totally unjustified.

in writing. unfair trading practices in business-to-business relationships have become increasingly prominent in recent years and, although it is difficult to assess the scale of the problem, there is a significant body of statistical and market-based evidence suggesting that unfair trading practices are relatively widespread, particularly in the food supply chain. many member states have recognised that unfair trading practices cause harm and have taken measures to combat them. however, there are also significant differences in the rules in this area between member states and the scale of the problem varies. in my view, the scale of the problem requires the adoption of eu legislation to ensure the proper functioning of markets and fair and transparent relationships between all actors in the food supply chain. i believe that strong, consistent action is needed to put an end to unfair trading practices in the eu food supply chain once and for all.

madam president, please. the panama papers, luxleaks and other scandals in recent years have made it clear that tax avoidance, aggressive tax planning, is one of the most serious problems facing governments in europe today. there are many important elements of this problem that have been raised in this debate and i think that the proposal that the commission has put forward and the report that parliament has produced identify the problems well. but we have to move on, and that's not enough. i want to highlight two areas that may not have been addressed in this debate: one is the nature of the tax system itself, the nature of european tax systems. of course, member states have the right to set their tax rates and to set their taxation methods, but we must know that as long as there are such fragmented tax systems in europe, companies in this european union will use the resulting tax optimisation opportunities, so the unification of taxation is inevitable in order to reduce tax avoidance. and the second is that it's not just about tax rates that are changing in general. this is legislation that is specifically tailored to specific companies. to give an example: in my country, hungary, last year, the american company general electric used a tax-fixing option under which, after earning some huf 4000 billion, or about eur 15 billion, it did not pay tax in the country where it operated, but as a result of sales and purchase agreements between various shady subsidiaries, it brought the tax-fixing option to hungary and there received tax benefits that could eventually reduce the corporate tax rate actually paid to 2%. i think this is a typical example of tax avoidance and these company-specific tax planning legislative processes also require the commission to pay very close attention. that's a two-card answer. i agree that the european union is not the united states. at the same time, i believe that the oecd standards should be applied to the fullest extent possible and that the existing instruments of the european commission and the european union should be used much more effectively to combat tax evasion. for example, in the case of taxation of such companies, as i have mentioned in the case of general electric, i think that the commission should take the strictest possible action, examine to what extent this violates, for example, the rules on unlawful state aid, the rules on the internal market, and in this case the commission should force european law, existing european law, to be applied.
mr president aggressive tax planning this is a concept that i'm afraid european citizens don't really understand, but i'd like to end my speech by saying a few words about it. so the practice of aggressive tax planning is totally unacceptable from the point of view of the integrity of the internal market, as well as social justice, and that is why i propose that we make the fight against tax fraud, tax evasion and tax avoidance a top political priority of the european union, that is to say, that we address these issues. europe cannot afford to let large multinational companies continue to take advantage of the differences between national tax systems without any problems, reducing the tax burden for themselves and increasing the tax burden for small and medium-sized enterprises and citizens who pay their fair share of tax. to achieve a reliable single market, member states need to harmonise their tax systems, which is a prerequisite for a well-functioning single internal market and economic and monetary union. the commission's directive very rightly seeks to address this situation with six specific anti-avoidance rules. the commission's proposal is to make the rules even more ambitious, since they now allow member states to deal effectively with corporate tax avoidance while ensuring free competition. one of the key elements in the fight against tax avoidance would be the introduction of a common consolidated corporate tax base, which could be a game changer in the fight against artificial tax base erosion and profit shifting strategies. the commission has already given a commitment to submit a proposal for a consolidated common corporate fund. it is important that this be published as soon as possible and that the negotiations on this issue be concluded as soon as possible. but i'm going to come back to aggressive tax planning. mr. president, i have to ask you... this is not just the fault of multinational corporations. these conditions are created by the member states of the european union. member governments create the rules that now result in large multinational companies paying at most under 5% and everyone else paying at most around 30%. this is shameful, this is untenable.

in writing. ‒ the world health organisation framework convention on tobacco control (fctc) is the first global treaty on health. the convention was created in response to the global epidemic of smoking and aims to address some of the causes of the phenomenon, including illicit trade in tobacco products. the eu's comprehensive strategy to combat cigarette smuggling has been in place since 2013. in this context, the eu has also strengthened the legal basis with the tobacco products directive, which is complemented by binding and enforceable anti-fraud agreements concluded by the eu and its member states with the four largest tobacco manufacturers (philip morris, japan tobacco international, british american tobacco (holdings) limited, imperial tobacco limited). the tobacco products directive already contains provisions on traceability and tracing, which have been developed in accordance with the fctc protocol. ratification of the fctc protocol is beneficial for public health and contributes to the fight against illicit tobacco trade, tax evasion and organised crime, which is why i voted in favour of the adoption of the report.
in writing. ‒ the world health organisation framework convention on tobacco control (fctc) is the first global treaty on health. the convention was created in response to the global epidemic of smoking and aims to address some of the causes of the phenomenon, including illicit trade in tobacco products. the protocol based on article 15 of the fctc on the elimination of illicit trade in tobacco products (fctc protocol) was adopted by the conference of the parties in seoul on 12 november 2012. the protocol is currently the only multilateral regulatory initiative in this field. the eu signed the fctc protocol on 20 december 2013. the protocol requires ratification by 40 parties for its entry into force. the eu's comprehensive strategy to combat cigarette smuggling has been in place since 2013. in this context, the eu has also strengthened the legal basis with the tobacco products directive, which is complemented by binding and enforceable anti-fraud agreements concluded by the eu and its member states with the four largest tobacco manufacturers (philip morris, japan tobacco international, british american tobacco (holdings) limited, imperial tobacco limited). the tobacco products directive already contains provisions on traceability and tracing, which have been developed in accordance with the fctc protocol. ratification of the fctc protocol is beneficial for public health and contributes to the fight against illicit tobacco trade, tax evasion and organised crime, which is why i voted in favour of the report.

in writing. ‒ the world health organisation framework convention on tobacco control (fctc) entered into force on 27 february 2005 and currently has 180 parties. the protocol, based on article 15 of the fctc, was adopted in seoul on 12 november 2012 and requires the ratification of 40 parties for its entry into force. the protocol establishes a complex system of measures, rules and policies to combat illicit trade in tobacco products. it aims to secure the supply chain of tobacco, tobacco products and manufacturing equipment by establishing a global traceability and tracing system. the ratification of the protocol is in line with the eu's comprehensive measures to improve supply chain security to combat cigarette smuggling in force since 2013. i voted for the motion.
in writing. ‒ the world health organisation framework convention on tobacco control (fctc) is the first global treaty on health. the convention was created in response to the global epidemic of smoking and aims to address some of the causes of the phenomenon, including illicit trade in tobacco products. the protocol based on article 15 of the fctc on the elimination of illicit trade in tobacco products (fctc protocol) was adopted by the conference of the parties in seoul on 12 november 2012. the protocol is currently the only multilateral regulatory initiative in this field. the eu signed the fctc protocol on 20 december 2013. the protocol requires ratification by 40 parties for its entry into force. the eu's comprehensive strategy to combat cigarette smuggling has been in place since 2013. in this context, the eu has also strengthened the legal basis with the tobacco products directive, which is complemented by binding and enforceable anti-fraud agreements concluded by the eu and its member states with the four largest tobacco manufacturers (philip morris, japan tobacco international, british american tobacco (holdings) limited, imperial tobacco limited). the tobacco products directive already contains provisions on traceability and tracing, which have been developed in accordance with the fctc protocol. ratification of the fctc protocol is beneficial for public health and contributes to the fight against illicit tobacco trade, tax evasion and organised crime, which is why i voted in favour of the report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the recommendation to give the go-ahead for a draft council decision on behalf of the eu on illicit trade in tobacco products. as explained in the reasoning for the recommendation, the world health organisation framework convention on tobacco control (fctc) is the first global health treaty, which entered into force on 27 february 2005. the eu signed the fctc protocol on 20 december 2013. the protocol requires the ratification of 40 parties for its entry into force and its ratification by the european union without delay would contribute significantly to the smooth entry into force and implementation of the fctc protocol. illicit trade in tobacco products causes an estimated €10 billion in lost revenue in the eu each year, in the form of unpaid taxes and duties alone. however, illicit trade and smuggling also undermine tobacco control policies and increase access to cheaper tobacco products. this process also involves serious health risks. analyses show that about 1 out of 10 cigarettes are sold illegally. while 15 years ago the eu market for illicit tobacco products was dominated by products smuggled into the eu by the main manufacturers, the market is increasingly characterised by a steadily increasing proportion of 'low-value' whites (these are other brands bought in non-eu countries and brought into the eu without paying taxes and duties, without a legitimate distribution network). the risk is increased by the fact that a significant proportion of tobacco products banned in the eu originate from third countries.

in writing. - i voted in favour of the recommendation. i agree with the report's finding that industrial production is increasingly taking place in global value chains and that therefore the removal of unnecessary barriers to trade and regulatory cooperation is essential to maintaining and strengthening a competitive and diverse industrial base in europe. as is well known, the automotive industry and its associated ancillary industries constitute a key economic sector in the european union. the automotive industry alone employs 12 million people and contributes 4% of the eu's gdp. this makes the eu one of the world's largest car manufacturers and the sector the largest investor in research and development. i think it is important to stress that the automotive industry offers a very strong added value at all stages of the chain and plays a significant role in safeguarding the euro area's trade balance. i support the eu strengthening the competitiveness of the eu automotive industry and safeguarding its global leadership in technology in order to maintain the vital position of the automotive industry. in line with the recommendation, i believe that international regulatory cooperation has the potential to promote a transparent, efficient and competitive economic environment, while at the same time creating and ensuring the highest levels of health and safety protection. in addition, regulatory coherence and transparency in the development and implementation of legislation are needed.
in writing. ‒ given the increasing interconnectedness of global markets (40% of european industrial products are made using imports from the upper levels of the supply chain) and the fact that industrial production increasingly takes place in global value chains, removing unnecessary barriers to trade and regulatory cooperation is essential to maintaining and strengthening a competitive and diverse industrial base in europe. i voted for it.
in writing. ‒ on 24 september 2012, the council authorised the commission to open negotiations with colombia and peru for the conclusion of the additional protocol to the trade agreement between the european union and its member states, of the one part, and colombia and peru, of the other part, to take account of the accession of croatia to the european union. the agreement liberalises trade in agricultural and industrial products and services. it also contains provisions on the origin of goods, technical barriers to trade, animal and plant health measures, competition, intellectual property and public procurement. croatia's participation in the trade agreement is a natural consequence of its accession to the union. the european parliament's agreement to this council decision is a mandatory element of the ratification process of the additional protocol and i therefore voted in favour of the report.

in writing. ‒ the trade agreement was signed in brussels on 26 june 2012. on 11 december 2012, the european parliament adopted a legislative resolution giving its consent to the conclusion of the agreement. on 24 september 2012, the council authorised the commission to open negotiations with colombia and peru for the conclusion of the additional protocol to the trade agreement to take account of the accession of croatia to the european union ('the protocol'). the council adopted a draft decision on the ratification of the additional protocol, which requires parliament's consent. in its report, the international trade committee stresses that croatia's participation in the trade agreement is a natural consequence of its accession to the union and therefore recommends that parliament give its consent to the conclusion of the additional protocol. i voted accordingly.
in writing. ‒ on 24 september 2012, the council authorised the commission to open negotiations with colombia and peru for the conclusion of the additional protocol to the trade agreement between the european union and its member states, of the one part, and colombia and peru, of the other part, to take account of the accession of croatia to the european union. the agreement liberalises trade in agricultural and industrial products and services. it also contains provisions on the origin of goods, technical barriers to trade, animal and plant health measures, competition, intellectual property and public procurement. croatia's participation in the trade agreement is a natural consequence of its accession to the union. the european parliament's agreement to this council decision is a mandatory element of the ratification process of the additional protocol and i therefore voted in favour of the report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the recommendation as it accepts that the trade agreement between the eu and its member states and colombia and peru be amended to take account of the accession of croatia to the eu. the adoption of this council decision by the ep is a mandatory element of the ratification process of the additional protocol. the adoption of this recommendation thus facilitates the process by which the republic of croatia, which acceded to the eu on 1 july 2013, is linked, under its act of accession, to agreements concluded or signed by member states and the eu with third countries prior to its accession.
in writing. ‒ the trade agreement between the european union and its member states, of the one part, and colombia and peru, of the other part, was signed in brussels on 26 june 2012 and certain provisions thereof have been applied, in accordance with article 330 of the agreement, between the european union and peru as from 1 march 2013 and between the european union and colombia as from 1 august 2013. i voted in favour of the motion.
in writing. ‒ the council regulations proposed by the rapporteur for adoption establish enhanced cooperation on jurisdiction, applicable law and the recognition and enforcement of judgments in matters of property regimes of international couples, covering both matters relating to matrimonial property regimes and the property aspects of registered partnerships. the critical element is same-sex marriage and its property implications. in the event of such an acceptance, all member states, including hungary, would be obliged to apply the property consequences of a marriage between persons of the same sex, a state which, moreover, has established at constitutional level that marriage can only be concluded between a man and a woman. several member states also expressed concern that even if future legal instruments did not require the introduction of unknown legal entities into their own national legal systems the recognition of property consequences arising from such foreign legal entities in their countries would have a direct impact on their national family law system and family law policy. i abstained from the vote because of all this.
in writing. ‒ visa-free travel within the eu, and greater freedom of establishment than before, has increased the number of international couples by orders of magnitude. however, negotiations between all member states on the original proposals made by the commission in 2011 on matters concerning the property regimes of international couples, including both matrimonial property regimes and the property aspects of registered partnerships, as regards jurisdiction, applicable law and the recognition and enforcement of judgments, have come to a standstill. in 2013, parliament gave a favourable opinion on the 2011 draft legislation, but it became clear at the end of 2015 that not all member states in the council would be able to agree with the proposals. in this context, enhanced cooperation was considered as an ideal solution, given that 23 member states agreed in principle to adopt the two acts. the commission therefore prepared proposals for further acts in early 2016 using the enhanced cooperation procedure, building on the agreement reached previously on the content. in the present case, the conditions for the enhanced cooperation procedure are met and parliament's consent to enhanced cooperation in this area is warranted. this decision will be the subject of a procedural decision and the related reports, the evaluation of their detailed content and separate decisions. that's why i voted to approve the cooperation.

in writing. ‒ by the end of 2015, it became clear that the 2011 commission proposal on matters concerning the property regimes of international couples, which was supported by parliament, could not be reached in the council with the necessary consensus for adoption. however, as 23 member states agreed in principle to the proposal, the council adopted the proposal for a decision authorising enhanced cooperation, which requires parliament's consent. enhanced cooperation is the final option with the participation of at least nine member states when the objectives of cooperation cannot be achieved within a reasonable time by the union as a whole. it shall respect the union treaties and union law, as well as the competences, rights and obligations of member states not participating in the cooperation. it shall promote the objectives of the union, protect its interests and strengthen its integration process. finally, it must not affect the internal market or economic, social and territorial cohesion, nor must it discriminate against or impede trade between member states and distort competition between them. the report of the committee on legal affairs clearly states that these conditions are met in this case and therefore recommends that parliament give its consent to enhanced cooperation in this area. i voted accordingly.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the recommendation to authorise enhanced cooperation in the field of property regimes for international couples, as it gives the 18 member states the opportunity to cooperate more closely. since the recommendation will not have any negative impact on member states not wishing to participate in this enhanced cooperation, there is no obstacle to its adoption. i welcome the pursuit of enhanced cooperation in this area, as there are many practical problems of property rights faced by citizens in an international marriage or civil partnership. in everyday cohabitation, but also in a possible divorce, it is often difficult to decide which court has jurisdiction and which laws apply to the case. it follows that these citizens must suffer unintended and adverse consequences. the establishment of judicial cooperation based on the principle of mutual recognition of judicial decisions in civil matters involving several states is intended to improve this situation.
in writing. ‒ the decision to apply enhanced cooperation in matters concerning the property regimes of international couples including both matrimonial property regimes and the property aspects of registered partnerships in respect of jurisdiction, applicable law and the recognition and enforcement of judgments was taken after negotiations between all member states on the original proposals made by the commission in 2011 had reached a deadlock. i supported him with my vote.
in writing. ‒ the recommendation concerns the accession of the european union to the protocol on the fight against illicit trade of the who framework convention on tobacco control. the protocol aims to prohibit all forms of illicit trade in tobacco products. the protocol defines illicit trade in tobacco products as any practice or conduct that is related to the manufacture, transport, acquisition, possession, distribution, sale or purchase of tobacco products and that is prohibited by law. to address this problem, the protocol targets the tobacco supply chain through measures taken by governments. this also requires the establishment of a global cargo tracking and tracing system within five years of the entry into force of the protocol. a global information sharing point will therefore be established within the secretariat of the who framework convention on tobacco control. it will be responsible for managing the establishment of national and regional cargo tracking and tracing systems. these are all positive steps and i have therefore voted in favour of the motion.
in writing. ‒ in my opinion, the european union should ratify the world health organisation's protocol on illicit trade in tobacco products without delay. that is why we voted today to allow the council to continue negotiations on behalf of the union for the conclusion of the protocol. this protocol contains actions and strategies to combat illicit trade in tobacco, which in the long term contribute to the fight against money laundering, the fight against cross-border organised crime and the enforcement of tax and customs obligations.

in writing. ‒ this draft council decision aims at ratifying the provisions of the protocol on obligations relating to judicial cooperation in criminal matters and the establishment of the facts of criminal offences, already mentioned in paragraph 1. the report of the committee on civil liberties, justice and home affairs, with very similar reasoning to that contained in the report of the committee on international trade on the ratification of the protocol, already mentioned in paragraph 1, recommends that parliament should also agree to this draft council decision. i voted accordingly.
in writing. ‒ the recommendation addresses certain provisions of the world health organisation's protocol on the illicit trade in tobacco products, namely judicial cooperation in criminal matters and the establishment of criminal facts. to clarify the definition, the protocol defines illicit trade in tobacco products as any practice or conduct that is related to the manufacture, transport, acquisition, possession, distribution, sale or purchase of tobacco products and that is prohibited by law. to address this phenomenon, the protocol targets the tobacco supply chain through measures taken by governments, such as the establishment of a global traceability and tracing system. the recommendation notes that the protocol encourages and improves international cooperation, the sharing of valid information, technical and law enforcement cooperation, and mutual legal and administrative assistance. i agree that the tobacco industry has a responsibility in this process to act effectively and clearly in dealing with the illicit trade in its products. the protocol recognises the irreconcilable conflict between the tobacco industry and its public health interests. in the interest of public health, i have voted in favour of the recommendation.
in writing. ‒ the world health organisation's protocol on illicit trade in tobacco products should be ratified by the european union without delay. the protocol aims to prohibit all forms of illicit trade in tobacco products. the protocol defines illicit trade in tobacco products as any practice or conduct that is related to the manufacture, transport, acquisition, possession, distribution, sale or purchase of tobacco products and that is prohibited by law. i voted for it.
in writing. ‒ the lack of data has implications in several areas of the financial instruments market. as regards market regulation, it is clear that most market rules cannot be applied until the reference data is available and the infrastructures are in place to collect the additional data needed for the calculation of transparency and the reporting of positions. the new framework requires trading venues and systematic internalisers to communicate certain reference data on financial instruments to competent authorities in a way that uniquely describes the characteristics of financial instruments covered by the mifid ii package. i voted in favour of the report. i consider it essential that a sufficiently clear legal position is established by mid-2016 as regards the final requirements of the relevant regulatory technical standards.

in writing. in principle, democracy, with elected leaders and citizens' right to vote, is one of the european union's founding principles. in fact, the latter is limited to 1 day every 4 1/2 years for the most part, while the former is overridden daily by the power of the international financial institutions. in this context, it is already a step forward that the proposed directives can dampen speculation and reduce uncertainty in the financial system. the partial deferral is justified by objective reasons.
in writing. ‒ the commission has proposed to amend directive 2014/65/ec on markets in financial instruments with regard to certain dates. the report by the committee on economic and monetary affairs recommends that parliament should support the commission's proposal with two amendments. i voted accordingly.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on markets in financial instruments which recommends postponing the application of the measures transposing directive 2014/65/eu by member states and the repeal of directive 2004/39/ec for 12 months, until 3 january 2018. the new framework introduced by regulation (eu) no 600/2014 and directive 2014/65/eu requires trading venues and systematic internalisers to provide competent authorities with data on financial instruments covered by that directive. however, the development of the new data collection infrastructure has not yet taken place. therefore, while article 93 of directive 2014/65/eu requires member states to apply the measures transposing that directive from 3 january 2017, its implementation is not appropriate as the absence of data collection infrastructures would affect the full scope of both regulation (eu) no 600/2014 and directive 2014/65/eu. it is therefore appropriate to postpone the deadline by 12 months as recommended in the report, until the necessary operational tasks have been fully completed by the competent national authorities and the parties concerned.
in writing. ‒ the development of a new data collection infrastructure has started to ensure efficient and coordinated data collection. to that end, the european securities and markets authority (esma) shall, in cooperation with the national competent authorities, establish a system of reference data on financial instruments. i voted in favour of the relevant document.
in writing. ‒ the report concerns the amendment of previous regulations on markets in financial instruments, as the required deadlines cannot be met. it became clear already during the legislative procedure that a significant number of measures would be needed to implement the directives, and a period of 30 months was therefore provided for between adoption and application, instead of the usual 18-24 months. however, it has since become clear that the core data infrastructures will not be operational until 3 january 2017. in practice, this means that if the date of application remains unchanged, neither the competent authorities nor the market operators will be able to apply the new rules. the instability of the financial system is the result of the process of deregulation and liberalisation that began in the early 1990s, and which is also the consequence of the power of international financial institutions rising above the influence and power of democratic structures of nation-states, elected leaders. the directives referred to in this submission may dampen speculation and reduce uncertainty in the financial system, but they do not eliminate it. in this particular case, the introduction of certain measures was essentially postponed, since the information system needed for them could not yet be set up. i supported this delay.
in writing. ‒ the draft proposal aims to postpone the application of the two instruments that make up the package of directives on markets in financial instruments (mifid ii) in view of the challenges faced by the european securities and markets authority, national competent authorities and stakeholders in relation to technical implementation. the challenges are of such a magnitude that the core data infrastructures will not be operational on 3 january 2017. i voted in favour of the report. i consider it essential that a sufficiently clear legal position is established by mid-2016 as regards the final requirements of the relevant regulatory technical standards.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the adoption of the report which, in addition to recommending the postponement of the application of the measures transposing directive 2014/65/eu by the member states and the repeal of directive 2004/39/ec to 12 months after the entry into force of this directive, i.e. 3 january 2018, citing the lack of technical conditions, also recommends the amendment of regulations (eu) no 596/2014 and (eu) no 909/2014. regulation (eu) no 596/2014 and regulation (eu) no 909/2014 of the european parliament and of the council contain references to the date of application of regulation (eu) no 600/2014 and directive 2014/65/eu. therefore, in order to ensure legal certainty, and in line with the recommendation, i consider it appropriate to amend those regulations in such a way that they refer to directive 2004/39/ec until the deferred application of regulation (eu) no 600/2014 and directive 2014/65/eu.
in writing. ‒ the lack of data collection infrastructures also makes it difficult for investment firms to apply best practice. trading venues and systematic internalisers will not be able to publish data related to the quality of execution of transactions on those venues. i supported him with my vote.
in writing. ‒ the council nominated the lithuanian minister of finance, rimantas šadžius, as a member of the court of auditors. on the basis of the evaluation of the proposed candidate's capabilities, the parliament's committee on budgetary control has heard the candidate at its meeting on 23 may 2016 and, on that basis, recommends in its report that parliament give a favourable opinion on the council's proposal to appoint rimantas šadžius as a member of the court of auditors. i supported the motion.
in writing. ‒ the cv of rimantas šadžius, the candidate for the court of auditors, is impressive. he obtained a law degree and a master's degree in law at vilnius university, but also a chemistry degree in moscow. he has also served as minister of finance, deputy minister of health and deputy minister of social and labour affairs of the government of lithuania. i voted for his nomination.
in writing. ‒ i supported the report on the 2015 eu report on policy coherence for development. the commission document was published in august 2015, ahead of the adoption of the un 2030 agenda for development (undp). the eu participated as co-legislator in the development of the pcd concept. the report summarises the results achieved so far and sets out a debate on future directions. it analyses five priority areas: trade and finance, food security, climate change, migration and security. in the light of the migration crisis, the stability of the union's neighbourhood should be the eu's top priority. i believe that closer cooperation between the eu institutions and the member states is important. i agree with the rapporteur that a european council meeting on pcd should be organised before the publication of the next commission report for 2017 to promote the interinstitutional and national debate on pcd within the eu. it is necessary to define the commitment of each union institution to the pcd.

in writing. this report is something intangible, neatly wrapped in a communication cloak, the point being that it does not specifically assess what needs to be done and, of course, who needs to provide the resources and how much. this is also true, in large part, of the un's 2030 agenda for sustainable development. there remains the continuing regret that little progress has been made in its implementation and style, and the finding that few studies have been produced and that they have been disputed. we need concrete solutions to real problems.
in writing. ‒ the european commission publishes a report on policy coherence for development (pcd) every two years. the latest, fifth report, was published in august 2015, shortly before the formal adoption of the 2030 agenda for sustainable development by the un summit in new york in september, which includes the objective of 'strengthening policy coherence for sustainable development'. the commission has also received comments from the united kingdom, the united kingdom and the united states on the application of the union state aid rules to the measures provided for in article 107 (3) (c) of the treaty. the 2016 resolution analyses and makes specific recommendations in five priority areas (trade and finance, food security, climate change, migration and security). the report also points out that the refugee crisis and the uncertainty in the eu's neighbourhood are fundamentally challenging the eu (for example, european solidarity and the schengen system), and that stabilising the eu's neighbourhood should therefore be a top priority for the eu, with the pcd focusing on external action. notes that the combined role of the vice-president of the commission/high representative of the union for foreign affairs and security policy has led to significant progress in the application of the pcd in the field of the union's external actions; i voted for the resolution.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the adoption of the report because it actually highlights a number of long-standing shortcomings in institutional and policy coordination in the wider field of development policy. i considered that, although the pcd as a european concept was born well before the refugee crisis, it could be said that in the current situation, the creation of a close alignment between development and migration policies has become a vital issue for the effective functioning of the union. it is in the report, but i would have stressed even more strongly the urgency of involving the common foreign and security policy in improving coherence: in this context, the eeas should treat the stabilisation of the eu's neighbourhood as a priority task, placing community development objectives and instruments at the service of the management and prevention of the refugee crisis. i considered it a positive element of the compilation that like many other eu development goals and documents it emphasises the promotion of gender equality. in addition, i would like to see a similar horizontal and coherent approach in the future to children as the most vulnerable and disadvantaged group, whether in the management of food, poverty, disease, refugees or war situations.
in writing. ‒ the european commission (ec) published its fifth biennial report on policy coherence for development (pcd) in august 2015, shortly before the formal adoption of the 2030 agenda for sustainable development at the un summit in new york in september, which includes the objective of 'strengthening policy coherence for sustainable development'. i voted for the present document.

in writing. ‒ the new alliance for food and nutrition security in africa (nafsn) initiative was established in 2012 under the g8 umbrella as a public-private partnership (ppp) to boost private investment in agriculture to improve food and nutrition security in sub-saharan africa. the aim of nafsn is to replicate in africa the model of the 'green revolution' implemented in asia in the 1960s and 1970s, based on monoculture crop production, mechanization, biotechnology, fertilizer dependence, long distribution chains and the cultivation of export crops. the limitations of this approach are well known, in particular the environmental risks involved. the development committee report questions the ability of large-scale ppps such as nafsn to contribute to poverty reduction and food security, as there is a high risk that the poorest communities will have to bear most of the social and environmental risks associated with them. it suggests that the eu and its member states should stop their current support for nafsn and instead invest in an agricultural model that is sustainable, supportive of smallholder farming and women, and that unlocks the potential of domestic and regional markets in a way that benefits family farmers and provides consumers with good quality food at affordable prices. i supported the motion.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report because the aim of the alliance in the title is to improve food security and nutrition in africa and thus help 50 million people to get out of poverty by 2020 in sub-saharan africa. the report highlights that investment in smallholder farming has been neglected in africa over the past 30 years, while low-income countries have become significantly more dependent on food imports, leaving them vulnerable to price fluctuations in international markets. the alliance (after some technical modifications) may be able to contribute to poverty reduction and food security. another agricultural model needs to be invested in, one that is sustainable, that also supports small-scale farming and the participation of women in a way that benefits local farmers and provides consumers with good quality food at affordable prices. the alliance aims to replicate in africa the green revolution model implemented in asia in the 1960s and 1970s, based on monoculture crop production, mechanization, biotechnology, fertilizer dependence, long distribution chains and the cultivation of export crops. in addition, host country policies aim to create a business-friendly environment through infrastructure, tax, land or trade policy reforms, facilitating access to land set aside for long-term rental, and regulatory reforms in the field of seeds.
in writing. ‒ the new alliance for food and nutrition security in africa (nafsn) initiative was established in 2012 under the auspices of the g8 as a major public-private partnership to boost private investment in agriculture to improve food and nutrition security in sub-saharan africa. the eu is responsible for coordinating the implementation of the ivory coast and malawi. i supported him with my vote.
in writing. ‒ international financial reporting standards are principles-based, approach-based accounting standards, interpretations and frameworks issued by the international accounting standards board (iasb) based in london, creating a common language for global financial reporting. from 2005, the standards will also be mandatory in the european union for the consolidated accounts of companies whose securities are admitted to trading on a regulated market in a member state of the union. the rapporteur calls on the standard-setters to ensure their coherence within existing accounting standards and to promote international consistency. it also called on the commission to urgently implement the recommendations on the extension of the public good criterion, i.e. that accounting standards do not jeopardise the eu's financial stability or impede the eu's economic development. so this is a technical issue, the application of international financial standards in the union, which i supported. at the same time, i should note that the existence of these standards only mitigates, but does not stop, the financial instability that resulted from the financial liberalisation and deregulation measures of the 1990s.
in writing. as i have pointed out on several occasions, the origins of financial instability lie in the financial liberalisation and deregulation measures of the 1990s. since then, there have been various attempts to promote stability, but these, by the logic of things, can only mitigate the problems. of course, this technical report, which aims to simplify the rules, should also be supported, but only radical solutions could really be taken to combat lability.
in writing. ‒ the international accounting standards board (iasb) develops high-quality, globally applicable accounting standards, thereby creating a common language for global financial statements. since 2005, publicly traded companies in the eu have been required to prepare their consolidated financial statements in accordance with these standards. the economic and monetary affairs committee reported that the application of international financial reporting standards in the eu has contributed to strengthening the single market and has enhanced the competitiveness of the european economy by enabling companies to attract capital and investments on global capital markets. however, the financial crisis has also shown that financial reporting standards need to be reviewed and improved. the report stresses the need to develop coherent financial reporting standards and considers it of utmost importance to ensure european influence throughout the standard-setting process, and particularly at its early stages, in order to ensure that international accounting standards represent the european economic interests. i voted for the resolution.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the evaluation of international accounting standards, as i believe it correctly highlights the importance of financial reporting standards and summarises in detail the areas where as the financial crisis has made clear revision and revision of standards are inevitable. i strongly support the part of the report which calls for the introduction of country-by-country reporting under ifrs, as this could play a decisive role in tackling tax avoidance and tax fraud. indeed, it is also urgently necessary to examine whether accounting standards allow for tax fraud and tax evasion and to identify measures to avoid and prevent possible abuses. it is also essential, as the report underlines, to be fully aware of the impact of accounting standards. therefore, both the international accounting standards board and the european financial reporting advisory group should give priority to strengthening their impact assessments, in particular with regard to the macroeconomy. finally, i welcome the view that only simple rules can be effectively applied and supervised. the complexity of ifrss should therefore be reduced in order to ensure the long-sought greater transparency and comparability of corporate financial data.
in writing. ‒ the international accounting standards board (iasb), based in london, develops high-quality, globally applicable accounting standards, thereby creating a common language for global financial statements. the rapporteur of the opinion recognises the importance of such globally applicable standards in improving competition and removing barriers to investment at a global level. i supported him with my vote.
in writing. ‒ i agree with the report's statement that the un is one of the principal custodians of international peace and security. there are now 16 un peacekeeping operations, more than ever before, involving 120,000 personnel. over the past decade, the situation has changed dramatically and in many areas, peacekeeping and counter-terrorism operations have become a part of everyday life that must be addressed. as african crises require a coherent global response that goes beyond purely security considerations, the role of the african union, in which the eu should play a significant role, should also be further strengthened. the report welcomes the strategic partnership between the un and the eu on peacekeeping and crisis management and its priorities for the period 2015-2018. at the same time, i would like to emphasise that the proper management of these complex partnerships, avoiding duplication of missions, is essential for the success of operations. the report urges the eu to work towards a proper division of labour and to focus on those areas where it can deliver the most added value. for these reasons, i voted in favour of the report.

in writing. ‒ the report of the foreign affairs committee praises the eu's peace support operations and advocates deepening cooperation with the un and the african union, in particular as regards their military and police contributions to un missions. it considers peacekeeping operations as a form of crisis response, aimed at preventing armed conflict, restoring and maintaining peace, implementing peace agreements and addressing challenges and emergencies arising from failing or weak states. notes that the security situation in africa has changed dramatically over the past decade with the rise of terrorist and insurgent groups in somalia, nigeria and the sahel-sahara region; the growing number of unstable states and ungoverned territories is driving many into poverty and lawlessness, creating corruption and violence, while easily-crossable borders within the continent are contributing to increased violence, reduced security and opportunities for crime. it therefore calls on the eu to step up its efforts to strengthen international security in cooperation with the un and the african union. i voted for the resolution.

in writing. ‒ i supported the report in the hope that it would help to raise awareness of the importance of closer coordination amongst many international organisations outside the union, beyond the un and the african union, that are interested in or involved in international and african peacekeeping operations. harmonisation of efforts and efficiency of governance are equally key to the prudent use of resources and to the coherence of civilian and military objectives and means. while the un and most of its african partners have a generally good track record of cooperation, the european union, as the largest financial contributor, cannot afford to be indifferent to efficiency issues in the future. the report can also help to promote the long-standing ambition that the eu has the appropriate common military toolbox to achieve the common european objectives agreed in the framework of the cfsp on a global basis.
in writing. ‒ peace support operations are a form of crisis response, usually in support of an internationally recognised organisation, such as the un or the african union, with a un mandate, for the purpose of preventing armed conflict, restoring, maintaining or building peace, implementing peace agreements, and dealing with challenges and emergencies arising from failing or weak states. i voted in favour of the present document.
in writing. ‒ many member states have recognised that unfair trading practices cause harm and have taken measures to combat them. however, there are also significant differences in the rules in this area between member states and the scale of the problem varies. in my view, the scale of the problem requires the adoption of eu legislation to ensure the proper functioning of markets and fair and transparent relationships between all actors in the food supply chain. i believe that firm, consistent action is needed to put an end to unfair trading practices in the eu food supply chain once and for all. for these reasons, i voted in favour of the adoption of the proposal.
