in writing. a balanced, supportive report, which highlights a long list of manifestations of unfair commercial practices. farmers are particularly vulnerable to multinational trading chains, as agricultural production already started cannot be stopped and products are perishable. it rightly lacks the existence of any eu legislation aimed at combating unfair practices between the various actors in the agri-food chain. he wants to see tough penalties for abuses of power in the food chain. it is essential to replace the missing legal framework.
in writing. ‒ in july 2014, the commission published a communication urging member states to examine how to provide greater protection for small food producers and retailers against unfair trading practices, which often occur in business relationships where one party is in a stronger position than the other. the report of the committee on the internal market and consumer protection finds that unfair trading practices in business-to-business relations have become more prominent in recent years, with unfair trading practices becoming relatively widespread, in particular in certain parts of the supply chain. in a march 2011 survey, 96% of respondents in the food supply chain said they had been exposed to at least one unfair trading practice. it urges decisive and consistent action to end unfair trading practices in the eu food supply chain once and for all. the scale of the problem calls for union rules to ensure the proper functioning of markets and fair and transparent relationships between all actors in the food supply chain, and for unfair trading practices to be clearly identified and sanctioned. i voted in favour of the draft resolution.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report because unfair trading practices affect both producers and consumers. a more transparent trading system is needed. these practices include late payment, restrictions on market access, unilateral or retroactive changes to contract terms, unexpected and unjustified termination of contracts, unfair transfer of business risks, and reimbursement of transport and storage costs to suppliers. unfortunately, all these bad practices are found in hungary, and the government has monopolized a government-owned chain of stores at the same time as it introduced the sunday shop closure. but there are many other tools, such as special taxes, selective controls and intimidation, which would be unthinkable in the single european market. i believe that one important gap in trade practices is the range of different levels of food tax burden, which also affects producers and consumers and has a significant budgetary impact due to vat fraud. in hungary, the food industry accounts for the largest share of 27%, but with government support, some traders can add various indirect charges such as insurance premiums. there is existing eu legislation against unfair trading practices between businesses and consumers, so i agree that we should extend this to the operators in the agricultural trade chain, as the competition rules cover only part of the area.
in writing. ‒ i believe that there is an urgent need for the eu and the world to produce more safe, healthy and nutritious food to combat problems such as malnutrition, obesity, cardiovascular disease, etc. as at least one third of food produced ends up as waste on average, and in some sectors even half, one of the most effective ways of meeting this forecasted demand without exhausting limited resources is to use technological solutions to increase production, improve distribution channels and eliminate food waste. i consider the progress made in applied research in recent years to be important, but greater efforts are needed to ensure the transfer of knowledge to end-users and to involve farmers and other users of agricultural technologies and products, including smallholders. i would like the commission to ensure that, alongside scientific and technological innovation, traditional techniques and economies continue to flourish, as they represent a huge asset: they are the guarantors of the diversity of culture, the countryside, history and tourism. at the same time, they provide a livelihood for a whole range of small farmers in many regions of europe. for these reasons, i voted in favour of the report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the adoption of the mcintyre report on technological solutions for sustainable eu agriculture. agriculture has always relied on new agricultural business models and practices, including new technologies and production methods aimed at increasing yields and adapting to new and changing environments. i believe that precision farming technologies are of paramount importance for development and innovation. i believe that the principles underpinning precision farming can bring significant benefits to the environment, increase farmers' incomes, rationalise the use of agricultural machinery and significantly increase resource efficiency, including the efficiency of water use for irrigation. i therefore encourage the european commission to promote policies that encourage the uptake of precision farming technologies in all types of farms, irrespective of their size or production profile. i voted against the passage of the new genetic modification technologies. these new technologies have not yet been subject to any safety testing of the processes and should therefore be subject to the general ban on gmos for the time being.
in writing. ‒ food demand is expected to increase by 70% by 2050. the decline in available land, environmental loss and degradation, water scarcity, increasing energy demand and the emergence of new pests and diseases are putting significant pressure on our natural environment. the report by the committee on agriculture and rural development states that technological innovation is an essential element of the solution. it advocates that the eu become a global leader in agricultural technology, innovation and sustainability. it calls for europe to have a dynamic agricultural sector that develops a wide range of innovation and technologies in all types of farming. it emphasises that the benefits of technological innovation should be available to all farmers. it also notes that european agriculture is still lagging behind many of its international competitors and that this can only be helped by sustained and prioritised investments in the research fund. i voted for the resolution.
in writing. ‒ i agree that intensive food production needs to be developed in a sustainable way because of population growth, as the world population is expected to reach 9.6 billion by 2050, an increase of about 2.4 billion people compared to the total world population today. that is why i voted in favour of the report. i believe that one important element of this process is the reduction of food waste, which has reached critical proportions in some member states. to address this, i propose that social instruments be developed at eu level. another important element is innovation, which i think will only be successful if the actual farmers are given the opportunity. i think the european innovation partnership is a good thing, but it would be nice to see the concrete results. in some member states, such as hungary, the balance between livestock and crop production is still a problem, as is the lack of responsible land use and precision tools such as efficient irrigation systems. another major challenge is energy, with global energy demand forecast to increase by 40% by 2030, and i agree that this demand needs to be met by increasing energy efficiency and building a secure energy mix that includes renewable energy. unfortunately, the hungarian government is lagging behind in this area as well. of course, all of this requires a source, and without it, we can only speak of a theoretical debate. the commission should therefore propose concrete solutions.
in writing. ‒ with the growth of the global population, meeting the demand for healthy food and optimal nutrition has become one of the greatest challenges in the world today. food demand is expected to increase by 70% by 2050. the decline in available land, environmental loss and degradation, water scarcity, increasing energy demand and the emergence of new pests and diseases are putting significant pressure on our natural environment. for farmers, therefore, the challenge of sustainably producing food is growing. i voted in favour of the s&d group's position.
in writing. ‒ i believe that population growth, higher average incomes and changing consumer habits will change dietary habits, leading to an increase in the demand for processed foods and animal proteins, such as meat and dairy products, in particular. at the same time, small and medium-sized family farms are an integral part of the european agricultural sector, the basis for creating socially and economically vibrant rural areas that contribute to the preservation of the cultural and natural heritage. these farms sometimes have difficulties in taking advantage of modern production methods and practices, which could provide them with a decent income and improve the living and working conditions of farmers and promote the creation of quality jobs. innovation must address food waste and in particular the problem of regular food waste, as more than 100 million tonnes of food are thrown away in europe every year, representing some 30 to 50% of the food produced in the eu. i believe that more cooperation is needed to reduce the current level of waste. the outdated regulatory framework should not restrict innovative ways of processing food waste and the exchange of best practices should be encouraged in order to combat food waste and loss. in the light of the above, i voted in favour of the adoption of the report.
in writing. ‒ in line with the european people's party's line, i voted in favour of the huitema report on agricultural innovation. agriculture has always developed new practices, techniques and production methods that have increased yields, improved the adaptability of agricultural practices to new and changing conditions and reduced production costs. it should be seen that agriculture and forestry are key parts of our world that provide goods and services beyond food production and that can be strengthened by promoting new developments. i see innovation as a prerequisite for sustaining this progress.
in writing. the report's greatest strength is its balance, in that it promotes the preservation of traditional farming structures where possible, while encouraging innovation where appropriate. it's really a good fit for, say, grazing livestock in the gray herd and, a little further away, large-scale farming with gps-controlled tractors. it is important to note that although the eu agri-food market is one of the most integrated markets in europe, it is necessary to establish a framework that ensures a level playing field and fair competition in the agri-food sector in all member states in order to stimulate economic development. all of this is supportable.
in writing. ‒ the report of the committee on agriculture and rural development states that the world population will exceed 9 billion people by 2050. at the same time, eating habits are changing rapidly, with more consumers demanding animal protein, such as dairy products and meat. this makes it imperative to reduce the ecological footprint of agricultural production in order to alleviate the pressure on our environment and arable land. it concludes that the cap must give greater emphasis to the needs of farmers, without compromising political objectives, and therefore leave sufficient flexibility to enhance innovation and competitiveness. precision agriculture and the use of big data will transform agriculture and help us produce more products with less use of resources and more targeted interventions to fight diseases and pests. it considers targeted incentives for production processes and investments to be essential. it is also calling for the updating of outdated legislation to adapt to new solutions, such as the replacement of fertilisers with manure produced from animal manure. i voted for the resolution.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report. i agree with the need to promote innovation and economic development in agriculture, which is why i voted in favour of the report. i agree that as far back as agriculture has been around, agricultural practices have changed, whether they're structural or production processes. i share the view that these changes have made agriculture one of the most dynamic sectors of the economy. but i believe that the drive for innovation will not be achieved by one stroke or by a mere central incentive. the importance of this needs to be understood at member state level and innovation and economic incentives need to be provided at local level. for example, to reduce food waste, social channels can be found, food should be used in time rather than thrown away. with regard to the new, innovative procedure for the award of a knighthood, i believe it is important that we receive a commission opinion as soon as possible in order to prevent unjustified social rejection. breeding is not to be confused with gmo techniques. but to create an environment that is conducive to innovation, we need to create harmony in the areas of energy, taxation and production, all of which have an impact on innovation. i also believe that it is important to increase knowledge and awareness of ecosystem issues, which will allow for a more rational use of the interaction between chemical and biological measures. targeted incentives linked to production processes and investments are therefore essential.
in writing. ‒ farming practices have been changing since agriculture began, whether they are structural or linked to the production process. these changes have made agriculture one of the most dynamic sectors of the economy: today's farming practices are modern. the development of the rural economy and the uptake of new technologies by the sector ensure that it keeps pace with wider economic developments. better use of the innovation capacity will ensure that agriculture can be part of many solutions. i supported him with my vote.

in writing. – the new skills agenda aims at improving the teaching and recognition of skills across the eu. it will boost employability and competitiveness and it will better respond to industry needs. the goal is to achieve a shared vision and a commitment to work together on improving the quality and relevance of skills formation, in order to keep step with the rapidly changing skills requirements of the labour market, equip everyone with a minimum set of basic skills and make qualifications easier to understand – thus helping workers and learners to move more easily within the eu. in this context, i welcome the comprehensive approach put forward by the commission to address the basic deficit of skills and the skills mismatch at all levels, including transversal, entrepreneurial and digital skills. we need to continue investing in europe’s human capital in order to maintain our competitiveness. i welcome very much the revised european qualifications framework, which will improve understanding of qualifications acquired abroad. i am convinced that it is important to promote the comparability of qualifications between the countries covered by the eqf and other countries, in particular neighbourhood countries such as ukraine. this will help to ease the transition to the labour market and to create jobs and growth.
in writing. the new european skills agenda aims to support the discovery and development of skills from childhood. this will create social capital that will increase employability and competitiveness in europe and thereby reduce poverty and social exclusion. as a good example of what already exists in this field, i would like to mention the hungarian talent support network, created by professor péter csermely. during the past year, the hungarian initiative was put into practice at european level and the eu-wide talent support network was established. the first 14 european talent centres were accredited last september, and this year 200 european talent centres from 24 countries have applied to be part of this network. and the discovery and nurturing of talent is the key to individual well-being, ensuring a more secure future for the rising generations. the new european skills agenda has a major role to play in this.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of setting up a parliamentary committee of inquiry to carry out a comprehensive investigation into alleged irregularities and maladministration in the application of eu law in relation to money laundering, tax evasion and tax fraud. cooperation between tax authorities in the member states is more important than ever to combat tax avoidance and aggressive tax planning. the global economic and financial crisis of recent years has brought the importance and validity of burden-sharing to the attention of the public. it is estimated that member states lose billions of euros in revenue due to corporate tax avoidance. companies take advantage of the complexity of tax rules and the lack of cooperation between member states to redistribute their profits and to minimise their tax liabilities. it is therefore essential to promote transparency and cooperation in the fight against aggressive tax planning and abusive tax practices. the importance of this has been further highlighted by the panama papers scandal, which makes the establishment of a commission of inquiry inevitable. the commission should also be able to verify whether the measures provided for in this regulation are in accordance with the opinion of the committee established by article 15 (1) of directive 2005/60/ec,

in writing. ‒ the first information technology agreement (hereinafter referred to as ita), concluded in december 1996 at the singapore ministerial conference, entered into force in 1997. while the agreement was originally concluded by only 29 wto members, it now has 82 participants. the ita requires that all parties to the agreement abolish and set at zero the most-favoured-nation duties on all information technology products covered by the agreement. in may 2012, six countries (the eu, the usa, japan, korea, taiwan and costa rica) entered into negotiations to extend the product scope of the agreement. they were joined by 21 other members. on 24 july 2015, an agreement was reached on an additional list of 201 it products. under this agreement, participants are required to submit schedules with a phasing-out commitment for each product, covering a transitional period of up to 7 years (3 years for normal phasing-out, 5 years for sensitive products and 7 years in exceptional cases). as a result of the negotiations, approximately 65% of the tariff groups will be completely abolished by 1 july 2016. by 2019, almost all imports of the products concerned will be duty-free. the extension of the ita is considered to be a milestone. this is the first major tariff reduction agreement since the wto was established, with huge job creation and gdp growth potential. that is why i voted in favour of parliament giving its consent to the agreement.

in writing. ‒ the first information technology agreement (hereinafter referred to as ita), concluded in december 1996 at the singapore ministerial conference, entered into force in 1997. while the agreement was originally concluded by only 29 wto members, it now has 82 participants. the ita requires that all parties to the agreement abolish and set at zero the most-favoured-nation duties on all information technology products covered by the agreement. the ita covers some 200 tariff groups, including computers, telephones, but also input units, components and machines for the production of information technology devices. in may 2012, six countries (the eu, the usa, japan, korea, taiwan and costa rica) entered into negotiations to extend the product scope of the agreement. they were joined by 21 other members. on 24 july 2015, an agreement was reached on an additional list of 201 it products. under this agreement, participants are required to submit schedules with a phasing-out commitment for each product, covering a transitional period of up to 7 years (3 years for normal phasing-out, 5 years for sensitive products and 7 years in exceptional cases). the agreement in the form of a declaration on the extension of the ita (and the roadmaps containing the commitment of the participants to phase-out) was adopted by the ministers of the participating countries at the 10th ministerial conference of the wto in nairobi on 16 december 2015. the extension of the ita is considered to be a milestone. that is why i voted in favour of parliament giving its consent to the agreement.

in writing. ‒ the first information technology agreement (hereinafter referred to as ita), concluded in december 1996 at the singapore ministerial conference, entered into force in 1997. while the agreement was originally concluded by only 29 wto members, it now has 82 participants. the ita requires that all parties to the agreement abolish and set at zero the most-favoured-nation duties on all information technology products covered by the agreement. the ita covers some 200 tariff groups, including computers, telephones and input units for the production of information technology devices. in may 2012, six countries (the eu, the usa, japan, korea, taiwan and costa rica) started negotiations to extend the product scope of the agreement. they were joined by 21 other members. on 24 july 2015, an agreement was reached on an additional list of 201 it products. under this agreement, participants are required to submit schedules with a phasing-out commitment for each product, covering a transitional period of up to 7 years (3 years for normal phasing-out, 5 years for sensitive products and 7 years in exceptional cases). as a result of the negotiations, approximately 65% of the tariff groups will be completely abolished by 1 july 2016. by 2019, almost all imports of the products concerned will be duty-free. the extension of the ita is a milestone. this is the first trade-reduction agreement of major scope since the wto was established, with the potential to create jobs and increase gdp, and i voted in favour of this agreement.

in writing. ‒ the ita requires all participants to eliminate and set at zero the most-favoured-nation duties on all information technology products covered by the agreement. the ita covers some 200 tariff groups, including computers, telephones, but also input units, components and machines for the production of information technology devices. under this agreement, participants are required to submit schedules with a phasing-out commitment for each product, covering a transitional period of up to 7 years (3 years for normal phasing-out, 5 years for sensitive products and 7 years in exceptional cases). as a result of the negotiations, approximately 65% of the tariff groups will be completely abolished by 1 july 2016. by 2019, almost all imports of the products concerned will be duty-free. the agreement in the form of a declaration on the extension of the ita (and the roadmaps containing the commitment of the participants to phase-out) was adopted by the ministers of the participating countries at the 10th ministerial conference of the wto in nairobi on 16 december 2015. the extension of the ita is considered to be a milestone. this is the first major tariff reduction agreement since the wto was established, with huge job creation and gdp growth potential. that is why i voted in favour of parliament giving its consent to the agreement.
in writing. ‒ in may 2012, the eu, the usa, japan, korea, taiwan and costa rica began negotiations on the extension of the scope of the information technology agreement concluded in singapore in december 1996. they were joined by 21 other participants in the original agreement. on 24 july 2015, they reached an agreement on an additional list of 201 it products, including new generation semiconductors, gps navigation systems, medical devices including magnetic resonance imaging devices, printed circuit board tooling machines, telecommunications satellites and touch screens. the annual trade in these products is estimated at over usd 1,3 trillion, representing about 10% of total global trade today. the council has submitted a draft decision on the conclusion of the agreement on behalf of the european union in the form of a declaration. the decision shall require the consent of parliament. the report of the committee on international trade points out that this is the first tariff reduction agreement since the establishment of the wto with a high volume and a huge potential for job creation and gdp growth and therefore recommends that parliament give its consent to the conclusion of the agreement. i voted accordingly.
in writing. ‒ the first information technology agreement (hereinafter referred to as ita), concluded in december 1996 at the singapore ministerial conference, entered into force in 1997. while the agreement was originally concluded by only 29 wto members, it now has 82 participants. the ita requires that all parties to the agreement abolish and set at zero the most-favoured-nation duties on all information technology products covered by the agreement. the ita covers some 200 tariff groups, including computers, telephones, but also input units, components and machines for the production of information technology devices. in may 2012, six countries (the eu, the usa, japan, korea, taiwan and costa rica) entered into negotiations to extend the product scope of the agreement. they were joined by 21 other members. on 24 july 2015, an agreement was reached on an additional list of 201 it products. the agreement in the form of a declaration on the extension of the ita (and the roadmaps containing the commitment of the participants to phase-out) was adopted by the ministers of the participating countries at the 10th ministerial conference of the wto in nairobi on 16 december 2015. the extension of the ita is considered to be a milestone. this is the first major tariff reduction agreement since the wto was established, with huge job creation and gdp growth potential. that is why i voted in favour of parliament giving its consent to the agreement.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the recommendation on an agreement to expand trade in information technology products, as it has a high potential for job creation and gdp growth. since the first it agreement was concluded in december 1996, it was timely to extend the range of products covered. for all information technology products covered by the agreement, the parties shall eliminate and set at zero the duties on the basis of the most-favoured-nation principle. it is encouraging that the products covered by the current extension of the it agreement cover eur 189 billion of eu exports and this figure is expected to increase significantly following the tariff reductions. the agreement results in lower prices for consumers but also for producers that depend on imported parts. however, as the recommendation notes, certain sectors will face increased competition. it is therefore welcome that the eu has managed to provide a longer phasing-in period for some sensitive products in the course of the negotiations.
in writing. ‒ the first information technology agreement (hereinafter referred to as ita), concluded in december 1996 at the singapore ministerial conference, entered into force in 1997. while the agreement was originally concluded by only 29 wto members, it now has 82 participants. the extension of the ita is considered to be a milestone. this is the first tariff reduction agreement since the establishment of the wto with a huge potential for job creation and gdp growth. i supported him with my vote.
in writing. ‒ the council decision proposed for support by the ep will make cooperation between member states more effective in tackling α-pvp, this dangerous psychotropic substance. α-pvp is a powerful psychostimulant. the substance detected in the 28 member states, as well as in turkey and norway, is mainly imported from china for the eu drug market and is distributed throughout europe. the presence of α-pvp was detected in a total of 115 deaths and 191 acute poisonings in eight member states. the purpose of the draft council decision is to call on the member states to subject α-pvp to control measures and criminal sanctions in accordance with the provisions of their legislation based on their obligations under the 1971 united nations convention on psychotropic substances. we all have a common interest in combating the use of psychotropic substances, so i naturally supported the adoption of the report.
in writing. ‒ the council has submitted a draft decision to subject 1-phenyl-2- ((pyrrolidine-1-yl) pentan-1-one (α-pyrrolidine-valerophenone, α-pvp) to control measures as a new psychoactive substance. it shall consult parliament before adopting its decision. the report by the committee on civil liberties, justice and home affairs recommends that parliament approve the council's draft. i voted accordingly.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report approving the draft council decision on the control measures to be applied to the new psychoactive substance 1-phenyl-2- ((pyrrolidine-1-yl) pentan-1-one (α-pyrrolidine-valerophenone, α-pvp). new psychoactive substances are new drugs in pure form or in preparation or new psychotropic drugs that may be harmful to health. i consider the council decision on the exchange of information, risk assessment and control of new psychoactive substances to be important, as i believe that the specific risks inherent in the development of psychoactive substances require rapid action by the member states. this is also important with reference to the council regulation as new psychoactive substances are not subject to criminal law regulation in all member states, problems may arise in cooperation between the judicial authorities and law enforcement services of the member states as the offence or offences in question are not equally punishable under the laws of the requesting and requested states.
in writing. ‒ i supported the document in line with the s&d group's position on the draft council decision to subject 1-phenyl-2-pyrrolidine-1-yl) pentan-1-one (α-pyrrolidine-valerophenone, α-pvp) to control measures as a new psychoactive substance.
in writing. ‒ the international convention on liability and compensation for damage in connection with the carriage of hazardous and noxious substances by sea, 1996, is the last of the international maritime organisation (imo) conventions on liability and compensation for damage arising from the carriage of hazardous and noxious substances by sea, including liquefied natural gas (lng) and liquefied propane-butane gas (lpg), which has not yet been ratified. based on experience with similar international systems governing liability for damage in connection with other maritime transport activities, imo has adopted and amended this international agreement by the 2010 hns protocol to supplement the system of maritime liability conventions with a specific agreement. neither the 1996 hns convention nor the 2010 protocol to the hns convention have entered into force. the conclusion of the 2010 protocol to the hns convention will ensure the uniform application of the rules on liability and compensation in respect of accidents caused by ships carrying dangerous and harmful substances by sea throughout the eu. it will also ensure that sufficient resources are available to compensate victims of such accidents. this interim report is a step towards the ep initiating a dialogue with the council and the commission to replace the current fragmented system with a regulation at international level. that is why i voted in favour of the report.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the interim report which makes recommendations to the council and the commission on the international convention on liability and compensation for damage in connection with the carriage of hazardous and noxious substances by sea, with a view to developing a coherent eu policy. i agree with the report that it is in the interest of the union as a whole to have a homogeneous system of liability for environmental damage caused by the transport of dangerous and harmful substances by sea. the report aims to contribute to this by making recommendations to ensure that the transposition of the international system is carried out in the most efficient and equitable way possible, without prejudice to the unity, integrity and effectiveness of the common rules of union law and without creating excessive inequalities for the victims of pollution and the shipping sector.
in writing. ‒ given that the transport of dangerous and harmful substances constitutes a significant part of the maritime freight transport, and given the global nature of the shipping industry and the expected cross-border impact of accidents involving consignments of dangerous and harmful substances, the rapporteur considers that it is in the interest of the union as a whole to have a homogeneous system of liability for environmental damage resulting from the transport of dangerous and harmful substances by sea, which can only be achieved if the council and the commission take due account of the recommendations of its parliaments. i supported him with my vote.
in writing. ‒ the 1996 international convention on liability and compensation for damage in connection with the carriage of hazardous and noxious substances by sea is the last of the international maritime organisation's conventions on liability and compensation for damage arising from the carriage of hazardous and noxious substances by sea, including liquefied natural gas and liquefied propane butane gas, which has not yet been ratified. the convention lays down the objective liability of the owner of a ship for any damage resulting from an accident involving dangerous and noxious substances carried on board the ship in question. it provides for a limited number of exceptions to the owner's strict liability, which are accompanied by the owner's obligation to have insurance or other financial security to cover his liability for damage covered by the convention. more importantly, they will establish a special compensation fund to compensate any person who suffers damage resulting from the transport of dangerous and harmful substances by sea, if he or she has not received full and adequate compensation from the ship owner and its insurer. the rapporteur wishes to initiate a dialogue with the council and the commission in order to develop a coherent eu policy on liability and compensation for environmental damage caused by the transport of dangerous and harmful substances by sea. i supported the proposal because it provides a reasonable and justified authorisation to accede to an international convention.
in writing. ‒ the 1996 international convention on liability and compensation for damage in connection with the carriage of hazardous and noxious substances by sea is the last of the international maritime organisation's conventions on liability and compensation for damage in connection with the carriage of hazardous and noxious substances by sea, which has not yet been ratified. the imo has adopted and amended this international agreement by the 2010 hns protocol to supplement the system of maritime liability conventions with a specific agreement. neither the 1996 hns convention nor the 2010 protocol to the hns convention have entered into force. the conclusion of the 2010 protocol will ensure the uniform application of the rules on liability and compensation for accidents caused by ships carrying dangerous and harmful substances by sea throughout the eu. this interim report is a step towards the ep initiating a dialogue with the council and the commission to replace the currently fragmented system with a regulation at international level. that is why i voted in favour of the report.

in writing. the report deals with a very important subject, given the huge volume of maritime freight transport and the significant proportion of dangerous and harmful substances involved. the nature of transport means that any accidents have cross-border effects and that compensation can only be provided under a single system of liability. the report is on the right track to ensure that the rules on liability and compensation for accidents caused by ships are applied uniformly across the eu. further dialogue with the council and the commission is also needed to develop a coherent union policy on environmental damage from the transport of dangerous and harmful substances by sea, both in terms of liability and compensation.
in writing. ‒ the council has presented a draft decision on the ratification by the member states, in the interest of the european union, of the protocol of 2010 to the international convention on liability and compensation for damage in connection with the carriage of hazardous and noxious substances by sea, with regard to aspects of judicial cooperation in civil matters, and on their accession to it. the decision shall require the consent of parliament. the committee on legal affairs makes a number of recommendations in its report and suggests that parliament should take the view that this interim report should be a further opportunity for the council and the commission to address these recommendations. it therefore recommends that parliament invite the council and the commission to hold further negotiations taking into account the recommendations. i voted for the report.
in writing. ‒ the 1996 international convention on liability and compensation for damage in connection with the carriage of hazardous and noxious substances by sea is the last of the international maritime organisation's conventions on liability and compensation for damage in connection with the carriage of hazardous and noxious substances by sea, which has not yet been ratified. the imo has adopted and amended this international agreement by the 2010 hns protocol to supplement the system of maritime liability conventions with a specific agreement. neither the 1996 hns convention nor the 2010 protocol to the hns convention have entered into force. the very specific nature of the jurisdictional system of the echr resulting from the efforts to prevent forum shopping and the legal and practical difficulties arising from the application of a different jurisdictional system to the union and to the other parties to the echr justify an exception from the general application of the recast brussels i regulation. the conclusion of the 2010 protocol will ensure the uniform application of the rules on liability and compensation for accidents caused by ships carrying dangerous and harmful substances by sea throughout the eu. this interim report is a step towards the ep initiating a dialogue with the council and the commission to replace the current fragmented system with a regulation at international level. that is why i voted in favour of the report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the interim report which, in the context of the international convention on liability and compensation for damage in connection with the carriage of hazardous and noxious substances by sea, makes recommendations to the council and the commission on aspects of judicial cooperation in civil matters. i agree with the report that the conclusion of the 2010 protocol to the hns convention will ensure the uniform application of the rules on liability and compensation for accidents caused by ships carrying dangerous and harmful substances by sea throughout the eu and will also ensure that sufficient resources are available to compensate victims of such accidents. therefore, an international system is more appropriate than regional solutions to ensure the uniform application of the relevant rules throughout the eu, if only because shipping is a global business with cross-border effects. i believe that the recommendations made in the interim report concerning the brussels i regulation help to ensure that the single system of liability is established in the most efficient and equitable way possible.
in writing. ‒ the rapporteur intends to initiate a dialogue with the council and the commission in order to develop a coherent eu policy on liability and compensation for environmental damage caused by the transport of dangerous and harmful substances by sea. i supported him with my vote.
in writing. ‒ the council has presented a draft decision on the conclusion, on behalf of the european union and its member states, of the protocol to the framework agreement on partnership and cooperation between the european union and its member states, of the one part, and the republic of the philippines, of the other part, to take account of the accession of the republic of croatia to the european union. the decision shall require the consent of parliament. in its recommendation to the committee on foreign affairs, the committee recommends that parliament give its consent to the conclusion of the agreement. i voted accordingly.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the recommendation as it accepts that the framework agreement on partnership and cooperation between the eu and its member states, of the one part, and the republic of the philippines, of the other part, be amended to take account of the accession of croatia to the eu. the adoption of this council decision facilitates the process by which the republic of croatia, which acceded to the eu on 1 july 2013, is associated with agreements concluded or signed by member states and the eu with third countries before 1 july 2013.
in writing. ‒ the eu should continue to provide financial assistance and capacity-building support to the philippines in the areas of poverty reduction, social inclusion, respect for human rights and the rule of law, promotion of peace, reconciliation, security and judicial reform, and implementation of effective policies to address disaster preparedness, relief and recovery, and climate change. i voted for it.
in writing. ‒ the council has presented a draft decision on the signing, on behalf of the union, of the framework agreement on partnership and cooperation between the european union and its member states, of the one part, and the republic of the philippines, of the other part. the decision shall require the consent of parliament. in its recommendation to the committee on foreign affairs, the committee recommends that parliament give its consent to the conclusion of the agreement. i voted accordingly.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the recommendation on a framework agreement on partnership and cooperation between the european union and the republic of the philippines, which expresses its support for the conclusion of the agreement. the eu is interested in maintaining dialogue with the countries of the region and in strengthening its external, economic and trade relations. by continuing to provide assistance to the philippines and support capacity building, the eu is contributing to poverty reduction, respect for human rights and the rule of law, and the promotion of peace, security and justice reform. the resolution also calls on the eu to take action to combat corruption and to ensure that the rule of law is upheld in the country. as the philippines is among the developing countries most exposed to climate change, eu support for capacity building in this area is of particular importance.

in writing. the agreement with the philippines, which is far from the eu's sphere of interest, is not likely to be challenged and can therefore be concluded with broad agreement. it seems obvious, but it somewhat clouds the picture, that the european union is strengthening its relations with an area in the us-china confrontation zone. even with the problems listed in the report, we are sympathetic, because we can appreciate the positive developments and the high level of commitment of your government to further dynamic progress. there is a lot at stake for a country if its government is moving in the right direction, especially if it is strategically located.
in writing. ‒ the committee on foreign affairs also tabled a motion for a resolution, together with its recommendation that the council approve the framework agreement on partnership and cooperation between the eu and the philippines and the protocol to that framework agreement to take account of the accession of the republic of croatia to the european union. i voted in favour of the draft resolution.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution on the framework agreement on partnership and cooperation between the european union and the republic of the philippines, which, in addition to welcoming the framework agreement on partnership and cooperation with the philippines and recognising the efforts made by the country so far, also draws the attention of the philippine government to the importance of promoting human rights and labour rights and the threat posed by isis. the resolution rightly points to the tensions in the south china sea region and the importance of addressing them in a peaceful manner, in accordance with the un convention on the law of the sea, and not by unilateral, provocative measures. as in the resolution, i encourage the philippines to work to further improve the investment environment by enhancing transparency and good governance through the implementation of un guidelines on the human rights responsibilities of business enterprises and by developing infrastructure. i also agree that regular contacts between the european external action service and parliament are necessary to enable parliament to monitor the implementation of the framework agreement and the achievement of its objectives.
in writing. ‒ the eu should continue to provide financial assistance and capacity-building support to the philippines in the areas of poverty reduction, social inclusion, respect for human rights and the rule of law, promotion of peace, reconciliation, security and judicial reform, and implementation of effective policies to address disaster preparedness, relief and recovery, and climate change. i voted for it.
in writing. ‒ the report concerns additional macro-financial assistance to be provided to tunisia. tunisia has managed to consolidate its democratic transition. it is governed by a grand coalition government, which was formed following free and transparent elections, and it has a modern civil society that is proactive and has been recognised by the tunisian national dialogue quartet with the nobel peace prize. however, tunisia is currently facing very serious difficulties. it has also suffered from a number of assassinations and terrorist attacks, which have significantly affected key economic sectors in the country, such as tourism. it is of the utmost importance to the union that tunisia succeed and defeat the calculations of those who want to destabilise the country. the commission will continue to support the development of tunisia in a concrete way that directly benefits the population. on these grounds, i supported the adoption of the report.
in writing. ‒ tunisia is currently facing very serious difficulties. it has also suffered from a number of assassinations and terrorist attacks, which have significantly affected key economic sectors in the country, such as tourism. in addition, the regional security situation is highly uncertain as the country borders libya. despite these challenges, tunisia continues to make important progress towards democratic transition and modernisation of the economic structure. it is currently negotiating a free trade agreement with the european union. the reforms have resulted in tunisia fully complying with the political conditions for the assessment of macro-financial assistance. in order to restore stability to the region, it is essential that tunisia be able to take further steps towards democratic governance and economic development. this package of support is the second in a series of measures envisaged by the commission in august 2015 at the request of the tunisian government in the form of a macro-financial assistance programme of eur 500 million, to be disbursed in the form of medium-term loans on favourable terms on the financial markets. this assistance programme will be used to support reforms aimed at improving tunisia's fiscal position, balancing its balance of payments and creating favourable conditions for investment. in view of the above, i voted in favour of the adoption of the report.
in writing. ‒ tunisia is currently facing very serious difficulties. it has also suffered from a number of assassinations and terrorist attacks, which have significantly affected key economic sectors in the country, such as tourism. in addition, the regional security situation is highly uncertain as the country borders libya. despite these challenges, tunisia continues to make important progress towards democratic transition and the modernisation of its economic structure, and is currently negotiating a free trade agreement with the european union. the reforms have resulted in tunisia fully complying with the political conditions for the assessment of macro-financial assistance. in order to restore stability to the region, it is essential that tunisia be able to take further steps towards democratic governance and economic development. on 15 may 2014, a support programme of eur 300 million was approved for tunisia. the first two instalments of the programme were paid in 2015 and the third will be paid in 2016. this package of support is the second in a series of measures envisaged by the commission in august 2015 at the request of the tunisian government in the form of a macro-financial assistance programme of eur 500 million, to be disbursed in the form of medium-term loans on favourable terms on the financial markets. this assistance programme will be used to support reforms aimed at improving tunisia's fiscal position, balancing its balance of payments and creating favourable conditions for investment. in view of the above, i voted in favour of the report.

in writing. ‒ the report is about limiting aggressive tax optimisation. the european council resolution of december 2014 recognised the need to 'urgently promote efforts to combat tax avoidance and aggressive tax planning at both global and union level'. since december 2014, the commission has already taken the first steps towards the union approach and in the meantime the organisation for economic cooperation and development (oecd) has also completed its work on the definition of global rules and standards for this purpose, which is used in this proposal. according to an oecd study, the aggressive tax optimisation of multinational companies is causing a global annual budget loss of between 100 and 240 billion dollars, and therefore requires coordinated action. i also voted in favour of the proposal because it does not restrict member states' sovereignty over their own tax systems too much.
in writing. ‒ a coordinated and harmonised implementation of tax systems is key to ensuring the proper functioning of the single market and the success of the capital markets union. i voted in favour of the report. i believe that the proposals contained therein will make the patent legislation clearer and more uniform. multinational companies still exploit the tax incentives associated with filing patents to artificially reduce the amount of their profits. in my opinion, this has a detrimental effect on truly innovative countries. i am pleased that the rapporteur has also confirmed the role of parliament. i myself believe that the european parliament should be entrusted with the task of monitoring the actual implementation of the directive in the 28 member states.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the bayet report on rules to combat aggressive tax planning practices. i welcome the establishment of the appropriate regulatory framework to prevent similar tax planning practices. it is shocking that a recent oecd study found that aggressive tax optimization by multinational corporations causes annual budget deficits of $100 to $240 billion worldwide. this represents 410% of the taxes paid by companies worldwide. this is particularly a sensitive revenue loss for those states where it is precisely this that reduces the resources available for investments to stimulate job creation, eradicate poverty and develop effective health care systems. we need to stop the practice of multinational companies exploiting the tax incentives associated with filing patents to artificially reduce the amount of their profits.

in writing. ‒ the commission has proposed to the council the adoption of a directive laying down rules against tax evasion practices directly affecting the functioning of the internal market. the council is to consult parliament before adopting the directive. the maltese parliament and the swedish parliament submitted reasoned opinions that the draft legislative act was not compatible with the principle of subsidiarity. in its report, the economic and monetary committee recommends that parliament approve the commission proposal with 91 amendments, taking into account the views of malta and sweden, and requests the commission to amend its proposal accordingly. i voted for the motion.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on rules against tax avoidance practices directly affecting the functioning of the internal market, as i agree with the main objective of multinational companies finally paying tax where they actually generate their profits. the aggressive tax optimization of multinational corporations has taken significant resources away from important areas such as health, education, and public services. this is an untenable situation and i agree with the rapporteur that in order to create a reliable single market, member states must harmonize their tax systems. european tax harmonisation is also a precondition for the creation of economic and monetary union. the report's comments were intended to make clearer and more effective the commission's proposal to limit tax avoidance by multinational companies by putting an end to the practice of multinationals conspiring to escape tax havens and to avoid paying tax on their profits. i also welcome the fact that the report has also clarified and harmonised patent legislation and strengthened the role of parliament.

in writing. ‒ the resolution contains a number of elements that can be supported. it points out that the emphasis on the war on terrorism has dangerously shifted the balance between the different powers of the state towards an expansion of the powers of governments to the detriment of parliaments and the judiciary. the use of state secrets is unprecedented, hindering public scrutiny of alleged human rights violations. the document is fundamentally correct in condemning the operation of secret cia prisons and the us's human rights-incompatible counter-terrorism methods. i do not agree, however, with the repeated emphasis on the extreme importance of transatlantic relations. however, as this case, which has been on the agenda for ten years, demands a full investigation and accountability, i have voted in favour.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the criticism in the motion for a resolution because i consider it unacceptable that the cia, with the cooperation of the authorities of certain member states, could have been involved in the illegal detention and torture of prisoners on the territory of the european union. the ep also stressed that the council, the commission and the member states concerned had not implemented or only partially implemented the proposals for measures and procedures put forward by parliament in this case. in my view, such methods will not make the fight against terrorism more effective, but they represent a serious and systematic violation of human rights and a burden on euro-atlantic political relations. i therefore expect that our present decision, as it stands, will lead the eu institutions and the member states concerned to examine the circumstances and to provide the european public and the european parliament with meaningful answers and measures.

in writing. ‒ the report aims to highlight the eu's backwardness in space technologies and industry and to make suggestions for development goals and possible directions. it is important to note that the parts that call for the eu and nato to coordinate and deepen civil and military developments in this area are not a solution. the eu must be independent and seek to develop and use its own technology independently of the us and nato, precisely because of the potential for military use of space technology. space technology also offers the possibility of addressing the question of common external and internal security, the protection of the eu's external borders and the control of illegal migration at the point of origin in a way that is appropriate and acceptable to all member states. at present, 60% of eu space technology and, within it, information communication satellites for civil and military use use components and software from the usa, which raises the question of how to guarantee adequate data protection for eu citizens. the coordination and integration of existing eu and national space research agencies and research institutes into a single umbrella organisation will allow developments to be project-based and competitive with the space technology developments and programmes of competing states, which is why i voted in favour of the report.
in writing. ‒ the security environment within and outside the union is becoming increasingly dangerous and challenging, with terrorist attacks and mass killings affecting all member states, to which member states must respond by adopting a common strategy and a coordinated response. the report therefore emphasises the importance of space-based devices and the further development of these capabilities. the union must work together to achieve an effective and coherent border management system, respond to challenges to our security, to unrest and armed conflict in our neighbourhood, and to migration, for which the development of these capabilities is essential. i believe that the union should improve access to space-based satellite communication, space observation, precision navigation and earth observation capabilities and ensure europe's independence in critical space technologies and access to space. i voted in favour of the report.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of setting up a parliamentary committee of inquiry to carry out a comprehensive investigation into alleged irregularities and maladministration in the application of eu law in relation to money laundering, tax evasion and tax fraud. cooperation between tax authorities in the member states is more important than ever to combat tax avoidance and aggressive tax planning. the global economic and financial crisis of recent years has brought the importance and validity of burden-sharing to the attention of the public. it is estimated that member states lose billions of euros in revenue due to corporate tax avoidance. companies take advantage of the complexity of tax rules and the lack of cooperation between member states to redistribute their profits and to minimise their tax liabilities. it is therefore essential to promote transparency and cooperation in the fight against aggressive tax planning and abusive tax practices. the importance of this has been highlighted by the panama papers scandal, which makes the creation of a commission of inquiry inevitable. the commission should also be able to verify whether the measures provided for in this regulation are in accordance with the opinion of the committee established by article 15 (1) of directive 2005/60/ec,

in writing. ‒ following the terrorist attacks in paris on 13 november 2015, france, invoking article 42 (7) of the treaty on european union, requested the assistance and support of the european union. the report of the committee on foreign affairs, in particular, examines the potential of space-based capabilities and services in relation to the common security and defence policy, the fight against terrorist attacks and mass murder affecting all member states, the safeguarding of stability, the fight against security challenges, in particular those arising from terrorism, the more effective assessment and identification of flows and routes of illegal immigrants, and the determination of the place of embarkation for those from north africa. calls for improving access to space-based satellite communications, space observation, precision navigation and earth observation capabilities and for ensuring europe's independence in critical space technologies and access to space. i voted in favour of the draft resolution.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report calling for the development of eu space research, instrument development and dual-use space-based capabilities. in formulating my opinion, i have taken into account the changes in the international security environment in europe and in the european union and its member states, the new types of challenges to which an effective response can only be given by a joint eu effort, along the same lines. i support the holistic approach of the report to the cfsp and csdp and the promotion of the dual use of european space capabilities, programmes and instruments, as is already the case for the galileo and copernicus programmes. i also agree that the material specifically highlights the interaction between the development of defence and civil space capabilities and the underpinning of technical and scientific progress in the member states. in general, i am convinced that without the development of its own space research and capabilities, the eu cannot have a meaningful global role in the future, and we must provide the european parliament with the appropriate political support.

in writing. ‒ the security environment within and outside the union is becoming increasingly dangerous and challenging, with terrorist attacks and mass killings affecting all member states, to which member states must respond by adopting a common strategy and a coordinated response. the report therefore emphasises the importance of space-based devices and the further development of these capabilities. the union must work together to achieve an effective and coherent border management system, respond to challenges to our security, to unrest and armed conflict in our neighbourhood, and to migration, for which the development of these capabilities is essential. the report emphasises that the union should improve access to space-based satellite communications, space observation, precision navigation and earth observation capabilities and ensure europe's independence in critical space technologies and access to space.
in writing. ‒ eu space activities are of paramount importance for innovation, economic growth and industrial competitiveness. satellite navigation, earth observation and satellite telecommunications services can make a vital contribution to the implementation of a wide range of union policies and bring significant benefits to all european citizens. galileo and the copernicus programme have a unique and innovative approach, and reliable and accurate positioning information from weather and earth observation data is of strategic importance. the union intends to spend more than eur 11 billion on infrastructure for the programmes over the period up to 2020. the report considers that in the future, business will be the main providers of space services, which will have a stimulating effect on the entrepreneurial sphere in the union, and supports the increased use of space data by both the public sector and the business community. space data and space services can play an important role in ensuring that europe is a leader in key technological directions such as the 'internet of things', 'smart cities', 'big data' and connected and autonomous vehicles.

in writing. ‒ the ppe, s&d, ecr, alde, verts/ale and efdd groups tabled a joint motion for a resolution on the introduction of space products on the market. i voted in favour of the joint motion for a resolution.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report because it identifies and proposes a number of aspects that could help to preserve europe's leading role in space technology and its civil and commercial exploitation. i agree with the call for the commission to develop a comprehensive strategy to this end, which will ensure that both copernicus and galileo and future programmes will have a high level of scientific and technical excellence and a continuous commercial viability, and thus the capacity to boost the european economy, with a focus on job creation. i consider it important that the report states that there is a need to improve the coherence between eu involvement in the space market and other eu policies, in particular the internal market, competition and energy policy. i also agree with the need expressed in the material to make future developments more consumer-oriented, while taking into account the interests of service providers.
in writing. ‒ eu space activities are of crucial importance for scientific and technological progress, innovation, economic growth, industrial competitiveness, social cohesion, the creation of skilled jobs and new businesses, and the creation of business opportunities in both purchasing and sales markets. i voted for it.
in writing. ‒ the political crisis in venezuela is deepening, which is why i have adopted the parliament's draft resolution. we need to monitor the socioeconomic situation in venezuela with increased attention, which is a cause of growing political uncertainty. we must assure the suffering people of our support and condemn the political elite who imprison their own opposition and those who criticize the system. the motion for a resolution provides a good basis for this. we must call on both sides to continue the dialogue, to the importance of compromise agreements and to the urgent resolution of the socio-economic problems of the country. the government must guarantee the right to freedom of expression and the full freedom of arbitrarily detained political prisoners. the eu should strongly advocate the release of political prisoners and arbitrarily detained persons, in line with the many un agencies and international organisations and the law on amnesty and national reconciliation.
in writing. ‒ the ppe, verts/ale, ecr, efdd, gue/ngl, alde and s&d groups have tabled a motion for a resolution on the situation in venezuela. among them, the ppe, ecr, alde and s&d groups reached an agreement and worked out a joint compromise proposal. i voted in favour of the compromise motion.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution as it reflects a compromise acceptable to me as well as to the party factions in the political opposition to the complex socio-political crisis in venezuela. in my view, the european union and the european parliament cannot remain silent in a situation where, in the political impasse following the venezuelan elections, there are massive violations of human rights, political prisoners are being imprisoned and the economic and social crisis in the country is at its lowest point. i therefore support the active involvement of the high representative for foreign affairs in the measures proposed in the parliament's decision to promote political consolidation and to include the issue on the agenda of the next european council meeting following the g7 resolution. in the short term, i expect this european parliament's decision to continue to contribute to the dialogue between the venezuelan government and the political opposition, and in this context to encourage the implementation of the most urgent measures to restore democratic relations, put an end to violations, release political prisoners and improve the provision of services to the population.
in writing. ‒ the rule of law and the principle of separation of powers are not properly respected in venezuela. there are about 2,000 people in prison, under house arrest or on probation for political reasons, including important political leaders. i voted in favour of the s&d group's position.
in writing. ‒ under regulation (eu) no 528/2012, the commission was required to adopt delegated acts setting out scientific criteria for endocrine-disrupting properties of active substances and biocidal products by 13 december 2013 at the latest. the commission established the joint research centre for this task, whose expert group adopted a report on 28 march 2013 on the identification and characterisation of endocrine disruptors. the european court of justice has ruled that regulation (eu) no 528/2012 does not contain any provision requiring the commission to carry out an impact assessment of the scientific risk-based criteria and that even if the commission considered such an impact assessment to be necessary, this did not exempt it from complying with the deadline set by the regulation. the court therefore held in its judgment that the commission had a clear, precise and unconditional obligation to adopt delegated acts to define the above-mentioned scientific criteria by 13 december 2013 at the latest, as provided for in the regulation. since the commission has failed to fulfil its obligations under the treaties, despite its role as guardian of the treaties vis-à-vis the member states, i have therefore voted in favour of the motion for a resolution calling on the commission to remedy its intentional failure immediately.
in writing. ‒ the commission's early adoption of the relevant legislative task is essential for effective action against endocrine disruptors and for the protection of human health and the environment. in its judgment in the case, the european court of justice clearly found that the european commission had failed to fulfil its legislative obligation in relation to the biocidal products regulation it was therefore justified to call on the european parliament to respect its obligations under union law by means of a decision. the risk-based scientific criteria should be established in an objective manner, on the basis of scientific data, and independently of any other considerations, in particular economic ones. the draft joint resolution is worded in a concise and factual manner and in the light of the above circumstances, and i therefore voted in favour of the report.
in writing. ‒ the commission's early adoption of the relevant legislative task is essential for effective action against endocrine disruptors and for the protection of human health and the environment. in its judgment in the case, the european court of justice clearly found that the european commission had failed to fulfil its legislative obligation in relation to the biocidal products regulation it was therefore justified to call on the european parliament to respect its obligations under union law by means of a decision. the risk-based scientific criteria should be established in an objective manner, on the basis of scientific data on the endocrine system, and independently of any other considerations, in particular economic considerations. the wording of the draft joint resolution is concise and factual and takes account of the above circumstances, and i therefore voted in favour of it in agreement with the group of the european people's party.

in writing. ‒ judgment of the general court of the european union of 16 december 2015 in case t-521/14 sweden v commission. in its judgment, the general court held that the commission had a clear, precise and unconditional obligation under regulation (eu) no 528/2012 of the european parliament and of the council of 22 may 2012 concerning the making available on the market and use of biocidal products to adopt delegated acts setting out scientific criteria for endocrine disrupting properties of active substances and biocidal products by 13 december 2013 at the latest. the commission has not provided any evidence that the measures in question are in breach of the principle of proportionality. the ep has therefore tabled a joint motion for a resolution with the efn, gue/ngl, efdd, alde, s&d and verts/ale, and the ppe and ecr groups. among them, s&d, gue/ngl, efdd and alde reached an agreement and drafted a joint compromise motion condemning the commission and calling for the immediate replacement of the omission, which was joined by the ppe and the verts/ale group. i voted in favor of the compromise motion.
in writing. ‒ scientific criteria are needed for the detection and management of endocrine disruptors. the european commission should have made these criteria public by the end of 2013, and i voted in favour of the joint resolution which calls for the presentation of this set of criteria as soon as possible and points out that, despite the repeated requests of the ep, no substantive action has been taken so far. given the importance of the issue for human health, it is important to emphasise that endocrine disruptors present clearly irreversible health risks even without criteria. but neither is a witch hunt, so we need a scientific judgment system to decide whether a drug is marketable. the issue has not only been addressed by the european parliament, but also by the world health organisation, which describes endocrine disruptors as a global threat, causing irreversible diseases such as sterility in some of the people and animals affected. i agree with the strong statement in the resolution that the european commission must come forward with the relevant delegated acts in a short time.
in writing. ‒ the unep/who report identified endocrine disruptors as a global threat, citing, among other things, the high incidence and growing trend of human endocrine disruption. new evidence is available that exposure to endocrine disruptors leads to reproductive disorders (infertility, cancer, birth defects) and the effects of these chemicals on thyroid function, brain function, obesity and metabolism, and on insulin and glucose homeostasis. i have followed the s&d group's position with interest.
in writing. ‒ on 9 february 2009, the company syngenta submitted to the competent authority of germany an application to place on the market foods, food ingredients and feed containing, consisting of, or produced from bt11 × mir162 × mir604 × ga21 maize. the application covers genetically modified varieties other than cultivation. these contain proteins that can cause cancer in the human body. our fundamental objection is that the authorisation mechanism for genetically modified food and feed is not democratic. the european commission regularly issues the necessary permits, but it is not supported by the majority of member states or the majority of eu citizens. in 2014, president juncker himself promised to put an end to this anti-democratic decision-making mechanism. on these grounds, i supported the objection against the commission implementing regulation.
in writing. ‒ the eu's gmo authorisation system is based on the precautionary principle. accordingly, the safety of genetically modified products should be ascertained before authorisation. the bt11 x mir162 x mir604 x ga21 maize resulting from the combination of the single lines is resistant to the active substances glufosinate-ammonium and glyphosate herbicides and to a number of insect pests of the orders lepidoptera and coleoptera. the cultivation of the gmo maize concerned may lead to an increased use of plant protection products containing such active substances, which may subsequently increase the residues in the crop. in 2015, the who classified glyphosate as a 'probable human carcinogen'. high doses also increase the incidence of resistant yeast populations. in the opinion of domestic experts, the safety studies on the product are not satisfactory. longer-term feeding trials should have been carried out to establish that these products do not pose a risk to human or animal health. in line with our country's gmo-free strategy, the basic law and the precautionary principle, we do not support the authorisation of gm products, and therefore i voted in favour of the parliament's objection to the placing on the union market of genetically modified maize bt11 x mir162 x mir604 x ga21.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution rejecting the placing on the market of products containing, consisting of or produced from genetically modified maize bt11 × mir162 × mir604 × ga21 and genetically modified maize combining two or three of the genetic events bt11, mir162, mir604 and ga21. this motion for a resolution was necessary because on 9 february 2009 syngenta france s.a.s. submitted to the competent authority of germany an application for the placing on the market of foods, food ingredients, and feed containing, consisting of, or produced from the maize referred to above. as described in the application, the maize contains proteins to protect against certain lepidoptera or coleoptera pests, which provide resistance to herbicides containing glufosinate-ammonium or glyphosate. however, these substances have been classified as 'probably carcinogenic' by the international agency for research on cancer, the who cancer agency. i believe that the current approval system for genetically modified food and feed is not working properly and that it needs to be corrected.
in writing. ‒ on 9 february 2009, syngenta france s.a.s. submitted to the competent authority of germany an application, in accordance with articles 5 and 17 of regulation (ec) no 1829/2003, for the placing on the market of foods, food ingredients, and feed containing, consisting of, or produced from bt11 × mir162 × mir604 × ga21 maize. i supported him with my vote.
in writing. ‒ the eu's gmo authorisation system is based on the precautionary principle. we cannot support the authorisation of gmos that can cross-breed with wild related species and spread in certain areas, even if they do not live in hungary but in southern europe. we believe that although there is little chance of viable pollen and seeds entering the environment from cut flowers, this route cannot be completely ruled out. however, the tolerance of sulphonylurea herbicides, if released, may significantly increase the survival and reproduction of gm carnation in the natural environment, to the detriment of wild related species. nor can the possibility of horizontal gene transfer between the gm hornwort and bacteria in the environment be completely excluded. in accordance with our country's gmo-free strategy, the basic law and the precautionary principle, i voted in favour of the parliament's objection to the placing on the eu market of genetically modified nails.
