vice-president of the commission. – madam president, as i stated before, the commission will continue to work to ensure that any future solution on whaling within the international whaling commission leads to a better overall conservation of whales worldwide and ultimately to a sizable reduction in the number of whales being killed under whatever whaling regime, commercial or scientific. the eu and japan are close allies and major international partners. the eu and japan are currently negotiating a strategic partnership and a free trade agreement. in these frameworks, the eu is pushing for the inclusion of a robust trade and sustainable development chapter in the fta and a robust article on the environment in the spa, but whaling as such is not part of the ongoing negotiations on these agreements between the eu and japan. our differences of approach on particular issues of whaling should not prevent us from strengthening our economic and political cooperation in other areas. many thanks for your comments and this discussion.
president-in-office of the council. – madam president, i thank the honourable members for all their inputs, which are extremely important for the coming months. this is something that we all share, namely that we do not approve of the current whaling activities of japan. i continue to be very concerned that japan has also failed to present sufficient evidence to justify their whaling activities. we are looking ahead now to the meetings that are going to be held soon on this issue. the issue of scientific whaling is discussed at the meeting of the scientific committee, which just started in bled. we have constantly recognised and supported the independence of that committee and we will keep to that position. we conveyed our serious concerns in view of the expert panel findings in 2015 and our position has not changed in that respect. the only way we can work on this is an effective conservation and management regime through joint efforts and by initiatives that promote mutual trust and cooperation. we stand really ready to engage with all partners at the iwc66, while reiterating the importance of respecting international obligations and our opposition to the conduct of so-called scientific whaling outside iwc control. as you know, we have made this démarche earlier. we will ensure that we will continue to take an active position in this debate against the policy that we all abhor and therefore we will also ensure that the european union and its member states are well prepared for the next meeting of the iwc in october.
in writing. – on 31st march 2014 the un’s international court of justice – in its legally-binding decision – ruled that japan’s state-subsidised whale-hunting in the southern ocean did not fall within the scope of scientific research and therefore was considered illegal. in spite of the ruling, japan has recently resumed whaling, exploiting a loophole that allows for a limited amount of hunting for scientific purposes. even though there has been a moratorium on commercial whaling since 1982, there is still supply of whale meat in japan due to imports and the sale of the meat that was hunted on scientific missions. however, the hunting of whales could not be justified by the alleged strong cultural attachment to whale meat, either – which was popular in the post-war period since it was a cheap source of protein – as, according to research conducted by greenpeace, whale meat consumption in japan amounted to about 30 grams per person on average in 2015 (whereas the stockpile of unsold frozen whale meat totalled up to 5 900 tons in 2011). following the suggestion of greenpeace, activism from within japan should be combined with international pressure. therefore, i urge the eu and the member states to take action and step up against this out-dated and illegal practice.

in writing. ‒ the proposal streamlines the procedures currently used between member states to verify the authenticity of certain authentic instruments, while complementing existing sectoral eu legislation by abolishing the requirement of double-checking and simplifying the use of copies and translations. it draws on existing sectoral union law and relevant international legal sources, while strengthening trust in authentic instruments issued in other member states. however, the proposal does not amend but complements existing sectoral union law, which contains provisions on supervision, or other formalities, or administrative cooperation. it also provides for the simplification of other formalities relating to the acceptance of authentic instruments in other member states, namely certified copies and certified translations. the enf group proposed that the european parliament reject the council's position adopted at first reading. i do not consider the refusal to be justified, as this regulation brings about considerable ease in everyday life and cost reduction for hungarians who work or study abroad. the rejection is a resolution against the principle of free movement within the union, which would harm the interests of the large number of hungarians who are hopefully temporarily finding their fortunes in the west. the proposal also simplifies legal procedures, as hungarian citizens can thus assert their interests in the field of private international law more easily and cost-effectively. i therefore voted against the rejection.
in writing. ‒ in 2013, the commission proposed to the parliament and the council the adoption of a regulation on the promotion of the free movement of citizens by simplifying the presentation of certain public documents in the european union and amending regulation (eu) no 1024/2012. the proposal aims to promote the free movement of citizens by simplifying the formal acceptance of certain public documents within the european union. it does not apply to the recognition of the content of authentic instruments, in particular in order to preserve the sovereignty of the member states in the field of family law. parliament adopted its position on the proposal at first reading back in 2013. however, the romanian senate submitted a reasoned opinion that the draft legislative act was not compatible with the principle of subsidiarity. following interinstitutional negotiations, a compromise text was agreed between the co-legislators and the commission, as reflected in the council's position adopted at first reading. the recommendation of the committee on legal affairs for second reading proposes that parliament should agree with the council's position at first reading and that the legislative act should be adopted in accordance with the council's position. i voted accordingly.
in writing. ‒ the purpose of this legislative act is to promote the free movement of citizens by simplifying the official acceptance of certain public documents within the european union. it does not apply to the recognition of the content of authentic instruments, in particular in order to preserve the sovereignty of the member states in the field of family law. following interinstitutional negotiations, a compromise text was agreed between the co-legislators and the commission. it thus covers public documents relating to marital status and certain other documents frequently requested by citizens, such as residence, nationality and criminal records. for these authentic instruments, the regulation provides for exemption from the double-certification and apostille formalities which are traditionally required for cross-border authentic instruments. it also provides for simplified acceptance arrangements for certified copies and certified translations. the current scope does not cover diplomas and certificates of qualification, documents proving disability and some documents relevant to businesses, but the regulation contains revision clauses that envisage the future extension of the scope of administrative simplifications as this new way of working becomes the norm in national authorities. in view of the above, i voted in favour of the recommendation.
in writing. ‒ the purpose of this legislative act is to promote the free movement of citizens by simplifying the official acceptance of certain public documents within the european union. it does not apply to the recognition of the content of authentic instruments, in particular in order to preserve the sovereignty of the member states in the field of family law. the mobility of eu citizens is a reality: some 12 million of them study, work or live in a member state other than their country of nationality. today, when union citizens and businesses exercise their rights of free movement or internal market freedoms, they may encounter administrative complications when submitting public documents to the authorities of other member states, for example as a result of cross-border mobility. i was supportive.

in writing. ‒ improving the competitiveness of the european rail industry requires a european training and education strategy that brings together rail supply companies, research institutes and social partners to jointly explore the skills needed for a sustainable and innovative rail supply industry. in this context, i believe that a feasibility study should be launched on the possible creation of a european railway sectoral training council. it is necessary to urge member states and/or regional bodies concerned to develop a framework for the provision of continuing training, in the form of a personal right to training, which ensures that the skilled workforce keeps pace with the growing needs of the sector and adapts to new market conditions, or is transferable to another industrial sector in the event of redundancy. in the light of the above, i voted in favour of the adoption of the report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution because i believe that the european rail supply sector is of enormous importance for european industrial growth, job creation and innovation. the european rail supply sector is of strategic importance for the rebirth of european industry, and it needs to maintain its global leadership. it includes many smes and leading companies in the sector and employs 400 000 people. their role is crucial to the revival of the railway industry. it is important to ensure that smes have access to finance, as this is one of the main challenges they face. the cosme programme and the structural funds can help facilitate access to finance, including in the form of guarantees and equity instruments. at the same time, it would be worthwhile to find alternative sources of funding, such as the sme instrument of the horizon 2020 strategy. the commission should support the increased use of eu financial instruments and resources available to smes, and we should find a way to make smes more dependent on one company, as it is clear that they are reluctant to expand due to a lack of resources and the increased risks of cross-border activity. to achieve this, we need to create appropriate synergies between funding sources alongside existing support programmes for the internationalisation of smes.
in writing. ‒ the european railway supply industry employs 400 000 people and accounts for 46% of the global railway supply industry. the entire railway sector, including operators and infrastructure, provides 1 million direct and 1.2 million indirect jobs in the european union. the sector is key to european industrial growth, job creation and innovation, and its development will contribute significantly to the achievement of the 20% reindustrialisation target. rail contributes significantly to climate change mitigation and to tackling other megatrends such as urbanisation and demographic change. in order to meet the union's 2030 climate and energy and decarbonisation objectives, a shift towards rail and other sustainable, energy-efficient, electrified modes of transport is necessary. the global competitiveness of the eu railway supply market is currently good, but in order to maintain this position, europe needs to put more emphasis on education and research. it is also particularly important to take into account the significant number of smes in the industry. these undertakings face significant financial and administrative burdens which are not borne by their competitors in third countries. particular attention should be paid to their support, in which the european small business package or even the efsi could play a significant role.
in writing. ‒ the report of the committee on industry, research and energy shows that the european rail supply sector employs 400 000 people, devotes 2.7% of its annual turnover to research and development and covers 46% of the world market. the total rail sector is responsible for 1 million direct and 1.2 million indirect jobs in the european union, indicating its importance for european industrial growth, job creation and innovation and its contribution to the 20% re-industrialisation target. the railway also makes a significant contribution to climate change mitigation and to tackling other megatrends such as urbanisation and demographic change. the objective of decarbonising transport clearly requires a shift towards rail and other sustainable, energy-efficient, electrified modes of transport. in this context, the report calls for action at union level to maintain the international competitiveness and global leadership of the european rail supply sector, to reduce unfair competition in the rail supply sector and to ensure a level playing field in global competition and mutual market access. i voted in favour of the draft resolution.

most of you have mentioned both social as well as religious and criminal sources for this process of a radicalisation, and i think you are right. it is a multi-faceted problem of which you have but we need to act, and i feel very much the support in this parliament for these actions taken by the council and others. we simply cannot allow those who want to hurt our system or our way of living in writing. it is estimated that 4,000 trained fighters radicalized in the middle east are currently in europe. and the news over the last few days is that the number is growing. this means that the threat of european citizens becoming victims of terrorist attacks and acts of violence is increasing day by day. and the trigger is radicalization, especially among second- and third-generation immigrant youth. we must act decisively against this phenomenon. i welcome the commission communication on this subject, which identifies seven specific areas where joint eu action can reduce radicalisation. i believe that only a comprehensive strategy can effectively combat this phenomenon. the most important thing to do is to identify and remove radicalized individuals from their communities so that they cannot spread their murderous ideas and send them back to their countries of origin. this requires an appropriate exchange of information at union level. on the other hand, prevention of radicalisation is necessary, for example in the fields of education and strengthening of social resilience, and appropriate steps should also be taken in the fields of deradicalisation and rehabilitation. our first duty, our responsibility to our children, is to give our citizens back their sense of security. and to do that, we need to do everything we can to successfully fight radicalisation.
in writing. – it is of utmost importance to treat radicalisation and violent extremism as social phenomena and not as problems of a single religion or ideology; therefore, i believe that we should treat the real root causes behind radicalisation, namely marginalisation, discrimination and inequality. the eu and the member states should focus on local capacity-building, awareness raising, integration and education instead of expanding their surveillance measures or deciding to build walls. moreover, i cannot emphasise enough not to link the recent influx of asylum seekers with the extremist attacks that took place: asylum seekers more often than not have been forced to flee from the same kind of people that carried out these horrendous crimes, and the purpose of these attacks is to divide our societies. last but not least, i would also like to highlight the gender perspective of the issue. recent research not only underlines the trend of extremist groups creating targeted propaganda to attract women, but also emphasises the underestimated role women can play in tackling extremism in their families and local communities, which was also enshrined in the resolution on the prevention of radicalisation and recruitment of european citizens by terrorist organisations adopted last november by the european parliament.

on behalf of the verts/ale group. – mr president, first of all i have to say thank you to both rapporteurs for those files. we have had important and difficult discussions regarding the renewable energy progress report and the energy efficiency implementation report. to be honest, in the end, i believe that what we achieved at the level of the itre committee is really promising, and i can support the report as it was voted in the itre committee. of course, there are a lot of important issues, and some of them have already been mentioned by the rapporteur, mr pieper, and my colleagues as shadows. i agree with them regarding the importance of the full implementation of the existing current legislation, and also better reporting from the member states, the importance of research and innovation, a consumer-centric approach, and so on. but instead of going through all the relevant issues, i would like to point out only one very important topic: the question of targets. i believe that what has really happened in europe and what we have achieved in europe in renewable energy and energy efficiency in the last couple of years has absolutely been the consequence of ambitious binding targets. if we lose this framework from the energy market in europe for the climate policy in europe, for energy efficiency and renewable energy in europe, then anything which is said about our goals regarding renewables, energy efficiency and climate are nothing but wishful thinking. it is not a programme, it is not a european contribution to the global effort, it is just wishful thinking. so, what we need is ambitious binding targets on the eu level for energy efficiency, and also targets on the national level. without them, we cannot achieve what we have to achieve according to the paris agreement.
it's a two-card draw. - mr. deputy, i have to ask you to leave. you've given a long analysis of the question of commitment. there are indeed commitments in paris, there are commitments in the european union and there are commitments at national level. but wouldn't it make more sense to change that rhetoric to talk about opportunities for innovation, not obligations?
mr. president, norway, one of the world's largest oil and gas producers, has announced that it will ban the use of diesel and petrol cars from 2025. saudi arabia, with the world's largest oil reserves, is currently implementing the world's most ambitious solar energy program. so it's not hard to see where the world is headed. we don't have to be fanatical environmentalists to understand why europe needs renewable energy. you don't have to like this, but you have to like the economic growth that's happening in europe because of renewable energy. you can love the millions of new jobs that have been created in this industry, and you have to love, of course, the technological innovation or energy independence that renewables bring to europe. it is therefore timely to talk about the progress of european policies on renewable energy. but because we see, and there was a consensus in this room, that we're going to achieve the 2020 targets, we're going to achieve them, we're going to do well, so it's worth looking beyond 2020. this is why we have proposed to maintain mandatory renewable energy targets beyond 2020 not only at european level but also at member state level, as this is the only way to provide predictability for the industry and, in parallel, the only way to demonstrate that if we have these targets, we will achieve them. and the other very important thing is that we have to roll out all the barriers to investing in renewable energy. there's an incredible amount of administrative, bureaucratic hurdles in europe today. it is the role of parliament to propose to the member states that these bureaucratic obstacles be removed. europe must be at the forefront of this change. just as oil and natural gas replaced the world of coal in the 20th century, the world of renewable energy is replacing the world of fossil and nuclear energy. europe must be at the forefront of this.

in writing. ‒ the european union and monaco negotiations on the automatic exchange of financial account information aim to improve international tax cooperation and compliance. the agreement could represent an important step forward in efforts to combat tax fraud and tax evasion and updates a past agreement ensuring that monaco applies measures equivalent to the eu directive on taxation of savings income in the form of interest payments. the aim is to address situations where taxable persons seek to conceal income or capital representing assets for which tax has not yet been paid. in line with oecd standards, the further provisions of the agreement aim to ensure that the information shared does not only cover income such as interest and dividends, but also account balances and income from the sale of financial instruments. the unconditional exchange of information under the new agreement should be provided upon request in line with the latest developments in the work of the oecd and the union in this regard.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the adoption of the report approving the protocol to the eu-monaco agreement on the automatic exchange of financial accounting information. under the eu-monaco agreement of 2004, monaco has introduced measures equivalent to eu rules on taxation of interest income from savings. the new agreement aims to use the enhanced rules following the eu legal framework revised in december 2014 and in line with the oecd recommendations. this has brought the eu and monaco to a higher level of cooperation in preventing and combating tax fraud and tax evasion, which is welcome as it makes it easier to detect cases where taxpayers try to hide assets or income from the authorities for which they have not paid tax.

in writing. ‒ the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) aims to support the reintegration into the labour market of workers and self-employed persons made redundant as a result of globalisation, as a result of major structural changes in world trade patterns, or as a result of the prolongation of the global financial and economic crisis or a new global financial and economic crisis. belgium has submitted an application to mobilise the egf, under the reference number egf/2015/012 be/hainaut machinery, for a financial contribution from the egf. the commission has examined the application and found that it complies with the requirements of the relevant regulation, and i have therefore voted in favour of the adoption of the proposal.
in writing. ‒ on 4 may 2016, the commission adopted a proposal for a decision to mobilise the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) for belgium to support the reintegration into the labour market of workers made redundant by two companies in the hainaut region. this is the sixth application to be examined under the 2016 budget and concerns the mobilisation of a total of eur 1 824 041 from the egf for the benefit of belgium. the application concerns 488 dismissed workers and approximately 300 young people not in employment, education or training (neets). the request was submitted to the commission on 17 december 2015 and supplemented by additional information until 31 december 2015. the commission has concluded that the conditions for a financial contribution from the egf are met in the application, in accordance with the relevant provisions of the egf regulation. the personalised services to be provided to redundant workers comprise the following six measures: assistance/counselling/integration; job search assistance; integrated training; aid for setting up a business; support for collective projects; aid for job search and training. the commission considers that the measures described above constitute active labour market measures falling within the scope of the eligible activities under article 7 of the egf regulation. these activities are not a substitute for passive social protection measures. on the basis of the above, i voted in favour of the adoption of the report.
in writing. ‒ the european globalisation adjustment fund aims to provide additional support to workers affected by the consequences of major structural changes in world trade. belgium has submitted an application to mobilise the fund to provide personalised services to 488 workers made redundant by carwall sa, caterpillar belgium sa and doosan sa in the hainaut region and to 300 unemployed young people under 25 who are not in training or education in the hainaut region. the measures planned for the 488 redundant workers are: assistance/counselling/integration; job search facilitation; integrated training; aid for setting up a business; support for collective projects and job search and training allowances, while 300 young people are to be provided with further education/training or with an introductory mobilisation and guidance to explore their interests; targeted training, personalised further training, job search, training and mobility allowances. the cost of the measures is eur 3 040 069. the commission proposed to the parliament and the council that the financial contribution to the measures under the egf regulation be increased to 60% and amount to eur 1 824 041. in its report, the committee on budgets proposes that parliament agree with the commission that the intervention criteria laid down by the egf regulation are met and that belgium is therefore eligible for the aid in question. i voted for the motion.
in writing. ‒ the fund aims to provide support for workers affected by the consequences of major structural changes in world trade or made redundant as a result of the global financial and economic crisis and to support their reintegration into the labour market. i voted in favour of the belgian request.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the recovery plan for bluefin tuna. the european union is a contracting party to the international commission for the conservation of atlantic tunas (iccat), which is the regional fisheries management organisation (rfmo) responsible for the management of tuna and tuna-like species in the atlantic ocean and its adjacent seas. the aim of transposing the iccat recommendations is to ensure that they are applied uniformly throughout the eu. the uniform application should aim at ensuring a level playing field for all operators in the tuna fishery, in particular non-eu fishermen. otherwise, i.e. if different rules apply to foreign fleets, the efforts of eu fishermen and the restrictions imposed on them will be in vain. the commission should be able to take action to ensure that the union's fishing fleet is able to comply with the iccat convention. it is important that the european parliament does not lose its competence in this matter. the absence of the ep's participation in international negotiations would mean that it would have no say in the negotiations in iccat and subsequently in other international fora. the transposition of the recommendations of the regional fisheries management organisations should remain a joint competence of the european parliament and the council under the ordinary legislative procedure.
in writing. one success story in the conservation of ocean fish stocks is that international restrictive measures have increased the bluefin tuna stock over the past decade to such an extent that it is now possible to increase the catches by 20% per year. the aim of the proposal is to be supported as it aims to consolidate the different regulations of the competent iccat committee, thereby ensuring that they are binding on all member states. the rapporteur rightly criticises the commission for putting eu fleets in a more difficult position with some of its measures and for wanting to operate by delegated regulations more than is absolutely necessary.
in writing. ‒ the european union is a contracting party to the international commission for the conservation of atlantic tunas (iccat). in 2006, iccat adopted a multiannual plan to restore the bluefin tuna stock, which expires in 2022. the commission has proposed to the parliament and the council to repeal regulation (ec) no 302/2009 and to consolidate the measures adopted in the recovery plan between 2012 and 2014 into a single regulation. the committee on fisheries' report recommends that parliament approve the draft at first reading with 40 amendments. i voted accordingly.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the recovery plan for bluefin tuna in the eastern atlantic and the mediterranean. in making my decision, i took into account the fact that, according to the international commission for the conservation of atlantic tunas (iccat), the bluefin tuna biomass has been following very favourable trends since 2008 and that there is solid scientific evidence that the bluefin tuna stock has reached a healthy level of abundance. based on the data provided by the regional organisation, the decision to bring forward to 2016 a total catch of (23 155 tonnes) is supported, which is still well below the total catch for 2017 and the total catch before the start of the recovery plan. i also welcome the fact that the iccat recommendations take into account the specificities of the different types of tuna gear and that in this context the report draws attention to the role of small-scale, traditional traps in conservation. the eu should pay particular attention to traditional traps when implementing the recovery plan, as these devices have a very low impact on marine ecosystems due to their low energy consumption and low by-catch. i also welcome the rapporteur's emphasis on the lack of involvement of the ep in international negotiations. i support the idea that the implementation of the recommendations of the regional fisheries management organisations should remain a joint competence of the european parliament and the council under the ordinary legislative procedure.
in writing. ‒ the european union is a contracting party to the international commission for the conservation of atlantic tunas (iccat), the regional fisheries management organisation (rfmo) responsible for the management of tuna and tuna-like species in the atlantic ocean and its adjacent seas. iccat has the power to adopt conservation and management decisions (or recommendations) in its area of competence; these acts are binding and should be incorporated into union law. i voted in favour of this document.
in writing. ‒ a fully amended version of a report previously returned to the commission is put to the vote. the stocks of cod, herring and sprat are interlinked subsystems of the baltic sea ecosystem. the commission's original proposal already sought to address the interdependence of species. the amendment proposal, with its scientific references and justifications, further strengthens the legislative process with a complex approach. the proposal seeks to ensure the sustainability of the species in question, while taking into account the livelihoods of small-scale coastal fisheries. the commission's new approach to complex thinking which is further refined by the rapporteur and the amending proposal is also characterised by providing a framework for the establishment of a management plan that takes account not only of the stock changes of individual species but also of the interplay between the reproduction, habitat and fishing conditions of all the species referred to. on these grounds, i voted in favour of the motion.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the multiannual plan for the fisheries of the stocks listed. the proposal aims to establish a multi-species management framework for the baltic stocks of cod, herring and sprat. cod, herring and sprat accounted for more than 94% of the baltic sea catches in recent years. the baltic sea is a closed body of water, and all three species are found there. it is therefore essential to adopt a regulation recognising the interactions between the species concerned, including the impact of cod on herring and sprat stocks. further measures necessary to achieve the maximum sustainable yield for the stocks concerned should be defined on the basis of the regionalised approach of the common fisheries policy. however, the rules should be more closely linked to the principle of specific regionalisation and should allow for timely responses in the event of a sudden change in the situation of the stocks concerned. in the case of multiannual plans, the voice of the region concerned should be heard and acted upon, with the involvement of the european parliament at the appropriate stage.
in writing. sea fish are essential to a healthy diet. both fresh and canned baltic cod are available in most eu countries, including my own. the sustainability of cod, herring and sprat fisheries is likely to be addressed by complex legislation, which is essential to promote the stability of the regional ecosystem. the preservation of traditional small-scale coastal fishing is also an important socioeconomic aspect.
in writing. ‒ a management plan for cod in the baltic sea has been in place since 2008, but this does not yet apply to herring and sprat. however, since cod feeds on sprat and herring, the size of the cod stock influences the size of the herring and sprat stocks and vice versa. in october 2014, the commission published a multiannual plan for the baltic stocks of cod, herring and sprat and their fisheries with the aim of establishing a single management framework for the three stocks. proposes that parliament and the council repeal regulation (ec) no 1098/2007, amend regulation (ec) no 2187/2005 and incorporate into a regulation a multiannual plan for the baltic stocks of cod, herring and sprat and their fisheries. the committee on fisheries' report recommends that parliament adopt the commission's proposal at first reading with almost 50 amendments. i voted accordingly.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the establishment of a multiannual plan for the stocks and fisheries of cod, herring and sprat in the baltic sea, as i welcome the commission proposal, which has been endorsed by the rapporteur, that a multi-species management plan is needed for the baltic sea. this approach is more efficient than species-only management and provides greater security for the balanced and sustainable exploitation of fish stocks and the stability of fishing opportunities, including the livelihoods of fishermen. i also agree with the view that the measures necessary to achieve the maximum sustainable yield for the stocks concerned should be taken in accordance with the principle of regionalisation. this would ensure that sudden changes in the situation of stocks can be responded to in a timely manner. i also support the proposals for the protection of cod stocks during spawning, the protection of small-scale fisheries and an early review of the new management plan.
in writing. ‒ the european commission published a multiannual plan for the baltic stocks of cod, herring and sprat and their fisheries in october 2014. the proposal aims to establish a multi-species management framework for the baltic stocks of cod, herring and sprat. cod, herring and sprat accounted for more than 94% of the baltic sea catches in recent years. i voted in favour of the document on the agenda.
in writing. ‒ i have accepted the report of the legal committee on matrimonial property regimes. the report shall give appropriate coverage of jurisdiction, applicable law and recognition and enforcement of decisions. however, it does not cover the capacity of spouses, the existence, validity and recognition of marriage, maintenance obligations and succession after the death of a spouse. the autonomy of the member states in the field of family law is therefore guaranteed. the regulation can be a very useful tool for international couples living in the european union. in agreement with the rapporteur, the proposal for a regulation on matrimonial property regimes is clearly in the interest of the union and of international couples living in the union. it allows them to end many confusing cases and legal difficulties. the current second proposal on this subject incorporates a substantial part of the amendments previously proposed by parliament.
in writing. ‒ the council decision on jurisdiction, applicable law and the recognition and enforcement of judgments in matrimonial property regimes could not be adopted in the absence of the consensus required for all agreements in the field of family law. however, as 23 member states agreed in principle to the proposal, the council adopted the decision authorising enhanced cooperation, which was also agreed by the parliament at its meeting of 7 june 2016. the commission has now proposed to the council that it adopt a regulation to that effect, which will have to consult parliament. the legal affairs committee report concludes that the proposal for a regulation on matrimonial property regimes is clearly in the interests of the union and of international couples living in the union. it will allow you to put an end to many confusing cases and legal difficulties. it contains a substantial part of the amendments previously proposed by parliament. it therefore proposes that parliament give a favourable opinion on the proposal. i voted accordingly.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the adoption of the report approving the commission proposal on jurisdiction, applicable law and the recognition and enforcement of judgments in matrimonial property regimes, as it is clearly in the interests of the union and of international couples living in the union. i agree with the aim of the proposal, which is to reduce the practical and legal difficulties of international spouses living in the union in the day-to-day management of their property, or even in the division of their property following separation or death of one of the spouses. these difficulties are often caused by the fact that the provisions governing the property consequences of marriages differ significantly both in the legal provisions of the member states and in the private international law. although not all member states have joined the initiative, 17 eu member states have decided to provide a greater degree of predictability and legal certainty for international couples living in the union through an enhanced cooperation procedure, while respecting the principle of proportionality.
in writing. ‒ the present proposal for a council decision on jurisdiction and the law applicable to, and the recognition and enforcement of, decisions in matrimonial property regimes is the second on this subject. following the blockage of negotiations between member states as all agreements in the field of family law must be adopted unanimously this proposal returns to parliament in the form of enhanced cooperation. i voted for it.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report of the committee on legal affairs on the law applicable to the property aspects of registered partnerships. this proposal is the same version of the cases concerning matrimonial property regimes. the scope of the matters relating to the property consequences of registered partnerships covers jurisdiction, applicable law and the recognition and enforcement of decisions. however, it does not cover the legal capacity of the spouses, the existence, validity and recognition of the partnership, maintenance obligations and succession after the death of the spouse. the autonomy of the member states in the field of family law is therefore guaranteed. this regulation does not affect the substantive law of the member states on registered partnerships or their property consequences.
in writing. ‒ this draft regulation is the counterpart of the draft regulation discussed in the previous point. its adoption in this form is justified by the same circumstances and is also clearly in the interests of the union and of international couples living in the union. the committee on legal affairs therefore recommends in its report that parliament should give a favourable opinion on this proposal as on the previous one. i voted accordingly.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the adoption of the report approving the commission proposal on jurisdiction, applicable law and the recognition and enforcement of judgments in matters relating to the property consequences of registered partnerships. in my view, the adoption of the proposal is in the interests of the union and of international couples living in the union, just as the proposal's counterpart seeks to make the property regime of married couples more predictable. the treaty on the functioning of the european union provides that the union is to facilitate access to justice, in particular by applying the principle of mutual recognition of judicial and extrajudicial decisions in civil matters. although the council concluded that unanimity could not be reached on the adoption of the draft regulations on the property aspects of registered partnerships, by february 2016, 17 member states had indicated their intention to establish enhanced cooperation between themselves in this area. i welcome this decision, as the increasing mobility of persons in the area without internal borders leads to an increase in the number of couples formed by persons of different member state nationalities, who also need to be guaranteed predictability and legal certainty.
in writing. ‒ the present proposal for a council decision on jurisdiction and the applicable law, as well as on the recognition and enforcement of judgments in matters of property law relating to registered partnerships is the second in this field. following the blockage of negotiations between member states as all agreements in the field of family law must be adopted unanimously this proposal returns to parliament in the form of enhanced cooperation. i voted for it.
in writing. - my fellow members of parliament! the decades-long civil war in eastern congo is now africa's most serious armed conflict. the unrelenting wave of murder and violence has also had a dramatic effect on the lives of the christian churches, which make up the majority of the population. one of the most powerful militias in the region, the terrorist group known as the international muslim brotherhood, has been carrying out a particularly brutal crackdown on christian denominations and churches in the eastern congo region. we must repeat here the desperate cry of the christian communities in the congo: as in many parts of the world, genocide is being perpetrated in africa by the followers of islamic extremism. the aggression of the muslim brotherhood fits well with the overall islamist advance that has unfolded in many parts of africa. the aim of the militias following the ideology of international jihadist movements is to establish caliphates under islamic law across the continent in countries with significant christian traditions. the recent atrocities and executions in may have forced thousands of families to flee eastern congo, while religious leaders are trying to hold on to the deeply traumatized faithful. the continued intimidation has made it even more difficult for the communities to survive, as the catholic, anglican, and other christian denominations have stopped holding services. the international community, including europe, has a moral obligation to apply political pressure immediately to bring peace to the congo. and while the persecution continues, all available humanitarian and development resources must be mobilized to prevent another wave of refugees.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the adoption of the parliament's resolution, hoping that the european parliament would thereby draw attention to a widespread violence and mass human rights violations against which the international community has been unable to act effectively for nearly two decades. i find it particularly worrying and unacceptable that irregular armed militias of various compositions operating along the country's eastern border are systematically and deliberately committing violence against women and children, and often recruiting young children to fight and commit murders. i therefore support the demand in the resolution that the international community, including the un security council, should take much more decisive action than has been the case so far to stop the violence and punish those responsible. i agree that the european union should take the lead in this endeavour, in line with our common foreign policy objectives for africa and our european principles of human rights, by sending a special observer to the region and initiating concrete international sanctions against the perpetrators.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report, as the aim is to increase the added value and optimise the efficiency of the existing framework. education and training play an important role in providing knowledge and professional skills that enable employees to be competitive and innovative. the number of people enrolled in higher education has increased dramatically over the past decade, but at the same time there is unprecedented youth unemployment. between 2011 and 2014, the average unemployment rate in the 28 member states of the union increased particularly among young people (aged 25 to 29) with tertiary education (+12.9%). this process must be stopped. the education and training 2020 strategy can be an important tool for promoting the knowledge economy and social inclusion. the objectives set an appropriate minimum threshold for qualifications and concern the raising of the level of education. an important aspect of a responsible education policy is the development of relations between schools and families. a supportive home environment can not only help to offset educational poverty but also to counter the appeal of violent extremism among young people. it is also important to involve parents in the current debates on education. parent organisations should be involved in the work of 'education and training 2020' and best practices should be applied in relation to cooperation between schools and families.
in writing. ‒ the commission carried out a synthesis evaluation of the education and training 2020 framework in 2014. the committee on culture and education's motion for a resolution on this point points out that education and training play an important role in the acquisition of the knowledge and professional skills needed to make employees competitive and innovative. they can also play an important role in the development of broad-minded, empathetic, inquisitive people and responsible citizens with a strong sense of identity, a good knowledge of their culture and traditions and a recognition and respect for common european values. the report welcomes the fact that the adjustment of the framework has placed equal emphasis on the objectives of employability and on social cohesion, equality, non-discrimination and civic competences. the report highlights that, although the number of people in higher education has increased exponentially over the past decade, this has been accompanied by unprecedented levels of youth unemployment in europe, including among those with a higher education qualification. it focuses in particular on the role of education and training in integrating the masses of people arriving in europe as migrants. i voted for the report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the adoption of the report on the follow-up to the strategic framework for european cooperation in education and training, as it not only highlights the achievements of the work carried out under 'education and training 2020' to date, but also rightly highlights the further opportunities and challenges in the field of education and training. i agree with the report that there are still huge problems in quality, accessibility and socioeconomic disparities in education and training and that ambitious, coordinated and effective policy measures are needed at both european and national level. i also share the rapporteur's concern about the growing radicalisation, violence, abuse and behavioural problems that are already emerging at the level of primary education. it would therefore be useful for the commission to carry out research at union level in this regard, examining the response of member states to such trends.
in writing. ‒ the commission carried out a synthesis evaluation of the education and training 2020 framework in 2014 in cooperation with the member states. the interested parties made a number of recommendations to the commission and the council with a view to increasing the added value of the framework and optimising its effectiveness. the role of informal management bodies was strengthened and feedback loops were introduced between working groups, dgs or high-level groups. some member states still need to improve the way they interact with formal and informal organisations by sending the right person to the right meeting and using substitution as little as possible. i was very much in favour of the s&d position.
in writing. ‒ the development of renewable energies requires a new approach that makes them a key pillar of the european union's energy model. the shift towards a sustainable energy production model is a societal priority that cannot be solved by the market alone. regulation and democratic participation are also necessary if we want to avoid negative social and environmental impacts. the eu's legal instrument is the renewable energy directive 2009/28/ec, which started the eu's transformation of the member states' energy structures. it sets binding targets and provides clear rules on supervision and monitoring. the commitment to promote biofuels in transport clearly harmed the food industry, rather than triggering a profound debate on the lack of coordination of logistics and urban planning policies and the need for comprehensive planning to ensure their sustainability. unfortunately, in many cases the report contains provisions which would allow the commission to set binding targets, to monitor them and to impose penalties if they are not met. this is clearly an interference with the energy mix of the member states. in many cases, the rapporteur expresses, implicitly or explicitly, the need to give the commission the power to adopt tax legislation within the member states' tax policies that favours renewable energy production and does not support fossil energy production and to achieve tax harmonisation in this area at eu level. all these factors combined to make me abstain.
in writing. ‒ i welcome the commission's commitment to making europe the world leader in renewable energy. this is not only necessary for industrial policy reasons, but could also contribute to reducing the dependence of certain central and eastern european member states on a single fossil fuel supplier, thereby enabling the energy independence and security of europe, the world's largest energy importer. in addition, we have a responsibility to act on climate change, which can be greatly helped by increasing the share of renewable energy. a policy on energy sources based on national targets will in the long term guarantee the industry and investors the security needed to invest in electricity generation capacity and in transmission and distribution infrastructure. it is important that the definition of the energy mix of the member states remains a national competence, and that each member state is able to develop its own renewable energy sources and shape its energy mix. state aid measures have helped to achieve the eu's objectives in many member states, but decisive political momentum is needed to achieve further, more substantial results. to achieve an efficient and renewable energy model by 2050, regulation at european level must address a number of obstacles to progress: it must promote investment and its democratic oversight, and create a stable investment framework.

in writing. ‒ the report of the committee on industry, research and energy proposes a resolution on the european commission's 2015 progress report on renewable energy. the report unanimously recognises that the union has a historic duty to combat climate change and to reduce its dependence on external energy sources. to this end, renewable energy must be made a key pillar of the european union's energy model. the report notes that with the adoption of the renewable energy directive 2009/28/ec, which sets binding targets, europe has started to transform the energy structure of the member states. however, while austria, bulgaria, the czech republic, denmark, estonia, finland, croatia, italy, latvia, lithuania, romania and sweden have already met their 2020 targets ahead of time or will soon do so, the report considers it necessary to call on belgium, the united kingdom, france, the netherlands, luxembourg, malta and spain to take further measures to ensure that their 2020 targets are met. it underlines that a decisive political push is needed if the eu is to meet and exceed the 2020 targets. the commission notes that the union's electricity market is characterised by a high level of renewable energy and that the union's electricity market is characterised by a high level of renewable energy. i voted for the bill.
in writing. ‒ i agree with the promotion of renewable energy and that it should be made a main pillar of the eu's energy model. i am absolutely right that we have a fundamental responsibility to fight climate change and a historic duty to fulfill. we must also reduce our dependence on energy sources from other parts of the world if we are to structure our production model, create quality jobs and lead the development of the strategic technologies on which our energy transition is based. i consider it a fundamental problem that the european council supports such a low target of 27% for the period after 2020 (to 2030). the fact that the target is only binding at eu level is also a concern, and thus gives some member states the opportunity to hide in the shadows of the best-performing member states. that is why i supported the report, which insists on a higher target and its binding nature at member state level. i think the age of government-linked energy lobbying is over, and i agree that energy policy is a social priority, not just an economic one. i share the view that regulation of the renewable energy sector at european level should address the many challenges that are holding back its development, promote public investment and democratic oversight, and create a stable investment framework for collective and democratic governance of the energy sector, with a view to achieving a fully self-sustaining, efficient and clean energy model by 2050.

in writing. ‒ between 1990 and 2014, the european union's gdp increased by 46%, while greenhouse gas emissions decreased by 23% over the same period. businesses and citizens are achieving economic growth with less of a burden on the climate, and eu directives to improve energy efficiency, reduce carbon emissions and increase the share of renewable energy in total energy consumption play a major role in this. the european union is well on track to meet its 2020 targets of reducing co2 emissions by 20%, increasing the share of renewable energy sources in total energy consumption to 20% and improving energy efficiency by 20%. this is largely due to the successful emissions trading system, which encourages investment in renewable energy and emission reductions. the commission's efforts to pursue a single climate and energy policy and a european electricity market are welcome, and it is setting even more ambitious targets. however, the mandatory 40% energy efficiency target for 2030 is excessive, as it would place an unacceptable burden on member states and impose unrealistic expectations on them. for these reasons, i did not support the adoption of the report in the final vote.

in writing. ‒ on 18 november 2015, the commission published its report on the implementation of directive 2012/27/eu of the european parliament and of the council on energy efficiency. the committee on industry, research and energy proposes that a resolution be adopted on this report. the plan states that greenhouse gas emissions in the union decreased by 23% between 1990 and 2014. over the same period, the union's gdp increased by 46%. notes that the union is on track to meet the 2007 targets of reducing co2 emissions by 20%, increasing the share of renewable energy sources in total energy consumption to 20% and improving energy efficiency by 20%. it is concerned, however, that the cost-cutting effect of energy savings is often eliminated by state special taxes and a complex reporting system. this is partly due to the contradictory eu climate legislation, the complexity of energy efficiency legislation and national energy policy actions, which have a significant impact on some aspects of the european approach. it therefore proposes to call on the european commission to make further efforts to achieve a single climate and energy policy and a european electricity market. i voted for the bill.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report because i believe that the issue of energy efficiency should be placed at the centre of the agenda to eradicate energy poverty. i believe that a 20% improvement in energy efficiency should not be a problem for member states and that we can even achieve a more ambitious target (40%) in the future. of course, this can only be achieved if member states really put this at the heart of their strategy. as a first step, i believe that improving energy efficiency in the home is the most important way to reduce energy poverty. i agree that the ets has an important role to play in both emissions and efficiency. i believe that reducing greenhouse gas emissions will also encourage investment in energy-efficient technologies. instead of punitive and incapacitating policies, we must prioritize policies that encourage innovation! i agree that the difficulty in meeting the targets can be partly explained by the fact that several countries have been in an economic and financial crisis. there is a need to address the partially contradictory eu climate legislation, the complexity of energy efficiency legislation and the national energy policy actions that have a significant impact on some aspects of the european approach. i find it interesting that the report states that 61% of imported natural gas is used in buildings (mainly residential buildings) and that an ambitious building renovation policy could reduce this by 60% in the short term. it's time to end the waste of energy and fossil fuels.

in writing. the uk's withdrawal will impoverish europe and the withdrawal will require long and complex negotiations. the task for the 27 is to restore trust in the eu and to prepare for substantive european reforms in line with citizens' expectations. there is a need for self-criticism, a rethinking of the flawed immigration policy that was a key element of the british campaign, respect for the principle of subsidiarity, well-timed and realistic responses to european crises and a better alignment of the eu with citizens' expectations in all areas. these are the content challenges that need to be addressed first. only if leaders of the member states and the eu institutions face the criticism of the union, learn from it and take political responsibility will they be able to regain the trust of their citizens. the fidesz-kdnp delegation to the european parliament will as before use all possible means to make the views and interests of hungarian citizens appear at the european level and draw attention to the necessary changes.
in writing. the outcome of the brexit referendum will fundamentally shape not only the future of the united kingdom but also that of the european union. it is therefore important that the process should be swift and as peaceful as possible, in order to put an end to the grievances that divide europe. we call on the commission and the council to do everything possible to preserve the gains of free movement of labour and to represent properly the interests of european citizens working in the uk. the outcome of the vote is also a signal to the european community that we need to build a stronger, more democratic, more transparent union with credible answers to the problems of democratic deficits, dysfunction and the refugee crisis. the key question for hungary is whether it can participate in this process. if our country is left out of a stronger integration, which is no longer primarily an economic issue, then we will not only face economic backwardness, but also the resulting loss of democratic value. even britain, with a much greater economic weight than our country, was forced to incur very serious economic losses on the first day after the vote. weakening european cooperation can lead to an increase in social and political conflicts within europe and to economic weakening. since no responsible political force in europe can want this, political communication that populistally disparages brussels must be stopped immediately. instead, we must build a better europe to protect and fulfil our common values.

on behalf of the s&d group. – mr president, as a matter of solidarity i am going to address my speaking points on behalf of my colleague seb dance, whose flight has unfortunately been delayed. i would like to thank the rapporteur and the shadow rapporteurs for all their work on this important file. emission limits for non-road mobile machinery (nrmm) might not sound like the sexiest subject, but it is an important piece of the jigsaw when it comes to tackling air pollution. in cities, non-mobile machinery such as construction equipment on building sites, trains and generators can significantly contribute to air pollution in the eu, and nrmm contributes around 15% of total nox emissions and 5% of total pm emissions. these harmful emissions are linked to low birth weights, asthma, pulmonary heart disease, strokes and a variety of cancers, and are estimated to cause 50 000 premature deaths across the uk alone every year, and 10 000 in london. this proposal is a perfect example of how trade in a common market can also deliver environmental and health benefits for citizens. rather than allowing manufacturers to undercut each other in a race to the bottom on environmental standards, these ambitious and binding measures on nrmm will ensure industry is manufacturing progressively cleaner engines for these machines, which will go a long way to cleaning up toxic air pollution in the eu. of course, should a post-brexit uk want to remain a part of the eu common market, which many proponents of brexit have said they support, the uk manufacturers will continue to be bound to these same rules, but without any national democratic representation having a say on how these rules are made. the inconvenient truth for those who sought to argue the environmental benefits of a britain outside the eu is that air pollution has an unfortunate habit of not respecting borders. over one third of the uk’s air pollution is blown in from across the english channel. cross-border cooperation and common laws across european countries will be crucial – whether britain is part of the eu or not – in ensuring we do not end up with a race to the bottom on environmental standards. any new regulations in the uk must reflect this reality. in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the agreement granting eu citizens visa-free short-stay visas. the agreement is both a success in deepening relations between the european union and the republic of peru and a further means of strengthening economic and cultural links and encouraging political dialogue on various issues. it would also strengthen regional coherence, as peru is one of the few latin american countries whose citizens require a visa, and would thus also make a significant contribution to bringing european citizens and peruvians closer together. the agreement will strengthen trade and investment. the eu is peru's third largest trading partner (mainly machinery and transport equipment) and the main recipient of peruvian exports (agro-food and mining products). in addition, the eu remains the largest investor in peru, with over 50% of foreign direct investment coming from the eu. strengthening the position of democracy and human rights remains an important issue for peru, and the visa liberalisation agreement can contribute to a balanced and in-depth political dialogue on human rights and specific issues such as the situation of women.

in writing. ‒ i supported the draft resolution on emission limit values and type-approval requirements for internal combustion engines in non-road mobile machinery and equipment, as the machinery covered by the draft regulation is responsible for a significant proportion of nitrogen dioxide emissions, so regulating the area is of paramount importance. air pollution as a serious threat to human health and the environment should be addressed as a matter of priority. the emission limit values for engines covered by the draft regulation are regulated by an existing directive. this directive has been amended several times, but several technical reviews have identified shortcomings in the current form of the legislation. the scope is too limited as it does not cover certain engine categories. the last time new emission stages were introduced was in 2004 when the directive was amended, which no longer reflects the current state of the art. in addition, the emission limit values for each engine category are not consistent. i consider it particularly important that a compromise has been reached with the council, which represents the member states, since the legislation will be in the form of a regulation and will thus enter national legal systems immediately.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on combating trafficking in human beings. trafficking in human beings is one of the most heinous forms of crime and the industry which unfortunately grows out of it must be completely eliminated. i agree with the report that in our societies, which are based on respect for human rights, including gender equality, there is no place for such activities. the concept itself should be interpreted in a holistic way, focusing not only on sexual exploitation but also on forced labour, organ trafficking, forced begging, forced marriage, the problem of child soldiers or the trafficking of infants. trafficking in human beings may also be a consequence of global economic and social inequalities, which may be exacerbated by social inequalities between men and women. this must be prevented, as violence against women is identified in the eu strategy as a trigger for trafficking in human beings.

in writing. ‒ energy labelling has environmental benefits, as consumers can compare products in terms of energy efficiency and make informed, cost-effective and environmentally-conscious purchasing decisions. however, the current labelling of energy consumption has become opaque and partly meaningless, mainly due to the overcrowding and diversification of the highest rated energy efficiency classes, which understandably confuses consumers. market surveillance in the member states also needs to be improved and would benefit from clearer and simpler management of product information and labelling schemes. a regulation of the european parliament and of the council establishing a framework for energy-efficiency labelling, which aims to provide greater transparency for consumers and authorities on energy-related products placed on the union market, is therefore a welcome objective. the commission proposal replaces the current framework directive on energy labelling and introduces a mechanism for the reallocation of energy efficiency classes. the proposal also provides for a product database and defines the obligations of operators. in view of the above, i voted in favour of adopting the motion for a resolution.
in writing. ‒ energy labelling has environmental benefits, providing consumers with relevant and comparable information on the energy performance of products anywhere in the union. this will help them to make environmentally conscious purchasing decisions, which is also good for saving money. however, the current labelling of energy consumption has become opaque and partly meaningless, mainly due to the overcrowding and diversification of the highest rated energy efficiency classes. the original aim of energy labelling was to provide citizens with information to help them understand the environmental impact and life cycle of different products. the assessment of directive 2010/30/ec has, however, revealed a number of shortcomings which, if addressed successfully, could lead to further significant energy savings. the commission proposal replaces the current framework directive on energy labelling and introduces a mechanism for the reallocation of energy efficiency classes. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'common carrier' in the context of the directive. the re-design is intended to ensure that the calculation of the energy class reflects both the absolute performance (energy consumption) and the relative performance (energy efficiency, taking into account relevant characteristics of the product model such as size, volume and/or comfort) of the product.

in writing. ‒ the revision of the energy labelling directive is highly necessary as the current system is very confusing. the ep report in its final form does not enable consumers to take informed decisions – although the whole energy union is meant to be consumer-centric. greens pushed for changes that would allow existing loopholes to be closed and real and accurate energy consumption to be shown. key aspects were (a) a new a-to-g energy label applying to all labelled products by 2023 at the latest; (b) a central product database containing all necessary technical information for checks and controls; (c) one single label for each product group; (d) provisions for stricter requirements on larger appliances; and (e) energy consumption information to be displayed in advertisements for labelled products. as these aspects are not fully reflected in the report, greens could not support the text in the plenary, and we abstained in the vote. nevertheless we were very much in favour of giving the rapporteur a mandate to start negotiations with the council so that the revision of the directive is not delayed any further.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report because i believe that by increasing energy efficiency we can not only protect our environment but also our money. in energy efficiency labelling, the single label has become a well-known concept accepted at eu level. in recent years, the ag scale has been replaced by a more ambiguous system, and i therefore support making the system clearer. with the refinement of the categories, we can now return to the ag designation. the fact that the majority of society favours more energy-efficient systems is not in dispute. however, it should also be borne in mind that higher-quality products also mean higher prices. in regions where livelihoods are a problem, energy efficiency is not the primary consideration, consumers will buy cheaper products. in fact, this regulation is not mandatory for used products, which also creates a loophole. i believe that lower energy prices are not negligible in the light of the objective of eliminating energy poverty and should also be an incentive to increase energy efficiency, both from the production and the consumer side. without this, we will not achieve the minimum reduction target of 27% by 2030, or at least regional disparities will persist. i think that the communication and education campaign on energy efficiency, as outlined in the report, is a good tool, but i also think that we should encourage the promotion of local renewable energy production.

in writing. ‒ by extending the tasks, powers and mandate of frontex, a european border and coast guard will be created to protect the eu's external borders, whether from migratory pressure or other unforeseen security threats, including international crime. the european border and coast guard shall consist of the european border and coast guard agency and the cooperation of the national authorities responsible for border management. the new agency will operate with 1500 border guards on standby, who can be deployed within seven days in any member state where the protection of the external borders is not adequately ensured. if a member state is unwilling to cooperate with the new agency, the reintroduction of internal border control may be a last resort. i voted in favour of the decision because the establishment of the guard is a concrete, practical step to protect our citizens and ensure the internal security of the union.

in writing. ‒ the commission has proposed to the european parliament and the council to adopt a regulation on the european border and coast guard and repealing regulation (ec) no 2007/2004, regulation (ec) no 863/2007 and council decision 2005/267/ec. eight schengen states (belgium, denmark, germany, hungary, austria, slovenia, sweden and norway) reintroduced internal border controls in response to the secondary movement of irregular migrants, which they considered to be a serious threat to internal security and public policy. this suggests that the tools and mechanisms developed over time to ensure the effective functioning of the schengen area are insufficient, given the scale of the current migration crisis and the threat posed by terrorist activities. the commission therefore proposes the creation of a european border and coast guard (ebcg) concept, which would consist of a new european border and coast guard agency replacing frontex and a set of national authorities responsible for border management, including coast guards to the extent appropriate to their border control tasks. the report by the committee on civil liberties, justice and home affairs recommends that parliament adopt the commission's proposal with more than 170 amendments at first reading. i was all the more pleased to vote for the draft because i am personally convinced that the schengen system can only be maintained if border protection, asylum and immigration policy are transferred from the competence of the member states to that of the community.

in writing. ‒ this is a gap-filling amendment to the legislation establishing the european maritime safety agency, adapted to the exceptional migration situation in the mediterranean over the last few years. one of the key elements of the amendment is the regulation of cooperation with the newly formed agency, the european border and coast guard agency and the european fisheries control agency. the cooperation aims to make the activities of the three organisations more cost-effective by sharing their resources in a reasonable way, while assisting the competent bodies of the member states in the fulfilment of their very diverse maritime safety and coast guarding tasks. it is important, however, that the envisaged enhanced cooperation should not imply the withdrawal of any decision-making powers from any member state concerned. i supported the adoption of the report.
in writing. ‒ the main objective of the proposal voted today is to build up eu cooperation between the european border and coast guard, the european maritime safety agency and the european fisheries control agency, in order to provide a more efficient and cost-effective service to national authorities carrying out border protection activities. the proposal also aims to create and provide multifunctional services for national authorities in the organisation of the coastguard. the european maritime safety agency shall promote the protection of the external maritime borders of the european union, inter alia, by providing information and data exchange, surveillance and communication services using appropriate technologies.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the establishment of a european fisheries control agency, the aim of which is to coordinate monitoring, prevention and control activities at european level in order to improve knowledge of the marine environment. national authorities with coast guard functions are responsible for a number of tasks. this places a heavy burden on the authorities and i therefore agree with the aim of the proposal to coordinate the operations of the three european agencies (the european fisheries control agency, the european maritime safety agency and the european border and coast guard agency) at sea and to share information useful for their actions. i am confident that they will be able to act in a joint and effective manner in the implementation of control, safety and surveillance operations, providing information, tools and training to national authorities. this cooperation is of paramount importance in the current migration situation to protect our external borders.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the proposal to align the tasks of the european fisheries control agency with those of the european maritime safety agency and the european border and coast guard agency in the area of cooperation in the performance of coast guard tasks. as the report describes, national authorities with coast guard functions are responsible for a number of tasks in such diverse areas as defence, security, maritime rescue, border control, environmental protection and general law enforcement. there are currently 316 such national authorities in the european union. these numerous authorities work together through 70 different structures. as a consequence, the current system of cooperation is slow and fraught with shortcomings, namely the lack of information on the powers, responsibilities and capabilities of other authorities, the limited number of operational tools, the lack of interoperability between systems and tools, and the limited possibility of joint planning and joint operations. and that's why i think this situation is not sustainable. i welcome the fact that the proposal will lead to coordination of monitoring, prevention and control activities at european level to improve knowledge of the marine environment and to promote concerted and cost-effective action.
