in writing. ‒ the commission has proposed to the parliament and the council that a regulation amending regulation (eu, euratom) no 883/2013 be adopted as regards the secretariat of the supervisory committee of the european anti-fraud office (olaf). the proposal aims to strengthen the independence of the olaf supervisory committee secretariat and thus ensure the more efficient functioning of the supervisory committee, as the european parliament has repeatedly asked the commission to do. under the proposed regulation, the secretariat of the supervisory board will no longer be provided by olaf but by the commission. the budget appropriations allocated to the secretariat of the supervisory committee shall be transferred from the current budget line to the commission budget line, and the establishment plan of olaf shall be transferred to the commission establishment plan. the proposed amendment therefore has no financial implications for the european budget. in its report, the committee on budgetary control recommends adopting parliament's position at first reading in line with the commission's proposal. i voted accordingly.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the legislative amendment proposed in the report, which aims to give the secretariat of the olaf supervisory committee greater operational autonomy, thereby facilitating the commission's more efficient functioning. as a member of the european parliament, i will continue to support any initiative that strengthens olaf and makes its work more effective, given the widespread corruption in many member states - perhaps most of all in my own country - often at governmental level, linked to the misuse of eu funds, which puts olaf in a position to meet significant additional burdens and expectations in the short term.
in writing. ‒ the purpose of this proposal is to strengthen the independence of the olaf supervisory committee secretariat and thus to ensure the more efficient functioning of the supervisory committee. the european parliament has on several occasions asked the commission to take measures to strengthen the independent functioning of the secretariat of the supervisory committee, for example in its report on the 2013 discharge procedure or in its resolution on the 2014 annual report of the supervisory committee of olaf. i was supportive.

in writing. ‒ on 2 december 2015, the european parliament adopted a decision setting up a special committee on tax rulings and other measures similar in nature or effect (taxe 2). the special committee submitted its report after the expiry of its six-month mandate. the report draws conclusions and makes recommendations against tax fraud and tax evasion, estimated by the commission at eur 1 trillion per year, and aggressive tax planning. it regrets, however, that the commission and the council continue to refuse to agree to the proposal for a regulation laying down detailed provisions governing the exercise of the european parliament's right of inquiry, and that this is why parliament's special committees and committees of inquiry still lack sufficient powers, such as the right to call witnesses or to exercise access to documents, as compared to similar committees of the parliaments of the member states and the us congress. it also objects to the fact that the council has recently made several comprehensive ex ante findings in tax matters without taking into account or even awaiting the opinion of the european parliament. i voted for the report.

in writing. ‒ the ban on whaling was imposed in 1986 by a decision of the international whaling commission. this measure was necessary because of the growing risk of extinction of the species. but japan, for almost incomprehensible reasons, has consistently ignored this and continued to hunt whales on pseudoscientific grounds - not sparing pregnant females. japan (and a few other countries) only temporarily abandoned the practice in 2014, despite continued international outrage and a damning ruling by the international court of justice. in 2015, he announced that he would continue to kill whales. the motion for a resolution tabled by each group condemns japan's conduct on this issue with due responsibility and firmness, and the consolidated joint motion properly integrates the resolutions of the groups, as a consensus has been reached on this issue. i voted yes to the resolution, of course.
in writing. ‒ on 31 march 2014 the un’s international court of justice – in its legally binding decision – ruled that japan’s state-subsidised whale-hunting in the southern ocean did not fall within the scope of scientific research and therefore was considered illegal. in spite of the ruling, japan has recently resumed whaling. following the suggestion of greenpeace, activism from within japan should be combined with international pressure. therefore, i voted in favour of the resolution of the european parliament which stands up against this outdated and illegal practice.
in writing. ‒ on this subject, the gue/ngl, efdd and verts/ale groups tabled a joint motion for a resolution of the european parliament, the ppe, s&d, ecr and alde each on their own. the groups reached an agreement and adopted a joint compromise motion. i voted for the motion.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the joint motion for a resolution because i do not think it is timely to restart whaling in japan. based on the data that we have, i think that this would threaten biodiversity. the resolution was prompted by the fact that in november 2015 the japanese fisheries agency informed the international whaling commission that it would resume whaling under the new scientific research whaling programme. this is a concern because in order to prevent the extinction of whale stocks and to allow them to recover, the international whaling commission (iwc) adopted a moratorium on all commercial whaling in 1982, which is still in force. the moratorium allows for an exception only for a limited number of whales hunted for strictly scientific purposes, known as 'special permit whaling'. the resolution describes how commercial whaling continues in many countries despite the moratorium, with japan for example having been conducting such whaling under special permits for decades. the commission has also provided information on the number of vessels that have been involved in the illegal whaling activities in the area of the north sea. that is why i am not going to open the possibility of whaling, and i stress that this debate could extend to the eu-japan trade agreement.
in writing. ‒ the proposal strongly supports the maintenance of a general moratorium on commercial whaling and a ban on international trade in whale products, while urging the abolition of unjustified 'scientific whaling' and supporting the designation of large ocean and marine areas as sanctuaries where all whaling is prohibited indefinitely. i voted in favour of the s&d position.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution on the eu guarantee to belarus by the european investment bank. the commission has assessed the current political, economic, social and environmental situation in belarus and has concluded that the relaxation of the union's restrictive approach towards belarus is duly justified and that the eib financing covered by the union guarantee is therefore available to belarus. i agree with the motion opposing the granting of this guarantee to belarus. in my view, the commission's assessment should have focused more on the fact that belarus remains a centralised and autocratic state with a strict control by the president in terms of its internal politics, and that belarus is the only country in europe that still applies the death penalty. the integrity of the recent elections has been called into question by significant issues and the situation of human rights and democracy raises further serious concerns, in particular with regard to freedom of assembly and association, and freedom of expression and freedom of the media. if progress has been made in the last two years, it is not to the extent that it outweighs the above-mentioned reservations. the commission notes that the commission has not provided any evidence that the guarantee was granted to the beneficiaries.

in writing. ‒ the report on the implementation of the un convention on the rights of persons with disabilities provides a comprehensive overview of the situation and the difficulties encountered. in this context, i would like to recall that persons with disabilities are often excluded from, or do not have effective access to, education and training services where personalised education processes are needed to take account of their level of disability. they should therefore be supported in developing their social, economic and educational potential. i stress that the necessary measures must be taken to ensure that all students with disabilities benefit from the benefits of reasonable accommodation necessary to enable them to exercise their right to an inclusive, quality education. member states and responsible regional and local authorities should be encouraged to strengthen their training programmes for all stakeholders involved in non-formal and informal learning. this will help them to play a role in overcoming school prejudices against people with disabilities, particularly those with intellectual and psychosocial disabilities. in the light of the above, i voted in favour of the adoption of the report.
in writing. ‒ in december 2010, the eu became the first regional integration organisation to accede to the un convention on the rights of persons with disabilities (crpd). the crpd is one of the human rights treaties with the most states parties and signatories. the convention has been signed by all 28 eu member states, ratified by 25 member states except finland and ireland, and the netherlands is close to acceding to the convention. following its accession to the convention, the eu, like the other states parties, was required to prepare an introductory report on the implementation of the convention. the commission submitted this in june 2014 and the crpd committee responded in may 2015. in its response, the commission largely took into account the recommendation adopted by parliament in may 2015. the eu is obliged to respond to the crpd committee's questions in this regard by september 2016. the ep therefore decided to draw up an own-initiative report in order to incorporate its opinion in the commission's reply. i voted in favour of the report submitted by the committee on employment and social affairs.
in writing. ‒ in addition to its content, the convention is also of major importance for reasons of principle, as it is the first and so far the only international human rights treaty to be ratified by the eu itself in december 2010. in accordance with the treaty, the eu has undertaken to report on the implementation of the convention and to review it regularly. i supported the report, which points out, among other things, that people with disabilities are still often excluded from mainstream society and deprived of their human rights. analysis of the reasons shows that while some of the commitments fall within eu competence, their implementation by the member states is not satisfactory. the members of the socialist group are committed to the protection and promotion of the human rights of disabled people. i agree that persons with disabilities are entitled to equal rights, inalienable dignity, equal treatment, independent living, autonomy, support from publicly funded schemes and full participation in society as full citizens. it should be noted that articles 21 and 26 of the charter of fundamental rights of the european union explicitly prohibit discrimination on the grounds of disability and provide for the equal participation of persons with disabilities in society. i can only imagine this in a stronger european union, and i am confident that we will be able to act together on a growing number of issues.

in writing. ‒ european surveys show that 68% of teenagers and 18% of children already drink energy drinks regularly. beverages commonly consumed as soft drinks by young people may contain as much as 27 grams of sugar and 87 milligrams of caffeine per can. moreover, according to the warning on the label of the products, their consumption is not recommended at all for children and pregnant women. the european commission's plan would have allowed these drinks to be marketed with labels claiming that they increase alertness and have a positive effect on concentration. the european food safety authority (efsa) concluded that the scientific basis of the claims was established. however, the intention of the legislator in regulating health claims made on foods was not to advertise products but to provide consumers with adequate information. we must take even greater responsibility for children and adolescents. we cannot promote drinks with contradictory messages that are recommended for adults to drink in limited quantities. the health of our youth cannot be sacrificed to economic interests. on these grounds, i voted in favour of the parliament's objection.

in writing. the minimum wage is currently in force in 22 of the 28 member states of the european union. however, it was the introduction of the german hourly wage that upset the mood of the undertakings concerned in almost all the member states. the procedure is still ongoing, but the european commission is expected to reach a conclusion by the end of this year. i welcome the fact that the commission has acted immediately and is examining the german legislation and continuing to consult the german state in the framework of the infringement procedure, but there are still many uncertainties: questions to which the community rules allow an answer that the german state's minimum wage law in its current form is incompatible with community law and questions which create an unresolved conflict of laws situation in the case of the joint application of the national law of two states at the same time. the situation has thus arisen where an employer may comply with one national law but the employee does not know the other. national laws do not overlap, they are equivalent, and conflict-free application is possible only if there is no overlap in the effects of the laws. this cannot be said for the german minimum wage, since the hungarian hauliers concerned for the purposes of the minimum wage rule are basically subject to hungarian law. i hope that the commission will take a decision on this critical issue as soon as possible, as our carriers cannot be kept in a state of uncertainty.

mr. president, since the paris climate summit, energy issues have been treated in this chamber as a sub-category of climate policy. it is perhaps no coincidence that the report also refers to the objectives of climate and energy when it is about the electricity market. and it is perhaps no coincidence that šefčovič, the commissioner responsible for the energy union, is not representing the commission in this case. of course, i think the objectives of the paris meeting must be met. but many are setting ambitious goals without taking security of supply into account. that renewable energy has fluctuating capacity and therefore limited proportions within a system. they don't consider affordability. not all countries are as rich as germany to pay a huge amount of money to adopt renewable energy. and among the low-carbon technologies, they only talk about renewable energy, whereas there's nuclear energy, which is clean energy. and i'll add: in 2014, a group of american scientists, known for their environmental work, said that nuclear energy has a long way to go in terms of climate protection. and another note: for a country, energy security is a matter of survival. this responsibility cannot be taken out of the hands of national governments.

in writing. - my fellow members of parliament! the european union devotes 59% of its total natural gas consumption and 12% of its oil consumption to heating and cooling, while every 1% increase in energy efficiency reduces natural gas imports by 2.6%. the union is therefore paying particular attention to the development of a heating and cooling strategy in order to achieve its climate objectives and reduce its dependence on energy suppliers. heating and cooling our buildings consumes nearly 35% of our total energy consumption, but with serious renovation work, this could be significantly reduced. the stock of inefficient walls without proper insulation and single-ply windows continues to be high. to this end, the energy performance of buildings directive was created, which sets mandatory minimum energy efficiency criteria for new investments. in industry, insulation and efficiency improvements can reduce emissions, as heating to the right temperature is often an integral part of the manufacturing process. however, the objective is to decarbonise the processes as completely as possible. however, for processes that are really high temperature, there is no solution for heating with electricity from renewable sources, so fossil fuels are needed. the union's priority is to make the best possible use of the resulting heat surplus, or rather, the resulting cold surplus. finally, the role of lng import terminals as important sources of district heating is worth highlighting.
my fellow members of parliament! the biggest cancer in all the european union cohesion programmes, in all the financial support programmes, is rampant corruption. we have a lot of news coming in from european union member states. unfortunately, the worst examples come from my country, hungary. where hardly a day has gone by in the last few years without the press uncovering a corrupt deal involving a government politician or a financier connected to him, an oligarch. the real problem is that these corruption cases are not followed by criminal prosecution and ultimately punishment. there are member states - hungary is one of them - where the prosecution is reluctant to take action in corruption cases involving pro-government politicians. it is no coincidence that it is always the member states that are most opposed to the creation of a common european prosecutor's office that are most afraid that their own politicians, their own environment, may be involved in these cases. that's the confession. if a government of a member state does not want to set up a common european union prosecutor's office to investigate this type of corruption, it is essentially saying that it does not want these corruption cases to be investigated. we therefore propose that, if not now, then in the post-2020 cohesion period only those member states that commit to setting up a common european union prosecutor's office should receive eu support. it's not possible to accept the money, but the crimes are not... in writing. the overall objective of european territorial cooperation is to reduce the impact of national borders, to reduce disparities between regions, to remove remaining obstacles to cross-border investment and joint work, to strengthen cohesion and to promote the harmonious economic, social, cultural and territorial development of the union as a whole. as some 38% of europe's population lives in border regions and as the union faces a major economic, financial and social crisis, key policies need to take these facts into account. i believe that european territorial cooperation has proven its effectiveness, but its potential needs to be further developed. it is important that the report highlights the potential of regional policy beyond the single market, the digital agenda, employment, mobility, energy, research, education, culture, health and the environment. i therefore ask the commission and the member states to consider maintaining european territorial cooperation as an important tool and even to give it a stronger role in the post-2020 cohesion policy, while significantly increasing its budget. however, i cannot vote in favour of the report because it contains several paragraphs (in addition to useful ideas) which would allocate cohesion resources to the integration of immigrants.
in writing. the european structural and investment funds are the main drivers of smart, sustainable and inclusive growth in the union. cohesion policy is an investment policy with tangible results, which has undergone highly exemplary reforms in recent times. the resulting results-oriented reform can serve as a model for other spending areas of the eu budget. cohesion policy faces a number of new challenges which need to be addressed while respecting the original and still relevant objectives of the policy and the specific needs of the regions. there is a general shift from infrastructure development towards development supporting the knowledge-based economy, but it should be borne in mind that infrastructure development cannot continue to be pushed into the background, because infrastructure is often lacking even in the more developed member states, development cannot always be solved on a market basis and adequate infrastructure connectivity is also a prerequisite for the functioning of the single internal market. the share of financial instruments has increased significantly over the period 2014-2020 at the expense of grants and this trend is expected to continue. i think it is important to stress that while financial instruments can be useful, they cannot provide a viable solution in all cases, as many developments have a significant social value but no direct financial benefit. therefore, before increasing the share of financial instruments, a thorough analysis of the results of their cohesion policy contribution is required.

in writing. ‒ i was unable to support the report on european territorial cooperation in the plenary vote. the report contains many valuable ideas. it is clear that, although european territorial cooperation has been an objective of cohesion policy since the 2007-13 programming period, it has not received the attention it deserves. however, several paragraphs suggest that cohesion funds, territorial development instruments, should also be used to support the social integration of migrants, to address the challenges posed by the refugee crisis, and to support measures in the area of migration and asylum. this proposal ignores the original objective of cohesion policy, which is to reduce disparities between the levels of development of the different regions and the backwardness of the least favoured regions and to strengthen economic, social and territorial cohesion (article 174 tfeu). this is not the much-vaunted solidarity but an investment policy where net contributors benefit at least as much as the countries receiving aid. i cannot agree that cohesion funds, which are so important for european regions, should be used for migration-related purposes. it's time to recognize that mandatory admissions, resettlement, doesn't work. migrants and refugees should be helped in their country of origin, not brought to the eu member states.

in writing. ‒ interreg, one of the four community initiatives of the european union, was launched in 1990 as a community initiative with a budget of eur 1 billion, with 11 beneficiary member states, exclusively to support crossborder cooperation. its initiatives are areas of cooperation of fundamental importance for the development and cohesion of the european region as a whole. it was later extended to transnational and interregional cooperation. a specific regulation was adopted for the period 2014-2020 for european territorial cooperation actions supported by the erdf. european territorial cooperation now involves all 28 member states and has become one of the two objectives of cohesion policy. the report of the regional development committee reviews the added value of european territorial cooperation, its contribution to the objectives of the europe 2020 strategy and best practices, and makes recommendations for the future. i voted in favour of the draft resolution.

in writing. ‒ as a member of the emis committee of inquiry, i voted in favour of the interim report on the examination of emission measurements in the automotive sector. this is a matter of great importance to the citizens of europe, both in terms of improving air quality and in terms of solving the volkswagen scandal. it is clear that volkswagen has deceived consumers and that our main objective must be to regain the trust of european consumers. the legislation should be enforced by manufacturers through the establishment of an appropriate real driving emission test cycle and an effective market surveillance system by national authorities. in the case of the diesel scandal, it should be emphasised that various economic interests cannot be allowed to override a sound public interest. we must also strongly call on the european commission and the joint research centre (jrc) to provide the committee with any relevant documents that could help the work of the committee. all relevant communications within the jrc and between the jrc and the directorate-general for internal market, the directorate-general for environment, the national authorities of the member states and the type-approval authorities of the european commission could be useful. furthermore, all documents relating to the activities of the various expert groups, as well as all official and informal correspondence between the commission and the european automobile manufacturers' association (acea). such disclosure and evidence gathering is essential to restore consumer confidence.
in writing. ‒ on 17 december last year, the european parliament adopted a decision setting up a committee of inquiry to investigate alleged breaches of eu law and alleged maladministration in relation to emission measurements in the automotive sector, and called on the committee to submit an interim report six months after the start of the work. at the end of the period, the panel shall, on the basis of the oral and written evidence submitted to it and examined by it, establish in its interim report the need for further investigations in all aspects covered by its mandate. it therefore proposes that parliament instruct the committee of inquiry to continue its work and support all measures and initiatives aimed at fulfilling its mandate, and ask the conference of presidents and the bureau to support all measures necessary to enable the committee of inquiry to fulfil its mandate. it also asks parliament to express the expectation that the governments, parliaments and delegated authorities of the member states will support the committee of inquiry in the performance of its tasks, in full respect of the principle of good faith cooperation enshrined in eu law. i supported the adoption of the interim report.

in writing. ‒ in its order of 26 november 2014, the central district court of pest requested the suspension of the immunity of istván ujhelyi, accused of committing the offence of defamation. the statements on which the indictment is based were made by istván ujhelyi on 25 april 2014, before he was elected to the european parliament in the 2014 european parliament elections. the committee on legal affairs therefore considers in its report that mr ujhelyi was not acting as a member of the european parliament when he made the statements in question and therefore proposes that the european parliament suspend mr ujhelyi's immunity. according to istván ujhelyi, on the other hand, under the xxxvi hungarian law on the national assembly of 2012, a candidate running in the elections to the european parliament in hungary is also entitled to the right of immunity, and therefore the european parliament should maintain its right of immunity. for my part, i consider the position of mr ujhelyi to be well founded and have therefore voted against the motion for a resolution tabled by the committee on legal affairs.
in writing. ‒ former member of the european parliament rosario crocetta, accused of making defamatory statements, a criminal offence under article 595 of the italian penal code, has requested that his immunity be maintained under articles 8 and 9 of protocol no 7 on the privileges and immunities of the european union in a criminal case pending before the court of justice of palermo. in its report, the committee on legal affairs states that the statements in question were made by ms rosario crocetta when she was a member of the european parliament and that it is apparent from the documents submitted to the committee and from the hearing in which she was heard that mr crocetta's statements have a direct and manifest connection with the performance of his duties as a member of parliament. the committee therefore considers that rosario crocetta was acting as a member of the european parliament in the case in question and therefore recommends that the parliament should maintain the immunity and privileges of rosario crocetta. i supported the recommendation of the legal affairs committee.

in writing. ‒ in its request of 28 march 2016, the greek prosecutor general requested the suspension of the parliamentary immunity of mr sotirios zarianopulos, member of the european parliament, in the context of the investigative procedure concerning the alleged commission of an unlawful act. the greek authorities intend to prosecute sotirios zarianopoulos for failing to comply with his legal obligations as a member of the municipality of thessaloniki in 2011. according to the report of the committee on legal affairs, it is clear that the proposed procedure is not linked to the mandate of mr zarianopoulos as a member of the european parliament but to his previous membership of the municipality of thessaloniki, and there is no reason to assume that the intention behind the proposed procedure is to impede the political activity of the member, even more so since the procedure covers all persons who were members of the municipality of thessaloniki during the period in question. the committee therefore recommends that the european parliament suspend the member's immunity. i voted accordingly.
in writing. ‒ in the request forwarded by the greek prosecutor general on 28 march 2016 and announced in plenary on 27 april 2016, the prosecutor general requests the suspension of the immunity of mr sotirios zarianopoulos in the context of the investigation procedure to be initiated by the prosecutor of thessaloniki in the case of the unlawful act. i followed the group's position in my decision.
in writing. ‒ the customs union of the european union was enlarged by the accession of the republic of croatia. consequently, under the rules of the world trade organisation (wto), the european union is obliged to open negotiations with wto members in respect of which croatia has so far had a so-called preferential tariff list. this becomes necessary if the tariff level resulting from accession to the union tariff system is increased for this reason beyond the level agreed by the acceding country in the wto. on 15 july 2013, the council authorised the commission to open negotiations on the basis of article xxiv:6 of the gatt. following those negotiations, the commission proposed to the council that the agreement be signed on behalf of the union. in the light of the above, i voted in favour of parliament's agreement to the draft council decision.

in writing. - i voted for the recommendation. the customs union of the european union was enlarged by the accession of the republic of croatia. consequently, under the rules of the world trade organisation (wto), the european union was obliged to enter into negotiations with wto members with negotiating rights in respect of the concessional lists of croatia in order to establish a possible compensatory adjustment. this adjustment had to be made as the rate of increase of the customs tariff level resulting from the transition to the eu external tariff system exceeds the level undertaken by croatia in the wto. having proposed to the council that the agreement in the form of an exchange of letters with china be signed on behalf of the union, the commission is required to give its consent to the parliament. the people's republic of china has the right to re-establish its previous trade rights, which have been somewhat eroded as a result of the enlargement of the eu customs union following the accession of croatia to the union. the commission was right to propose (1) an increase of the tariff quotas and (2) a reduction of the current fixed duty rates to offset the losses as a means of compensation for the chinese products concerned.
in writing. ‒ the customs union of the european union was enlarged by the accession of the republic of croatia. consequently, under the rules of the world trade organisation (wto), the european union is obliged to open negotiations with wto members in respect of which croatia has hitherto had a so-called preferential tariff list. this becomes necessary if the tariff level resulting from accession to the union tariff system is increased for this reason beyond the level agreed by the acceding country in the wto. the commission was given the necessary backstop to open negotiations on 15 july 2013 by the council, on the basis of article xxiv:6 of the gatt. following those negotiations, the commission proposed to the council that the agreement be signed on behalf of the union. in the light of the above, i voted in favour of parliament's agreement to the draft council decision.

in writing. ‒ the customs union of the european union was enlarged by the accession of the republic of croatia. croatia has thus adopted the eu external tariff system, which has led to some erosion of the former trade rights of the people's republic of china, as stated in the report of the international trade commission. as regards the restoration of china's former trade rights, the commission has opened negotiations on the basis of the council's mandate of 15 july 2013 and proposes that the council sign the agreement in the form of an exchange of letters with the people's republic of china on behalf of the union. the council shall also obtain the consent of the european parliament. in its report, the committee on international trade recommends that parliament give its consent to the conclusion of the agreement. i voted accordingly.

in writing. ‒ the customs union of the european union was enlarged by the accession of the republic of croatia. consequently, under the rules of the world trade organisation (wto), the european union was obliged to enter into negotiations with wto members with negotiating rights in respect of the concessional lists of croatia in order to establish a possible compensatory adjustment. such adjustment shall be made where the rate of increase in the level of customs duties resulting from the transition to the eu's external tariff system exceeds the level of the acceding country's wto commitments. i voted for the report.
in writing. ‒ the customs union of the european union was enlarged by the accession of the republic of croatia. consequently, under the rules of the world trade organisation (wto), the european union is obliged to open negotiations with wto members in respect of which croatia has hitherto had a so-called preferential tariff list. this becomes necessary if the tariff level resulting from accession to the union tariff system is increased for this reason beyond the level agreed by the acceding country in the wto. following the negotiations, the draft agreement was initialled in nairobi on 18 december 2015 and the council subsequently adopted its decision on the signing of the draft agreement on 11 april 2016. i voted in favour of the report, as the european parliament's agreement to this council decision is necessary for the ratification of the additional protocol.

in writing. ‒ i have given my consent to the council position at first reading with a view to adopting a regulation amending regulation (ec) no 471/2009 of the european parliament and of the council on statistics relating to the external trade of the eu with third countries. the amendments introduced by the treaty of lisbon called on the commission to adapt the rules for the adoption of decisions relating to trade policy to the new system of delegated and implementing acts. most legislation in the field of the common commercial policy has been brought into line with the new constitutional system. as the commission committed itself to implementing the second wave of comitology adjustments by the end of the 7th parliamentary term, it was proposed to amend the regulation on community statistics, the only legislative act in the field of the common commercial policy to include a regulatory procedure with scrutiny.
in writing. ‒ on 12 march 2014, parliament adopted its position at first reading on the draft regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending regulation (ec) no 471/2009 on community statistics relating to external trade with third countries, as regards the delegation of power and the implementing powers to be conferred on the commission with a view to adopting certain measures. the tripartite negotiations that followed were suspended after several rounds pending the adoption of a new interinstitutional agreement on improving the quality of legislation. following the adoption of that agreement in december 2015, the negotiating groups of parliament and the council reached an agreement on the regulation in question. on 16 june 2016, the council adopted its position at first reading, confirming the agreement. in its report, the committee on international trade recommends that parliament endorse the position adopted by the council at first reading and thereby give effect to this regulation in accordance with the council's position. i voted accordingly.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution by which parliament endorses the outcome of more than two years of legislative preparatory work in the council, in first reading, and through several fora and rounds of interinstitutional consultation. the draft law reflects the institutional changes brought about by the treaty of lisbon and the amendments to the comitology rules necessitated by the requirement of 'better law-making', on the basis of the union's competence in international trade and statistical reporting.
in writing. ‒ in the light of the amendments introduced by the treaty of lisbon and the subsequent adoption of regulation (eu) no 182/2011 (on implementing acts), the commission was invited to adapt the rules for the adoption of decisions on trade policy to the new system of delegated and implementing acts. i voted for the report.
in writing. ‒ the european commission has been collecting data on natural gas and electricity prices since the 1970s. in 1990, the council adopted a directive laying down a procedure to improve the transparency of gas and electricity prices paid by industrial end-users; this does not, however, apply to household consumers. the increasing complexity of the internal energy market and the lack of legally binding rules on reporting have made it increasingly difficult to obtain reliable and up-to-date data on natural gas and electricity prices, in particular for the retail sector. the report aims to maintain the quality of the electricity and natural gas price surveys for the household sector, to provide a broad picture of the market and to maintain the high quality of flood data. the proposal would not impose any additional burden on reporting authorities and would continue to be carried out by the competent national authorities. the purpose of this report is to clarify the objectives and to make certain provisions clear to reporting authorities and companies.

in writing. ‒ i abstained from the vote because i considered the report to be a report of principle. european statistics on natural gas and electricity prices should be established or made compulsory, as they already exist for industrial prices. nevertheless, because of the rapporteur's personality alone (his group is against eu and integration), i believe that the subject should be examined in more depth. i believe that in this and many other areas, we can only achieve results at eu level through stronger integration. whether it's comparability of energy prices or something else. i agree that comprehensive, comparable and timely data can be a serious check for member states.
in writing. ‒ the major changes of recent years, such as new technologies, fluctuating raw material prices or the rapid expansion of renewable electricity generation, have fundamentally changed the european energy market. the report aims to achieve three objectives. firstly, a union-wide electricity market should be established, providing clear price signals for new investments. secondly, we need to create a european infrastructure for secure energy supply. third, regional cooperation in energy policy should be strengthened, in particular with regard to the development of new energy generation equipment, interconnectors and support schemes, and the integration of renewable energy sources into the european internal market. achieving these objectives is in europe's common interest, as the integration of electricity markets will improve the secure, cost-effective and environmentally sound supply of energy. it is important that the overall structure of the member states' national energy structure and energy supply is respected throughout the development of the new strategy. the efficient use of energy storage, network development, the construction of appropriate interconnectors and the widest possible use of renewable sources are essential to the completion of the internal market. better integration and coordination of electricity markets holds many opportunities to achieve common european objectives for a safer, more cost-effective and sustainable energy supply.

in writing. ‒ on 15 july 2015, the european commission published its consultative communication on european electricity systems, launching a public consultation on what the newly created electricity market should look like in order to achieve the energy policy objectives of security of supply, environmental sustainability and value for money. better integration and coordination of electricity markets holds many opportunities to achieve common european objectives of a secure, cost-effective and environmentally sustainable energy supply, but the design of energy markets, in particular electricity markets, is still strongly nationalised. in its report, the committee on industry, research and energy proposes the adoption of a resolution which is critical of but fundamentally supportive of the commission's proposed package of measures in this area. i supported the draft resolution.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report because i believe that our energy supply objectives as set out in the eu treaty can only be achieved through closer integration of the energy market. it is important to ensure a secure, affordable, efficient and sustainable energy supply for the whole of the eu. i agree with the report that to achieve climate and energy objectives, the energy system of the future must be more flexible, so we need to invest in all four flexibility solutions: flexible generation, grid development, demand response and storage. i think it is important in the redesign of the energy market not only to aim at full market integration but also to promote renewable, safe energy production and not fossil or nuclear energy production in any way. i have to note here the unfortunate fact that hungary has not issued a permit for wind power plants for 10 years, citing the lack of storage capacity and technologies, and imposes an extra tax on solar systems. so i think it's doubtful that we'll reach the 13% renewable target by 2020. i believe that we need to encourage the development of renewable (local) energy sources in the member states and that we need to devote more resources to r&d&i in energy storage.
in writing. ‒ on 15 july 2015, the european commission published a number of documents on the european internal market, including the consultative communication on european electricity systems discussed in this report. i have supported the present final document in accordance with the position of the group.
in writing. ‒ the european union devotes 59% of its total natural gas consumption and 12% of its oil consumption to heating and cooling, while every 1% increase in energy efficiency reduces natural gas imports by 2.6%. the union is therefore focusing on the development of a heating and cooling strategy to achieve its climate targets and reduce its dependence on energy suppliers. heating and cooling our buildings consumes nearly 35% of our total energy consumption, but with serious renovation work, this could be significantly reduced. the stock of inadequately effective walls without proper insulation and single-ply windows continues to be high. to this end, the energy performance of buildings directive was created, which sets mandatory minimum energy efficiency criteria for new investments. in industry, insulation and efficiency improvements can achieve lower emission reductions, as heating to the appropriate temperature is often an integral part of the manufacturing process. however, the objective is to decarbonise the processes as completely as possible. however, for processes that are very hot, heating with electricity from renewable sources is not an option, so fossil fuels are needed. the union's priority is to make the best possible use of the resulting heat surplus, or rather, the resulting cold surplus. finally, it is important to highlight the role of lng import terminals as district heating sources.

in writing. ‒ on 16 february this year, the commission published its communication 'a european union heat strategy'. the draft resolution of the committee on industry, research and energy on the communication focuses on three main issues. notes that in the countries that joined the union after 2004, thermal renovation of buildings is the easiest way to ensure that energy is used more efficiently and that carbon emissions are significantly reduced; it also urges financial measures to this end. it points out that cooling is the biggest problem in the mediterranean countries of europe due to the gradual warming, and that the solution may be to use suitable architectural solutions, insulation and reversible heat pumps that remove heat in hot weather and absorb heat in cold weather. it eventually reaches the sun, which is a significant source of heat, but which is not properly exploited by cells that heat water or generate electricity. i voted in favour of the draft resolution.
in writing. ‒ the importance of heating and cooling and the priorities for action have diverged across member states. overall, however, about 50% of the eu's final energy demand is used for heating and cooling. i therefore agree that in the countries that joined the union after 2004, the greatest potential for efficiency improvement lies in the thermal renovation of buildings. it's the easiest way to ensure that we're using energy more efficiently and significantly reducing carbon emissions. i think it's an important ratio that 1 percent energy savings will reduce natural gas imports by 2.6 percent, and i hope that, along with energy efficiency, the fossil ratio will also decrease dramatically. i also agree that the amount of money for the thermal renovation of entire housing estates, especially for buildings built with panel technology, should be significantly increased. in hungary, for example, where the tax burden is so high, the inhabitants have concrete problems with their livelihood, but modernization is a complex issue for them. i think the reversible heat pump system is good, particularly energy efficient, and has great potential for heating and cooling. i share the view that the heating and cooling sector should reflect the 2015 paris agreement on climate change (cop21) and can only hope that the heating and cooling sector will be based on 100% renewable energy sources by 2050 at the latest, in line with the union's energy and climate objectives. in view of all this, i voted in favour of the report.
in writing. ‒ the importance of heating and cooling varies from one member state to another. this means that the priority of the steps to be taken in these countries has diverged. it should also be emphasised that in the countries that joined the union after 2004, the greatest potential for efficiency improvements lies in the thermal renovation of buildings. i voted for it.
in writing. ‒ the report submitted by the regional development committee is on the implementation of the thematic objective of improving the competitiveness of small and medium-sized enterprises. it calls on the member states to help smes develop, to simplify access to credit and to ensure greater coordination of all eu investment policies targeting smes. in addition, the report calls on the commission, together with the member states and the managing authorities, to encourage the creation of a network of universities, research centres, social and economic actors and public institutions to support the development of entrepreneurial skills. as a quarter of smes are currently engaged in external trade, the report recommends progress and appropriate support (through more efficient use of the structural and investment funds) in this area as well. increase the share of cohesion policy resources for smes to increase their international competitiveness. increased support for smes is an objective i agree with and voted for. at the same time, i would note that smes can only develop if aggregate demand in the economy increases.
in writing. ‒ it is right that the commission pays greater attention to good governance and quality public services. a transparent, consistent and innovative public procurement system is important for smes, and it is therefore important to remove as much as possible the obstacles to the participation of smes in tenders, to eliminate excessive bureaucratic burdens, to avoid imposing additional conditions at national level, while implementing as soon as possible the provisions of the existing legislative framework on dispute settlement in public procurement. at the same time, i do not believe that smes can help to integrate immigrants if they are given the right incentives.
in writing. ‒ i abstained in the vote on the report on improving the competitiveness of smes. the report contains many useful ideas. smes can undoubtedly play an important role in europe's recovery, as some 23 million small and medium-sized enterprises, representing 99% of all businesses, make a significant contribution to economic growth, social cohesion, innovation and job creation. however, one paragraph of the report refers to the integration of refugees and migrants, for which, as the report explains, appropriate support and incentives to support the activities of small businesses can provide an innovative opportunity. the original contractual purpose of cohesion policy was to reduce disparities between the levels of development of the various regions and the backwardness of the least-favoured regions (article 174 tfeu). i cannot agree that cohesion funds, which are so important for european regions, should be used for migration-related purposes. it's time to recognize that mandatory admissions, resettlement, doesn't work. migrants and refugees should be helped in their country of origin, not brought to the eu member states.

in writing. ‒ at the september plenary session of the european parliament, i voted in favour of the report on the european union strategy for the alpine region, which is the fourth macro-regional strategy of the union. the eu strategy for the alpine region covers 48 regions in seven countries, five of which are eu member states, and two others in switzerland and lichtenstein. macro-regional strategies enable these countries to create strategic investments for the benefit of the whole region, taking into account the three-generation principle. the strategy is based on three pillars of development. the first pillar aims to increase the competitiveness and cohesion of the alpine region, including the promotion of sustainable and competitive tourism. the second pillar aims at improving accessibility, providing adequate transport, energy and ict infrastructure. the third pillar is about sustainability, environmental protection, biodiversity and the protection of ecosystems. the alpine macro-region has considerable potential which can be further exploited through cooperation between countries and regions.

in writing. ‒ i have adopted the report on the eu strategy for the alpine region. the alpine region has significant economic potential in the eu, as the macro-strategy affects some 80 million people in 48 regions in seven countries, five of which are eu member states (austria, france, germany, italy and slovenia). it is particularly welcome that an important part of the strategy is the development of the labour market through the improvement of the skills of the workforce and the creation of new jobs in the green economy. funding from existing union sources such as cosme, horizon 2020 or erasmus+ is needed to use new technologies in key areas of the economy, based on innovation and smart specialisation strategies. these resources can greatly help to create new jobs in the region. the report also focuses on the promotion of economic activities in the region by smes active in agriculture, tourism and trade. these businesses are the main source of employment in the alps, but further diversification is needed. similarly, investment in digital infrastructure should be treated as a priority and fast and efficient broadband access should be provided to the population of areas far from large urban centres. this enables digital and online services such as e-commerce, digital market channels, teleworking and other opportunities.

in writing. ‒ at the september plenary session of the european parliament, i voted in favour of the report on the european union strategy for the alpine region, which is the fourth macro-regional strategy of the union. the eu strategy for the alpine region covers 48 regions in seven countries, five of which are eu member states, and two others in switzerland and lichtenstein. macro-regional strategies enable these countries to create strategic investments for the benefit of the whole region, taking into account the three-generation principle. the strategy is based on three pillars of development. the first pillar aims to increase the competitiveness and cohesion of the alpine region, including the promotion of sustainable and competitive tourism. the second pillar aims at improving accessibility, providing adequate transport, energy and ict infrastructure. the third pillar is about sustainability, environmental protection, biodiversity and the protection of ecosystems. the alpine macro-region has considerable potential which can be further exploited through cooperation between countries and regions.
in writing. ‒ the commission presented the action plan for the eu strategy for the alpine region in july 2015. it is the fourth eu macro-regional strategy, following the eu strategies for the baltic sea region, the danube region and the adriatic and ionian region. the draft resolution of the committee on regional development analyses this strategy. it underlines that the eu strategy for the alpine region provides the opportunity for the countries of the region to invest in projects with an impact on the whole of the union and not just at a regional level. the strategy will allow the development of new forms of multilevel governance, based in the regions but with the participation of the eu institutions. the draft strategy sets out the main proposals and priorities under three pillars: i. improving the competitiveness, prosperity and cohesion of the alpine region. ii. providing accessibility and transport connections for the people living in the alpine region. iii. ensuring sustainability in the alps: protecting the alpine heritage and promoting the sustainable use of natural and cultural resources. i voted for the bill.
in writing. ‒ in december 2013, the european council invited the commission to present an eu strategy for the alpine region. the commission has responded to the call, which is the fourth eu macro-regional strategy, building on the experience gained in the eu strategies for the baltic sea region, the danube region and the adriatic and ionian region. the eu strategy for the alpine region covers 80 million people and 48 regions in 7 different countries, five of which are eu member states (italy, france, slovenia, austria, germany) and the other two are switzerland and liechtenstein. there is already active cooperation between smaller regions, but the eu strategy for the alpine region offers the opportunity to create strategic investments for the benefit of the whole region. that is why i voted in favour of the report. the region can solve its transport and logistics problems along the pillars of the common strategy, but only if they coordinate their ideas from the local level. they can also strengthen their competitiveness and cohesion, and last but not least, ensure sustainability. i hope that the danube region will be able to exploit its development potential in the same way as the alpine region, which is expected to be successful.
in writing. ‒ following initial steps taken by the alpine region at the end of 2011, the european council in december 2013 invited the commission to present an eu strategy for the alpine region. the commission responded to the call and submitted an action plan for the strategy in july 2015. this is the fourth eu macro-regional strategy, building on the experience gained in the eu strategies for the baltic sea region, the danube region and the adriatic and ionian region. i supported him with my vote.
in writing. ‒ the document is a report on the eu emergency fund for africa initiative, which seeks to take initiatives focusing on migration and its root causes. an important detail of the text is that ngos should be given the maximum opportunity to participate in the development of migration reception, return and other strategies, in decisions on the use of the financial framework of the fund. the rationale for this is highly questionable after the exposure of the activities of the soros foundations in this area. the report states that regional funds cannot be used for border protection (even for countries with schengen borders) and cannot be used to improve security. and in effect, he's saying that the safety of the local population, the sense of safety, the public safety in general, is not important if this is an anti-immigrant policy. i voted against the report because of all that.
in writing. ‒ i consider the adoption of the report to be very important and i voted in favour of it, as the emergency fund can contribute to addressing the root causes of destabilisation, forced displacement and illegal migration by promoting resilience, economic opportunities, equal opportunities, security and development. the document draws attention to the importance of addressing the causes of migration and supporting those in need, as mass migration poses a new humanitarian and security challenge to europe. a transparent strategy that works with ngos and leaders with significant local knowledge to deliver more effective assistance will hopefully be able to provide protection for those in need in their own country. the report also draws attention to the fact that eu migration policies should focus primarily on addressing the root causes of migration, involving ngos and civil society.

in writing. ‒ i voted on a report that is important for development and humanitarian aid. the emergency fund was established to promote stability in africa and to contribute to the proper management of mass immigration. it should be borne in mind that eu migration policies should focus primarily on the root causes of migration and have as a main objective to investigate and address the root causes of poverty in countries of origin. union migration policies should aim to create peace and stability and to strengthen economic development, with a view to ensuring a healthy life for all at all ages, achieving gender equality and the emancipation of all women and girls, and working more closely with third countries to promote the return and reintegration of migrants, including highly skilled migrants, to their countries of origin, and to facilitate voluntary return and readmission in a way that enhances their opportunities. africa continues to have a very high population growth rate and a slowly declining fertility rate, which will lead to a sharp increase in the young working-age population in the near future. we need to address this through aid, so that it brings social and economic benefits to the continent, and not leads to mass migration.

in writing. ‒ the draft resolution of the committee on development was inspired by the current developments in the migration crisis. the emergency fund for stability in africa and addressing the root causes of irregular migration was established at the valencian summit on migration on 11-12 november 2015 and aims to address the root causes of destabilisation, forced displacement and illegal migration by promoting resilience, economic opportunity, equal opportunities, security and development. it focuses on five priority areas: 1) unlocking the benefits of migration; 2) legal migration and mobility; 3) protection and asylum; 4) preventing and combating illegal migration; 5) return, readmission and reintegration. the draft resolution takes account of financial possibilities, the role of civil society, non-governmental organisations, local authorities and international organisations, extends funding to the least developed countries, calls for transparency and clarity to achieve the objectives more effectively, and stresses the importance of coherence in eu policies and commitment to human rights. i voted for the bill.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the proposal, mainly in the hope that it would induce changes that would allow the fund to better fulfil its fundamental objective of addressing the causes of mass migration at the root. i also hope that this will lead the member states to recognise their responsibility and to contribute the €1.8 billion voted and committed to the operation of the fund (as opposed to the minimum member state transfer of just €81 million that has been made so far). however, i agree with most of my colleagues in the ep that it is wrong to use the fund's resources for border control, in complete contradiction to its original purpose. i also regret that the fund is not part of the eu budget and therefore not subject to parliament's control; i am convinced that correcting this situation by means of this decision would also remedy the above problems of payment and distribution of funds.
in writing. ‒ the creation of the eu emergency fund for africa, signed by the president of the commission and 25 eu member states, as well as norway and switzerland, was initiated by the european and african partners at the valletta summit on migration on 12 november 2015 with the main objective of promoting stability in the region and contributing to better management of migration. the specific purpose of the emergency fund is to address the root causes of destabilisation, forced displacement and illegal migration by promoting resilience, economic opportunities, equal opportunities, security and development. i supported this document.
in writing. ‒ in recent decades, the reconciliation of work, private and family life has been recognised as a fundamental right, but further progress is needed to ensure that everyone can achieve the right balance between work and private life. in december 2015, the commission published a roadmap entitled 'a new start: tackling the challenges of work-life balance for working parents' with the aim of increasing women's participation in the labour market by modernising the existing eu legal and political framework and adapting the current labour market. the joint draft report by the committee on employment and social affairs and the committee on women's rights and equal opportunities, while welcoming the commission's initiative, takes the view that improving the work-life balance requires action at eu level. accordingly, it urges the revision of directive 92/85/eec on maternity leave for pregnant workers, the review of the implementation of directive 2010/18/eu on parental leave and the adoption of a directive on paternity leave and a directive on carers' leave. the former would be to ensure that men take their share of caregiving duties, and the latter to enable workers to care for their relatives. i voted for the bill.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report, which shows that the reconciliation of professional, private and family life has been recognised as a fundamental right over the past decades. i think it is very important to emphasise that there are many circumstances which can make it difficult for women to work - for example, if there are children, elderly people or other dependants in the family - since the responsibility for the family and the household is most often borne by women. as a result, they are often forced to work part-time or in precarious forms of employment, and this creates disparities in pay and pensions. i agree that there are several main reasons why the framework for achieving work-life balance needs to be modernised at eu level and i therefore welcome the commission's initiative. i think that the hungarian government should also introduce more targeted measures to ensure that the work-life balance is maintained in practice.
in writing. ‒ in recent decades, the reconciliation of professional, private and family life has been recognised as a fundamental right. while initiatives to this end have been taken at both european and national level, this is still an area where further progress is needed to ensure that everyone can achieve the right work-life balance. this not only contributes to the well-being of the individual but also benefits society as a whole, in part because people who have a good work-life balance are more productive workers. i supported the group's position in the final vote.

in writing. you are only as big as you feel is the saying. let's be clear, europe is the world's largest economy and the world's strongest economic and political power. let's act like it. the eu economy is growing faster than the united states this year. in almost all member states, public debt and budget deficits have been brought under control. president juncker has announced the launch of a new investment programme, which is expected to create more than 5 million jobs in europe. europe is strong, and to talk about its decline is political hysteria. true, there are challenges from the russian security threat to the british withdrawal. as the commission has been urging, we need a common eu army. we can't rely on the united states alone for our security. there can be no scenario in which europeans do not feel safe in their own country. we must also embark on a brutal economic development that will enable every european to live well, better than his parents. third, a quick solution to the refugee crisis cannot wait. the eu visa, border guard and common asylum policy are the solution, not individual member state solutions. but let us remember that europe is not small and powerless. europe still accounts for more than a fifth of the world's economic output, despite having only 7% of the world's population. let us act accordingly when we talk about the state of the eu.

in writing. ‒ the union is switzerland's most important economic partner, given its geographical and cultural proximity, and in particular its political and economic importance. accordingly, the union has established closer relations with switzerland through a number of agreements than with any other country outside the european economic area (eea). switzerland is the union's fourth largest trading partner after the united states, china and russia, and the union is switzerland's most important trading partner. following the rejection of switzerland's accession to the eea agreement in 1992 and the mutual recognition of the crucial role of cooperation, a series of bilateral agreements (e.g. the so-called 'bilateral i. package') were concluded. these covered, inter alia, the free movement of persons, land and air transport, agriculture, research and technical barriers to trade and public procurement and entered into force on 1 june 2002. as switzerland has access to and benefits from the internal market and its enlargement, as do the member states of the union, it benefits politically, economically and culturally from a wider internal market in which free movement, including that of hungarian nationals, is a key element and the restriction of which by switzerland is unacceptable. i therefore voted in favour of the recommendation, which is also relevant to brexit, in line with the rapporteur's opinion.

in writing. ‒ the agreement on the free movement of persons was signed in 2000 by switzerland and the then 15 eu member states. since the enlargement of the union on 1 may 2004 does not automatically extend to the new member states, the agreement has been amended by a protocol and extended to the 10 new member states. in accordance with the accession of bulgaria and romania to the union on 1 january 2007, the agreement was amended again with the entry into force of protocol ii in 2009. protocol iii was established with the accession of croatia to the union in 2013. however, this was initially blocked by switzerland following the referendum against mass immigration on 9 february 2014, to which the union responded. on 4 march 2016, switzerland and the union finally signed protocol iii extending the agreement on the free movement of persons to croatia. the council adopted a draft decision on the conclusion of the protocol, subject to the agreement of the european parliament. in its report, the committee on employment and social affairs recommends that parliament give its consent to the conclusion of the protocol. i voted accordingly.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the european parliament giving its consent to the signing of protocol 3 to the agreement on the free movement of persons, supplementing the agreement concluded in 2000 on the basis of the second bilateral convention between the eu and its member states and the swiss confederation. i took into account the fact that the content and scope of most of the numerous agreements in existence between the two parties are automatically adapted to the enlargement of the eu, whereas the agreement on the free movement of persons and employment is not, and therefore a new additional protocol is needed following the accession of croatia. switzerland is now practically part of the single internal market and the eu, croatia and switzerland have an important interest in its continued smooth functioning, including in the movement and employment of their citizens. in this respect, the seven-year transitional period laid down in the draft, in order to ensure gradualness, is in line with previous similar provisions. however, as regards the developments to be expected in the near future, as a member of the relevant ep delegation, i must keep in mind that the unfortunate outcome of the 2014 swiss anti-immigration referendum is contrary to the agreement with the eu and that, in the absence of an agreement that provides a mutually appropriate legal solution, the entire legal basis of our system of relations with switzerland may be lost.

in writing. ‒ the tripartite social summit for growth and employment is tasked in accordance with the treaty and with due regard for the competences of the eu institutions and bodies to ensure continuous coordination between the council, the commission and the social partners. at european level, it provides an opportunity for the social partners to contribute to the implementation of the union's strategy for growth and jobs through their social dialogue. to this end, the summit draws on the work of the council, the commission and the social partners and on the negotiations between them in the various conciliation fora on economic, social and employment issues. following the institutional change brought about by the treaty of lisbon to establish the presidency of the european council, the 2003 decision establishing the tripartite social summit for growth and employment should be reviewed. in order to maintain the logic of the treaty and the institutional background of the trilateral social summit for growth and employment, the roles and responsibilities conferred on the rotating presidency of the council by the 2003 council decision should be transferred to the newly established presidency of the european council. i supported the proposal because it represents a reform of the eu's platform for social dialogue, in a form adapted to the lisbon treaty. the forum can provide an opportunity for peripheral countries to finally act against the pay gap between the centre and the periphery and other forms of employment colonization.
in writing. ‒ in exercising its right to assent under the special legislative procedure, the european parliament adopted a position on the draft council decision on the tripartite social summit for growth and employment and repealing decision 2003/174/ec. the change concerned mainly technical and procedural issues. the basis for this is the tripartite social summit on growth and employment, established by council decision 2003/174/ec of 6 march 2003, which formalized the practice of informal high-level meetings organised since 1997 under the european employment strategy and then the lisbon strategy. in 2003, the commission presented a proposal for a decision to institutionalize the practice of high-level consultations between the eu institutions and the social partners in the eu. however, following the institutional change brought about by the treaty of lisbon to establish the presidency of the european council, the 2003 decision establishing the tripartite social summit for growth and employment had to be reviewed. (the legal basis for the adoption of the council decision was provided for in article 352 tfeu.)

in writing. ‒ the tripartite social summit on growth and employment was established by council decision 2003/174/ec of 6 march 2003. on a proposal from the commission, the council adopted a draft decision repealing that decision and introducing new rules for the trilateral social summit on growth and employment. the council must obtain parliament's consent before adopting the draft. in its report, the committee on employment and social affairs recommends that parliament give its consent to the draft council decision. i voted accordingly.
in writing. ‒ the tripartite social summit on growth and employment was established by council decision 2003/174/ec of 6 march 2003. the aim is to institutionalise the practice of high-level consultations between the eu institutions and the social partners in the eu. the summit was largely focused on promoting the exchange of views at the highest level between the commission, the eu presidency and the eu social partners on the employment and social aspects of the lisbon strategy (up to 2010 and beyond) and the europe 2020 strategy. the treaty of lisbon has introduced significant institutional changes and a review of this decision is therefore warranted. the review has been ongoing since 2013, in this case in the form of an approval given by the european parliament to the european council. the changes will make the summit more efficient and will now also allow the chair of the employment and social affairs committee to participate as a permanent guest. this is how we strengthen representative democracy, which is why i voted in favour of the recommendation.
in writing. ‒ the tripartite social summit for growth and employment was established by council decision 2003/174/ec of 6 march 2003, which formalized the practice of informal high-level meetings organised since 1997 under the european employment strategy and then the lisbon strategy. i supported the current proposal.
in writing. ‒ the objective of the review of directive 2006/87/ec is to harmonise technical standards for inland waterway transport, taking into account the specifications of the european committee for the standardisation of inland waterways (cesni). cesni was established to promote the harmonisation of standards for the european inland waterway sector. in this light, inland navigation would be characterised by an appropriate level of safety and efficiency, taking into account scientific and technical developments in the sector. the move would therefore provide a higher degree of legal certainty and allow for timely adaptations to technical progress, and would contribute to the maintenance of high safety standards throughout the union without hampering innovation and safety. taking into account the importance of the safety and efficiency of inland navigation and the need for professional and technical development as essential elements of competitiveness and modern inland navigation, i agree with the revision efforts and therefore, as a member of the fidesz people's party delegation, i support the report with my vote.

in writing. ‒ i supported the report by my colleague, mr belet, on the technical requirements for inland waterway vessels. the council position amends directive 2009/100/ec and repeals directive 2006/87/ec. the parliament and the council agreed on the overall objective of the directive, which would be to create a harmonised and coherent framework with the aim of guaranteeing the same level of safety for inland waterway vessels. both institutions supported the rationalisation of the use of resources to develop technical standards and adapt them to scientific and technical progress. during the negotiations at first reading, parliament's priorities included the uniform application of technical requirements and the ensuring of a high level of safety and efficiency in inland navigation.
