in writing. ‒ the commission has proposed to the parliament and the council the adoption of a directive laying down technical requirements for inland waterway vessels, amending directive 2009/100/ec and repealing directive 2006/87/ec. parliament adopted its position on the proposal at first reading. the parliament and the council agreed on the overall objective of the directive, but disagreed on the adaptation of the annexes to technical standards. the negotiating team of parliament and the council reached an agreement on the matter on 17 march 2016. the council adopted its position at first reading in accordance with that agreement. the committee on transport and tourism recommends that parliament should agree to this position and give the draft directive legal force. i voted accordingly.
in writing. ‒ i see the uniform application of technical requirements for inland waterway vessels in the european union as a good example of closer integration. that is why i voted in favour of this recommendation at second reading. the european parliament supported the recommendation at first reading, with the aim of ensuring a high level of safety and efficiency in inland navigation and the provision that the directive would be reviewed every three years. the agreement between the ep and the council clarifies legal clarity (e.g. by setting clear geographical boundaries), reduces administrative burdens and ensures the european parliament's institutional prerogatives, in particular in updating technical standards. i believe that these uniform requirements will make a significant contribution to efficient, dynamic and safe inland waterway transport and will facilitate the application of new and innovative technologies.
in writing. ‒ on its first reading, parliament supported the uniform application of technical requirements for inland waterway vessels in the european union, with a view to ensuring a high level of safety and efficiency in inland navigation. it also welcomed the rapid adaptation of standards to scientific and technical progress. parliament also requested a periodic review of the directive every three years to assess cooperation with the relevant international organisations. i supported him with my vote.
in writing. ‒ economic partnership agreements (epas) are the system of trade and development agreements between african, caribbean and pacific states and the eu. its purpose is to support regional and global integration and trade among acp countries. gmp is another important step towards deepening regional integration, provided that the effectiveness of control is adequate and the necessary follow-up measures are in place. in addition, it is essential to involve civil society as a partner in economic processes, which can be facilitated by the appropriate allocation of available resources. monitoring of the contribution to sustainable fair trade will be particularly important in the context of gmp. in this context, i voted in favour of the european parliament giving its consent to the draft council decision on the conclusion, on behalf of the european union, of the economic partnership agreement between the european union and its member states, of the one part, and the countries associated with the economic partnership agreement of the southern african development community, of the other part (sadc gpm countries).

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the council decision on the conclusion of the economic partnership agreement between the union and the southern african development community (sadc). the agreement is centred on the southern african customs union (sacu), the oldest such cooperation system in the world. the economic partnership agreement (epa) is intended to promote trade and development among sadc member states, as the union has allowed sadc-epa countries to be exempted from existing export duties and to levy new export taxes in exceptional circumstances, in the event of specific revenue needs, to promote young industries or for environmental protection purposes. this economic partnership agreement has the potential to bring about fundamental positive changes and contribute to sustainable economic development and to trade and integration within the deepened region. however, sadc states should pursue trade and development friendly domestic policies and pursue structural reforms, and the union should provide support for capacity building and trade.
in writing. ‒ economic partnership agreements (epas) are the framework for trade and development agreements between african, caribbean and pacific states and the eu. they are designed to support the acp countries' regional and global trade integration. gmp is another important step towards deepening regional integration, provided that the effectiveness of control is adequate and the necessary follow-up measures are in place. in addition, it is essential to involve civil society as a partner in economic processes, which can be facilitated by the appropriate allocation of available resources. monitoring of the contribution to sustainable fair trade will be particularly important in the context of gmp. in this context, i voted in favour of the european parliament giving its consent to the draft council decision on the conclusion, on behalf of the european union, of the economic partnership agreement between the european union and its member states, of the one part, and the countries associated with the economic partnership agreement of the southern african development community, of the other part (sadc gpm countries).
in writing. the need for changes in trade between the eu and third countries, and the unacceptable pursuit of access to developing countries' markets at all costs. the policy has been primarily to serve the interests of multinational corporations, whose power continues to grow as markets expand. the ever-widening market brings uncertainty to economies, worsening the situation of those who live off work and wages. the report cannot be supported because trade agreements would be needed whose cornerstone is to increase the population holding capacity of the area. this is a transfer of technological knowledge rather than a mutual opening of markets, which can actually help developing countries catch up.
in writing. ‒ seven of the 15 members of the southern african development community (sadc) - angola, botswana, lesotho, mozambique, namibia, swaziland and south africa - have started negotiations with the union for an economic partnership agreement (epa). this is the sadc-gpm group. at the end of 2007, botswana, lesotho, swaziland, mozambique and namibia concluded interim interregional gpms with the union. the provisional gpm also contains a clause allowing angola and/or south africa to join quickly if they so wish. the agreement was signed by botswana, lesotho, swaziland and mozambique in june 2009. although namibia had initialled the agreement more than nine years earlier, it ultimately decided not to sign it. both parties decided to continue negotiations on a comprehensive regional gpm covering services, investment and trade-related rules. the union concluded negotiations with six members of the sadc gpm (botswana, lesotho, namibia, mozambique, south africa and swaziland) on 15 july 2014. angola did not ultimately initial the agreement, but may join in the future due to its special accession clause. the council adopted a draft decision this year on the conclusion of the initial economic partnership agreement, but this will require parliament's consent. in its report, the committee on international trade recommends that parliament give its consent to the conclusion of the agreement. i voted accordingly.
in writing. ‒ i could not vote in favour of the eu-south africa development community (sadc) partnership agreement because it could be detrimental to the most vulnerable african economic operators in its current form. the draft draft, while supported at government level by all the negotiating parties, is a full-fledged free trade agreement in its practical effect, and poses a real risk of market disadvantages for local small and medium-sized enterprises, handicraftsmen and others, who are still weak due to the eu's economic overweight. i also think that the eusadc agreement should be treated with caution because it would be the first of a series of similar partnership agreements with countries in the poorest regions of the world, for which an unbalanced regulation could create an unfavourable precedent.
in writing. ‒ the cotonou partnership agreement, when it was established in 2000, called for fundamental changes to the long-standing non-reciprocal trade preferences that have defined economic and political relations between the african, caribbean and pacific (acp) group of states and the european union for almost 40 years. i voted in favour of the motion that is now on the agenda.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report because i believe that this proposal for a council directive will allow for a wider application of workers' rights and that such international labour standards will encourage member states that have not yet ratified them to do so. the fisheries industry has experienced significant growth, but this growth has not been accompanied by improvements in working conditions and safety. workers in the fishing industry often face harsh or difficult working conditions, spending long periods at sea and often being exposed to unpredictable and dangerous conditions. this agreement guarantees fishermen working under the jurisdiction or flag of a member state of the union adequate living conditions, the right to return home, regular health checks and social protection. i am convinced that agreements to protect workers are an important tool in the fight against exploitation (for example, forced labour, child labour) and therefore i consider it essential to establish a minimum and a maximum age. i believe that the adoption of international labour standards, the involvement of civil partners (e.g. cogeca, etf, europêche, ilo) together ensure the protection of workers and decent working conditions.
in writing. ‒ workers in the fishing sector require special protection, taking into account, among other things, the specific characteristics of work on fishing vessels, the high risk of fatal and non-fatal accidents and the risk of occupational diseases compared to other sectors. i was in favour of the document under consideration.
in writing. ‒ i voted against the resolution condemning poland because it touches on issues of subsidiarity, can be interpreted as a political attack, is counterproductive and damages the credibility of the polish people and the european institutions. the resolution of the internal political dispute surrounding the polish constitutional court is not a competence of the union, and the rule of law mechanism is not provided for in the eu treaties, so that the procedure or the penalty to be imposed on poland at the end of it is legally inapplicable. the existing eu treaties do not empower the commission to initiate such a measure, and there is therefore a risk that the mechanism based on the invoicing of undefined concepts serves purely political purposes and not the interests of eu citizens. i do not consider it fortunate that in the current climate of growing anti-eu sentiment, parliament and the commission should be meddling in the internal affairs of a sovereign member state instead of seeking rational solutions to the challenges that threaten the very existence of europe, and that is why i voted against the adoption of this resolution.

in writing. ‒ i supported the motion for a resolution because i consider it to be a major breakthrough in relations between the european union and its member states, in terms of the functioning of the democratic rule of law, the european democratic principles and the rule of law, and the monitoring and possible sanctioning of breaches of the law. i consider it fully justified and founded on eu law that the commission should examine the steps taken by the new polish government to dismantle or restrict democratic institutions, in particular the reduction of the constitutional tribunal's powers, discuss them with the polish government and, if necessary, propose sanctions. i am convinced that with today's decision the ep can also contribute to solving the polish constitutional crisis. in considering my vote, as a hungarian opposition member, i could not ignore the important lesson that if the commission and the european parliament had acted with similar consistency in the past against a hungarian government that has long been violating european democratic norms in similar or even more serious ways, the state of democracy in my country might not have worsened to the current situation.

in writing. ‒ i voted in agreement with the rapporteur on the report on relations with tunisia. tunisia should be included among the countries with high priority in the european neighbourhood policy. the process of peaceful democratic transition is a successful example in the arab world, and the eu's engagement with tunisia is of great importance for the security of the region as a whole and for the security of europe. deep cooperation is needed, particularly in the fight against terrorism, as tunisia has been hit by numerous terrorist attacks in the past year and the islamic state is recruiting a large number of young people in the country.
in writing. the report rightly points out that the instability in libya and its ripple effects are a serious threat to the stability of tunisia and the region as a whole, as tunisia is currently hosting one million displaced libyans. but the material also ignores the fact that the situation in libya is the result of some eu member states attacking libya without un authorization, in violation of international law. and a lot of that goes back to the incitement of terrorism. the report is seriously flawed and cannot be supported in its entirety, only in its details, because it is justified in some of its elements, such as the fight against human trafficking.
in writing. ‒ tunisia, which has been a successful example for the arab world in its peaceful democratic transition, is in a difficult socioeconomic situation and faces security challenges. the committee on foreign affairs' motion for a resolution looks at how the eu can support tunisia's democratic transition, which is facing serious difficulties in the areas of political reforms and institutions, economic and social development, security and defence, and mobility, research, education and culture. i voted in favour of the adoption of the draft resolution.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report, fully agreeing with the positive assessment and support it reflects for the building of democracy in tunisia, and the stabilising role the country plays in the region. i consider it important that the further development of the political and economic relations with the european union and its member states continue to provide tunisia with a significant contribution to combating the effects of terrorism, economic difficulties and unemployment, in particular by developing its judicial and security institutions. i am convinced that a resolution of this clear support from the european parliament can contribute to the completion of these positive processes in tunisia.
in writing. ‒ tunisia is currently in a difficult socio-economic situation and is facing security challenges due to the libyan situation. the tunisian economy is heavily dependent on foreign investment, tourism and exports of products to the eu. an economy can only flourish if democracy can flourish. i supported him with my vote.
in writing. ‒ the report deals with social dumping within the european union and essentially says that undeclared employment and disguised self-employment can lead to distortions of competition, which can result in long-term damage to social security systems, an increase in precarious jobs and a deterioration in the protection of workers and the quality of employment in general. the increasing trend towards outsourcing and subcontracting may provide opportunities for the abuse or circumvention of existing labour and social legislation. therefore, addressing those abuses is essential for maintaining freedom of movement in the internal market and solidarity within the union. on the basis of the above, the report is to be supported, but i think that some comments are appropriate in the interests of clarity. the free movement of goods, services and capital between countries where the average wage differential between the individual countries is ten times (denmark-bulgaria) or even four times (germany-hungary) leads to social dumping in the first place and no such regulation helps, at best, to moderate the extreme cases. the report stresses the need for upward social convergence, while the opposite is happening in the union, with a declining middle class, precisely because of the huge wage gaps, exacerbated by the pressure of immigration and cheap (chinese) imports, which also push wages downwards.
in writing. ‒ the fidesz-kdnp delegation to the european parliament voted unanimously and decisively against the ep report on social dumping. the document identifies a threat to the free movement of services in eu citizens legally employed in another member state, particularly workers from central and eastern europe. instead of defining the concept of 'social dumping', the report sought to define the posting of legally employed workers to another eu member state as social dumping. the report attempts to conflate the status of workers legally posted to another member state under existing eu legislation, and of carriers providing cross-border services, with the situation of, inter alia, undeclared workers and those working in the domestic and care sector (especially home care), which is unacceptable. as is well known, the proportion of posted workers within the union is less than 1% of the union labour market. the question arises as to why the european commission has forced the start of the revision of the legislation on posted workers when the deadline for its transposition has not yet expired. it is also a well-known fact that western european companies are much more capital-intensive, whereas in central and eastern europe, one of the main elements of competitiveness is lower labour costs. the difference between the two could be resolved, albeit in a limited way, by legislation on posted workers, the review of which would be reasonable and proportionate only if adequate experience were available.

in writing. ‒ the european union is building on the single and common internal market, while the competence in the social area remains with the member states. the report by the committee on employment and social affairs deals with the asymmetry between the completion of the internal market and highly heterogeneous social rights. as the intense competition between economic operators encourages companies to reduce labour costs, this asymmetry creates undesirable competition between companies. this is contrary to the principle of fair competition between firms, the proliferation of abusive practices and the use of unfair social competition undermines the principle of the internal market and undermines confidence in european integration, and encourages protectionism and unilateral social decisions by member states. the report calls for measures to address the legislative and regulatory gaps that are conducive to the emergence of unfair competition in the internal market. these include strengthening the controls and inspections resulting from the application of the legislation in force, modernising the register of work performed and a single digital document ensuring portability of social rights for all european workers. it proposes the establishment of a european list of companies responsible for serious infringements such as undeclared work and the establishment of minimum wages, which in certain sectors could be extended to the community level. i voted in favour of the draft resolution.
in writing. ‒ in order to avoid contradiction with my duties as vice-president of the people's party, in cases where the faction votes differently from the hungarian representatives in the roll-call voting, i will not participate in the vote directly. i do not press the ballot button, but i do raise my hand to indicate to the pp group the voting position that we had previously agreed on. i did the same thing in this case.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report because it makes the right statements in an area that is important to me personally. the rapporteur notes that, in addition to the aspirations for peace and prosperity after the second world war, the founders of 'europe' defined it as a democratic area where, in addition to a prosperous economy, a high level of social protection is ensured. in reality, however, while great progress has been made in the economic sphere, the member states have retained their competence in the social sphere, apart from certain principles laid down in the treaty and in certain directives. i agree with the observation that there is an asymmetry in practice between the internal market in the making and the highly heterogeneous social rights. i believe that there is an inverse principle between the development of the social system and economic development, which is often misunderstood: member states are economically successful when they maintain a quality social system (and not the other way around). i agree that in an asymmetric system competition between companies is created, which also hinders the maintenance of a high level of social protection within europe (i.e. intense competition between economic operators encourages companies to reduce expenditure). unfortunately, the gender pay gap is further burdened by social dumping. i believe that the european minimum wage, which the party of european socialists dreamed of for a decade, would have a positive impact on social rights!

in writing. ‒ subject: ep opinion on the proposal for a council decision amending council decision (eu) 2015/1601 of 22 september 2015 establishing, in the framework of the consultation procedure, transitional measures in the interest of italy and greece in the area of international protection. the proposal is essentially to create a legal framework for a mandatory relocation scheme, ostensibly to help greece and italy, but in reality to implement the great immigration plan to divide europe. it would oblige member states to facilitate the entry of millions of people who are clearly not refugees in the sense of international law but economic immigrants, alien to european culture, on the basis of the admission quotas foreseen for member states. the proposal goes further than the council's proposal and is based on the principle of full, unconditional liberal acceptance and firmly rejects the principle of protecting the identity of the member states. the proposal states that resettlement should not be at the expense of relocation, both of which are important tools of solidarity. relocation is a form of internal solidarity between member states, while resettlement and humanitarian or other forms of reception are external solidarity with third countries hosting the majority of refugees. it's all a play on words, but the essence is the same: the great project of the dismantling of the nation-states, the abandonment of the identity and culture of europe. on the basis of all these considerations, i have, of course, refused to accept the report.
in writing. ‒ i would like to point out that this way of distributing asylum seekers is still not considered a suitable way to resolve the situation, since each state has the sovereign right to decide who it will accept on its territory. furthermore, forced relocation increases the traction effect and is not responsive to the management of secondary migration movements. the eu has also provided support to the government of the drc in the form of grants, loans and other financial assistance to the drc. in my view, europe and refugees have a common interest in allowing refugees to return to their home countries once the causes of their flight have been mitigated or eliminated. and that doesn't mean bringing in migrants and distributing them, it means getting aid there. in addition to turkey, other states hosting large refugee camps also need to be helped. the european parliament's report instead of merely putting the eu-turkey agreement into a technical form seeks to extend and accelerate the scope of this failed mechanism, which will only make it even more difficult for this already dysfunctional system to function. in view of all this, i voted against the report.

in writing. the commission is taking its usual form, trying to find solutions at the level of slogans, strictly on the basis of the repeatedly failed neoliberal economic policy. the proposals of the committee on employment and social affairs are well-intentioned, but they are not very practical, given that average wages within the union vary by a factor of 5 to 10, and the wage differentials in developing countries are a distortion of competition. it should be understood that it is impossible to impose the same economic policy on so many different countries. the committee is much more critical than the original commission document, and its assessment of the situation is much better, so its amendments are supported, as opposed to the original document.
in writing. ‒ the commission has proposed to the council the adoption of a decision on guidelines for the employment policies of the member states. the council shall consult parliament before adopting the proposal. in its report, the committee on employment and social affairs recommends that parliament adopt the commission proposal as amended, with seven amendments and five new guidelines, and asks the commission to submit its proposal to the council amended accordingly. i voted accordingly.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report, the points of which are being presented for the second time by the european parliament to the commission and the council respectively. the commission's proposal for a directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to asbestos at work is a very important one. the treaty on european union clearly states the objective of the coordination of the economic policies of the member states within the union. it also provides that the european union shall adopt measures (for example, in the form of guidelines) to coordinate the employment and social policies of the member states. i regret to note that these principles are not being fully respected, and that more and more member states are pursuing a policy of special treatment. in particular, some member states are ignoring the spirit of the treaty (c), which in my view reinforces the phenomenon of the democratic deficit with the eu. i think we should not only talk about job creation, but also about quality jobs. a member state (e.g. hungary) should not be able to include in its employment data the citizens working abroad or slave labourers on a monthly wage of eur 150. in this context, i am pleased that the proposals put a strong social focus on europe 2020 and on the economic and labour policies and challenges of the member states.
in writing. ‒ member states and the union shall seek to develop a coordinated strategy for the achievement of the objectives set out in the treaty on european union in the field of employment, and in particular the development of a skilled, trained and adaptable workforce and labour markets responsive to economic change. i voted for the motion.
in writing. ‒ the motion for a resolution details the importance of the european union's accession to the convention as a signatory to the convention in combating illegal trade in wild fauna and flora. the eu is one of the main destinations for trade in these living animals and plants, and the main market for products made from them. the proposal makes recommendations for changes to the decision-making mechanism and the financing and implementation of the convention and aims to increase the number of species listed in the appendix. the amendments will help to detect and tackle corruption and abuse and illegal trade more effectively and encourage more effective information exchange and coordination of controls between member states and across the eu. on the basis of all this, i have accepted the proposal.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution on the main objectives of the cop17 meeting in johannesburg. the eu's accession to cites is an essential step towards achieving the wider objectives of the union's environmental protection policy and ensuring the regulation of international trade in endangered species of wild fauna and flora, and in promoting the un's sustainable development policies for the period up to 2030. the accession of the european union to cites has made its position more transparent. this is a logical and necessary step to ensure that the european union can fully meet its environmental policy objectives.
in writing. ‒ the committee on the environment, public health and food safety has proposed the adoption of a resolution on the strategic objectives of the union for the 17th meeting of the conference of the parties to the convention on international trade in endangered species of wild fauna and flora (cites), to be held in johannesburg, south africa, from 24 september to 5 october 2016. the draft welcomes the eu's accession to cites and the fact that the eu is now participating as a party to the conference for the first time. the draft specifically addresses the protection of certain endangered animal and plant species, such as the african elephant, the broad-billed rhinoceros, the african lion, the red-cockaded woodpecker, the tiger and the asian big cat, as well as the agar tree and the rose tree, and the adoption of measures to promote their conservation. i voted in favour of the adoption of the draft resolution.
in writing. ‒ the convention on international trade in endangered species of wild fauna and flora is the world's largest convention on the conservation of global wildlife, with 181 member states. wildlife trade is the fourth largest black market (after drugs, people and arms) and this illegal trade is also affecting the eu. the proposal calls for strong action against corruption and organised crime in wildlife trade; calls for more effective measures against illegal online trade; calls for the establishment of an effective sanctions system, and calls for consumer awareness and traceability to be strengthened. in view of all this, i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution and i trust that hungary will actively participate in the implementation of these commitments. i think that the hungarian political elite, who want to hunt, cannot afford to arbitrarily change the list of protected animals, but rather i suggest that they do everything possible to act together.
in writing. ‒ the question arose earlier as to what the main strategic objectives of the european union will be at the forthcoming conference of the parties to the convention on international trade in endangered species of wild fauna and flora (cites) to be held in johannesburg, south africa, from 24 september to 5 october 2016. i voted yes to the final vote on the relevant document.
in writing. ‒ despite the increasing use of e-services and online shopping, traditional postal services are still indispensable today. they are particularly needed in remote regions where there is no adequate internet coverage. the third postal directive paved the way for the completion of the internal market for postal services as early as 2008. by 2013, market opening was achieved in all member states. however, significant changes have occurred in the postal services market in the recent period which require a review of the application of the directive. traditional paper-based communications - the delivery of letters, newspapers and magazines - are declining rapidly, while the volume of parcel delivery is increasing thanks to electronic shopping. it is very important to provide cross-border postal services beyond domestic services, at transparent and affordable prices, using the acquis of the present day (e.g. track-and-trace). one of the main priorities is to maintain and promote effective competition in the postal services sector, while taking into account the needs of users. in view of the above, i voted in favour of the adoption of the report.

in writing. ‒ the committee on transport and tourism's motion for a resolution reviews the state of play of postal services since their liberalisation following the 2008 revision of the postal services directive. notes that the decline in paper-based communication and correspondence has been offset by the increase in parcel traffic as online shopping has become more widespread; the commission has also identified a number of areas where the postal sector is particularly vulnerable to the effects of the digital divide. i voted in favour of the draft resolution.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the proposal to amend the european postal services directive, taking into account the significant changes that have taken place in this area since the adoption of the 2008 eu legislation aimed at liberalising the field. of these, traditional postal services and correspondence are particularly affected by the rapid spread of digitalisation, while the demand for parcel delivery has been completely changed and expanded by the expansion of e-commerce. the amendment of the legislation will help european service providers to compete and adapt better to new conditions, while paying due attention to the job-creation potential of the sector in the european labour market.
in writing. ‒ the 2008 review of postal services has achieved the main objectives of the liberalisation of european postal services. over the last five years, as well as due to the growth of e-commerce, the retail segment of the parcel delivery market has grown rapidly, while competition is slowly emerging in the letter delivery market, despite the full opening of the union market. i supported the current proposal.
in writing. ‒ the report considers it important that smes understand the complexities, benefits and risks of external financing. therefore, increasing the financial literacy of smes is a prerequisite for creating a capital market culture where entrepreneurs are willing to consider using capital market solutions. in my view, initiatives such as the capital markets union will exacerbate the problems faced by european smes in accessing finance. this is because they increase the financialisation of the economy, and thereby reduce macroeconomic stability and growth. improving sme financing would also require tightening the financial sector's grip on power and bringing it under state control by strengthening regulation, and establishing a clear link between lending activity and actual production. the typical role of smes is to meet local needs, to participate actively in the local economy. if an sme wants to enter the international market, it can usually do so only if it has a strong foothold in the domestic market. this includes financial security, which deteriorates as funds move away from the workplace. sme financing can be solved by local banks that lend to small businesses in a targeted way and are aware of their activities and can assess the risk of lending. since the report does not encourage this, i have refused to accept it.
in writing. as an economist and on the basis of my international experience, i must say that the minority opinion which emerged during the committee's discussion of the subject should be considered correct. initiatives such as the capital markets union will exacerbate the access to finance problems of european smes by increasing the financialisation of the economy, thereby reducing macroeconomic stability and growth, and by shifting microeconomic risks from large financial players to smes, which will become dependent on increasingly complex and opaque financial instruments. the general solution is to bring the financial sector under state control by strengthening public banking institutions and regulation and to establish a clear link between lending activity and actual production. the sme segment is a local need, and financing is best done with local banks that lend to small businesses and know their business so they can assess the risk of lending. if an sme wants to enter the international market, it can usually only do so if it has a strong foothold in the domestic market. your financial security deteriorates as funds move away from the workplace.
in writing. ‒ the economic and monetary committee's motion for a resolution reviews the financing possibilities for smes in the context of the capital markets union. it states that bank lending is still the most important source of finance for smes and is likely to remain so. however, this is significantly hampered by the significant strengthening and re-implementation of the prudential and supervisory framework for banks in order to safeguard financial stability as a direct consequence of the financial crisis. in order to mitigate possible negative consequences for smes, the so-called sme multiplier was therefore introduced, i.e. the requirement that the capital requirement for credit risk exposure of smes be multiplied by 0,7619. the draft accords priority to this factor. the draft also addresses non-bank financing of smes, including securitisation, listing on a stock exchange, crowdfunding and peer-to-peer lending. finally, it states that the best way to ensure the development of smes is a simple and fair tax system that ensures a level playing field for all businesses, not only in corporate taxation but also in income taxation. i voted for the bill.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on access to finance for smes and increasing the diversity of sme finance in the cmu. the report rightly notes that european smes are very diverse, have different business models, face different challenges and therefore have different financing needs. as the report emphasises, the crisis hit the financing of micro, small and medium-sized enterprises (msmes) harder than that of large enterprises. this situation still exists today and i therefore support the call for diversified and more public and private funding opportunities for smes not only in the start-up phase but throughout their life cycle. diversification is essential because there is no one-size-fits-all approach to funding, and a wide range of tailor-made programmes, tools and initiatives are needed. furthermore, in line with the report and the action plan on a capital markets union, i also believe that smes need to be better connected to financing opportunities, as there are still many obstacles to smes using market-based and other innovative financing methods. finally, i welcome the part of the report that deals with the distortions caused by the tax system. i agree with the rapporteur that we should have a simple and fair tax system that ensures a level playing field for all businesses.
in writing. ‒ european smes are very diverse, with a large number of micro-enterprises, often operating in traditional sectors, and an increasing number of new start-ups and fast-growing innovative enterprises; as these business models face different problems, their financing needs are also different. i voted in favour of the motion under consideration.
in writing. ‒ with around 99% of european enterprises being smes, their capacity to create jobs has a major impact on the performance of the european economy. since the two biggest challenges we face today are reducing unemployment and stopping migration flows, smes must be at the heart of eu entrepreneurship policy-making and all necessary steps must be taken to strengthen the capacity of this sector to create jobs. this is only possible on the basis of an in-depth mapping of existing links. the sme sector in europe is diverse and fragmented. despite the internal market rules, there are still significant differences in the regulatory framework for smes within the european union, in particular with regard to the stability and security of that framework. it is clear that the largest smes in central and eastern europe are small compared to their western counterparts. while the growth of stable economies is fostered by effective interactions between smes and large enterprises, in many southern and eastern european member states, the difficult economic conditions have left their mark on the proper development of smes. this is why national and european policies need to address skills issues in order to create the necessary environment for business development and to increase the capacity of enterprises to create jobs. the report addresses these issues, and i voted in favour of adopting the report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report, as the two biggest challenges we face today are reducing unemployment and stopping migration flows. with around 99% of european enterprises being smes, their capacity to create jobs has a major impact on the performance of the european economy. small and medium-sized enterprises must therefore be at the heart of the development of entrepreneurship policy in the eu and all necessary steps must be taken to strengthen the capacity to create jobs in this sector. this is only possible on the basis of an in-depth mapping of existing links. the sme sector in europe is diverse and fragmented. despite the internal market rules, there are still significant differences in the regulatory framework for smes within the european union, in particular with regard to the stability and security of that framework. it is clear that the largest smes in central and eastern europe are small compared to their western counterparts. while the growth of stable economies is fostered by effective interactions between smes and large enterprises, in many southern and eastern european member states, the difficult economic conditions have left their mark on the proper development of smes. to achieve this, national and european policies need to address skills problems (skill shortages, regulatory uncertainty and administrative burdens) in order to create the necessary environment for business development and to increase the capacity of enterprises to create jobs. the report addresses these problems, which is why i voted for it.
in writing. since i have been a member of the european parliament, i have seen a lot of reports that highlight the important role that smes play in creating jobs in the eu. the reports underline that smes should therefore be supported in every possible way, both through access to resources and through reducing their administrative burdens. despite years of apparent eu ambition, the situation is not good today, and the report makes it clear that access to finance is still one of the main obstacles to the creation and growth of smes. smes are at a serious competitive disadvantage compared to multinational companies which shift their profits to member states or third countries that are tax havens. the substance is not sufficiently robust in terms of its strengths and lacks concrete solutions, but it should be supported.
in writing. ‒ the report of the committee on employment and social affairs is based on the importance of creating new jobs. it notes that smes are the source of new jobs and the engine of the european economy: 85% of jobs in europe were created by smes in the last decade and in 2015, small businesses contributed 71% of the growth in employment in non-financial enterprises. the report stresses that in order to create the healthy environment needed for business development and to increase the capacity of enterprises to create jobs, national and european policies need to address skills problems (skill shortages, non-compliance, brain drain), alleviate regulatory uncertainty and administrative burdens, and tackle undeclared work and the de facto privileged position of multinational companies. stresses furthermore the importance of a stable regulatory environment, regulatory quality and enforcement as the right way to reduce the costs for smes, including labour costs; it is also one of the essential prerequisites for job sustainability and for the ability of smes to create high-quality jobs. i supported the adoption of the report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on better exploiting the job creation potential of smes. as smes are the engine of the european economy, it is crucial, as the report stressed, that member states provide better conditions for sme job creation, including by reducing skills shortages, simplifying unnecessary and overly complex regulatory burdens, increasing innovation capacity and improving access to finance and public procurement. i welcome the report's reference to the frequent preferential treatment of multinational companies and its negative impact on smes. in order to ensure a level playing field and to enhance the job creation capacity of smes, profit shifting practices by multinational companies should be tackled. the report also made an important call for support for the creation and development of cooperative enterprises, cooperation with trade unions and educational institutions, and the promotion of entrepreneurship among people from vulnerable groups. financing is also key to the job creation capacity of smes. the report also made valuable findings in this area. however, i note that increasing labour market flexibility often leads to a reduction in the protection of workers.
in writing. ‒ the rapporteur believes that europe is currently facing two major challenges: unemployment and migration flows, which will have many implications for the future. the high unemployment rate threatens the demographic outlook, as many young people prefer not to start a family in the absence of a job. the long-term consequences of this situation are the pressure on social security systems and pension systems, which also threatens the future of this generation. i supported the s&d position in the final vote on the proposal.
in writing. ‒ the fidesz-kdnp delegation to the european parliament voted unanimously and decisively against the ep report on social dumping. the document identifies a threat to the free movement of services in eu citizens legally employed in another member state, particularly workers from central and eastern europe. instead of defining the concept of 'social dumping', the report sought to define the posting of legally employed workers to another eu member state as social dumping. the report attempts to combine the status of workers legally posted to another member state under existing eu legislation with that of carriers providing cross-border services, with the unacceptable situation of, inter alia, undeclared workers and those working in the domestic and care sector (especially home care). as is well known, the proportion of posted workers within the union is less than 1% of the union labour market. the question arises as to why the european commission has forced the start of the revision of the legislation on posted workers when the deadline for its transposition has not yet expired. it is also a well-known fact that western european companies have much higher capital strengths, whereas in central and eastern europe, one of the main elements of competitiveness is lower labour costs. the difference between the two could be resolved, albeit in a limited way, by legislation on posted workers, the review of which would be reasonable and proportionate only if adequate experience were available.
in writing. ‒ the report of the employment and social affairs committee is on council directive 2000/78/ec of 27 november 2000 establishing a general framework for equal treatment in employment and occupation, the ultimate aim of which was to create a level playing field in employment and occupation. the implementation of the directive has brought about a number of results, but serious problems remain. the report states that discrimination affects all areas of people's lives, employment being just one of them. the data on employment equality are otherwise scarce, partly because the employment equality directive does not require member states to collect them. however, the perceptible differences in other areas can be inferred for this area as well. 40% of roma job seekers experience discrimination, 75% of gays do not hold hands with their partner in public, 38% of jewish respondents said they do not wear symbolic jewish clothing in public, and 37% of muslim respondents experienced discrimination and 11% experienced a hate crime. i voted for the report.
in writing. ‒ the report analyses the experience of the employment equality directive over 15 years and makes suggestions for further improvements. the rapporteur has produced a balanced material which also includes aspects of discrimination on grounds of gender, race, religion, political convictions, disability, age or sexual orientation. although some member states have already implemented the directive - and therefore workers are better informed - others are still lagging behind. the report mentions among the shortcomings the lack of equality data, awareness, the role of civil and social society and access to justice. i think it's important that the report puts a lot of emphasis on age and disability discrimination, the importance of data collection and lifelong learning and training. i believe that the review of equal opportunities in employment is important and that all forms of discrimination should be avoided, which is why i voted in favour of the report. i am convinced that the hungarian government should also introduce more targeted measures to ensure that the principle of equality is applied in practice.
in writing. ‒ the treaty on european union states that the union is founded on the values of respect for human dignity, freedom, democracy, equality, the rule of law and respect for human rights. fifteen years have passed since the adoption of the employment equality directive, the ultimate aim of which is to create a level playing field in employment and occupation. i voted in favour of the document under consideration.
in writing. ‒ the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) was established to support and show solidarity with workers made redundant as a result of major structural changes in world trade patterns (more than 500 workers per enterprise) and the egf aims to contribute to smart, sustainable and inclusive growth and to promote sustainable employment by preparing and supporting redundant workers for a new job. in contrast to the european social fund, the co-financing rate is much lower (60%) and the average duration of the application process is 41 weeks (2013 data) and the average grant per head is around eur 4500. hungary has not used this possibility so far, as mass layoffs took place almost exclusively before 2010 and the existing procedural rules are still not sufficiently flexible for our country. the fund is also a major instrument for dealing with the consequences of the economic crisis, which is why i voted in favour of adopting the report.
in writing. ‒ the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) was established to support and show solidarity with workers made redundant as a result of major structural changes in world trade patterns (more than 500 workers per enterprise) and the egf aims to contribute to smart, sustainable and inclusive growth and to promote sustainable employment by preparing and supporting redundant workers for a new job. in contrast to the european social fund, the co-financing rate is much lower (60%) and the average duration of the application process is 41 weeks (2013 data) and the average grant per head is around eur 4500. hungary has not used this possibility so far, as mass layoffs took place almost exclusively before 2010 and the existing procedural rules are still not sufficiently flexible for our country. the report was prepared by sógor csaba, a hungarian member of parliament from the other side of the border, whose work contributed greatly to making the report even more acceptable to the fidesz-kdnp parliamentary group, and i therefore voted in favour of the adoption of the report.

in writing. the european globalisation adjustment fund can be managed with a budget that is embarrassingly low in relation to eu gdp. the very intention to allow solidarity with workers who have lost their jobs as a result of the major structural changes in world trade due to globalisation in the form of mass redundancies is right. however, experience shows that the fund's resources are actually used to mitigate the damage caused by the profit-making activities of large companies in the central countries, which is highly questionable. in my view, it should be used primarily in the less developed member states, where the impact of globalisation is matched by the negative economic impact of the stronger eu member states.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the adoption of the report on the experience of the european globalisation adjustment fund 2007-14. the fund was set up 10 years ago as an emergency instrument outside the eu's multiannual financial framework, primarily to support european workers and small and medium-sized enterprises who have lost their jobs as a result of the international economic and trade realignment. in my experience, there is still a need for job creation, retraining and business support in this area, but the knowledge of the instrument, the attitude of some member states towards it and the use of the available resources are not yet sufficient. i am confident that the conclusions and corrective proposals contained in the report adopted will contribute to making better use of the potential of this important eu fund in the future, especially in terms of creating new, genuine european jobs.
in writing. ‒ the role of the egf is to enable solidarity to be shown with workers who have lost their jobs as a result of major structural changes in world trade due to globalisation in the context of mass redundancies, in cases where these redundancies have a significant negative impact on the regional or local economy. i voted for the report in the final vote.
madam president, first of all let me thank my colleague mr neuser for his good work. we have recognised that acp-eu cooperation is a unique achievement. it has intensified the ties between acp and eu countries for the last four decades. i would like to highlight two elements that would improve the situation of the peoples of the partner countries: first, placing the 2030 agenda and the sustainable development goals at the centre of the new agreements; and, second, placing the human—rights aspect at the centre of european action. migration and displacement will dominate the acp-eu agenda for the future. a new agreement must address this expanding challenge. to increase political oversight, we need a strong parliamentary dimension in the new cooperation agreement. we must guarantee that european development partnerships are concluded only with regimes respecting human dignity. where governments cannot be our partners, we must bring on board local communities that are ready to cooperate with us. faith-based communities and their organisations represent the real local power in very many places. they often manage development programmes that are already functioning well. their efficiency on the ground is remarkable. my strongest message today is that we must engage better with local communities and faith-based organisations in coordinated – and i underline again coordinated – dialogue. let me draw attention to the importance of local small and medium-sized enterprises: they are key to the improvement of communities and the extension of social cohesion. lastly, the situation is quite clear: let us have cooperation with local powers and international actors to address the humanitarian situation which can no longer be overlooked in many acp countries.
mr. president, i have to ask you... it is in the interest of europe and of refugees that refugees are able to return to their home countries as soon as the causes of their situation have been mitigated or eliminated. so we need to eliminate the triggers and help where the problem is, not bring it here. to this end, it is vital that people who are forced to flee can live in suitable living conditions in camps close to their home countries. and one of the most important elements of that is education. providing education is essential not only for the healthy development of the child but also for the future of their own community. you can't just drop an entire generation out of education, just to avoid radicalization. that's why it's very important for syrian children to be able to get an education in lebanon. and i'm glad that hungary is also directly supporting the provision of education in the refugee camps in lebanon, jordan, iraq, with concrete offers, or the construction of hospitals.

mr. president, it's been 60 years since the hungarian people rose in unprecedented unity in october 1956 against the communist dictatorship and the soviet bolshevik rule that invaded their country. the hungarian revolution of 1956 and the war of independence continued with the prague spring in 1968, and then the polish solidarity freedom movement in the 1980s. in the pivotal year of 1989, the common struggle of our peoples in central and eastern europe led to the fall of soviet communism and the change of regime led to the reunification of a divided europe. freedom is one of the european community's most fundamental values. it is worth remembering the hungarian 1956 and those who sacrificed their lives for freedom as one of the most outstanding events in our common history. we must follow their example and continue our fight against all oppressive powers and totalitarian regimes.

mr president, mr secretary general, i have to ask you to please leave. we have a formal meeting scheduled, but we're also going to make an important content decision. with our vote, the european union will ratify the paris agreement on climate change. although several countries have already done so, including hungary, this will be a decisive step in terms of entry into force. the european union's member states have been at the forefront of the fight against climate change. they set ambitious goals and achieved them. but when even more ambitious goals are set, i would like to make two comments. perhaps it is not a waste of time, because we have many responsibilities for the people of europe and for the european economy. so for more radical than radical measures, we have to take into account that europe is only responsible for 10% of emissions, and globally, there is no reduction, just a shift. these aspects must therefore be taken into account in order to ensure the competitiveness of the european economy. the other thing to note is that the most important thing about the paris climate agreement is that it is legally binding. but the european union must also be a force for good in all of this, and it is not possible for the united states as one of the biggest emitters to make its position and then its achievement dependent on who comes to power in the presidential election. enforcement means that each party fulfils what it has agreed to.
in writing. ‒ the adoption of the paris agreement marks a turning point towards a comprehensive and joint action at global level. its implementation will accelerate the transition to a climate-resilient and climate-neutral global economy. the paris agreement set the goal of keeping temperature rise below 2°c, set limits on greenhouse gas emissions and set as a priority the assistance to countries that are more vulnerable to climate change. the goal of the agreement is to leave a more sustainable, equitable, and healthy planet for future generations. the approval of the european parliament, which fulfilled the conditions for the entry into force of the agreement, was key to its implementation. hungary was the first member state of the european union to complete the internal ratification procedure of the paris agreement. in this light and in line with the position of the fidesz-kdnp group, i voted in favour of ratification.

in writing. ‒ the 21st conference of the parties to the unfccc, held in paris from 30 november to 12 december 2015, adopted the text of an agreement to strengthen global responses to the challenge of climate change. the commission has called for the paris agreement to be signed and ratified as soon as possible, and the european council, in its decision of 18 march 2016, underlined the importance of the convention being adopted by the eu and its member states as soon as possible. the agreement was initialled by the commission and the council, and by all 28 member states, at a high-level signing ceremony in new york on 22 april 2016. the ratification of the agreement requires a council decision with the consent of parliament. the committee on the environment, public health and food safety has proposed in its report that parliament give its consent to ratification of the agreement. i voted accordingly.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report approving the proposal for a council decision. i agree that the paris agreement is historic in terms of the fight against climate change and the number of countries that have signed it. it is important to note that by the end of cop 21, a total of 187 parties had notified their intended national contributions to the agreement. the convention represents a turning point towards comprehensive and joint action at the global level and towards a transition to a climate-neutral global economy. the paris agreement shall enter into force 30 days after at least 55 parties responsible for at least 55% of their greenhouse gas emissions have deposited their instruments of ratification, acceptance, approval or accession with the united nations. it is important to note that, as a first step, the commission and the council signed the agreement on behalf of the european union and all 28 member states at a solemn high-level signing ceremony in new york on 22 april 2016. meps consider it unthinkable that the paris agreement will enter into force without the eu's signature, given the eu's leading role in the fight against climate change. it therefore urges the council and each member state to take the necessary steps to complete the eu and national validation process by the end of 2016 at the latest.
in writing. ‒ the paris agreement is a historic milestone in the fight against climate change. we heard the position of un secretary-general ban ki-moon at the parliament's sitting today. taking collective action to protect the environment is our first priority and the eu institutions have a key role to play in this. i voted in favour of the recommendation.
in writing. ‒ the commission proposes to mobilise the european union solidarity fund (eusf) to provide financial assistance following the disaster in greece on 17 november 2015 (earthquake affecting the ionian islands in particular lefkada and the northern parts of ithaca and kefalonia ). the quakes reached a magnitude of 6.1 on the richter scale. the greek authorities initially estimated the total direct damage caused by the disaster at eur 66 073 345. as the above amount represents 2,1% of the gdp of the nuts 2 region of the ionian islands concerned (based on eurostat 2014 data) and exceeds the regional gdp threshold of 1,5%, the disaster is a regional disaster within the meaning of article 2 (3) of the eusfa regulation. in accordance with article 4a (2) of the eafrd regulation, at the request of greece, the commission paid an advance of eur 164 798, representing 10% of the contribution from the fund. the amount to be paid after deduction of the 10% advance already paid shall be eur 1 487 036. on the basis of the above, i voted in favour of the adoption of the report.

in writing. ‒ the european union solidarity fund aims to enable the union to respond to emergencies and express solidarity with the population of regions affected by disasters in a rapid, efficient and flexible manner. following the earthquake that struck the ionian islands on 17 november 2015, greece submitted an application on 5 february 2016 to mobilise the fund. the greek authorities have estimated the direct damage caused by the earthquake at eur 66 073 345. this amount exceeds the regional gdp threshold of 1,5% and the earthquake is therefore considered a regional disaster. the commission therefore submitted to the european parliament and the council a proposal for a decision to mobilise eur 1 651 834 from the solidarity fund for greece in the form of commitment and payment appropriations. i voted for the motion.
in writing. ‒ the report summarises the ep and the emi's decision on the assistance to be charged to the european union solidarity fund following the earthquake in the greek ionian islands in november 2015. the committee on budgets recommends that the report be adopted swiftly in order to allow the earmarked funds to be disbursed as soon as possible. i voted in favour of the report.
in writing. ‒ the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) aims to support the reintegration into the labour market of workers and self-employed persons made redundant as a result of globalisation, as a result of major structural changes in world trade patterns, or as a result of the prolongation of the global financial and economic crisis or a new global financial and economic crisis. finland has submitted an application, under reference number egf/2016/001 fi/microsoft, for a financial contribution from the egf, following a redundancies in microsoft mobile oy and eight related suppliers, amounting to 2161 persons, under the regulation on the mobilisation of the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf). the application complies with the eligibility criteria set out in the egf regulation. finland plans six types of measures for the benefit of the dismissed workers concerned by the application: coaching and other preparatory measures; employment and business services; labour market training; salary support; start-up aid; and reimbursement of travel, accommodation and relocation costs. on the basis of the above, i voted in favour of the adoption of the report.

in writing. ‒ the european globalisation adjustment fund was established to provide additional support to workers affected by the consequences of major structural changes in world trade. on 11 march 2016, finland submitted to the commission an application to mobilise the fund, in order to facilitate the reintegration into the labour market of workers made redundant by microsoft in finland and by eight related suppliers and downstream companies. the measures concern 1441 of the 2161 workers made redundant. six types of personalised services are intended to be provided to redundant workers upon request, namely (i) counselling and other preparatory measures, (ii) employment and business services, (iii) labour market training, (iv) salary support, (v) start-up aid and (vi) reimbursement of travel, accommodation and relocation costs. the commission has concluded that the conditions for a financial contribution from the fund have been met and that the planned measures constitute active labour market measures falling within the scope of the eligible activities and has therefore submitted to the parliament and the council a proposal for a decision to mobilise eur 5 364 000 from the fund in the form of commitment and payment appropriations for finland. i supported the motion.
in writing. ‒ the adoption of the proposal gives the green light for the application of the european globalisation adjustment fund in several regions of finland. the fund would provide eur 5 364 000 to deal with the wave of redundancies at microsoft, which affected 2 161 people, and to integrate the unemployed into the labour market. i voted in favour of the report.
in writing. ‒ the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) aims to support the reintegration into the labour market of workers and self-employed persons made redundant as a result of globalisation, as a result of major structural changes in world trade patterns, or as a result of the prolongation of the global financial and economic crisis or a new global financial and economic crisis. sweden submitted an application on 31 march 2016 for a financial contribution from the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) under the reference number egf/2016/002 se/ericsson. the measures are expected to involve 918 of the 1556 redundant workers eligible for the egf contribution. in the it and telecommunications sector, faced with stagnating growth and stronger competition from asian manufacturers, ericsson reduced its production of telecommunications hardware and gradually reduced its staff in sweden. for the regions concerned, a relatively large group of older workers with similar backgrounds were made redundant and the majority of these workers do not have the skills sought in the local labour market. the personalised services for redundant workers co-financed by the egf include: counselling and career guidance; protected and supported employment and rehabilitation measures; education and training; and job-search allowance. participants aged 50 and over receive special attention in motivation training and career planning. on the basis of the above, i voted in favour of the adoption of the report.

in writing. ‒ the european globalisation adjustment fund was established to provide additional support to workers affected by the consequences of major structural changes in world trade. on 31 march 2016, sweden submitted to the commission an application to mobilise the fund, in order to facilitate the reintegration into the labour market of workers made redundant by telefonaktiebolaget lm ericsson in sweden. the measures concern 918 workers made redundant. four types of personalised services are intended to be provided to redundant workers upon request, namely: (i) counselling and career guidance consisting of detailed analysis and personalised planning, guidance, counselling and motivational training and career planning; (ii) protected and supported employment and rehabilitation measures; (iii) education and training; (iv) financial allowance for job search. the commission has concluded that the application fulfils the conditions for a financial contribution from the fund and that the planned measures constitute active labour market measures falling within the scope of the eligible activities and has therefore submitted a proposal for a decision to the european parliament and the council to mobilise eur 3 957 918 from the fund in the form of commitment and payment appropriations for sweden. i supported the motion.
in writing. ‒ the adoption of the proposal gives the green light for the use of the european globalisation adjustment fund in several regions of sweden. the fund would provide eur 3 957 918 to help telefonsaktiebolaget lm ericsson cope with the wave of redundancies affecting 1 556 people and to integrate the unemployed into the labour market. i voted for the report.
in writing. ‒ on 1 april 2016, the deputy prosecutor general of the hellenic republic requested the suspension of the immunity of mr giorgos grammatikakis, member of the european parliament, in connection with proceedings proposed by the public prosecutor's office of the city of retimno, concerning a suspected breach of trust committed in retimno (crete) as an associate in the course of his duties between 2000 and 2002. in its report, the committee on legal affairs notes that the proposed legal proceedings are clearly not linked to the office of member of the european parliament of mr grammatikakis, but to his former position as rector of the senate of the university of crete, and that there is no indication that they were initiated with the aim of causing political damage to the member in question. therefore, in accordance with the request of the member concerned, mr grammatikakis, it proposes to the parliament that the immunity be suspended. however, the report notes that the proposed court proceedings relate to a meeting held on 8 march 1996 and that a previous court proceeding in relation to the same case had already covered the period from 2000 onwards and had resulted in the acquittal of all the accused. it also expresses its dissatisfaction with the fact that the suspension of immunity is requested 20 years after the events took place and that the greek judicial system did not bring charges against giorgos grammatikakis during this period and only now, during his term as a member of the european parliament, intends to do so. i voted for the report.
in writing. ‒ the rapporteur proposes to suspend the immunity. i voted in favor of the motion.
my fellow members of parliament! i ask you to imagine the following situation: you go to a demonstration, you exercise your basic human right to express yourself. the demonstration is brutally broken up, you are produced in handcuffs, you are imprisoned, and then you are subjected to arbitrary criminal proceedings. and then imagine that you're a patriot, you express strong opinions, critical opinions, and then you find yourself accused of a terrorist act that could get you life. if you imagine these situations, you will have no doubt that you must vote yes, as i did, to the motion, the essence of which is that everyone has the right to protection in criminal proceedings, and that this must be provided free of charge and of a high standard to those in need.
in writing. ‒ the draft directive of the european parliament and of the council on provisional immunity from costs for suspects and accused persons deprived of liberty and on immunity in european arrest warrant proceedings can be considered as part of the roadmap to strengthen the procedural rights of the accused in criminal proceedings adopted on 30 november 2009 with the aim of establishing common minimum rules in the member states. after difficult negotiations, a mutually acceptable text has been reached and as a member of the fidesz people's party delegation, i vote in favour of the initiative. in my view, a satisfactory compromise has been reached in the trilateral negotiations, which successfully contributes to the definition of common european minimum standards and does not impose a disproportionate burden in the field of criminal procedure.

madam president, what could the european union do to stop the mass and increasingly intolerable migration of people to europe, taking into account the rights of migrants in a deprived situation and the rights of europe's indigenous peoples? well, first of all, by dealing with the root causes of wars, armed conflicts. what would that take? he also blocks the financing of isis and other terrorist organizations. what would that be? the supply of arms to dictatorships and proxy wars by eu member states and companies should be strictly controlled and prohibited. and we should also be scrutinizing every transaction that could potentially be used to fund isis and other terrorist organizations because someone is supporting them. what do they do instead? they're making a show of exporting drugs that are punishable by death, hundreds of pages of documents. they control this, they regulate that, but they don't control the arms trade and isis funding. this is not a solution!
in writing. ‒ eu-wide export controls are a tool of external trade policy that serve broader policy objectives. export controls are an important policy tool of the european union. regulation (ec) no 1236/2005 on the fight against torture is a unique instrument that contributes to the protection of human rights and to the global eradication of the death penalty and torture by controlling products and activities that may be used in the context of the death penalty, torture or other cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment or punishment. the regulation expresses the european union's long-standing ambition to combine prohibitions with requirements for authorisation of trade in the products listed in its annexes. it introduces a ban on equipment and technical assistance intended solely for torture and the execution of the death penalty (annex ii) and a licensing system for products which, if misused, are suitable for torture and execution by lethal injection (annex iii). the draft opinion also proposes the creation of a group for the coordination of installations and the introduction of a periodic review mechanism and a more regular system for sharing information and reporting in order to strengthen control and the effective implementation of the regulation. in view of the above, i voted in favour of the adoption of the proposal.

in writing. ‒ regulation (ec) no 1236/2005 on the fight against torture is a unique instrument that contributes to the protection of human rights by controlling products and activities that may be used in the context of the death penalty, torture or other cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment or punishment. it shall contribute to the achievement of the global abolition of the death penalty and torture by combining prohibitions with trade authorisation requirements for listed products. it introduces a ban on devices that can be used exclusively for torture and the execution of capital punishment and a licensing system for products that, if misused, are suitable for torture and execution by lethal injection. in 2014, the commission proposed to the european parliament and the council to amend that regulation in order to review the union control of trade in instruments of torture and to update the list of controlled products. in its report, the committee on international trade recommends that parliament adopt the draft at first reading with 38 amendments. i voted accordingly.
