in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution because i believe that it reaffirms the european union's leading role in the fight against the death penalty and torture worldwide. the new 'emergency procedure' for instruments and substances used for capital punishment and torture will allow states to ban the export or transfer of such items, even on the basis of a clear suspicion, and to prohibit their online trade, advertising, training and knowledge transfer. the eu's experience in the past of such restrictions having made a significant contribution to the fight against this repulsive and inhumane practice in partner countries, i am confident that with the ep's decision , which enjoys wide political support , this will continue even more effectively, until the total abolition of torture and the death penalty.
in writing. ‒ the torture regulation contributes to the global abolition of the death penalty and torture, which is a longstanding eu objective. it shall contribute to the achievement of those objectives by combining prohibitions with the requirements for authorisation of trade in the listed products. it introduces a ban on equipment and related technical assistance intended solely for torture and the execution of the death penalty and a licensing system for products which, if misused, are suitable for torture and execution by lethal injection. i supported the adoption of the report, in agreement with the s&d group's position.
in writing. ‒ this report concerns the approval of the strategic cooperation agreement between china and europol. such a strategic agreement excludes the exchange of personal data, and therefore the issue of data protection is not relevant in this case. the information exchanged may include the field of expertise, general situation reports, results of strategic analysis and information on criminal investigation procedures and crime prevention methods, as well as training activities and the provision of advice and support for specific criminal investigations. the strategic cooperation agreement between china and europol would help and strengthen the fight against organised crime and contribute to strengthening international law enforcement cooperation. on these grounds, i supported the adoption of the report.
in writing. ‒ the exchange of information with law enforcement agencies of third country partners is of paramount importance for the successful fight against organised crime. according to the european police office (europol), china is increasingly important in the fight against organised crime as a country of origin, destination and transit. the strategic cooperation agreement to be concluded between europol and china is therefore important, allowing for the exchange of expertise, general situation reports, strategic analysis results, information on criminal investigation procedures and crime prevention methods, as well as advice and support for specific criminal investigations. europol clearly needs to work with china, which is why i voted in favour of adopting the report.

in writing. china's dynamic development is unfortunately not limited to the economy, but also to its increasingly important role in international crime, and in some sectors of organised crime it is a clear frontrunner. such areas are illegal immigration, trafficking in human beings, drug-related crime, euro counterfeiting, intellectual property infringement, sports corruption, cybercrime and money laundering activities. the proposal to establish strategic cooperation between europol and china, which may concern the exchange of operational, strategic, technical or classified data, is therefore clearly to be supported.
in writing. ‒ the european police office (europol) has a clear operational need to cooperate with china. according to europol, china is becoming increasingly important as a country of origin, destination and transit in the fight against organised crime. in addition, china is home to a number of highly influential organized crime groups. the conclusion of international cooperation agreements with third countries or international organisations shall be approved by the council after consulting parliament. the council has now proposed to approve the agreement on strategic cooperation between china and europol. the agreement excludes the exchange of personal data, so the issue of data protection is not relevant in this case. the report by the committee on civil liberties, justice and home affairs recommends that parliament approve the council's draft as it would help and strengthen the fight against organised crime and contribute to strengthening international law enforcement cooperation. i voted accordingly.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the european parliament's opinion agreeing to the council's approval of the strategic cooperation agreement between europol and the people's republic of china. i took note that europol had already concluded an agreement with a third country (brazil) with the same content. it is clear that china's importance in the fight against international organised crime, its role as a prime source and transit country, including in particular in the areas of international illicit trade and smuggling, the trade in drugs and counterfeit goods, money laundering and cybercrime, is an indispensable partner for the effective protection of european security interests. to this end, the agreement shall facilitate better exploitation of the various possibilities for exchanging methodologies, information and experience. however, i consider it important that the agreement excludes the disclosure of personal data to the other party, so that there should be no concern regarding the protection of data of european citizens in relation to the contract.
in writing. ‒ the strategic agreement between europol and the ministry of public security of the people's republic of china provides for the exchange of information, but excludes the sharing of personal information. i voted in favour of the conclusion of a strategic cooperation agreement between china and europol as it would help in the fight against organised crime and contribute to strengthening international law enforcement cooperation.
my fellow members of the house of representatives! this report is also closely linked to the roots of migration, as it is about the relationship between the european union and africa. i voted in the spirit of what an african university professor, who felt a responsibility for his country and his continent, told me at a conference when i asked him what the european union could do to end the misery in africa. he said that what he could do was to break the multifaceted, corrupt relationship that exists between corrupt european political and economic leaders, western european multinational corporations and corrupt african local leaders, and that is essentially the plundering of africa's natural resources, its raw materials and other resources. europe therefore has a heavy responsibility in the african misery, which cannot be cured by mass immigration of african people.
in writing. ‒ the economic partnership agreement serves the smooth and gradual integration of acp countries into the world economy, in particular the full exploitation of regional integration and south-south trade. the specific activities should be carried out in accordance with the principle of subsidiarity, through regional agreements adapted to specific regional needs and to the common interests of the eu and the region. in assessing the agreement, it should be noted that the vast majority of the acp countries, in terms of population, are african countries with a population approaching one billion, while the caribbean countries have a population of only 39 million and the pacific countries 11 million. so the relationship with africa is crucial to the agreement, not just because of the population, but because it can be a starting point for immigration to europe. it is in europe's fundamental interest to conclude agreements with african countries that would help people to remain in their countries, for example by developing agriculture, industry and trade to meet local needs and by transferring the know-how needed for this purpose free of charge. on the contrary, as the quoted parts of the report show, the main objective is to integrate african countries into the world economy, which in practice means the acquisition of their markets by multinational companies. i abstained from voting on the report.
in writing. ‒ the overall objectives of the cotonou agreement, which provides a contractual framework for relations between the european union and the african, caribbean and pacific group of states (acp), clearly include: reducing and eventually eradicating poverty, in line with the objectives of sustainable development and gradual integration of the acp countries into the world economy. the partnership is based on certain core values and principles, including respect for human rights and fundamental freedoms, democracy based on the rule of law and transparent and accountable governance. unfortunately, progress towards the objectives of poverty reduction and the integration of acp countries into the world economy has been insufficient. this is particularly relevant today, as some acp countries are sending out significant numbers of economic migrants, further complicating the management of the influx of refugees from war zones into europe. the new agreement must be a political project based on the principle of accountability and must clearly leave behind the donor-favoured mentality. i believe that cooperation should be in areas of common interest where mutual benefits are expected, not just in economic terms, but also in peace, security, human rights and the rule of law, good governance and democracy, migration, the environment, climate change. cooperation should contribute to the well-being of the population in both acp and eu member states. in view of the above, i voted in favour of the adoption of the report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the future of acp-eu relations. the report addresses important issues such as the elimination of the donor-beneficiary relationship and the establishment of a relationship based on equality and autonomy. with this new approach, the eu can provide more effective and practical help to tackle the region's pressing problems, such as poverty and social inequalities. the report supports the budgetisation of the european development fund (edf) to provide more targeted and transparent funding for regional initiatives. i agree with the importance of establishing a dialogue and coherent policy coordination. in the light of this, cooperation with the countries of the region (african union, un) should be based on a more open relationship-building approach in the coming period. i believe it is important to support the private sector, also in this respect, by promoting the aforementioned self-reliance. i believe that the development of the region must be supported along these lines, and i have therefore voted in favour of the resolution.
in writing. ‒ as a member of the interparliamentary delegation for africa, the pacific and the caribbean, i voted in favour of the report on the eu-acp relationship. in this context, particular attention should be paid to the issue of migration. with the right link between these regions and the eu, with a well-directed and clear-cut development policy, with humanitarian aid, the causes of migration, such as the threat of war, poverty and mass starvation, can be addressed. the eu has a primary interest in helping locally in cooperation with international organisations to contribute to solving the problem where it arises, rather than bringing it into the union.

in writing. ‒ the african, caribbean and pacific group of states (acp) was established by the georgetown agreement of 1975 and revised in 1992. the partnership agreement between the acp states, of the one part, and the european community and its member states, of the other part, was established by the cotonou agreement, signed in cotonou on 23 june 2000 and revised in 2005 and 2010. in view of the changes that have taken place in the political and economic arenas of the acp group and in the european union since the signing of the cotonou agreement, the development committee report proposes that parliament adopt a resolution calling for a new structure to be adopted to make cooperation more effective and adapt it to new challenges. the draft resolution outlines the considerations to be taken into account in the drafting of the new agreement. i voted for the bill.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of adopting the report and its recommendations, appreciating that it puts a new foundation on cooperation with 79 partner countries under the cotonou agreement, which is due to expire in 2020. i believe that the report contains realistic proposals for a new and more effective framework for cooperation, which takes account of both the eu's united action and the divergences between the partners' situations. i consider it important that, in the context of changing circumstances, it pays particular attention to the effects of climate change and mass impoverishment, as well as to the phenomena closely linked to the global migration crisis. i am convinced that in the years ahead, it will need to engage in even broader and deeper consultation and cooperation with these important partners of the union and its member states than it has done so far.
in writing. ‒ acp-eu cooperation is a valuable and unique achievement that has strengthened the links between the peoples, countries and parliaments of the acp and the eu over the past 40 years; stresses that, in the light of the commitment of the acp countries to act together as a group, in order to increase the efficiency of cooperation and adapt it to new challenges, a new structure should be adopted which places the inherently universal aspects of the acp-eu acquis, such as human rights, gender equality, human development, commitment to good governance and democracy, the objective of the rule of law and the exchange of good practices, in a common framework, while the most important activities should be carried out in accordance with the principle of subsidiarity, i.e. through regional agreements that are specific to the region and are in line with the eu's specific needs and common interests. i voted for the report.

member of the commission. – mr president, i have here some very short concluding remarks but i cannot resist, i would like to react to some of your questions and comments. why are we establishing an eppo which needs to have clear added-value? we see the statistics of olaf: on average only about 40% of the recommendations of olaf are sent to the member states with a clear purpose: investigate and prosecute. we have been saying for years: what can we do? the member states do not prosecute and we cannot remain helpless. we must act here. i am not criticising any specific member state, but this is the general situation. vat: yes, it must be included in pif and the eppo because, besides the many arguments which you have set out here, we have also case law. we have the case which clearly stipulates that vat is a source for the financial budget. with regards to vat, believe me, it is not easy to push the eppo towards its final adoption because we needed to open the second line of negotiations vis-a-vis the ministers of finance and vis-a-vis the tax authorities, because we will need also all these authorities to be on our side. then, especially, when the eppo is working fully, we will need not only national prosecutors, but also the police, tax authorities – and whistle-blowers – to cooperate with the eppo. we will need the cooperation of a very wide and complex puzzle of institutions at the member states’ level. so that is why we need to do this right and in a convincing way so that it will bring real added value. this added value can be, and must be, measured by finance. of course these are the benefits which we speak about: the money which will one day be brought back to national budgets and the eu budget. we are working on setting up the proper threshold for structural funds and agricultural funds and customs: at the moment this is eur 10 000, but we will continue to discuss this. for vat it should be really only a big scope of fraud, so we speak about three or five million euro for cross-border vat fraud. i want to have the eppo doing big things. it should not be established, as i said before, to replace national prosecution; it must do only big things creating big benefits. yes, we need unanimity in the council. so this will need a very strong push in regard to several member states. for me it is clear that the cohesion countries, especially, must be there because it would not be logically if we established the eppo to prosecute fraud on eu funds without having some of the member states which receive the money, which receive more than they contribute. so here i have had, along with my colleagues, a lot of work in some of the member states. the final point: speaking about the benefits. i spoke about the financial benefits, but here we must be fully aware that it is the thrust of the people in europe, taxpayers, at stake. i am always absolutely frustrated when i hear the critics, and i read the articles of the critics of the eu, who say that structural funds are only a source for fraud and corruption. where is all that ethos? this is the policy of solidarity. the rich countries are contributing money to the poorer countries and the critics say it is only there to be stolen and cheated on, and all those benefits, all those good projects, all the jobs and all that prosperity, which has been created over years thanks to this money, is forgotten. i think that we need to act here and to show taxpayers and all those critics that yes, this is the distribution of massive amounts of money, but the money is well managed and controlled. it is our duty to act, and to create the eppo as a really strong, competent and functioning european body. we have three decisive months ahead of us and i count on your support so that we will manage first the negotiations in the council and also the consent in parliament to be achieved in a reasonably short time.
president-in-office of the council. – mr president, i would like to thank the honourable members for all the interventions and statements made which, in my view, clearly show the importance they attach to the establishment of eppo. at the same time, we have heard you highlight many aspects that we need to address in the remaining period of negotiations during the slovak presidency. i would like to make just two points here in my concluding remarks. first of all, it is clear to the presidency that we need to ensure that outstanding reservations are lifted in the period remaining and that the gaps in the text must be addressed properly. i dare say that we are close to finalising the text and getting an agreement on it. we will, of course, include some of the outstanding provisions, like judicial review cooperation between eppo and eurojust, in the new consolidated version. second, as many of you have indicated, it is vital that the eppo regulation be made coherent with the eurojust regulation and with the pif directive. it is clear that we need to make progress on this because the pif directive should contain the substantive law to be applied by eppo. so that message is well taken, mrs gräßle, and the presidency will try to address it in the remaining period. i wish to thank members once again and look forward to further cooperation.
in writing. in shaping the european public prosecutor's office, the council has already watered down the original commission proposal by creating the college of prosecutors, increasing the powers of national prosecutors and weakening the powers of the eppo. but there are a few things that i think neither the commission nor parliament can allow: the eppo should not be allowed to look only at cases that national prosecutors consider to be within the competence of the eppo, but should look at all cases in order to examine their actual competence. in any event, vat should remain in the protection of the financial interests of the union (pif) directive and thus fall under the jurisdiction of the general prosecutor's office. it is therefore not permissible for the prosecution to have jurisdiction only in cases where the union's share exceeds 50%, since the european interest of vat is necessarily below the above threshold. vat, as the court of justice has recognised, is an own financial resource of the union and, as such, it must be able to protect it effectively, especially when crossborder vat fraud schemes are widespread in many eu countries and cannot or do not want to be effectively detected by the authorities of the member states. failing that, the commission should withdraw its proposal and, where appropriate, consider giving the european union anti-fraud office appropriate powers instead of a public prosecutor's office.

in writing. ‒ the hague convention of 25 october 1980 on the civil aspects of illegal removal of children has established a system which allows for cooperation between contracting states to find a solution to the problem of illegal removal of children. the biggest problem in such cases is the national nature of the legal systems of the states. the convention aims to resolve such situations at international level by stipulating that the law of the state of the child's residence is applicable and that the case falls within the jurisdiction of the court of that state. the convention also establishes a system to ensure the immediate return of children who have been illegally removed. the eu currently has exclusive external competence in this area, as confirmed by the court of justice in opinion 1/13. the member states can therefore no longer act on their own. the problem arises from the fact that the convention does not provide for the autonomous action of international organisations, and thus, following the accession of peru to the convention, a council decision is required authorising two member states austria and romania which have not yet accepted peru's accession to accept peru's accession. this will allow the entry into force of the convention between peru and the european union as a whole. in view of the above, i voted in favour of the adoption of the report.

in writing. ‒ the hague convention of 25 october 1980 on the civil aspects of the removal of children establishes a system which allows for cooperation between contracting states to find a solution to the problem of the removal of children. the biggest problem in such cases is the national nature of the legal systems of the states. the convention aims to resolve such situations at international level by stipulating that the law of the state of the child's residence is applicable and that the case falls within the jurisdiction of the court of that state. the convention also establishes a system to ensure the immediate return of children who have been illegally removed. the eu currently has exclusive external competence in this area, as confirmed by the court of justice in opinion 1/13. the member states can therefore no longer act on their own. the problem arises from the fact that the convention does not provide for the autonomous action of international organisations, and thus, following the accession of peru to the convention, a council decision is required authorising two member states austria and romania which have not yet accepted peru's accession to accept peru's accession. this will allow the entry into force of the convention between peru and the european union as a whole. in view of the above, i voted in favour of the report.
in writing. ‒ the hague convention of 25 october 1980 on the civil aspects of the removal of children establishes a system which allows for cooperation between contracting states to find a solution to the problem of the removal of children and which ensures the immediate return of the child who has been removed. the convention has been ratified by all the member states of the european union. peru has notified its intention to accede to the convention. since the convention does not provide for independent action by international organisations, the european union cannot ratify an amendment to the treaty to that effect. however, since the opinion of the european court of justice of 14 october 2014 states that the eu currently has exclusive external competence in this area, those member states which have not yet ratified this supplement (austria and romania) will now only be able to do so with the authorisation of the european council. the council therefore intends to adopt a decision authorising austria and romania to ratify the accession of peru, subject to consultation of the parliament. in its report, the committee on legal affairs recommends that parliament approve the council's proposal for a decision. i voted accordingly.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of parliament's approval of the proposal because i am convinced that this will also strengthen the international protection of children who are illegally taken abroad. i am aware that the relevant hague convention has proved to be one of the most widespread and in practice successful international legal instruments over the past three decades, often and actively used by states parties as a legal basis for establishing jurisdiction and conducting proceedings in respect of children who have found themselves in difficult and contentious situations following the divorce of their parents. the eu currently has exclusive external competence to act in such matters, but for the new states acceding to the convention, member state ratification or a corresponding council decision is required for the entry into force of the between peru and the eu, as appropriate. given that the hague convention can be made more effective the more states that join the system, i welcome peru's accession.

mr president i was very pleased to see the term "food self-sufficiency" in the world food and food security report. we've long known that the solution to hunger is food sovereignty, which conceals the fact that every nation, every community has the right to control and use its own land, and that's why it's illegal for foreigners or even domestic oligarchs to take it. and part of food self-determination is that every nation, every community has the right to grow its own food. i must therefore say that this objective, which is rightly stated in this report, is in direct opposition to what the european union is doing in the opposite direction, for example with the free trade agreements with either canada or the united states, which are in direct opposition to bringing food from far away to europe.
in writing. ‒ the resolution is surprisingly firm and almost radical in its support for concepts such as food self-determination. the text makes several references to the importance of this, particularly for developing countries. unfortunately, the reference is nowhere connected to the counterproductive nature of global food trade. a few years ago, the world organization of family farmers, via campesina, so clearly and so specifically addressed the global problem of hunger and malnutrition. the hungry today were once small farmers who could feed themselves, and they were ruined by the influx of cheap food from richer countries, which was only caused by subsidies. the draft fails to recognise that hunger and malnutrition are systemic problems (capital's resource-sucking role) that cannot be permanently remedied by aid and political rhetoric. the adoption of the text of the motion for a resolution will have profound consequences. if the commission or the council wish to maintain this, it will only be possible if free trade agreements are revised. i voted for the motion.
in writing. ‒ my vote on the report was based on two main considerations: firstly, in order to significantly reduce or eliminate economic migration, developing countries need to promote the production of the necessary quantity and quality of food on the ground in a way that is sustainable in the long term, with minimal environmental pollution and the efficient use of natural resources. on the other hand, in accordance with the hungarian basic law, i oppose the use of gmo seeds, the trade of products produced in this way.
in writing. the problems are systemic, the result of world trade and agricultural support systems, that small farmers who once supported themselves, their families, their small communities, are now starving. only the end of land grabbing and food self-sufficiency can be a real alternative. indeed, quality and organic food can also be produced in small farms, so the waste of food must be stopped and the processes reversed. the resolution is clearly worthy of support.
in writing. ‒ the committee on development's motion for a parliament resolution deals with global nutrition and food security. it focuses on the importance of breastfeeding for human development and future life chances, food waste the european union produces a total of 88 million tonnes of food waste a year, while 842 million people worldwide, 12 per cent of the world's population, go hungry the priority of local food production, support for smallholder farmers and women farmers as food producers, access to arable land, the effects of producing food crop-based biofuels and the right to water. it recalls the commission's commitment to spend eur 3,5 billion to reduce the backwardness by at least eur 7 million by 2025 and expects the commission to honour this commitment. i voted in favour of the draft resolution.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the motion because i believe that we need global solutions to ensure the world's food and food security. international organizations and governments are working to end malnutrition and hunger by 2030. all this can be achieved by increasing productivity, sustainable and climate-resilient agriculture and food production. the aim of eliminating child hunger, which is also found in the eu, is also mentioned as an explicit objective in the recommendations of international organisations. the european union therefore needs to put things right before the issue can be resolved. the hungarian government first started to report poverty statistics in increasingly incomplete form since 2010, and then simply changed the way it calculated them. it hides the identities of disadvantaged families, the elderly, starving children, making it much harder to solve. i believe that making compulsory the use of uniform european statistics on children and pensioners would help to put an end to this blood-curdling practice. during the debate on the motion i also said that high taxes on food not only deepen poverty and make it harder to access food, but also that there is a significant amount of vat fraud in the eu due to differences in the tax burden. but there is a solution to this, and that is to harmonise food taxes at eu level.
in writing. ‒ coordinated and accelerated action is needed to end malnutrition in order to meet the 2030 agenda and to achieve sustainable development goal 2 on ending hunger. one third of the food produced worldwide, some 1.3 billion tons, is wasted, while 842 million people worldwide - 12 percent of the world's population - go hungry. the commission must fulfil its obligations and ensure appropriate forms of assistance to eradicate hunger, in accordance with its mandate. i supported the resolution.

in writing. ‒ the proposal supports the establishment of an efficient and independent european public prosecutor's office to reduce the current fragmentation of national law enforcement efforts to protect the eu budget, thereby strengthening the fight against fraud in the european union. the vat abuse is indicated as the reference base. the main problem with the proposal is that a european public prosecutor would be a prominent organisational tool in the process of integration, which seeks to gradually abolish national sovereignty, and could be misused later on against those who act and act against the interests of the eu, not just against the misuse of eu funds. in 2013, the hungarian parliament found the concept of the european public prosecutor's office to be in breach of the principle of subsidiarity and adopted a resolution to that effect. despite its purpose, i did not support the proposal because of the potential for abuse and the erosion of the sovereignty of the member states.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution on the european public prosecutor's office, which the green group was involved in drafting and which reaffirms parliament's position ahead of the next meeting of the justice and home affairs council on the public prosecutor's office. the motion for a resolution confirms, inter alia, that the office of the prosecutor-general should have a view on all matters that may fall within its competence for any reason; that vat matters, like eu own resources, should fall within the competence of the office of the prosecutor-general.
in writing. ‒ a joint motion for a resolution was tabled on this issue by the ppe, s&d, alde and verts/ale groups. the draft proposes to strengthen parliament's commitment to the establishment of an efficient and independent european public prosecutor's office in order to reduce the current fragmentation of national law enforcement efforts to protect the eu budget, thereby strengthening the fight against fraud in the european union. it urges the council to speed up the preparation of the regulation establishing the european public prosecutor's office. i voted for the motion.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution on the european public prosecutor's office and eurojust, which reaffirms parliament's support for the establishment of an effective and independent european public prosecutor's office (eppo). the prosecution of crimes against the union budget is currently the exclusive competence of the member states. this fragmentation is highly damaging as it prevents the investigating and prosecuting authorities of the member states from ensuring the same level of protection and prosecution. i therefore support the motion calling on the council to step up its efforts to reach agreement on the draft directive on combating fraud affecting the financial interests of the union by means of criminal law (pif) and to resume negotiations with parliament to establish the eppo. it is also appropriate that the eppo should have primary competence for the offences defined in the pif directive and should also have competence for cases where union funding exceeds eur 10 000, but does not amount to 50% or more of the co-financing. the eppo should be able to take effective action against any criminal offence affecting the union budget.

madam president, i apologise for the slight confusion. let me begin by saying outright that, of course it goes without saying, that the epp supports transparency. but transparency is actually a much more complex issue than it appears at first sight. i think at the heart of it is the problem of the relationship with transparency and trust. it is not clear cut; it is not automatic; it is not a direct, either causal or correlative, relationship. indeed, the complexity is such that there is a lot of argument to suggest that the greater the transparency, the lower the trust, because why should people trust if they already have everything written down? indeed, there are many people – i do not know if it is a majority or a minority – who say, if this much can be made transparent there must be something else that is hidden. it is, therefore, an ongoing, probably an infinitely repeatable process which can never be reached. and therefore i would say that if we are talking about transparency there has to be a finite quality to it, which i do not actually see at this particular time. so, the culture of trust is something that has to be more important, should supersede in some ways transparency itself, in order to generate the necessary trust in the institutions. now i would go on to say that actually, from what i see, the central difficulty is the remoteness of all the institutions of the european union from the citizens. here, and the vice-president we will know what i am about to say, what is happening to the european citizens’ initiative, which is a way of building trust, separately from transparency? i would also add here the problem of security. too much openness makes people vulnerable to the various security services, who are very busy indeed in brussels, in strasbourg and who knows where else. lobbying register, yes, i think that is absolutely right. it is not a silver bullet. i think there is no silver bullet, but at the centre of the problem is legitimacy. how can the european union generate and build on its existing legitimacy, which is a little bit thin in certain parts of the world?

mr president when it comes to voting on a report related to international financial reporting standards, voters who know me may rightly ask, on what basis am i even going to vote on this issue, since i'm not an economist, i'm not a financial expert. but every day, as a lawyer and as a representative, i meet people who suffer from the effects of banking speculation. so the financial economist who helps me with the voter rolls, i ask him to give me some professional advice that will ultimately reduce the possibility of speculation. so, we have a systemic problem here, international financial speculation. as long as the neoliberal financial economic system that is currently in place in the world is in place, it will not be abolished, but because we thought, together with my experts, that these standards could reduce speculation, i voted for the report.
in writing. ‒ the global financial crisis that began in 2008 has put the role of international financial reporting standards in financial stability and growth, in particular the accounting of losses realised in the banking system, on the agenda of the g20 and the eu. the commission notes that the bank's financial statements were not updated in the course of the financial crisis, as accounting standards before the crisis did not function properly, for example resulting in procyclicality in the accounting of profit and loss, i.e. underestimating the accumulation of risks during the recovery phase of the cycle, and there was no common and transparent methodology for the valuation of illiquid and impaired assets. the resolution calls for the international financial reporting standards to be put on a new footing. in my view, this regulation does not eliminate the possibility of financial crises, because it is fundamentally linked to the liberalisation of the financial sector and the subsequent concentration, but it can to some extent curb speculation, and therefore i supported the adoption of the regulation despite my reservations.
in writing. ‒ the european commission intends to adopt a regulation amending regulation (ec) no 1126/2008 adopting certain international accounting standards with regard to ifrs 9. on 26 september 2016, mr roberto gualtieri, member of the european parliament, submitted a question to the commission for an oral answer on behalf of the economic and monetary committee on the possible negative impact of ifrs 9 on long-term investments and financial stability. the draft opinion of the economic and monetary committee points out that, partly due to the lack of reliable data, there is a lack of impact assessments on ifrs 9 and therefore calls for a better understanding of the impact of ifrs 9 on the banking sector, the insurance sector and financial markets in general, and the financial sector as a whole. it is also concerned that the accounting treatment of certain financial instruments held directly or indirectly as long-term investments under ifrs 9 may be contrary to the objective of promoting long-term investments. it therefore considers that further studies, analyses and ex post evaluations are necessary. i voted in favour of the draft resolution.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution on international financial reporting standards. the new ifrs 9 standards aim to improve the financial reporting of financial assets by addressing problems that have emerged during the crisis. the draft motion rightly points out that the commitment to better regulation certainly requires an impact assessment. i also agree with the finding that there is a need to further examine the practical impact of ifrs 9 on the banking and insurance sector and the financial sector in general. overall, the new standards, as the draft proposal highlights, should serve the eu's long-term objectives.

in writing. ‒ the european union adopted the resolution for the next un climate conference. this will be a follow-up to last year’s paris agreement. i welcome the decision of the european parliament on the ratification of the paris agreement. we greens call on the eu to commit to further emissions reductions for 2030. now we will need action and implementation, but it is a good sign that the european union will be able to stand firmly in marrakesh and will stay a key player in fighting climate change.
in writing. ‒ the fight against global warming was previously aimed at limiting the global average temperature to 2°c above pre-industrial levels. however, all parties to the kyoto protocol have committed to limiting this to much lower levels and to making further efforts to limit the temperature increase to 1.5°c. another objective is to balance anthropogenic emissions from different sources and removals of greenhouse gases by sinks in the second half of the century. the report by the committee on the environment, public health and food safety looks at the global efforts to achieve these objectives and the possibilities for the european union to contribute to them to the greatest extent possible. i voted for the bill.
in writing. ‒ the motion for a resolution aims to summarise the european parliament's positions for the marrakesh climate conference in november. it raises specific topics such as urging the ratification of the paris agreement, the pre-2020 ambitions and kyoto protocol, the cop22 negotiating priorities, the role of non-state actors, a comprehensive effort across all sectors, non-co2 emission reductions, climate finance, climate resilience and adaptation, and climate diplomacy. i share the view that there is scientific evidence that warming and change in the climate system is occurring, and that the main cause of this is accelerated human activity since the middle of the 20th century. with this proposal, i urge all countries to accelerate the transition to near-zero greenhouse gas emissions and climate resilience as agreed in the paris agreement, in order to avoid the worst impacts of global warming. the agreement therefore encourages a shift of investments away from fossil fuel-related investments towards low-carbon and safe investments. the european union must also play a leading role in the conciliation process, which is why i voted in favour of the motion. i am pleased that the relevant eu institutions have also ratified the paris agreement, so that the climate summit in morocco can rightly be called a 'party to the agreement'.
mr president the bucket is a bucket, a conspiracy theory, a conspiracy theory. but as more conspiracy theories are revealed to be true, it was a shame to laugh so much at those who spread them. it's also the fact that our food, the food we eat, the food we're forced to eat, the food we eat on a daily basis, is potentially life-threatening. as this report, the schaldemose report, shows, the contaminants in the food we eat can cause cancer, can cause fertility problems, can cause chronic diseases, because of hormones that go into the food, because of packaging that contaminates the food for too long. well, of course, for too long when food comes from the other side of the world. i find it very tragic that on the one hand the european parliament is constantly negotiating these free trade agreements, and on the other hand it is trying to reduce the damage and disaster caused by them. the foundations should be shut down.
in writing. ‒ wrapping paper, kitchen and eating utensils used in everyday life are regularly in contact with food. when they come into contact, their components are transferred to food. these chemicals can be harmful to human health and can alter the composition of food. the european union has established a general safety regime and has introduced specific safety rules in four areas: plastics, ceramics, regenerated cellulose and active and intelligent materials. member states are given the possibility to introduce similar special rules in several areas. however, this leads to different product safety rules, which may create barriers to the internal market. the european union aims to harmonise regulations and to develop further specific eu regulations. it is also important to address the shortcomings in the implementation of the legislation in force. the european union aims to preserve and protect the health of consumers and to ensure the efficient functioning of the internal market. to this end, the european parliament calls for a review of the existing framework regulation. in view of all this, i voted in favour of the report.
in writing. ‒ food contact materials are widely used in everyday life for food packaging, as well as in the form of kitchen utensils, cutlery, etc. these substances are subject to legally binding rules at union level, laid down in framework regulation (ec) no 1935/2004. it lays down general safety requirements applicable to all substances and articles which may come into contact with food, but also provides for the possibility of adopting specific measures for 17 substances listed in annex i to the framework regulation. however, only four of these materials have been subject to specific measures at union level so far: plastics, ceramics, regenerated cellulose and active and intelligent materials. for other materials that come into contact with food (e.g. paper and paperboard, metals and alloys, glass, coatings, silicones, rubbers and printing inks), member states may adopt specific measures at national level. the absence of specific union measures for most of the substances listed in annex i has led to restrictions on the internal market and to a loss of competitiveness and innovation. the draft resolution of the committee on the environment, public health and food safety cautiously urges further harmonisation at eu level of the 13 non-harmonised substances, giving priority to those that pose particular risks to human health or are in greater demand on the eu market. i voted for the report.
in writing. ‒ food contact materials include not only food packaging but also kitchen utensils, cutlery, etc. in contact with food depending on their composition and properties these substances may transfer their constituents to food and the constituents may harm human health or alter the composition of food. this process is known and therefore food contact materials are already regulated at eu level by a framework regulation (1935/2004/ec). it sets general safety requirements for 17 substances and there is a specific eu action for four others (plastics, ceramics, regenerated cellulose and active and intelligent materials). for other food contact materials, member states are currently able to adopt specific measures at national level, so there are still many gaps and gaps in standards that hinder innovation. i therefore agree that the current legislation needs to be amended, not only by broadening the material scale, but also in details such as risk assessment, traceability, compliance and control. i also agree with the report that joint action is needed for substances that do not pose a health risk in order to improve controllability. i believe that the provision of healthy food is in our common interest and i have therefore voted in favour of the report.
mr president i would like to briefly describe the tenth section of the report on monitoring the application of eu law, which may be of particular concern to hungarians. he says that member states should avoid making eu rules unnecessarily burdensome when applying eu law, as this leads to misunderstanding of the eu's legislative activity and increases unjustified eu scepticism among citizens. we hungarians want to be very careful not to create unjustified eu-skepticism, so we interpret all the european union norms that want to extend the competence of brussels and the union to determine who we have to live with on our own land, how many migrants we have to accept, or how many, what mass of migrants the union wants to settle in our country. so we're trying to meet the expectations perfectly.
in writing. ‒ the proposal assesses the commission's 2014 report on the application of eu law. the report concludes that member states are unable to meet the unrealistic implementation deadlines for legislation, leading to tacit acceptance of delayed application; calls on the european institutions to agree on a more appropriate timetable for implementing regulations and directives. the proposal calls for the commission to be more active in combating the misapplication of directives. the proposal to force integration is permeated by concerns about the weakening of the effectiveness of eu law, which the rapporteur believes is 'systemically undermined by the fact that it is not applied properly by the member states and by the inadequate monitoring by the commission'. the main message of the report is that the enforcement of eu law in the member states needs to be made even more effective, and that it is therefore strongly pro-integration and therefore not acceptable from a eurorealist point of view. the previous report included at least some system-critical elements, which are essentially missing here. in view of these considerations, i did not support the motion.
in writing. ‒ the motion for a resolution summarises in a professional and comprehensive way the current state of play, the results and the problems of the application of eu law, and i therefore voted in favour of the adoption of the report.
in writing. the greek representative who wrote the previous report had a much better sense of democracy and was therefore more critical of the system itself, for understandable reasons. the report is not acceptable on the basis of european realism, because it blindly relies on the commission. his financial-economic approach is also based on the repeatedly failed neoliberalism. the fact that parliament still has very little access to information on the eu pilot procedure and on pending cases severely limits the possibilities for meps. it is therefore very difficult to assess whether the decrease in the number of formal infringement procedures is due to compromise solutions between the commission and the member states or rather to the fact that member states are better complying with eu law.
in writing. ‒ i supported the adoption of the report because it gives an accurate picture and makes remarkable findings and recommendations on the experience of implementing eu law two years ago. it points to the key role of the commission in the control but also recalls that the ultimate responsibility for implementing eu law lies with the member states. the report welcomed some improvements in this respect in 2014, mainly reflecting a decrease in the number of infringement procedures. i also agree with the specific proposal that in future the commission should examine more closely the compliance of associated and candidate countries with eu law on the same basis as the member states. as the hungarian representative, i also considered this report to be particularly appropriate for drawing appropriate lessons for the future in the light of the fact that recently the government of the eu member state hungary, in relation to an important eu policy or community decision (regulation of migration), has made a direct, provocative challenge to the eu legal order, principles and practice: in a referendum campaign, it called on its population to reject the primacy of community law, to reclaim the competence of national decision-making. on this basis, i will be increasingly of the opinion that european law needs to be protected urgently, and that the commission should choke off the seeds of such a legal policy before it can unleash its disruptive effect on eu law.
in writing. ‒ the objections are based on the fact that the commission has submitted a draft implementing act for the five gm maize and cotton plants in question which does not impose any restrictions on the marketing and use of these gm plants. the parliament and the envi committee consider that the commission has exceeded its powers by these acts and would allow the import and marketing of these products in the european union without respect for the precautionary principle. unfortunately, the efsa studies do not contain sufficient data and information to show that these plants are harmless to human health. i supported the adoption of the motions to withdraw the european commission's authorisation implementation plans.
in writing. ‒ in accordance with the hungarian basic law and the precautionary principle, i oppose the authorisation of gmo products and consider that the draft commission implementing decision is not in line with union law as it is incompatible with the objective of regulation (ec) no 1829/2003, which, in accordance with the general principles laid down in regulation (ec) no 178/2002, is to serve as a basis for a high level of protection of human life and health, animal health and welfare, the environment and consumer interests with regard to genetically modified food and feed, while ensuring the effective functioning of the internal market. the report calls on the commission to withdraw its draft implementing decision, and i therefore voted in favour of adopting the report.
in writing. bt11 maize produces cry1ab toxin, which is a bt protein similar to the toxin of mon 810. this gives it the ability to defend itself against different species of lepidoptera. it also expresses the pat protein, which confers tolerance to the herbicide glufosinate ammonium. the available scientific knowledge provides sufficient grounds to assume that in-house lines and hybrids from maize line containing the bt11 gene structure pose a risk to the environment. in view of all this, in accordance with the hungarian basic law and the precautionary principle, i do not support the authorisation of gm products.

in writing. the most basic human right is the right to health and to healthy food. the resolution rightly points out that the commission disregards eu law when it intends to place various gm seeds on the market. and in accordance with the precautionary principle, that cannot happen. most member states prohibit the spread of gmos by their national laws or by their basic laws. the commission's attitude is worrying, at a time when large masses are rightly protesting against the conclusion of ceta and ttip.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution of the european parliament on the draft commission implementing decision concerning the placing on the market of genetically modified maize bt11 (syn-btø11-1) for cultivation. a marketing notification for bt11 maize was submitted by syngenta seeds sas (formerly novartis seeds) to the competent french authorities in 1996 and again in 2003. this corn contains the cry1ab protein and the pat protein, which provides resistance to glufosinate-ammonium herbicides. this herbicide, on the other hand, is considered to be a reproductive toxicant and should be phased out by the end of 2017. according to the european food safety authority (efsa), vertical wind movements or gusts of wind experienced during pollination can transport pollen up to several kilometres. the commission draft implementing decision requires a minimum isolation distance of 5 metres between bt11 maize fields and protected habitats, despite the fact that efsa clearly states that a 20 metre isolation distance around a protected habitat would be recommended. efsa also stated that the risk assessment of the cultivation is incomplete. i therefore agree that the draft commission implementing decision is beyond its powers and that the efsa recommendations are therefore not appropriate.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the draft commission implementing decision on the placing on the market of seeds of genetically modified maize 1507 (das-ø15ø7-1) for cultivation. the resolution describes how in 2001 pioneer overseas corporation and dow agrosciences europe notified the competent spanish authorities of the placing on the market of 1507 genetically modified maize. this maize contains the cry1f protein from bacillus for the control of pests and produces the pat protein which provides tolerance to glufosinate-ammonium herbicides. since glufosinate is considered a substance harmful to reproduction, the exclusion criteria for substances already authorised should apply when the authorisation is to be renewed. in addition, the efsa scientific panel on gmos identified as a concern for the cultivation of maize 1507 the possible development of resistance to cry1f in the targeted insects of the order of butterflies, as the development of resistance could lead to a change in the defence against the insects, which could have a detrimental environmental impact. the commission has defined in its draft implementing decision a lower isolation distance than that which efsa has identified as clearly proven. for these reasons, i agree that the draft commission implementing decision goes beyond the defined implementing powers and that the risk assessment of the cultivation by efsa is deficient.
in writing. ‒ in accordance with the hungarian basic law and the precautionary principle, i oppose the authorisation of gmo products and consider that the draft commission implementing decision is not in line with union law as it is incompatible with the objective of regulation (ec) no 1829/2003, which, in accordance with the general principles laid down in regulation (ec) no 178/2002, is to serve as a basis for a high level of protection of human life and health, animal health and welfare, the environment and consumer interests with regard to genetically modified food and feed, while ensuring the effective functioning of the internal market. the report calls on the commission to withdraw its draft implementing decision, and i therefore voted in favour of adopting the report.
in writing. domestic scientific evidence has shown that the persistent presence of mon810 maize in the ecosystem under investigation may have adverse effects. it produces 1500 to 2000 times more bt-toxin than is released from the bt-toxin containing plant protection product dipel in a single treatment under conventional plant protection. furthermore, the remains of the bt plants decayed more slowly than the non-toxin producing lines. after harvesting, 8% of the toxin produced by the plant remained in the area, and a significant amount of this active toxin was detected in the soil 11 months later. in our view, the available scientific knowledge provides sufficient grounds to assume that domestic lines and hybrids from maize line containing the mon 810 gene structure pose a risk to the environment. in view of all this, in accordance with the hungarian basic law and the precautionary principle, i do not support the authorisation of gm products.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the draft commission implementing decision on the renewal of the authorisation for the placing on the market for cultivation of genetically modified maize mon 810 (mon-øø81ø-6) in the european parliament. the proposal describes that on 11 and 18 april 2007 monsanto europe s.a. submitted three applications to the commission for the renewal of the marketing authorisations for foods, food ingredients and feed currently produced from mon 810 maize. on 9 march 2016, monsanto europe s.a. sent a letter to the commission requesting that the part of the application concerning cultivation be treated separately from the rest of the application. this genetically modified maize contains the cry1ab protein from the sub-species bacillus thuringiensis kurstaki, which confers resistance to certain pests of the order of butterflies. according to the european food safety authority (efsa), evidence shows that between 95 and 99% of pollen emissions are deposited up to 50 metres from the pollen source, but that vertical winds or wind gusts can release dispersing pollen into the atmosphere and travel significant distances, up to several kilometres. i agree that the draft commission implementing decision exceeds the implementing powers provided for in regulation (ec) no 1829/2003 and that the efsa assessment of the cultivation is incomplete. the resolution therefore calls on the commission to withdraw its implementing regulation.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution on the placing on the market of genetically modified maize mon 810 (mon-øø81ø-6). the proposal describes that on 11 and 18 april 2007 monsanto europe s.a. submitted three applications to the commission for the renewal of the marketing authorisations for foods, food ingredients and feed currently produced from mon 810 maize. this maize contains a cry1ab protein derived from the bacillus, which provides resistance to certain pests of the order of butterflies. member states expressed concerns that there are no long-term feeding and toxicity studies and that the risk assessment is not adequate. it has become a general decision-making practice, also exceptional, for genetically modified (gm) food and feed to send the dossier back to the commission for final approval. the fundamental problem is that while production necessarily takes place in the territory of a member state, trade in gmos is cross-border, which means that the ban on national sales and use proposed by the commission could not be enforced without the reintroduction of import border controls. i therefore agree that the draft commission implementing decision does not comply with union law, does not provide a basis for a high level of protection of human life and health, animal health and welfare, the environment and consumer interests with regard to genetically modified food and feed.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the draft commission implementing decision authorising the placing on the market of products containing, consisting of, or produced from genetically modified cotton 281-24-236 × 3006-210-23 × mon 88913 (das-24236-5×das-21ø23-5×mon-88913-8). on 12 march 2009, dow agrosciences europe submitted to the competent authority of the netherlands an application for the placing on the market of foods, food ingredients, and feed containing, consisting of, or produced from the abovementioned cotton. this cotton contains the protein phosphinotricin acetyltransferase (pat) which provides resistance to glufosinate-ammonium-containing herbicides. it also contains the proteins cry1f and cry1ac, which provide protection against some pests. glyphosate was classified as a substance likely to cause cancer in humans in 2015 and, since the entry into force of regulation (ec) no 1829/2003, authorisation decisions have been adopted by the commission in accordance with the applicable legislation without the opinions of the member state committees. the legislative proposal to amend regulation (ec) no 1829/2003 was rejected by parliament in 2015 on the grounds that while production necessarily takes place in the territory of a member state, trade in gmos is cross-border, meaning that the ban on national 'sale and use' proposed by the commission could not be enforced without reintroducing import border controls. i agree that the draft commission implementing decision goes beyond the implementing powers provided for in regulation (eu) no 1829/2003, and therefore i voted in favour of the proposal.

mr president the rapporteur rightly draws attention to the importance of preventing organised crime and corruption from entering the legal order of individual states and, of course, their economies. however, it should be noted that the current european legal and instrumental framework is not able to deal with the phenomenon of corruption being systematised by a particular political regime or government for its own power and the personal enrichment of its leaders, surrounded by self-interested legislation, as if legitimising the quasi-state corruption network. today, the hungarian economy is suffering most obviously from this, to which the eu legal order does not find a meaningful answer. for example, olaf is unable to investigate and uncover a corruption case involving european funds if it has to be referred for further action to the national authority or prosecutor whose head, possibly because of his relationship with the victim, is the personal beneficiary of the crime. the establishment of the european public prosecutor's office is an important and urgent task which can provide a partial answer to such legal challenges, but only joint action by member states against such governments can be effective, assuming the full unity and political determination of the european council.
the rapporteur. mr president, honourable members of the commission, ladies and gentlemen, i would like to take this opportunity to present to you, in the interest of reporting, a report on liquefied natural gas and natural gas storage. i am proud to say that together with the shadow rapporteurs we have succeeded in creating a comprehensive framework that will be able to promote the development of european gas markets in the long term and support security of supply. this strategy is not a stand-alone strategy but an integral part of the system established by previous decisions of the parliament. it is consistent with the objectives of the energy union package and takes into account the other reports of the gas winter package. i believe that only within this framework can such work be undertaken, and we have acted accordingly. when we prepared the report, we had the following objectives in mind: to stimulate competition in the market to reduce consumer prices, to promote security of supply by increasing diversification, and last but not least, to always keep sustainability in mind. the report covers many important topics, but let me highlight those which i believe are the most important of these: first of all, of course, the situation of the vulnerable member states must be settled. it is essential to show solidarity with those member states which have no alternative and can only source natural gas from one source. adequate storage capacity can help these countries for a while, but the only long-term solution is diversification of resources, of which lng is a great tool. the second major issue is infrastructure. in order to improve the use of existing tools, we must first connect the isolated networks. the european commission's list of priority projects includes investments that could create these links and address the most problematic bottlenecks. in summary, in order to make the most of the investments we have, we must first make the ones we have not. and third, we have to highlight that the physical infrastructure, the hardware itself is not enough without the software. and software, in this case, is tariffs, standards, procedures. their coordination is as important as physical connection. in addition to these topics, we also discussed the role of lng in transport and decarbonisation, and the potential of the european union as an active player in the international natural gas market. in conclusion, i would like to express my sincere thanks to all those who contributed to this report, in particular the shadow rapporteurs. i believe that without the cooperation of the factions, we could not have achieved so much. my fellow members of parliament! i believe that this report deserves our support, because it draws on the initiatives of all the political groups and incorporates the ideas of each of them, so that we can say that it is a real compromise and another decisive step towards the common goal of the energy union. thank you very much for your attention.

rapporteur for the opinion of the committee on constitutional affairs. – madam president, thank you vice-president and also incidentally very much my thanks to the rapporteur and everybody else who has worked very hard on this dossier. a human rights mechanism has three necessary conditions to meet if it is to be successful, and this is what i would very much like to see myself. first of all, it must have a legal base, giving it immunity from political interference. it follows that this mechanism will only acquire legitimacy if it is not used to target member states in order to punish them. secondly, the mechanism must be completely even-handed as between member states. the slightest hint of different treatment will delegitimise it, so no cherry picking, no opportunistic targeting. this, of course, will require continuous monitoring. the third is consistency of implementation, but here a balance has to be struck between subsidiarity and all european practice. too much of the latter runs a danger of centralisation – the jacobin temptation. if the jacobins get their way, there is no chance at all that the rule-of-law culture will take root in the european union.

in writing. ‒ the recommendation adopted today on the agreement between the european union and the people's republic of china on the short-stay visa waiver for holders of diplomatic passports contributes to the deepening of diplomatic relations with china. the agreement provides for visa-free travel for up to 90 days in any 180-day period for citizens of the union holding a valid diplomatic passport or eu 'laissez-passer', and for citizens of china holding a valid diplomatic passport to enter the union under similar conditions. the agreement takes eu-china relations to a new level and i therefore vote in favour of adopting the recommendation as a member of the fidesz people's party delegation.
in writing. ‒ by its decision of 14 september 2015, the council authorised the commission to open negotiations with the people's republic of china and to develop negotiating directives for an agreement on the short-stay visa waiver for holders of diplomatic passports. the negotiations began on 21 september and took the form of an exchange of written notes. the parties initialled the agreement on 3 and 4 november 2015 respectively. on 26 january 2016, the council adopted a decision on the ratification of the agreement, subject to the assent of the european parliament. the agreement provides for visa-free travel for up to 90 days in any 180-day period to the territory of the other contracting party by citizens of the union holding a valid diplomatic passport or eu 'laissez-passer' and by citizens of china holding a valid diplomatic passport. the provisions of the agreement shall not apply to the united kingdom and ireland and, in the case of france and the netherlands, shall apply only to the european territories of those two states. the report of the committee on civil liberties, justice and home affairs recommends that parliament give its consent to the conclusion of the agreement. i voted accordingly.

in writing. ‒ the financial and economic crisis and the subsequent austerity measures have put pressure on national budgets. countries with budgetary problems may have difficulty in securing sufficient resources for the national co-financing of cohesion policy programmes. in order to ensure the smooth use of the cohesion funds, member states experiencing temporary budgetary difficulties are assisted and given financial assistance under the common provisions regulation (cpr). from 1 january 2014 to 30 june 2016, greece, cyprus, ireland, romania and portugal were eligible for this additional payment. the financial assistance programmes for cyprus, ireland, portugal and romania expired during this period, greece being the only country still benefiting from the assistance programme. in view of the continued fragility of the greek economy, the commission proposed that the additional aid be continued. as the commission's proposal represents a targeted and budget-neutral solution for member states facing temporary liquidity problems, i voted in favour of the parliament's report in the plenary vote.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report because i agree that the financial and economic crisis puts member states under considerable pressure and that pan-european interests must be taken into account in this case. in many member states, the european structural and investment funds are the only source of investment due to the crisis, and national co-financing of cohesion policy projects can also be a problem. the report amends certain provisions of regulation (eu) no 1303/2013 relating to the financial management of member states experiencing or threatened with serious difficulties with respect to financial stability. under article 24 of the regulation, several member states were entitled to an increased payment, of which only greece is now covered by the adjustment programme until the end of 2018. these changes will ensure the smooth implementation of the eu's main financial instrument, the european structural and investment funds (esifs), and will provide a targeted and budget-neutral solution to the two member states experiencing temporary liquidity problems.

in writing. ‒ member jane collins has applied for the preservation of her privileges and immunities in connection with the ongoing criminal proceedings in the queen's bench division of the high court in london. in his request, he claims that the timetable of the legal proceedings against him prevented him from travelling to parliamentary sittings, but the legal affairs committee points out in its report that article 7 of the protocol on the privileges and immunities of the european union, to which mr collins refers, does not apply to restrictions resulting from legal proceedings. the mep also claims that meps cannot be investigated, detained or prosecuted for opinions or votes they have given in the course of their duties. in its report, the committee on legal affairs notes that the civil action for damages for defamation and libel brought against jane collins in the united kingdom concerns allegations made by the member at a party conference. according to the committee on legal affairs, there is therefore no direct and obvious link between the statements at issue and the duties of ms collins as a member of the european parliament, since they are not connected with her activities as a member of the european parliament or with the policies of the european union. in the light of the above, it proposes that the parliament should not maintain the privileges and immunities of jane collins. i voted accordingly.
in writing. ‒ in may 2016, jane collins applied for the preservation of her privileges and immunities in connection with ongoing criminal proceedings before the queen's bench division of the high court in london. i voted in accordance with the decision of the group.
in writing. ‒ representative mario borghezio is charged in a criminal case pending before the milan court with sharing views based on supremacy and racial or ethnic hatred in a radio program. the member requested that his privileges and immunities in the case be maintained, on the ground that members of the european parliament cannot be investigated, detained or prosecuted for opinions expressed or votes cast in the performance of their duties. however, the committee on legal affairs states in its report that the statements allegedly made during the interview have no direct and obvious connection with the parliamentary activities of the member and are contrary to article 21 of the charter of fundamental rights of the european union and cannot therefore be considered as having been made by a member of the european parliament in the exercise of his official duties. it cannot therefore be assumed that mr borghezio was a member of the european parliament in the present case and therefore proposes that the parliament should not invoke his immunity and privileges. the report also recommends that parliament express its regret that the milan court refused to stay proceedings against mr borghezio, despite having been informed that proceedings under the parliament's rules of procedure were pending in order to preserve the privileges and immunities of the member. i voted accordingly.
