in writing. ‒ in the 2014 revision of the regulation on rail transport statistics, the european parliament included several important elements in the legislation, such as the question of ertms-equipped track sections, accessible stations or the statistical data collected on accidents. the report approved today reflects the positive results of the interinstitutional consultations. the european union has spent millions of euros to implement the ertms rail system, with varying degrees of success. it is therefore important to have a real picture of the railway sections on which the system is operational and on which it may be introduced in the near future. the list of accessible stations is very important for the disabled, and reliable statistical data are essential for this. unlike the european commission, parliament believes that the collection of data on railway accidents is also essential and important, with particular attention to accidents in the transport of dangerous goods. the cooperation of the member states, eurostat and the european railway agency (era) is essential to achieve this common objective. this will enable the commission to improve its control of railway safety. cooperation shall allow the parties concerned to complement each other's data and avoid duplication in the data collection process or excessive administrative burden for either institution. in light of these, i voted in favour of the bill.
in writing. ‒ in the 2014 revision of the regulation on rail transport statistics, the european parliament included several important elements in the legislation, such as the question of ertms-equipped track sections, accessible stations or the statistical data collected on accidents. the report approved today reflects the positive results of the interinstitutional consultations. unlike the european commission, parliament believes that the collection of data on railway accidents is also essential and important, with particular attention to accidents in the transport of dangerous goods. to reduce the number of fatalities in railway accidents, we need to improve the data collection system. it is essential that member states, eurostat and the european railway agency (era) work together to achieve the common objective of increasing the accuracy, transparency and easy comparability of rail transport statistics with other modes of transport. this required the signing of two memoranda of understanding between eurostat and the commission and between the era and the commission, which allow the parties concerned to complement each other's data and avoid duplication in the data collection process and the imposition of excessive administrative burdens on either institution. in view of these, i voted in favour of the adoption of the legislation as a member of the hungarian people's party delegation.

in writing. ‒ inland waterways play a significant role in several countries in reducing the burden on rail and road transport, reducing accidents and promoting environmentally friendly freight transport. policies to strengthen this role should be based on objective, comparable and reliable statistical data. current statistics on inland waterway transport are insufficient to provide guidance and to allow an assessment of union policy in this sector. the european parliament extended the scope of the regulation to passenger transport in addition to freight transport at first reading. this puts inland waterway transport on a par with maritime, air and road transport, which are also collected for freight and passenger transport. this can significantly improve the safety and efficiency of inland waterway transport. that is why i voted in favour of the regulation.
in writing. ‒ policies to strengthen the role of inland navigation should be based on objective, comparable and reliable statistical data. current statistics on inland waterway transport are insufficient to provide guidance and to allow an assessment of union policy in this sector. the european parliament extended the scope of the regulation to passenger transport in addition to freight transport at first reading. this puts inland waterway transport on an equal footing with maritime, air and road transport, for which data are also collected for freight and passenger transport. parliament and the council also agreed to regulate the commission's powers to adopt delegated acts, which were valid for five years. i am pleased that this regulation has been adopted after several years of work and i believe that the use of the statistical data collected will help to significantly increase the safety and efficiency of inland waterway transport. therefore, as a member of the hungarian people's party delegation, i voted in favour of the adoption of the regulation.

in writing. ‒ over the past few years, i have seen that the creation of a harmonised system of sanctions has become indispensable for effective joint action. the rapporteur's proposals will certainly simplify and harmonise customs procedural sanctions, and the simplification and harmonisation of customs procedures could reduce the administrative and cost burden on european, including hungarian, businesses. for the reasons i have just given, i voted in favour of the report.
in writing. ‒ the customs union is one of the european union's pillars, the backbone of the single market. however, there is still no integrated approach to the enforcement of customs legislation, including the imposition of sanctions, i.e. although the rules are the same, the sanctions applied for their infringement differ significantly. these differences undermine the level playing field between economic operators in the european union, as they may lead to a company losing its status as an authorised economic operator in one member state and another company committing the same infringement in another member state. the european commission therefore proposed to the parliament and the council on 13 december 2013 to adopt a directive on a union legal framework for customs infringements and sanctions. it has submitted the commission's proposal to parliament. the lithuanian and swedish parliaments submitted reasoned opinions to the effect that the draft legislative act was not compatible with the principle of subsidiarity. in its report, the committee on the internal market and consumer protection, after consulting the european economic and social committee, recommends that parliament adopt the commission proposal at first reading, subject to 42 amendments. i voted accordingly.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the eu legal framework for customs infringements and sanctions, which aims to eliminate differences between member states in the implementation of customs legislation, including the imposition of sanctions. it is regrettable that, despite the fact that the customs union is one of the eu's pillars, the same rules are infringed with different levels of sanctions within the union. furthermore, like the report, i consider the lack of trust between public administrations, which is also due to differences, to be a serious problem. in order to create greater legal certainty and fair competition, the customs authorities of the member states should also act in a uniform manner in the area of sanctions, in order to avoid distortions of competition and to protect effectively the financial interest of the union. the introduction of integrated rules envisaged in the report should therefore be supported, taking into account the proportionality recommendations in the context of the customs union sanctions.
in writing. ‒ the customs union and trade policy are the exclusive competence of the european union, and therefore only the eu can develop a common approach to the enforcement of customs legislation. member states have undertaken to pursue two objectives, in particular to ensure that the liaison between customs authorities and the performance of customs authorities are as effective as if they were operating as a single body, ensuring uniform checks and supporting legitimate business and adequately protecting the financial interests of the union. however, it is quite clear that a coherent action by the customs authorities of the member states on enforcement, including sanctions, cannot be achieved without an integrated approach, especially given the significant differences between the sanctioning systems of the member states, as highlighted in the 2010 report of the customs sanctions project group. i supported the report.

in writing. ‒ the report of the committee on civil liberties, justice and home affairs points out that organised crime is a global threat and thus requires a joint and coordinated response from the european union and its member states. it shall review international conventions on organised crime and the fight against corruption, money laundering and fraud in this field, as well as decisions and proposals adopted by the various union institutions in this field. it urges the proper transposition of existing legislation, the monitoring of its implementation and the evaluation of its effectiveness, and the speedy establishment of legislation needed to combat it effectively. it considers it necessary to establish a stronger legislative framework, to improve police and judicial cooperation at eu level, to prevent organised crime and corruption from infiltrating the legal economy, and attaches the utmost importance to the early establishment and adequate empowerment of the european public prosecutor's office. it specifically addresses issues of counterfeiting, drug trafficking, betting, match-fixing, tax havens, environmental crime, terrorism and trafficking and smuggling of human beings. i voted in favour of the draft resolution.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report, given that it rightly draws attention to the importance of preventing the integration of organised crime and corruption into the legal order and national economy of the individual states. the report also highlights that the current european legal and instrument framework is unable to deal with the phenomenon of a political regime or government systematising corruption for the sake of its own power and the personal enrichment of its leaders, surrounding it with self-serving legislation, as if legitimising a quasi-state corruption network. as a hungarian socialist, opposition representative, this is an important aspect for me, because today the hungarian economy is suffering most obviously from this phenomenon, to which the eu legal order has not yet found a substantive answer. among the measures proposed, the establishment of the european public prosecutor's office is a particularly important and urgent task which can provide a partial answer to such legal challenges, but in my view only joint action by member states, assuming the full unity and political determination of the european council, can be effective against such governments in the future. i hope that the report which has just been adopted will help to recognise this.

in writing. ‒ the french communist representative's presentation on the situation of human rights and migration in third countries shows an unconditionally pro-immigrant approach. it looks at everything from this perspective, advocating the creation of a pathway for full and legal migration, and only vaguely indicating that human trafficking should be tackled and the roots addressed locally. it starts with the false premise that economic immigration is a basic human right. it is attempting to extend and further expand the concept of refugee and the rights associated with it to all economic migrants on this erroneous international legal basis, which would place a new burden on european nation states. a report that is so pro-immigrant that it solves nothing, but inflates the phrases of the already obviously failed "willkommenskultur", contains nothing new in substance. it contains everything that characterizes the plan to eliminate the traditional european nations. in view of the foregoing, i rejected the report.
in writing. ‒ the report, in my view, sets out exaggerated expectations for the treatment of migrants, beyond the financial capacity of the host countries. it doesn't make a clear distinction between economic migrants and refugees from war zones. this is actually encouraging economic migration. it raises important questions for the future, but the solution to the problem seems far off. in view of all this, and in line with the epp, i could not support the adoption of the report.
in writing. during the south slavic war, we encountered real refugees. the old people, women and children came to hungary. the men were defending their country, so they didn't come. they had little money, since there was no real estate to sell in a war zone. they were genuinely happy to have whatever accommodations, food, and clothing they could find. they didn't demand, they didn't threaten, they didn't trash. they quietly, humbly accepted what they were given. they didn't want to impose their own customs on us. especially not their religion. they helped where they could. then, when the time came for them to return to their own country, they thankfully said good-bye to us. that's what real refugees are. now, these are hardly the cases of today's migrants, so there's a very big problem with this report. just as there are and will be very big problems with the 80% of young men in the troops disguised as refugees. does anyone know how many of them have committed war crimes or crimes against the state? does the person who called them in take responsibility for them? or at least read the relevant passages of the geneva convention?
in writing. ‒ the draft resolution of the committee on foreign affairs looks at the human rights problems arising from the handling of the migration crisis. it places great emphasis on the clear distinction between the concept of migrant and refugee, and draws attention to the human rights problems arising from the conflation of the two categories. it is ruthlessly confronting the challenges and risks of respecting the rights of migrants. calls on the union institutions to place the rights of migrants and refugees as a separate item on the agenda of the dialogues with the third countries concerned, and to give priority to the funding of european projects aimed at protecting ngos working to protect the rights of vulnerable people and migrants, human rights defenders, journalists and lawyers; i voted for the bill.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the situation of human rights and migration in third countries, which provides a comprehensive overview of the challenges related to migration. the report rightly recalls that developing countries host the largest proportion of refugees and migrants in the world, putting a huge strain on their support systems. i welcome the rapporteur's call for member state governments and national parliaments to put an end to the criminal legal frameworks that criminalize migrants and to adopt short, medium and long-term solutions to guarantee the safety of migrants. when i was considering my vote, the parts of the report dealing with the protection of migrant children played a big role. the text also addresses concerns about the well-being of migrant children, girls and women in a number of aspects. it is also commendable that the report also addresses the threat posed by climate change. i also urge the union and its member states to support the least developed countries in the fight against climate change, in order to avoid a worsening of poverty and an acceleration of the number of people displaced by environmental problems.
in writing. ‒ migration is a global and multidimensional phenomenon with many causes, including economic conditions (e.g. developments in the distribution of goods and economic integration at regional and global levels), social and political conditions, the situation in relation to work, violence and security, the gradual deterioration of the state of the environment and the increasing severity of natural disasters. i supported the report in line with the s&d group's decision.
in writing. ‒ in my view, the increasing globalisation and internationalisation of business activities and supply chains is making the role of international companies in ensuring respect for human rights more important and creating a situation where international standards, rules and cooperation are crucial to preventing human rights abuses in third countries. unfortunately, human rights violations continue to occur in third countries, including as a result of decisions taken by the management of certain eu companies and businesses, as well as by individuals, non-state actors and states. the report reminds corporate actors that they must respect human rights in their global operations, regardless of where users live and whether the host member state is complying with its own human rights obligations. therefore, there is a need for continuous, effective and coherent action at all levels, including national, european and international levels, to address effectively and immediately human rights abuses by transnational corporations and to address effectively legal problems and uncertainties arising from the extra-territorial dimension of corporations and their behaviour. in the light of the above, i voted in favour of the adoption of the report.

in writing. ‒ the union is founded on the values of human dignity, freedom, democracy, equality, the rule of law and respect for human rights, and these principles guide its international action (including trade policy). the draft resolution of the committee on foreign affairs, however, points out that business enterprises, including those within the european union, sometimes cause or contribute to human rights abuses and affect the rights of vulnerable groups such as minorities, indigenous peoples, women and children, and contribute to environmental problems. it therefore calls for the obligations of companies, member states and the commission to protect human rights and urges the parties concerned to take the necessary steps to protect human rights. i voted for the bill.
in writing. ‒ the union is founded on the values of human dignity, freedom, democracy, equality, the rule of law and respect for human rights, including the rights of persons belonging to minorities. these principles also govern its international actions (including trade policy). i supported the report.
in writing. ‒ according to the international energy agency, the coming decades could be the golden age of natural gas. partly due to the development of the international market and partly due to the advantageous properties of natural gas, the role of natural gas in national energy mix is expected to increase. as the cleanest fossil energy source, it can replace the much more polluting fuels in both electricity generation and transport, thereby contributing to decarbonisation. import of lng could provide a solution to the expected significant decrease in production within the union and could lead to diversification of resources in member states that are dependent on a single supplier. the union strategy on lng and natural gas storage is part of the energy union winter package. it aims to make the natural gas system more diversified and flexible, thereby contributing to a more secure, predictable and competitive supply of natural gas. the report points out that increasing the utilisation of existing infrastructure is a top priority, but where necessary, the necessary new investments must also be made. in order to increase efficiency, particular attention should be paid to european gas storage facilities. it is also necessary to build and bi-directionalize the associated wiring with particular regard to missing interconnectors and to apply appropriate transmission tariffs. the necessary developments could allow the benefits of gas diversification and competition to be enjoyed outside the host countries. by adopting the report, the european parliament has declared that it is crucial to resolve the situation of vulnerable member states.

in writing. ‒ the ini report on an eu strategy for liquefied natural gas and gas storage was adopted today (415+/225-/15). greens/efa voted against the report as it is very much in favour of expansion of lng and related infrastructure. such developments – based on distorted projections – would result in stranded assets and lock the eu into carbon intense infrastructure. this would create unnecessary costs and delays in achieving energy transition and the decarbonisation of energy systems in the eu. the gyürk report also urges the establishment of new markets for lng and the elimination of market barriers to a global free trade, which would lead to increased imports of fracked gas, regardless of the clear negative effects on the environment. continued reliance on fossil fuels is also in conflict with the eu’s commitments made in paris as part of the new global climate agreement. unfortunately, progressive text proposals, such as on methane leakage and sustainable production conditions, were not included in the final report. in short, we voted against the report because it neglects the context of the eu energy and climate targets and the urgent need to tackle climate change and to phase out fossil fuels.

in writing. there are many environmental problems, many of which are caused by fossil fuels. however, it is necessary to distinguish the use of natural gas within this, because it contains less pollutants than oil, compared to coal, so that when burned, it does not or does not burden our environment with heavy metals, sulfur compounds, nitrogen oxides, micro-particulate matter. for this reason and for diversification reasons, the report contains eligible elements for lng. but it is unacceptable that ukraine is trying to place the burden of natural gas supplies on the taxpayers of the union by buying expensive us-sourced lng instead of cheap russian gas and thereby providing not only the ukrainian population but also their industrial companies with the opportunity to compete with eu petrochemical companies.
in writing. ‒ the draft resolution of the committee on industry, research and energy reviews the role of natural gas, including lng, and its storage in the european union's energy policy, with particular regard to the union's energy dependence, security of supply, energy poverty, the targeted reduction of greenhouse gas emissions and the transition to a low-carbon economy. it shall take into account the european infrastructure for the storage of natural gas and the recovery of liquefied natural gas. it urges the necessary steps to be taken to achieve an energy union that reduces the use of energy, in particular non-renewable energy. i voted in favour of the draft resolution, although i did not see in it any call for more decisive action to curb the use of non-renewable energy.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of a report because i agree that liquefied natural gas reduces our dependence on conventional pipelines, but i am afraid that the approach offers only a short-term solution. i think that basically we should be boosting carbon-free energy production and energy efficiency. i agree that we should address this at eu level, but the report is not clear. on the one hand, it calls for eu-wide action and investment, and on the other, it only occasionally calls for caution. i find little in the way of sustainability or energy efficiency logic, even if this has changed somewhat in a positive direction in the final vote (e.g. by putting more emphasis on the paris climate agreement). reducing dependence on a few suppliers is necessary and may lead to price reductions. i disagreed with the recommendation in the report that the union should provide the necessary infrastructure. i think we're spending billions of euros unnecessarily on a project that will probably be replaced by renewable energy in a few decades. instead of investing in fossil fuels, we should be investing in alternative energy sources!

in writing. ‒ since 2009, there has been a regulation governing the eu's fisheries control system, which in principle applies to the whole eu. however, the uniform interpretation of its paragraphs in all member states has so far failed. the rapporteur visited the ports and fishing establishments of the most affected eu member states, from italy to france, from spain to belgium and germany. the experience gained in the field has resulted in a very practice-oriented report to provide a common understanding of fisheries controls. the controls on the conduct of fishing, the correct use of gear, the quality control of fishery products and other elements of the product range vary widely between member states. there are also very significant differences in terms of severity and consistency, as well as in the application of sanctions. in the course of their work, fishermen in different ports experience different interpretations and application of the rules. this hurts their sense of justice and results in their not taking their obligations seriously. based on all this experience, the report proposes solutions that are sufficiently thorough and practice-oriented to harmonise the system of control of fishing activities within the eu, and i therefore supported its adoption.
in writing. ‒ this non-legislative report focuses on the coordination of fisheries controls between eu member states with sea-basin. the question of the uniform application of eu law and its effectiveness is of particular importance to me. this is how it should be in all eu member states. i voted in favour of the thomas report.
in writing. sea fish and seafood are very important for the diet and are a healthy source of protein for the eu population. however, this is subject to a number of conditions, which is why a regulation on the eu fisheries control system has been in place since 2009, without any harmonisation or uniform interpretation of its paragraphs in all member states. it is commendable that the rapporteur has gained direct experience by visiting the ports and fisheries institutions of the eu member states most affected. he has personally heard the fishermen and the administrative experts and, with the knowledge he has acquired, he has put on the table a very accurate, practical report which can only be supported.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report which calls for simpler, more comprehensive and more uniform rules in the common fisheries policy, particularly in the areas of transparency, cooperation, innovation and equal treatment. fisheries control currently varies from one member state to another and from one fishing area to another, and the report makes proposals to overcome this fragmentation. we need to ensure the uniform application of legislation in the eu, without which there are efficiency issues. for example, in some member states, a single inspectorate carries out checks from the fishing gear to the consumer, while in others there are several authorities simultaneously to carry out these tasks. the single control system should be a priority in order to achieve the objectives of the common fisheries policy. the next review of the control regulation should establish effective rules to be able to prevent, detect and sanction abuses in a uniform manner. i agree that the european fisheries control agency should have a greater role in this process. to this end, it is important to establish closer cooperation between the member states, the office and the european commission.
in writing. ‒ fishermen often complain that their fisheries controls were much stricter than those of their neighbours, whether in another member state or in another fishing zone. fishermen everywhere also claim that their profession is the most controlled of all. this sense of injustice raises a real question: the question of the uniform application of the law and thus its effectiveness. since it is likely that the rules will not be applied with the same rigor, it is feared that a situation will arise in which the rule will not be respected on the grounds that it is not the same for everyone. i voted for the report.
in writing. ‒ from their accession to the present, the transport infrastructure of the eastern eu member states has undoubtedly undergone significant modernisation and improvement with the eu's continuous support. however, for historical and geographical reasons, the focus has been on projects aimed at rebuilding connections to and from the western member states. this was to be changed and somewhat offset by the adopted report. however, in addition to the east-west transport axis, the development of the north-south link is of great importance, which can lead to economic recovery in the central and eastern european member states in particular. the report is unique in that it addresses the challenges and future opportunities in the region in terms of road, rail, water and air transport and interoperability in a single document. hungary is also concerned by the fact that it is proposing to exploit several possibilities that also affect hungary. these included the further development of the via carpathia project and the construction of a route through the eastern half of the country from north to south, which was highlighted in the document. the report also highlights the development of relations with the candidate countries, whether ukraine or the western balkan countries. the financial framework necessary to achieve the ambitious targets will be provided by the resources of the european structural and investment funds, the european network financing facility (enf), the european investment bank (eib) and the european bank for reconstruction and development (ebrd), and by the instruments of the european fund for strategic investments and the exploitation of synergies between them. i therefore voted in favour of the report.

in writing. ‒ the draft of the committee on transport and tourism draws attention to the challenges of accessibility and connectivity of the transport infrastructure in estonia, latvia, lithuania, poland, the czech republic, slovakia, hungary, slovenia, croatia, romania and bulgaria. the transport infrastructure of these member states has undergone significant modernisation and development from the pre-accession period to date with the continuous support of the union, but there are still serious shortcomings in the accessibility and interconnectivity of transport infrastructure in the central and eastern parts of the union. the report suggests that member states and the commission should focus on building the missing links, removing bottlenecks and ensuring seamless connections. as the development of transport infrastructure requires large investments, the ceec member states and the commission should enhance cooperation at all stages of transport policy and project planning. i supported the bill.

in writing. ‒ the draft resolution of the committee on civil liberties, justice and home affairs states that the european union is a community of values; among the guiding principles of the first articles of the treaties are democracy, the rule of law and fundamental rights, which are also conditions for eu membership. however, while the union has a wide range of instruments at its disposal to implement its legislation and the treaties, this is no longer the case for the enforcement of the treaty obligations in the areas of democracy, the rule of law and fundamental rights. the european commission is faced with resistance or explicit rejection when it comes to enforcing commonly agreed rules or recognising the union's right to enforce them. the report therefore considers it essential to adopt a framework that allows the eu to address not only violations of specific eu legislation, but also serious threats (and risks) to democracy, the rule of law and fundamental rights. it therefore proposes the adoption of a european union pact for democracy, the rule of law and fundamental rights in the form of an interinstitutional agreement, the annex to the proposal also contains a specific proposal for its text. i voted for the motion all the more gladly because i myself have long felt the need to bring such an agreement under control.
in writing. ‒ in order not to contradict myself due to my duty as vice-president, in cases where the faction votes differently from the hungarian representatives in the roll-call votes, i will not participate directly in the vote. i do not press the ballot button, but i do raise my hand to indicate to the pp group the voting position that we had previously agreed on. i did the same thing in this case.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the adoption of the report because i consider it important and timely, given that the european parliament and the commission have, since their creation, been obliged to create a legal basis for effective action against member state governments that violate common european democratic standards. unfortunately, this lack of action is most evident in the union's inability to act against the leadership of my country, as the eu for lack of adequate eu legal basis and mechanism, or for lack of political will has been unable to prevent and sanction the repeated violations of the orbán government, its policy of disregard for european norms and the fundamental rights of its own citizens. in this context, i hope and urge that the legislation and interinstitutional agreement establishing the proposed new mechanism will also provide a powerful eu response to the legal tricks of the orbán regime: it will address the situation where the government of a member state uses its substantial parliamentary majority to amend legislation or even the constitution to cover up or subsequently legalise violations. the report now adopted could provide an impetus for further european legislative work in this area.
in writing. ‒ the report on the establishment of the eu mechanism on democracy, the rule of law and fundamental rights underlines that the union is founded on the values of human dignity, freedom, democracy, equality, the rule of law and respect for human rights, including the rights of persons belonging to minorities. this is one of the prerequisites for mutual recognition and trust within the union, the document stresses. although this eu mechanism is not legally sufficiently well-founded, and given that it can also provide an appropriate framework for the protection of the minority and linguistic rights of hungarian communities living outside hungary's borders, i voted in favour of the report.
in writing. ‒ while the european union has a number of tools at its disposal to ensure respect for the principles of democracy, the rule of law and fundamental rights, there are significant gaps and in practice these tools are limited in scope, inadequate and ineffective, or unlikely to be used. the illiberal rule of the orbán government is a disgrace to hungary and a disgrace to europe. the enlightened european community needs mechanisms that give us the tools to deal with governments that ignore our core values. this was once the loudest demand of fidesz. they were in opposition then, but now they're in opposition to europe.

internship, to take up a course of study, which has been a successful approach and we need to expand on that. i can assure mr eickhout that i am not about self—congratulation. frankly, i remove every country, to announce that i saw the extent of the problems that we are in. i have also said quite clearly that this is a project that could also fail if we are not very careful. so in that sense i am very far from being self-congratulatory. i think we have quite a number of issues we need to solve. indeed i believe eco—design makes a huge contribution to solving some of our issues and to getting our economy to where it is going to be completely sustainable and therefore very competitive in a world, in this fourth industrial revolution, which is changing very quickly to a sustainable economy. the quicker we do that and the more we invest in that, the better we will come out of this, also in terms of employment and competitiveness. of course, the issue of migration will be first and foremost on our minds in the year to come. that is beyond any doubt but, there again, everybody needs to accept their responsibility. this is somewhere where we cannot have a european union of à la carte solidarity. if we have a problem that is faced by the union as a whole, every single member state will have to take their share of the responsibility in solving the problem. that is the gist of think could be the core of what we need to do. europeans want more protection. they want to regain control of their destinies. that was the core of the debate during the brexit campaign. that is what in writing. i am pleased to note that today marks the end of four years of work and, in line with my report adopted by the european parliament on 25 october 2011, innovative and knowledge-based economies can no longer be achieved without content and forms that are accessible to people with disabilities and that are introduced by binding legislation. as a reminder, the european commission originally put forward a much more limited proposal, which we in parliament have considerably expanded. in addition to the public sector services originally proposed, the scope now covers a wide range of public services. the accessibility requirements will apply not only to websites but also to mobile applications, as the use of standards is also required by law. finally, the representative bodies of people with disabilities are involved in the implementation, which takes a good two years, about 21 months. the work is not over: the audiovisual package and the european accessibility act are on their way.
in writing. there is a strong body of scientific evidence to support the harmful effects of industrially produced trans fats. excessive consumption of these foods not only increases the risk of cardiovascular disease but is also associated with morbid obesity and type 2 diabetes. mandatory labelling, voluntary industry commitments do not in themselves provide sufficient protection for consumers. the european commission's report published in december 2015 reached similar conclusions: the most effective means of prevention could be to regulate the content of industrial trans fats. hungary was among the first to regulate the maximum acceptable levels of trans-fatty acids in food by regulation, following denmark and austria in 2014. the regulation states that no food may be placed on the market if the amount of trans-fatty acids in 100 grams of total fat exceeds 2 grams. the hungarian example has since been followed by latvia. following the introduction of the mandatory legislation, the percentage of foods containing trans-fatty acids above the legal limit has decreased significantly in the short period of time in the countries concerned, with significant public health benefits. it is noteworthy that the food industry recognising its social responsibility is playing an increasing role in reducing trans fats. taking advantage of the consensus situation, it is therefore important that the european commission proposes union maximum levels for these artificial fats as soon as possible. on these grounds, i voted in favour of the resolution.

in writing. ‒ the motion for a resolution concerns the mid-term review of the multiannual financial framework for the period 2014-2020. stresses the european parliament's continuing concern that the resources available under the current multiannual financial framework are insufficient; the roadmap has been shaped by a number of new crises and priorities in recent years, namely the migration and refugee crisis, external emergencies, internal security issues, the agricultural crisis, european fund for strategic investments funding and persistently high unemployment. it considers that the revision of the multiannual financial framework provides a unique opportunity to overcome the budgetary difficulties currently threatening the credibility of the european union. calls on the council to take its responsibility, put its words into action and ensure a realistic, credible, comprehensive and sustainable eu budget for the remaining years of the current financial framework; i agree with the arguments and therefore with the motion for a resolution.
in writing. ‒ the ep's motion is in line with the parliament's report on the review of the financial framework for 2014-2020 adopted at the july plenary session. in this, despite the unanimous opposition of hungarian mps, they supported forced resettlement and harsh financial sanctions against countries that refused. at the same time, fidesz meps will only approve a financial framework review and an eu budget that does not even include these penalties at the level of ideas. in the review, the european commission proposes an increase of eur 12.8 billion. at the same time, the liquidity crisis created during the previous seven-year framework, when the commission was unable to pay the invoices submitted to the member states after the projects had been implemented, must be avoided. we can only support any proposal if we have the appropriate guarantees: there will be sufficient funds in the annual budgets to pay for the catch-up programmes and agricultural subsidies already in place. the text of the motion for a resolution confirms the ep report calling for financial penalties against member states that do not accept mandatory quotas in july, and i therefore did not support the adoption of the motion.

in writing. in assessing the budgetary report, i indicated that a mid-term review of the mff 2014-2020 was warranted, given the unforeseen emergencies that have developed in the union. these include the migration and refugee crisis, external emergencies, internal security issues, the agricultural crisis, the financing of the european fund for strategic investments (efsi) and persistently high levels of unemployment. i fully agree with the report, because it is an unacceptable attitude that rich member states, which derive all their profits from their companies, are unwilling to contribute even 1% of their gdp to solving such major problems. it is very timely that the council should lead not only in fine words but also in deeds.
in writing. ‒ the draft resolution of the committee on budgets highlights a number of new crises and priorities that have emerged in recent years, namely the migration and refugee crisis, external emergencies, internal security issues, the agricultural crisis, the financing of the european fund for strategic investments and the persistently high level of unemployment, especially among young people, as well as the recent ratification by the union of the agreement on climate change. in this context, the european parliament reiterates its constant concern that the resources available under the current multiannual financial framework are insufficient. stresses that a significant additional amount of resources from the union budget is needed to respond adequately to these challenges; recalls in this context that article 311 tfeu provides that 'the union shall provide itself with the means necessary to attain its objectives and carry out its policies'. it is convinced that the revision of the mff provides a unique opportunity to overcome the budgetary difficulties currently threatening the credibility of the european union. it also points out that in order to restore confidence in the european project, a union budget that is more transparent and accessible to citizens is needed. proposes therefore to call on the council to assume its responsibility and to ensure a realistic, credible, comprehensive and sustainable eu budget for the remaining years of the current financial framework; i supported the bill.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution on the insufficient resources available under the mff. they agree that new crises and priorities have emerged in recent times, such as the refugee issue, external emergencies and internal security issues, the crisis in agriculture, persistently high unemployment and climate policy challenges. in the light of all this and taking into account the conclusions of the review carried out in the first half of the financial cycle, i believe that the possibility of adding additional resources should be examined. only in this way can political commitments and the eu's strategic objectives meet and the credibility of the european union be preserved. i agree that this cannot be achieved by simply redistributing resources, because that would be at the expense of existing programmes and policies. the proposal specifically calls for the cuts in the budget made at the launch of the european structural and investment funds to be reinstated in the second half of the financial cycle, as these cuts have significantly affected horizon 2020 and the european network development fund. the commission also calls for an increase in the amounts of the chapters on migration and the refugee crisis. i also agree with the proposal and the plan to simplify financial instruments initiated by the european commission.
in writing. ‒ the revision of the mff provides a unique opportunity to overcome the budgetary difficulties currently threatening the credibility of the european union. i voted for the s&d position.
in writing. ‒ the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) aims to support the reintegration into the labour market of workers and self-employed persons made redundant as a result of globalisation, as a result of major structural changes in world trade patterns, or as a result of the prolongation of the global financial and economic crisis or a new global financial and economic crisis. estonia has submitted an application for a financial contribution from the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) under the reference number egf/2016/003 ee/petroleum and chemicals. the commission has examined the application and found that it complies with the requirements of the relevant regulation, and i have therefore voted in favour of the adoption of the proposal.
in writing. estonia has submitted an application for a financial contribution from the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) under reference number egf/2016/003 ee/petroleum and chemicals. the measures are expected to involve 800 of the 1 550 redundant workers eligible for egf assistance. the european parliament agrees with the commission that the conditions set out in article 4 (2) of the egf regulation are met and that estonia is therefore entitled to a financial contribution of eur 1 131 358 under that regulation for the following personalised services: financing of training costs in the framework of support for school-based studies, reimbursement of training costs to employers, labour market training, traineeships, debt management counselling, psychological counselling, study grants for school-based studies, scholarships, transport and housing allowances and language training. these measures have been developed in accordance with the needs identified in the estonian regional development strategy and are in line with the shift towards a resource-efficient and sustainable economy. on the basis of the above, i voted in favour of the adoption of the report.

in writing. ‒ the european globalisation adjustment fund was established to provide additional support to workers affected by the consequences of major structural changes in world trade. on 11 may 2016, estonia submitted to the commission an application to mobilise the fund, in respect of redundancies in estonia in the companies eesti energia as, nitrofert as and viru keemia grupp as. the measures affect around 800 of the 1550 redundancies, as they are intended to target redundancies considered particularly vulnerable from a labour market perspective and some workers have stated that they cannot participate in the measures. the following personalised services are intended to be provided to the dismissed employees: financing of training costs in the framework of support for studies in the school system, reimbursement of training costs to employers, labour market training, internship, debt management counselling, psychological counselling, study grant for continuing studies in the school system, scholarship, transport and housing allowance for estonian language training. the commission has concluded that the application meets the conditions for a financial contribution from the fund and that the planned measures constitute active labour market measures falling within the scope of the eligible activities and has therefore submitted to the parliament and the council a proposal for a financial contribution from the fund of eur 1 131 358. i supported the motion.
in writing. ‒ the european globalisation adjustment fund was established to provide additional support to workers affected by the consequences of major structural changes in world trade. i supported the motion.
in writing. ‒ as you know, the european parliament has already stressed in the kosa report adopted on 25 october 2011 that innovative and knowledge-based economies cannot be developed without the content and forms of mandatory legislation that are accessible to people with disabilities. such services include smartphone applications and information tools used in the mass media to facilitate the daily lives of people with disabilities, as well as websites accessible to the blind, subtitled content for the hearing impaired including mass communication services and online services for sign language users. it is therefore a great achievement that gradually, fully accessible websites will be made available not only to public sector organisations but also to public-service organisations, in order to enable disabled people to live independently as defined by the un convention on the rights of persons with disabilities and to participate in all aspects of life in society. in order to ensure social inclusion, it is therefore necessary to make the websites of public sector organisations, as well as those providing basic services to the public, such as those relating to pensions, health, education, social and key document services, or information and services provided by interest groups, accessible to all people, as far as is technologically possible and reasonable. the involvement of representatives and experts from the organisations concerned is also an important success. so it was clear that i had voted to support the passage of the legislation.

in writing. ‒ as you know, in my report adopted by the european parliament on 25 october 2011, i stressed that innovative and knowledge-based economies cannot be developed without the content and forms of mandatory legislation that are accessible to people with disabilities. such services include smartphone applications and information tools used in the mass media to facilitate the daily lives of people with disabilities, as well as websites accessible to the blind, subtitled content for the hearing impaired including mass communication services and online services for sign language users. therefore, it is a great achievement that progressively, fully accessible websites not only of public sector organisations but also of public-service organisations can be made available, in order to enable persons with disabilities to live independently, as defined in the relevant un convention, and to participate in all aspects of life in society. in order to ensure social inclusion, it is therefore necessary to make the websites of public sector organisations, as well as those providing basic services to the public, such as those relating to public procurement, health, education, social and key documentation services, or information and services provided by interest groups, accessible to all people, as far as is technologically possible and reasonable. the involvement of representatives and experts from the organisations concerned is also an important success. so it was clear that i had voted to pass the legislation.
in writing. ‒ the commission has proposed to the european parliament and the council the adoption of a directive of the european parliament and of the council on the accessibility of public sector bodies' websites and mobile applications. parliament adopted its position at first reading on 26 february 2014. following the subsequent consultations, the council also adopted its position at first reading and the report of the committee on the internal market and consumer protection recommends that parliament agree to it at second reading. i voted accordingly.
in writing. ‒ as you know, the european parliament already stressed in the kosa report adopted on 25 october 2011 that innovative and knowledge-based economies cannot be developed without the content and forms of mandatory legislation that are accessible to people with disabilities. such services include smartphone applications and information tools used in the mass media to facilitate the daily lives of people with disabilities, as well as websites accessible to the blind, subtitled content for the hearing impaired including mass communication services and online services for sign language users. it is therefore a great achievement that gradually, fully accessible websites will be made available not only to public sector organisations but also to public-service organisations, in order to enable disabled people to live independently as defined by the un convention on the rights of persons with disabilities and to participate in all aspects of life in society. in order to ensure social inclusion, it is therefore necessary to make the websites of public sector organisations, as well as those providing basic services to the public, such as those relating to pensions, health, education, social and key document services, or information and services provided by interest groups, accessible to all people, as far as is technologically possible and reasonable. the involvement of representatives and experts from the organisations concerned is also an important success. so it was clear that i had voted to support the passage of the legislation.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the recommendation on the opening of websites at second reading. the recommendation relates to the adoption of a directive of the european parliament and of the council on the accessibility of public sector bodies' websites and mobile applications. the report clearly targets the disabled, but the draft also includes the elderly. with a few exceptions, the draft requires all public administrations to make their websites and mobile applications accessible. all of this helps people who are blind or visually impaired, deaf or hard of hearing, or who have limited mobility. the involvement of public service broadcasters was discussed during the drafting of the recommendation and the final agreement is that this area will be covered by a separate sector specific legislation. i believe that in the digital age, not only do we need to treat all citizens equally, but we also have the technical conditions for that when we talk about access to information. i share the view that this directive is an important step towards an inclusive digital society, ensuring that public authorities' websites and mobile applications are accessible to all.
in writing. ‒ the proposal for a council position at first reading on the adoption of a directive of the european parliament and of the council on the accessibility of public sector bodies' websites and mobile applications, which is part of the ordinary legislative procedure, was supported by me.
in writing. ‒ the draft phytosanitary regulation, based on the political agreement between the european parliament and the council, was designed primarily to simplify and harmonise. in addition to the inclusion of a large number of legislative acts (mostly directives) in a single framework, the fight against pests has required greater emphasis on the prevention principle, a more reasonable prioritisation of pests, the strengthening of scientific research and the fair sharing of costs and responsibilities. the final text is in line with hungarian national interests. i therefore voted against the attempt by one of the parliamentary groups to block the adoption of the text.
in writing. ‒ the draft phytosanitary regulation, based on the political agreement between the european parliament and the council, was designed primarily to simplify and harmonise. in addition to the inclusion of a large number of legislative acts (mostly directives) in a single framework, the fight against plant pests requires greater emphasis on the prevention principle, a more reasonable prioritisation of pests, the strengthening of scientific research and a fair sharing of costs and responsibilities. the final text is in line with hungarian national interests. i therefore voted against the attempt by one of the parliamentary groups to block the adoption of the text.
in writing. ‒ the commission has proposed to the european parliament and the council to adopt a regulation on protection measures against pests of plants, amending regulations (eu) no 228/2013, (eu) no 652/2014 and (eu) no 1143/2014 and repealing directives 69/464/eec, 74/647/eec, 93/85/eec, 98/57/ec, 2000/29/ec, 2006/91/ec and 2007/33/ec. parliament adopted its position at first reading on 15 april 2014. the austrian federal council submitted a reasoned opinion that the draft legislative act was not compatible with the principle of subsidiarity. following the subsequent consultations, the council adopted its position at first reading and the committee on agriculture and rural development recommends in its report that parliament should agree to it at second reading. i voted accordingly.
in writing. ‒ in may 2013, the european commission proposed new rules on plant pest control measures. the regulation includes new tools such as a system of risk analysis criteria that group these pests according to their most serious consequences. it also places a greater emphasis on high-risk commercial products from third countries and allows for better monitoring and early eradication of emerging pests. the need for a closer european action in the field of plant health is also a concern, and i therefore voted against the liberal recommendation rejecting the agreement. the key factor of plant health is the attraction of sustainable and competitive agriculture, horticulture and forestry, and through these, public health. the socialist and democratic group is committed to guaranteeing the highest level of security and is a major supporter of the precautionary import regime. the new rules allow temporary bans on products that pose a risk of new pests or are suspected of posing a health risk. it also requires that organisations importing plants or plant products, including those traded via the internet, carry a phytosanitary certificate and introduces a plant passport system for plants purchased for planting.
in writing. ‒ the term 'european semester' is a typical eu linguistic invention to hide the point. in fact, it is a semiannual process whose essence and purpose is to adopt centrally the basic data and economic and social objectives that will determine the budget of the member states for the following year, to enforce the achievement of the union's objectives. this is a practical way of drastically restricting the sovereign national parliaments from independently carrying out one of their most important tasks, namely the creation of budgetary law. the economic and social policies formulated in the context of the european semester are neoliberal, austerity-oriented, federalist and anti-democratic. the report submitted was entirely consistent with this view, so i naturally rejected it.
in writing. ‒ in connection with the report, i would like to emphasise that youth unemployment has decreased in most member states in recent times, but this figure remains a serious concern. in 2015, youth unemployment in europe decreased to 19,7%. the commission recalls that the union industry was not able to obtain sufficient spare capacity to meet the demand for biodiesel. i would like to emphasise the importance of digital skills, entrepreneurship and soft skills. a stable and high-quality job and a safe environment are very important for establishing independence and starting a responsible family. europe's ageing population requires that young people be activated as a matter of urgency, and that they be encouraged to start families and to adopt children.
in writing. ‒ the crisis has shown that europe needs to take steps to improve its economic model and restore its competitiveness. this requires both public funding and targeted investments. however, the potential of the single market is not being realised at present. the union should support member states to significantly increase cross-border trade and to act urgently to make better use of digital technologies. i voted in favour of this report and i myself believe that the highest level of political oversight should be restored, the transposition and implementation of eu rules should be harmonised and more effective means should be developed to ensure that the single market really benefits citizens and businesses.
in writing. a number of proposals for amendments to the report, which are eligible for support, highlight the fundamental problems of the eu's economic philosophy. i have to stress many times that the roots of the problems are systemic, that the particular neoliberal economic philosophy has not offered any real solutions, and it will not. until now, it was expected that the necessary changes would be brought about by market forces, whereas the state's role was to keep the budget deficit in check and to ensure the freedom of the markets. i'm telling you, it's not gonna work this way. of course, if the goal is not sustainable development and a union of livable member states, then the path may be good.
in writing. ‒ the report of the economic and monetary committee outlines the main developments in economic developments expected for 2016: low growth, investment deficit, high unemployment, especially among young people, negative inflation. notes that the europe 2020 strategy, which for the first time included the fight against poverty in the union's programme, will not achieve the objective of reducing poverty in the union; it concludes, in general, that the eu's capacity for growth must be improved, allowing for the creation and maintenance of quality jobs. action against excessive taxation of labour. it attaches particular importance to inclusive education systems, particularly in vocational education, which enable people to acquire skills relevant to the needs of the labour market, and stresses the importance of research and development and the renewal of education systems and vocational training, in particular lifelong learning. it aims to close the innovation gap between the eu and other economies, with a focus on research and development spending. it concludes that public and private support for research and higher education institutions is essential to a more competitive european economy and that the weakness or absence of such infrastructure places some countries at a significant disadvantage. i voted in favour of the draft resolution.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the european semester for economic policy coordination. i welcome the fact that the report refers repeatedly to the importance of solidarity within the union and recalls that socially responsible reforms must be based on solidarity, integration, social justice and the fair distribution of goods. i agree with the report's policy call to avoid taxing work excessively, as excessive taxation reduces the incentives for inactive people, the unemployed, second-time workers and low-wage earners to return to the labour market. like the report, i welcome the fact that the european semester now focuses more strongly on employment and social performance, all the more so as the european semester process should contribute to addressing existing and emerging societal challenges, thereby also ensuring the emergence of a more efficient economy. i fully support the report's call for member states to urgently take action to ensure that decent work is accompanied by a living wage and that people have access to an adequate minimum income and social protection. it would also be useful for the commission to include social impact assessments in the country-specific recommendations to better understand the impact of the major structural reforms advocated, in particular on job creation and economic growth.
in writing. ‒ the european union economy is expected to grow less than expected in the european economic outlook for spring 2016, as euro area gdp is expected to grow by only 1.6% and reach 1.8% by 2017, which is lower than previously estimated. in the european union, challenges are linked to the deteriorating international environment, the failure to implement sustainable reforms and the divergence in economic and social performance across the union. i voted for the report.
in writing. ‒ there is a significant body of scientific evidence on the harmful effects of industrially produced trans fats. excessive consumption of these foods not only increases the risk of cardiovascular disease but is also associated with morbid obesity and type 2 diabetes. mandatory labelling, voluntary industry commitments do not in themselves provide sufficient protection for consumers. the european commission's report published in december 2015 reached similar conclusions: the most effective means of prevention could be to regulate the content of industrial trans fats. hungary was among the first to regulate the maximum acceptable levels of trans fats in food by regulation, following denmark and austria in 2014. the regulation states that no food may be placed on the market if the amount of trans-fatty acids in 100 grams of total fat exceeds 2 grams. the hungarian example has since been followed by latvia. following the introduction of the mandatory legislation, the percentage of foods containing trans-fatty acids above the legal limit has decreased significantly in the short period of time in the countries concerned, with significant public health benefits. on these grounds, i voted in favour of adopting the resolution.

in writing. the european parliament, with the support of the green group (586 votes in favour, 19 against and 38 abstentions), voted in favour of the resolution on trans-fatty acids, in which we call on the european commission to set a legal eu limit value for the use of industrial trans-fatty acids as soon as possible, as further steps are needed to protect human health. the commission has already carried out a number of studies on trans-acids and international organisations have demonstrated that their high consumption poses a risk to human health. industrially produced foods and beverages contain high levels of trans-fatty acids, mainly from low-cost raw materials and industrially produced foods. excessive consumption of trans fats can cause obesity, increase the risk of certain cancers, and cardiovascular disease. the european union has a duty to act against their excessive use. the issue of adequate consumer information remains unresolved, but it is even more important to introduce european-level regulation beyond the individual measures of the member states.

in writing. ‒ the report by the committee on the environment, public health and food safety takes the view that trans-fatty acids are consumed mainly in the form of industrially produced, partly hydrogenated vegetable oils modified by the addition of hydrogen atoms. now both the european food safety authority, the who, and the us food and drug administration are calling for a reduction in the consumption of trans fats, recognizing their health risks. the draft therefore urges eu action to significantly reduce the intake of trans-fatty acids by the population, asking the commission to set a legal eu limit value for industrial trans-fatty acids as soon as possible. notes that according to who, a labelling policy for trans fats is the most costly solution, while in countries where a ban on trans fats has been introduced, the financial impact has been minimal, given the low implementation and control costs; i voted for the motion.

in writing. ‒ trans-fatty acids are unsaturated fatty acids that have been used by the food industry since the 1950s in foods derived from ruminants, such as dairy and meat products, as well as in products of plant origin (porridge, peas, lettuce and canola oil), and in industrially produced, partly hydrogenated, products prepared for cooking on the stove and in the oven. according to who, naturally occurring trans fats are unlikely to pose a health risk in current diets due to their relatively low intake. however, frequent consumption of partially hydrogenated vegetable oils carries an increased risk of diseases (cardiovascular disease, infertility, endometriosis, gonorrhoea, alzheimer's disease, diabetes, obesity and certain cancers) and efsa recommends that the consumption of trans fats should be kept as low as possible. the motion for a resolution reiterates its concern about the risks of trans-fatty acids to human health and describes that the restriction of trans-fatty acids has been shown to have rapid and significant health benefits. it therefore calls on the commission to set a legal eu limit for industrial trans-fatty acids as soon as possible in order to reduce the intake of trans-fatty acids by all groups of the population. since these fatty acids are not necessary in processed foods and are even unhealthy, i voted in favour of the motion.

the rapporteur. madam president, i have to ask you to leave. first of all, i'd like to thank all my fellow mps, the shadow rapporteurs, the advisers, my colleagues and everyone who has contributed to the report. the economic crisis has affected young people in a very sensitive way, with long-term consequences. youth unemployment has risen, the gap between certain groups of young people has widened, and some of them have become increasingly excluded from social life. many of them had uncertain futures and social passivity was on the rise. young people are one of europe's greatest resources, the key to its future. the european union and the member states should therefore not ignore the potential of the creativity, creativity and knowledge of europe's 90 million young people. analysis of the statistical data for the past period shows that there are positive trends in education and employment indicators, although the indicators still show wide variations when measured in some member states. in the light of these results, we need to continue to look for better solutions to the new challenges facing young people, and it is very important that more systematic cooperation is needed across a number of policy areas, including employment, education and training, social policy, youth policy, sport, culture and other areas. youth unemployment has decreased in most member states in recent years, but the current figure remains a cause for great concern. for example, that almost 27 million young people are at risk of poverty. the poverty rate, the need for part-time work and the temporary work that often lasts longer are higher among young people than among the general population, indicating a low quality of life for this generation. therefore, encouraging job creation and youth employment should be an important priority. the risk of inactivity, poverty and social marginalisation affects young people in different ways. for those who have fewer opportunities in life or live in less developed regions, disadvantages often accumulate. they are more likely to be 'neet' young people, so it is very important to have catch-up programmes, social and talent development programmes to overcome these disadvantages and to have a wide awareness of the opportunities available. in this context, the support for mother tongue education for national minorities should be emphasised, as this is an important priority in the report and in line with the opinion of the committee of the regions on the same subject. europe also needs to mobilise young people urgently because of the ageing of its population: well-informed family and youth policies, home-building grants and family tax breaks can be of great help. some countries have recognised this and the indicators have started to improve, such as hungary, but we still have work to do in this area. the report stresses the importance of the role of the family, school, sport and religious communities in the socialisation of young people, as well as the importance of involving local and regional authorities in youth policy. knowledge, skill, is still the greatest value. the unemployment rate for graduates is still lower than for those without qualifications. it is therefore important to improve the quality of education and to better and more effectively align it with the needs of the labour market. we need to better align school and education with the world of work to give young people a better chance of entering the labour market. increase the dominance of digital and applied sciences, and improve digital and other skills. recognition of skills acquired through informal, non-formal and lifelong learning, and cross-border mutual recognition of academic degrees and higher qualifications in the european labour market are very important.

in writing. i am strongly opposed to any attempt to cover, on a voluntary or compulsory basis, the management of crisis situations caused by social and demographic changes from the budgetary resources of the cap. it is of the utmost importance to me that the resources of the cap actually reach the farmers. that is why i will not be able to support the andrieu report, along with my hungarian colleagues from the people's party. i have to do this despite the fact that the text proposes a strong and adequately funded common agricultural policy, an objective which is fully in line with the interests of hungarian farmers. however, the draft report also contains provisions which directly jeopardise the future financing of the cap. paragraphs 21 and 77 of the report and recital ai suggest that agricultural resources should also be used to support social and demographic projects. it is of the utmost importance to us that the resources of the cap actually reach the farmers. we cannot therefore allow the management of crises caused by social and demographic change to be covered by direct payments or rural development funds, either on a voluntary or compulsory basis. the financing of social issues has no place in the common agricultural policy and, therefore, union support for the most deprived persons was excluded from this policy in 2013. unfortunately, the same proposal was also mentioned in the omnibus package of proposals, the proposed amendment to the eu legislation which forms the backbone of the structural funds and the cap. we will stand up here to defend the common agricultural policy.

in writing. ‒ the discharge for the 2014 financial year of the european joint undertaking for the development of fusion energy and iter (established in 2007 for a period of 35 years), i.e. the approval of the use of its financial resources, was postponed by the european parliament in april 2016 as the long-awaited and long-delayed iter action plan was not presented at that time. in the meantime, this material has been prepared and the rapporteur proposes in this second report to grant the exemption. the commission considers that the exemption is not necessary to ensure that the beneficiary is able to continue to benefit from the aid. joint undertakings bring together industrial and research organisations (mainly in the form of ppps) in order to facilitate research, new technologies and demonstration activities, and to accelerate the uptake of the technology concerned. in this case, this training covers a number of areas, such as air traffic control, low-carbon energy, nano and cleaner flight technologies, computing, and nuclear fusion. i agree with the socialist and democratic approach that it is worth supporting joint ventures that guarantee clear benefits to eu citizens, and that is why i voted in favour of this report.
