in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution because i am convinced that the european union cannot remain silent in the face of the worsening international war situation and humanitarian crisis in the region bordering europe. the report recalls the intolerable security and humanitarian situation in northern iraq, particularly in the wake of the siege of mosul, the consequences of jihadist terror, genocide, and the systematic persecution of yazidis, christians and other religious and ethnic minorities. i hope that our strong parliamentary resolution will encourage the eeas and the eu member states, and the union as a whole, to take more decisive and concrete action as a global actor.
in writing. ‒ the turkish government has the right and responsibility to respond to the coup attempt. i would like to stress, however, that the failed military takeover cannot be used as an excuse by the turkish government to further suppress the legitimate and peaceful opposition and to impede the peaceful exercise of freedom of expression by journalists and the media through disproportionate and unlawful actions and measures. i would like to remind you that a free and pluralistic press is an essential element of democracy, as are due process, the presumption of innocence and the independence of the judiciary. the turkish authorities should deal with the media and journalists in the most sensitive manner possible. freedom of expression and freedom of the press remain central to the functioning of a democratic and open society. in the light of the above, i have voted in favour of the motion.
in writing. turkey was already considered one of the worst-ranked countries in terms of press and media freedom before the failed coup attempt. since the coup, the situation has deteriorated significantly. thousands of people were imprisoned and fired from their jobs. in a resolution adopted by a large majority, parliament called on the turkish government to drop the unfounded charges against journalists and to abandon the conceptual proceedings against writers and journalists. the eu institutions and its member states must take consistent action to ensure that the union's partners, in particular those countries with close links to the eu, also uphold the fundamental principles of human rights and democracy. the union can only do this consistently if it continuously and appropriately safeguards these fundamental values within its borders.
in writing. ‒ a motion for a resolution on this subject was tabled by the enf, efdd, s&d, ecr, gue/ngl, alde, ppe and verts/ale groups. of the eight groups, the latter seven reached an agreement and drafted a joint compromise proposal. i voted for the compromise motion.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution, expressing my view that it is unacceptable that the erdogan government, under the pretext of the recent coup attempt, is using an anti-terrorism law that provides for too broad and vague powers of the authorities to severely restrict press freedom, imprison journalists, and close down editorial offices and organs. the decision draws attention to the fact that one of the most important of the fundamental values of the european union is the freedom of the press, the guarantee of the diversity of the press and the safety of its staff, which is particularly expected to be respected by a significant partner and candidate country such as turkey. the european parliament's resolution on the situation in turkey is a welcome step forward in the fight against terrorism. however, as a representative of the hungarian opposition and a democrat, i cannot ignore the current parallel with the situation in hungary, where the regime - with more subtle means - also severely restricts the freedom of the press, prosecutes or takes into its own hands an editorial office critical of the government that exposes the corruption of its leaders (népszabadság case). with regard to the european parliament's current resolution, i am convinced that the eu's criticism of turkey cannot be effective and credible unless it takes a similarly strong stand against the orbán regime's restrictive measures on press freedom in one of its member states.
in writing. ‒ the proposal is primarily a response to the deteriorating security situation in the european union's neighbourhood. this could lead to a renewed nuclear weapons exercise as a deterrent. in addition, the failure to implement effective steps towards disarmament and non-proliferation poses additional risks. the resolution calls on the nuclear-weapon states to take concrete measures to reduce the risk of nuclear explosions and to take immediate action to rapidly reduce the number of nuclear weapons. in addition, the motion expresses concern about the role and attitude of russia, which has significantly increased the nuclear threat. as a result, the security situation worldwide has deteriorated, stability and predictability have been shaken, and the relationship between nato and russia has deteriorated significantly. the proposal also supports the convening of the nuclear security summit 2016, recognising that the unauthorised trade and use of nuclear materials represents a direct and serious threat to the security of the world.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution because it reflects the growing concern of european public opinion about the potential dangers of the policies of certain nuclear-weapon states and their governments and the future of international security as a whole. as vice-chair of the ep delegation for ukraine and of the association committee, i am particularly sensitive to facts and doubts, supported by my own experience, concerning russia's regional and global ambitions. the destabilisation of ukraine by military means, the illegal annexation of the crimean peninsula, the political threats to nato, and in particular to the baltic states, which are not devoid of nuclear elements, by the putin regime, represent a real and easily actionable threat in the eu's immediate eastern neighbourhood, which requires a firm and united eu response, including a comprehensive and concrete response from the eeas. the current ep decision, in my view, provides the appropriate political background and incentive for this and hopefully influences the governments of the member states towards a unified political action.
in writing. ‒ the proposal is primarily a response to the deteriorating security situation in the european union's neighbourhood. this could lead to a renewed nuclear weapons exercise as a deterrent. in addition, the failure to implement effective steps towards disarmament and non-proliferation poses additional risks. the resolution calls on the nuclear-weapon states to take concrete measures to reduce the risk of nuclear explosions and to take immediate action to rapidly reduce the number of nuclear weapons. in addition, the motion expresses concern about the role and attitude of russia, which has significantly increased the nuclear threat. as a result, the security situation worldwide has deteriorated, stability and predictability have been shaken, and the relationship between nato and russia has deteriorated significantly. the proposal also supports the convening of the 2016 nuclear security summit, recognising that the unauthorised trade and use of nuclear materials represents a direct and serious threat to the security of the world.
in writing. ‒ in europe, nearly 100 million citizens of all ages are volunteers, and their work contributes to around 5% of the eu's gdp. the commission should take into account the economic value of the products and services provided by volunteers when formulating a policy that focuses more on volunteers. it is important that the european voluntary service is based on the provision of quality volunteer places and respects the principles of the volunteers' charter and the quality charter for student mobility. it is also necessary that the european voluntary service be based on a structure that encourages volunteering organisations to become host organisations, thereby providing them with appropriate support and training, while strengthening the role of coordinating organisations that support a large number of host organisations, for example in terms of administration and training. in the light of the above, i voted in favour of the adoption of the report.
in writing. ‒ a motion for a resolution was tabled on this subject by the s&d, ppe, gue/ngl, alde, ecr and verts/ale groups. the six groups reached an agreement and worked out a joint compromise proposal. i voted for the compromise motion.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution on volunteering and the european voluntary service, which i share the view that volunteering is one of the most visible expressions of solidarity, promoting social inclusion and contributing to the development of a well-functioning civil society and to economic growth. i also agree with the finding that a supportive environment plays a crucial role in ensuring that as many european citizens as possible participate in volunteering, thus guaranteeing a safe and sustainable support for the volunteering infrastructure, in particular for organisations employing volunteers. it is therefore necessary for member states to set up adequately funded national volunteering schemes and to improve access to quality information on volunteering opportunities at both national and local level, in particular through existing youth information networks.
in writing. ‒ my report assesses the results of the eu youth strategy for the 2013-2015 cycle. youth policy is a member state competence, the european union's role is to coordinate and support. since no legislative action can be taken at eu level in this area, the eu youth strategy 2010-2018 adopted the so-called open method of coordination, whereby member states are free to decide whether to accept or incorporate recommendations made by the eu into their national youth strategies. for many young people, finding a stable and quality job is a challenge and a major obstacle to independence. youth unemployment has decreased in most member states in recent years, but remains a serious concern. in 2015, youth unemployment in europe decreased to 19,7%. the commission recalls that the union industry was not able to obtain sufficient spare capacity to meet the demand for biodiesel. my report highlights the importance of digital, entrepreneurial and soft skills. a stable and high-quality job and a safe environment are very important for establishing independence and starting a responsible family. europe's ageing population requires that young people be activated as a matter of urgency, and that they be encouraged to start families and to adopt children. my report emphasises the importance of the role of the family, the school, religious communities and sport in the healthy development and socialisation of young people, while also highlighting the involvement of local and regional communities in youth policy.

in writing. ‒ the report of the committee on culture and education takes stock of the results of the latest three-year cycle of the eu youth strategy. the eu youth strategy 2010-2018 identifies eight areas of action: education and training, employment and entrepreneurship, health and well-being, participation, voluntary activities, social inclusion, youth and the world, creativity and culture. the two general priorities of the strategy are to facilitate the transition from school to work and to promote the active civic engagement, social inclusion and solidarity of young people. the report finds a wide gap between two groups of young people: those who are purposeful, studying, confident of finding a good job and participating in social, civic and cultural life, and those who have little hope of fulfillment and are at risk of marginalisation. this division threatens social cohesion and long-term sustainable economic growth. and europe, because of its ageing population, urgently needs to activate young people, to encourage responsible family life, to encourage child-rearing. i voted for the resolution.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the evaluation of the eu youth strategy 2013-2015. the text makes a number of important calls to member states to make positive changes in the face of youth unemployment, poverty and other challenges. it is particularly welcome that the rapporteur mentions the specific problems affecting refugee and migrant youth, as well as young girls and women. at the same time, i think it is important to note that the hungarian ruling party, of which the rapporteur is a member, consistently ignores the values set out in the report: its education and employment policies make the future of generations impossible, and, instead of teaching european union knowledge and values, it makes it difficult for many to integrate into society with xenophobic, exclusionary messages. i therefore urge the rapporteur to start implementing the positive recommendations summarised in his report with great energy in his party's domestic policy.

in writing. ‒ it is of the utmost importance to me that the resources of the cap actually reach the farmers. i was forced to reject the andrieu report on the link between the common agricultural policy and job creation, together with my hungarian colleagues from the people's party. i did so despite the fact that the text proposes a strong and adequately funded common agricultural policy, an objective which is fully in line with the interests of hungarian farmers. however, the report also includes provisions which directly jeopardise the future financing of the cap. paragraphs 21 and 77 of the report suggest that agricultural resources should also be used to support social and demographic projects. it is of the utmost importance to us that the resources of the cap actually reach the farmers. we cannot therefore allow the management of crises caused by social and demographic change to be covered by direct payments or rural development funds, either on a voluntary or compulsory basis. the financing of social issues has no place in the common agricultural policy and, therefore, union support for the most deprived persons was excluded from this policy in 2013. unfortunately, the same proposal has also been included in the omnibus package of proposals for the proposed amendment of the eu legislation on the structural funds and the cap. here too, we will take consistent action to prevent the diversion of rural development funds from the structural funds and between them, even if it is voluntary.

in writing. ‒ the committee on agriculture and rural development reports that rural areas cover more than 77% of the eu's territory and that many jobs in these areas depend on agriculture and the agri-food sector. agriculture and agri-food account for 6% of eu gdp, representing 15 million businesses and 46 million jobs. it points out that the economic crisis has hit rural areas hardest, and that these areas have experienced unprecedented declines due to austerity policies. the report urges change in the light of the fact that in 2014, 13% of beneficiaries received 74% of the cap direct payments. as small farms are more labour-intensive and 53% of those employed on farms are classified as small farms, this is clearly not helping job creation within agricultural production. looking ahead, the report advocates modernisation and investment and attributes tourism an important role in solving rural problems. it is of the opinion that direct payments under the cap should be granted only to persons whose main activity is agriculture and that in future cap resources should provide more support to slow down the disappearance of small and medium-sized farms and enterprises which are concentrated in producer organisations. i voted for the bill.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report because i believe that one of the main objectives of the cap is to create jobs in rural areas. unfortunately, we have seen a significant decline in employment in these areas over the past decades, particularly in the eastern and central european regions. this was despite the fact that a number of job-creating measures were introduced through the various funds. in my view, efficiency is hampered in some member states by blatant government corruption, and the resources devoted to job creation are not able to effectively change the situation. small farms' cooperatives should be supported, agricultural employment should be made attractive, and the interests of young people should be taken into account. the future of rural areas does not depend solely on agriculture, i agree that the range of activities of farms should be diversified in order to achieve sustainable business development and that young people and women should be involved as much as possible. providing basic services and connectivity can help to maintain the population and avoid depopulation. the direction we take can be defined at the guideline level at most, but real solutions need to be found in bottom-up initiatives. member states should introduce more targeted measures to create rural jobs, all with strong central control.

in writing. according to a recent survey, 80% of hungarians would abolish the clock. although the survey is not representative, it does reflect the opinion of the people. most of them are in the dark about the time change twice a year, in spring and autumn. they don't understand why it's necessary. the majority of respondents to the survey mentioned imbalances and difficult transitions as their primary problem. now, a number of studies have shown that the economic reasons that were stated in the past are not necessarily relevant, and that we have to expect negative and unpleasant outcomes alongside the positive outcomes. for humans, the problem is the changeover to daylight saving time in early spring, as waking up earlier disrupts people's circadian rhythms, leading to fatigue and insomnia. the disruption caused by this changeover is also not negligible from a transport point of view. long-distance buses and trains lose an hour at the spring changeover while they wait an hour at the autumn restoration at the stations to adjust to the restored time. the safety aspect is also worth mentioning, since waking up earlier can lead to fatigue, increased inattention, and thus increased accidents. few provisions have such a unified citizen position. we can't ignore the majority opinion. i therefore ask the commission to review this provision in the light of the current economic, health and safety conditions.

in writing. it is not right that european citizens do not feel safe within the eu. russian aggression, the threat of terrorism, the eu's common border guard and the lack of a european army reinforce this feeling. it is therefore not a diabolical idea that if the eu has a central budget, a common foreign policy - and the line is still long - then eu soldiers should protect our external borders, be responsible for the security of european citizens. the shock brexit vote and the decline of nato only reinforce this need for a european defence community. it is time for europe to take responsibility for its own security. with a common eu army, a european military headquarters, a rapid international response force, a defence council of defence ministers, europe can be a much more confident superpower. with a joint army, we can show aggressive neighbouring powers, like putin's russia in recent years, that we are serious about protecting the eu's values and borders. having an eu army means two things: the eu's voice will be much stronger on the international stage, and there will never be war between european nations.
in writing. the political and military necessity for the creation of a european defence union was created by the deteriorating security environment in the eu over the years, the threat from our southern and eastern neighbourhood, and new types of security challenges. i support a swift eu decision-making to this end, as the main purpose of establishing european defence autonomy is to take responsibility for the security of eu member states, especially in the face of the unbridled and unfounded threats of putin's russia following the example of the ukrainian aggression. the ep has an important role to play in building the necessary political will, because the eu's solidarity in defence cannot be relied on by national governments alone. the one-sided, selfish approach to solidarity, the neglect of the ability to defend oneself, has never prevented the leaders of some countries from taking the guarantees of their allies' defence for granted. there are also member states - such as hungary under the orbán regime - where existing defence capabilities are used for anti-democratic domestic policy purposes (mass control, policing, border barrier construction) that are contrary to eu values. we also expect the european defence union to protect our common european values and to preserve the union's prestige as an international standard-bearer of democracy and human rights. i therefore urge that, as soon as the preparation of the defence union is under way, appropriate political and legal safeguards be built into the system to prevent such unfair behaviour by member states.
in writing. water transport plays a key role in connecting the different regions of the european union in an environmentally friendly and more energy-efficient way, which can also include the use of new, innovative technologies such as solar and wind energy. i would stress that better use of available capacity for waterborne passenger transport can not only help reduce congestion and co2 emissions, but also improve air quality and overall provide better transport services. a form of transport can be developed which also benefits tourism, as it allows tourism to flourish along the waterway. it can also help boost the economy of a lesser-known region, create new jobs and create small businesses. it is very important to me that the majority of passengers on domestic shipping travel on ships that meet common eu safety standards. this requires appropriate training for staff, which is accepted throughout europe. i regard the importance of this report as a positive and i will support it with my vote.
madam president, i would like to welcome the agreement in principle on visa-free travel for ukraine, which i hope will be followed soon by a positive conclusion to the process. ukraine has been on the path of european integration for two years, and the education reform on the agenda, which would amend the article on the language of instruction in the education act to the detriment of national minorities, is a cause for concern. according to the draft law, students of a particular nationality would have the right to receive education in their mother tongue, along with the ukrainian language, only at the primary and secondary levels, and only in places where the national minority in question lives in a block. human rights and fundamental freedoms and the rights of national minorities are important elements of the eu-ukraine association agreement. the draft law thus contradicts international obligations, but also violates the constitutional rights of ukrainian national minorities. i hope that this non-european process, which represents a major setback in the practice of minority law, can be stopped and that ukraine will strive to become a state of law respecting its minorities.

in writing. increasing competitiveness and economic development require investment incentives. the commission's investment plan envisaged the mobilisation of at least eur 315 billion of additional investment over three years and the restoration of investments to pre-crisis levels. while the commission is trying to prove the success of the european fund for strategic investments, i think it is important to stress that the fund also raises a number of problems. firstly, the audit powers of the eu institutions are reduced for all financial instruments, so-called financial resources outsourced from the eu budget, and the possible market-correcting effects are not known. on the other hand, the conditions and criteria for obtaining funds are much less transparent than in the other areas of implementation, which is further reinforced by the reference to bank notes. furthermore, the investment fund approach focuses strictly on the financial return of projects, ignoring broader or cross-cutting socio-economic policy considerations. i consider that improving the investment environment is essential to supporting european investment. we need to increase the predictability of the regulatory environment, expand and diversify funding sources, reduce administrative burdens and identify additional challenges that are the main impediments to a recovery in investment.
in writing. since the crisis, investment figures have shown a very different picture. unfortunately, during the discussion of the proposals for the semester, it became clear that investment continues to be hampered by both regulatory and non-regulatory challenges. it is therefore important to mention that identifying and addressing challenges to investment should be part of efforts to improve framework conditions, reduce administrative barriers and eliminate regulatory bottlenecks. i welcome the fact that the european commission has started to explore again in this cycle the policy areas and tools that can provide an overview of the main challenges that are holding back investment at national level. i also believe that the analysis of the challenges identified in the annual growth survey should be continued in the context of the european semester. i believe that it is time to re-launch dialogue with the member states - including in the form of thematic discussions in the council and in council committees - in order to identify these challenges and possible steps and measures to overcome them, otherwise the european semester process will not be able to fulfil the role we intended it to play when we created it.

in writing. money laundering has become one of the most profitable and largest businesses in the world today. according to the imf, the volume of money laundering is equivalent to 2 to 5% of the combined gdp of all countries on earth. as a result, the subject has received a steady increase in professional interest internationally in recent years. the legislative process is producing new results at both international and national level, giving lawmakers a number of additional tasks and providing theoretical specialists with new research topics. this is the case with this innovative proposal, which i welcome and i am pleased that this report contains a series of measures to combat effectively money laundering by criminal organisations. the proposed initiatives will finally coordinate and integrate existing standards and create a more targeted and focused risk-based approach to combat money laundering more effectively across the eu.

in writing. ‒ i would like to draw attention to the fact that 30% of the world's seas are overfished, with significant environmental pressures from multiple sources, and that marine fish stocks are therefore at risk. it is understandable that the european union is forced to restrict sea fishing to the extent necessary to maintain marine fish stocks. the cfp should therefore pay much more attention to sustainable fisheries, i.e. aquaculture, and in particular freshwater fisheries. a significant part of the hungarian wetlands is located in natura 2000 areas. these fish farms do not represent any threat to the natural values of these areas. in fact, in many cases it is our closed systems of wetlands that have created and preserved unique associations of aquatic habitats. therefore, freshwater aquaculture should be given priority and maximum support from the union. in view of the above, i supported the adoption of the report.
in writing. ‒ in line with the guidelines of the european people's party, i supported, together with my fidesz colleagues, the adoption without a vote of the dodds report on the long-term plan for cod stocks and the fisheries exploiting those stocks. this step approved the final text of the legislation in the second reading agreement concluded by the ep and the council. the new legislation is necessary because the old fishing plan used a complex catch system. this has resulted in a decline in cod stocks in practice. the new rules provide more flexibility in terms of tacs and quotas and streamline the rules on the landing obligation. progress has also been made in tightening the return of unusable fish. 30% of the world's oceans are overfished, and marine fish stocks are in danger. it is therefore understandable that the european union is forced to restrict marine fisheries appropriately in order to maintain marine fish stocks. the cfp should therefore pay much more attention to sustainable fisheries, i.e. aquaculture, and in particular freshwater fisheries. a significant part of the hungarian wetlands is located in natura 2000 areas. these fish farms do not represent any threat to the natural values of these areas. in fact, in many cases it is our closed systems of wetlands that have created and preserved unique associations of aquatic habitats. therefore, freshwater aquaculture should be given priority and maximum support from the union.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report, which aims to adapt and clarify the agreement establishing the principles of the common fisheries policy and supporting its implementation. the draft was blocked by both the european commission and the european parliament in the previous parliamentary term, as the european council had unilaterally adopted measures on fishing plans for european waters. this was followed by a ruling by the european court of justice, which found that the european council had erred in its allocation of the annual capital plan and in its unilateral adoption of part of it. in short, the council has bypassed the ep as a co-decision-making body in the area of fisheries policy. following the court's decision, the s&d group was actively involved in the development of the principles of the cap, such as the introduction of the precautionary principle instead of annual catch limits, supplemented by a system of fishing licences and fishing capacity. the draft regulation would also put an immediate end to the days-at-sea cod fishing practice, which is a major contributor to depletion. this material is fully in line with the reformed common fisheries policy, which will come into force on 1 january 2017, and will ensure legal certainty for fishermen.

in writing. ‒ on 12 september 2012, the commission presented its proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending regulation (ec) no 1342/2008 with a view to adapting and clarifying the provisions of regulation (ec) no 1342/2008. on 19 december 2012, the council adopted a regulation without incorporating all the provisions of the proposal for a regulation, with article 43 (3) tfeu as legal basis and adopting only the amendments to articles 9 and 12 of regulation (ec) no 1342/2008. i have followed the group's position on this matter with some hesitation.
in writing. ‒ the report addresses the fight against tax evasion and tax avoidance and is a follow-up to the 2011 council directive on administrative cooperation in the field of taxation. the swissleaks, luxleaks, panama papers and bahamian leaks - which are unique examples of a global phenomenon - have highlighted the urgent need for greater tax transparency and much closer judicial coordination and cooperation. this directive emphasises that the commission should analyse the possible role of the banking system and financial services providers in facilitating money laundering. the union could intervene, with its increased powers in the financial and banking field, through a regulation on stricter controls and transparency of banking and financial transactions. i voted in favour of the action taken by the committee on anti-money laundering and tax evasion. however, the underlying reason is the financial liberalisation of the 1990s, which, if maintained, will always allow tax avoidance and money laundering, albeit to a lesser extent than before.
in writing. ‒ money laundering has become one of the most profitable and largest businesses in the world today. according to the imf, the volume of money laundering is between 2 and 5% of the combined gdp of all countries on earth. as a result, the subject has received a steady increase in professional interest internationally in recent years. the legislative process is producing new results at both international and national level, giving lawmakers a number of additional tasks and providing theoretical specialists with new research topics. this is the case with this innovative proposal, which i welcome and i am pleased that this report contains a series of measures to combat effectively money laundering by criminal organisations. the proposed initiatives will finally coordinate and integrate existing standards and create a more targeted and focused risk-based approach to combat money laundering more effectively across the eu. unfortunately, the interconnection of registers is essential for the usability of this information due to the cross-border nature of business transactions and the interconnectedness of the internal market. it is therefore urgently necessary to link the registers and make them available to the authorities and obliged entities. so that's the most important thing we have to do.

in writing. ‒ the presentation concerns the annual report of the european central bank for the year 2015. the report highlights that the euro area remains characterised by high unemployment, excessively low inflation and significant macroeconomic imbalances, including a current account deficit. productivity growth in the euro area is very low, reflecting the decline in investment since the start of the crisis, the failure to implement structural reforms and weak domestic demand. the report essentially calls for monetary integration, which we do not agree with, because on the one hand it does not have the economic conditions, as some of the amendments suggest, and on the other hand it imposes an integration which we ourselves reject.
in writing. ‒ the ecb's role will be further enhanced, as it will be given new tasks in a wide range of areas, and thus more attention will be paid to its activities. i therefore consider it important to work even more closely with parliament in order to achieve genuine democratic control. i welcome the fact that, as in previous years, this year's report has insisted on the fact, clearly laid down in the treaties, that the central bank's sole and main role is to maintain the stability of the exchange rate - and thus the single currency, the euro - and thus to put the ecb's policy in the right context. i also think it is important to recognise that without the ecb's long-term refinancing operations last year, europe would have had to expect much greater exchange rate volatility. consequently, a much larger money supply would probably have accumulated in the markets, often in the form of bad stocks, which could have led to inflationary growth and then to excessive exchange rate growth. however, i see the ecb also having to start executing these one-off money market operations immediately as soon as the stress in the banking sector eases and if economic indicators relating to inflation make this decision possible. as regards the future, i agree with the importance of the introduction, which should reflect the diversity within the national banking sector.

in writing. the report argues that deeper monetary integration can be the cure for all problems. but if that were true, it would have helped by now, but that's not what we see in the real world, but the unemployment rate in the eu, according to official figures, is somewhere between 4.6% and 24.9% in the member countries that use the euro, real growth is around 1.5%, and investment is down. the overall picture is dominated by severe macroeconomic imbalances characterised by low inflation and a current account deficit. the high level of non-performing loans and undercapitalisation in the banking sector is particularly marked in some member states. from the looks of it, we're gonna have to find another cure for the underlying problem.
in writing. ‒ the european central bank has submitted its report for 2015. the draft resolution of the committee on economic and monetary affairs and industrial policy seeks to address the economic problems of the euro area: high unemployment, excessively low inflation, significant macroeconomic imbalances, declining levels of investment, lagging structural reforms and, as a consequence, very low productivity growth. it supports the ecb president's view that without appropriate fiscal policies at the level of the member states and ambitious and socially balanced structural reform programmes, the single monetary policy alone cannot stimulate aggregate demand. it is committed to the rapid, gradual and complete completion of banking union. it is concerned about the risk of a property and asset bubble due to the extremely low (negative) interest rate policy and recommends that the ecb be called upon to take appropriate action. i voted for the bill.
in writing. ‒ the ecb's role will be further enhanced, as it will be given new tasks in a wide range of areas, and thus more attention will be paid to its activities. i therefore consider it important to work even more closely with parliament in order to achieve genuine democratic control. i welcome the fact that, as in previous years, this year's report has insisted on the fact, clearly laid down in the treaties, that the central bank's sole and main role is to maintain the stability of the exchange rate - and thus of the single currency, the euro - and that this has helped to put the ecb's policy in the right context. i also think it is important to recognise that without the ecb's long-term refinancing operation last year, europe would have had to expect much greater exchange rate volatility. consequently, a much larger money supply would probably have accumulated in the markets, often in the form of bad stocks, which could have led to inflationary growth and then to excessive exchange rate growth. however, i see the ecb also having to start executing these one-off money market operations immediately as soon as the stress in the banking sector eases and if economic indicators relating to inflation make this decision possible. as regards the future, i agree with the importance of the introduction, which should reflect the diversity within the national banking sector.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the european parliament's report on the annual report of the european central bank for 2015, and i also welcome the work of the european central bank in protecting the euro, which has proved indispensable to the preservation of the financial stability of the euro area. i also agree with the report that without appropriate fiscal policies at member state level and ambitious and socially balanced structural reform programmes, the single monetary policy alone cannot stimulate aggregate demand. i now call on the ecb to carefully assess the risks of the emergence of a property and asset bubble due to ultra-low negative interest rate policies in particular in certain large cities and to submit proposals together with the esrb specifically for the development of macroprudential recommendations to address this problem. i also agree with the statement that it is essential to continue the monetary dialogue in order to ensure the transparency of monetary policy and of parliament towards the wider public.
in writing. ‒ with regard to the possible withdrawal of the united kingdom from the european union, president draghi has rightly stated that the extent to which the economic outlook will change will depend to a large extent on the timing, the course and the final outcome of the negotiations ahead. the euro area has been resilient so far, but this uncertainty factor could make the baseline scenario look negative, the document says. i voted in favour of the group's position in the final vote.
in writing. ‒ the report is about a green paper on financial services for the general public. it is based on the fact that financial exclusion is a widespread and serious problem across europe, making life very difficult for people who lack adequate access to at least the most basic financial services. the green paper on retail financial services therefore focuses mainly on financial services offered to citizens seeking cross-border services. it believes that efforts should continue to be made to dismantle barriers and curb existing protectionist trends that hinder innovation in consumer financial services. i disagree with the report. brexit has shown that unfounded integration has its limits, and that crossing them can lead to disintegration. the main problem is that while they want to centralize everything and bring it under the control of brussels, the bureaucrats in brussels are not responsible for the economic and social problems that this centralized integration causes. (for example, the indebtedness of peripheral countries or the decline in living standards.) we say no to any further attempts at integration of this kind, and the union's coat of arms must be re-buttoned from the beginning.
in writing. ‒ the political importance of european integration of the services market should not be underestimated, especially at a time when the union's unity, the promotion of cohesion within and outside the euro area and the avoidance of unions within the union are all essential. the creation of a common market for financial services is a joint responsibility of all member states. i am aware of the different situations in the member states, the difficulties encountered in opening up the market and the importance of recognising the progress made. however, double standards and exceptions are not allowed under any circumstances. the principle of the internal market without practical steps would undermine the confidence of european citizens in the eu's reform agenda. most importantly, the members of the european council and the competitiveness council should be entrusted with the task of keeping the internal market in services regularly on the political agenda, alongside a clear timetable for removing obstacles to free movement. in the end, europe can only embark on the path of growth if member states commit themselves to a genuinely free and open internal market in services for the benefit of all citizens.

in writing. the report's premise is largely correct given that financial exclusion is a widespread and serious problem across europe, making life difficult for people who lack adequate access to the most basic financial services. the details should be supported as a welcome objective to enable consumers to identify and compare safe, sustainable and simple products in the range available to them. but the report as a whole is not acceptable, because as brexit has shown, unfounded integration has its limits and can even lead to disintegration. the power-hungry centralization of the brussels bureaucracy, coupled with a complete lack of accountability, proved to be a dead end, as expected. we are faced with a host of unresolved social and economic problems, primarily in the peripheral countries: unemployment, falling living standards, debt, etc.
in writing. ‒ on 10 december 2015, the commission published a green paper entitled 'financial services for consumers: better products, more choice and more opportunities for consumers and businesses'. the report by the economic and monetary affairs committee concludes that the creation of a well-functioning single market for financial services to consumers is a major project, but one that is worth the effort. it suggests that parliament should take the view that the green paper was presented at the right time, that the commission took the right steps and that the procedure chosen was the right method. it shall also take into account the challenges to be faced in order to promote the agenda for financial services to the public. i supported the bill.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the green paper on financial services for consumers. i welcome the public consultation on the green paper on financial services for consumers. it is appropriate that the report addresses the additional opportunities offered by digitalisation, which will also create new opportunities for consumers, investors and smes in terms of competition, cross-border activities and innovation. i also agree with the rapporteur that digitalisation alone is not enough to create a genuine european market for financial services to consumers. indeed, many barriers, such as different tax, social, judicial, health, contracting and consumer protection systems, and different languages and cultures, cannot be overcome by digitisation alone. one of the most important points of the report, in my view, is that it highlights the need for an adequate legal framework to protect consumers and that it draws attention to the fact that financial and non-financial data collected from consumers from different sources are increasingly being used by financial services providers for different purposes. i welcome the fact that the report emphasises that the use of personal data and large data sets relating to financial services providers should be in line with union data protection legislation.
in writing. ‒ with regard to the initiative on financial services for consumers, the rapporteur believes that the commission has taken the right steps and that the arbitration procedure is the right approach. i supported him with my vote.
in writing. ‒ the security situation both within europe and in the surrounding region has deteriorated significantly in recent times. the main security threats currently facing the union are terrorism, hybrid threats, economic volatility, cyber and energy insecurity, organised crime and climate change. no single member state or organisation can tackle the unprecedented new challenges on its own. in this situation, the eu must do all it can and find the means to guarantee security. the report stresses that europe needs political will and determination to guarantee its long-term security. it also urged the eu member states to make use of the possibilities offered by the treaty of lisbon for the common security and defence policy (csdp), in particular through permanent structured cooperation. the defence union must be effectively funded and coordinated with nato. in addition, a meeting of defence ministers should be established within the council to provide permanent political leadership and coordinate the development of a european defence union. the increasingly negative perception of risks and threats in europe makes the establishment of a european defence union urgent. this is mainly due to the deteriorating security of the european union's borders, especially those shared with its eastern and southern neighbours. in view of the above, i voted in favour of the adoption of the report.

in writing. ‒ in the longer term, my party, the democratic coalition, is thinking about making the european union a federation, creating a united states of europe. it is clear that the creation of a european defence union is an essential step in this direction. however, the establishment of a defence union is also needed in the short term. it is becoming increasingly clear that the migration crisis can only be effectively tackled by a common policy, including its protection aspects. the union must also assume its responsibility for dealing with crises that threaten the security of the world, which again requires the formulation of a common defence policy. nor can the situation continue indefinitely whereby nato is the main guarantor of the security of the member states of the european union, but the burden of this is disproportionately placed on the united states of america. the election of donald trump as president suggests that the us will quickly end this unilateralism, and a possible move like this cannot come unprepared to the european union. moreover, the us will obviously be more willing to take more deliberate steps in this direction if the eu is more serious about doing its part to protect itself and its security. finally, the imminent withdrawal of the main adversary, the united kingdom, from the eu, provides a better opportunity than ever to take more decisive steps towards the creation of a european defence union. i voted for the bill.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of a resolution based on a parliamentary report arguing in favour of the creation of a european defence union. i believe that the objective conditions for a greater degree of defence autonomy in europe are in place: the eu, with the existing capabilities of each member state, could in principle be the strongest defence alliance in the world. from a military and economic perspective, the sheer number of overlaps and parallels would clearly require a concertation of capabilities and assets, with the aim of achieving more security for less money. the treaty of lisbon and the series of political decisions taken under the cfsp also provide the necessary legal basis for the completion of union solidarity in the field of defence, both under the cfsp and the edu. the political and military necessity of the edu was created by the deteriorating security environment in the eu over the years, new types of security challenges, terrorist, cyber and hybrid threats, and above all the military-political threat in our immediate southern and eastern neighbourhood. i believe that the report, in addition to explaining these reasons, contains useful organisational and legislative proposals for the establishment of the defence union. i am convinced that the ep will make a decisive contribution to building the political will needed at eu level through this resolution and its further political and legislative activities.

in writing. ‒ small and medium-sized enterprises in transport play a significant role in the operation of european roads and make a significant contribution to the eu economy and job creation. the report we have just voted on is about the opportunities and challenges facing these companies, and it is therefore very important that it is on the agenda for the plenary. however, i regret to say that i find that this positive line is contradicted by paragraph 37 of the report, which calls into question the derogation for light vehicles on the grounds that they are unjustifiably present in international traffic. however, it should be pointed out that there are no reliable data on this and that if these carriers were to comply with all the requirements for vehicles over 3,5 tonnes, this could lead to disproportionate financial and administrative overheads. therefore, i cannot support this point in the report. but overall i agree with the report and i voted in favour of it.

in writing. ‒ the draft resolution of the committee on transport and tourism takes as its starting point the fact that in europe a large proportion of commuters travel by road, causing bottlenecks, congestion and delays on the roads of europe's cities. this is despite the fact that europe's geography, its many rivers, waterways, estuaries, long coastlines and islands offer extraordinary opportunities for water transport. there are many areas in europe where travelling by ferry or cruise ship would be more sustainable, easier and faster, and would enhance the social and economic well-being of the region, while protecting europe's environment and the health of its citizens. in order to ensure the efficient and effective use of the available capacities, the commission should develop a european strategy for the development of the maritime transport sector. i voted for the bill.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report because i agree that waterborne passenger transport, including sea ferries, inland ferries, dams and leisure cruises, is essential to achieving a more sustainable and efficient european transport sector. i agree with the author that better use of existing capacity and further development of waterborne passenger transport can not only help reduce congestion and co2 emissions, but also improve air quality and provide better transport services overall. the report describes that water transport is already one of the most sustainable ways of travelling and i agree that there is further potential to make ships even more environmentally friendly and energy efficient. but i think that we can only achieve this by researching innovative technologies in areas such as solar and wind, onshore electricity and alternative fuels. the report also offers a solution by identifying the eu funds available for these such as the cohesion, structural, regional, interreg, horizon 2020, the european network and transport facility, the ten-t and the esf.
in writing. ‒ waterborne passenger transport, including sea ferries, inland ferries, dams and leisure voyages, is essential to achieving a more sustainable and efficient european transport sector, supported by policies on safety, environmental standards, cross-border cooperation and competitiveness, and on quality of service, passenger rights and accessibility. i voted for it.

in writing. ‒ eighty-nine meps tabled a motion for a resolution initiating proceedings before the european court of justice on the compatibility of the eu-canada free trade agreement (ceta) with the eu's basic treaties. in particular, the court was asked to give an opinion on the investor-state dispute settlement mechanism (isds). this procedure allows global companies to sue member countries in a private court if they consider that the state restriction on their activities has caused them to lose profits. the restriction may be for environmental, public health or other socioeconomic reasons, in the enforcement of which a sovereign government acts with the mandate received from the population. nevertheless, its decisions are subject to appeal, and the said court proceedings often award substantial sums to the investment firm. the european parliament voted a stunning 419 to 258 against and 22 abstentions to reject the motion. it is clear that the 'no' vote represents the interests of global economic operators, even at the cost of an international agreement which they support, which may be contrary to the eu treaties. of course, i voted yes to the motion.
in writing. ‒ today's vote was on a procedural question on the canada-european union free trade agreement. the entry into force of the fta by the union is expected to be voted on by the european parliament in december this year, which will be the date for a decision on the merits. in addition to the european parliament, member states, among others, have the possibility of seeking the opinion of the court of justice of the european union on this or any other question relating to the agreement, even after entry into force by the union.

in writing. ‒ poor air quality is the leading environmental cause of death in the european union, leading to 400 000 premature deaths per year. the directive on the reduction of national emissions of certain atmospheric pollutants aims to reduce air pollution and its harmful effects on human health and the environment throughout the union. the new rules require member states to reduce their emissions of sulphur dioxide (so2), nitrogen oxides (nox), volatile organic compounds (nmvocs), ammonia (nh3) and fine particulate matter (volatile dust with a diameter of less than 2,5 micrometres). the biggest problem for hungary from the outset was the level of its 2030 reduction commitment for ammonia and small particulate matter (pm2,5) emissions related to residential heating, which affect agricultural performance. it was also disputed whether the proposal includes a regulation of methane emissions, given that methane is not an air pollutant but a greenhouse gas and would therefore be better addressed in the area of climate protection. as a result of our position during the lengthy negotiations, the targets in the adopted version can be met from a technical point of view and, under pressure from the member states, methane was finally removed from the regulation. although the dutch presidency pursued the negotiations with considerable effort and used unusual procedural techniques to force the final decision, i voted in favour of the agreement in the light of the above.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report because i believe it makes ambitious proposals to the european commission's proposal. important compromises have been reached in the legislative process of the ep, and i trust that the member states will actively support it. in fact, i think that if we could take faster and more decisive action to reduce emissions, the 2030 target could be reached even sooner. as the report states, air pollution causes 400 000 premature deaths in europe each year, but it does not stop there: the entire ecosystem is threatened by emissions from human activities. everything has a huge cost, so the sooner we get rid of it, the sooner we can spend this huge amount of money on something else, like a proper health care system or a real education that gives you real knowledge. i believe that a comprehensive approach covering all sectors is needed.

in writing. ‒ fact-based policymaking should be a cornerstone of eu law. legislation should be based on detailed and comprehensive impact assessments that show why a piece of legislation addresses the central question of the necessity and proportionality of the proposal and how it measures whether action at union level would be most effective. the answer is clear: air quality is a major transboundary problem for human health and the environment, which seriously affects the lives of all eu citizens and requires immediate action. i supported him with my vote.
in writing. ‒ the global financial crisis that erupted in 2007 highlighted the problems and shortcomings of banks' risk and crisis management practices. in 2011, the basel committee on banking supervision published its basel iii framework, which contains new global regulatory standards for the capital adequacy and liquidity of banks and their implementation plan. most importantly, banks need to raise their current capital. they'll have to increase the capital ratio from 4% to 6%. the core capital must cover the bank's revenue losses in a crisis situation. the other element of basel iii is the appropriate design of liquidity requirements. financial institutions shall have sufficient liquid assets to cover their so-called net liquidity outflows for 30 days in a situation of severe stress. the motion for a resolution is about finalising the basel iii agreement. the various provisions will be phased in by 2019. i supported the motion for a resolution because it reduces the likelihood of financial crises. but i also want to emphasize that the only way to solve this problem once and for all is to go back to the pre-1990s glass-steagall act, which prohibits commercial banks from having investment banking functions or owning securities firms.
in writing. the causes of the financial crisis that emerged in 2007 are deep-rooted and have been clear to those familiar with the banking system's operational features for some time, with the most superficial manifestations being problems and shortcomings in banks' risk and crisis management practices. in order to avoid further similar crises, partial solutions are offered by the basel iii framework, which includes new global regulatory standards for the capital adequacy and liquidity of banks and the related implementation plan. the resolution is a clear step forward in the financial security of european citizens and should be supported even if a comprehensive solution cannot be achieved in this way.
in writing. ‒ the basel iii agreement of 2010 was an international response to the financial crisis of 2008-2010 developed by the basel committee on banking supervision (bcbs). it was intended to gradually strengthen the operational security of commercial banks, in particular by requiring them to increase the core‐capital ratio from the current 4% to 6%. the draft resolution of the economic and monetary committee on the finalisation of the agreement stresses two principles: firstly, that overall capital requirements should not be significantly increased, while at the same time strengthening the overall financial position of european banks; and secondly, that a level playing field should be ensured at global level, by reducing and not deepening the differences between jurisdictions and banking models. the report notes with concern that the preliminary analysis of the bcbs's recent draft suggests that the reform package at its current stage is not in line with these two principles and recommends calling on the competent bodies to review the proposals in this respect and to ensure that these principles are respected during the finalisation and monitoring of the new rules. i voted for the bill.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution on the finalisation of the basel iii agreement, and i welcome the work of the basel committee on banking supervision (bcbs) on consolidating global standards and principles for the prudential regulation of banks. i agree with the rapporteur that the rescue packages for banks during the crisis must not be repeated and that banks must be sufficiently recapitalised to support the real economy. i also welcome the call in the motion for greater transparency and accountability and for continued dialogue between the institutions to enhance the legitimacy and recognition of bcbs decisions. i also welcome the fact that one of the important points in the motion for a resolution is that, unlike other jurisdictions, banks play a key role in the european economy in financing households and businesses, especially smes. this should continue to be taken into account while seeking to diversify the forms of financing of the european economy.
in writing. ‒ the proposal calls for, inter alia, a sound framework for financial stability and growth that is comprehensive and balanced, enabling it to include dynamic supervisory practices and not focusing on static regulation of mainly quantitative aspects. i voted in favour of the s&d group's position in the final vote.
in writing. ‒ the european security environment has deteriorated significantly in recent times, becoming more flexible, complex, dangerous and unpredictable. these threats are taking on an increasingly diverse range of forms, both traditional and hybrid. the security of the eu member states is closely interlinked, yet member states react to common threats and risks in a disjointed and fragmented way. this lack of coordination is one of the vulnerabilities of union action. to address these problems, a thorough and substantial review of the csdp (common security and defence policy) is needed to enable the eu and its member states to make a decisive contribution to the security of the union. the report stresses that the establishment of permanent structured cooperation (article 42 (6) of the treaty on european union) would allow for the creation of a self-defence or a permanent self-defence structure. through csdp missions, the eu could intervene across the full spectrum of crisis management, including in the areas of crisis prevention and resolution. in addition, the eu should encourage member states to meet nato's capability targets, which require defence spending to be increased over time to at least 2% of gdp. the instruments of the csdp also promote better cooperation and coordination between member states, in particular in the fight against terrorism. finally, csdp missions including border support, capacity building, military training missions and naval operations contribute to international peace and stability. i voted in favour of the report.

in writing. ‒ the draft resolution of the committee on foreign affairs notes that the european security environment has deteriorated significantly, outlines the new security challenges facing the union and calls on the eu to adapt to these security challenges, in particular by making more effective use of the csdp instruments in line with other external and internal instruments, and calls for better cooperation and coordination between member states, in particular in the fight against terrorism. as no country can face the current security challenges alone, it calls for a thorough and substantial review of the common security and defence policy, so that the eu and its member states can make a decisive contribution to the union's security, to the management of international crises and to the exercise of the eu's strategic autonomy. it urges close cooperation with nato and that the eu encourage its member states to meet nato's capability targets, which require defence spending to be increased to at least 2% of gdp. it called for the deepening of european defence cooperation and the establishment of a permanent eu command for csdp missions and operations, both civilian and military. i voted for the bill.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report because it gives an accurate, realistic, yet critical picture of the problems facing the eu's common security and defence policy, while also indicating possible ways forward, in particular by creating a greater degree of defence autonomy for europe. it points out that the mass of overlaps and parallels would clearly require coordination of defence capabilities and assets of the member states and a substantial use of existing capabilities and assets at european level (e.g. battlegroup units). the political and military rationale for a closer and more autonomous european defence is given convincing support in this report by the deteriorating security environment in the eu over the years, the new types of security challenges, the threats of terrorism, cyber and hybrid threats, and above all the military policy threat in our immediate southern and eastern neighbourhood. in my own experience, the report also suggests that governments cannot be the only ones to rely on solidarity between member states in defence matters, because the unilateral, selfish approach to eu solidarity, the disregard for their own defence capabilities, does not prevent the leaders of some countries from taking the defence guarantees of their allies for granted. i believe that this report and this parliament's decision can help to raise awareness at eu level of the need to build political and legal safeguards into the future csdp and defence union to prevent such unilateral behaviour by member states.

in writing. it is common for reporting agents to create a link by making something less acceptable a vote on the basis of health, human or minority rights, the interests of small and medium-sized enterprises, etc. i've seen a lot of stuff on the ep, but i've never seen anything this rough. to link in one report the activities of the national media of a rule of law with the propaganda machine of the world's current largest terrorist organization, equating the two, is mind-boggling. but this was further exacerbated by the fact that the eu's propaganda campaign was used by the rapporteur to fight the state actor. he doesn't want to harass terrorists, because he thinks they're harmless. anyone with eyes and ears open to the world can see the unprecedented media dominance of overseas-funded ngos and the press, but also the writings of udo ulfkotte and other fact-finders. does this kind of crude propaganda intervention not please the people involved? it is deeply irresponsible, it is blatantly extreme, and it is very sad that the democracy that exists is so deeply flawed.
in writing. ‒ the report of the committee on foreign affairs aims to tackle radicalism and terrorist propaganda through enhanced cooperation between member states and the eu. it specifically addresses two threats: russia's use of existing relations and meetings with eu partners for propaganda purposes and to publicly undermine the union's common position, rather than for genuine dialogue, and the disinformation and radicalisation methods of isil/daesh information warfare. it outlines the eu's strategy against propaganda, which focuses on actively promoting respect for fundamental rights and freedoms, as support for freedom of expression, freedom of assembly, the right of access to information and media independence in neighbouring countries strengthens the eu's counter-propaganda efforts. calls for the strengthening of media pluralism and the objective, impartiality and independence of the media, including non-state actors, in the european union and its neighbourhood, and expresses its consternation at the problems with media independence and freedom in some eu member states; i voted for the bill.
in writing. ‒ today, in line with the position of the european people's party, i voted with my fidesz colleagues in favour of a report to strengthen strategic communication to counter anti-eu propaganda by third parties. the document stresses that anti-eu propaganda aims to divide member states, paralyse decision-making processes, undermine the credibility of the eu institutions and undermine the european narrative based on democratic values, human rights and the rule of law. the report calls on the eu and its member states to take consistent action across the union against the hate speech of intolerant, radical preachers, which is a fertile ground for the growth of terrorist organisations such as the islamic state and al-qaeda. the report therefore stresses the importance of quality journalism, education and training for high-quality analysis and calls on the commission to put forward legislative initiatives to combat targeted disinformation more effectively.
in writing. ‒ i have refrained from accepting the report because, while it identifies a major and novel challenge to european integration and peace on the continent, and while it makes proposals to exempt it, it also makes statements with which i cannot identify. however, i was particularly attentive to the russian propaganda efforts described in the report, among others, because they are also strongly present in my own country, in particular with regard to the indications of financial and political support for far-right forces, influence on public opinion and undermining eu membership. this is particularly difficult to counter in this case, as moscow can count on a partner in the orbán regime, not an opponent, who follows and openly praises putin's political methods and essentially implements putin's scenario in migration and eu ambitions. the common eu-wide response outlined in the report is also important in this case because it is an internal phenomenon, the government of an eu member state, which can easily find followers within the union if the union is not able to put a stop to this dangerous political game at the highest level. i believe that this is not only part of, but a precondition for, the effective implementation of the communication strategy against external anti-eu propaganda.
in writing. ‒ today, in line with the position of the european people's party, i voted with my fidesz colleagues in favour of a report to strengthen strategic communication to counter anti-eu propaganda by third parties. the document stresses that anti-eu propaganda aims to divide member states, paralyse decision-making processes, undermine the credibility of the eu institutions and undermine the european narrative based on democratic values, human rights and the rule of law. the report calls on the eu and its member states to take consistent action across the union against the hate speech of intolerant, radical preachers, which is a fertile ground for the growth of terrorist organisations such as the islamic state and al-qaeda. the report therefore stresses the important role of quality journalism, education and training in ensuring high standards of quality analysis and calls on the commission to put forward legislative initiatives to combat targeted disinformation more effectively.
in writing. ‒ the union is committed to ensuring that its action at international level is in line with principles such as democracy, the rule of law, respect for human rights and fundamental freedoms, freedom of the media, access to information, freedom of expression and media pluralism. the union and european values are under attack in many ways, including by russian state propaganda. we have to do something about it. but this proposal was a bad approach, so i abstained.
in writing. ‒ deaf people have the right to participate in politics. there is a need for qualified sign language interpreters to provide unimpeded access to the political process during elections, public consultations and other events. sign language interpreting is not a service, but a basic human right: it is the mother tongue of the person who uses sign language. interpreting enables deaf and deafblind people to live independently and to participate fully and equally in society. the decision invites the commission to examine the situation regarding equal access to education for deaf and hard of hearing children in the member states and to fully implement the insign european pilot project aimed at improving communication between deaf and hard of hearing people and the eu institutions. if one of the elements of the access to education, employment and training triangle is removed, deaf people remain at a disadvantage: interpretation and accessibility play a key role. deaf, deafblind and hard of hearing pupils and their parents should therefore be given the opportunity to learn the national or regional sign language used in their environment, through pre-school services or school education. in hungary, this is guaranteed by law, and it's time to make this a daily practice and for all members of society to pay attention to people with disabilities. i therefore voted in favour of the resolution.

in writing. ‒ the resolution seeks to have the commission withdraw the most extensive renewal of the authorisation for the placing on the market in the union of herbicides containing or containing such an active substance. bentazone is a selective herbicide applied 1 to 15 days after germination of crops, which kills broadleaf weeds. a number of studies have already been published in the united kingdom on benthazone, detailing that benthazone can be diluted in groundwater and, due to the higher concentration it generates, may inhibit not only soil and crops, but also the animal world and, in particular, the reproduction of small mammals. this is an indirect threat to human health, especially since benthazone-containing herbicides are the most widely used herbicides in the eu. it is important to note that in order to refuse the authorisation, efsa again demonstrated in its scientific evaluation that it had carried out a scientific evaluation which was highly questionable from a professional point of view and superficial, ignoring the toxicity to mammals and its examination in the scientific consultation. as the motion calls for the repeal of the commission's marketing authorisation regulation, i supported it.
in writing. ‒ the committee on the environment, public health and food safety has tabled a motion for a resolution on the renewal of the approval of the active substance bentazone under regulation (ec) no 1107/2009 of the european parliament and of the council concerning the placing of plant protection products on the market, and amending the annex to implementing regulation (eu) no 540/2011. the draft resolution proposes to establish that the draft commission implementing regulation exceeds the implementing powers provided for in regulation (ec) no 1107/2009, and that the commission has infringed the provisions of regulation (ec) no 1107/2009 and the precautionary principle as set out in article 191 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union by applying the confirmatory information procedure to the active substance benthazone. the draft proposes that parliament invite the commission to request and assess the relevant missing information before deciding on approval, and to ask it to withdraw its draft implementing regulation and to submit a new draft. i voted for the motion.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution on the renewal of the authorisation of the active substance benthazone as a plant protection product. the current authorisation expires on 30 june 2017 and the european commission has proposed to extend it (until 2032). however, it was suspected that it could be detected in groundwater as a result of intensive use and that it could also have adverse effects on human reproduction. i agree with the motion that these substances should only be used responsibly and in moderation and i consider it important that only renewals of such substances should be decided on the basis of adequate scientific evidence and food safety. if there's any doubt about these chemicals, we can't use them. the motion will not immediately withdraw the authorisation of bentazone, but in the light of the precautionary principle, i am convinced that it should not be renewed immediately. a very quick, serious and comprehensive investigation is needed to prevent this. i do not consider the available assessments to be satisfactory. there are alternative ways of using them effectively and of replacing or reducing the use of traditional forms of farming. last but not least, i believe it is important to strengthen the role of phytosanitary practitioners, to tighten the authorisation procedure and the use in case of suspicion.
