on behalf of the s&d group. - mr president! as in the case of tax evasion and avoidance, the creation of a european vat system free from corruption requires above all political will. only together can member states effectively tackle vat fraud and only by complete agreement can they adopt the rules necessary to remove unnecessary administrative barriers and thus make life easier for european businesses. because the more complex a system is, the easier it is to circumvent. the commission's commitment to the creation of an effective single eu vat area is therefore particularly welcome, especially as the current vat system is not able to prevent fraud. i would add that in the case of the single eu vat area, we do not necessarily agree with pilot projects which introduce different logics into the vat system. the commission estimates that vat revenue is lost every year by about 170 billion euros, of which cross-border fraud alone is worth at least 50 billion euros, although i fear that the real figures are much higher, in some places they say 1000 billion euros a year, which we lose because of our bad or malfunctioning vat system. the member states must therefore do all they can to ensure that information is exchanged effectively between them, since without this and without the coordination of tax policies between member states, the fight against tax fraud and tax evasion will never be effective. it is also appropriate that the commission closely monitor the functioning of national tax authorities, avoiding unfortunate cases such as the one in hungary, where the national tax and customs office was reported by its own staff for assisting, or at least ignoring, the fraud of tax amounts of more than eur 3 billion per year in the case of large domestic and multinational companies enjoying the protection of government circles. the hungarian government has ended this case with a public interest litigation, and we see the responsibility of the member states.

in writing. ‒ jordan is one of the countries most directly affected by the syrian crisis, due to its geographical location. its economy, which is based primarily on services and industry, has been sensitive to the military actions affecting the region since 2011. in this difficult situation, however, jordan stands out as a country that has welcomed a significant number of displaced persons. the conflicts in syria and iraq are depriving jordanian products of their traditional markets. the ongoing conflicts in neighbouring countries continued to disrupt jordan's external trade in 2015, with growth slowing down (2.4%) and the remaining external financing needs for 2016-2017 estimated at usd 3,2 billion. in the first half of 2016, the unemployment rate reached a record high of 14,6% of the active population (33% of young people in the labour force, 23,7% of women in the labour force). in order to overcome the economic difficulties, the european union must ensure that it supports its partner, whose policy on the reception of refugees is commendable. the objective is to ensure that the macro-financial assistance programme is put into effect as soon as possible in order to allow jordan to benefit effectively from it during this crucial period. in my view, the genuinely needy people who have been forced to flee as a result of the war and the neighbouring countries that have taken them in need need must be helped on the spot. in the light of the above, i voted in favour of the adoption of the report.

in writing. ‒ jordan is one of the countries most directly affected by the syrian crisis, due to its geographical location. the economy, which is mainly based on services and industry, has been affected by the unrest that has hit the region since 2011. in this difficult situation, however, jordan stands out as a country that has welcomed a significant number of displaced persons. the conflicts in syria and iraq are depriving jordanian products of their traditional markets. the ongoing conflicts in neighbouring countries continued to disrupt jordan's external trade in 2015, with growth slowing down (2.4%) and the remaining external financing needs for 2016-2017 estimated at usd 3,2 billion. in the first half of 2016, the unemployment rate reached a record high of 14,6% of the active population (33% of young people in the labour force, 23,7% of women in the labour force). in order to overcome the economic difficulties, the european union must ensure that it supports its partner, whose policy on the reception of refugees is commendable. the objective is to ensure that the macro-financial assistance programme is put into effect as soon as possible in order to allow jordan to benefit effectively from it during this crucial period. as a member of the fidesz-kdnp delegation, i voted in favour of the report, as it is in line with the hungarian government's desire to provide aid on the ground to those who are in real need and who are forced to flee as a result of the war, and to the neighbouring states that are hosting them.
in writing. ‒ the proposal concerns the coordination of the activities and supervision of institutions providing occupational retirement provision at european level. an 'employer's pension institution' is an institution which, irrespective of its legal form, operates on a funded basis, is set up separately from any supporting undertaking or professional organisation and whose purpose is to provide pension benefits in connection with gainful employment. this is all part of the so-called three-pillar pension system, the introduction of which - mainly because of the capital-backed part, which is also the subject of this proposal - was attempted by the international monetary fund in the 1990s to impose on all the countries to which it lent. the essence of this pension system is to reduce public liability (less public pension), to make self-sufficiency mandatory through private insurance companies (i.e. to divert pension contributions from the state to private insurance companies). what the report wants is to make the capital protection scheme general in such a way that any private pension fund can provide services anywhere in this protection scheme with eu security rules of course. the whole point, of course, is that a large part of the pension contributions - in addition to a minimal portion paid to the state - could be drawn into international financial speculation, as the report clearly shows. in view of all this, i voted against the motion.
in writing. ‒ i believe it is important that older people and people with disabilities are not at risk of poverty and can enjoy an adequate standard of living. an important element in combating poverty and insecurity among older people is that occupational pensions also provide adequate protection against biometric risks. when establishing a pension scheme, employers and workers or their representatives should consider the possibility of extending the pension scheme to cover old age and the risk of occupational disease and to provide a survivor's pension. i voted in favour of the report.
in writing. if anything, pension schemes are a classic case of the veterinary horse. while governments expect workers to plan for their own livelihood for the rest of their lives, pension regulations are constantly being changed, with some delay in some countries and harsher regulations in others. it would be both lawful and moral to change an agreement between an individual and the state, from the first day of employment, only with or without the consent of the employee, in his favour. no more post-retirement raising and tricking. the report's stated aim of drawing a large part of the pension contributions, apart from a minimal part paid to the state, into international financial speculation is completely unacceptable. the introduction of the three-pillar pension system was also opposed by trade unions in 1997, and rightly so.
in writing. ‒ the commission has proposed to the european parliament and the council the adoption of a directive on the activities and supervision of institutions for occupational retirement provision. the economic and monetary committee states in its report that, according to the advisory working party of the legal services of the european parliament, the council and the commission, the commission proposal does not contain any substantive amendments other than those indicated, but only the provisions of existing legislation which have not been changed and the consolidation of these amendments. the committee therefore proposes that parliament adopt the single structured act at first reading with amendments taking into account the recommendations of the advisory working party of the legal services of the european parliament, the council and the commission. i voted accordingly.
in writing. ‒ this legislative process will improve the protection of members of occupational pension schemes and encourage the development of stable cross-border schemes. that is why i voted in favour of the report. the commission's proposal aims to improve the governance and transparency of institutions providing occupational pension schemes. the commission has also been active in promoting the development of the european audiovisual sector. the pension institutions continue to operate in accordance with national social and labour standards, so the proposal recognises the specificities of national systems. for example, it will retain national controls, but will not create eu-wide supervision. however, the text favours crossborder programmes, to which provisions should be added to prevent possible arbitrage, i.e. the possibility of market distortions. the report places a strong emphasis on national social and labour provisions, with particular regard to the protection of programme members, and introduces the concept of a duty of care to avoid competition between crossborder cooperation programmes. it is perhaps the first eu pension legislation to take environmental, social and governance factors into account in investment decisions.

in writing. ‒ i would like to express my appreciation to the ombudsman for initiating an inquiry into the extent to which member states respect the charter of fundamental rights in the implementation of actions funded by eu funds, for example projects aimed at the institutionalisation of persons with disabilities rather than their integration into society. i support the european ombudsman in continuing these investigations to ensure the transparency and added value of the projects. i welcome the cooperation between the ombudsman and the european parliament in the eu framework of the un framework convention on the rights of persons with disabilities, and in particular their call for full implementation of the convention and adequate resources for it at eu level. i support the ombudsman's efforts to address issues of discrimination, the rights of minority groups and the rights of older people. in the light of the above, i voted in favour of the adoption of the report.
in writing. ‒ on 3 may 2016, the european ombudsman, emily oreilly, presented her annual report for 2015 to the european parliament. in its report, the committee on petitions informs that in 2015 the european ombudsman's office assisted 17 033 eu citizens. 261 complaints and 17 complaints were closed by the commission, which itself did not open an investigation. eight of these were strategic studies, dealing with key issues such as transparency in the transatlantic trade and investment partnership, whistleblowing, the european citizens' initiative, fundamental rights in eu cohesion policy and expulsion by frontex. in 145 inquiries closed by the ombudsman in 2015 (52,3% of the total number of cases), the case complained of was either resolved by the institution concerned or reached a friendly solution. in 79 cases (28,5%) no maladministration was found, in 59 cases (19,5%) no further investigation was warranted and in 30 cases (10,8%) maladministration was found. in 19 cases (2.2%) other measures were taken. the ombudsman made critical observations to the institutions in 19 cases and issued draft recommendations in 11 cases, which were accepted in full or in part by the institutions. on this basis, the committee on petitions recommended that parliament approve the report submitted for 2015. i voted accordingly.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the adoption of a report assessing the european ombudsman's activities over the past year. i agree with the generally positive assessment of the report to the ep on the results of the ombudsman's efforts, particularly in the areas of transparency of the activities of the eu institutions, conflicts of interest of eu officials, the fight against corruption, the strengthening of the lobby register and controls, the transparency of ttip, ceta and other eu-level international negotiations, whistleblower protection and other issues affecting the eu's credibility, authority and effectiveness in the eyes of its citizens. as a politician who regularly deals with citizens, i am of course aware of the narrow limits imposed by the legal basis of the european ombudsman's work, especially in the case of deficiencies, corruption and other abuses at the member state level, but in the light of the positive direction and corrective proposals that can be read from this report, i am confident that this ep decision will also contribute to future legal and practical changes in the ombudsman's work, which will also allow for the handling of such cases.
in writing. ‒ the report is about the path towards final vat and the fight against vat fraud. the vat system in the european union, which has been in place since 1993, was designed as a transitional system, but it was also exposed to the risk of fraud from the outset. despite many initiatives, fraud has not been eliminated. the commission estimates that the loss of tax revenue in the union as a whole is around eur 170 billion per year, of which disappearing trader-type criminal organisations alone account for between eur 40 and eur 60 billion per year. the current coexistence of many different vat keys is also a problem, creating a high level of uncertainty for companies doing business across borders. the report says that next year the commission will propose a definitive vat system that is simple, sufficiently stable and efficient, and less prone to fraud. however, member states should be allowed to set their own rates of taxation, as long as they comply with the minimum rates applicable under the vat directive. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the taxation of the eu's citizens is not distorted.
in writing. ‒ the vat system in the european union, which has been in place since 1993, was designed as a transitional system. taxation of trade between member states will be replaced by a definitive system based on taxation of the supply of goods or services in the member state of origin. the council shall adopt appropriate directives to complete the common system of vat and, in particular, to progressively reduce or abolish the arrangements which differ from that system. the commission communication of 7 april 2016 on the vat action plan states that the time for reform has come and that the long delay on the path towards a single union vat area has ended. however, the report of the economic and monetary committee states that the proposed initiatives and the timing do not represent a decisive breakthrough. instead of fundamentally reforming a 20-year-old transitional regime, the commission is content to propose enhanced cooperation, and hopes that tax authorities will show more trust in each other, set a timetable and carry out other assessments. the report suggests that a permanent vat system could be created by extending reverse taxation to all business transactions across europe. this procedure has already proved successful in a number of member states in sectors exposed to fraud and it cannot be concluded that the system would not work in a wider context. i voted in favour of the draft resolution.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the road to a definitive vat system and the fight against vat fraud. as the report mentions, vat fraud represents a staggering loss of revenue for the union, with cross-border fraud alone worth at least eur 50 billion. like the report, i believe that only coordinated efforts by the member states can change this situation. i agree with the conclusion that the cooperation and exchange of information between the tax authorities of the individual member states has not been satisfactory in the past and that it is therefore essential to improve the efficiency of the vat information exchange system. there is a great need to simplify the vat system in the future, especially in the interest of smes, also in terms of administrative burdens and definitions. another important element of the report, which i also support, is the call to member states to allow the exchange of information with judicial and law enforcement authorities, such as europol and olaf, in line with the recommendation of the european court of auditors. i also support the creation of a single, strong and independent european public prosecutor's office, capable of detecting, prosecuting and bringing to justice those responsible for crimes affecting the financial interests of the union, including vat fraud.
in writing. ‒ the european union is a key player in the fight against wildlife crime, but also one of the most important target markets for illegal wildlife products. this illegal trade has become a multibillion-euro crime industry dominated by criminal organizations. the risk of exposure is minimal, and the financial return is high. efforts to reduce broader environmental crime play a particularly important role in combating threats to peace and security. the 2016-2020 action plan reinforces the eu's role in the global fight against illegal wildlife trade. the eu needs to reduce the demand for and supply of illegal wild plant and animal products using the tools at its disposal. it is the collective responsibility of the eu member states to face this challenge and to halt the rapid loss of some of the world's most prized species. this will not only help to preserve biodiversity for future generations, but also to develop and strengthen the eu security framework, improve the quality of life of local communities and strengthen the rule of law. on these grounds, i supported the report.
in writing. ‒ the committee on the environment, public health and food safety in its report concludes that illegal trade in wildlife represents a serious threat not only to the survival of many plant and animal species, but also to the rule of law, human rights, global governance and the well-being of local communities, and above all to the survival of the world's ecosystems. the illegal trade in wildlife and plants has become a multibillion-euro crime industry dominated by criminal organisations. the risk of exposure is minimal, and the financial return is high. the european union is a major player in the fight against wildlife crime, but it is also one of the most important target markets for illegal wildlife products and a transit and often origin point for illegal wildlife trade. the action plan calls for immediate action to end the capture and illegal trade of protected species and to curb the demand for and supply of illegal wildlife products. it reinforces the eu's role in the global fight against illegal wildlife trade through prevention, enforcement, cooperation and action. i supported the adoption of the report.
in writing. ‒ the european union and its member states have a shared responsibility to act against the drastic decline of many of the world's precious species, for example by tackling the illegal trade in wildlife. this is how we can preserve biodiversity for future generations, and it is in this spirit that i voted in favour of this report. the report describes the illegal trade in wildlife as an organised international crime with an estimated annual value of some eur 20 billion and that this activity is closely linked to other forms of organised crime. this practice is the sixth wave of mass extinction of species and it must be stopped. i therefore welcome the report on the commission's action plan against illegal wildlife trade. this action plan highlights the need for concerted action to address the root causes of wildlife trafficking, to effectively implement and enforce existing legislation and to strengthen global cooperation between countries of origin, transit and destination. the report stresses that the identification and allocation of adequate financial and human resources is essential for the implementation of the action plan and recommends that member states establish a coordinating office and a sanctioning system based on the model used in the fight against trafficking in human beings.
in writing. ‒ small and medium-sized enterprises in transport play a significant role in the operation of european roads and make a significant contribution to the eu economy and job creation. the report we have just voted on is about the opportunities and challenges facing these companies and it is therefore very important that it is on the agenda. however, i regret to say that i find that this positive line is contradicted by paragraph 37 of the report, which calls into question the derogation for light vehicles on the grounds that they are unjustifiably present in international traffic. however, it should be stressed that there are no reliable data on this and that if these carriers also had to comply with all the requirements for vehicles over 3,5 tonnes, this could impose a disproportionately high financial and administrative burden on them. therefore, i cannot support this point in the report. but overall i agree with the report and i voted in favour of it.

in writing. ‒ the committee on transport and tourism reports that small transport enterprises are essential for european mobility. thanks to their better knowledge of the local market, their proximity to customers and/or often their dynamism and innovative capacity, they improve individual passenger transport, especially within densely populated areas, in the last mile of the highway. the report considers that the situation has never been more favourable for the development of sustainable solutions that, despite the limited capacity of transport infrastructures, allow for environmentally friendly responses to the increasing mobility needs. (while emissions in other sectors of the european economy have decreased overall over the past 10 years, the transport sector continues to grow and currently accounts for about a quarter of total eu emissions.) the 21st conference on climate change confirmed that the transport sector must play its part in the transition to a low-carbon economy as soon as possible. in 2050, which is a short time, 80 percent of the population will be living in cities. urban mobility will therefore become even more important and the development of multimodal, clean and integrated transport will become inevitable. the report makes suggestions to turn many challenges into opportunities for small businesses. i was in favor of accepting it.
in writing. ‒ the report states that the lack of relevant statistical data makes it difficult to assess the real situation of small transport enterprises in europe. however, it is clear that the transport sector is also facing major challenges and opportunities with the emergence of the collaborative economy. the report therefore makes suggestions that may be of use to these companies. as a person who is passionate about small and medium-sized enterprises, i voted in favour of the report. i agree that efforts to create a single european transport area must be accelerated and that this requires closing the gaps in the application of the law. the existing exemptions and controls should be harmonised and anti-competitive practices, such as social dumping, which can lead to serious distortions, should be abolished. i also consider it important to encourage convergence between the traditional economy and new business models, including community business models, in a way that encourages innovation, consumer protection and fair competition.

in writing. the exchange of crime prevention and prosecution data with other states is essential to guarantee the security of european citizens. however, such exchange of data can only take place with adequate protection of the personal data of union citizens. it is therefore of great importance that the agreement with the government of the united states of america on the protection of personal data relating to the prevention, investigation, detection and prosecution of criminal offences, which establishes a framework of standards and requirements for the conditions for the processing of data exchanged between the member states of the union and the united states, be adopted. the agreement provides adequate data protection safeguards, thereby aiming at a high level of protection of the rights of data subjects. i consider it important to emphasise that the agreement does not, in itself, constitute a legal basis for the transfer of personal data to the united states. i would also like to point out that, thanks to the persistence of the european parliament, the us side has taken legislative measures to ensure that eu citizens have access to justice in the united states.
in writing. the european union has strict data protection standards. principle that data must never be used for purposes incompatible with the original purpose and that personal data must be lawfully collected and processed for lawful purposes under strict conditions. it is important that these principles are shared by the union's partners, thus protecting the data of european citizens worldwide. this is particularly true for close and important partners such as the united states, with whom the eu has not only close trade links but also close cooperation in law enforcement. the recently created eu-usa privacy shield is also about protecting europeans' data, and we expect the same from the agreement between the united states of america and the european union on the protection of personal data in relation to the prevention, investigation and detection of crime. in addition to ensuring a high level of protection of personal data, we also believe that the framework agreement on data protection should also increase the effectiveness of international law enforcement by making law enforcement information exchange between the united states and the european union and its member states more effective.

in writing. – since 2014 scandals have been highlighting the problems related to the commissioner’s declaration of interest. commissioner canete’s scandal, president barroso’s case has proven that we need a code of conduct, which improves the restrictions of the post-office employment and strengthens the competence of the ad-hoc ethical committee responsible for the assessment of conflict of interests. unfortunately the proposal president juncker presented recently, which would increase the lobby ban from 1.5 to 3 years for the president of the commission and to extend the cooling-off period for commissioners from 1.5 to 2 years is an insufficient one. former commissioners are entitled to a transitional allowance for three years, precisely prevent conflicts of interest, but in the meanwhile they can start working as a lobbyist after only two years? that is unacceptable and imbalanced. such measures are exactly the reasons for extremists and euro-sceptics to criticizing the eu institutions. besides the 3 years ban former commissioners should be required to make publicly available all information on their meetings and telephone calls with officials of the european institutions or officials of the governments of the member states up to 10 years after they have ceased to hold office.
in writing. if the european commission and the european union as a whole want to remain credible in the eyes of the electorate, then it cannot be allowed that the former commission president, who played a major role in triggering the global economic crisis, should be transferred to goldman sachs after a year and a half of his mandate. nor can the former energy commissioner be allowed to fly to budapest on a private jet of a pro-russian businessman to advise the hungarian government on the enlargement of the pax. this has to change. this can't happen again. the code of conduct needs to be tightened for both current and former commissioners. i therefore fully support the proposal that eu commissioners should be able to reside only with the permission of the college for three years after their term of office has expired. they may only take up employment which does not raise suspicion of conflict of interest. you can't be an oil lobbyist if you were an eu commissioner for the environment. this is the basis for a functioning, authentic and democratic european union. the european parliament has the political responsibility for ensuring that the code of conduct is respected. as elected meps, we will always take action in the future if we see that the activities of a commissioner raise ethical questions.
the following is the summary of the report on liability, compensation and financial guarantees in offshore oil and gas operations (a8-0308/2016) by mr kostas chrysogonos on behalf of the committee on legal affairs (a8-0308/2016) [2015/2352 (ini) ]
madam president, please. i very much agree with the report that any activity that harms the environment and human life should be subject to collective redress and severe sanctions. the commission should also be able to assess the impact of the 2013 directive on the implementation of the directive in the member states. i also consider the 'polluter pays' principle to be an important means of preventing damage, as we have already stressed in other areas, such as the resolution on the red-hot disaster in hungary. i would like to eliminate the use of fossil oil and natural gas entirely, but i would like to ensure that it is gradual, because it is an operation with infinite risks. in this area too, the commission should encourage member states to focus on renewable energy sources.
in writing. in april 2010, the deepwater horizon oil rig sank following an accident, spilling nearly 5 million barrels of crude oil into the sea. the disaster was caused by a simple device - a failure of the detonation control system - but it went down in history as one of the greatest natural disasters ever. it is, of course, a legitimate expectation that, learning from the american example, europe will not only try to prevent a similar disaster from occurring, but will be prepared to deal with it both technologically and legally. at the same time, we have to be very careful that this kind of effort doesn't choke the very industry that we want to regulate. the extraction of oil and gas from the north sea and the mediterranean is essential for europe's energy supply. it is important that companies extracting in these regions do not feel that we are trying to make them unable to do so, but that they see a helping hand from the union, which will regulate legal relations and help to minimise risks. besides protecting the existing mine, it's just as important not to discourage potential future investment. the black sea, the eastern mediterranean basin and the barents sea, in particular, could provide a long-term solution to europe's energy needs and would greatly reduce its dependence on external suppliers. we must strive to ensure that any regulation we introduce stabilises the business environment and creates predictability.
on behalf of the ppe group. mr president, mr commissioner, mr minister, i have to ask you to stop. anything that fosters hatred, violence, intolerance in society is unacceptable. not just on paper, but in practice. however, i regret that eu decision-makers generally fail to condemn intolerant attitudes towards traditional national minorities. i would like to draw attention - as one of the co-chairs of the traditional national minorities intergroup - to the intolerant attitudes that are being adopted in the member states of the european union against european citizens who have always lived in their homeland, who have not moved, against traditional national minorities. such as discrimination and incitement to hatred against them in the press, banning and sanctioning the use of their national symbols and restricting the use of their mother tongue. these are deeply regrettable matters and the european commission should deal with these matters. because all this intolerance makes european citizens belonging to traditional national minorities feel like second-class citizens in their own country.

in writing. fighting racism is about standing up for our belief in the rule of law, human dignity, and ultimately democracy. it's about how, as equal citizens, we're all part of something bigger, a community. it is the duty of all to respect fundamental human rights and to act against violations. racial discrimination is unacceptable in its very essence, and we must act against it, whether it comes up in a friendly conversation, in political speech, or in legislation. we must treat cultural diversity as a value and oppose any attempt to divide, antagonize or scapegoat our fellow human beings. racism, racial prejudice, is the source of all the evil that man can do to man and to mankind. let's learn from our history. the exclusion of certain groups of people is increasing worldwide, and it can be countered by a common will and a courageous confrontation.

in writing. ‒ regulation (eu) no 952/2013 of the european parliament and of the council establishing the union customs code was adopted on 9 october 2013. its provisions were fully applied on 1 may 2016, when it was found that the wording of article 136 of the regulation was deficient. the draft regulation proposed by the commission aims to correct this. i voted in favour of the proposal as recommended in the report of the committee on the internal market and consumer protection.
in writing. ‒ an appropriate level of customs regulation plays an important role in improving competitiveness. to fulfil its full role, the customs system needs to be modern and efficient. i agree with the rapporteur that timely and transparent information flows between the parties concerned should be possible. in addition, close cooperation between customs administrations and market surveillance authorities should be encouraged to stop irregular products at the border. that is why i voted in favour of the report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the proposal to amend the regulation establishing the union customs code as regards goods temporarily leaving the customs territory of the union by sea or air. the report accepting the commission proposal should be supported as it correctly pointed out the shortcomings of the regulation establishing the customs code. the competent authorities of the member states do not have a legal basis under the present regulation to apply a number of provisions to goods which temporarily leave the customs territory of the union during transport by sea or air between two points in the customs territory of the union, provided that the transport is carried out by direct route without a stop outside the customs territory of the union. in the absence of a clear legal basis for the presentation of these goods to customs, effective customs supervision cannot be achieved, for example, because the amount of import duties and other charges cannot be correctly established. i therefore agree with the proposal to amend article 136 of the regulation to fill this gap, thereby ensuring equal treatment of goods.
in writing. ‒ the full application of the provisions of regulation (eu) no 952/2013 of the european parliament and of the council of 9 october 2013 establishing the union customs code and implementing and delegated acts to this code on 1 may 2016 has revealed certain shortcomings in its wording. i supported the related motion.
in writing. ‒ the report contains an amendment to regulation (eu) no 1286/2014 on key information documents for retail investment products. the original regulation itself seeks to protect the public from the misrepresentation of investment packages offered by banks and various financial institutions. the information requirements in force for such products are uncoordinated and do not help retail investors to compare different products and understand their characteristics. as a result, they often make investments without understanding the risks and costs involved, and as a result, they sometimes suffer unexpected losses. to address this, this regulation lays down information rules and obligations that enable retail investors to understand and compare the main characteristics and risks of retail packaged investment products and insurance-based investment products. i supported the adoption of the report, but i must add an amendment. it is good that the public is spared the greater delusions, but on the other hand, it is only a matter of banks and other financial institutions speculating with the public's money. the role of banks, according to the textbooks, is to channel savings to investors, but what has emerged from the financial deregulation of the 1990s is nothing more than a casino capitalism, where savings have been completely disconnected from productive investment.
in writing. ‒ in addition to investor and consumer protection considerations, the economic crisis has also highlighted the need to review the different and outdated regulations for retail investment products in the member states. this proposal therefore aimed at creating a uniform standard to help retail investors to have easily comprehensible and comparable information on products available on the market before making investment decisions. the priips regulation was the result of years of preparatory work and focused on the development of uniform rules on information and marketing processes for retail packaged investment products and insurance-based investment products. the purpose of the regulation is to specify the form and content of the key information document (kid) and to make it mandatory for investment products to be submitted before the conclusion of the contract. the priips regulation therefore further strengthens transparency alongside the concept of ethical life insurance. in the light of the above, i voted in favour of the adoption of the report.
in writing. ‒ in addition to investor and consumer protection considerations, the economic crisis has also highlighted the need to review the different and outdated regulations for retail investment products in the member states. this proposal therefore aimed at creating a uniform standard to help retail investors to have easily comprehensible and comparable information on products available on the market before making investment decisions. the result of several years of preparatory work was the so-called 'priips regulation', which focused on the development of uniform rules on information and marketing processes for retail packaged investment products and insurance-based investment products. the purpose of the regulation is to specify the form and content of the key information document (kid) and to make it mandatory for investment products to be submitted before the conclusion of the contract. the priips regulation therefore further strengthens transparency alongside the concept of ethical life insurance. i myself voted in favour of this report, as i believe that the unification of product information is essential for comparability.

in writing. ‒ agreements providing for visa-free short-stay travel are generally seen as both a success in deepening relations between the european union and the country concerned, which is of great political importance, and as a further means of strengthening economic and cultural links and encouraging political dialogue on a range of issues, including human rights and fundamental freedoms. the available data on mobility show a high level of trust in visa applicants and a low number of rejected applications. such countries pose no threat to irregular migration or to security and public order. i also consider it important that visa-free travel is not a negligible means of bringing the population of the european union and the citizens of the country concerned closer together. the visa waiver agreement will allow citizens to benefit fully, more cheaply and more easily from the opportunities offered by the partnership.
in writing. ‒ regulation (ec) no 539/2001 was amended on 20 may 2014 by regulation (ec) no 509/2014 of the european parliament and of the council, which included the republic of kiribati among the third countries whose nationals are exempt from the visa requirement when crossing the external borders of the member states. subsequently, the commission, on the authority of the council, opened negotiations with a view to the conclusion of a bilateral agreement between the european union and the republic of kiribati. the council adopted a draft decision on the ratification of the agreement signed in brussels on 23 june 2016, subject to parliament's consent. the report of the committee on civil liberties, justice and home affairs recommends that parliament give its consent to the conclusion of the agreement. i voted accordingly.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the european parliament giving its consent to the council, on behalf of the european union, signing an agreement with the republic of kiribati on the mutual granting of visa-free short-stay visas for all categories of passports. in considering the proposal, i took into account that this step is in line with the intentions and objectives of the cotonou agreement governing relations between the eu and the acp countries, and could facilitate the development of economic and trade relations and tourism, and thus contribute to the achievement of the union's development policy objectives in the region. i took note of the recent efforts made by kiribati to improve the living standards of its population and to uphold human rights, while also appreciating the important contribution made by the ep, through the acp-eu parliamentary delegation, to the process of establishing the visa waiver agreement.
in writing. ‒ relations between the european union and the republic of kiribati are governed by the partnership agreement between the members of the african, caribbean and pacific group of states, of the one part, and the european union and its member states, of the other part (the cotonou agreement). i voted for it.

in writing. ‒ the european union solidarity fund is an important instrument for responding adequately to major natural and extraordinary regional disasters in the eu and in the candidate countries, and for expressing solidarity with the regions and states eligible for support. the facility is one of the eu funds that provides the most tangible, concrete support to local and regional communities. the report summarises the most significant changes the fund has undergone in recent years to respond more effectively and quickly to disasters and to provide more flexible solutions. a factual description of the functioning of an eu fund, which was created for a fundamentally good purpose, and of the changes that have taken place in recent years in relation to the fund. i was in favor of accepting it.
in writing. ‒ applications submitted under the solidarity fund should be processed as quickly as possible, within a maximum of 12 weeks from the submission. all decision-making levels should respond quickly and effectively to ensure that financial assistance is made available to the disaster area as soon as possible. it is untenable that in some cases it took more than one year for the financial assistance to reach the beneficiaries. preventive action and the search for synergies with the cohesion funds, in particular for infrastructure projects, are part of effective action, as they reduce the costs associated with the necessary post-disaster measures. the parliament's report recommends closer cooperation between the different levels of decision-making and calls for greater transparency and better communication with stakeholders. i voted in favour of the adoption of the report on the evaluation of the solidarity fund.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the evaluation of the solidarity fund in the european parliament's plenary vote in strasbourg. the processing time for applications submitted under the solidarity fund shall be as short as possible and shall not exceed 12 weeks from the submission of the application. all decision-making levels should respond quickly and effectively to ensure that financial assistance is made available to the disaster area as soon as possible. it is untenable that in some cases it took more than one year for the financial assistance to reach the beneficiaries. preventive action and the search for synergies with the cohesion funds, in particular for infrastructure projects, are part of effective action, as they reduce the costs associated with the necessary post-disaster measures. the parliament's report recommends closer cooperation between the different levels of decision-making and calls for greater transparency and better communication with stakeholders.

in writing. ‒ the european union solidarity fund was set up after the floods of 2002. the fund shall aim to provide an immediate expression of union solidarity with countries affected by major natural disasters. the european commission presented its 2014 report on the mobilisation of the fund in october 2015. the regional development committee decided to examine the operation of the fund and report back to parliament. the report focuses on the fund's response speed and the need for a prevention policy that takes advantage of the complementarity between the fund and other eu instruments, in particular cohesion policy. i supported the adoption of the report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report. the document recalls that the european union solidarity fund (eusf) was established to enable the european union to respond to major natural disasters and to express european solidarity with europe's disaster-stricken regions. it provides that, in all cases where it is necessary to ensure the timely availability of budgetary resources, the fund may be mobilised for the purpose of making advances up to a maximum amount of eur 50 000 000, by entering the corresponding appropriations in the general budget of the union. the proposal for the current decision of the european parliament and of the council to which this report responds was not made in the context of a specific disaster. instead, it aims to allocate eur 50 million in the 2017 union budget in the form of commitment and payment appropriations to pay advances in a timely and efficient manner in the event of a disaster that may occur in the following year. i consider it important that this eu financial support, in addition to reinforcing the clear political message of solidarity, also provides the assistance urgently needed by the citizens concerned.
in writing. ‒ following the tragic floods of 2002, the european union set up the european union solidarity fund. this fund shall allow for the immediate expression of union solidarity with countries affected by major natural disasters. in addition to the member states, the fund may also support candidate countries. i supported the current proposal.
in writing. ‒ the ep's agenda includes a proposal by albrecht, the green party rapporteur, to ask the ep to agree to the conclusion on behalf of the european union of an agreement between the united states of america and the european union on the protection of personal data relating to the prevention, investigation, detection and prosecution of criminal offences, and to propose the adoption of a draft council decision to that effect. the albrecht proposal looks at these aspects and their balancing and concludes that the aspects of law enforcement, judicial cooperation and the protection of the personal rights and personal data of european citizens are both valid and balanced. the commission's proposal does not address the concerns raised by the european data protection supervisor, among others, about framework agreements. in the light of the above, the gue and alde for essentially similar reasons in separate motions for a resolution propose that the framework agreement should now be referred to the european court of justice for an opinion on its compatibility with the treaties, rather than for approval. i voted yes to the motion.
in writing. ‒ the exchange of crime prevention and prosecution data with other states is essential to guarantee the security of european citizens. however, such exchange of data can only take place with adequate protection of the personal data of union citizens. it is therefore of great importance that the agreement with the government of the united states of america on the protection of personal data relating to the prevention, investigation, detection and prosecution of criminal offences, which establishes a framework of standards and requirements for the conditions for the processing of data exchanged between the member states of the union and the united states, be adopted. the agreement provides adequate data protection safeguards, thereby aiming at a high level of protection of the rights of data subjects. it is also important to emphasise that the agreement itself does not constitute a legal basis for the transfer of personal data to the united states, and i can therefore vote in favour of the agreement.

in writing. ‒ a motion for a resolution was tabled on this subject by the gue/ngl and alde groups. the two motions, each with a different argument, raise doubts as to whether the draft agreement is compatible with the treaties and the charter of fundamental rights and propose that parliament seek an opinion from the court of justice on the compatibility of the proposed agreement with the treaties. since i consider that the proposed agreement adequately guarantees the protection of individuals' personal data, non-discrimination and the right to an effective remedy and to a fair trial, i considered the concerns of the two groups to be unfounded. so i rejected both proposals.

in writing. ‒ explanation of vote: us-eu agreement on the protection of personal data in connection with criminal offences: exchange of data on crime prevention and prosecution with other states is essential to guarantee the security of european citizens. however, such exchange of data can only take place with adequate protection of the personal data of union citizens. it is therefore of great importance that the agreement with the government of the united states of america on the protection of personal data relating to the prevention, investigation, detection and prosecution of criminal offences, which establishes a framework of standards and requirements for the conditions for the processing of data exchanged between the member states of the union and the united states, be adopted. the agreement provides adequate data protection safeguards, thereby aiming at a high level of protection of the rights of data subjects. it is also important to emphasise that the agreement itself does not constitute a legal basis for the transfer of personal data to the united states, and i can therefore vote in favour of the agreement.
in writing. ‒ the exchange of crime prevention and prosecution data with other states is essential to guarantee the security of european citizens. however, such exchange of data can only take place with adequate protection of the personal data of union citizens. it is therefore of great importance that the agreement with the government of the united states of america on the protection of personal data relating to the prevention, investigation, detection and prosecution of criminal offences, which establishes a framework of standards and requirements for the conditions for the processing of data exchanged between the member states of the union and the united states, be adopted. the agreement provides adequate data protection safeguards, thereby ensuring a high level of protection of the rights of data subjects. it is also important to emphasise that the agreement does not, in itself, constitute a legal basis for the transfer of personal data to the united states.
in writing. ‒ by its decision of 3 december 2010, the council authorised the commission to conclude an agreement between the european union and the united states of america on the protection of personal data processed and transmitted for the purposes of the prevention, investigation, detection or prosecution of criminal offences, including terrorist offences, in the framework of police cooperation and judicial cooperation in criminal matters. the text of the agreement was initialled on 8 september 2015 after five years of negotiations. the agreement aims to ensure a high level of protection of the fundamental rights and freedoms of individuals, in particular the right to privacy, with regard to the processing of personal data, where personal data are transferred to the competent authorities of the european union and its member states and of the united states for those purposes. the council adopted a draft decision on the ratification of the agreement, for which it requested parliament's consent. in its opinion, the committee on legal affairs concluded that the envisaged agreement is based on an appropriate legal basis, guarantees a high level of protection of the fundamental right to personal data and will improve law enforcement cooperation with the united states. the committee on foreign affairs has written to assure parliament of its support for the proposed agreement. on this basis, the committee on civil liberties, justice and home affairs recommends in its report that parliament give its consent to the conclusion of the agreement. i voted accordingly.
in writing. ‒ on 3 december 2010, the council adopted a decision authorising the commission to open negotiations for an agreement between the european union and the united states of america on the protection of personal data processed and transmitted for the purposes of the prevention, investigation, detection or prosecution of criminal offences, including terrorist offences, in the framework of police cooperation and judicial cooperation in criminal matters. i supported him with my vote.
in writing. ‒ in august 2016, ghana (and later côte d'ivoire) decided to ratify the transitional economic partnership agreement (tpa) concluded with the european union in 2007 as a result of the delay in signing the eu-west africa economic partnership agreement (epa). the agreement provides for a contractual safety net and guarantees duty-free access to the union market until the regional agreement is concluded. the transitional agreement provides for its provisional application and will be replaced by a full regional economic partnership agreement on the date of its entry into force. although ghana's export revenues are dominated by gold, cocoa and crude oil, the union has become a primary target for ghana's 'non-traditional' exports, reflecting the increasing diversification and value-added production within the country. ghana's imports are dominated by ships, vehicles and refined petroleum. the country is trying to stabilize its position as a transit and maritime hub for landlocked countries. while excluding certain sensitive agricultural and processed products from liberalisation, the tpa also introduces safeguards to allow the re-introduction of duties in case of a sudden increase in imports threatening to distort the economy and endanger food security. in view of the above, i voted in favour of the report.

in writing. ‒ in 2007, a transitional economic partnership agreement was concluded between the european union and ghana, guaranteeing duty-free access for ghana to the eu market. as ghana is a member of the economic community of west african states (ecowas) and negotiations between the eu and ecowas for a comprehensive regional economic partnership agreement have begun, the transitional agreement has not yet been ratified. however, given that the convention initialled on 30 june 2014 has not yet been ratified due to the hesitation of some ecowas member states, ghana decided on 3 august 2016 to ratify the interim economic partnership agreement with the eu, which provides for provisional application, pending its entry into force and to replace it with a full regional economic partnership agreement on the date of its entry into force. the council has drawn up a draft decision for eu ratification of the tpa, but this will require parliament's consent. in its report, the committee on international trade recommends that parliament give its consent to the conclusion of the agreement on such terms. i voted accordingly.

in writing. ‒ i voted with a reservation on the draft resolution on the implementation of the previously agreed economic partnership agreement between the eu and ghana, recognising the importance of the agreement and considering the doubts raised about its specific economic content. i am aware that it is important for the ghanaian economy to continue to enjoy duty-free access to the european market for certain products after the expiry of the interim agreement with the eu in october this year, and this partnership could provide a framework for this. i also considered that ghana is a democratic country where the government and the legislature are unanimous in supporting the agreement. however, i could not ignore the serious concerns expressed - in particular by my own group - that the commission had asserted its primacy during the negotiations on the agreement and that the text thus entailed economic risks to ghana's disadvantage in several respects. it is clear that ghana would also benefit from developing european trade relations with the eu under an agreement envisaged under the aegis of ecowas, but the fact that this multilateral agreement is still being worked out does not enjoy the support of all parties and thus does not provide a short-term solution for ghana's export positions. in view of the complex and contradictory situation of the case, i have decided not to vote on the specific motion for a resolution.

in writing. ‒ article 13 of council regulation (eu, euratom) no 1311/2013 of 2 december 2013 on the multiannual financial framework for the period 2014-2020 established an exceptional reserve of up to 0,03% of the union's gross national income. the commission has proposed to the parliament and the council that the contingency margin be mobilised in the general budget of the union for the financial year 2016. the aim of the proposal is to provide a commitment appropriation of eur 240,1 million, above the commitment ceiling of chapter 3 of the multiannual financial framework, to meet the needs arising from the migration, asylum and security crisis. in its report, the committee on budgets recommends that parliament approve the commission's proposal to mobilise the emergency reserve. i voted accordingly.

in writing. ‒ the report on the council position on draft amending budget no 4/2016 of the european union for the financial year 2016 is part of the agreement between the european parliament and the council negotiating delegations on the union budget for 2017. draft amending budget no 4/2016 reduces the level of payment appropriations by eur 7 284,3 million and therefore reduces national contributions accordingly. the european parliament believes that towards the end of the current financial framework there will be a significant accumulation of payment requests, and it is therefore important to avoid the liquidity crisis that occurred during the previous seven-year framework, when the commission was unable to pay the invoices submitted to the member states after the projects had been implemented. in the context of the review of the multiannual financial framework, we can only support any proposal if we receive adequate guarantees: there will be sufficient resources in the annual budgets to pay for the catch-up programmes already in place and for agricultural subsidies. on the basis of the above, i voted in favour of the adoption of the report.
in writing. ‒ the report on the council position on draft amending budget no 4/2016 of the european union for the financial year 2016 is part of the agreement between the european parliament and the council negotiating delegations on the union budget for 2017. draft amending budget no 4/2016 reduces the level of payment appropriations by eur 7 284,3 million and therefore reduces national contributions accordingly. as regards the revenue side of the budget, the draft amending budget no 4/2016 includes a revision of the forecast for traditional own resources (i.e. customs duties and sugar levies) and for resources based on value added tax (vat) and gross national income (gni), as well as the accounting and financing of the uk corrections concerned. the european parliament believes that towards the end of the current financial framework there will be a significant accumulation of payment requests, and it is therefore important to avoid the liquidity crisis that occurred during the previous seven-year framework, when the commission was unable to pay the invoices submitted to the member states after the projects had been implemented. in the context of the review of the multiannual financial framework, we can only support any proposal if we receive adequate guarantees: there will be sufficient resources in the annual budgets to pay for the catch-up programmes already in place and for agricultural subsidies. on the basis of the above, i voted in favour of the adoption of the report.

in writing. ‒ draft amending budget no 4/2016 adopted by the commission on 30 september 2016. the draft proposes updating appropriations to take account of recent developments in migration and security issues, reducing payment and commitment appropriations as a result of the global realignment, extending the european fund for strategic investments, amending the staff establishment plan of frontex and updating revenue appropriations. on 24 november 2016, the council adopted its position on the draft and forwarded it to parliament. the committee on budgets report, also based on the position expressed in a letter by the committee on regional development and the committee on civil liberties, justice and home affairs, expresses serious concerns about some of the measures envisaged, but nevertheless recommends that parliament approve the council position on draft amending budget no 4/2016, thereby definitively adopting the amendment. i voted accordingly.

in writing. ‒ the report on the council position on draft amending budget no 5/2016 of the european union for the financial year 2016 is part of the agreement between the european parliament and the council negotiating delegations on the union budget for 2017. draft amending budget no 5/2016 follows the closure and entry into force of the ratification process of decision 2014/335/eu, euratom, which contains limited changes, such as a reduction in the cost of collecting traditional own resources, a reduction in the rate of call of the budgetary resource based on vat for some member states and a gross reduction in the gni-based contribution for some member states. draft amending budget no 5/2016 aims to incorporate the impact of own resources adjustments with retroactive effect for the financial years 2014, 2015 and 2016 into the revenue side of the union budget for 2016. the european parliament's plenary approved the council position on draft amending budget no 5/2016. on the basis of the above, i voted in favour of the adoption of the report.

in writing. ‒ the european union solidarity fund aims to enable the union to respond to emergencies and express solidarity with the population of regions affected by disasters in a rapid, efficient and flexible manner. germany submitted an application on 19 august 2016 to mobilise the fund, following a series of short but extremely severe floods in the region of lower bavaria in may and june 2016. the application submitted by germany meets the requirements for determining the financial contribution from the fund. on the basis of the above, i voted in favour of the adoption of the report.
in writing. ‒ the european union solidarity fund aims to enable the union to respond to emergencies and express solidarity with the population of regions affected by disasters in a rapid, efficient and flexible manner. germany submitted an application on 19 august 2016 to mobilise the fund, following a series of short but extremely severe floods in the region of lower bavaria in may and june 2016. the application submitted by germany meets the requirements for determining the financial contribution from the fund. for the general budget of the european union for the financial year 2016, the european union solidarity fund shall be mobilised to provide germany with the sum of eur 31 475 125 in commitment and payment appropriations. on the basis of the above, i voted in favour of the adoption of the report.

in writing. ‒ the european union solidarity fund aims to enable the union to respond to emergencies and express solidarity with the population of regions affected by disasters in a rapid, efficient and flexible manner. germany submitted an application on 19 august 2016 to mobilise the fund, following a series of short but extremely severe floods in the region of lower bavaria in may and june 2016. the application submitted by germany meets the requirements for determining the financial contribution from the fund. for the general budget of the european union for the financial year 2016, the european union solidarity fund shall be mobilised to provide germany with the sum of eur 31 475 125 in commitment and payment appropriations. on the basis of the above, i voted in favour of the adoption of the report.
in writing. ‒ in the wake of the floods in lower bavaria in may and june 2016, the commission proposed to the parliament and the council that the european union solidarity fund be mobilised. seven people died in the disaster, and two months later, more than 2,000 people were unable to return to their homes. the town of simbach am inn was almost completely destroyed and there was severe damage to basic infrastructure: water supply, sewage treatment and electricity grid. in their application, the german authorities estimated the total amount of damage directly caused by the disaster at eur 1 259,005 million, which corresponds to 3,03% of the lower bavaria region's gdp, i.e. more than 1,5% of the regional gdp, and thus constitutes a 'regional disaster'. the german authorities estimated the eligible costs of the necessary emergency operations at eur 94,196 million. in line with previous practice, the commission proposes to take account of 2,5% of the total direct damage up to the 'significant disaster' threshold, bringing the total amount of the proposed aid to eur 31 475 125. the committee on budgets, in its report, finds that the german application fulfils the requirements laid down for determining the financial contribution from the fund and therefore proposes that parliament approve the mobilisation of the fund for the purpose of the financial contribution to be granted to germany. i voted for the motion.

in writing. ‒ on 19 october 2016, the commission adopted a proposal for a decision of the european parliament and of the council on the mobilisation of the european union solidarity fund to provide assistance to germany. the commission has also adopted a communication on the implementation of the european year of the environment, which aims to promote the use of renewable energy sources in the union. on 21 november 2016, the council adopted its position on the draft and forwarded it to the european parliament. in its report, the committee on budgets notes that draft amending budget no 6/2016 covers the proposed mobilisation of the european union solidarity fund in relation to the floods in germany in may and june 2016 and therefore proposes that parliament endorses the council position on draft amending budget no 6/2016 and thereby definitively adopts the amendment. i voted accordingly.

in writing. ‒ the european union solidarity fund is a special instrument defined in the mff regulation and the corresponding commitment and payment appropriations should be entered in the budget above the ceilings of the mff. i followed the s&d's position.
in writing. ‒ the report concerns the use of the emergency reserves in 2017. to deal with exceptional cases, regulation (eu) no 1311/2013 established an exceptional reserve of up to 0,03% of the union's gross national income. in accordance with this, the commission calculated the maximum amount of the contingency reserve for 2017. however, it is foreseeable that the expenditure ceilings thus set will not be sustainable in 2017, and the commission has therefore proposed to mobilise an amount of eur 1164 million from the exceptional reserves above the ceiling in order to finance additional expenditure arising from the migration and humanitarian challenges. since we're on a hard road here, i've been advocating raising the ceiling.
in writing. ‒ the proposal for a decision of the european parliament and of the council on the mobilisation of the contingency margin for 2017 is part of the agreement between the negotiating delegations of the european parliament and the council on the union budget for 2017. the european commission, having examined all the possibilities for financing additional and unforeseen commitment needs, proposed in its draft budget the mobilisation of the contingency reserve of eur 1164,4 million to supplement the commitment appropriations relating to expenditure in chapter 3 of the general budget of the european union for the financial year 2017, above the payment ceiling of eur 2578 million in current prices. the european parliament report adopted the commission proposal. on the basis of the above, i voted in favour of the adoption of the report.

in writing. ‒ article 13 of council regulation (eu, euratom) no 1311/2013 established an exceptional reserve of up to 0,03% of the union's gross national income. as additional funding needs are likely to arise in 2017 in relation to internal security crises and current humanitarian, migration and asylum challenges, the commission has submitted a proposal for a decision to mobilise this exceptional reserve in 2017. this is necessary in order to address the needs arising from the migration, asylum and security crisis by increasing the commitment appropriations in the general budget of the european union for the financial year 2017 beyond the ceilings of chapters 3 and 4 of the multiannual financial framework. in its report, the committee on budgets, having regard to the opinion of the committee on civil liberties, justice and home affairs, recommends that parliament give its consent to this proposal for a decision. i voted accordingly.

in writing. ‒ after examining all the possibilities for financing additional and unforeseen commitment needs, the commission proposed in its draft budget the mobilisation of the exceptional reserve of eur 1164,4 million. i was supportive.
in writing. ‒ the report concerns the mobilisation of the flexibility instrument to finance immediate budgetary measures to deal with the current migration, asylum and security crisis. as you know, the flexibility instrument was set up in 1999 with the aim of enabling additional payments to be made when the ceiling for a budgetary objective (budget line) has been reached, without having to renegotiate the budget as a whole. the flexibility instrument was initially set at eur 200 million per year, currently eur 471 million, but could be carried over if not used. in this case, the commission proposes to mobilise the flexibility instrument in order to supplement the resources in the general budget of the union for 2017 with eur 530 million, in addition to the ceiling of chapter 3 (security and union citizenship), to finance measures in the areas of migration, asylum and security. the report also suggests that the annual amount of the flexibility instrument should be increased to eur 2 billion. we should also support the use and increase of the flexibility instrument, as the management of the migration situation requires.
in writing. ‒ the proposal for a decision of the european parliament and of the council on the mobilisation of the flexibility instrument for 2017 is part of the agreement between the negotiating delegations of the european parliament and the council on the eu budget for 2017. the european parliament notes that the 2017 ceilings of chapter 3 do not provide sufficient resources to finance urgent measures related to migration, refugees and security. it therefore agrees to mobilise the flexibility instrument in the form of commitment appropriations amounting to eur 530 million. this ensures that the resources mobilised to deal with the migration crisis are not diverted to the detriment of other eu programmes already in place. cohesion and agricultural funds should not be reduced when determining the resources to deal with the migration crisis. on the basis of the above, i voted in favour of the adoption of the report.

in writing. ‒ under council regulation (eu, euratom) no 1311/2013 of 2 december 2013 on the multiannual financial framework for the period 2014-2020, the flexibility instrument is intended to allow the financing of clearly identified expenditure which could not be financed within the limits of the ceilings of another chapter or chapters. the commission has presented a proposal for a decision to the european parliament and the council to mobilise the flexibility instrument to supplement the resources of the general budget of the european union for 2017 with eur 530 million, in addition to the ceiling of chapter 3, to finance measures in the areas of migration, asylum and security. in its report, the committee on budgets, having regard to the opinion of the committee on civil liberties, justice and home affairs, considers that the resources available in the general budget of the european union for 2017 to finance the necessary measures in the fields of migration, asylum and security should be increased beyond the ceiling of chapter 3. it therefore proposes that parliament give its consent to the mobilisation of the flexibility instrument in the form of commitment appropriations for an amount of eur 530 million and approves the commission's proposal for a decision to that effect. i voted accordingly.

in writing. ‒ the commission has proposed to mobilise the flexibility instrument to supplement the resources of the general budget of the european union for 2017 with eur 530 million, in addition to the ceiling of chapter 3, to finance measures in the areas of migration, asylum and security. i voted for it.
in writing. ‒ the report concerns the mobilisation of the european union solidarity fund to provide advances from the general budget of the union for 2017. the european union solidarity fund (eusf) was set up to express european solidarity with europe's disaster-stricken regions. the fund provides financial support to member states in the event of major natural disasters, i.e. when the damage caused by a disaster exceeds eur 3 billion or 0.6% of the country's gross national income, whichever is lower. the proposal for the current decision of the european parliament and of the council is not related to a specific disaster. instead, it aims to allocate eur 50 million in the 2017 union budget in the form of commitment and payment appropriations to pay advances in a timely and efficient manner in the event of a disaster that may occur in the following year. i supported the adoption of the report.
in writing. ‒ the european union solidarity fund (the 'fund') aims to enable the union to respond to emergencies and express its solidarity with the population of regions affected by disasters in a rapid, efficient and flexible manner. in all cases where it is necessary to ensure the timely availability of budgetary resources, the fund may be mobilised for the purpose of making advances up to a maximum amount of eur 50 000 000, by entering the corresponding appropriations in the general budget of the union. the proposal for the current decision of the european parliament and of the council is not related to a specific disaster. the objective is to allocate eur 50 million in the union budget for 2017 to pay advances in a timely and efficient manner in the event of a disaster that may occur in the following year. the advance may be paid at the request of a member state after the commission has carried out a preliminary assessment of the application to mobilise the solidarity fund. the amount of the advance shall not exceed 10% of the expected financial contribution or eur 30 million. the solidarity fund shall reinforce the clear political message of solidarity while providing the assistance urgently needed by the citizens concerned. the rapid reaction framework, including the payment of the advance, will enable the union to achieve these objectives. the ep therefore supported the inclusion of the above amounts in the 2017 budget. on the basis of the above, i voted in favour of the adoption of the report.

in writing. ‒ the european union solidarity fund was set up after the floods of 2002. the fund shall aim to provide an immediate expression of union solidarity with countries affected by major natural disasters. article 10 of the multiannual financial framework for the period 2014-2020 allows the mobilisation of the fund up to an annual ceiling of eur 500 million in 2011 prices, in addition to the ceilings of the relevant chapters of the financial framework. in this context, the commission has submitted a proposal for a decision to the european parliament and the council which does not aim at mitigating the damage caused by a specific disaster, but at allocating eur 50 million in the 2017 union budget in the form of commitment and payment appropriations, in order to allow for the timely and efficient payment of advances in the event of a disaster that may occur in the following year. in its report, the committee on budgets recommends that parliament approve the draft decision. i voted accordingly.
