in writing. ‒ the european union solidarity fund (eusf) was established to enable the european union to respond to major natural disasters and to express european solidarity with europe's disaster-stricken regions. i supported the current proposal.
in writing. ‒ the report concerns the common draft text of the general budget of the european union for the financial year 2017, approved by the conciliation committee in the context of the budgetary procedure. the report covers the items agreed by the council, the commission and parliament in the conciliation committee. the commission shall be empowered to adopt delegated acts in accordance with article 290 concerning the establishment of the european data protection supervisor. perhaps the most discussed issue during the negotiations was the 5% reduction in staff. in my view, the budget is a symbol of the eu's neoliberal economic policy, and this is reflected above all in the continuing restrictions, such as the proposed 5% reduction in the number of employees, which, by the way, makes no sense except to satisfy the completely wrong german neoliberal economic policy. although a budget is obviously necessary for the functioning of the union, i rejected this budget because of the neoliberal economic policy of the union, thus expressing our disagreement with the economic policy of the union, which has had tragic results.
in writing. ‒ it is essential that the eu budget can keep pace with member state implementation of regional development programmes, which will accelerate in 2017, and that cohesion funds are available in the right order of magnitude. the eu budget has the resources to allow the european commission to pay in full the bills that arise from the implementation of completed projects in the member states. it also succeeded in ensuring that the resources mobilised to deal with the migration crisis were not diverted to the detriment of other eu programmes already in operation. cohesion and agricultural funds should not be reduced when determining the resources to deal with the migration crisis. the 2017 union budget does not include any provision for sanctions against member states that refuse to adopt mandatory quotas. on the basis of the above, i voted in favour of the adoption of the report.
in writing. ‒ it is essential that the eu budget can keep pace with member state implementation of regional development programmes, which will accelerate in 2017, and that cohesion funds are available in the right order of magnitude. the eu budget has the resources to allow the european commission to pay in full the bills that arise from the implementation of completed projects in the member states. we also managed to ensure that the resources mobilised to deal with the migration crisis were not diverted to the detriment of other eu programmes already in place. cohesion and agricultural funds should not be reduced when determining the resources to deal with the migration crisis. the 2017 union budget does not include any provision for sanctions against member states that refuse to adopt mandatory quotas. the socialists and liberals have proposed a budgetary mechanism to punish member states that do not take in illegal immigrants despite a mandatory resettlement quota system. this attack was thwarted during the adoption of the 2017 budget. on the basis of the above, i voted in favour of the adoption of the report.

in writing. ‒ on 18 july 2016, the commission adopted the draft general budget of the european union for the financial year 2017. on 12 september 2016, the council adopted its position on this and forwarded it to parliament. parliament adopted its resolution on this on 26 october 2016, with a number of budgetary amendments to the draft. the conciliation committee, composed of delegates from parliament, the council and the commission, adopted the joint text. in its report to the conciliation committee, the delegation of the european parliament proposes that parliament approve this joint text, thereby definitively adopting the general budget of the european union for the financial year 2017. i voted accordingly.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report approving the figures for the 2017 budget with amendments. i would point out that the final budget for this year provides for a commitment appropriation of eur 157 851.8 million and a payment appropriation of eur 134 430.4 million. the commission established the profitability of the sampled union producers by expressing the pre-tax net profit of the sales of the like product to unrelated customers in the union as a percentage of the turnover of those sales. in the course of the negotiations, the european parliament succeeded in reinstating in several places the figures proposed by the european commission and reduced by the european council. accordingly, two important themes, 'growth and jobs' and 'youth employment' were reinforced with eur 200 and eur 500 million respectively. in addition, additional resources will be provided for the dairy and livestock sectors hit by the crisis (eur 500 million) and for the 'global europe' initiative for growth and jobs, which is also intended to tackle the migration and refugee crisis at its roots, with a further eur 730 million. i find the proposed figures acceptable, with the observation that, of course, the amount spent on sustainable job creation (including for young people) is never enough.
in writing. ‒ the total amount of commitment appropriations in the 2017 budget is eur 157 857,8 million. the total amount of eur 1100,1 million in commitment appropriations is thus left open below the ceilings of the mff for 2017. i supported the document.

in writing. ‒ the report is the european parliament's resolution on the financial interests of commissioners, summarising the ep's views and demands on the issue of commissioners' conflicts of interest. the proposals put forward are acceptable, their aims are clearly to promote transparency and to exclude any link with the economic sphere, but the question is whether this will be possible in practice. i also supported amendment no 1 extending the duration of post-office recruitment restrictions for commissioners for at least three years or at least for as long as the former commissioner is entitled to the transitional allowance under the relevant regulation. the commission has also been informed that jean-claude juncker has ordered an inquiry into his predecessor, josé manuel barroso, who, to the dismay of many, has recently taken up a job at goldman sachs, the us investment bank. the proposal also considers that the declaration of financial interests and, more broadly, the verification of potential conflicts of interest affecting the members of the commission should go beyond a single procedure for the appointment of the commission. in this regard, it considers that any substantial change in the financial interests of a commissioner or any reallocation of tasks between members of the commission during his or her term of office creates a new situation of possible conflict of interest and should therefore be the subject of a new parliamentary scrutiny procedure.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the european parliament's motion for a resolution on the earthquakes in italy. the proposal stresses that the recent earthquakes in italy have wiped out entire villages, seriously damaged local and regional infrastructure, economic activity and, in many cases, historical and cultural heritage, and that consequently a major reconstruction effort is needed to repair the damage suffered. the motion for a resolution draws attention to important issues such as the growing importance of providing adequate accommodation for homeless people as winter approaches, the need to accelerate related research to prevent this, the need to ensure advance payments for the number of affected areas as soon as possible and the need to make the most of synergies between existing instruments to ensure an effective response.
in writing. ‒ the european parliament's rules of procedure state, in connection with the commission's approval, that parliament expects full disclosure of information on the financial interests of commissioners-designate and that their declarations in this regard are to be sent to the committee responsible for legal affairs for scrutiny. the scope of this inquiry is outlined in the report of the legal affairs committee. it states that the verification of the absence of conflict of interest cannot be equated with the assessment of the suitability of the candidate and must be a precondition for the hearing. notes that the role of the legal affairs committee is to assess any conflict of interest and, where appropriate, to make recommendations for its resolution; these may include the waiver of certain financial interests or the modification of the portfolio. finally, it states that the examination of possible conflicts of interest between commissioners cannot be limited to the procedure for appointing the commission; any substantial change in the financial interests of a commissioner or any reallocation of tasks between members of the commission during his term of office creates a new situation for the purposes of possible conflicts of interest and should therefore be the subject of a new parliamentary examination procedure. i supported the adoption of the report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report and the motion for a resolution because it raises the possibility of serious abuse of office and also proposes a solution. i am convinced that the declarations of interests of eu commissioners, the conflict of interest rules and the code of conduct applicable to them need to be reviewed and enforced not only for the candidate and the outgoing commissioner, but also - at least as rigorously - for the incumbent european commissioner. in considering this question, as a hungarian representative, i had in mind the recent case of my country's government, which, by lobbying the european commission, with the help, influence and advice of a commissioner in office, was promoting the adoption of a contract with an external party that was questionable from the eu's point of view. (a commissioner who, under the current conflict of interest rules, did not even consider it a matter of concern to accept a high-value favour from this lobbyist.) for me, this, together with the case of the former president of the commission in the private sector, proves that a thorough review of the european commission's rules on conflict of interest, transparency and public service ethics is warranted, to which this ep decision can provide an important stimulus.
in writing. ‒ the rapporteur intends to outline the scope of the examination of financial interests by the committee on legal affairs. to this end, it intends to describe the european parliament's internal procedures for appointing the new commission and for its term of office, and the transparency requirements imposed on its members. i supported him with my vote.
in writing. ‒ following the explosion of the deepwater horizon oil platform on 20 april 2010 and the resulting oil pollution, the safety of offshore oil and gas activities directive was adopted with the aim of establishing minimum requirements to prevent major accidents and limit the consequences of such accidents in relation to offshore oil and gas activities in the eu. as the deadline for legal harmonisation has long passed, the foundations of an eu-wide regulatory framework should now be in place. the liability systems of the member states vary, and most civil claims arising from accidents involving widespread pollution may be enforced by procedures which vary from one member state to another. with a few exceptions (france, the netherlands, denmark), the current liability rules only cover ship-related damage and are also suitable for the recovery of lost profits in the event of a direct causal link. however, there is no such convention on compensation for damage caused by offshore oil and gas activities and those conventions would in all likelihood not cover such accidents, as offshore oil and gas installations would probably not qualify as 'ships' under the convention. the commission should work closely with member states to ensure that union compensation and financial security schemes for offshore oil and gas activities are modernised. that is why i voted in favour of the report.

in writing. ‒ the legal committee report addresses the issue of liability, compensation and financial guarantees for traditional damage caused by offshore oil and gas activities. it concludes that the commission should work closely with member states to ensure that the union's compensation and financial security schemes for offshore oil and gas activities (i) provide for compensation for traditional damage caused by accidents to third parties in offshore oil and gas activities; (ii) establish an effective compensation system to handle the relevant payments; and (iii) ensure that economic operators and other liable parties have the appropriate financial means to meet compensation claims. i supported the adoption of the report.
in writing. ‒ following the explosion of the deepwater horizon oil platform on 20 april 2010 and the resulting oil pollution, the safety of offshore oil and gas activities directive was adopted with the aim of establishing minimum requirements to prevent major accidents and limit the consequences of such accidents in relation to offshore oil and gas activities in the eu. as the deadline for legal harmonisation has long passed, the foundations of an eu-wide regulatory framework should now be in place. member states have different systems of liability and most civil claims arising from accidents involving widespread pollution may be enforced by different procedures in different member states. with a few exceptions (france, the netherlands, denmark), the current liability rules only cover ship-related damage and are also suitable for the recovery of lost profits in the event of a direct causal link. however, there is no such convention on compensation for damage caused by offshore oil and gas activities and those conventions would in all likelihood not cover such accidents, as offshore oil and gas installations would probably not qualify as 'ships' under the convention. the commission should work closely with member states to ensure that union compensation and financial security schemes for offshore oil and gas activities are modernised. that is why i voted in favour of the report.
in writing. ‒ offshore oil and gas activity has a number of negative effects. while there is a chance of catastrophic natural disasters, these extraction methods and products also cause permanent damage that can only be remedied by joint action. of course, member states also have a responsibility in this regard. the commission has also been asked to provide information on the environmental impact of the use of plastics in the production of certain products. i supported the report, which states that activities that harm the environment and human life should be punished with severe penalties, the precautionary principle should be applied and compensation should be linked to collective redress. the directive on marine fossil extraction was adopted in 2013, but its transposition in the member states is lagging behind in several countries. one very important tool for mitigating damage is the 'polluter pays' principle, which has already been introduced in other areas of european legislation. in the case of hungary, this approach was also clearly expressed in the european parliament resolution on the occasion of the fifth anniversary of the red sands disaster. a transparent and rapid compensation process and a strict monitoring system are required. we must phase out fossil and nuclear energy as gradually and as rapidly as possible.
in writing. ‒ offshore oil and gas activities are increasingly taking place farther from land and often in much deeper waters than before. some activities are carried out in extremely difficult conditions, such as in the arctic, or in places where a large part of the income is dependent on tourism, such as the mediterranean or the aegean. i supported the document.

in writing. ‒ i supported the adoption of the resolution in which the european parliament expresses its grave concern at the deterioration of the internal situation in the democratic republic of the congo. in my view, the eu cannot accept that the congolese government, in breach of its international commitments, including the cotonou agreement, is not guaranteeing the democratic rights of the opposition, is violently attacking those who oppose it and is allowing the spread of street violence. i agree that the eu, through the eeas and the high representative, should take a strong stance to promote the democratisation that is essential for the economic and social development of this key country in the central african region. i also expect the european parliament's decision to support the work of the high representative and to contribute to a more favourable political process in the democratic republic of congo and thus in the region as a whole.
in writing. ‒ regarding congo, human rights groups have repeatedly reported that the human rights situation in the country has deteriorated in the run-up to the elections, with the freedom of expression, assembly and protest being weakened, including through the use of excessive force against peaceful protesters, journalists, political leaders and others. i voted in favour of the s&d motion.
in writing. ‒ i believe that training of skilled and highly qualified local staff should be a priority in order to ensure access to energy in developing countries and that a significant part of funding should be devoted to this objective. i voted in favour of the report.
in writing. ‒ the development committee report looks at the access to energy for people in developing countries. the commission has also launched a new initiative to reduce energy poverty, to take on public and governmental tasks related to electrification, to ensure that an additional 500 million people in developing countries have access to sustainable energy sources by 2030, to address the huge african potential of renewable energy, to improve the coordination of various international initiatives to promote access to energy, to address the problems of access to water and food security, to phase out subsidies for fossil fuels and to achieve universal access to energy with minimal greenhouse gas emissions. i voted for the report.
in writing. ‒ the motion for a resolution calls for the provision of clean energy to developing countries. given the objectives of the marrakesh climate summit and the fact that these countries are the ones most affected by climate change, i voted in favour of the motion. i agree that sustainable access to affordable, reliable and secure energy is essential to meet basic human needs and rights and is one of the foundations of development. of course, there are security and geopolitical aspects to this, because energy issues can lead to conflict. i therefore agree that the energy poverty situation of developing countries should be taken into account and that the eu should play a strong role in reducing it. in each country, priority should be given to clean energy according to the specific capabilities, for example, in african countries, diversified renewable solar, hydro and wind energy production would be the right solution, especially in rural areas. all of this is to avoid that eliminating energy poverty means not increasing emissions.
in writing. ‒ the objective of achieving universal access to energy is closely linked to the objective of achieving climate justice. i supported the social democratic position on the matter.
in writing. ‒ this own-initiative report of the european parliament concerns the evaluation of the implementation of the european order for payment (eufmh) directive. the eufmh aims to facilitate the recovery of amounts in cross-border proceedings. the procedure is optional, which means that it is available as an alternative to the many equivalent national procedures in cross-border cases. the procedure allows creditors to easily obtain payment orders for the recovery of uncontested civil and commercial claims. an application for an order may be submitted by post or by electronic means, does not require the assistance of a lawyer and can be executed in another member state without further formalities. a number of legal issues have arisen in relation to the transposition of the directive. first of all, the interest rate, the automation of the procedure, the forms and the use of languages. overall, the directive has provided a good procedural basis and the experience gained in its implementation does not justify any urgent amendment. however, the commission should pay due attention to the application of the directive in the future. in agreement with the above, i voted in favour of the report.

in writing. ‒ regulation (ec) no 1896/2006 of the european parliament and of the council of 12 december 2006 establishes the european order for payment procedure. it aims to facilitate the recovery of amounts in cross-border proceedings. it allows creditors to easily obtain payment orders for the recovery of uncontested civil and commercial claims. an application for an order may be submitted by post or by electronic means, does not require the assistance of a lawyer and can be executed in another member state without further formalities. the report of the committee on legal affairs states that while the main advantage of the procedure is in principle simplicity and speed, in some member states the issuing of an order can take up to six months. it shall take into account the problems of filling in and submitting the relevant forms online and the fact that in many member states it is not possible to submit the application in a foreign language. it follows the european court of justice's ruling that the effectiveness of consumer protection law requires that the court at least examine whether the contractual term on the basis of which the undertaking is seeking payment is fair to the consumer. the report calls for the european order for payment regulation to address these problems. i voted for its acceptance.

in writing. the situation of fundamental rights in the european union did not show significant progress in 2015, especially with regard to minority rights. i would like to draw attention to the fact that minority communities continue to face barriers to the exercise of their linguistic rights, to access to justice and other public services such as education, health and social services. member states should make further efforts to remove disproportionate administrative and legislative barriers that may hinder linguistic diversity at european or national level. i would encourage the commission to set a policy standard for the protection of minorities in line with the copenhagen criteria, which apply to both candidate and member states. there is a need to exchange good practices and apply best practice in addressing minority issues throughout the european union. i would encourage those member states which have not yet done so to ratify as soon as possible the framework convention for the protection of national minorities and the european charter for regional or minority languages, and those which have ratified to comply with them. this applies to both candidate and association countries. member states should guarantee the right to use minority languages and protect linguistic diversity within the union. i propose to strengthen the commission's plan for the teaching and use of regional languages, as this is the way to tackle linguistic discrimination in the eu.
in writing. i was pleased to note that this year's report also deals with the rights and protection of minorities in the european union in a separate section, thanks to the amendments proposed by meps, which significantly improved the initial draft. the report also contains several important points for the future of minority protection in europe. first of all, i would like to stress the importance of ratifying international and regional human rights treaties, which would allow the establishment of uniform systems for the protection of minorities throughout europe. i would like to ask those member states which have not yet done so to ratify them as soon as possible. i would like to draw the commission's attention to the need to develop and adopt common policy standards for the protection of minorities in the eu, also with a view to clarifying the copenhagen criteria and their application both in the member states and in the candidate countries. without them, the establishment of a system of protection of minorities at eu level is unthinkable. the report also addresses the importance of minority and regional languages. i would like to mention here a particular aspect of language discrimination, which is called geo-blocking. for example, geographical restrictions on digital content prevent minorities from accessing publicly useful content in their mother tongue. i sincerely hope that in the future we will be able to report on real progress in these areas.

mr president, let us go back to the beginning: why reform the rules of procedure at all? if we ask this question, the answer is, or should be, clear: to make the work of parliament more effective; to improve it. if nothing else we owe this to the citizens whom we represent, and it follows. this is very much in the interest of parliament itself. does anyone actually want to be a member of a badly-functioning parliament? a great deal of work has gone into the preparation of the new rules of procedure. some of it is technical – necessarily so; the outcome is that they are a more coherent, more cogent set of rules by which parliament operates. but this reform also means innovation, meaning that some of the rules to which we had become accustomed will change. while we all subscribe to change in theory, there are those who dislike it in practice. restructuring the rules of procedure was a complex and lengthy task involving high levels of experience. in other words, we are looking at expertise in action. to reject this expertise would be tantamount to the worst kind of populism, the kind that in other contexts we denounce every day of the week. with the new rules of procedure, the work of parliament will become more accountable and more focused. it will undergo a modernisation to bring it into line as co-legislator under the lisbon treaty. one particular innovation should be universally welcome. mep ranking has been generally deleterious to the work of parliament, and other colleagues have said the same thing. under the new rules, these excesses that mep ranking has induced should be curbed. so, as epp coordinator, my congratulations to mr corbett and the other members of the working group. this reform should be supported unreservedly.

in writing. ‒ on 10 december 2013, parliament adopted its position at first reading on the commission proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council establishing specific conditions for fishing for deep-sea stocks in the north-east atlantic and provisions for fishing in international waters of the north-east atlantic and repealing council regulation (ec) no 2347/2002. the council subsequently discussed the proposal in detail between january 2014 and november 2015. the negotiating groups of parliament and the council reached an agreement on the proposal following five rounds of trilateral consultations held between 17 november 2015 and 30 june 2016. the text of the agreement was adopted by the committee on fisheries on 12 july 2016. the council then adopted its position at first reading confirming the agreement. in its report, the committee on fisheries recommends that parliament agree with the council's position adopted at first reading, given that it is in line with the agreement reached in the trialogue. i voted accordingly.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the recommendation on deep-sea stocks and fisheries, which has already been submitted to the european parliament for second reading. compared to the first, three years ago, significant compromises have been made to make fishing in international waters sustainable. the recommendation suggests that the eu firstly define the area where deep-sea fishing is allowed, thereby freezing its fishing footprint. this geographical limit will apply to vessels fishing for deep-sea species, i.e. those whose catches of deep-sea species represent more than 8% of the total catch. it also stresses that parliament has envisaged specific sanctions against those who infringe the regulation. the compromise agreed on a 800-metre-deep limit that will better protect the endangered deep-sea ecosystem. i think it is important to mention that new, stricter transparency rules are being introduced by introducing obligations to make information on vessels fishing for european deep-sea species available to the public and to report all catches. the commission will assess this data annually and adjust the fishing zone accordingly (by means of implementing acts).

in writing. ‒ the part of the annual report on the situation of fundamental rights adopted by the european parliament concerning national and linguistic minorities, unlike in previous years, has been particularly strong. the fidesz-kdnp delegation therefore supported this political decision, which had no legal relevance, following the recommendation of the people's party. however, it voted against the text on a number of points, including those falling within the competence of the member states. it is of particular importance that the text includes the best minority protection report in recent years, the reference to the kalmár report of the council of europe, and the call for it to become part of eu law. the rights of persons belonging to national minorities are human and fundamental rights which the union is bound to respect under the treaty on european union. it is therefore right to expect european decision-makers, and in particular the european commission, to treat these violations with the same attention and condemnation as they do the rights of traditional national minorities, insofar as they are considered as part of fundamental rights.

in writing. ‒ the draft resolution of the committee on civil liberties, justice and home affairs on the situation of fundamental rights in the european union is very thorough: it takes into account the rights of women, children, minorities, persons with disabilities, the elderly, roma and lgbti people. it addresses some of the most important and topical issues for the promotion of human rights, such as migration, integration and social inclusion, trafficking in human beings and discrimination, xenophobia, hate crime and hate speech. with regard to migration, i consider it particularly important that the draft (a) states that the fundamental rights of migrants and refugees are violated in many cases at the external borders of the european union and calls on the member states and the eu institutions to respect international and eu law and the charter of fundamental rights of the european union in border control actions and asylum procedures; (b) calls for reception conditions that do not deprive people of their fundamental right to a decent standard of living and to physical and mental health and that are in line with existing fundamental rights and asylum legislation; (c) calls on the member states to refrain from inciting fear and hatred towards migrants and refugees among their citizens for political gain. i voted in favour of the adoption of the draft resolution.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of adopting the report, which gives a comprehensive and fundamentally realistic picture of the application of fundamental human rights in the member states of the european union. i consider it important that the summary gives due weight to the violations that threaten the most vulnerable groups in society, such as violence against women and children, discrimination against certain minorities, and various forms of hate speech. the report also addresses, in a manner appropriate to its relevance and timeliness, the responsibilities of the union and the member states in the face of new fundamental rights challenges and problems arising from the refugee crisis and the wave of migration. however, as an mep from a member state which is unfortunately perhaps the most affected by official wrongdoing - such as the rule of law, the breakdown of democratic political rights, the unlawful and inhumane treatment of refugees, and the continued discrimination against roma and other minorities - i would have found it appropriate to condemn more strongly, in some parts of the report, practices that are contrary to european standards, rather than general terms that blur the member states' specific responsibilities.
in writing. ‒ the report calls on member states, inter alia, to: refrain from creating fear and hatred among their citizens towards migrants and asylum seekers for political gain. as a committed opposition to the orbán regime, i supported the document, along with other important findings in the report.
in writing. ‒ the report aims to draw the attention of policy-makers to the fundamental difficulties and lack of resources of the cultural and creative sectors and to make proposals in this regard. the sector is underfunded and has a difficult rate of return across europe, which in many cases discourages investors. the sector is severely affected by the difficulties in the enforcement of patents and copyright due to the widespread consumer use of digital and online platforms. the report calls for proposals for solutions, guarantee instruments and dedicated resources under horizon 2020 to address these problems. the rapporteur advocates the promotion of cultural activities not only in traditional craft trades but also in the visual and performing arts, especially those related to folk arts, and thus the preservation of culture. the rapporteur calls positively on the commission and the member states to 'take care to safeguard cultural heritage, cultural and linguistic diversity and traditional knowledge, as well as european and national, regional and local expertise'. this represents a new resource and opportunity for hungarian minorities across the border, which also obliges the member states concerned to promote the preservation of cultural diversity by enhancing the rights to minority language education and the use of minority languages.
in writing. ‒ the report emphasises the need to support innovative and research-oriented european cultural and creative industries, which can ensure the preservation of linguistic and cultural diversity, while offering innovative and high-quality services. this includes, for example, various works of art, audiovisual products (films, television programmes, video games), music, cultural heritage, festivals, etc. the creative and cultural industries contribute to the preservation and transmission of european knowledge and values, while also contributing to the creation of jobs, investment and competitiveness. the future of the creative and cultural industries is therefore particularly important. creative industries are particularly strong in the european r&d market. in many cases, low barriers to entry allow people to enter the frontier of a given area who would otherwise be unable to invest in more capital-intensive investments. this feature also opens up the possibility for a wider range of people to participate in european innovation. creativity is rooted in all forms of culture and art and should be an integral part of education. it is therefore particularly important to remind member states to include arts, music, theatre and film education in their school curricula, as these are key factors in deepening knowledge of cultural heritage, artistic practice and creativity.

in writing. ‒ culture, art and creativity: the world is in fact linking this image and these values to europe. in the 21st century europe, in the transition to the digital economy, smes are increasingly replacing traditional manufacturing processes and traditional value chains. producing quality content, the ability to innovate, to tell a story, to imagine and to evoke emotion has become our most valuable commodity today. we must do all this, we must support, we must encourage and we must protect. i supported the document.
in writing. ‒ the constitutions and legal systems of the union and its member states, and of all the countries of the eastern partnership, launched in 2009 at the initiative of azerbaijan, belarus, georgia, the republic of moldova, armenia and ukraine, enshrine women's rights and gender equality. however, social discrimination is significant and gender stereotypes not only hinder women's greater participation in the labour market and political life, but also maintain the social acceptance of gender-based and unreported violence against the police. women are markedly excluded from positions of power, both in the executive and parliamentary branches, mainly due to discriminatory practices. the gender pay gap is particularly large, ranging from 24% to 50%, and the horizontal and vertical segregation of the labour market is critical. women therefore tend to accept low-paid or unreported jobs, especially in rural areas. the report aims to highlight the obstacles to women's social inclusion and how greater gender equality would help achieve the objectives of the eastern partnership and the european neighbourhood policy. it also lists examples of good practice, relevant and successful projects promoting women's rights and gender equality in the eastern partnership countries. i voted for the bill.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on women's rights in the eastern partnership countries. as the report points out, one of the main objectives of the european union's foreign and neighbourhood policy is to ensure security, peace, stability and prosperity for all. and women do play a fundamental role in this. i am therefore pleased that the gender dimension will be included in the regular reports on developments in the neighbourhood. i also find it appropriate that the rapporteur notes that women's rights and gender equality are also enshrined in the constitutions and legal systems of all the eastern partnership countries, although social discrimination and gender stereotypes are still a serious problem. i think it is important to note that the member states of the european union are facing similar problems, such as violence against women, low participation of women in decision-making processes and gender pay gaps, and that the eu member states must make serious efforts to improve the situation.

mr president, a six-month presidency cannot be expected to solve the union's major problems, but it can be expected to move forward in the right direction. the most important issue for the union is perhaps the migration situation, and the member states are most divided on the issue of mandatory quotas. the slovak government has a clear view on this. in september, he declared that the mandatory refugee quota was dead. well, if that's true, then you're walking among us as a zombie, a walking dead, because at the eu summit you said that the existing resettlement programs should be accelerated, and this week you're talking about how to enforce the principle of responsibility and solidarity. i hope that those who sent an invitation as prime minister to come here, not to refugees, but to people migrating in the hope of a better life, will also be held accountable, and solidarity will not only mean the absurd €250,000 that should be paid for a non-admitted migrant, but also, in the case of hungary, the €500 million that it has spent on protecting the schengen borders.
mr president, in its global strategy the eu has committed to act globally to address the root causes of conflict and poverty, and to promote human rights. in line with this commitment, this annual report reiterates that human rights remain a priority in our external policies, but they are increasingly under threat worldwide. at the hands of the authoritarian regimes, the space for civil society is shrinking, and violence against defenders is increasing. individuals are persecuted for their faith, the christians still being the most harassed religious community globally, in places like iraq, syria and pakistan. in china, in a climate of fear, prominent rights defenders are harassed, tortured and go missing. uyghur scholar, ilham tohti, remains in jail. tibetans live in constant fear for their existence. prominent lawyers in china, such as jiang tianyong, have gone missing in an ongoing widespread detention. considering the current migration crisis in europe, it is worth mentioning that the report distinguishes between migrants and refugees, in accordance with adequate legal procedures. our report echoes our strong commitment to european values and universal human rights.
mr president, i am pleased to note that the report devotes an entire chapter to the situation of people with disabilities. on my initiative, the report includes a thorough examination of the effectiveness of projects for people with disabilities and the involvement of ngos representing people with disabilities in the implementation of projects, in line with the principle of 'nothing about us without us'. i believe that the un convention on the rights of persons with disabilities should be followed and more projects should be set up to support disabled people in their own communities, to support the social integration of disabled people. it's not about talking, it's about acting. we don't need to export democracy, we need to strengthen local communities. local ngos need to be involved, because they know exactly what is needed locally and they can help ensure that the aid actually reaches the people for whom it is intended.
mr president, i would like to illustrate this very important point with a concrete example. i have been in iraq in the past few days, in the mosul area, and i know how committed mrs mogherini is to this area and to the normalisation of the situation. so i'd like to say three sentences about the human rights situation. nothing else can be done until we guarantee security from a human rights perspective. there's nothing worth talking about until we can get people who are opposites to sit down at the table. hundreds of thousands of refugees want to return home, but there is no hope yet. there are three things that europe can be helped with: water, electricity, education. it's as simple as that, but it's a whole different thing to do. there is one thing that needs to be taken into account, and i would like to draw your attention to it. millions of people are going to leave iraq if we don't help. we help or they come.
in writing. the european union must not give up its ambition to remain a flag-bearer and a valid example of the application of human rights and democracy in the world. this requires, more than ever, coherence and credibility in the union's external and internal policies in the face of the latest global challenges, notably the refugee crisis. the credibility of our migration policy in particular, which has recently been undermined from within by the inhuman, degrading and discriminatory treatment of refugees by some eu governments. the report by mr weidenholzer, which is very thorough and important, also confronts us with dramatic facts in this respect, but avoids naming specific member states. as a hungarian politician and a democrat, i cannot ignore this, because the systematic violation of the rights of refugees is unfortunately being carried out by the orbán government, which today provides the most shameful example in europe. the government that on human rights day is relocating refugees still stranded in the country to more humiliating conditions than ever before, to a tented camp unsuitable for wintering. the regime whose new anti-terrorism law allows a court to declare a syrian refugee a terrorist and sentence him to ten years (!) in prison for using loudspeakers and throwing stones to protest against a wall and barbed wire on the hungarian border, all without causing any personal injury. this is part of the overall picture of human rights in europe today and i believe it represents a serious internal challenge for the eu as a community of democratic values.

going to concentrate on a few more specific issues since this is not the first, and probably won’t be the last document dealing with our global strategy and its implementation. first of all, let me thank the rapporteur for the exemplary work which as usual he put into the report, both in the draft and in the negotiations. we are glad to be able to be part of many of the compromises. the report rightly highlights the possibility and the wish and even, to some degree, the fact that europe could be a diplomatic superpower. it is something that we should all strive for, and we agree that this is the goal, but there are quite a few steps along the way until we fully reach that potential. just to mention one single example: the eu has more diplomatic representations around the globe than any of the member states, but nevertheless so far we have been unable to pool even our consular functions. so the blocks that come are usually not from the other institutions, not from the european parliament and not from the council, but from the member states. a diplomatic superpower should not speak with many different voices. we can only become a diplomatic superpower if we remain committed to an integrated and common foreign policy. for that we need to convince our member states as well. secondly, i would like to mention the claims that we need significant defence capability development. we agree that we need to have power in order to be able to keep and foster peace around the world. that also requires power, we fully agree with that. we also agree that we are not there yet. we need further developments in this field. however, what we’re slightly worried about is the militarisation of foreign policy: that is something which needs to be avoided, and it needs to be avoided because a military policy cannot dictate the needs of diplomacy. last but not least, as the vice president has already mentioned, the development policy needs to be an integrated one, fully agreed between all the institutions. this is something that requires primacy to be given to development and not to security.

in writing. the european council meeting on 15 and 16 december will have on its agenda a number of urgent issues that need to be resolved as soon as possible. one such issue is immigration, which is becoming more urgent every day, as tens of thousands of immigrants arrive in europe each week in search of a better life. it is irresponsible to say that we are helping all immigrants when unemployment is high among eu citizens and a significant number of people are struggling to make ends meet. the main causes of migration must be prevented, and this requires a strengthening of partnerships with third countries, in particular african states. the basic needs of the people must be met and they must be offered a perspective on the future in their homeland. at the same time, it is crucial to strengthen the union's external borders, as demonstrated by the deficiencies in controls revealed in the wake of the tragic terrorist acts of recent months. eu citizens have a right to expect security, and this requires strengthening the fight against illegal immigration and terrorism. in dealing with the migration crisis, the union must not lose sight of the protection of its own citizens and the development of its own member states. cohesion and agricultural resources shall not be reduced when determining the resources to be used to deal with the migration crisis.
in writing. - mr president, i have to go. the eu investment fund, launched in 2014 and known as the juncker plan, has proved a huge success across much of europe. billions of euros have been mobilised in most member states for investment projects that have led to safer and more efficient energy supplies, faster internet, fewer bottlenecks and better lives for european citizens. the juncker plan gave the most money to those countries that were able to convince the european investment bank, which allocated the funds, of their country's competitiveness. member states competed for investment, but unfortunately not all member states were able to come up with competitive ideas worth eu billions. for example, in hungary and cyprus, little has been invested under the scheme. while only €17 million was mobilised in hungary, €160 billion was mobilised in the other 27 member states for risky projects with an eu guarantee. unfortunately, this shows where hungary stands in the eu nations' competitiveness rankings. if governments make an effort, if they make good proposals, the juncker plan will lead to projects that improve the lives of their citizens. of course, this requires that national governments represent the interests of their own citizens and not be concerned with themselves.
in writing. ‒ regulation (eu) 2015/848 of 20 may 2015 on insolvency proceedings entered into force on 26 june 2015. it shall apply from 26 june 2017, with the exception of the part concerning the system for the interconnection of national insolvency registers, which shall apply from 26 june 2019. the annexes to the regulation contain the insolvency proceedings (annex a) and experts (annex b) relating to its application. in december 2015, poland informed the commission that it had implemented a major reform of its national restructuring law, which entered into force on 1 january 2016, and requested that the lists in annexes a and b to the regulation be amended accordingly. the commission has examined whether poland's request complies with the requirements of that regulation and has submitted a proposal to the european parliament and the council to align the scope of the revised regulation to the current polish legal framework until it applies. the proposal is technical in nature and does not contain any substantive amendments. the aim and content of the proposal are satisfactory, but three further technical amendments are necessary. the first two amendments reflect the position of the united kingdom and ireland on the commission proposal under protocol 21 on the position of the united kingdom and ireland in respect of the area of freedom, security and justice. the third amendment aims to align the date of application of the amending regulation with regulation (eu) 2015/848. in view of the above, i shall vote in favour of the amendment to the proposal.

in writing. ‒ the purpose of the referral is to approve the protocol to the partnership and cooperation agreement between the european communities and their member states, of the one part, and the republic of uzbekistan, of the other part, on the extension of the provisions of the agreement to bilateral textile trade. this would provide for the reciprocal granting of the most favoured nation status; trade without quantitative restrictions; the principle of free transit; trade at market prices. the submission shall also include a safeguard clause and any prohibition or restriction on import, export or transit justified on grounds of public morality, public policy or public security. in the current state of cooperation, it is appropriate for the european parliament to give its consent to the signing of the protocol on the textile sector, but in the event of the suspension of the implementation of the commitments by the uzbek authorities, the parliament maintains the entry into force of articles 2 and 95 of the partnership agreement. in the light of the above, i have voted in favour of the rapporteur's proposal.

in writing. ‒ the committee on international trade has attached a motion for a resolution to the proposal referred to in paragraph 2. the partnership and cooperation agreement between uzbekistan and the eu of 1999 does not cover bilateral textile trade. the contribution to the extension was linked by the european parliament in its report adopted in december 2011 to the improvement of the situation in uzbekistan in the field of child and forced labour in the annual cotton harvest. the ilo in its 2015 report on the control of cotton harvesting in uzbekistan found that child labour in cotton harvesting has been virtually eliminated, but it could not make a similar statement on forced labour. the draft resolution of the committee on international trade proposes to welcome the results achieved and to recognise the measures taken by the government of uzbekistan to eliminate forced labour, and expresses the view that parliament should give its consent to the extension of the partnership and cooperation agreement to bilateral textile trade in recognition of the efforts made by the government of uzbekistan in this field. it also makes recommendations and expectations to the uzbek authorities with a view to further normalising the situation and calls on the eu bodies to monitor the process and to assist in structural reforms in uzbekistan. i voted for the bill.
in writing. ‒ in december 2011, the european parliament decided to postpone its decision to agree to the eu-uzbekistan textiles protocol and to adopt an interim report to investigate allegations of child and forced labour on cotton plantations in uzbekistan. in that interim report, parliament stated that it would only give its consent if the uzbek authorities allowed the ilo observers to carry out a thorough and unhindered inspection, confirming that concrete and substantial reforms had been carried out with significant results, resulting in the effective abolition of forced labour and child labour practices at national, provincial and local levels. i supported the resolution.
in writing. ‒ the trade agreement between the european union and its member states, of the one part, and colombia and peru, of the other part, was signed in brussels on 26 june 2012 and certain provisions thereof have been applied, in accordance with article 330 of the agreement, between the european union and peru as from 1 march 2013 and between the european union and colombia as from 1 august 2013. article 329 of the trade agreement provides for the possibility for additional member states of the andean community to accede to the agreement. the european union and ecuador concluded accession negotiations on 17 july 2014. on 20 november 2015, the european parliament adopted its resolution on the accession of ecuador to the trade agreement (2015/2656 ((rsp)) urging the government of ecuador to take similar measures based on the action plans submitted by colombia and peru. following the adoption of the resolution, the rapporteur visited ecuador in march 2016. in view of the above, the granting of consent by parliament is justified, but it is important to note that the monitoring and evaluation of existing agreements is a key priority of the common commercial policy. the commission is therefore required to keep parliament informed of the implementation and monitoring of this agreement. in view of the above, i have voted in favour of the motion.

in writing. legislation on fishing activities is a success story among both eu and un-level regulation. indeed, a look back over a decade has shown that it has been possible to ensure the conservation of marine fish stocks in a sustainable way, while supplying the eu's internal market with sufficient quantities of good quality fish. the report, which is clearly to be supported, will help to maintain a balanced fisheries management in scandinavia in the future.
in writing. ‒ the agreement between denmark, norway and sweden on mutual access to the skagerrak and kattegat fisheries, which entered into force on 7 august 1967, recognised that fishing rights in this area are traditionally reserved to the fishermen of the three countries concerned. denmark joined the eu in 1973 and sweden in 1995, and the commission became responsible for the management of the agreement in question in respect of these two member states. in the light of recent developments in international fisheries law, in particular the 1982 un convention on the law of the sea and the 1995 un fish stocks agreement, norway considered that the existing agreement was not in conformity with the provisions of the convention on the law of the sea in force and therefore terminated the agreement with effect from 7 august 2012 and entered into formal negotiations with the commission with a view to the development of a new agreement. the new agreement was signed on 15 january 2015. the council has drawn up a draft decision on the ratification of the agreement, which requires the consent of the parliament. in its report, the committee on fisheries proposes that parliament give its consent to the conclusion of the agreement. i voted accordingly.
in writing. ‒ the committee on fisheries has attached a draft resolution to its report referred to in paragraph 5. the draft proposes to invite the commission and the council to keep parliament fully informed of the implementation and renewal of the agreement. it also suggests that norwegian customs duties on food and fishery products originating in the union should be in line with the agreement on the european economic area and the principles of free trade in this area. i voted for the bill.
in writing. ‒ by accepting the recommendation, i have agreed to the draft agreement between the european union and the kingdom of norway on mutual access for vessels flying the flags of denmark, norway and sweden in the skagerrak fishing zone. the recommendation describes that the agreement maintains the historical fishing rights of the danish, norwegian and swedish fishermen in this area without prejudice to the rights of the fishermen of other states, while also ensuring that appropriate fisheries management and conservation measures are taken in these waters. i agree that the agreement will facilitate the implementation of a reformed fisheries management system within the union in line with the principles of the new common fisheries policy and the introduction of mandatory measures to maintain stocks above levels that produce maximum sustainable yield. i also agree that the access of any third country to the internal market should be based on reciprocity and that the duties imposed on food products from the union in the case of norway should be in line with the agreement on the european economic area. this should be done without imposing duties on food and fishery products originating in the union which are contrary to the principles of free trade in food, including fishery products.
in writing. ‒ the agreement between denmark, norway and sweden on reciprocal access to the skagerrak and kattegat fisheries entered into force on 7 august 1967. this agreement, which complements the bilateral fisheries agreement concluded between the european union and norway in 1980, allowed the three states parties to fish outside their own baselines but within a maximum distance of 4 nautical miles in the waters of the skagerrak and the kattegat. i supported the motion.
in writing. ‒ the exchange of information with law enforcement agencies of third country partners is of paramount importance for the successful fight against international organised crime. according to the european police office (europol), georgia is playing an increasingly important role in the fight against organised crime, and more specifically drug-related or economic crime, trafficking and smuggling of human beings, and crime committed by mobile organised criminal groups. the operational and strategic cooperation agreement to be concluded between europol and georgia shall allow for the necessary exchange of information and provide for the organisation of crime prevention activities and training. europol clearly needs to deepen its cooperation with georgia, which is why i voted in favour of this initiative.
in writing. ‒ the exchange of information with law enforcement agencies of third country partners is of paramount importance for the successful fight against international organised crime. according to the european police office (europol), georgia is becoming increasingly important in the fight against terrorism and organised crime, precisely because it is a transit country for so-called foreign fighters and a vital partner in the fight against georgian criminal organisations. the operational and strategic cooperation agreement to be concluded between europol and ukraine would help and strengthen the fight against terrorism and organised crime, which is essentially international in nature. europol clearly needs to deepen its cooperation with georgia, and as a member of the fidesz people's party delegation i voted in favour of this initiative.
in writing. any cooperation that can enhance the effectiveness of the fight against organised crime, including between europol and georgia, which is likely to contribute to improving the security of eu citizens, should be supported. even if i have my reservations about it and the material doesn't dispel all doubts. a more fundamental concern is the actual treatment of personal data, especially in countries with a somewhat uncertain status. the problem is even greater when large-scale data exchange and investigations are carried out by serious apparatuses to screen out a few criminals, while masses of trained, combat-trained adult terrorists from war zones enter the union and are given protection as poor underage refugees. with a cannon in his sling, while he's dragging you into the tank. palmyra has just been taken by terrorists with the help of a high-powered diversionary infiltrated as a refugee. what about you, europe?
in writing. ‒ the council has drawn up a draft implementing decision approving the conclusion by europol of the agreement on operational and strategic cooperation between georgia and the european police office (europol). it shall consult parliament before adopting its decision. the report by the committee on civil liberties, justice and home affairs recommends that parliament approve the council's draft. i voted accordingly.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the ep giving its consent to the agreement between europol and the government of georgia on strategic and operational cooperation in law enforcement. the agreement can clearly also contribute to the security of the eu and its member states by strengthening joint action against cross-border crime. i am also aware that it raises questions, since it is concluded on a legal basis which predates the treaty of lisbon, which may be problematic from the point of view of data protection and the reduction of the ep's decision-making role. however, given that several similar agreements have been concluded between europol and third states in recent times, the refusal of parliament's consent could not be accepted in this case either from a political or practical point of view.
in writing. ‒ under the current council decision on europol, the council, after consulting the european parliament, is to authorise the conclusion of international cooperation agreements with third countries or international organisations. such an agreement may cover the exchange of operational, strategic, technical or classified information. the operational cooperation agreement shall also include the exchange of personal data. i supported him with my vote.
in writing. ‒ the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) aims to support the reintegration into the labour market of workers and self-employed persons made redundant as a result of globalisation, as a result of major structural changes in world trade patterns, or as a result of the prolongation of the global financial and economic crisis or a new global financial and economic crisis. spain has submitted an application for a financial contribution from the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) under the reference number egf/2016/004 es/comunidad valenciana automotive. the commission has examined the application and found that it complies with the requirements of the relevant regulation, and i have therefore voted in favour of the adoption of the proposal.
in writing. i support all requests to provide assistance to workers in the eu periphery, including spain, one of the countries most affected by the crisis caused by the eu's economic policies. the rapporteur also wisely draws attention in a timely manner to the alarming figures of the european automotive industry. this is already part of a longer-term trend, during which the union lost almost half of its market share between 2000 and 2015. at the same time, the sector is booming in asia and stagnating in the rest of the world. so the peaceful slumber of those in power is unique to europe.
in writing. ‒ the european globalisation adjustment fund was established to provide additional support to workers affected by the consequences of major structural changes in world trade. on 21 june 2016, spain submitted to the commission an application to mobilise the fund to support the reintegration into the labour market of bosal s.a., a company operating mainly in the region of valencia, which has made redundancies affecting the majority of the employees concerned by the application, following its bankruptcy and closure. the application concerns 250 redundant workers and is for a total of eur 856 800 from the egf. the services to be provided to redundant workers comprise the following 12 measures: 6 measures are personalised services under article 7 (1) (a) and (c) of the egf regulation, the other 6 measures are benefits and incentives under article 7 (1) (b) of the egf regulation. the personalised services account for more than 75% of the total. the commission has concluded that the application meets the conditions for a financial contribution from the fund and that the planned measures constitute active labour market measures falling within the scope of the eligible activities and has therefore submitted to the parliament and the council a proposal for a financial contribution from the fund of eur 856 800. i supported the motion.
in writing. ‒ the european globalisation adjustment fund was established to provide additional support to workers affected by the consequences of major structural changes in world trade. i voted in favour of the related motion.
in writing. ‒ this regulation which the commission is now proposing to repeal allowed member states to compensate railway undertakings for payments in respect of obligations which are not borne by undertakings in other modes of transport. as the commission states in its proposal, the regulation is no longer in line with the current legal environment. i share this view with the commission as a member of the hungarian people's party delegation. i also agree that the current wording of the regulation is discriminatory, since it makes the possibility of compensation available only to the 40 companies listed in the annexes to the regulation. therefore, it is not possible to maintain the regulation in force. parliament adopted its position at first reading on 26 february 2014. at that time, the european parliament supported the repeal of the regulation but asked that the repealing provision not enter into force until two years later. following the adoption of parliament's position at first reading, interinstitutional negotiations took place under the luxembourg and dutch presidencies of the council. on 19 april 2016, parliament's negotiating team reached an agreement with the council presidency.

in writing. ‒ the commission proposal to amend regulation (ec) no 1370/2007 has the general objective of improving the quality and operational efficiency of rail passenger services. this would improve the competitiveness and attractiveness of rail in relation to other modes of transport and further develop the single european railway area. in order to achieve the general objective, the commission proposes to apply mandatory competitive tendering for public service contracts in order to increase the competitive pressure on domestic railway markets. the objective is to increase the efficiency and improve the quality of rail passenger services. those measures shall be accompanied by provisions ensuring a favourable framework for competitive tendering procedures, including rules on access to rolling stock. the commission proposal is closely linked to the proposed amendments to directive 2012/34/eu establishing a single european railway area, which introduce open access rights for railway undertakings and strengthen the provisions governing infrastructure managers with regard to enhancing non-discriminatory access to railway infrastructure. following the adoption of parliament's first reading position on 26 february 2014, interinstitutional negotiations were held under the luxembourg and netherlands presidencies of the council (with the aim of reaching an early second reading agreement). following six tripartite consultations, parliament's negotiating team reached an agreement with the council presidency on 19 april 2016.

in writing. ‒ the commission has proposed to parliament and the council to repeal council regulation (eec) no 1192/69 on common rules for the normalisation of the accounts of railway undertakings. on 26 february 2014, parliament adopted its position at first reading, supporting the repeal of the regulation but requesting that the repealing provision enter into force only two years later. interinstitutional negotiations were subsequently held, resulting in an agreement between parliament's negotiating team and the council presidency on 19 april 2016. on 17 october 2016, the council adopted its position at first reading in accordance with the agreement.in its report, the committee on transport and tourism proposes that parliament agrees with the council's position at first reading and thereby declares that the legislative act has been adopted in accordance with the council's position. i voted accordingly.
in writing. ‒ regulation (eec) no 1192/69 on common rules for the normalisation of the accounts of railway undertakings the repeal of which is now proposed by the commission allows member states to compensate railway undertakings for payments in respect of obligations which are not borne by undertakings in other modes of transport. these obligations may include, inter alia, special payments for accidents at work which are to be paid by railway undertakings, but which are borne by the state for undertakings in other modes of transport , pensions for railway workers who normally retire earlier from strenuous work, or payment of costs relating to railway crossing facilities. the regulation was adopted before the liberalisation of the railway market. at that time, the regulation was intended to ensure that railway undertakings and undertakings in other modes of transport operate on a level playing field in terms of social costs and externalities. the commission considers that, after a number of railway packages transforming the railway sector, the regulation no longer takes into account the current legal environment. i agree that the current wording of the regulation is discriminatory, since it makes the possibility of compensation available only to the 40 companies listed in the annexes to the regulation. for all these reasons, i voted in favour of the recommendation.
in writing. ‒ the regulation on common rules for the normalisation of the accounts of railway undertakings which the commission is now proposing to repeal allows member states to compensate railway undertakings for payments in respect of obligations which are not borne by undertakings in other modes of transport. i was not in favour of the enf proposal, following the s&d's position.
in writing. ‒ the commission proposal to amend regulation (ec) no 1370/2007 has the general objective of improving the quality and operational efficiency of rail passenger services. this would improve the competitiveness and attractiveness of rail in relation to other modes of transport and further develop the single european railway area. in order to achieve the general objective, the commission proposes to apply mandatory competitive tendering for public service contracts in order to increase the competitive pressure on domestic railway markets. the objective is to increase the efficiency and improve the quality of rail passenger services. those measures shall be accompanied by provisions ensuring a favourable framework for competitive tendering procedures, including rules on access to rolling stock. the commission proposal is closely linked to the proposed amendments to directive 2012/34/eu establishing a single european railway area, which introduce open access rights for railway undertakings and strengthen the provisions governing infrastructure managers with regard to enhancing non-discriminatory access to railway infrastructure. following the adoption of parliament's first reading position on 26 february 2014, interinstitutional negotiations were held under the luxembourg and netherlands presidencies of the council (with the aim of reaching an early second reading agreement). following six tripartite consultations, parliament's negotiating team reached an agreement with the council presidency on 19 april 2016.
in writing. ‒ the fourth railway package has been under negotiation for years, with the european parliament having adopted its first reading at the end of the previous parliamentary term in february 2014. in view of the document adopted by the european council which differed significantly from the ep's opinion, interinstitutional negotiations were continued between october 2015 and april 2016 in order to bring the positions closer together. the final agreement with the council was reached on 19 april 2016 in the framework of the trilogues. the package of proposals adopted is a success for users and railway companies and a further step towards the single european railway area. for users, the change means a more dynamic and user-friendly service in the future, as well as a higher quality and more frequent service. the general objective of the proposals is to open up the market for domestic rail passenger services, improve the quality of services and increase operational efficiency, which would improve the competitiveness and attractiveness of rail in relation to other modes of transport. from the outset, it was of paramount importance for hungary to maintain the current form of the hungarian state railways and to adopt the current form and functioning of the integrated company győrsopronebenfurti vasút zrt. we have managed to reach an agreement on these issues that is acceptable to us and that avoids unnecessary, costly and lengthy reorganisations. so as a member of the hungarian people's party delegation, i supported the report.

in writing. the parliament has already given a decision on the first reading of the regulation on the opening of the market for domestic passenger transport services by rail, which is otherwise somewhat controversial. to put it mildly, there is mixed experience with market liberalisation, which is essentially about large, often state-owned, companies in the developed eu countries gaining access to budget support from the less developed countries. the vote on the substance is no longer on the substance as a whole, but on the amendments, since the substance has unfortunately been adopted by parliament. the amendments to the draft budget are those which deal mainly with workers' rights and are therefore eligible for support.
in writing. ‒ the commission has proposed to the parliament and the council the adoption of a directive amending regulation (ec) no 1370/2007 as regards the opening of the market for domestic passenger transport services by rail. the aim was to improve the quality and operational efficiency of rail passenger services, and the commission proposed mandatory tendering of public service contracts to increase the competitive pressure on domestic rail markets. parliament adopted its position at first reading on 26 february 2014. the lithuanian parliament, the luxembourg chamber of deputies, the senate and the chamber of deputies of the netherlands, the austrian federal council and the swedish parliament also submitted reasoned opinions to the effect that the draft legislative act was not compatible with the principle of subsidiarity. interinstitutional negotiations were subsequently held, resulting in an agreement between parliament's negotiating team and the council presidency on 19 april 2016. the council adopted its position at first reading on 17 october 2016, in accordance with the agreement. in its report, the committee on transport and tourism proposes that parliament agree with the council's position at first reading and thereby declare that the act will be adopted in accordance with the council's position. i voted accordingly.
in writing. ‒ the european commission has amended regulation (ec) no 1370/2007 to improve the quality and operational efficiency of rail passenger services. as one element of this, the commission proposes the mandatory competitive tendering of public service contracts. in addition, the competent authorities would be required to clearly define the rules on public service obligations applicable to public passenger transport services and their scope, for example by allowing the competent authorities to combine cost-covering services with non-cost-covering services. this is essentially the compensation of the net financial effects of the operation of the public service obligations in a cost-effective manner. the draft also includes social aspects, such as the obligation for public service providers to comply with the obligations laid down in applicable legislation and collective agreements in the field of social and labour law. however, i believe that this second phase of the proposal has been watered down too much, because the liberalisation of the railway market only makes sense if it is combined with open competition and social and labour protection for workers. they were not explicitly mentioned in the present proposal due to the efforts of the people's party and i did not consider this acceptable in this form.
in writing. ‒ in order to achieve the overall objective, the commission proposes to apply mandatory tendering for public service contracts in order to increase the competitive pressure on domestic railway markets. the objective is to increase the efficiency and improve the quality of rail passenger services. those measures shall be accompanied by provisions ensuring a favourable framework for competitive tendering procedures, including rules on access to rolling stock. i was very much in favour of the s&d position.
