in writing. ‒ the commission has proposed to the parliament and the council the adoption of a directive amending directive 2012/34/eu as regards the opening of the market for domestic passenger transport services by rail and the management of rail infrastructure. the proposal aims to open up the market for domestic passenger transport services by rail in order to increase the competitive pressure on domestic rail markets and to increase the volume and quality of passenger transport services, and to strengthen the governance of infrastructure managers to ensure equal access to infrastructure. parliament adopted its position at first reading on 26 february 2014. at the same time, the french senate, the lithuanian parliament, the luxembourg house of representatives, the dutch house of lords, the dutch house of commons and the swedish parliament submitted reasoned opinions to the effect that the draft legislative act was incompatible with the principle of subsidiarity. interinstitutional negotiations were subsequently held, resulting in an agreement between parliament's negotiating team and the council presidency on 19 april 2016. the council adopted its position at first reading on 17 october 2016, in accordance with the agreement. in its report, the committee on transport and tourism proposes that parliament agree with the council's position at first reading and thereby declare that the act will be adopted in accordance with the council's position. i voted accordingly.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the recommendation on the second reading of the fourth railway package on the market pillar and its governance directive. the main objective of the legislative proposal is to increase the competitiveness of domestic rail passenger transport markets and to improve the quantity and quality of passenger transport services by opening up the domestic rail passenger transport services market. rail freight and international passenger services were opened to competition in 2007 and 2010 respectively, in order to increase the efficiency of public funding of passenger services. the commission also considered that the measure was necessary to ensure that the infrastructure was not used for the purpose of the public service obligations. the current proposal aimed to strengthen coordination between infrastructure managers and railway companies and to consolidate cross-border cooperation between infrastructure managers. the changes will increase competition, ensure financial transparency and fair financing conditions. increased competition is expected to increase the attractiveness of railways, which will be more responsive to consumer needs, and will also increase the need for trained railway workers and operators of service facilities.
in writing. ‒ one of the objectives of the proposal is to open up the market for domestic rail passenger services in order to increase the competitive pressure on domestic rail markets and to increase the volume and improve the quality of passenger services. the rail freight and international passenger services were opened to competition in 2007 and 2010 respectively with the adoption of the previous railway legislative packages. the proposal should be read in conjunction with the proposed amendments to regulation (ec) no 1370/2007 and, in this context, aims to increase the efficiency of public funding of passenger transport services. i was very much in favour of the s&d position.
in writing. ‒ the commission proposal aims to contribute to a more efficient, interconnected and sustainable operation of the ten-t by creating a framework that improves the functioning of ports and helps them adapt to changing transport and logistics requirements. the main objectives of the proposal include the modernisation of port services and operations and the establishment of a framework to attract port investment. in this regulation, the commission set itself the objective of counterbalancing the weak competition and possible market abuse in order to increase the efficiency of port services. the clear framework of state aid rules is an important requirement for fair competition between ports on a level playing field. the proposal is in line with other important eu policies and objectives, such as the white paper on transport, the european network financing facility and the blue zone initiative. this regulation will apply to all maritime ports identified in the ten-t guidelines and will, in the commission's view, not impose additional burdens on ports that are already functioning well and will create the conditions for other ports to meet the structural challenges they face. in view of this, as a member of the hungarian people's party delegation, i supported the report.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on access to the market for port services and the establishment of a framework for financial transparency in ports. european ports make a major contribution to the long-term competitiveness of european industries. this is why i support - and i agree with the commission's proposal - the creation of a more efficient, more interconnected and more sustainable ten-t. this is indeed essential to develop a framework that improves the functioning of ports and helps them adapt to changing transport and logistics requirements. the fact that the material has been given an important role in ensuring fair competition between ports, one of the central elements of which is a clear framework of state aid rules, is to be welcomed. among the amendments tabled by the rapporteur, i particularly agree with the amendments on the social provisions governing the port labour law system, which advocate the enforcement of workers' rights, such as better training and safety conditions.

in writing. ‒ the council intends to appoint juhan parts of estonia as a member of the court of auditors, but is obliged to consult parliament on the appointment. the parliament's committee on budgetary control has assessed the merits of the proposed candidate and has heard the candidate at its meeting on 5 december 2016. on this basis, it recommends that parliament give a favourable opinion on the council's proposal to appoint juhan parts as a member of the court of auditors. i voted accordingly.

in writing. ‒ the treaty establishing the european coal and steel community expired in 2012. the member states then decided to replace the contract by a research fund to support innovation in the coal and steel sectors. the fund contributes around €50 billion a year to innovation, benefiting both industrial companies, small businesses and research institutions. the priorities for support have not changed significantly since the establishment of the fund, but the way the scheme has operated in practice has shown that further fine-tuning is needed. the subsequently introduced horizon 2020 research and development programme also provides funding for those involved in innovation. the coordination of the two programmes is essential for their effective operation. accordingly, the two main objectives of the present proposal are to harmonise the operation of the research fund for coal and steel and horizon 2020 in terms of financing, control and management processes. both the coal and steel industries in hungary have a long tradition. the commission therefore concluded that the union industry did not suffer material injury within the meaning of article 3 (5) of the basic regulation. it is important that the knowledge accumulated in the industries is not lost and is able to support the country's economy and competitiveness up to date, adapting to the changed economic and technological environment.

in writing. ‒ the treaty establishing the european coal and steel community (ecsc) was signed in 1951; since then, the eu has been supporting coal and steel research for more than 50 years. this was done by transferring the assets of the esf (and the interest accruing thereon) to a research fund for coal and steel (rfcs) after the expiry of the contract in 2002. the programme shall be financed from the revenue generated by the remaining assets of the former esdc. the report describes that the rfcs complements horizon 2020 and provides around eur 50 million per year in support of r&d&i activities for the steel (72,8%) and coal (27,2%) industries. it brings together eu industrial partners, smes, leading research centres and universities and helps them to develop their expertise and innovate within the sector. the report responds to a commission proposal to amend this legal basis in order to facilitate access to funding through simplified rules, in particular by bringing it proportionately closer to the rules of the general research framework programme 'horizon 2020'. the second objective is to ensure that the commission, through the amendments, manages the programme with due transparency and in accordance with the commission's rules on expert groups. in view of the late publication of the commission proposal and the ep's position in the process of being formulated, i voted in favour of the report and its amendments.
in writing. ‒ the eu has been supporting coal and steel research for more than 50 years. it all started with the treaty establishing the european coal and steel community (ecsc), signed in 1951. i supported the current proposal.

in writing. ‒ the report examines the possibilities for reducing price volatility in agricultural markets. it gives a good historical overview of the cap's changing objectives from the early 1990s onwards, and its proposals are framed in a way that is almost contextual. the report can also be seen as a necessary and timely precursor to the cap review and adjustment paths for the financial cycle 2014-2020 in at least the three areas it undertakes. these areas are: 1) the need to establish and strengthen producer organisations; 2) the need to strengthen and promote the second pillar risk management tools among farmers; 3) the need to improve market transparency by setting up price monitoring centres. the work is particularly valuable for the depth of detail with which it attempts to uncover the causes of price fluctuations that are unfavourable to both farmers and consumers. in doing so, it appropriately criticises the adverse effects of free trade rules, the consequences of exposure to weather, rising input prices, and falling profitability, which result in millions of farms disappearing from the eu economy in a single cycle. i supported the report because of its timeliness and its objective findings.
in writing. a comprehensive, fairly detailed, supportive report that really seeks to explore the causes of agricultural price fluctuations. it rightly criticises the negative effects of free trade regulation, which in general create a disadvantageous situation for both producers and consumers. it is incompatible with the legitimate demand for sustainable development and the commitment to good quality food that hundreds of thousands of small farms fail every year in the eu because of regulatory failures and the rise of multinational companies.
in writing. ‒ the draft resolution of the committee on agriculture and rural development states that the main risk to european farmers is the volatility of agricultural prices, and that the cap's risk management tools are not able to mitigate this risk. the draft envisages that the european union will have to find a solution to this situation, through the development of instruments within the cap that will make it possible to combat price fluctuations effectively. i voted for the bill.
in writing. ‒ we need concrete tools to counter price volatility in agricultural markets, which is most pronounced among producers and often does not reach the rest of the food chain. the exception is the consumer sector, which is often the victim of unfair commercial practices. i agree that the instability and imperfection of agricultural markets, the globalised nature and complexity of agricultural markets, the weather-related volatility of supply, the increased health risks and the uncertain balance of food supply will make farmers even more vulnerable to price fluctuations. the instruments identified in the report such as support for producers and their organisations, a better and more transparent contracting system and a better agricultural market and price monitoring system will reduce price fluctuations if they reach genuine producers or their organisations. these instruments, these subsidies, are not wasted resources, because one of the main objectives of the cap is to create food security. another important fact is that the sector is increasingly exposed to the adverse effects of climate change, in addition to competition, and therefore needs to be developed. we will therefore develop a deeper and more coherent policy with targeted instruments at eu and member state level to ensure multifunctional and sustainable agricultural production and fair prices. for all these reasons, i voted in favour of the motion.
in writing. ‒ agricultural activity is dependent on biological processes. it is therefore highly dependent on climatic conditions and diseases of plants and animals. farmers have no control over natural factors. the performance of agricultural holdings is therefore much more uncertain than that of undertakings in other sectors of the economy. i supported him with my vote.

in writing. ‒ at today's plenary session in strasbourg, meps voted in favour of a report on visa liberalisation and simplification of the suspension mechanism for visa exemptions. the report says that the suspension mechanism will be simplified and speeded up, while progress can also be made with regard to visa-free travel for ukraine and georgia. it is important that the granting of visa-free travel to ukraine and georgia strengthens cultural and economic cooperation with the neighbouring states of the european union. the european commission already concluded last december that ukraine had fulfilled the criteria of the visa liberalisation action plan (vlap), but the introduction of visa-free travel was still pending. ukraine started work in 2008 to meet the conditions for visa-free travel and has done so, and therefore has a legitimate desire for the eu to lift visa restrictions for its citizens as soon as possible and allow them to enter the eu in a dignified manner, which is also seen as a recognition of its reform efforts.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the approval of the regulation establishing the agreement between the council and the european parliament on the adjustment of the list of countries subject to visa requirements for entry into the eu, with a view to making it faster and more flexible than at present, with a view to increasing the number of travellers and the rate of applications rejected, and with a view to exceptional circumstances, and to temporarily suspending the status of certain countries. however, i am confident that the proposal will ensure that human rights and the right to respect for private life, the right to a fair and transparent trial, data protection in accordance with eu rules and the human dimension will continue to be given equal weight in the future in the procedure under the amended rules. i consider the new rules to be an important concrete achievement, in that they will soon allow visa-free entry for citizens of georgia, one of the european union's important eastern neighbourhood partners.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the motion to raise an objection to the draft commission implementing directive amending the council directive on protective measures against the introduction into the community of organisms harmful to plants or plant products and against their spread within the community. the objection is that the draft commission implementing directive jeopardises the rules on the introduction into the union of fruit susceptible to certain pests, in particular black spot disease and xanthomonas disease of citrus fruits. moreover, it is not compatible with the objective of regulation (eu) 2016/2031 which aims to identify the plant health risks posed by pathogens, animal or parasitic plant species, strains and biotypes harmful to plants or plant products and provides for measures to reduce those risks to acceptable levels. the outbreak of xylella fastidiosa in italy and the spread of invasive species in europe demonstrate the need to ensure the pest-free status of all imported plants or plant products. one infected plant can destroy an entire industry, an indigenous ecosystem, or the economy of a region.
in writing. ‒ the resolution aims to help those affected by the use of thalidomide, an anti-nausea drug that was introduced in the 1950s. the drug company that made the drug covered up the side effects on pregnant women, resulting in thousands of births worldwide with physical and mental illnesses as a result of the drug's harmful side effects. unfortunately, in a criminal trial in the 1970's, the company was able to get the case settled without payment of damages. the victims, who are in their 50s and 60s, have reported worsening effects of their birth defects, which have induced increased healthcare costs, increasingly expensive therapeutic treatments. the eu commissioner responsible, recognising the problem, has made references to the need to address the settlement of the healthcare costs of these victims at eu level, but no substantive action has been taken so far. parliament therefore calls on the commission to take steps to represent the interests of victims at eu level and to provide them with resources for their healthcare, and to oblige the company to accept its own liability and pay a reasonable amount of compensation to the victims in the event of a retrial. on the basis of the foregoing, i have voted in favour of the adoption of the motion.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution which raises the issue of the elderly victims of the thalidomide scandal to eu level, as many of them could be put in a worse position than before without support. in my view, the decision rightly undermines the primary responsibility of the pharmaceutical company and the german government, but it also rightly calls on the governments of several other eu member states, and in particular the spanish authorities, to take the necessary measures to ensure that victims who have been excluded from the fund for this purpose also receive the aid. i hope that the swift action and greater flexibility that this decision has called for will enable the victims concerned to experience in concrete terms the value of european solidarity.
in writing. ‒ the motion for a resolution draws the commission's attention to the fact that, despite the incentives provided for in the previous regulation, little substantial progress has been made in the research and development of paediatric medicinal products. since the entry into force of the regulation, a total of two specific paediatric cancer medicinal products have been genericised. unfortunately, pharmaceutical companies have used the incentives (typically financial resources) to develop cancer drugs that can be made primarily for children, but also allow therapeutic treatment of similar cancers in the adult population. so, once again, the profit-oriented approach has overridden the constructive and forward-looking intention of the legislator. the proposal therefore calls on the commission to draw up a report on the interim review of the practical functioning of the regulation and to develop new incentives to attract companies to develop medicines to promote the therapeutic treatment of serious diseases specifically designed for children. on the basis of the above, i voted in favour of the adoption of the motion for a resolution.
in writing. ‒ i would like to draw the attention of the parliament to the fact that early paediatric trial plans and early scientific and regulatory dialogue and cooperation with the european medicines agency will allow companies to optimise global paediatric development and, in particular, to develop even more feasible paediatric trial plans. i voted for the motion to pass.
in writing. ‒ many children suffer from a rare childhood disease but do not have access to paediatric medicines. over-the-counter medication is often based on experience rather than targeted clinical research. in fact, the development of new paediatric medicines lacks the innovation and incentives needed in many areas. while there is no doubt that the paediatric regulation has had a positive impact on the development of certain paediatric medicines and has brought tangible benefits in many childhood diseases, there is a very high number of areas where insufficient progress has been made. with these in mind, i agree that we need to promote innovation in paediatric medicines to ensure that all children are treated with medicines that are proven to be effective and safe. the proposal urges the european commission to review the regulation of paediatric medicines, to make paediatric developments more than disease-based, to develop disease and drug ranking models and to develop incentives that facilitate research. i therefore voted in favour of the motion for a resolution.
in writing. ‒ in its present form, the ep committee on petitions is only a substitute for european citizens who are vulnerable to the arbitrary practices of member states and eu bodies against eu-declared values. in 2015, 483 petitions were declared admissible and there is still a lot of misunderstanding about the scope of the union's activities, as indicated by the high number of petitions declared inadmissible (33,8%). although the report notes that it regrets that petitioners still do not receive sufficient information on the reasons for the inadmissibility of petitions, it does not see any proposal for a substantive change in the rules. it is clear that the petition system needs to be radically transformed to ensure that this right granted to european citizens is not used arbitrarily, in a discriminatory way, according to the subject, as was the case with the professionally based petition of foreign currency borrowers. the report, while containing elements critical of the current practice, does not propose any radical change, which is why i abstained in the final vote.
in writing. ‒ i would like to emphasise that petitions play an important role in the legislative process, as they identify gaps and shortcomings in the transposition of community legislation and serve as a useful and direct resource for other parliamentary committees in their legislative work in their respective spheres of competence. the committee on petitions welcomes the increased cooperation between it and the other parliamentary committees and the fact that petition-related matters are dealt with more frequently in plenary sessions. i believe that petitions should not be the sole responsibility of the committee on petitions, but should be the shared responsibility of all parliamentary committees. i think that more efforts should be made to share the information needed to properly assess petitions.
in writing. welcomes the report as at least regrettable that petitioners still do not receive sufficient information on the reasons for the inadmissibility of their petitions, but this is a welcome development as it does not contain any proposal for a substantive change in the rules. it is a matter of outrage to all people of good will that the committee, although it considered the petition acceptable, then arbitrarily rejected it on the basis of a completely erroneous, even cynical, reasoning. the commission notes that the commission has not provided any evidence that the hungarian authorities have not provided any evidence that the measures in question are compatible with the internal market. no wonder many people view the committee on petitions as a rogue organization.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the adoption of the report on the activities of the committee on petitions of the ep for 2015. the number of petitions received by the committee in the year under review was significantly down, by 47% compared with the previous year, but the possibility of having recourse directly to the committee on petitions and, through its work, to the only directly elected eu institution, the european parliament, remains important for the transparency of the eu's workings, its closeness to citizens and the experience of eu citizenship. the report also provides a detailed breakdown of the data by member state and important additional findings. these show that a significant number of the submissions concern the areas of environmental protection and social rights, which is a remarkable fact both as a left-wing representative and as a member of the envi committee, and also for my own representative work. i also appreciated that the report highlights the legal and practical limitations on the work and powers of the committee on petitions and its examination, while at the same time making substantive suggestions on several points for overcoming them in the future.
in writing. ‒ the commission is obliged to share information on international air transport negotiations with the competent committee of the ep, the committee on transport and tourism, in order to reach a common agreement between the european parliament and the european commission. the resolution was drafted in the context of this process and is supported by the hungarian people's party delegation. the motion stresses, inter alia, that in order to allow members to decide at the end of the negotiations whether or not to give their consent, parliament must follow the process from the beginning. this is also in the interest of the other institutions, as it allows them to identify and address at an early stage any concerns which, by reason of their gravity, could call into question parliament's willingness to give its consent.

in writing. ‒ i intended to vote in favour of the motion for a resolution on international air transport agreements. in accordance with the european aviation strategy, the council authorised the commission to open negotiations on aviation security agreements with japan and china and to open negotiations on aviation security agreements at union level with asean, turkey, qatar and the united arab emirates. i agree with the motion for a resolution that the european parliament should follow the process from the beginning. all the more so since at the end of the negotiations, you have to make a decision about whether or not to give your consent. it is true that it is also in the interest of the other institutions to identify and address at an early stage any concerns which might call into question parliament's willingness to give its consent. i also welcome the call for the commission to allow the members of the european parliament to have access, in parallel with the council, to all relevant documents, including negotiating directives and consolidated texts, on an equal footing.
on behalf of the s&d group. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the european parliament is here. the s&d group also believes that it is essential that the european customs union, as one of the cornerstones of the union, should function properly and effectively, and in a way that serves the best interests of european businesses and citizens. it is hoped that the new customs code introduced from may 2016, with a full implementation deadline of december 2020, will indeed result in greater legal certainty, uniformity and simplified customs rules in practice. this would in particular benefit small and medium-sized enterprises, which are particularly disadvantaged by complex customs rules and procedures and thus have to bear the additional tax burden due to tax evasion and tax evasion by multinational companies. if these areas do not change for the benefit of smes, the european union's competitiveness will suffer. the other key group, besides smes, whose interests should be served by the new customs code is the european consumer. the new customs legislation should therefore better protect consumers from goods that are harmful to health and the environment and illegal. to ensure that the new rules really lead to a simpler, faster and safer customs union, we urge that during the transition period, problems arising are continuously monitored and the system is adjusted so that all member states comply with the requirements from 2021. in conclusion, mr president, i wish you and all european citizens a very happy christmas and a successful 2017.
